literature_claim: Germline/neural-developmental and dense postnatal conditional Adam10 deletions have strong cortex and synapse phenotypes.
main_caveats: There were only 20-69 Adam10-programmed cells per measured group, true DNA indel rates were not measured, and hippocampal CA1/CA3 groups were not recovered for Adam10.
summary: Adam10 produced no BH-supported downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 9 neuronal cell groups in which it was recovered.
why_it_matters: This is the central result: the postmitotic, sparse Adam10 perturbation did not elicit a stress, synaptic, Notch-target, APP-processing, or other whole-transcriptome program in surviving NeuN+ nuclei, despite uniformly negative but FDR-flat Adam10 self-transcript changes.

literature_claim: ADAM10 cleaves APP, Notch-family receptors, and multiple neuronal synaptic adhesion substrates.
main_caveats: Several obvious family members or pathway genes, including Adam9, Adam17, Adam19, Bace1, Psen2, Ncstn, and Hes genes, were not target labels in the parquet and therefore could not be directly perturbed.
summary: Measurable APP, Notch, and synaptic-adhesion relatives failed to form a shared Adam10-like RNA module.
why_it_matters: ADAM10 is biochemically central to APP α-cleavage, Notch S2 cleavage, and neuroligin/neurexin/cadherin-family ectodomain shedding, but perturbing nearby represented genes yielded either target-only, null, or one-gene idiosyncratic surfaces rather than a convergent postnatal neuronal transcriptome.

main_caveats: Wdr26 is a data-driven comparator rather than an ADAM10 pathway member; signature correlations were computed from all Wilcoxon scores because Adam10 had no significant genes.
summary: The Adam10 all-gene signature sat at the empirical noise floor while Wdr26 proved that comparable recovered cell numbers can produce hundreds to thousands of DE genes.
why_it_matters: The best positive neighbor of Adam10 was a safe-target control and the strongest negative neighbor, Wdr26, generated large FDR<0.10 responses in five Adam10-matched cell groups; Adam10 is therefore not simply hidden by a universally insensitive low-count stratum.

literature_claim: ADAM10 is the major neuronal APP α-secretase, and ADAM10 Alzheimer-associated variants reduce α-secretase activity.
main_caveats: The screen did not quantify Aβ, sAPPα, sAPPβ, APP C-terminal fragments, or ADAM10 protein activity.
summary: The Adam10 null should not be read as absence of Alzheimer-relevant α-secretase biology.
why_it_matters: The disease-linked endpoint of ADAM10 loss is reduced APP α-cleavage with reciprocal Aβ-biased processing, a protein-fragment phenotype that snRNA-seq of sparse postmitotic neuronal nuclei does not directly read out; the dataset mainly says there is no broad acute neuronal RNA biomarker for that axis.

literature_claim: Complete or biallelic ADAM22/LGI1-ADAM22 disruption causes severe postnatal synaptic and epileptic phenotypes in mice and humans.
main_caveats: DNA indel burden and ADAM22 protein loss were not measured; the screen reads nuclear RNA, not AMPAR currents, Kv1-channel clustering, or seizures.
summary: Adam22 loss produced a strongly buffered neuronal snRNA-seq surface: one downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 21 recovered cell groups and 355046 tested Adam22 rows, despite recurrent mild decreases in Adam22 mRNA.
why_it_matters: The result rewrites the experiment as a mostly negative perturbation on the transcriptional axis rather than a failed target; the on-target mRNA behavior was compatible with the expected modest CRISPR transcript effect, while downstream cell-state remodeling was essentially absent.

literature_claim: PUM3 is annotated as an RNA-binding PUF-family gene, but no cited source places it downstream of ADAM22.
main_caveats: A single FDR<0.10 gene at FDR 0.0725 does not establish a pathway; it did not recur in represented PSD/TARP/AMPAR/Kv1 comparator perturbations.
summary: The only downstream Adam22 hit was Pum3 up-regulation in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: PUM3 is an RNA-binding PUF-family protein, so the singleton hit is most consistent with a narrow post-transcriptional compensation hypothesis rather than a recovered LGI1-ADAM22 synaptic program.

literature_claim: ADAM22 anchors LGI1-dependent PSD-95/TARP/AMPAR and Kv1/MAGUK protein assemblies that tune synaptic transmission.
main_caveats: The assay could only test mRNA abundance of module members and common secondary response genes, not receptor localization or synaptic currents.
summary: Adam22 did not transcriptionally engage the canonical AMPAR, MAGUK, TARP, Kv1, immediate-early, or ISR/UPR modules expected if sparse deletion caused a cell-autonomous excitability or stress state.
why_it_matters: This makes the Adam22 null informative: the P16 mosaic perturbation did not trigger an injury, seizure-activity, or receptor-subunit mRNA cascade detectable by snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: The literature places ADAM22 next to PSD-95/DLG4, stargazin/CACNG2, AMPARs, Kv1 channels, and LGI/ADAM paralogs.
main_caveats: LGI1/LGI2/LGI3/LGI4 and ADAM11/ADAM23 themselves were not perturbation targets in the parquet, so the strongest ligand/paralog tests were unavailable.
summary: Represented direct complex or receptor-subunit comparators did not phenocopy Adam22: Cacng2, Dlg4, and Kcna1 were downstream-null in all Adam22-matched groups, and Gria1/2/3/Kcna2 each produced only one isolated downstream row elsewhere.
why_it_matters: The expected linear PSD/TARP/AMPAR/Kv1 neighborhood is flat as a transcriptional network in this screen, arguing that Adam22 is embedded in a protein-localization/electrophysiology module rather than a shared acute RNA state.

main_caveats: The comparison used the full continuous Wilcoxon-score surface and all observed signs, not a shared FDR gene set; it is useful mainly to rule out strong convergence.
summary: The unbiased Adam22 signature neighbors were extremely weak: continuous score cosines peaked at Syn1 r=0.0367 and Stag2 r=0.0300, whereas the strongest negative non-safe neighbors were Ikzf3, Wdr26, and Il1rapl2 with |cosine|<0.018.
why_it_matters: These tiny similarities prevent overinterpretation of Dlg4's rank-9 nomination and show that Adam22 lacks a robust shared FDR-level transcriptomic module with synaptic-vesicle, chromatin, or unrelated broad perturbations.

literature_claim: Genetic ADAM22 deficiency is sufficient for seizures and encephalopathy, while hypomorphic mice show that residual ADAM22 can buffer the lethal phenotype.
main_caveats: No electrophysiology or animal-level seizure readout was collected; sparse edited cells may not cross a network threshold.
summary: Sparse postnatal Adam22 loss failed to mimic the transcriptional footprint one might expect from biallelic ADAM22 epileptic encephalopathy or lethal mouse loss.
why_it_matters: The screen suggests that ADAM22 disease biology should be followed with synaptic physiology, protein localization, LGI1-ADAM22 quantity, and circuit-network assays rather than relying on a cell-autonomous stress or immediate-early RNA biomarker.

literature_claim: ADAMTS17 loss is established as an extracellular matrix/fibrillin disease mechanism with ocular and skeletal consequences rather than as a neuronal transcription-factor mechanism.
main_caveats: Functional DNA indels were not measured; very small classes such as 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut are lower confidence individually, but the same null recurs in larger groups.
summary: Adamts17 produced a pan-neuronal null DE surface: every one of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups had 0 non-self genes at FDR<0.10, and the best downstream Adamts17 q value was 0.274.
why_it_matters: The strongest result is therefore not a cell-selective transcriptional program but the absence of an acute postmitotic neuronal program in a screen that sampled all 23 major neuronal groups for this target.

literature_claim: Adamts17 knockout in skeletal growth plate and chondrocytes alters fibrillin-2 deposition and down-regulates BMP-Smad1/5/8 signaling; ADAMTS17 also localizes to fibrillin microfibrils and WMS variants can impair secretion.
main_caveats: Direct Bmpr/Smad perturbations mostly lacked target-level engagement metrics and produced at most one or two significant downstream genes; the conclusion is absence of a module, not proof each pathway perturbation was a complete knockout.
summary: The fibrillin/BMP-SMAD program predicted from Adamts17 growth-plate biology was not recovered in postmitotic neurons: Fbn1, Fbn2, BMP/TGF-beta markers all had Adamts17 FDR=1.0, and represented Fbn1, Bmpr, Tgfbr, and Smad perturbations were themselves flat or single-gene responders.
why_it_matters: The expected Adamts17→microfibril→BMP-SMAD axis is context-locked to matrix-producing tissues in this assay rather than being a general neuronal transcriptional module.

main_caveats: Correlation was computed from Wilcoxon scores over all matched genes rather than restricted to Adamts17 FDR-significant genes, because Adamts17 had no such genes.
summary: Genome-wide score-space neighbors of Adamts17 were noise-scale: the strongest positive neighbor was Nipa1 at r=0.0363 and the strongest negative neighbor was Wdr26 at r=-0.0251.
why_it_matters: The Adamts17 surface is not part of a coherent detected signature family; Nipa1 was also null, while Wdr26 was a strong but unrelated responder with negligible anticorrelation.

literature_claim: Dync1li2 encodes dynein, cytoplasmic 1 light intermediate chain 2; the literature/database prior gives a dynein-cargo identity but no established ADAR1-regulated direction.
main_caveats: Single FDR<0.10 gene at FDR 0.0955; no co-regulated dynein or transport module was recovered.
summary: Adar produced one FDR-threshold downstream hit: Dync1li2 was selectively down-regulated in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: The actual responder is not an interferon gene but a dynein light-intermediate-chain transcript, so the only positive Adar biology in this screen points to a very narrow trafficking/cytoskeletal marker rather than to the canonical ADAR1 innate-immune module.

literature_claim: ADAR2/Adarb1 has nonredundant brain RNA-editing functions, including the essential Gria2 Q/R editing event, whereas ADAR1 is the ADAR family member most directly tied to endogenous dsRNA immune tolerance.
main_caveats: The Flnb-dominated Adarb1 expression module is a same-assay comparator, not a proven direct ADAR2 editing substrate.
summary: Adar did not phenocopy the ADAR-family comparator Adarb1; Adarb1 drove a recurrent Flnb-dominated module across 13 matched groups whereas Adar had no shared significant genes.
why_it_matters: The same CRISPR/snRNA assay was able to recover an ADAR paralog response, so Adar flatness is not a family-wide analysis failure; postnatal neurons separate ADAR1 from the ADAR2/Adarb1 transcriptomic response.

literature_claim: ADAR1 deficiency or AGS alleles activate MDA5/MAVS and downstream type-I-IFN/dsRNA-sensor programs, including in mouse brain disease models.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure RNA editing, DNA indels or non-neuronal inflammatory amplification.
summary: The literature-predicted MDA5/type-I-interferon response was absent after Adar perturbation in every measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: ADAR1 loss is expected to unmask endogenous dsRNA and up-regulate ISGs; because Ifih1, Mavs, Stat1/2, Irf7/9, Isg15, Ifit, Oas and Rsad2 transcripts were all FDR-negative, these sparse P16 NeuN+ cells did not enter the AGS-like IFN state.

main_caveats: Score correlations were computed over the model-visible DE surface, not over editing sites or protein phenotypes.
summary: Unbiased cross-target neighbors were essentially zero-correlated and included safe-target controls, so no hidden Adar-like transcriptional module was nominated by the full perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The nearest and farthest score-vector neighbors are themselves null-like, making any data-driven pathway assignment for Adar weaker than the negative conclusion that the perturbation was globally buffered in this assay.

comparators: all measured targets in the matched cell groups
literature_claim: Mouse Flnb is an ADAR2-edited transcript.
main_caveats: The dataset measures Flnb mRNA abundance rather than Flnb editing; the Flnb decrease may be direct, compensatory, or selective.
summary: Flnb is the dominant recurrent abundance biomarker of Adarb1 perturbation, down in 13 cell groups and ranked as the strongest Flnb-depleting perturbation in every matched responding group.
why_it_matters: The screen converts an RNA-editing enzyme perturbation into a simple abundance readout: Flnb down-regulation is much more recurrent than any canonical receptor/channel substrate mRNA change.

literature_claim: Flna is an ADAR2-edited filamin substrate in knockout comparisons.
main_caveats: Flna crossed FDR<0.10 in only one cell group, and no editing-site measurements are available.
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is the only cell group with a multi-gene Adarb1 response, combining Flnb down, Flna down, Zfp941 down, and Fam20c up.
why_it_matters: The only dual-filamin response concentrates in one thalamic glutamatergic population, sharpening the otherwise Flnb-only surface into a specific vulnerable cell-type state.

main_caveats: Zfp941 is a single marker with one FDR value near 0.10 in 191 MB P MY GABA and a low perturbed-cell count in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
summary: Zfp941 down-regulation is confined to posterior Adarb1 responders and always appears with strong Flnb down-regulation.
why_it_matters: This separates the thalamic and hindbrain/pineal tail of the response from the broader Flnb-only response and prevents over-generalizing Zfp941 to cortical or striatal groups.

literature_claim: ADAR2 edits conserved neuronal receptor and ion-channel transcripts, with Gria2 Q/R editing being the essential mouse survival substrate.
main_caveats: The assay did not quantify A-to-I editing, so unchanged mRNA abundance does not mean unchanged editing.
summary: Adarb1 loss did not change the abundance of the canonical edited ion-channel and receptor substrate mRNAs Gria2, Gria3, Gabra3, Htr2c, Kcna1, or Ryr2.
why_it_matters: The result warns that this snRNA-seq DE surface should not be read as an editome: ADAR2 biology can be active at individual A-to-I sites while bulk mRNA abundance of receptor substrates is flat.

literature_claim: Adar is the other catalytically active mammalian ADAR family member, and Gria2, Htr2c, Kcna1, Gabra3, Ryr2, and Flnb are literature-obvious edited substrates or pathway neighbors.
main_caveats: Loss of an edited substrate by CRISPR is not equivalent to expression of its unedited protein isoform.
summary: Adar and direct substrate perturbations failed to phenocopy Adarb1 in the model-visible DE universe.
why_it_matters: A directly measured contrast rules out the simplest expectation that perturbing the active ADAR family member or single edited receptor genes reproduces the Adarb1 FLNB signature in this acute abundance assay.

main_caveats: This is an exact-overlap comparison restricted to the 19 Adarb1 FDR<0.10 features; Psmb4 also had two opposite features.
summary: Tpr, Ogt, Uba5, and Psmb4 were the strongest same-direction restricted neighbors of the sparse Adarb1 signature.
why_it_matters: The dataset nominated a non-obvious FLNB/filamin convergence group rather than ADAR paralogs as Adarb1 neighbors, suggesting that Flnb reports a broader vulnerable regulatory state.

main_caveats: The comparison uses only exact FDR<0.10 overlaps and therefore cannot prove whole-transcriptome anticorrelation.
summary: Rnpc3, Sin3a, and Wdr26 opposed Adarb1 on the same restricted Flnb, Flna, Zfp941, or Fam20c features.
why_it_matters: The same cell-type features can flip direction under other perturbations, arguing that the Adarb1 pattern is not an invariant stress artifact of these genes.

literature_claim: Complete ADAR2 deficiency can cause severe neurological phenotypes, including seizure-prone early death in mice and microcephaly, intellectual disability, and seizures in humans with biallelic ADARB1 variants.
main_caveats: Sparse CRISPR in juvenile postmitotic neurons is not a germline or whole-brain knockout, and primary editing loss was not assayed.
summary: Adarb1 produced a large number of cell-type zeros and one-gene effects rather than a broad transcriptional stress program.
why_it_matters: The sparse surface constrains the biological interpretation: post-P16 mosaic loss is sufficient to perturb Flnb abundance in selected neurons, but not sufficient to drive a generalized excitotoxic, interferon, UPR, autophagy, or synaptic-collapse program detectable by this DE pipeline.

literature_claim: AC1 is a neurospecific Ca2+/calmodulin-stimulated cAMP producer with major roles in synaptic plasticity rather than a housekeeping transcription factor.
main_caveats: DNA indel engagement was not measured; target mRNA changes are expected to be weak and cannot prove failure or success of editing.
summary: Sparse P16 Adcy1 loss of function was barren at FDR<0.10 in all 20 recovered neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: A calcium-stimulated adenylyl cyclase can be essential for cAMP-dependent plasticity without being a constitutive, cell-autonomous basal-transcription driver in juvenile wild-type neurons.

literature_claim: Ca2+/CaM-stimulated AC1/AC8 signal through PKA and ERK to CREB/CRE-dependent transcription during L-LTP and long-term memory.
main_caveats: The literature program is strongly activity- and plasticity-coupled; this screen assayed resting nuclei without a synchronizing stimulus.
summary: The expected activity-dependent cAMP/PKA/ERK/CREB immediate-early program was absent.
why_it_matters: All tested Fos/Jun/Egr/Nr4a/Npas4/Arc/Bdnf markers were FDR=1.0, so Adcy1 perturbation did not recreate the CREB-regulated transcriptional state that is recruited during stimulated L-LTP and memory paradigms.

literature_claim: NMDA-receptor calcium can activate CaM-sensitive adenylyl cyclases and the AC1-cAMP arm supports thalamocortical and hippocampal plasticity.
main_caveats: Restricted to transcriptional overlap; NMDARs have many Adcy1-independent outputs, and comparator perturbations often had larger recovered cell counts.
summary: NMDAR subunit perturbations were detectable where Adcy1 was flat.
why_it_matters: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced 238 downstream FDR<0.10 calls in matched groups, ruling out the idea that this analysis universe is globally blind to upstream excitatory calcium-signaling perturbations.

literature_claim: AC1 is embedded in a calcium/calmodulin-to-cAMP signaling network that can feed PKA, ERK/MAPK, and CREB-dependent transcription.
main_caveats: Counts summarize FDR genes, not matched biochemical flux through cAMP, PKA, or ERK.
summary: Some calcium/cAMP/CREB nodes responded, but the Adcy1 branch remained silent.
why_it_matters: Calm1, Calm3, Camk2a, Camk2b, Creb1, Braf, Ppp3ca, and Pde4b all had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 call in matched groups, whereas Adcy1 and multiple PKA/EPAC/PDE nodes did not; the cAMP pathway is therefore selectively, not uniformly, visible in basal snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: Cells can express multiple transmembrane adenylyl cyclase isoforms, and AC signaling is redundant and compartmentalized.
main_caveats: The key Ca2+/CaM paralog Adcy8 was absent as a perturbation target, so AC1/AC8 double-loss redundancy could not be directly tested.
summary: Single transmembrane adenylyl-cyclase perturbations were family-wide buffered in the matched brain groups.
why_it_matters: Adcy3 and Adcy5, the other represented adenylyl cyclase targets, also produced zero downstream genes in the 20 Adcy1-matched groups, consistent with isoform redundancy and compartmentalization rather than an AC1-specific failure mode.

literature_claim: No prior claim was needed for the unbiased neighbor test.
main_caveats: Neighbor search on a null signature mostly ranks noise; it is useful only as a check that no strong convergence was missed.
summary: Unbiased cross-perturbation neighbor search found no robust Adcy1-like transcriptional signature.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive and negative whole-score correlations were only +0.0296 and -0.0183 and included safe-target or unrelated perturbations, so the dataset nominated no hidden pathway neighbor for a flat Adcy1 response.

literature_claim: In Fmr1-knockout neurons, excessive Adcy1 translation increases ADCY1 protein and Adcy1 reduction normalizes ERK1/2- and PI3K-mediated signaling, excess protein synthesis, dendritic spines, and autism-related behaviors.
main_caveats: This dataset did not perturb Fmr1 and did not measure protein synthesis, ERK phosphorylation, or behavior.
summary: Wild-type Adcy1 LoF did not resemble the Fragile-X ADCY1 overexpression state.
why_it_matters: The screen shows no broad WT juvenile neuron transcriptional toxicity or CREB immediate-early collapse after Adcy1 targeting, refining Fmr1-model rescue by Adcy1 reduction to a disease-state, hyperexpression-dependent mechanism.

literature_claim: ADCY3 is a cilia-enriched adenylyl cyclase that converts ATP to cAMP and lies upstream of PKA/CREB-regulated transcription.
main_caveats: DNA indels and AC3 protein activity were not measured; olfactory epithelium, olfactory bulb, hindbrain, and most non-neuronal ciliated cells were outside the assayed compartment.
summary: Adcy3 loss was a pan-neuronal downstream null in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR assay.
why_it_matters: ADCY3 has a strong ciliary cAMP literature, but deleting it after neuronal specification did not create a detectable basal nuclear RNA program in any recovered neuronal class; the result should be read as transcriptomic buffering, not as a failed perturbation inferred from the target mRNA.

direction: Adcy-family null; CREB-axis restricted response after Creb1/Crebbp only
literature_claim: Gs stimulates adenylyl cyclases to raise cAMP, PDEs degrade cAMP, PKA phosphorylates CREB, and activated CREB can drive CREM/CRE-containing transcription.
main_caveats: The conclusion is restricted to basal 3-4 week snRNA-seq; it does not exclude seconds-to-hours cAMP, PKA, or phospho-CREB changes after receptor stimulation.
summary: The expected cAMP linear pathway did not phenocopy: Adcy1 and Adcy5 were also downstream-null, Gnas/Gnal and Pde4b/Pde4d were flat or singleton responders, and only the nuclear Creb1/Crebbp arm produced a restricted TH signature.
why_it_matters: This separates membrane/ciliary cAMP production from durable CREB-dependent nuclear remodeling in juvenile postmitotic neurons and shows that Adcy3 did not converge on the Crem-rich CREB1 response even though that response was detectable elsewhere in the parquet.

literature_claim: The BBSome and intraflagellar-transport machinery control GPCR and membrane-protein trafficking in primary cilia, and ciliary ADCY3-cAMP signaling is linked to MC4R-dependent weight control.
main_caveats: Only a small subset of ciliary genes was represented and most comparator target transcripts were weakly changed at the RNA level.
summary: ADCY3 was not an outlier among measured ciliary genes: Bbs5, Ttc8, Ift88, Cep290, and Rpgrip1l perturbations were also essentially flat in neuronal nuclear RNA.
why_it_matters: The shared near-null argues that ciliary disease biology in this experiment is displaced to protein trafficking, receptor localization, cilium morphology, or circuit physiology rather than to a large steady-state neuronal RNA state.

literature_claim: No prior biological relationship was assumed for these unbiased nearest neighbors.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed over all matched Wilcoxon scores, so for a null target they mostly rank noise-floor structure rather than FDR-supported biology.

why_it_matters: The data-driven search did not nominate a hidden convergent pathway: Grin2b, the top positive neighbor, had its own L2/3 IT synaptic program that was absent after Adcy3, while the most anticorrelated targets were null or self-only.

main_caveats: The screen did not perturb dense MC4R-positive PVH or VMH ensembles and did not record behavior, odor responses, cAMP, or phosphoprotein endpoints.

literature_claim: ADCY enzymes generate cAMP downstream of GPCRs, AC5 is striatum-enriched, and mouse germline AC5 loss disrupts corticostriatal plasticity and striatum-dependent behavior.
main_caveats: DNA indels, cAMP, and phospho-PKA engagement were unmeasured; 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for Adcy5.
summary: Adcy5 CRISPR perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across all recovered neuronal groups: 22 measured cell groups each had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: AC5 is a GPCR-cAMP effector, but acute postmitotic loss in this sparse snRNA-seq assay did not create a constitutive mRNA state; its canonical biology is better placed in cAMP kinetics, phosphorylation, excitability, and stimulus-evoked corticostriatal plasticity.

literature_claim: PDE10A inhibition increases striatal cyclic-nucleotide signaling and can drive CRE-mediated transcription.
main_caveats: The group is a coarse CNU-LGE/LSX class rather than purified D1 or D2 medium spiny neurons, and the Pde10a signature itself contained only two FDR<0.10 genes in this group.
summary: The striatal-like CNU-LGE cAMP module was inducible by Pde10a loss but not by Adcy5 loss: Pde10a knockdown up-regulated Scg2 and Crem, whereas the same two genes were FDR-flat after Adcy5.
why_it_matters: This shows that the screen could detect a cAMP-linked transcriptional output in a central-nucleus GABA group, so the Adcy5 null is not explained by a blanket inability of snRNA-seq to see CRE-linked genes.

literature_claim: ADCY1, ADCY3, and ADCY5 are distinct CNS adenylyl cyclase isoforms with region-specific expression and regulation within the larger transmembrane ADCY family.
main_caveats: Only Adcy1 and Adcy3, not every membrane ADCY paralog, were represented as matched perturbation targets.
summary: The represented membrane adenylyl-cyclase paralogs shared the absence of downstream DE: Adcy1, Adcy3, and Adcy5 each produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their recovered cell groups.
why_it_matters: The expected paralog controls did not phenocopy Pde10a or expose a hidden ADCY-like transcriptomic module; individual acute loss of a membrane cAMP synthase is buffered at basal nuclear RNA levels.

literature_claim: GPCRs signal through G alpha subunits to regulate adenylyl cyclases and cAMP/PKA, and AC5 participates in D2- and mGluR-dependent striatal plasticity.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic only and mixes activating receptors, inhibitory receptors, cAMP phosphodiesterases, and PKA/CREB subunits whose biochemical effects have opposite signs.
summary: Most represented upstream and downstream cAMP-pathway perturbations were also nearly silent in basal transcriptome, even when Prkaca showed strong own-transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: The Adcy5 result sits in a broader GPCR-G protein-PKA axis that is not constitutively transcriptional in this assay; this separates basal mRNA quiescence from the well-established second-messenger pathway.

literature_claim: No specific literature comparator was implicated by these data-driven neighbors.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score vectors and restricted to targets with at least 50000 matched group-gene features; they are useful as a rejection control, not as evidence of Smc1a or Ndufb8 biology downstream of Adcy5.
summary: A data-driven full-surface signature search yielded only trivial Adcy5 neighbors; the top positive score correlation was Smc1a at r=0.0329 and the strongest negative annotated target was Ndufb8 at r=-0.0180.
why_it_matters: The weak Adcy5 nominal genes should not be over-read as a hidden coherent module: cross-target correlations across the model-visible universe failed to nominate a robust convergent or anti-correlated perturbation program.

literature_claim: ADCY5-related dyskinesia is caused by ADCY5 mutations; the original familial dyskinesia study identified gain-of-function ADCY5 mutations that increase the cAMP-producing activity of AC5.
main_caveats: The assay did not introduce patient missense alleles and did not measure evoked motor-circuit signaling, so the result is a boundary on this LoF screen rather than a disease model.
summary: The null CRISPR-LoF surface does not phenocopy ADCY5 movement-disorder alleles, particularly dominant gain-of-function alleles that elevate cAMP.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic reasoning should remain allele- and state-specific: reducing Adcy5 after P16 in a mosaic subset of neurons can be transcriptomically silent even though ADCY5 mutations that alter AC5 enzymatic activity cause childhood hyperkinetic disease.

literature_claim: ADD1 biology is dominated by regulated adducin/spectrin/actin membrane-skeleton and neuronal structural functions, including axon-diameter control, corpus-callosum and ventricle phenotypes, and AMPA-receptor plasticity.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; snRNA-seq cannot directly score axon diameter, axonal transport, spine morphology, or receptor turnover.
summary: P16 Add1 loss-of-function was pan-null at the single-nucleus transcriptional level: all 21 recovered neuronal classes had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The main phenotype in this assay is an absence of a cell-autonomous nuclear program, not a missed focal response; even groups with 63-104 perturbed nuclei stayed flat at the whole-transcriptome FDR threshold.

main_caveats: Only mRNA abundance was tested; phosphorylation, localization, and membrane-skeleton geometry were not measured.

summary: The post-literature synaptic-adhesion and activity-response query was completely unrecovered in the Adgrl2 DE surface.
why_it_matters: If sparse Adgrl2 editing had produced a large secondary transcriptional compensation for lost excitatory input, genes encoding latrophilin partners, glutamate receptors, postsynaptic scaffolds, or immediate-early activity markers were plausible responders; none reached FDR<0.10.

literature_claim: Latrophilins act with FLRT and teneurin ligands, and Lphn2 can be redundant with Lphn3 in cerebellar Purkinje-cell parallel-fiber synapses.
main_caveats: The comparison tested single-gene Perturb-seq phenotypes only; it did not test double Adgrl2/Adgrl3 loss or structural synapse endpoints.
summary: Represented latrophilin-family and FLRT/Teneurin/UNC5 comparators did not form a shared transcriptional module with Adgrl2.
why_it_matters: The literature points to Adgrl1/Adgrl3 paralogy and to FLRT/Teneurin/UNC5 extracellular recognition, but matched DE queries showed near-zero score cosines versus Adgrl2 and no broad downstream programs after single perturbation of Adgrl1, Adgrl3, Tenm3, Tenm4, Unc5c, or Unc5d; Flrt3 produced only two singleton DEGs.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on the full Wilcoxon-score vector because Adgrl2 had no significant signature of its own; such small cosines should not be mechanistically interpreted.
summary: The nearest data-driven Adgrl2 neighbors were algorithmic weak-signature neighbors, not biologically convergent FDR modules.
why_it_matters: Full-rank score correlations nominated Fbxo11, Syncrip, and Ndufb9 as the closest positive named targets and Sv2a, Macf1, and Nr4a1 as the closest negative named targets, but all cosines were close to zero and their measured FDR surfaces had zero to two downstream genes, so the neighbor analysis rejects a hidden shared strong module.

literature_claim: ADGRL2 has been linked to embryonic brain malformation and to endothelial barrier control.
main_caveats: The developmental variant was not a matched acute mouse null allele, and non-neuronal endothelial nuclei were not sampled.
summary: The flat neuronal result refines, rather than contradicts, embryonic and endothelial ADGRL2 disease biology.
why_it_matters: The human-developmental and endothelial parts of ADGRL2 biology live in embryonic germinal/cytoskeletal or vascular adhesion contexts that this P16 NeuN+ neuronal Perturb-seq design largely excludes; the null therefore warns against treating the postmitotic neuronal screen as a negative test of those disease mechanisms.

literature_claim: Germline Lphn3-null mice show region- and age-dependent bulk DGE, especially affecting cell-adhesion and calcium-signaling genes.
main_caveats: Downstream genes exclude the Adgrl3 transcript itself; DNA indels were not measured, and non-transcriptional synapse morphology was not assayed.
summary: Adgrl3 produced no downstream gene at FDR<0.10 in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups in this P16-to-P37/44 CRISPR snRNA-seq screen.
why_it_matters: This is a strong negative on the whole-nucleus RNA axis and prevents over-ascribing nominal genes to synaptic, stress, or compensatory pathways.

literature_claim: Germline Lphn3 knockout can disrupt dopamine-related protein markers and behavior rather than necessarily causing a large compensatory Adgrl-family mRNA response.
main_caveats: A target-transcript decrease is not a DNA indel measurement, and the affected cell groups are broad rather than dopamine-neuron-specific.
summary: Four groups had significant Adgrl3 self-RNA reduction but still showed 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The groups with the clearest target-transcript drop demonstrate that the null cannot be dismissed solely as absence of observable Adgrl3 RNA modulation.

literature_claim: LPHN3 functions through FLRT and teneurin binding plus latrophilin GPCR signaling in excitatory synapse formation.
main_caveats: Tenm2, Flrt1, and Flrt2 were not represented as measured comparators, and cell-surface ligands need not phenocopy a postsynaptic receptor at the transcriptome level.
summary: Latrophilin paralogs and represented FLRT/Tenm/Unc5 relatives did not converge with Adgrl3; most were completely downstream-flat in matched groups.
why_it_matters: A physical synapse-adhesion module in the literature did not translate into a shared postnatal nuclear transcriptional module, supporting pathway-level readout uncoupling rather than an isolated Adgrl3 anomaly.

main_caveats: Correlation was computed over all shared Wilcoxon score rows, which is intentionally conservative for a target with no FDR-level downstream DE.
summary: The unbiased cross-target search found no robust positive or negative Adgrl3 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The largest absolute Wilcoxon-score correlation with Adgrl3 was only 0.033, so unrelated ranked neighbors should not be mistaken for a biological module.

literature_claim: ADHD-linked Lphn3 missense alleles can selectively impair Gα13/RhoA signaling, and alternative Lphn3 exons can alter G-protein coupling and synapse formation.
main_caveats: The dataset tested gene disruption, not splice editing or individual human missense variants.
summary: The Adgrl3 LoF transcriptomic null does not test ADGRL3 variant-specific GPCR coupling mechanisms.
why_it_matters: ADHD-associated missense variants can be signaling-selective, and Lphn3 splice variants bias receptor coupling; a pan-LoF pooled gRNA perturbation with a gene-level nuclear RNA readout should not be used to rule out those allele-specific cellular mechanisms.

literature_claim: ADGRV1/VLGR1 is implicated in developing CNS expression, Usher syndrome, and stereocilia ankle-link biology.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; no conclusion should be drawn for cochlear hair cells, retina, embryonic CNS, or non-neuronal lineages.
summary: Acute Adgrv1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered postmitotic neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The strongest dataset-level claim is a context-specific negative: ADGRV1 loss did not trigger a durable cell-autonomous snRNA program in juvenile-to-young-adult NeuN+ neurons, despite broad recovery of the target across the taxonomy.

literature_claim: ADGRV1 is an adhesion GPCR, so other adhesion-GPCR perturbations are a measurable family-level comparator even though the core USH2 complex was absent from the target set.
main_caveats: The same-complex USH2A, whirlin and PDZD7 perturbations were not represented, so this is a family-level rather than ankle-link-complex contrast.
summary: Adgrv1 lacked a meaningful cross-perturbation signature neighbor; the closest data-driven neighbors had absolute Pearson correlations below 0.05 and the measured adhesion-GPCR relatives were themselves null.
why_it_matters: This rejects an easy family-module interpretation: neither the data-driven neighborhood nor the represented adhesion-GPCR family exposes a hidden Adgrv1-like transcriptomic program.

literature_claim: VLGR1 has been linked to G-protein regulation of MAG and to autophagy-related molecular changes after VLGR1 deficiency.
main_caveats: Marker-gene absence does not test protein-level MAG abundance, GPCR second-messenger flux, or autophagic flux in the lineages used in prior work.
summary: Adgrv1 loss failed to activate candidate MAG/myelin, GPCR immediate-early, autophagy, or unfolded-protein-response genes in the sampled nuclei.
why_it_matters: ADGRV1 literature contains signaling and autophagy priors that could have produced secondary mRNA programs; their absence makes the null informative for the assayed neuronal state and argues against a chronic nuclear stress response after acute P16 editing.

literature_claim: SMIM10L1 has prior evidence in adipose progenitor PTEN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR biology but not as a known neuronal ADIPOR2 transcriptional effector.
main_caveats: Only 37 perturbed nuclei supported the effect, and no second FDR<0.10 gene defined the pathway.
summary: Adipor2 loss produced a one-gene responder, Smim10l1 up-regulation, restricted to 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: The screen does not show a pan-neuronal adiponectin-receptor transcriptome; it nominates a narrow MGE-derived GABAergic state in which a noncanonical membrane-associated gene is sensitive to Adipor2 perturbation.

literature_claim: Adiponectin receptors are expected to engage AMPK, PPAR-alpha, fatty-acid oxidation, and ceramide catabolism, and such activity can feed mitochondrial, antioxidant, autophagy, or stress programs in responsive metabolic contexts.
main_caveats: The marker panel cannot detect lipid species, ceramidase activity, or phosphorylation events directly.
summary: The CNU-MGE Smim10l1 hit was uncoupled from canonical AMPK/PPAR-alpha/fatty-acid-oxidation, ceramide, autophagy, ER-stress, ISR, and redox transcriptional programs.
why_it_matters: Adipor2 is a lipid-metabolic adiponectin receptor; the absence of these expected secondary transcripts means the observed neuronal response is not a simple loss of the textbook AdipoR2 metabolic axis.

literature_claim: APPL1 and AMPK are canonical adiponectin receptor signaling nodes; Ppara is the direct AdipoR2 PPAR-alpha effector, and Ppard, Pparg, and Ppargc1a are adjacent PPAR/PGC-1 lipid-metabolic comparators.
main_caveats: Adipor1, Adipoq, and Cdh13 were not perturbation targets, and the represented pathway genes were themselves transcriptionally flat.
summary: Represented APPL1, AMPK-alpha2, PPAR, and PGC-1-axis perturbations did not phenocopy Adipor2 and did not induce Smim10l1 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: The Adipor2 output is isolated from directly measured canonical pathway neighbors, so it should not be annotated as a generic PPAR/AMPK knockdown signature.

main_caveats: The neighbor metric used all Wilcoxon-score dimensions and is dominated by a near-null Adipor2 profile.
summary: A blind score-vector scan found no strong transcriptomic neighbor for Adipor2: Asxl3 and Eef2 were the closest positive and negative targets, but both similarities were near zero and neither shared the CNU-MGE Smim10l1 hit.
why_it_matters: The measured Adipor2 signature is too sparse to be placed confidently into a broader perturbation module; the single CNU-MGE output should be interpreted as isolated until replicated.

literature_claim: Published SMIM10L1 functional work links its knockdown to adipose progenitor differentiation and PTEN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling, not to neuronal adiponectin receptors.
main_caveats: Single-gene, 37-cell signal with no known Smim10l1 neuronal mechanism.
summary: Smim10l1 is an exploratory candidate sentinel for Adipor2 loss in 054 CNU-MGE GABA because its FDR<0.10 induction was unique to Adipor2 among 1,731 perturbations in that cell group.
why_it_matters: Even a one-gene response can be useful if it marks the rare condition in which a receptor perturbation breaks through basal transcriptomic buffering.

literature_claim: ADK is an adenosine kinase in purine salvage and a major regulator of intracellular, extracellular, and nuclear adenosine pools.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; this is a transcriptomic null in sampled neurons, not a test of astrocytic ADK or electrophysiological adenosine tone.
summary: Acute Adk loss produced no BH-significant downstream neuronal transcriptome in any of the 23 recovered cell groups.
why_it_matters: Under P16 sparse CRISPR of NeuN-positive cells, ADK is transcriptomically buffered across every recovered neuronal group rather than restricted to a hidden responder.

literature_claim: No literature relationship was used; these were phenotype-first neighbors.
main_caveats: Signatures were compared over shared z-score vectors; because Adk had no FDR<0.10 genes, any rank ordering is dominated by weak global structure.
summary: The computed Adk nearest neighbors did not define a biological module.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative z-score neighbors were separated from zero by only |r|<=0.047, and those neighbor surfaces were themselves null or tiny single-gene responders, so cross-target analysis rejects an Adk-centered transcriptional module rather than assigning Adk to the Npy5r/Zic3/Chrna2/Fbxo11 signatures.

literature_claim: ADK regulates adenosine, which can signal through GPCR adenosine receptors, and nuclear ADK-L is linked to adenosine-receptor-independent transmethylation.
main_caveats: The direct Adora receptors, Ada, Nt5e, Entpd genes, and Slc29 transporters were not gene targets in this parquet; the tested targets are downstream or adjacent proxies.
summary: Represented cAMP, phosphodiesterase, purine, and methylation-node perturbations failed to phenocopy Adk.
why_it_matters: Although ADK biology should feed adenosine receptors, cAMP/PKA signaling, purine salvage, and transmethylation, the represented indirect targets Adcy1, Adcy3, Adcy5, Pde1c, Pde4b, Pde4d, Pde10a, Prkaca, Prkar1a, Nt5c2, and Dnmt3a had near-zero Adk correlations and at most sparse unrelated FDR genes. The expected pathway is therefore not transcribed as a stable cell-autonomous RNA module by sparse postnatal Adk loss.

literature_claim: Human ADK deficiency and mouse Adk models link ADK to brain disease, synaptic plasticity, development, and epilepsy-relevant adenosine and methylation mechanisms.
main_caveats: This is not a direct measurement of adenosine, DNA methylation, neuronal firing, or astrocytes.
summary: The Adk null argues against using this NeuN-enriched P16 screen to down-rank ADK as an adenosine-augmentation or epileptogenesis target.
why_it_matters: ADK druggability biology is dominated by astrocytic extracellular adenosine, ADK-S/ADK-L compartmentalization, methylation, development, and network physiology, so the null is best read as assay displacement rather than absence of ADK function.

literature_claim: ADNP is a high-confidence neurodevelopmental regulator active in ChAHP, with broad developmental expression and strong cortical developmental functions.
main_caveats: The screen starts at P16 and assays NeuN-enriched nuclei; it will miss embryonic progenitor effects and non-neuronal biology.
summary: P16 Adnp loss produced a narrow corrected neuronal response: 5 of 21 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with 45 genes, while two taxonomy groups were not recovered for this target.
why_it_matters: The Adnp phenotype in this acute mosaic juvenile assay is not a pan-neuronal chromatin-crisis signature even though ADNP protein is a core chromatin regulator; the responsive surface is concentrated in thalamic and midbrain classes plus one-gene Pvalb/Sst hits.

literature_claim: ADNP recruits CHD4 in the HP1-CHD4-ADNP ChAHP complex and Adnp/Chd4 conditional knockouts coregulate genes involved in cortical growth.
main_caveats: Chd4 also has Adnp-opposite hits such as Rnf112 and Eno2, consistent with CHD4 functions outside ADNP/ChAHP; overlap was evaluated only on the 54 corrected Adnp tuples.
summary: Chd4 was the only high-confidence mechanistic neighbor of Adnp: it was the top positive signature neighbor and shared same-direction FDR hits including Pvalb Cacnb3 and the thalamic Cpne7/Xylt2/Srrm4/Cacng7/Aifm3/Uchl1/Echdc2 cluster.
why_it_matters: The strongest cross-perturbation result recovers the biochemical ChAHP relationship directly inside postmitotic juvenile neurons and separates it from looser ASD/chromatin similarity.

literature_claim: Adnp-deficient mouse models have synaptic and dendritic-spine abnormalities; Cacnb3 encodes a voltage-dependent calcium-channel beta subunit.
main_caveats: Cacnb3 is still a single gene in each cell class; calcium-current or channel-protein measurements were not collected.
summary: Cacnb3 was the recurrent positive Adnp biomarker, induced in Pvalb, midbrain glutamatergic, and midbrain/pons GABA groups and also induced by Chd4 perturbation in Pvalb neurons.
why_it_matters: A calcium-channel beta-subunit response is a compact readout of the Adnp/Chd4 postmitotic synaptic-calcium arm and gives a better candidate reporter than the target transcript itself, which stayed FDR-flat in every group.

literature_claim: Plppr3 is a phospholipid-phosphatase-related gene and Atp9a encodes a lipid-transporting ATPase with neurological mouse-mutant phenotypes.
main_caveats: The inference rests on two recurrent genes, and Plppr3 was not significant in the thalamic group.
summary: Adnp repression of Plppr3 and Atp9a marks a small membrane-lipid/endosomal module across midbrain and thalamic responders.
why_it_matters: The module is distinct from ChAHP target-gene de-repression and points to membrane-trafficking adaptation as one of the secondary outputs of acute Adnp loss.

literature_claim: Adnp haploinsufficiency has synaptic phenotypes, and Rab3a is annotated as a synaptic-vesicle RAS-family GTPase with synaptic-transmission phenotypes in mouse mutants.
main_caveats: Only one FDR gene was detected and the Sst group had 28 perturbed cells.
summary: Sst interneurons showed an isolated but corrected presynaptic-vesicle hit, Rab3a down-regulation, rather than the Cacnb3 induction seen in Pvalb neurons.
why_it_matters: The two cortical interneuron classes that responded did so through different synaptic genes, arguing against a single pan-interneuron Adnp output.

literature_claim: Xylt2, B3glct, and Sdc3 are annotated as proteoglycan/glycosylation or cell-surface matrix genes.
main_caveats: Several members are cell-surface adhesion genes rather than enzymes, so this should be treated as a surface-composition module, not a single linear pathway.
summary: The 151 thalamic response included a mostly down-regulated cell-surface glycan/proteoglycan component, led by Xylt2 and joined by B3glct, Sdc3, Ptpru, Pcdh1, and Cdh24.
why_it_matters: This branch is not the textbook Wnt or chromatin-axis readout of ADNP, but it is the clearest extracellular/surface remodeling program inside the strongest neuronal responder.

literature_claim: SRRM4 and UCHL1 are annotated neural splicing/ubiquitin-handling genes; the other genes nominate metabolism and redox from their measured transcript changes.
main_caveats: The redox interpretation is gene-list based; no glutathione or mitochondrial activity assay accompanied the snRNA-seq.
summary: The same thalamic signature carried a secondary RNA/protein-handling and metabolic/redox skew: Srrm4, Cpsf6, Uchl1, and Anapc7 were down, Eif4b was up, and Gsr/Aifm3 rose while Acsl3/Acat1/Eno2/Echdc2 fell.
why_it_matters: Adnp perturbation in the strongest postnatal responder therefore alters neuronal RNA processing, ubiquitin handling, and metabolism in addition to surface genes.

literature_claim: ADNP was originally linked to a SWI/SNF-related autism syndrome and to BRG1/SWI-SNF biology, while CHD4 can also function in NuRD; these relationships make BAF and NuRD genes obvious comparators.
main_caveats: Only targets present in the parquet could be tested; Adnp2, HP1 Cbx genes, Mbd3, Gatad2a, Hdac1, and Hdac2 were not represented as perturbations.
summary: The literature-obvious chromatin and NDD comparators did not substitute for Adnp: BAF-adjacent Smarca2/Smarca4/Smarcc1/Smarcc2/Arid1b, NuRD-associated Gatad2b, Auts2, and Chd8 showed weak, absent, or distinct overlap with Adnp.
why_it_matters: This prevents collapsing all chromatin-remodeler ASD targets into one postmitotic neuronal signature; ChAHP membership, not a generic SWI/SNF or ASD label, best explains the Adnp neighbor structure here.

literature_claim: Earlier Adnp loss causes embryonic brain-formation defects and ADNP has been linked to Wnt/β-catenin neural differentiation and synaptic phenotypes.
main_caveats: Repeat-element de-repression and CTCF loop rewiring are not directly quantified by gene-level 10x snRNA-seq.
summary: Corrected Adnp loss did not recover Wnt/β-catenin, neural-induction, cell-cycle, or broad canonical synaptic-marker programs in the P16 NeuN+ assay.
why_it_matters: The absence is informative because many Wnt, progenitor, and synaptic sentinels were tested at gene level; it places those canonical ADNP programs outside the acute postmitotic transcriptomic axis captured here.

literature_claim: Alpha1A adrenergic receptors are neuromodulatory GPCRs linked to norepinephrine-evoked neurotransmission and cognition.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not assayed, and this finding concerns basal endpoint snRNA-seq rather than ligand-evoked receptor function.
summary: Sparse postnatal Adra1a loss produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 22 recovered neuronal groups, including 052 Pvalb Gaba where the Adra1a RNA row itself decreased significantly.
why_it_matters: This converts an all-zero DE surface into a biological statement: basal alpha1A adrenergic receptor loss is buffered on the mature neuronal snRNA axis rather than producing a broad constitutive activity, stress, or compensation program.

main_caveats: The neighbor analysis is residual whole-transcriptome correlation, not shared FDR-gene overlap, because Adra1a had no FDR genes to overlap.
summary: A model-visible residual signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Adra1a transcriptional neighbor; the largest centered Pearson correlation was only 0.043 and involved a safe-target control.
why_it_matters: The lack of FDR genes is not concealing a coherent but subthreshold whole-genome trajectory; the genome-wide shape of Adra1a is indistinguishable from null-background variation.

literature_claim: Alpha1 receptors are Gq-coupled GPCRs embedded in a broader neuromodulatory receptor family.
main_caveats: The canonical alpha1 paralogs Adra1b and Adra1d and the Gq alpha subunits Gnaq and Gna11 were not represented as targets, so the closest same-subfamily test was unavailable.
summary: Represented adrenergic-family and Gq-linked GPCR perturbations did not form an Adra1a-like basal transcriptomic module; the few responding comparators had only one to three FDR<0.10 genes in matched groups, while Adra1a had none.
why_it_matters: The result rejects a simple expectation that all catecholamine or Gq-coupled receptor losses phenocopy each other in postmitotic neuronal snRNA-seq, and it records that the most direct alpha1 paralogs and Gq alpha subunits were not testable in this perturbation universe.

literature_claim: Long-term alpha1A activation and alpha1A positive allosteric modulation improve plasticity and cognition in mouse models.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq tested chronic LoF without norepinephrine stimulation, not acute receptor activation or disease-model rescue.
summary: Adra1a loss did not down-regulate a maintained activity/CREB immediate-early program in any recovered neuronal class, despite direct Creb1 and Camk2a perturbations producing detectable small signatures elsewhere in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: Alpha1A agonism and PAM studies invoke synaptic plasticity and p-CREB biology; the screen indicates that those therapeutic effects should not be expected to appear as a broad basal Fos/Arc/Egr/Npas4/Bdnf-like neuronal LoF signature at P37-P44.

direction: Ppp2r2b up in Pvalb; Zdhhc21 down in Sst
literature_claim: Alpha2A-AR is a CNS GPCR with presynaptic and postsynaptic neuromodulatory functions, not a known PV/SST-restricted terminal transcription factor.
main_caveats: Each responding cell group contributed only one significant gene, so no broad pathway can be inferred.
summary: Adra2a produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 23 assayed neuronal cell groups: Ppp2r2b up in 052 Pvalb Gaba and Zdhhc21 down in 053 Sst Gaba.
why_it_matters: The measured result is an interneuron-restricted, two-gene response rather than a pan-neuronal alpha2A adrenergic transcriptional program.

literature_claim: PPP2R2B encodes the PP2A B55β regulatory subunit, and PP2A regulatory B subunits influence substrate selectivity and catalytic activity.
main_caveats: Ppp2r2b perturbation itself yielded no FDR<0.10 downstream genes; the Adra2a evidence is one transcript in one cell class.
summary: Ppp2r2b was selectively up-regulated after Adra2a perturbation in Pvalb neurons, nominating a PP2A-B55 regulatory compensation.
why_it_matters: A phosphatase regulatory subunit is a plausible counterweight to altered cAMP/PKA tone, but the single-gene pattern keeps this as a focused hypothesis, not a demonstrated phosphatase cascade.

literature_claim: Alpha2A-AR can be palmitoylated, and ZDHHC21 can palmitoylate alpha1D adrenergic receptor in vascular cells.
main_caveats: Zdhhc21 was not a perturbation target in the parquet, and no direct ADRA2A-ZDHHC21 relationship was measured.
summary: Zdhhc21 was selectively down-regulated after Adra2a perturbation in Sst neurons, suggesting cell-type-specific adjustment of a palmitoyltransferase rather than a shared alpha2A program.
why_it_matters: Palmitoylation can tune receptor and membrane-signaling localization, making Zdhhc21 a biologically plausible adaptive marker, but the known adrenergic ZDHHC21 link is alpha1D in vascular tissue rather than alpha2A in SST interneurons.

literature_claim: Alpha2A-AR stimulation rapidly inhibits cAMP and modulates HCN, Ca2+, and K+ currents.
main_caveats: Only steady-state snRNA was measured; phosphorylation, cAMP microdomains, and membrane currents were not.
summary: Adra2a perturbation did not induce a detectable immediate-early, CREB/cAMP-feedback, G-protein, HCN, KCNJ, or KCNQ transcript program in any assayed group.
why_it_matters: The absence of these genes supports the interpretation that alpha2A loss primarily perturbs local second-messenger and ion-channel physiology rather than basal nuclear RNA abundance.

literature_claim: Alpha2A receptors signal through Gi/o, cAMP, and HCN/other ion-channel effectors, while alpha2A and alpha2C receptors both regulate noradrenergic transmitter release.
main_caveats: Adra2c, Gnai1, Gnai2, and Gnai3 were not perturbation targets; most represented comparators were themselves sparse responders.
summary: Adrenergic receptor, G-protein/cAMP, PDE, HCN/KCNQ/KCNJ/Ca2+-channel, GABAB, and Ppp2r2b perturbations were directly queried and did not converge with Adra2a.
why_it_matters: The null is pathway-wide in this assay: obvious receptor relatives and downstream effectors were also flat or unrelated, arguing against a missing same-pathway transcriptional module.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation is dominated by a very weak Adra2a signature and should be used as evidence of flatness, not pathway assignment.
summary: Data-driven Adra2a signature neighbors had near-zero correlations and did not share the Pvalb/Sst Adra2a marker genes.
why_it_matters: This places Adra2a in the flat-signature regime of the screen; the nearest neighbors are not mechanistic phenocopies.

literature_claim: Alpha2A-AR mediates alpha2 agonist sedation, analgesia, anesthetic sparing, and fast cAMP/ion-channel physiology in vivo and in PFC networks.
main_caveats: The screen did not measure acute receptor pharmacology, norepinephrine release, cAMP, ion currents, or behavior.
summary: The Adra2a basal snRNA null should not be read as evidence that alpha2A is an inert or poor CNS drug target.
why_it_matters: Alpha2A mutant mice show loss of clinically relevant alpha2 agonist responses, but this perturb-seq design lacked acute agonist stimulation and functional electrophysiology.

literature_claim: macroH2A1 is a histone variant that regulates hippocampal transcription and memory in mice.
main_caveats: The module is a single FDR10 gene in 71 perturbed nuclei; it should be treated as a focused biomarker hypothesis, not as a multi-gene chromatin program.
summary: Adra2b produced a one-gene, FDR<0.10 response in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, down-regulating the histone-variant gene Macroh2a1.
why_it_matters: The only recovered Adra2b transcriptional phenotype falls in an amygdala/CA1/dentate-enriched glutamatergic class and points to chromatin regulation rather than to a broad canonical GPCR immediate-early program.

literature_claim: alpha2B is a GPCR upstream of adenylate-cyclase-inhibiting adrenergic signaling and MAPK signaling.
main_caveats: The tested gene panel is a sentinel set, not a formal gene-set enrichment test; the conclusion rests on the complete lack of any other FDR10 gene in the Adra2b surface.
summary: Adra2b loss did not activate a detectable cAMP/MAPK or immediate-early transcript program even in the one responsive group.
why_it_matters: A Gi/o alpha2B receptor can signal to adenylate cyclase and MAPK, so a strong chronic cell-autonomous receptor perturbation could have left Fos/Jun/Egr/Arc/Npas4 mRNA; its absence confines the measured effect to Macroh2a1.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on Wilcoxon score vectors over the model-visible rows shared with Adra2b; it is useful for rejection here because the absolute correlations were near zero.
summary: Unbiased cross-target signature neighbors were extremely weak: Aff2 was the top positive real-gene neighbor and Grm7 the strongest negative real-gene neighbor, but neither shared the Macroh2a1 hit.
why_it_matters: Adra2b is not embedded in a recurrent whole-transcriptome perturbation class in this dataset; even the best data-driven neighbors appear to be numerical edge cases around a nearly flat signature.

literature_claim: alpha2A, alpha2B and alpha2C adrenoceptors have subtype-specific physiology; mouse brain presynaptic autoreceptor function is dominated by alpha2A/alpha2C rather than alpha2B.
main_caveats: Adra2c was absent from the perturbation universe, so the most relevant alpha2C comparison is a literature expectation rather than a measured contrast.
summary: The measured adrenergic receptors did not phenocopy Adra2b: Adra2a had a separate two-gene interneuron response, Adra1a/Adrb2/Adrb3 were FDR-flat, and Adra2c was not represented.
why_it_matters: This preserves alpha-adrenergic subtype specialization in the screen: the alpha2B surface is not interchangeable with the better-established central alpha2 autoreceptor subtype Adra2a.

literature_claim: A human ADRA2B deletion variant is associated with emotional memory and decreases GRK-mediated receptor phosphorylation/desensitization.
main_caveats: The screen did not assay emotional learning, norepinephrine challenge, or the del301-303 allele itself.
summary: The weak mouse Adra2b loss-of-function surface should not be read as a direct negative model of the human ADRA2B del301-303 emotional-memory allele.
why_it_matters: The human allele reduces receptor desensitization and is read out under emotional stress or memory paradigms, whereas this experiment made sparse postnatal loss-of-function indels and sampled resting neuronal nuclei; the expected allele- and state-dependent program was therefore not the perturbation delivered here.

literature_claim: β2AR is a catecholamine-activated GPCR whose canonical outputs require receptor stimulation and second-messenger signaling rather than constitutive transcription-factor occupancy.

main_caveats: Two taxonomy groups were not tested for Agps; most measured groups had modest perturbed-cell counts; DNA editing and lipid depletion were not measured.
summary: Agps produced FDR-supported downstream transcriptional signal only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Dhcr24, Lmtk3, and Cyp51 were up-regulated; the other 20 measured Agps groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This converts a mostly flat perturbation into a spatially restricted thalamic sterol/membrane response rather than a global neuronal Agps phenotype.

literature_claim: Plasmalogen synthesis is peroxisomal, AGPS lies in the pathway, plasmalogen homeostasis can regulate cholesterol biosynthesis, and SREBP2 activates cholesterol-pathway transcripts.
main_caveats: Only Dhcr24 and Cyp51 crossed FDR<0.10 in the Agps-alone signature; the primary plasmalogen lipid defect was not assayed.
summary: The Agps responder up-regulated two cholesterol-biosynthesis enzymes, Dhcr24 and Cyp51, consistent with a small sterol rebound after perturbing ether-lipid synthesis.
why_it_matters: It links an AGPS loss-of-function perturbation to a compensatory cholesterol-output module in postnatal neurons, a readout the assay could detect despite not measuring ether lipids directly.

literature_claim: MARCH6 controls SQLE/HMGCR and cholesterol-synthesis flux, while SREBP2 is a master activator of cholesterol genes.
main_caveats: Agps shared only Dhcr24 and Cyp51 at FDR<0.10; Marchf6 and Srebf2 produced much broader signatures.
summary: Marchf6 loss converged with Agps on Dhcr24 and Cyp51 induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Srebf2 loss drove the same sterol genes in the opposite direction.
why_it_matters: The sterol genes induced by Agps sit in a perturbation-defined cholesterol module rather than being isolated hits, and Srebf2 provides the expected transcription-factor inversion.

main_caveats: The neighbor score was restricted to three Agps FDR genes; the mechanistic connection between Agps and Mib1 is not established by this dataset.
summary: Mib1 was the top positive data-driven neighbor of the Agps three-gene 151 signature and itself induced a broad sterol program in the same cell group.
why_it_matters: This nominates a non-textbook comparator that would have been missed by restricting analysis to known ether-lipid enzymes.

literature_claim: AGPS and FAR1 operate in the early peroxisomal ether-lipid pathway, but FAR1 feedback is substantially post-translational and need not equal Agps transcriptional loss.
main_caveats: GNPAT and PEX7 were not represented as perturbation targets; Far1/Pex downstream signatures were sparse, making absence of phenocopy stronger than any alternate positive program.
summary: Far1, Pex1, Pex14, and Hmgcr did not reproduce the Agps Dhcr24/Cyp51/Lmtk3 signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Acute postmitotic Agps does not behave like a generic ether-lipid, peroxisome-biogenesis, or cholesterol-enzyme perturbation in this neuronal screen, sharpening the specificity of the sterol rebound.

direction: up after Agps only among these restricted comparisons
literature_claim: LMTK3 has neuronal functions in endocytic trafficking and mouse behavior.
main_caveats: This is a single FDR gene and did not recur as an FDR hit in Marchf6 or Srebf2 perturbations.
summary: Lmtk3 was the only non-sterol FDR-supported Agps downstream gene and was not part of the Srebf2/Marchf6 sterol core.
why_it_matters: Because LMTK3 is linked to neuronal endocytic trafficking, its induction could mark a membrane-traffic or excitability branch of Agps loss that is not captured by sterol enzymes alone.

why_it_matters: The AT1R partner Agtr1a, the AT2 receptor Agtr2, the pro-renin receptor/V-ATPase accessory gene Atp6ap2, and Rac1 all failed to reproduce the 054 Elmo1 response, making the Agtrap hit an isolated CNU-MGE GABA event rather than a generic AT1R transcriptional or ELMO1-Rac module.

main_caveats: Neighboring was computed on all-gene Wilcoxon scores for a near-null target, so the absolute cosines are small and should be used to reject strong convergence, not to assert mechanistic coupling.
summary: Agtrap had only weak all-gene score neighbors, and the closest 054 CNU-MGE GABA neighbors did not share a corrected Elmo1 signature.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation landscape rejects a hidden broad module: global Agtrap cosine similarity was near zero, and Htr2a, the nearest non-safe 054 neighbor with any corrected genes, regulated Kcnma1 and Cbx4 rather than Elmo1.

summary: A lymphocyte-defined GP78-UBAC2-LMBR1L Wnt-control mechanism did not manifest as a neuronal Wnt response after Amfr loss, even though direct Ctnnb1 and Lrp6 perturbations down-regulated the Wnt reporter Axin2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: This separates AMFR’s adaptor-dependent Wnt-client biology from the canonical Wnt transcriptional machinery in postnatal neurons: the Wnt axis was assay-detectable, but AMFR was not the limiting gate into it.

literature_claim: AMFR/gp78 can regulate mitofusin-dependent mitophagy and neurodegeneration-linked substrates in cell models, and human biallelic AMFR loss-of-function causes autosomal-recessive hereditary spastic paraplegia with altered lipid biology in a preclinical model.
main_caveats: The screen excluded spinal cord and glia, sampled only a short postnatal interval, and did not assay axon length, mitochondrial turnover, lipid pools, substrate protein abundance, or viability losses.
summary: The lack of an early neuronal UPR, sterol, or Wnt transcriptome after mosaic Amfr loss suggests that AMFR-associated hereditary spastic paraplegia is unlikely to be reproduced by a 3-4 week autonomous nuclear stress program in juvenile brain neurons alone.
why_it_matters: Biallelic AMFR loss causes a human corticospinal disease, but the screen points toward slow protein/lipid/axon-maintenance, developmental, spinal, or non-neuronal effects rather than an acute pan-neuronal ER-stress burst.

literature_claim: Germline or congenital human AMMECR1 variants cause a multisystem X-linked syndrome including craniofacial, erythroid, hearing, kidney, bone or heart phenotypes and sometimes neurodevelopmental delay.
main_caveats: This establishes transcriptional silence in survivor neuronal nuclei after a sparse postnatal CRISPR perturbation; it does not disprove AMMECR1 requirements during embryogenesis or in non-neuronal organs.
summary: Acute postnatal Ammecr1 loss of function was transcriptomically silent across all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The dominant result is not a missed pathway but a true FDR-level absence: 371796 downstream Wilcoxon tests produced no gene at FDR<0.10, sharply separating this P16-to-P37/44 neuronal assay from congenital AMMECR1 disease contexts.

literature_claim: AMMECR1L mRNA and protein were increased in an AMMECR1-inactivated patient context, and AMMECR1 and AMMECR1L can dimerize in the nucleus.
main_caveats: AMMECR1L protein abundance and AMMECR1L knockout phenocopy could not be tested because the readout is snRNA-seq and Ammecr1l was not represented as a perturbation target.
summary: Ammecr1 CRISPR did not induce the paralogous AMMECR1L compensatory transcript in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: AMMECR1L induction in human loss-of-function samples is a concrete, assay-detectable expectation; its complete FDR=1 absence argues that the compensation described in patient cells is context-specific rather than a universal immediate mRNA feedback loop.

literature_claim: AMMECR1 loss has been linked to cell-cycle control and, in A549 cells, knockdown suppresses proliferation, promotes cell-cycle arrest and increases apoptosis.
main_caveats: The screen profiled neuronal nuclei rather than actively cycling lung-cancer cells; apoptosis without captured survivor nuclei or without mRNA remodeling would require orthogonal survival assays.
summary: The proliferative cell-cycle and apoptosis programs expected from AMMECR1 knockdown in A549 cells were not recovered in postmitotic neurons.
why_it_matters: Markers spanning proliferation and apoptosis were explicitly measured and never reached FDR<0.10, so the null is not caused by an unreadable secondary stress axis; rather, the A549 phenotype appears tied to cycling cells.

main_caveats: Neighbor ranks are whole-surface Wilcoxon score correlations built from a null target; the tiny coefficients are useful mainly as evidence against a robust module, not as mechanistic similarity.
summary: Data-driven cross-perturbation search placed Ammecr1 in a near-zero, null-like neighborhood rather than in a coherent positive or negative module.
why_it_matters: The best whole-surface neighbors had Wilcoxon-score correlations of only r=0.031 down to r=-0.015 in the first ranks, confirming that Ammecr1 has no strong shared transcriptomic signature with any directly queryable perturbation in this universe.

literature_claim: FACL4/ACSL4 and AMMECR1 are neighboring Xq22.3 AMME-region genes; Acsl4 is the represented mouse ortholog of that disease-region comparator.
main_caveats: The prior is a disease-locus relationship, not a same-complex prediction, and the Acsl4 response itself is very small.
summary: Acsl4, the only represented AMME/Xq22 disease-region comparator, did not phenocopy Ammecr1.
why_it_matters: A literature-obvious locus neighbor was directly testable and rejected as a convergent neuronal comparator: Acsl4 correlated r=0.0036 with Ammecr1 and had only one downstream DEG in the shared cell groups despite significant Acsl4 self-transcript loss in four groups.

literature_claim: Ank/ANKH is a neuronal multipass transporter that also controls extracellular ATP, citrate, and PPi handling in other tissues.
main_caveats: Genomic indels were not directly measured, and the absence of downstream RNA changes does not rule out altered ATP, PPi, or citrate flux.
summary: Ank mRNA was measurably depleted without any FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in several broad neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates target-transcript behavior from pathway activation: even cell groups with clear Ank self-reduction did not mount a detectable transcriptional compensation, stress, or identity response after P16 mosaic CRISPR loss.

literature_claim: Loss of ANKH/Ank perturbs extracellular ATP/citrate/PPi metabolism and tissue mineralization, while seizure injury can increase neuronal Ank immunoreactivity.
main_caveats: The test covers RNA markers in neuronal nuclei only; it does not measure metabolites, extracellular crystals, chronic seizure physiology, or calcifying mesenchymal cells.
summary: The canonical extracellular pyrophosphate/mineralization axis and generic neuronal stress markers were not induced or repressed after Ank perturbation.
why_it_matters: If Ank loss had forced young neurons toward an osteogenic/mineralization-like state or a strong ISR/UPR/immediate-early response, the snRNA-seq readout should have detected markers such as Alpl, Enpp1, Slc20a2, Xpr1, Spp1, Runx2, Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Xbp1, Fos, or Jun; instead all targeted markers remained FDR=1.0 in every measured group.

literature_claim: SLC20A2 and XPR1 are cellular phosphate transporters linked to PFBC, and PDGFRB is an autosomal-dominant PFBC gene whose disease biology implicates vascular calcification/glial responses.
main_caveats: Slc20a2, Xpr1, and Pdgfrb did not show significant self-transcript depletion in these neuronal groups, so this is a context-matching contrast rather than a definitive genetic epistasis test.
summary: Three represented brain-calcification/phosphate-homeostasis comparators, Slc20a2, Xpr1, and Pdgfrb, also failed to converge with Ank in the same neuronal Perturb-seq assay.
why_it_matters: The shared flatness of Ank with SLC20A2/XPR1 phosphate transporters and the PFBC pericyte-receptor gene Pdgfrb argues that acute sparse perturbation of postmitotic NeuN+ neurons is poorly matched to vascular or extracellular calcification phenotypes.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation used all matched score features and is uninformative for extracellular metabolite phenotypes; the top negative neighbor was tested in only 9 Ank-matched groups.
summary: Ank had no meaningful transcriptome-wide positive or negative signature neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The nearest Wilcoxon-score neighbors were essentially uncorrelated, so the parquet does not nominate a hidden responder pathway that phenocopies Ank loss; cross-target interpretation should therefore concentrate on why the Ank axis is off this readout rather than on a strong co-signature.

literature_claim: The strongest neuronal AnkR priors emphasize Pv+ interneuron and Purkinje membrane localization phenotypes, not a P MY Pineal Glut B4galnt1 RNA response.
main_caveats: 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 37 perturbed nuclei and the response is supported by one downstream gene.
summary: Ank1 produced only one downstream FDR<0.10 event across 22 recovered neuronal groups: B4galnt1 down in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: The observed Ank1 LoF response is a single low-cell-count posterior glutamatergic island rather than a broad ankyrin/spectrin transcriptional response.

literature_claim: B4GALNT1 is a ganglioside-biosynthesis enzyme, and B4galnt1-null or complex-ganglioside-deficient mice implicate complex gangliosides in axon-myelin integrity.
main_caveats: Only B4galnt1, not a broader ganglioside pathway, crossed FDR<0.10; B4galnt1 was not itself represented as a perturbation target.
summary: B4galnt1 down-regulation nominates ganglioside biosynthesis as a candidate Ank1-sensitive marker in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: B4galnt1 encodes GM2/GD2 synthase, and complex gangliosides participate in axon-myelin stability, making the singleton biologically evocative despite the lack of a multi-gene lipid program.

literature_claim: AnkR loss impairs Pv+ interneuron PNN/Kv3.1b organization and Purkinje Kv3.3/beta-III-spectrin function.
main_caveats: Transcript absence does not measure Kv3 protein localization, WFA-positive perineuronal nets, or membrane excitability.
summary: Canonical AnkR partners in Pvalb and cerebellar neurons were uncoupled from the Ank1 nuclear RNA response.
why_it_matters: The assay did not recover PNN or Kv3-channel transcript changes in the cell classes closest to the AnkR literature, so a true protein-localization phenotype could be missed by snRNA-seq DE.

literature_claim: Ankyrins, spectrins, and Kv3 channels form specialized membrane-localization systems rather than a single interchangeable transcriptional complex.
main_caveats: Ank3, Sptbn2, and Sptbn4 were not perturbation targets, so the exact AnkG and Purkinje beta-III/beta-IV spectrin contrasts could not be measured.
summary: Measured Ank1 relatives and AnkR/Kv3 neighbors did not converge with Ank1 or with one another as a shared RNA module.
why_it_matters: The negative cross-perturbation result preserves the distinction between a membrane scaffold pathway and an acute nuclear program: Ank2, Sptb, Kcnc1, and Kcnc3 were flat across all measured groups, while Sptan1 and Kcnc2 had only isolated non-overlapping singleton effects.

main_caveats: Signatures were ranked over many nonsignificant Wilcoxon scores; r values are tiny and should be used as a null-like diagnostic rather than mechanistic similarity.
summary: Ank1's empirical whole-surface neighbors were null-like and had near-zero score correlations.
why_it_matters: The unbiased cross-perturbation analysis did not reveal a hidden convergent module; it mostly placed Ank1 next to safe or near-null perturbations.

literature_claim: AD studies identified cortical ANK1 epigenetic changes and ANK1 up-regulation in laser-captured AD microglia, with no matching increase in neurons or astrocytes from the same subjects.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay lacked microglia and an aged neurodegenerative inflammatory state.
summary: The juvenile neuronal Ank1 LoF null is orthogonal to the Alzheimer's ANK1 signal in aged human microglia.
why_it_matters: A lack of broad neuron-intrinsic transcriptional response should not be read as evidence against disease-associated ANK1 regulation in microglia or aged human cortex.

literature_claim: Prior Ank2 loss or AnkB440-deficiency models disrupt embryonic cortical development, axon branching and guidance, synaptic proteome composition, and excitability/AIS phenotypes.
main_caveats: Functional indels and AnkB protein loss were not assayed; the result is a high-confidence transcriptional null, not a high-confidence organismal or electrophysiologic null.
summary: Ank2 produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: This is a strong negative result for a sustained, cell-autonomous nuclear RNA program after sparse P16 Ank2 loss, and it bounds downstream interpretation to off-axis AnkB biology rather than undiscovered FDR-level genes.
