009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ATP6V0A1 neurological disease includes dominant missense and biallelic variant mechanisms that perturb endolysosomal acidification and early neural development.
main_caveats: A silent snRNA surface cannot separate insufficient biallelic editing from edited-cell loss or purely post-translational vesicle-pH phenotypes.
summary: The ATP6V0A1 disease prior is refined toward developmental, missense, and direct physiology mechanisms rather than a generic postmitotic loss-of-function transcriptional state.
why_it_matters: Human de novo missense variants and homozygous/hypomorphic mouse models cause acidification, survival, mTORC1, autophagy, and synaptic phenotypes, whereas a P16 mosaic CRISPR perturbation leaves the juvenile-young-adult nuclear transcriptome flat. That disconnect warns against using this screen to rank ATP6V0A1 therapies by nuclear DE rescue alone.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: V-ATPase acidifies lysosomes, endosomes, Golgi compartments, and synaptic vesicles, and pathogenic ATP6V1A variants perturb lysosomal homeostasis in severe neurodevelopmental disease.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; the four downstream hits are singletons and the assay does not capture pH, flux, electrophysiology, or lost edited cells.
summary: Acute juvenile Atp6v1a perturbation produced only four downstream FDR<0.10 gene-by-cell hits across 20 recovered neuronal groups, with several groups showing target RNA reduction but no downstream response.
why_it_matters: A core lysosomal V-ATPase A-subunit loss was expected to create a broad stress/autophagy transcriptome; the measured surface instead shows that most recovered postmitotic neurons transcriptionally buffer this perturbation over the 3-4 week assay window.

literature_claim: Severe organelle/proteostasis stress can activate an integrated stress response involving ATF4-dependent induction of DDIT3/CHOP.
main_caveats: Single FDR gene at FDR 0.08821 in 33 perturbed cells; other ISR/UPR genes were only nominal or absent.
summary: Ddit3 was the only canonical ISR/UPR sentinel recovered at FDR<0.10 and was confined to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: Ddit3/CHOP up-regulation is a plausible nuclear reporter of organelle or proteostasis stress; its isolation argues for a focal alarm state rather than global terminal UPR after Atp6v1a perturbation.

literature_claim: The ubiquitin-proteasome system and autophagy-lysosome system form interconnected proteostasis routes; PSMB4 and PSMC1 are core 20S and 19S proteasome components.
main_caveats: Global cosines were small because the Atp6v1a phenotype is sparse; convergence is dominated by subthreshold genome-wide direction plus a few exact FDR overlaps.
summary: The Atp6v1a score vector was closest to proteostasis perturbations, with Psmb4 and Psmc1 ranking first and second among 1765 other targets and sharing same-direction Ddit3 or Golga4 hits.
why_it_matters: This positions the weak Atp6v1a response near a ubiquitin-proteasome stress axis and suggests that only a small slice of the lysosome/proteasome compensation network became transcriptional in this assay.

literature_claim: V1, V0, accessory, and Rabconnectin/RAVE nodes participate in V-ATPase acidification biology, and V-ATPase subunit mutations are linked to neurodevelopmental lysosomal disease.
main_caveats: Only the V-ATPase relatives represented in the parquet could be tested; some comparators were not recovered in all Atp6v1a-matched groups.
summary: V-ATPase subunits and regulators did not recapitulate the four Atp6v1a downstream genes in matched cell groups.
why_it_matters: Same-pump membership was not sufficient to predict a matched Perturb-seq state: Atp6v1e1 and Atp6v1b2 were weak positive neighbours, but Atp6v0a1, Atp6ap2, Dmxl2, and Atp13a2 were flatter or divergent and no V-ATPase relative shared an exact Atp6v1a FDR gene.

literature_claim: Golgins act as selective tethering factors for Golgi transport vesicles.
main_caveats: Single-gene response only; no other Golgi markers passed FDR<0.10 in this Atp6v1a group.
summary: Golga4 was specifically up-regulated after Atp6v1a perturbation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The hit nominates Golgi/secretory tethering as a possible compensatory node in one cortical IT population, consistent with V-ATPase action throughout endomembrane compartments but not yet supported by a multi-gene Golgi program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: LTA4H catalyzes leukotriene B4 biosynthesis and also has aminopeptidase activity.
main_caveats: Single-gene hit; non-neuronal inflammatory lineages were not assayed in this NeuN-enriched dataset.
summary: Lta4h was the strongest Atp6v1a downstream hit, up 1.174 logFC at FDR 0.000869 in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
why_it_matters: A leukotriene-metabolism enzyme in a NeuN-enriched neuronal population is an unexpected cell-autonomous candidate output of Atp6v1a perturbation, but the lack of additional eicosanoid genes makes it a biomarker hypothesis rather than an inflammatory program.

literature_claim: CHD2 is a chromatin remodeler whose pathogenic variants, like ATP6V1A variants, are associated with developmental epileptic encephalopathy.
main_caveats: Single FDR gene in 39 perturbed cells; the data do not show CHD2 protein activity or a broader chromatin-remodeling module.
summary: Chd2 was up-regulated in 191 MB P MY GABA after Atp6v1a perturbation.
why_it_matters: The isolated induction links ATP6V1A and another developmental-epileptic-encephalopathy gene at the transcriptional level in one inhibitory midbrain/hindbrain-related group, suggesting a low-confidence chromatin compensation candidate.

literature_claim: V-ATPases acidify lysosomes, endosomes and other organelles and thereby support membrane traffic, protein degradation and autophagy.
main_caveats: The screen does not measure organelle pH, V-ATPase protein, autophagic flux, or DNA indels; a non-transcriptional acidification phenotype could exist below the snRNA threshold.
summary: Atp6v1e1 loss produced a strongly buffered transcriptional surface: only 10 downstream FDR<0.10 genes appeared across 20 measured neuronal groups, and none belonged to a coordinated TFEB, autophagy, lysosomal cathepsin, UPR, or ISR module.
why_it_matters: V-ATPase is a core acidification machine, so a broad degradative-organelle stress response was the obvious prediction. Its absence says this P16, sparse neuronal CRISPR experiment did not phenocopy pan-V-ATPase chemical collapse at the RNA level.

literature_claim: Brain V-ATPase energizes synaptic vesicle membranes for neurotransmitter loading, making postmitotic neurons plausible sites for V-ATPase phenotypes.
main_caveats: Only eight genes passed FDR<0.10 and none passed FDR<0.05; the genes suggest signaling-state remodeling but do not directly measure synaptic-vesicle acidification.
summary: The only multi-gene Atp6v1e1 response was in 308 CB GABA, where Cacnb4, Tnik, Jmjd1c, Stmn4, Strip2 and Akain1 were up-regulated while Gpr162 and Pde4a were down-regulated.
why_it_matters: The cerebellar GABAergic signature points to a selective neuronal signaling and cytoskeletal state rather than a generic lysosome-biogenesis response.

literature_claim: No literature comparator was used for these idiosyncratic singleton DE genes.
main_caveats: Each call rests on one FDR<0.10 gene and very small perturbed-cell counts of 27 to 28 nuclei.
summary: The non-cerebellar significant Atp6v1e1 signal was limited to one down-regulated gene in each responding CNU-HYa group: Chp1 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and Snrpn in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: These singleton responses keep the hypothalamic CNU-HYa signal visible while separating it from the cerebellar module; they should not be inflated into a shared V-ATPase stress program.

literature_claim: No prior Ranbp2-Wdr26-V-ATPase relationship was assumed; this was nominated from the perturbation matrix.
main_caveats: Eef2, Zeb2 and Sp7 were rejected as FDR-overlap comparators despite high vector ranks; B9d1 shared only Strip2, so Ranbp2 and Wdr26 carry most of the comparison.
summary: The best data-driven convergence was not the V-ATPase family: Ranbp2 was the top positive neighbor and Wdr26 the top negative neighbor across the three Atp6v1e1 responder groups, with the statistically supported same and opposite overlaps concentrated in 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: This places the cerebellar Atp6v1e1 signature in a broader 308 CB GABA cell-state axis marked by Gpr162, Pde4a, Strip2 and Cacnb4, and separates that axis from textbook acidification-complex membership.

literature_claim: ATP6V1E1, ATP6V1A, ATP6V1B2, ATP6V0A1 and ATP6AP2 encode subunits or accessory proteins of the V-ATPase, and human or mouse studies link several V-ATPase subunits to developmental, epileptic or multisystem disease.
main_caveats: Only V-ATPase relatives present as targets in the parquet could be tested; Atp6v1b2 was not recovered in all Atp6v1e1 responder groups.
summary: Literature-obvious V-ATPase comparators did not phenocopy Atp6v1e1: Atp6v0a1 was completely flat downstream, Atp6v1a and Atp6ap2 produced only sparse singleton responses, and Atp6v1b2 produced a Pvalb-restricted signature absent from Atp6v1e1.
why_it_matters: Membership in the same proton pump was not enough to predict the P16 neuronal snRNA response; subunit identity and cell context dominated the measured transcriptome.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Because V-ATPase is ubiquitous, broad V-ATPase-directed therapies are challenging and require selectivity to avoid toxicity.
main_caveats: This is an inference from pooled CRISPR LoF, not a pharmacologic inhibitor experiment.
summary: Atp6v1e1 LoF in postmitotic neurons is a poor transcriptional proxy for pan-V-ATPase inhibition: neither Atp6v1e1 nor the tested V-ATPase relatives produced a common lysosomal-collapse signature.
why_it_matters: The result cautions against treating a flat E1 snRNA signature as evidence that neuronal V-ATPase inhibition is harmless, and against assuming that inhibiting one subunit will report the biology of every other subunit.

literature_claim: ATP8A2 loss is linked to cerebellar and axonal disease biology, whereas CNOT7 and DDX10 function in RNA turnover/ribosome biogenesis rather than in the P4-flippase core.
main_caveats: Only two genes crossed FDR<0.10 and both were modest, so the RNA-metabolism interpretation is a marker-pair hypothesis rather than a full pathway claim.
summary: Atp8a2 produced its only robust downstream DE in 308 CB GABA, where Cnot7 and Ddx10 were both up-regulated at FDR 0.0724.
why_it_matters: The response is anatomically aligned with cerebellar ATP8A2 disease biology but mechanistically narrow: two RNA-metabolism genes, not a broad lipid-flippase, axon-injury, apoptotic, ISR, UPR, or proteostasis program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ATP8A2 is a membrane PS/PE flippase whose chronic loss produces axonopathy and sensory-neuron degeneration in mice.
main_caveats: DNA indels and membrane lipid asymmetry were not measured; absence of mRNA stress does not mean absence of a biochemical PS-flipping phenotype.
summary: Canonical Atp8a2 stress, axon-injury, apoptosis, and P4-family compensation were absent from all 23 acute postnatal neuronal transcriptomes.
why_it_matters: The negative program test converts the broad null from a generic caveat into a mechanistic refinement: PS/PE flippase loss can be severe in animals but remain largely off the nuclear mRNA axis after P16 sparse perturbation.

literature_claim: P4-ATPases include ATP8A2, ATP9A, and ATP11C, but they differ in CDC50 dependence, substrate specificity, and tissue requirements.
main_caveats: The closest ATP8A paralog Atp8a1 and the ATP8A2 partner Tmem30a were absent as perturbation targets, so the strongest same-complex/paralog contrasts could not be performed.
summary: The P4-family targets represented in the parquet, Atp9a and Atp11c, did not converge with the Atp8a2 CB-GABA signature.
why_it_matters: Atp9a shows that a P4-family target can have strong self-mRNA knockdown in this assay yet still lack a broad downstream transcriptome; this makes Atp8a2's flat surface biologically interpretable rather than simply an on-target-expression failure.

main_caveats: Full-score cosine over a mostly flat Atp8a2 profile is inherently conservative; the calculation is useful mainly for showing that no robust neighbor exists.
summary: Atp8a2 had no meaningful whole-transcriptome signature neighbors in the model-visible perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The near-zero top positive and negative cosine values, including Safe_target labels, reject a strong Atp8a2 co-response module and constrain interpretation of the CB-GABA signal to a restricted two-gene effect.

literature_claim: ATP9A loss impairs endosomal recycling, Rab5/Rab11 regulation, neurite morphology and excitatory synaptic transmission.
main_caveats: The two downstream calls are single genes near a permissive FDR<0.10 threshold; DNA indels and protein loss were not measured.
summary: Atp9a loss was broadly buffered at the nuclear-transcriptome level, with only Rnf41 up in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Sc5d down in 053 Sst Gaba reaching downstream FDR<0.10 across 22 recovered cell groups.
why_it_matters: The perturbation engaged the Atp9a transcript in most recovered groups but produced only two downstream hits, separating Atp9a's known trafficking and synaptic biology from a broad cell-autonomous stress or identity program in this P16-to-P37/44 in vivo assay.

literature_claim: RNF41 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that participates in USP8-linked cytokine receptor sorting and processing.
main_caveats: Rnf41 is the only significant downstream gene in this cell group; no RNF41 protein activity or receptor-trafficking phenotype was measured.
summary: The CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic response was limited to up-regulation of the ubiquitin-ligase gene Rnf41.
why_it_matters: RNF41 participates in ubiquitin-dependent control of membrane-receptor trafficking, so its isolated induction is a plausible compensatory endosomal-quality-control marker rather than a generic neuronal stress program.

literature_claim: SC5D encodes sterol C5-desaturase/lathosterol oxidase in cholesterol biosynthesis.
main_caveats: This is a one-gene, transcript-only lipid-metabolism signal; no cholesterol or lathosterol measurements are available.
summary: Sst interneurons showed a single lipid-metabolic response, down-regulating Sc5d after Atp9a perturbation.
why_it_matters: SC5D lies in sterol/cholesterol biosynthesis, making it a candidate marker of membrane-lipid compensation in a GABAergic class even though the screen did not resolve lipid species or organelle membranes directly.

literature_claim: ATP9A localizes to early/recycling endosomes, supports transferrin and GLUT1 recycling, works with SNX3-retromer in Wntless sorting, can complex with ATP9B, and modulates Rab5/Rab11 activation.
main_caveats: RAB5/RAB11 activity and cargo localization are protein/cell-biological states, so the mRNA-negative result cannot exclude a trafficking defect.
summary: Atp9a depletion did not transcriptionally regulate recovered Atp9b, Rab5/Rab11, transferrin/GLUT1 cargo, Wntless, USP8, or retromer-core transcripts.
why_it_matters: The expected ATP9A mechanism is endosomal recycling and small-GTPase activation; the absence of a cognate mRNA module argues that this acute neuronal perturbation did not create a secondary nuclear stress or retromer-compensation program detectable by snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: ATP9A is part of endosomal SNX3-retromer biology and an ATP9A/ATP9B paralog pair, whereas ATP8A2 is a neuronal P4-ATPase family member with known neurologic phenotypes.
main_caveats: Atp9b, Mon2, Dopey2 and Snx3 were not represented as perturbation targets, so only Vps35 and Atp8a2 could be tested as target-level comparators.
summary: The literature-obvious Vps35 retromer and Atp8a2 P4-ATPase comparators did not phenocopy Atp9a in either Atp9a responder group.
why_it_matters: This keeps pathway membership from being over-interpreted: within the same dataset, the recoverable Vps35 and Atp8a2 DE surfaces were cell-type-shifted away from Atp9a and did not reproduce the Rnf41 or Sc5d calls.

main_caveats: The neighbor search compares all Wilcoxon score entries, so it is dominated by null dimensions when Atp9a itself has only two downstream FDR hits.
summary: Unbiased whole-score neighbors of Atp9a were extremely weak, with top cosine values between -0.026 and 0.034 after excluding Safe_target controls.
why_it_matters: The nearest transcriptomic neighbors are best read as a low-amplitude/noise-like neighborhood rather than as a convergent pathway, so cross-perturbation analysis independently supports the conclusion that Atp9a lacks a broad mRNA phenotype in this dataset.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Atr is essential in proliferating embryonic and cerebellar progenitors but can be deleted in postmitotic neurons without overt DDR activation or loss of brain architecture.
main_caveats: DNA indels and ATR protein loss were not measured; 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut were missing for this target; the assay reads basal snRNA rather than electrophysiology or neuron abundance.
summary: Sparse postnatal Atr loss was transcriptionally buffered across every measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: The strongest dataset-level result is the absence of any FDR<0.10 downstream DEG in 21 tested neuronal classes, despite direct Atr testing in each class; this argues that acute Atr loss in NeuN+ postmitotic neurons does not create a sustained basal nuclear stress transcriptome.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Atr deletion or inhibition in proliferating cells, including cerebellar granule neuron progenitors, causes replication-associated DNA damage, p53 activation, apoptosis, and a p53-dependent RNA response.
main_caveats: The panel is representative rather than an exhaustive damagesome gene set; absence is at the single-nucleus mRNA level only.
summary: Atr perturbation did not induce the p53, apoptosis, UPR/ISR, or autophagy transcripts predicted for a replicating-cell ATR catastrophe.
why_it_matters: Loss of ATR during S phase should collapse forks into DNA damage and p53-dominated injury programs; their absence shows that the P16 NeuN+ screen sampled a post-replicative state rather than the progenitor state in which ATR biology is normally transcriptionally obvious.

literature_claim: ATR-Seckel biology implicates the nervous system, and postmitotic neuronal Atr deletion alters intrinsic firing and presynaptic SYT2/PROT biology without activating DDR markers.
main_caveats: The published synaptic phenotype used targeted conditional models and protein/electrophysiology readouts; this screen did not assay presynaptic protein localization or firing.
summary: The neuronal null is compatible with an ATR role that is postmitotic but presynaptic and largely non-transcriptional.
why_it_matters: A flat transcriptome should not be read as neuronal irrelevance: conditional postmitotic Atr deletion has been reported to perturb firing and presynaptic vesicle regulation without DDR activation, which basal snRNA-seq of sparse young neurons is poorly positioned to detect.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ATR and DNA-PKcs are related PIKK-family DDR kinases with partially overlapping substrates, whereas mTOR is a structurally related PIKK outside the canonical DDR kinase triad.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed on Wilcoxon z-score vectors; Atr had no high-amplitude DEGs, so correlation magnitudes are expected to be near zero.
summary: Neither unbiased signature search nor DDR/PIKK-family comparators produced an Atr-like module.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative transcriptomic neighbors of Atr were essentially uncorrelated, and pathway-adjacent targets represented in the parquet, including Prkdc, Mtor, Wrn, Trp53, Ddb2, and Setx, also failed to converge; this makes the null a pathway-wide postmitotic buffering result rather than a missed single canonical neighbor.

literature_claim: CNNM2 loss is linked to hypomagnesemia, seizures, intellectual disability, and impaired brain development, but a CNNM2-Atrn relationship has not been established.
main_caveats: Singleton DEG from only 29 perturbed cerebellar GABA nuclei; the Atrn self transcript in the same group trended down but was not FDR-significant.
summary: Atrn perturbation produced a single robust downstream event: Cnnm2 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: This makes CNNM2 a candidate ion-homeostasis readout of acute neuronal Atrn loss in cerebellar GABA neurons, rather than a generic whole-brain Atrn stress program.

literature_claim: Germline Atrn loss causes CNS myelination defects and spongiform/vacuolar neuropathology.
main_caveats: Self-transcript knockdown is not DNA indel engagement; the result only shows that substantial Atrn mRNA shifts did not force an acute neuronal snRNA-seq program in these survivor nuclei.
summary: Atrn self-transcript depletion could be detected without downstream propagation.
why_it_matters: 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut had FDR-significant Atrn mRNA decreases yet no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, arguing that the flat surface is not simply the absence of any measurable Atrn transcript perturbation.

literature_claim: Mahoganoid/MGRN1 phenocopies Atrn genetically and MGRN1 regulates TSG101-dependent endosomal and autophagosome-lysosome trafficking.
main_caveats: Mgrn1 and Tsg101 themselves were not perturbation targets, so the contrast uses pathway-neighbor Rab7 and V-ATPase-related targets rather than the exact Atrn partner pathway.
summary: The acute Atrn surface did not recover an MGRN1/TSG101-like endolysosomal or autophagy stress signature.
why_it_matters: If Atrn loss in the assayed neurons immediately triggered the protein-turnover and endosome-to-lysosome biology associated with mahoganoid/MGRN1, the whole-transcriptome screen could have detected secondary stress or lysosomal genes; instead Atrn had only Cnnm2, while represented Rab7, Atp6ap2/Atp6v0a1, and Atp6v1e1 perturbations produced different or absent surfaces.

literature_claim: Atrn is a transmembrane accessory protein for agouti/Agrp melanocortin signaling and Atrn mRNA is present in rat hypothalamic nuclei.
main_caveats: MC4R, the most relevant central melanocortin receptor, was not a measured perturbation target, and broad HY cell groups need not contain enough Agrp/POMC/MC4R neurons.
summary: The Atrn screen did not expose a melanocortin/Agrp transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: Atrn is a melanocortin accessory factor in pigmentation and energy-balance genetics, but the available Agrp/Mc1r/Mc2r perturbations were also flat and the critical Mc4r/Asip comparators were not represented, so this snRNA-seq assay gives no evidence that the broad hypothalamic neuronal groups captured an Atrn-dependent melanocortin circuit.

main_caveats: Because Atrn itself had one downstream FDR gene, the correlation ranking is a weak-signature diagnostic, not mechanistic proof about the top-neighbor genes.
summary: Atrn had no strong empirical signature neighbor in the model-visible universe.
why_it_matters: The closest positive and negative whole-surface neighbors all had |r|<0.05, so the Atrn result should be read as a singleton/near-null surface rather than as convergence with a hidden pathway module.

literature_claim: CNNM2 affects magnesium handling and neurodevelopmental seizure phenotypes.
main_caveats: Cnnm2 target engagement by DNA indel sequencing was not measured; the lack of a Cnnm2 signature should not be over-read as an effective Cnnm2 knockout null.
summary: Cnnm2 up-regulation after Atrn did not behave like a reciprocal Cnnm2-loss module in cerebellar GABA cells.
why_it_matters: Direct Cnnm2 perturbation had 85 cerebellar GABA nuclei but no FDR<0.10 downstream genes, supporting the interpretation that Cnnm2 is a marker of the Atrn response rather than a phenocopying driver in this readout.

literature_claim: Embryonic and postnatal forebrain Atrx models make a broad forebrain neuronal response plausible.
main_caveats: Many null groups had fewer perturbed cells than 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
summary: Atrx generated FDR<0.10 downstream genes in only 3 of 18 measured cell groups, led by a 9-gene 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature.
why_it_matters: The P16 postmitotic Atrx response is sharply more restricted than expected from broad embryonic forebrain ATRX requirements.

literature_claim: No prior Atrx literature found in scope predicts Csf2ra down-regulation in these groups.
main_caveats: This is a marker hypothesis in two cell groups, not evidence that CSF2RA signaling is a direct ATRX target.
summary: Csf2ra was the only recurrent robust downstream gene, down in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This single transcript is a compact marker of the sparse midbrain/thalamic Atrx response.

literature_claim: Canonical ATRX literature emphasizes heterochromatin, replication stress and transcriptional control rather than a named lipid-homeostasis output.
main_caveats: Three-gene module in one cell group; directness is unknown.
summary: The main 151 TH response included down-regulation of membrane-lipid and surface-processing genes Cyp46a1, Pnpla6 and Pigk.
why_it_matters: The response extends beyond canonical chromatin maintenance into neuronal cholesterol, phospholipid and GPI-anchor transcripts.

literature_claim: Postnatal Atrx deletion can alter hippocampal synaptic structure, while BEGAIN and ABLIM1 are synaptic or actin-linked proteins.
main_caveats: The cortical component is a one-gene signal.
summary: Atrx up-regulated a small structural arm: Begain, Ablim1 and Pxdn in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Limd2 alone in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The up direction argues against loss of neuronal identity and suggests a restricted postsynaptic/cytoskeletal or extracellular-matrix compensation.

literature_claim: CHD4/NuRD and ATRX-DAXX are distinct neurodevelopmental chromatin-remodeling systems.
main_caveats: Neighbor ranking used only the 11 significant Atrx coordinates.
summary: Chd4 was the #1 positive data-driven neighbor of Atrx and shared Begain up-regulation and Cyp46a1 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: A NuRD ATPase, rather than H3f3a, was the closest measured positive comparator for the sparse Atrx signature.

literature_claim: Sin3-HDAC complexes are context-dependent chromatin regulators.
main_caveats: Opposition was measured on a restricted Atrx signature in one cell group.
summary: Sin3a was the #1 negative Atrx neighbor and significantly reversed Begain, Cyp46a1, Pnpla6 and Resp18 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The Atrx state is not a generic chromatin-repressor loss state; Sin3-HDAC loss drives an opposite local program.

literature_claim: ATRX cooperates with DAXX/H3.3 at heterochromatin and can physically interact with MeCP2.
main_caveats: Daxx itself was not represented as a target.
summary: Literature-obvious H3.3/heterochromatin and MeCP2 comparators did not phenocopy Atrx: H3f3a was flat, while Setdb1 and Mecp2 shared 0 Atrx FDR genes.
why_it_matters: The P16 neuronal Atrx state cannot be reduced to simple H3.3 depletion, H3K9-neighbor loss, or MeCP2 loss.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Earlier severe Atrx loss can cause p53-mediated neuronal apoptosis and DNA-damage sensitivity.
main_caveats: Cells dying before capture would not appear as nuclei.
summary: Atrx did not induce a p53/DNA-damage apoptotic program in any measured cell group.
why_it_matters: The many zero-DE groups are not concealing a canonical apoptotic cascade that gene-level snRNA-seq should have detected.

literature_claim: Germline Atxn1 loss and developmental ATXN1-CIC disruption cause behavioral and forebrain phenotypes, but those studies do not predict a selective 151-TH transcriptomic state after postnatal single-gene CRISPR.
main_caveats: The 005 and 007 cortical signals are tiny; the dominant 151-TH effect is a 212-cell mosaic CRISPR signature with unmeasured DNA indels.
summary: Acute Atxn1 loss-of-function produced a dominant thalamic response: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained 256 FDR<0.10 downstream genes, whereas only 2 and 4 genes were detected in the two cortical IT responders and 20 measured groups had no FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The result localizes wild-type Atxn1 dependence to a specific juvenile thalamic glutamatergic state rather than to all Atxn1-expressing or SCA1-relevant neurons.

literature_claim: ATXN1 binds CIC, and ATXN1/ATXN1L-CIC complexes repress transcriptional targets while ATXN1-family dosage can regulate CIC stability.
main_caveats: The whole-profile cosine is diluted by many jointly flat cell groups; convergence is strongest when the comparison is restricted to the responding 151-TH signature.
summary: Cic was the strongest positive full-profile neighbor of Atxn1 and sharply converged in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: 177 of 256 Atxn1 FDR genes were also significant under Cic with the same direction.
why_it_matters: The unbiased neighbor search rediscovers the biochemical ATXN1-CIC repressor complex in one neuronal subtype, arguing that the thalamic Atxn1 state is a CIC-linked loss-of-repression program rather than an unrelated off-target stress response.

literature_claim: CIC target derepression often includes ETV1, ETV4, ETV5, DUSP4, DUSP6, SPRY4 and CCND1, and Atxn1 loss can derepress Bace1 through CIC-ETV4/5-related regulation.
main_caveats: Etv4 was positive in logFC but not statistically supported; absence of the ETV genes could reflect low baseline expression in this thalamic state.
summary: The recovered CIC-like module was selective rather than a blanket canonical Etv program: Bace1 and Dusp4 were induced in 151 TH, but Etv4, Etv5, Dusp6 and Ccnd1 were measured and were not FDR-significant.
why_it_matters: It refines the ATXN1-CIC model by showing that postmitotic thalamic neurons can converge with Cic loss without derepressing the classic ETV1/4/5-centered cassette prominent in cancer, immune and developmental systems.

literature_claim: Loss of Ataxin-1 can potentiate Alzheimer's pathogenesis by elevating cerebral BACE1 transcription.
main_caveats: Single-gene marker at FDR 0.039; BACE1 protein and amyloid processing were not assayed.
summary: Bace1 was a significant Atxn1-loss marker only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, not in the other 20 FDR-null groups.
why_it_matters: Because BACE1 up-regulation is a reported deleterious effect of Atxn1 loss, the thalamic Bace1 hit flags a cell-type-restricted liability for non-allele-selective ATXN1 lowering while also showing that the liability was not ubiquitous in this juvenile neuronal assay.

literature_claim: ATXN1-CIC disruption can alter neuronal maturation and maintenance in brain circuits, but a neuropeptide/BDNF-biased adult thalamic signature was not an established Atxn1 loss-of-function readout.
main_caveats: The DE list does not directly distinguish homeostatic compensation from a fate-state shift within the 151-TH cluster.
summary: The 151-TH Atxn1/Cic-like state paired down-regulation of postsynaptic and excitability genes with induction of Bdnf and regulated-secretory/neuropeptide genes.
why_it_matters: This suggests that the transcription factor perturbation is read out as a neuronal state change rather than as a generic cell-stress response: Grin2c, Gabrb2, Rab3c, Camk2a, Cacna1g and Lrrc7 decrease while Bdnf, Scg3, Chgb, Pcsk1n, Pnoc and Adcyap1r1 rise.

literature_claim: ATXN1-family/CIC complexes have been linked to extracellular-matrix gene regulation through Etv4-dependent Mmp control in development.
main_caveats: The ECM connection is indirect and most prior molecular detail comes from lung development rather than thalamic neurons.
summary: Atxn1 loss in 151 TH induced a coupled neurite-cytoskeleton, glycosylation, lipid and extracellular-matrix remodeling program.
why_it_matters: Up-regulated Wdr1, Macf1, Add3, Nefl, Ank2 and Ablim genes point to structural remodeling, while Mgat5, Dpy19l3, St6galnac6, Tecr, Pmvk, Hmgcr, Frzb, Col24a1 and Mmp15 show that the state also rewires membrane composition and pericellular matrix genes.

literature_claim: No specific Atxn1 literature was needed to interpret this measured secondary arm.
main_caveats: Module calling is manual and based on a small set of FDR-supported genes.
summary: A smaller metabolic arm of the 151-TH response induced Aldh1l2, glycolytic/amino-acid transport genes, and mitochondrial redox components without a coherent UPR/ISR signature.
why_it_matters: The response contains metabolic adaptation downstream of the Atxn1-Cic transcriptional hit, but it should not be over-read as canonical unfolded-protein, integrated-stress, or proteasome rebound because those modules were not coherently represented among the FDR<0.10 genes.

literature_claim: ATXN1 physically and genetically intersects RORa in SCA1 models, and several ataxia genes are tied by disease class rather than by a shared ATXN1-CIC complex.
main_caveats: Rora shares some same-direction 151-TH genes, so the contrast is quantitative rather than absolute.
summary: Atxn1 did not phenocopy the literature-obvious Rora or ataxia-gene comparators in the thalamic responder.
why_it_matters: Rora is an ATXN1 interactor in SCA1 cerebellar biology and Atxn2, Atxn7 and Atxn10 are ataxia-associated targets in the same screen, yet their measured 151-TH and whole-profile similarities were far below Cic. Disease naming therefore did not predict acute postnatal LoF transcriptomic neighborhoods.

literature_claim: No prior Dstyk-Atxn1 relationship was used; Dstyk was data-nominated and then rejected as a biologically strong anti-signature.
main_caveats: Full-vector cosine values are small because most Atxn1 dimensions are flat.
summary: The screen revealed no strong mirror-image Atxn1 signature: Dstyk was the strongest broad gene anti-neighbor but had only a -0.020 full-profile cosine and no 151-TH FDR overlap.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting weak negative correlations as pathway opposition; Atxn1's informative cross-perturbation structure is dominated by positive convergence with Cic.

literature_claim: Developmental ATXN1-CIC disruption affects forebrain upper-layer neuronal maturation far more broadly than six genes.
main_caveats: Six FDR<0.10 genes total; no shared significant genes with Cic in these cortical cells.
summary: Atxn1 produced a reproducible but very small cortical IT response involving Wnt/synaptic-terminal genes rather than a local copy of the thalamic CIC program.
why_it_matters: Cyfip2 and Dvl2 in L4/5 IT and Stx1a, Syn3, Stxbp2 and Kctd4 in L2/3 IT are FDR-supported, but six total genes across two groups implies a buffered cortical response to single Atxn1 loss at P16.

literature_claim: Mouse and in-vitro work shows that Atxn10 can be essential in selected developmental, epithelial, and cerebellar-neuron contexts.
main_caveats: Sparse postmitotic neuronal CRISPR loss, not complete systemic deletion; DNA indels and non-neuronal phenotypes were not measured.
summary: Atxn10 loss produced a restricted postnatal neuronal response: 7 of 22 recovered groups had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, with 052 Pvalb Gaba dominating.
why_it_matters: The main axis is selective vulnerability rather than a pan-neuronal loss-of-function transcriptome.

literature_claim: The integrated stress response induces ATF4-linked amino-acid/redox modules, and Pvalb interneurons are a stress-vulnerable fast-spiking class.
main_caveats: ATF4 itself was not FDR-significant; the inference rests on downstream ISR-compatible genes.
summary: 052 Pvalb Gaba mounted the main adaptive Atxn10 program, coupling ISR/amino-acid response genes with regulated-secretory/neuropeptide up-regulation.
why_it_matters: The CHAC1-ASNS-EIF4EBP1/ATF5 axis makes stress detectable at the RNA level in a single vulnerable class.

literature_claim: No ATXN10-specific publication established Atp1a3 as a loss-of-function readout.
main_caveats: Transcriptional only; it does not directly measure Na/K-ATPase activity or firing.
summary: Atp1a3 was the most recurrent same-direction downstream marker of Atxn10 perturbation, falling in four responder classes.
why_it_matters: A shared ion-pump/synaptic down-module links otherwise distinct responders and nominates a compact readout for the active Atxn10 state.

literature_claim: ATXN10 was reported to promote neuritogenesis through Ras-MAPK signaling.
main_caveats: The cortical and CNU-HYa HY components are very small.
summary: A cytoskeletal/tubulin component was present from the thinnest cortical effect to the Pvalb, thalamic, and midbrain signatures.
why_it_matters: The 2-gene 005 and 1-gene 066 effects become sparse echoes of a broader structural-remodeling axis.

literature_claim: No literature-obvious ATXN10 comparator predicted Eef2, Psmb4, or U2af2 as the closest pooled Perturb-seq neighbors.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed only on the 359 Atxn10 FDR<0.10 features.
summary: Eef2, Psmb4 and U2af2, not ATXN10 textbook relatives, were among the closest empirical Atxn10 neighbors.
why_it_matters: Cross-target convergence reframes the response as a restricted proteostasis/RNA-processing module rather than an isolated ataxin phenotype.

literature_claim: ATXN10 physically interacts with OGT in brain.
main_caveats: The screen did not measure O-GlcNAcylation.
summary: Ogt, a literature ATXN10 interactor, only partially overlapped Atxn10 and had a different cell-type footprint.
why_it_matters: ATXN10 loss did not behave like local OGT loss across this P16 neuronal assay.

literature_claim: SCA10 is an intronic ATTCT-repeat disease, whereas SCA1, SCA2 and SCA7 are genetically distinct polyglutamine SCAs.
main_caveats: Only Atxn1, Atxn2 and Atxn7 were represented among ataxia-name comparators in the queried set.
summary: Atxn1, Atxn2 and Atxn7 did not phenocopy Atxn10 despite sharing spinocerebellar-ataxia naming.
why_it_matters: The Atxn10 module should not be treated as a generic ataxia-gene LoF module.

literature_claim: SCA10 AUUCU RNA can sequester hnRNP K and induce PKCdelta/caspase apoptosis; siRNA work predicted cerebellar-neuron survival dependence after ATXN10 loss.
main_caveats: 308 CB GABA is not a purified adult Purkinje or repeat-expansion model, and the assay did not measure cell abundance.
summary: The 308 CB GABA null and global absence of caspase/hnRNP K/PKCdelta markers argue that coding Atxn10 CRISPR loss did not recapitulate SCA10 repeat-RNA toxicity.
why_it_matters: LoF of the coding gene is not equivalent to suppressing the expanded intronic repeat RNA.

literature_claim: ATXN10 overexpression promoted Ras-MAP kinase-Elk-1-dependent neuritogenesis in PC12 cells through Gβ2.
main_caveats: Only 10 genes reached FDR<0.10 in this group.
summary: The 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut response was a small up, not down, immediate-early/MAPK-feedback signature.
why_it_matters: The cortical result suggests a compensatory activity/MAPK-feedback state rather than simple loss of an ERK-output transcriptome.

literature_claim: ATXN2 is a conserved cytoplasmic RNA-binding and stress-granule protein, but the literature does not predict that acute Atxn2 loss in otherwise wild-type juvenile neurons should be pan-transcriptional.
main_caveats: Only 14 downstream genes passed FDR<0.10 and the responding group is an aggregate taxonomy class.
summary: Atxn2 loss produced a robust downstream transcriptional response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, despite recovery in 21 neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The response is not a pan-neuronal consequence of removing a broadly acting RNA-binding protein; in this P16-to-P37/44 sparse CRISPR setting it resolves to one thalamic glutamatergic class.

literature_claim: ATXN2 participates in RNA metabolism through P-body and stress-granule interactions, while SON/SR-rich factors are linked to pre-mRNA splicing and nuclear speckles.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq measured transcript abundance, not splicing isoforms, RNA binding, or protein-level granule dynamics.
summary: The negative arm of the 151 signature hit RNA-processing and nuclear-speckle factors, including Srsf11, Rsrp1 and Son.
why_it_matters: This aligns the only Atxn2 response with RNA metabolism, the target's canonical molecular axis, while showing that a cytoplasmic stress-granule protein can secondarily lower nuclear splicing-factor transcripts in one thalamic class.

literature_claim: Syt7 is required for facilitation at several central synapses, so Syt7 up-regulation is directionally consistent with a presynaptic plasticity or release-modulation response.
main_caveats: The genes nominate a module but the assay did not measure synaptic physiology or neurite morphology.
summary: Atxn2 perturbation up-regulated a small synaptic and neurite-structure module in 151, including Syt7, Sncb, Cspg5, Tln2, Crmp1, Stmn4, Ncdn and Gprasp1.
why_it_matters: The positive arm looks like neuronal wiring or presynaptic compensation rather than a canonical ISR, UPR, or cell-death program; Syt7 is a synaptic-facilitation calcium sensor, making the strongest up-regulated gene a plausible activity-homeostasis readout.

literature_claim: ATXN2 physically and functionally connects to DDX6/P-bodies, stress granules, translational control, mTOR and TDP-43 toxicity.
main_caveats: A post-transcriptional or protein-localization defect could occur without changing the corresponding mRNA; the conclusion is limited to secondary transcriptional programs.
summary: The screen did not recover a robust ATXN2 partner, TDP-43, stress-granule, UPR/ISR, autophagy or mTOR transcript program after Atxn2 loss.
why_it_matters: Because stress and proteostasis programs would be visible to snRNA-seq, their absence argues that acute wild-type Atxn2 loss is buffered in most P37/44 neurons and that the observed 151 response is not a generic stress-granule collapse signature.

literature_claim: No ATXN2-specific prior connected Zbtb7a or Elp1 to this 14-gene thalamic signature.
main_caveats: The neighbor metric used only the 14 FDR<0.10 Atxn2 genes in one cell group; Zbtb7a and Elp1 have much broader signatures.
summary: Restricted-signature analysis placed Zbtb7a and Elp1, not a textbook ATXN2 partner, as the strongest same-direction neighbors of Atxn2 in 151.
why_it_matters: The dataset nominates a shared local state involving Gprasp1 up and Srsf11/Rsrp1/Son/Coro6/Tspoap1 down; this should be treated as an empirical neighborhood rather than inferred from ATXN2 complexes.

literature_claim: No ATXN2-specific literature predicted Yy1 or Psmb4 as inverse signature neighbors.
main_caveats: The inverse call is local to the 151 Atxn2 signature and is not evidence that YY1 or the proteasome directly antagonizes ATXN2.
summary: Yy1 and Psmb4 were the top inverse restricted-signature neighbors of Atxn2 in 151.
why_it_matters: Opposite regulation of Syt7/Ncdn/Crmp1/Stmn4 and the presynaptic genes under Yy1 or Psmb4 perturbation helps separate the Atxn2 state from generic chromatin-factor or proteasome-loss injury programs.

literature_claim: Intermediate ATXN2 polyglutamine expansions increase ALS risk and ATXN2 reduction suppresses TDP-43 toxicity in mouse models.
main_caveats: The assay did not model TDP-43 aggregation, ALS motor neurons, spinal cord, or ATXN2 polyglutamine expansions.
summary: ATXN2's ALS/stress-granule relatives did not phenocopy Atxn2 single-gene loss: Tardbp and Matr3 were broad, Tia1 was nearly flat, and their 151 overlap with Atxn2 was small or mixed.
why_it_matters: The result keeps the therapeutic ATXN2/TDP-43 relationship oriented correctly: reducing Atxn2 in wild-type neurons is not equivalent to perturbing TDP-43-family RNA-binding proteins and does not by itself induce a TDP-43 disease-like transcriptome.

literature_claim: SCA2 is caused by ATXN2 CAG expansion; this does not imply that ataxia-named LoF targets should phenocopy wild-type Atxn2 LoF.
main_caveats: This is a loss-of-function comparison among gene names rather than a knock-in comparison of repeat-expanded alleles.
summary: Spinocerebellar ataxia-family targets represented in the parquet diverged from Atxn2: Atxn1 and Atxn10 responded but shared little of the 151 Atxn2 signature, whereas Atxn7 was flat.
why_it_matters: Repeat-ataxia membership alone was not a useful predictor of acute postnatal neuronal LoF transcriptomes, arguing against collapsing ATXN2 to a generic ataxin/polyglutamine class in this screen.

literature_claim: ATXN7 is a TFTC/STAGA-SAGA subunit whose loss can perturb H2B ubiquitination and produce neural, retinal, photoreceptor, or Purkinje phenotypes in fly and zebrafish loss-of-function systems.
main_caveats: Functional DNA indels were not measured; the statement is limited to sparse acute CRISPR loss of the wild-type mouse locus in P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ nuclei.
summary: Atxn7 gRNA targeting was transcriptomically buffered across the postmitotic neuronal panel: 20 measured groups and 1021 perturbed nuclei yielded zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Atxn7 is a SAGA chromatin coactivator subunit, so this is an informative negative result: disrupting the wild-type locus after P16 did not create a broad SAGA-collapse, proteostasis, integrated-stress, redox, autophagy, or synaptic-maintenance transcriptional program in any sampled neuronal class.

literature_claim: Polyglutamine spinocerebellar ataxias and Huntington disease are dominant repeat-expansion disorders, but they arise from otherwise distinct proteins; ATXN7 also has ATXN7L paralogs that could buffer partial loss of normal function.
main_caveats: Only a subset of SCA and polyQ genes was represented; Cacna1a and Ppp2r2b were themselves flat in the matched groups, and same-SAGA targets were absent.
summary: Related ataxia and polyglutamine-family targets did not phenocopy Atxn7 loss: Atxn10, Atxn1, Htt, and Atxn2 produced FDR<0.10 genes in matched cell groups, but all had near-zero vector similarity to Atxn7.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that disease-family membership is not sufficient to define a shared postmitotic CRISPR LoF state; Atxn7 is specifically flat even in the same assay where other Atxn or polyQ-associated genes can move the transcriptome.

literature_claim: SCA7 is caused by toxic polyglutamine-expanded ATXN7, and lowering both mutant and wild-type Atxn7 can improve SCA7 mouse phenotypes.
main_caveats: The screen did not sample retina or Bergmann glia, did not express expanded Atxn7, lasted only 3-4 weeks, and measured RNA rather than protein aggregation or motor/visual physiology.

why_it_matters: Nonallele-specific Atxn7 lowering has been beneficial in SCA7 mouse models, and this dataset adds that partial wild-type Atxn7 disruption did not produce a short-term nuclear RNA stress response in 20 sampled healthy neuronal classes.

why_it_matters: The result is an interpretable negative in the measured P16-to-P37/44 sparse neuronal context: AUH is present as a tested transcript, yet loss did not trigger a nuclear mitochondrial-stress, amino-acid, proteostasis, or synaptic program detectable by snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: AUTS2 is known to regulate Rac1/Cdc42-dependent neuronal cytoskeleton biology, while DPYSL/CRMP proteins participate in neurite and dendrite morphogenesis.
main_caveats: The finding rests on one FDR<0.10 gene and does not establish Dpysl4 as a direct AUTS2 target.
summary: Auts2 loss produced a single robust downstream hit: Dpysl4 was up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The isolated thalamic Dpysl4 response links the only positive Auts2 transcriptome effect to a DPYSL/CRMP cytoskeletal gene rather than to a broad chromatin or stress cascade.

literature_claim: Developmental Auts2 loss is linked to PRC1/P300/CK2 transcriptional activation, RNA metabolism, dentate/cortical development, and Purkinje Cacna1a/synapse maturation.
main_caveats: True DNA indel engagement was not measured; snRNA-seq would miss morphology and electrophysiology.
summary: Auts2 was almost globally transcriptionally buffered after P16 mosaic CRISPR, with 1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 22 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result separates acute postmitotic Auts2 loss from the broad developmental transcriptional, RNA-metabolism, and Purkinje maturation phenotypes seen in earlier or lineage-targeted models.

literature_claim: The PRC1-AUTS2 complex uses CK2 and P300 to convert PRC1 toward transcriptional activation, and AUTS2 syndrome overlaps phenotypically with CREBBP/EP300-associated Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome.
main_caveats: Csnk2b is a CK2 regulatory subunit rather than the full CK2 holoenzyme; the direct PCGF3/5 and RING1B PRC1 targets were not represented.
summary: Csnk2b and Crebbp were transcriptionally active where Auts2 was nearly flat, while Ep300 was flat; none shared the robust Auts2 Dpysl4 response.
why_it_matters: The AUTS2-PRC1 biochemical neighborhood is not interchangeable in this in vivo postmitotic transcriptome: CK2/CBP perturbations can elicit DE without an Auts2-like signature.

main_caveats: The convergence contains only one Auts2 FDR<0.10 gene; it should be treated as a biomarker hypothesis, not a CTCF-AUTS2 mechanism.
summary: Ctcf was the top positive pre-literature Auts2 neighbor and shared the same robust Dpysl4-up event in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The one robust Auts2 downstream gene is not private to Auts2; it marks a thalamic Dpysl4 module that can also be induced by a chromatin perturbation outside the textbook AUTS2 pathway.

literature_claim: AUTS2 activates Rac1 and suppresses Cdc42 through cytoplasmic interactions that regulate lamellipodia, filopodia, neuronal migration, and neuritogenesis.
main_caveats: The primary literature measures GTPase activity and morphology; transcriptomic non-convergence does not falsify cytoskeletal coupling at the protein level.
summary: Direct Rac1 and Cdc42 perturbations were flat or nearly flat and did not converge with Auts2.
why_it_matters: This argues that the known AUTS2-Rac1/Cdc42 pathway is not reported as a broad steady-state transcriptome downstream program in this P16-P37 snRNA assay.

literature_claim: AVPR1A is a V1a GPCR acting through phosphatidylinositol-calcium signaling, whereas SRSF6 is an SR-family splicing regulator with no established position in the canonical V1a pathway.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10; the Srsf6 increase should be treated as a biomarker candidate, not as proof of a broad splicing program.
summary: Avpr1a loss produced a single robust transcriptomic event: Srsf6 up-regulation in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: The response nominates a very narrow postnatal neuronal state, and the only robust marker is an RNA-splicing factor rather than a canonical AVPR1A second-messenger transcript.

literature_claim: V1a activation signals through phosphatidylinositol-calcium pathways and can induce c-Fos and Egr-1 after ligand stimulation.
main_caveats: The literature induction program is mostly ligand-evoked and includes non-neuronal systems; this screen measured unstimulated basal snRNA after mosaic loss of function.
summary: The Srsf6-positive group did not carry a broader V1a Gq/PLC/PKC/MAPK or immediate-early-gene signature.
why_it_matters: It separates chronic basal Avpr1a loss in postmitotic neurons from acute agonist-evoked V1a signaling, which is expected to be dominated by calcium/PKC and ERK-linked outputs.

literature_claim: OXTR, AVPR1A, AVPR1B, and AVPR2 are paralogous nonapeptide receptors, but brain vasopressin/oxytocin actions are region- and receptor-specific.
main_caveats: Several pathway members either were not perturbation targets or had modest cell counts; the conclusion is restricted to the represented perturbations and FDR<0.10 transcriptional phenotypes.
summary: Directly represented nonapeptide and PLC/PKC pathway perturbations did not phenocopy the Avpr1a 110/Srsf6 response.
why_it_matters: The expected relatives were measurable and negative: Avpr1b, Oxtr, Plcb1, Prkca, and Prkcg were all flat in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, so the Avpr1a singleton is not a generic Gq-coupled neuropeptide-receptor artifact.

main_caveats: The neighbor search used 220 Avpr1a nominal features because the FDR-level signature contained only Srsf6; similarities should be read only as a screen diagnostic.
summary: Nominal-surface signature neighbors were rejected as robust Avpr1a phenocopies.
why_it_matters: Rho, Snca, and E2f1 were the top positive non-safe sparse neighbors and Gclm, Il4ra, and Dmxl2 were the top negative neighbors, but none reproduced a significant Srsf6 response in the Avpr1a-positive cell group.

literature_claim: V1a loss or replacement changes mouse social-recognition behaviors, and the V1a antagonist balovaptan reached autism trials with mixed-to-negative efficacy across later trials.
main_caveats: The screen did not assay behavior, ligand challenge, receptor pharmacology, or peripheral AVPR1A actions.
summary: Avpr1a behaved like a circuit- and state-dependent GPCR target rather than a target with a large basal cell-autonomous transcriptional footprint.
why_it_matters: The flat postnatal neuronal DE surface does not negate AVPR1A behavioral pharmacology or V1a-antagonist druggability, but it warns that basal snRNA is a poor standalone biomarker axis for V1a antagonist efficacy.

summary: Axl perturbation failed to recover the innate-inflammatory, TAM-compensation, neurotrophin, ISR/UPR, autophagy, or apoptosis programs predicted from TAM biology in other systems.
why_it_matters: The FDR-null surface is informative because canonical sentinels were explicitly assayed: Socs1, Socs3, Tnf, Il1b, Ccl2, Nfkbia/Nfkbib, Mertk, Tyro3, Gas6, Pros1, Bdnf/Ngf/Ntf3 receptors, Atf3/Atf4/Ddit3/Trib3, Hspa5/Hsp90aa1, Bax/Bcl2/Bcl2l11/Casp3, and Sqstm1/Becn1/Map1lc3b all remained FDR=1.00 in all 22 measured groups.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on nominal Axl score features because Axl had no FDR<0.10 genes; the neighbor result is a rejection of robust convergence, not evidence for Syn1- or S1pr2-related mechanism.
summary: A dataset-wide nominal-score neighbor search found no strong Axl-like perturbation signature.
why_it_matters: The best positive neighbor, Syn1, had cosine 0.115 and only two FDR genes of its own, while the strongest overall negative neighbor was a Safe_target and the strongest named-gene negative neighbor was S1pr2 with no FDR genes, so cross-target analysis did not reveal a hidden convergent neuronal module for Axl.

direction: Ndor1 and Herc1 up in 059; no FDR<0.10 downstream response in the other 22 measured groups
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes passed FDR<0.10; B3gat3 editing was not measured by DNA indel sequencing.
summary: B3gat3 produced a real but extremely restricted neuronal RNA response: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA was the only one of 23 measured groups with any downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The main phenotype in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic neuronal assay is not a pan-neuronal glycosaminoglycan-transcription response, but a two-gene, LGE/LSX GABA-only signal on a mostly flat surface.

literature_claim: NDOR1 encodes a diflavin NADPH oxidoreductase and HERC1 encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase that regulates neuronal presynaptic membrane dynamics.
main_caveats: Interpretation rests on two FDR-significant genes; the absence of FDR changes in UPR/ISR/autophagy/proteasome markers prevents calling this a broad stress pathway.
summary: The 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA response consisted of up-regulation of Ndor1 and Herc1, nominating a small redox/ubiquitin-ligase marker pair rather than a broad canonical GAG module.
why_it_matters: NDOR1 is an NADPH-dependent electron-transfer enzyme and HERC1 is a neuronal E3 ligase linked to presynaptic vesicle dynamics, so these two transcripts are plausible readouts of a small adaptive state but not proof of oxidative stress, autophagy, or proteasome remodeling.

literature_claim: B3GAT3 is the glucuronyltransferase that completes the GAG-protein linker required before HS and CS/DS chain polymerization.
main_caveats: The curated marker test addresses RNA feedback, not HS/CS chain abundance, sulfation pattern, or pericellular matrix structure.
summary: Acute B3gat3 loss did not transcriptionally feed back onto the common linker, heparan-sulfate/chondroitin-sulfate enzyme set, proteoglycan core genes, or canonical stress modules.
why_it_matters: The result separates the expected biochemical lesion, defective Golgi addition of GAG chains to proteoglycans, from what snRNA-seq recovered: virtually no GAG-biosynthetic mRNA compensation and no detectable UPR/ISR or autophagy rebound.

direction: nonconvergent; Ext2-specific effects outside the B3gat3 responding group
literature_claim: XYLT1, B3GAT3, EXT2, GLCE, HS6ST2, and glypicans participate at different steps of the proteoglycan/GAG or HS pathway, but shared pathway membership is biochemical rather than a prediction of identical mature-neuron RNA signatures.
main_caveats: The contrast is against a weak B3gat3 signature; most related targets were also nearly flat in 059.
summary: Represented GAG/HS pathway perturbations did not phenocopy B3gat3 in the matched 059 responder, and the only robust downstream relatives-of-interest signal, Ext2, appeared in other glutamatergic groups on Epha5 and Slc6a17.
why_it_matters: Direct measurement of pathway neighbors rejects a simple same-pathway-equals-same-signature model for postnatal neurons: B3gat3, Ext1, Ext2, Glce, Gpc6, Hs6st2, and Xylt1 have sharply different DE surfaces in this assay.

main_caveats: The neighbor query used the 51 genes with nominal p<0.01 in 059 because only two genes were FDR-significant; all nominated neighbors were rejected by FDR criteria.
summary: The data-driven 059 B3gat3 signature had no robust positive or negative neighbor among the 1742 other targets measured in that group.
why_it_matters: The top correlations were driven by subthreshold ranks in otherwise null perturbations, so the B3gat3 two-gene response should not be promoted to a larger convergent module without external validation.

literature_claim: B3GAT3 loss reduces multiple classes of GAG-modified proteoglycans and human disease is dominated by developmental skeletal, connective-tissue, and cardiac phenotypes, while HSPGs also guide neural development and synaptic specificity.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure glycan structures, extracellular proteoglycan turnover, or perturbation-induced loss of neurons from the sampled pool.
summary: The mostly null P16 neuronal transcriptome argues that B3GAT3-linked phenotypes are displaced from ongoing, cell-autonomous neuronal RNA regulation toward proteoglycan biochemistry, earlier wiring, and non-neuronal matrix-rich tissues.
why_it_matters: This refines, rather than contradicts, linkeropathy biology: a juvenile NeuN+ snRNA-seq assay can miss altered HS/CS chains while still showing that broad mature-neuron secondary transcription is not a dominant consequence of sparse postmitotic B3gat3 loss.

literature_claim: B9D1 is a broadly used ciliary B9-complex transition-zone component whose loss can disrupt ciliogenesis and Hedgehog-dependent development.
main_caveats: The responder group contained 62 perturbed nuclei, and two taxonomy groups had no B9d1 rows.
summary: B9d1 produced one FDR-supported response, a 25-gene signature restricted to 308 CB GABA, while 20 other recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The positive biology is not a pan-neuronal ciliary-loss signature; it is concentrated in a cerebellar GABAergic population after postnatal perturbation.

literature_claim: No B9D1-specific literature prior predicted this exact postnatal CB-GABA synaptic up-module.
main_caveats: Program assignment is made from a sparse 25-gene signature and should be treated as transcriptomic.
summary: The B9d1 CB-GABA responder signature upregulated synaptic and neuronal-signaling transcripts including Homer3, Doc2b, Scn4b, Nptx1, Dlg2, Grm7, Lrp8, Cdh2, Stac, and Plppr5.
why_it_matters: The measured response points to altered cerebellar neuronal state or connectivity rather than a direct transcriptional readout of ciliary transition-zone assembly.

literature_claim: No literature prior linked postnatal neuronal B9d1 loss to Col5a1/Col18a1 induction.
main_caveats: The extracellular-matrix interpretation rests on two FDR-supported genes.
summary: Two extracellular-matrix genes, Col5a1 and Col18a1, were among the strongest B9d1-induced CB-GABA genes.
why_it_matters: The collagens indicate that the CB-GABA response is not limited to receptor or synaptic RNAs and may include niche or adhesion remodeling.

literature_claim: No B9D1-specific literature prior predicted this exact CB-GABA membrane/cytoskeletal RNA module.
main_caveats: These genes support a broad remodeling label but do not define one proven biochemical pathway.
summary: B9d1 upregulated several membrane/cytoskeletal regulatory transcripts in CB GABA, including Arhgap31, Arap1, Garnl3, Atl2, Strip2, Ptprr, Phc2, and Pogk.
why_it_matters: Small-GTPase and membrane-scaffold changes are plausible secondary adaptations to perturbing a ciliary gate, even when the gate defect itself is not directly visible in snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: B9D1 and the B9 transition-zone module are expected to control ciliary cargo gating and, during development, Hedgehog signal transduction.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot exclude altered ciliary protein localization without an accompanying nuclear RNA response.
summary: The B9d1 CB-GABA signature did not recover a canonical Hedgehog, ciliary-GPCR, ciliary-assembly, or broad stress transcriptional program; Gas8 was the only cilium-adjacent FDR gene.
why_it_matters: This separates the observed postnatal CB-GABA RNA state from the embryonic Hedgehog and ciliary-localization defects that dominate the B9D1 literature.

literature_claim: No established B9d1-Ranbp2 relationship was used as a prior.
main_caveats: The neighbor call is restricted to the 25-gene B9d1 CB-GABA signature and is not a mechanistic proof of direct interaction.
summary: Ranbp2 was the strongest same-direction data-driven neighbor of the B9d1 CB-GABA signature, sharing 11 FDR-supported genes in the same direction.
why_it_matters: The convergence nominates a non-obvious cross-perturbation relationship for the CB-GABA state and shows that many B9d1 genes recur under an independent perturbation.

literature_claim: No established B9d1-Wdr26 antagonism was used as a prior.
main_caveats: Wdr26 had a much broader CB-GABA response than B9d1, so the contrast identifies opposite regulation, not pathway specificity.
summary: Wdr26 opposed the B9d1 CB-GABA signature, reversing 22 of 25 B9d1 FDR genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The near mirror-image relationship argues that the 25 genes form a regulatable cerebellar module rather than stochastic low-cell-count DE.

literature_claim: B9D1 belongs to a transition-zone ciliary network whose related genes regulate ciliogenesis and ciliary membrane composition.
main_caveats: The direct B9-complex partners Mks1 and B9d2 were absent from the perturbation universe.
summary: Represented ciliary and Hedgehog comparators were flat in 308 CB GABA and did not share an FDR-supported B9d1 signature gene.
why_it_matters: The expected ciliary relatives did not phenocopy B9d1, refining the CB-GABA signature as B9d1-selective in this assay rather than a generic cilium-perturbation response.

literature_claim: Bach2 has been reported in differentiating embryonic neuronal cells, whereas Dnajc5 and Yeats2 annotate to synaptic-vesicle chaperone and ATAC chromatin functions.
main_caveats: Only two FDR-significant genes support the L4/5 signature; Dnajc5 and Yeats2 are single-gene markers rather than a coherent recovered Bach2 pathway.
summary: Bach2 produced a real but extremely narrow L4/5 IT cortical response: Dnajc5 and Yeats2 were up at FDR<0.10 only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, while every other measured group was null or weak.
why_it_matters: A postmitotic neuronal Bach2 perturbation did not behave like a broadly active immune-style lineage switch; the only robust genes point to isolated synaptic-vesicle chaperone and chromatin-cofactor markers in one intratelencephalic cortical class, not a multi-gene inflammatory or antioxidant program.

literature_claim: BACH proteins heterodimerize with small Maf factors, and NRF2/small-Maf heterodimers regulate antioxidant-response-element genes.
main_caveats: The decisive Mafg effect is in Pvalb rather than Bach2's L4/5 responder group; oxidative stress was not imposed, and Nfe2l2 itself was flat in this basal dataset.
summary: Loss of Bach2 did not de-repress Hmox1 or a canonical ARE/cytoprotection program, even though the same parquet shows that Mafg loss can activate Hmox1 strongly in Pvalb neurons.
why_it_matters: BACH factors and small Mafs are expected to meet at Maf-recognition or ARE-like regulatory elements; the cross-perturbation split suggests that, in these juvenile neurons at basal state, Mafg is limiting for a heme-oxygenase branch whereas Bach2 is not.

literature_claim: Bach2 is a bZIP Maf partner linked to AP-1/Maf-dependent and ARE/NF-E2-like transcriptional control.
main_caveats: Bach1, Mafk, Maff, Bcl6 and Prdm1 were not represented as perturbation targets, so the test covers only the subset of the obvious pathway neighborhood present in the parquet.
summary: Represented sMaf/CNC/AP-1/Maf-family relatives did not phenocopy the Bach2 L4/5 signature.
why_it_matters: Mafg, Nfe2l1, Maf, Mafb and Jund had their few significant genes in Pvalb, thalamic, midbrain/hindbrain or cerebellar groups, Nfe2l2 had none, and every tested related perturbation had zero FDR<0.10 genes in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; the expected family-level similarity is therefore rejected in the matched data.

main_caveats: The neighbor search was dominated by a very small Bach2 signature; absence of convergence is robust, but the actual private signature remains only two genes.
summary: Bach2 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the rest of the target universe.
why_it_matters: The closest non-Safe global neighbors had cosine magnitudes below 0.03 and failed the matched-surface check, so Bach2's two-gene L4/5 response should be treated as a private, low-complexity signature rather than a reusable Perturb-seq module shared with Ttll5, Nkx6-2, Dpm1 or Cdin1.

literature_claim: Dnajc5 and Yeats2 have known neuronal chaperone/synaptic-vesicle and chromatin-reader annotations, respectively, but neither is a canonical BACH2 target.
main_caveats: Privacy in a single screen is not external replication; the marker hypothesis rests on two L4/5 genes only.
summary: Dnajc5 and Yeats2 are hypothesis-generating L4/5 readouts of Bach2 perturbation rather than generic responders.
why_it_matters: No other target in the parquet significantly changed either gene in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut at FDR<0.10, so a future Bach2 validation in this cell class can test whether these two genes are reproducible immediate readouts of the perturbation.

literature_claim: BAIAP2/IRSp53 is an excitatory postsynaptic membrane-actin scaffold whose loss perturbs dendritic spines, NMDA receptor physiology, and behavior.
main_caveats: DNA indel frequencies and protein depletion were not measured; a nuclear snRNA null does not test spine morphology, actin bundling, or synaptic currents directly.
summary: Baiap2 was a pan-assay transcriptional null: all 23 recovered neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 after P16 CRISPR loss of function.
why_it_matters: This separates the presence of a Baiap2 indel perturbation from a nuclear RNA-state shift; the strongest Baiap2 biology in this assay is the absence of a robust downstream transcriptional response.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: BAIAP2/IRSp53 couples Rac1 and Cdc42 signaling to actin regulators including WAVE-pathway effectors and to PSD-95/Shank-containing excitatory postsynaptic assemblies.
main_caveats: The panel tested transcript levels of selected canonical genes; it does not measure protein localization, GTP loading, phosphorylation, or F-actin architecture.
summary: The expected PSD, glutamate-receptor, Rho-actin, and immediate-early transcriptional candidates were not recovered as Baiap2 downstream genes in any cell group.
why_it_matters: The result localizes the acute Baiap2 effect, if present, upstream of transcript abundance and at the membrane/actin/PSD layer measured by imaging or electrophysiology rather than by snRNA-seq.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: IRSp53 loss in mice alters NMDAR-related synaptic physiology, and abnormal NMDAR function is linked to Baiap2-dependent behavioral phenotypes.
main_caveats: The receptor-subunit programs are not a perfect mechanistic positive control for a PSD actin scaffold; they only show that direct receptor perturbations can be transcriptionally visible.
summary: Direct NMDA receptor perturbations diverged from Baiap2: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced recurrent DE in matched neurons, whereas Baiap2 had none.
why_it_matters: The assay was capable of detecting receptor-coupled neuronal RNA programs in several of the same cell groups, so Baiap2 silence is more specific than a blanket failure to read glutamatergic perturbations.

literature_claim: BAIAP2/IRSp53 is BAI1-associated and directly linked to PSD-95 and Shank-family scaffold assemblies; SynGAP1 is an abundant disease-linked excitatory PSD comparator.
main_caveats: Comparators span an adhesion receptor and PSD scaffolds rather than a single obligate complex, and Baiap2 has no FDR genes with which to test shared-direction overlap.
summary: BAI1/PSD scaffold comparators did not phenocopy a hidden Baiap2-like module: Adgrb1, Shank2, Dlg4, and Syngap1 each had zero downstream DE across the matched groups, while Shank3 and Dlgap4 were sparse with two and ten genes.
why_it_matters: Expected IRSp53-associated scaffold genes are themselves largely buffered in this juvenile mosaic snRNA readout, arguing that the flat Baiap2 surface belongs to a broader class of structural postsynaptic scaffolds rather than to Baiap2-specific assay failure.

main_caveats: Cosines were computed from signed Wilcoxon z-scores over the measured Baiap2 feature space and summarize low-amplitude rank structure, not FDR-supported genes.
summary: Unbiased signature matching found no credible Baiap2 module: the best positive and negative z-score cosines were only 0.0305 and -0.0185.
why_it_matters: Very weak extrema, plus Safe_target perturbations at the edges of the Baiap2 neighbor list, make the data-driven Grin2b/Il1rapl1/Shank2 and Eef2/Gfpt1 calls useful as audited non-convergences rather than as biological modules.

literature_claim: BAP1/PR-DUB is a chromatin H2AK119ub1 deubiquitinase with strong developmental, proliferative, and homeostatic roles in other systems.
main_caveats: The assay is postmitotic and mosaic; DNA indels and BAP1 protein loss were not measured.
summary: Bap1 had a sparse, cell-state-restricted postmitotic neuronal response: 34 downstream FDR<0.10 genes confined to Pvalb, TH-Prkcd/Grin2c, and MB glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: A chromatin deubiquitinase with embryo- and cancer-lineage functions did not behave as a pan-neuronal essential transcriptional regulator when removed acutely at P16.

literature_claim: Secretogranin II is a large dense-core vesicle protein in endocrine, neuroendocrine, and neuronal tissues and the precursor of secretoneurin.
main_caveats: Only Scg2 was recurrent at FDR<0.10; the secretory interpretation is a marker hypothesis, not a measured vesicle phenotype.
summary: Scg2 was the only recurrent Bap1 responder gene, down in both 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: This nominates regulated secretory-granule output as the clearest shared neuronal consequence of Bap1 loss, rather than a generic Polycomb or DNA-damage target list.

literature_claim: PR-DUB is expected to regulate transcriptional output through H2AK119ub1 control rather than directly encoding a fixed stress pathway.
main_caveats: The modules are inferred from a 25-gene list without an enrichment p-value, and each submodule is represented by only a few genes.
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut program combined up-regulation of Cnot9, Cstf2, Aifm3, Peg3, Ank2, Cdkl1, and Nlgn2 with down-regulation of Hdac1, Acly, Gsto1, Tpp1, Stt3b, Sema5a, Prkch, Klf6, and Rreb1.
why_it_matters: The strongest cell class did not show a single canonical stress axis; it showed a small mixed adjustment of RNA processing, chromatin/metabolism, degradative-redox, mitochondrial, and synaptic/neurite genes.

literature_claim: HCN genes regulate neuronal excitability, while CCDC39 is required for motile-ciliary axonemal dynein regulatory complex assembly.
main_caveats: Only two genes were significant; Ccdc39 is a motile-cilia gene and the screen does not assay ciliary ultrastructure or electrophysiology.
summary: The 155 MB Glut response consisted only of Ccdc39 and Hcn3 down-regulation.
why_it_matters: This preserves the small but FDR-supported MB glutamatergic effect without inflating it into a full motile-cilia or HCN-channel pathway.

literature_claim: ANKRD11 is a chromatin regulator required for normal neural precursor proliferation, neurogenesis, and gene-expression control.
main_caveats: Whole-profile cosines were only about 0.03 and Dpm1, Ift43, and Arid1a were rejected as meaningful restricted FDR-overlap neighbors.
summary: The unbiased whole-profile scan placed Hnrnpc and Ankrd11 closest to Bap1, with Ankrd11 and Hnrnpc sharing down-regulation of Rreb1 and Ankrd11 also sharing Scg2 down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The nearest positive neighbors were RNA/chromatin neurodevelopmental regulators rather than the textbook PR-DUB partners, suggesting a weak postmitotic convergence module around TH neuronal gene-expression control.

literature_claim: BAP1 acts in ASXL-containing PR-DUB complexes with FOXK and OGT/HCFC1-associated chromatin regulation.
main_caveats: Unmeasured PR-DUB components, especially Asxl1, Asxl2, Foxk1, and Hcfc1, were not available as direct perturbation comparators.
summary: Asxl3 and Foxk2 were flat and Ogt was broad but nonmatching, so the measurable PR-DUB relatives did not phenocopy acute Bap1 loss in any matched neuronal group.
why_it_matters: Same-complex divergence argues that BAP1's neuronal output is not explained by simply disrupting every PR-DUB recruitment component at P16.

main_caveats: The anti-neighbors are broad and not direct BAP1 complex members; their contrast is phenotypic rather than mechanistic.
summary: Wdr26, Sin3a, Tpr, Psmb4, and Psmc1 were the strongest negative Bap1 neighbors and reversed more Bap1 significant features than they shared.
why_it_matters: The same dataset clearly detects broad proteostasis and chromatin-stress perturbations; Bap1's small signature is therefore not a generic failure to recover secondary transcriptional stress.

literature_claim: BAP1 loss in proliferative systems is linked to cell-cycle and cell-death regulation.
main_caveats: Absence is evaluated at 3-4 weeks post-perturbation and could miss earlier transient stress before harvest.
summary: Bap1 did not induce canonical ISR, UPR, proteasome, autophagy-adaptor, or p53/cell-death marker transcripts in the three cell groups that had real DE.
why_it_matters: Because Psmb4 and Psmc1 perturbations generated thousands of DE genes in the same matched space, the lack of an Atf4/Ddit3/Hspa5/Xbp1/Cdkn1a/Bax module after Bap1 loss is an informative negative result, not a snRNA-seq readout mismatch.

literature_claim: BAP1 loss-of-function variants classically predispose to cancer, whereas rare missense alleles rather than classical tumor-predisposition LoF alleles have been tied to Küry-Isidor neurodevelopmental disease.
main_caveats: The screen is not a variant-effect assay and did not test the human missense alleles.
summary: The weak postnatal neuronal LoF signature aligns better with allele- and timing-specific BAP1 neurodevelopmental biology than with a simple mature-neuron tumor-suppressor LoF model.
why_it_matters: It cautions against projecting BAP1 tumor-predisposition loss-of-function or Küry-Isidor missense mechanisms directly onto acute juvenile brain knockouts.

literature_claim: BAZ1B/WSTF is a chromatin-remodeling B-WICH component with broad roles in DNA-dependent nuclear processes.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in each responding group; no chromatin or protein readout was collected.
summary: Baz1b produced a two-gene, two-cell-group FDR response: Sfi1 down in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and Atp1b2 down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The dataset resolves Baz1b as an extremely sparse responder in acute juvenile neurons, not a broadly acting chromatin perturbation at the snRNA level.

literature_claim: Loss or haploinsufficiency of BAZ1B can broadly perturb gene expression and development in neural progenitors, neural crest and whole-animal settings.
main_caveats: Self-transcript loss is an imperfect proxy for indels; buffering is inferred from survivor nuclei after 3-4 weeks.
summary: Four groups with FDR-level loss of the Baz1b self-transcript, and two groups with nearly single-gene downstream effects, did not show broad secondary cascades.
why_it_matters: A flat downstream surface cannot be dismissed as failed guide activity: in several classes the target RNA itself fell substantially, but canonical stress or transcriptional programs remained absent.
