literature_claim: α2δ-1 and α2δ-2 are gabapentin and pregabalin targets that regulate voltage-gated calcium-channel trafficking and synaptic transmission.
main_caveats: CRISPR loss after P16 is not equivalent to acute or chronic ligand pharmacology, and α2δ-1 is the more direct neuropathic-pain target.
summary: A gabapentinoid-binding α2δ-2 loss-of-function perturbation lacked a nuclear RNA biomarker in this assay.
why_it_matters: For α2δ-2, pharmacological or genetic engagement can plausibly act through channel trafficking and synaptic electrophysiology without a large cell-autonomous transcriptomic footprint; absence of snRNA DE should not be equated with absence of functional target engagement.

literature_claim: CaVβ2 is an auxiliary MAGUK-like β subunit that binds high-voltage-activated CaV α1 channels and regulates their surface expression and gating.
main_caveats: DNA indel burden was not measured; the Cacnb2 mRNA itself was not significantly depleted, but weak or intact target transcript is expected in this platform and does not rule out edited alleles.

why_it_matters: The main result is not a hidden cell-type-specific channel program but strong buffering of an acute P16 mosaic β2-subunit loss-of-function at the level of basal snRNA-seq. That narrows the assay-visible consequence of Cacnb2 to either evoked physiology, other lineages, or combinations with other CaVβ subunits.

main_caveats: The screen captured unstimulated nuclei 3-4 weeks after editing; it did not assay an acute depolarization challenge or phospho-CREB.
summary: The β2/CaV1.2 excitation-to-transcription expectation was not recovered: activity-, CREB-, and MAPK-responsive genes including Fos, Jun, Egr1, Egr3, Npas4, Nr4a1, Arc, Bdnf, Dusp1, Dusp6, and Homer1 were all nonsignificant after Cacnb2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Because these are exactly the nuclear genes a chronic Cav1/β2 defect could have shifted if it changed basal calcium-to-CREB signaling, their absence makes the null informative rather than a simple single-nucleus readout failure.

literature_claim: CaVβ subunits regulate CaV1/CaV2 high-voltage-activated channels, CaV3 channels are β-independent, and Cacnb4 loss is neurologically active in the lethargic mouse.
main_caveats: Most CaV-family effects were zero or singletons; Cacna1c and Cacna1b, the most obvious Cav1.2/Cav2.2 pore comparators for β2, were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Represented CaV relatives mostly failed to phenocopy each other: Cacnb4, Cacna1a, Cacna1e, Cacna2d2, Cacng2, and Cacng3 had no downstream FDR<0.10 signature in matched groups, Cacna1d and Cacna2d1 gave only singleton responses, whereas the β-independent T-type channel Cacna1g produced a 14-gene response restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The related-target comparison says that lack of Cacnb2 signal is not the same as a universal inability to detect calcium-channel perturbations; the only multi-gene calcium-channel response in this target neighborhood came from a low-voltage CaV3 pore subunit rather than from an HVA β-subunit partner.

literature_claim: No specific Cacnb2 literature predicts convergence with the data-driven Safe_target, Fbxo11, Maf, Pou3f3, Psmb4, or Psmc1 comparators.
main_caveats: The neighbor calculation used weak full-surface residual correlations because Cacnb2 had no FDR<0.10 genes from which to form a robust restricted signature.
summary: Whole-surface Cacnb2 neighbors were themselves essentially null and had only tiny residual correlations, whereas unrelated Psmb4 and Psmc1 perturbations produced the two broadest DE surfaces in the same Cacnb2-measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: This rejects the data-driven neighbors as mechanistic partners and turns them into a null diagnostic: Cacnb2 lies near the flat part of the analysis universe, while the same Wilcoxon workflow detects thousands of downstream genes for proteasome perturbations in matched neuronal classes.

literature_claim: Cacnb2 loss is strongly cardiac-developmental in mice, adult cardiomyocyte deletion causes calcium-channel dysfunction, and human CACNB2 variants have been linked to L-type-current cardiac disease and altered channel function in ASD cohorts.
main_caveats: The screen lacks heart, retina, peripheral neurons, evoked activity, and DNA indel measurements; it only tests coding loss-of-function in survivor neuronal nuclei.
summary: The Cacnb2 neuronal null argues that CACNB2 cardiac and neurodevelopmental disease alleles should not be modeled as a generic, basal postmitotic neuronal loss-of-function transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Brugada/short-QT alleles act in L-type current in cardiomyocytes and autism-associated CACNB2 missense variants alter channel function; neither context was reproduced by a sparse P16 brain CRISPR perturbation, so disease follow-up should prioritize allele-specific electrophysiology and the relevant excitable lineage before expecting a durable snRNA-seq biomarker.

literature_claim: CaV beta subunits primarily regulate high-voltage-activated calcium-channel trafficking and gating through protein interactions with alpha1 subunits.
main_caveats: DNA indels and beta4 protein loss were not measured; self-transcript knockdown alone neither proves nor excludes functional knockout.
summary: Cacnb4 was a genome-wide downstream null in every recovered neuronal group, with only the Cacnb4 transcript itself reaching FDR<0.10 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This turns a superficially weak screen result into a biological statement: acute beta4 loss in sparse P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic neurons did not launch a steady-state snRNA-seq program, even where the target transcript was detectably depleted.

literature_claim: Beta4 is a preferred regulatory partner of P/Q- and N-type channels and belongs to a CaV auxiliary-subunit disease network that can be partly reshuffled in lethargic brain.
main_caveats: Correlation used whole Wilcoxon-score vectors dominated by non-significant genes because Cacnb4 had no downstream FDR genes.
summary: The Cacnb4 signature had no substantive positive or negative neighbor and did not converge with the represented voltage-gated-calcium-channel relatives.
why_it_matters: The nearest genome-wide neighbors were essentially random, and canonical relatives such as Cacnb2, Cacna1a, Cacna1g, and Cacna2d2 sat near r=0; the Cacnb4 result is not a hidden CaV-family transcriptional module.

literature_claim: P/Q and beta4 channelopathies in intact animals can be followed by thalamic T-type current elevation, GABAergic remodeling, and activity-linked beta4 nuclear transcriptional regulation.
main_caveats: The screen sampled basal nuclei, not induced spike-wave network activity or patch-clamp T-type currents.
summary: Cacnb4 loss did not recover the thalamic T-type or GABAergic-remodeling program expected from organismal absence-epilepsy models.
why_it_matters: Cacna1g, Cacna1h, Cacna1i, GABA_A-receptor subunits, Slc6a1, Kcnma1, and vesicle-release transcripts were all FDR=1.0 in Cacnb4-perturbed cells, arguing that classic spike-wave remodeling is not a cell-autonomous basal mRNA consequence of sparse postnatal beta4 loss.

main_caveats: The comparator genes are calcium-handling nodes, not beta4 paralogs; their signatures are small to moderate.
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was not globally refractory to calcium perturbation: Cacna1g, Atp2b1, and Calm1 all produced FDR-detectable DE in the same group where Cacnb4 had none downstream.
why_it_matters: This comparison rejects a pure cell-group power/readout explanation for the thalamic Cacnb4 null; other calcium-handling nodes crossed the transcriptional threshold in the matched cell group.

literature_claim: Cacnb4 loss in lethargic mice causes ataxia/seizures and impairs parallel-fibre volley and Purkinje-cell firing in adult cerebellum.
main_caveats: 308 CB GABA pools multiple cerebellar inhibitory populations and contained only 60 Cacnb4-perturbed nuclei; hindbrain neurons were outside the tissue scope.
summary: The cerebellar GABA group showed no Cacnb4 self-depletion and no downstream DE, despite the known adult lethargic cerebellar phenotype.
why_it_matters: The CB GABA null separates a strong Purkinje/parallel-fibre firing phenotype in beta4-deficient mice from a sparse, group-level, basal nuclear transcriptome readout.

main_caveats: The neighbor metric was computed on a Cadm2 profile with no FDR-significant downstream genes, so the ranking is useful only for rejection, not for discovering Cadm2 mechanism.
summary: Cadm2 had no robust data-driven signature neighbor across the full perturbation universe; its highest positive and negative Wilcoxon-z correlations were |r|<0.03 and could not be kept as FDR-supported convergence.
why_it_matters: The all-target search converts an apparently featureless Cadm2 profile into an interpretable negative: the null is not hiding a reproducible genome-wide transcriptional module similar to another perturbation in this screen.

literature_claim: CADM/SynCAM and several neurexin/neuroligin-related adhesion systems organize synaptic contacts, but several act redundantly or through subcellular contact architecture rather than a known nuclear program.
main_caveats: Cadm1, Cadm3, and Cadm4 were absent as perturbation targets, so same-family loss-of-function phenocopy could not be measured.
summary: Cadm2 did not phenocopy measurable synaptic-adhesion perturbations such as Nrxn1/2/3, Nlgn3, Cntnap1/2, Lrrtm1/3/4, Ptprt, Grid1/2, or Nectin1; those targets were themselves mostly downstream-flat or restricted to isolated one-gene effects.
why_it_matters: Related synaptic adhesion genes did not define a common cell-state module in this postnatal snRNA-seq assay. The expected CADM paralogs could not be perturbed directly, and indirect adhesion comparators supplied no shared-direction FDR overlap with Cadm2.

literature_claim: Cadm2/SynCAM2 has reported roles in axon-axon guidance, astrocyte-associated tripartite synapse formation, whole-animal energy balance, and impulsivity-related behaviors.
main_caveats: The screen does not measure synapse number, mossy-fiber ultrastructure, glutamate-transporter localization in astrocytes, adult behavior, or long-range circuit function.
summary: The screen did not recover the synapse, axon-guidance, astrocyte-interface, or behavioral circuitry programs that the Cadm2 literature would nominate; it therefore narrows the acute Cadm2 phenotype away from a large post-P16 cell-autonomous neuronal mRNA program.
why_it_matters: Human CADM2 variants and germline mouse mutants affect behavior and metabolism, but those effects are likely to arise from development, circuit physiology, astrocyte-neuron architecture, or subcellular synaptic adhesion rather than an easily detectable Cadm2-only neuronal transcriptomic state three to four weeks after sparse CRISPR editing.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: CAPS2/Cadps2 is a spatially restricted regulator of dense-core-vesicle and neurotrophin release rather than a ubiquitous neuronal transcription factor.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene passed FDR<0.10, and the target DNA indel rate was not measured.
summary: Cadps2 loss was buffered to an almost flat snRNA-seq surface: 1 downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 22 measured neuronal groups, confined to Gnl3 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
why_it_matters: The principal dataset result is not a canonical neurotrophin transcriptome but the absence of one after postmitotic sparse loss of a dense-core-vesicle priming factor.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Cadps2 biology is dominated by localized BDNF/NT-3 and neuropeptide secretion through dense-core vesicles, whereas Gnl3/nucleostemin is a nucleolar GTPase involved in stem-cell proliferation and pre-rRNA processing.
main_caveats: The mechanistic link between Caps2 perturbation and Gnl3 is not established, and a single BH-significant transcript can be a false discovery.
summary: The only Cadps2 DEG, Gnl3, points to a solitary nucleolar/ribosome-biogenesis marker and is uncoupled from BDNF/NT-3, Trk, immediate-early, Pvalb, and neuropeptide-cargo transcripts.
why_it_matters: It prevents interpreting the 009 response as a recovered BDNF or dense-core-vesicle cargo program; the dataset supports at most a weak Cadps2-Gnl3 sentinel rather than a broad neurotrophin transcriptional cascade.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: CAPS2 intersects with dense-core-vesicle priming and exocytosis machinery, and CAPS proteins are vesicle-associated neuronal secretion regulators.
main_caveats: Comparisons are restricted by the single Cadps2 DEG and by the absence of Cadps, Bdnf, Ntf3, Syt1, Snap25, Vamp2, and Stx1a as perturbation targets.
summary: Measured neurotrophin-receptor and vesicle-release perturbations did not phenocopy Cadps2 in 009: Stxbp1 had an Ankrd13d-only response and Ntrk2/Ntrk3/Unc13/Cplx/Syt2/Stx1b/Dnm1/Rab3gap1 perturbations had no 009 FDR<0.10 signature.
why_it_matters: The only Cadps2 transcriptomic effect is not a generic consequence of perturbing Trk signaling or core synaptic-vesicle release; related pathway targets either respond elsewhere or remain flat without sharing Gnl3.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Neighbor ranking used the only Cadps2 FDR gene, so it has one effective feature and is hypothesis-generating only.
summary: The data-driven Gnl3 neighbors were rejected as true Cadps2 signature neighbors: the top same-direction and opposite-direction ranks for Gnl3 in 009 were all sub-FDR.
why_it_matters: The full parquet did not reveal a robust, non-textbook perturbation that converges with or directly opposes the one-gene Cadps2 response.

literature_claim: Calmodulin is encoded by three identical-protein paralogs but their transcripts are differentially regulated in rodent brain.
main_caveats: The 007 and 052 calls each rest on one downstream gene, and engagement is inferred from RNA rather than DNA indels.
summary: Acute Calm1 loss was not a pan-neuronal transcriptional perturbation; only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had a multi-gene response, while 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba had singleton responses.
why_it_matters: Calm1 mRNA was reduced in many recovered neuronal groups, so the restricted response argues that a single calmodulin gene can be phenotypically buffered in most postmitotic neurons and only exposes a small transcriptional state in selected classes.

literature_claim: Ca2+/CaM regulates CaM kinases and PMCA pumps, pathways that could couple calcium signals to plasticity and calcium clearance.
main_caveats: Program naming is based on only 20 FDR<0.10 genes; Atp2b1 has a small absolute logFC despite robust FDR.
summary: The principal 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response mixed Rasgrp2, Resp18, Vamp1, Tuba1a/Tuba1b, Coro6, Eno2, Fabp5, Tecr, Peg3, Mest, Maged1, and Aifm3 induction with Atp2b1 and Car4 repression.
why_it_matters: The signature is more consistent with a small thalamic secretory, cytoskeletal, lipid-metabolic, and calcium-clearance adjustment than with collapse of all calmodulin-dependent signaling.

literature_claim: CALM1, CALM2, and CALM3 encode identical calmodulin proteins but show distinct brain mRNA regulation.
main_caveats: Calm2 guide activity at the RNA level was weak, so the strongest contrast is between Calm1 and the better-engaged Calm3 guides.
summary: Calm2 and Calm3 did not phenocopy Calm1: Calm2 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes and Calm3 had three non-overlapping singleton genes.
why_it_matters: The three loci encode the same calmodulin protein, so their different Perturb-seq surfaces show that postnatal single-gene LoF is dominated by paralog dosage, expression context, or guide engagement rather than by a shared calmodulin-protein depletion state.

literature_claim: Calmodulin signals through CaMK, calcineurin/NFAT, calcium pumps, and ion-channel effectors.
main_caveats: Only pathway genes present as perturbation targets can be rejected, and some canonical nodes such as Cacna1c, Camkk1/2, Camk4, Ppp3cb, and Nfatc1/2/4 were not represented.
summary: CaM effector perturbations were mostly flat or divergent; Atp2b1 and Ppp3r1 responded in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but shared almost none of the Calm1 genes.
why_it_matters: Atp2b1 is a Calm1 downstream gene, yet direct Atp2b1 loss induced Fos/Nr4a1/Vgf/Cck/Ptprn rather than the Rasgrp2/Peg3/Resp18 Calm1 module, separating a PMCA perturbation from the Calm1 state.

main_caveats: Comparisons were restricted to Calm1 FDR<0.10 features; some neighbors have thousands of DE genes, so shared features may be embedded in pleiotropic responses.
summary: The top data-driven signature neighbors were Zbtb7a, Cic, and Huwe1, while Camta1, Tpr, and Prpf6 were the strongest inverse neighbors.
why_it_matters: The Calm1 151 module sits in the same gene-expression space as chromatin/transcriptional perturbations and opposite to several broad RNA or nuclear perturbations, not next to the textbook calmodulin pathway.

literature_claim: Calmodulinopathy is caused largely by CALM1-3 missense variants with early cardiac and occasional neurological manifestations.
main_caveats: The assay did not introduce patient alleles and excluded cardiomyocytes, the dominant clinical disease tissue.
summary: The weak transcriptional consequence of Calm1 LoF supports separating postnatal neuronal single-gene haploinsufficiency from dominant calmodulinopathy alleles.
why_it_matters: Published CALM1-3 disease is dominated by heterozygous missense variants that poison Ca2+ binding or channel regulation; this LOF screen did not reproduce a broad neuronal Ca2+-stress or channel-response program.

main_caveats: Resp18 recurrence is two cell groups only, with one singleton signature in 007.
summary: Resp18 was the only recurrent downstream gene, up in both 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Resp18 provides the one cross-glutamatergic marker of the otherwise sparse Calm1 response surface and can anchor validation of the small responder set.

literature_claim: Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent kinases and calcineurin can connect calcium signals to CREB/NFAT-dependent gene expression.
main_caveats: Absence is judged at whole-gene snRNA resolution and cannot exclude acute phosphorylation or electrophysiological phenotypes.
summary: Calm1 loss did not activate a classical Fos/Junb/Arc/Npas4/Egr/Nr4a activity-dependent transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: The screen would have captured a robust secondary nuclear response to disrupted calcium signaling; its absence makes the null surface informative rather than a simple snRNA-seq readout failure.

literature_claim: Calm1, Calm2 and Calm3 are distinct genes that contribute to the same Ca2+-binding calmodulin protein, which regulates enzymes, phosphatases and ion channels.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation and total CaM protein were not assayed; the mostly flat Calm2 mRNA self-response is expected in this platform and does not prove lack of editing.
summary: P16 mosaic Calm2 loss produced no BH-significant downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Calmodulin sits atop many Ca2+-dependent enzymes and channels, so a pan-calmodulin defect would be expected to perturb activity-regulated programs. The observed all-zero downstream surface instead shows that single-locus Calm2 perturbation is strongly buffered in postmitotic neurons, most plausibly by continued Calm1 and Calm3 production of the same protein.

literature_claim: Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent kinases and Ca2+-CREB signaling couple neuronal calcium entry to plasticity and activity-regulated genes including BDNF.
main_caveats: The comparison is at the RNA-signature level; NMDAR subunits are only pathway neighbors, not CaM paralogs.
summary: Calm2 did not trigger the Ca2+/CaM-activity transcriptional genes that are recovered after NMDA-receptor perturbations in the same DE universe.
why_it_matters: The null is not explained by snRNA-seq being unable to see a neuronal Ca2+-signaling response: Grin1, Grin2a and Grin2b perturbations yielded activity/synaptic genes such as Nptx2, Bdnf, Ptgs2, Rgs2, Jun, Scg2, Vgf and Camk2n1, whereas the same pre-specified panel never reached FDR<0.10 after Calm2 loss.

literature_claim: The three Calm genes encode indistinguishable calmodulin protein but can be differentially regulated at the transcript level.
main_caveats: The comparison may include guide-efficiency and expression differences; only Calm1, not Calm2/3, produced more than three downstream calls.
summary: The identical calmodulin-coding loci do not form a shared FDR signature: Calm1 has a sparse thalamic response, Calm3 only three singleton downstream calls, and Calm2 has none.
why_it_matters: The paralog contrast turns a flat Calm2 surface into a family-level result: transcript identity at the protein level does not guarantee equivalent gRNA engagement or equivalent downstream transcriptional consequences for a single locus in juvenile neurons.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Score correlations were computed on genome-wide weak Wilcoxon statistics rather than on a Calm2 FDR signature, because Calm2 had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes.
summary: A whole-universe signed-Wilcoxon neighbor search found no meaningful positive or inverse Calm2 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top score correlations across the 22 shared Calm2 cell groups were only r=0.031 for Glis3 and r=-0.016 for Flrt3 among fully matched targets; these apparent neighbors have singleton or absent FDR signatures and were rejected as convergence partners.

literature_claim: Calmodulinopathy is caused by CALM1/2/3 sequence variants, with most curated variants being heterozygous missense variants thought to act dominantly and producing severe early arrhythmia phenotypes.
main_caveats: No cardiomyocytes were assayed, and no pathogenic missense allele was introduced.
summary: The neuronal Calm2 LoF null is consistent with calmodulinopathy being mainly a dominant missense, lineage-biased disease model rather than simple Calm2 haploinsufficiency.
why_it_matters: It cautions against interpreting a sparse CRISPR LoF profile as absence of risk from pathogenic CALM2 alleles: the screen removes one normal transcript in mouse brain neurons, while the clinical literature centers on heterozygous CALM1-3 missense mutations that poison CaM regulation of excitable channels, especially in the heart.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Calmodulin is a major neuronal Ca2+ sensor, but vertebrates encode the identical CaM protein from three non-allelic genes that create a redundant pool.
main_caveats: True DNA editing and CaM protein abundance were not measured; sparse CRISPR of Calm3 alone is not a triple-CaM knockout.
summary: Postnatal Calm3 knockdown produced a detectable Calm3 mRNA decrease in most measured neuronal groups but only three robust downstream DE genes across the entire 22-group response surface.
why_it_matters: The first-order finding is buffering: a single calmodulin gene can be transcriptionally depleted in juvenile postmitotic neurons without generating a broad Ca2+/CaM transcriptional collapse, consistent with a three-gene identical-protein CaM system.

literature_claim: Neurochondrin negatively regulates Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent CaMKII phosphorylation, and CaMKII is an abundant neuronal CaM effector.
main_caveats: Single-gene DE only; Ncdn protein and phospho-CaMKII were not assayed.
summary: Ncdn was selectively induced downstream of Calm3 in Pvalb interneurons.
why_it_matters: Ncdn is a CaMKII-adjacent neuronal gene; its isolated induction nominates a Pvalb-specific CaM/CaMKII feedback edge rather than a pan-neuronal stress or immediate-early response.

literature_claim: Calmodulin directly regulates Cav1.2 gating, and dominant CALM variants can cause calmodulinopathy through disturbed ion-channel regulation.
main_caveats: The screen measures Cacna1c mRNA, not Cav1.2 current or Ca2+-dependent inactivation; the disease literature is dominated by cardiac missense variants rather than neuronal Calm3 loss-of-function.
summary: Cacna1c was selectively reduced downstream of Calm3 in Sst interneurons.
why_it_matters: Cacna1c encodes Cav1.2, a direct CaM-regulated L-type Ca2+ channel; a slow decrease in the pore-forming channel transcript is a plausible channel-abundance adaptation to altered CaM control, but it is confined to Sst nuclei in this assay.

literature_claim: Slc38a1 is a sodium-coupled glutamine transporter that can regulate neurotransmitter filling and synaptic function.
main_caveats: The strongest functional Slc38a1 evidence is from GABAergic neurotransmission, whereas the Calm3 hit is in a glutamatergic hypothalamic/mammillary group.
summary: Slc38a1 was selectively reduced downstream of Calm3 in the hypothalamic CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic group.
why_it_matters: This nominates amino-acid and neurotransmitter-precursor transport as the only robust non-canonical Calm3 output; because Slc38a1 couples glutamine uptake to transmitter metabolism, it is a concrete marker for validating altered neuronal metabolite supply after Calm3 depletion.

literature_claim: Calm1, Calm2, and Calm3 encode identical vertebrate calmodulin protein but have non-allelic genomic organization and independent regulation.
main_caveats: Calm2 self-transcript was not robustly depleted in these three groups, so the negative Calm2 comparison is weaker than the Calm1 comparison.
summary: The identical-protein paralogs Calm1 and Calm2 did not phenocopy Calm3 on the Ncdn, Cacna1c, or Slc38a1 anchors.
why_it_matters: The matched perturbations separate transcript-source genetics from CaM protein identity: in this mosaic P16 brain assay, the Calm3 anchor genes are not the interchangeable consequence of lowering any one calmodulin transcript.

literature_claim: CaMKII and calcineurin are major neuronal targets of Ca2+/calmodulin.
main_caveats: Loss of an effector subunit is not mechanistically identical to reducing CaM, and this comparison is restricted to steady-state snRNA-seq anchors.
summary: CaMKII and calcineurin subunit perturbations represented in the screen failed to reproduce the Calm3 anchor genes in matched responder groups.
why_it_matters: The Calm3 signature is not simply the transcriptional mirror of losing a major CaM effector such as Camk2a, Camk2b, Camk2g, Ppp3ca, or Ppp3r1; it is more consistent with either a calmodulin-pool effect or proximal signaling changes that are not encoded as steady-state effector-transcript abundance.

main_caveats: The antineighbor was found on only three Calm3 anchors and should not be interpreted as a direct biochemical relationship between Psmb4 and Calm3.
summary: The strongest FDR-supported data-driven antineighbor was Psmb4, which reversed two Calm3 anchors instead of converging on them.
why_it_matters: Psmb4's opposite Ncdn and Slc38a1 directions argue that the Calm3 anchors are not merely generic low-cell-count artifacts; a broad non-CaM perturbation drives those same coordinates the other way.

literature_claim: CaMKIIα is a forebrain excitatory synaptic kinase required for NMDA-receptor-dependent plasticity and adult Camk2a function can rescue electrophysiological phenotypes.
main_caveats: The four-gene FDR signature is small and engagement was not assayed by indel sequencing; the self-transcript was weakly negative but not FDR-significant.
summary: Camk2a loss generated a very sparse transcriptional response: 4 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, all confined to two cortical glutamatergic groups, with no FDR signal in 20 other measured groups.
why_it_matters: The result localizes the detectable nuclear-RNA consequence of acute postnatal Camk2a perturbation to cortical projection neurons and shows that the canonical synaptic kinase can be largely buffered at the whole-transcriptome level.

literature_claim: Voltage-gated sodium-channel β subunits, including β1/SCN1B, regulate channel function as well as neuronal adhesion and development.
main_caveats: The channel interpretation rests on a single down-regulated β-subunit transcript; no sodium-channel α subunit crossed FDR<0.10 in this Camk2a group.
summary: L4/5 IT cortical neurons carried a three-gene mixed signature, with Pnisr and Fhl1 increased and the sodium-channel β1 subunit gene Scn1b decreased.
why_it_matters: Scn1b down-regulation nominates an excitability and cell-adhesion axis as a candidate secondary marker of Camk2a loss in one IT cortical compartment, while Pnisr and Fhl1 currently behave as single-gene markers rather than a recurrent pathway.

literature_claim: Rasal1 has C2-domain calcium sensitivity, RasGAP activity, neuronal membrane translocation after calcium elevation, interaction with CaMKII, and effects on NMDA-mediated CaMKII phosphorylation in hippocampal culture.
main_caveats: This is a one-gene L5 ET effect with 38 perturbed cells; the data measure Rasal1 RNA, not Ras-GTP, Rasal1 localization, or CaMKII phosphorylation.
summary: L5 extratelencephalic cortical neurons down-regulated Rasal1 after Camk2a perturbation.
why_it_matters: Rasal1 is a calcium-responsive RasGAP that can bind CaMKII and modulate NMDA/CaMKII signaling in developing hippocampal neurons, so its selective loss in L5 ET cells suggests a local feedback from the CaMKII lesion onto a calcium-Ras gate.

literature_claim: NMDA-receptor calcium influx activates CaMKII, which controls AMPA-receptor trafficking during LTP.
main_caveats: The mismatch is transcriptomic; it does not test acute phosphorylation of AMPARs or synaptic potentiation.
summary: Camk2a did not phenocopy upstream NMDA-receptor subunits even though Grin2a and Grin2b were among the strongest matched cortical comparators.
why_it_matters: The assay could detect Bdnf/Nptx2/Scg2 and Vgf/Nr4a1/Npas4/Egr3-like cortical activity programs after NMDA-receptor subunit perturbation, but those programs were absent at FDR<0.10 after Camk2a loss; NMDAR subunit loss therefore has transcriptional consequences outside the acute CaMKIIα node, or stronger than the node sampled by this perturbation.

literature_claim: CaMKIIα and CaMKIIβ, their calmodulin activators, NMDA receptors, AMPA receptors, and PSD scaffolds all intersect excitatory postsynaptic plasticity but have distinct molecular functions and isoform distributions.
main_caveats: Only comparator genes represented in the parquet were tested, and the comparison is at single-nucleus RNA rather than kinase or receptor physiology.
summary: The Camk2a RNA signature did not converge with CaMKII paralogs, calmodulins, Dlg4, or AMPAR subunits.
why_it_matters: Camk2b and Camk2g were directly measurable and were nearly silent, while calmodulin, NMDAR, AMPAR, and PSD-95 perturbations had either different FDR genes or no DE; this rejects a simple same-pathway or same-paralog transcriptomic module for acute Camk2a LoF.

main_caveats: The correlation is diluted by a biologically sparse signature; it is useful mainly as evidence against a large shared transcriptome.
summary: Camk2a lacked a strong data-driven transcriptomic neighbor in the complete perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The closest whole-surface neighbor was Grin2b with r=0.0357 and the most anti-correlated neighbor was Kcnb1 with r=-0.0264; these near-zero correlations and zero FDR-anchor overlap show that the four-gene Camk2a signature is idiosyncratic rather than a member of a broad recurrent RNA module.

main_caveats: Single downstream gene at FDR 0.051763 with 86 perturbed cells; Tmem25 is not by itself a pathway-level signature.
summary: Camk2b loss produced a nearly flat basal snRNA-seq phenotype: across 22 recovered cell groups, 145 MH-LH TH Glut was the only effect group and Tmem25 was its single downstream DEG at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The main biological result is not a broad CaMKII stress, synapse, or activity transcriptome; it is an isolated, low-dimensional response, so the screen argues for buffering of acute juvenile Camk2b loss on the basal nuclear-RNA axis.

literature_claim: CaMKIIbeta has a distinctive F-actin-targeting structural role within CaMKII biology that is not simply interchangeable with CaMKIIalpha.
main_caveats: Camk2d was not represented as a measured target in the queried comparator set; the contrasts are transcriptional, not phosphoproteomic or structural spine measurements.
summary: The measured CaMKII paralogs did not phenocopy Camk2b: Camk2a had only four downstream FDR<0.10 genes, Camk2g had none, and their whole-transcriptome score correlations with Camk2b were only 0.014810 and 0.021282.
why_it_matters: Even same-family CRISPR loss did not define a shared CaMKII mRNA module in postmitotic neurons, supporting the interpretation that CaMKII alpha/beta/gamma biology is being buffered or displaced away from bulk basal transcription rather than missed only because the wrong paralog was targeted.

literature_claim: Ca2+/calmodulin activates CaMKII, and activated CaMKII binds the GluN2B/NR2B cytoplasmic tail downstream of NMDAR Ca2+ entry to localize and maintain CaMKII activity at synapses.
main_caveats: The NMDAR subunit signatures are themselves cell-group-specific; they demonstrate detectability of receptor-linked RNA programs, not that every NMDAR biochemical effector must change transcript abundance after Camk2b CRISPR.
summary: Perturbing calmodulins and NMDAR/PSD targets did not share Camk2b's sparse response; Grin2a, Grin2b, and Grin1 generated real transcriptional signatures in matched groups, whereas Calm1-3, Grin1/2a/2b/2d/3a, Dlg4, and Syngap1 shared no FDR<0.10 genes with Camk2b.
why_it_matters: The screen could detect receptor-proximal glutamatergic effects, including L2/3 IT CTX Glut responses to Grin2a and Grin2b, so Camk2b flatness is selective uncoupling from the Ca2+/CaM-NMDAR/PSD RNA programs that were assay-detectable for upstream nodes.

main_caveats: Neighbor calling used whole-DE Wilcoxon z-score vectors; for an almost-null target, all rank positions are small-effect and should be treated as negative controls rather than mechanistic convergence.
summary: Unbiased whole-universe score-vector comparison found no strong positive or negative Camk2b neighbor: the best positive real targets were Kcnc1 and Taok1 at r≈0.031, and the strongest negative real targets, Fbxo11 and Ranbp2, were only r≈-0.02.
why_it_matters: There is no hidden recurrent transcriptional module that would rescue the isolated Tmem25 hit; the Camk2b surface is closer to a buffered signature than to either a convergent disease module or a coherent inverse state.

literature_claim: Mouse Camk2b mutant phenotypes include developmental and motor requirements, and de novo CAMK2A/CAMK2B variants cause human neurodevelopmental disease through altered CaMKII function.
main_caveats: This screen contains only CRISPR loss-of-function assignments and no rescue, electrophysiology, behavior, or variant knock-in readout.
summary: The flat CRISPR-LoF RNA phenotype does not contradict CAMK2B disease genetics; it says that sparse juvenile loss is a poor proxy for the activity-dependent, developmental, and allele-specific CaMKII mechanisms implicated by human missense variants.
why_it_matters: This is a therapeutic interpretation warning: absence of basal snRNA-seq toxicity after partial mosaic loss should not be read as evidence that reducing CAMK2B activity is biologically silent in developing circuits or in gain-/loss-of-function variant contexts.

literature_claim: A germline Camk2g knockout can affect motor and innate behaviors while showing limited hippocampus-dependent learning and plasticity phenotypes in adult mice.
main_caveats: DNA indels and CAMK2G protein were not measured; the one significant transcript change was Camk2g itself in 155 MB Glut, not a downstream program.
summary: Camk2g loss of function produced no downstream gene at FDR<0.10 in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: This makes the main phenotype a buffered steady-state transcriptome rather than a missed narrow pathway: broad cortical, hippocampal/amygdalar, thalamic/hypothalamic, midbrain, and GABAergic groups were measured and all were flat downstream of the self transcript.

literature_claim: γCaMKII knockdown prevents stimulated nuclear CaM/CaMKIV/pCREB signaling and c-Fos induction, while CaMKII is a Ca2+/CaM decoder at glutamatergic synapses.
main_caveats: The assay was not an evoked-depolarization or phospho-protein assay, so it tests persistence of that program at baseline rather than acute excitation-transcription coupling.
summary: The expected activity-dependent CREB/immediate-early-gene axis was absent from the basal Camk2g snRNA signature.
why_it_matters: γCaMKII can relay Ca2+/CaM to the nucleus during stimulation, but neither Fos/Jun/Egr/Npas4/Arc/Bdnf/Crem nor CAMKII/CaM compensatory transcripts became significant after the P16 mosaic perturbation.

literature_claim: CAMK2A, CAMK2B, CAMK2G, and CAMK2D encode homologous CaMKII isoforms that can participate in related Ca2+/CaM biology, and analogous CAMK2A/B Arg/Lys-Pro gain-of-function mutants can disrupt neurodevelopment.
main_caveats: Camk2d was not a perturbation target in the parquet; all isoform comparisons are loss-of-function rather than pathogenic gain-of-function alleles.
summary: CaMKII-family knockouts did not converge on a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptomic module.
why_it_matters: Camk2a, Camk2b, and Camkmt were directly represented and had only 4, 1, and 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across Camk2g-matched groups, so the flat Camk2g result is not simply hiding a CaMKII-paralog expression-response program.

literature_claim: Ca2+ entry, CaM, CaMKII, and CREB occupy the same activity-dependent signaling neighborhood around synaptic plasticity and excitation-transcription coupling.
main_caveats: These are pathway-neighbor rather than same-protein perturbations; shared-direction overlap cannot occur because Camk2g has no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
summary: NMDAR, calmodulin, calcineurin, and CREB perturbations can produce FDR-detectable signatures in the same cell-group universe where Camk2g is flat.
why_it_matters: The matched comparator surface argues that the lack of Camk2g downstream DE is target-specific: Grin1, Grin2b, Grin2a, Calm1, Creb1, and Ppp3r1 yielded 131, 78, 29, 22, 21, and 14 downstream genes, respectively, across Camk2g-matched groups.

This ties the neuronal abundance program to co-transcriptional RNA processing and chromatin-coupled elongation rather than to a generic CDK perturbation, because Cdk8 was flat in all matched groups.

literature_claim: AFG3L2/SPG7 annotate mitochondrial proteostasis and AHI1-positive gene sets annotate ciliary or centrosomal biology, but this organelle block has not been a canonical reported Cdk13 output.
main_caveats: The organelle label is inferred from the identities of recurrent genes; organelle function was not assayed directly.
summary: The larger subcortical signatures coupled RNA-processing changes to repression of mitochondrial, centrosomal, and ciliary maintenance genes.
why_it_matters: Cdk13 loss repeatedly down-regulated Coq2, Spg7, Afg3l2, Prkn, Ahi1, Dzip3, Cep350, Sclt1, and Tmem260 in the same cell groups that carried the strongest Bend6/Amy1/Rnpc3 response, nominating organelle maintenance rather than a proteasome or ISR rebound as the main secondary arm of this perturbation.

literature_claim: Cyclin K/CDK12 and CDK12/13 inhibition can reduce DNA-repair and cell-cycle transcripts, and Cdk12/Cdk13 depletion can affect Cdk5-linked axon elongation in neuronal differentiation models.
main_caveats: The assay would miss intron retention or alternative last-exon usage that leaves total gene counts unchanged.
summary: Postmitotic neuronal Cdk13 loss did not recover the proliferative CDK12/13 DNA-damage, G2/M, or Cdk5-axon expression programs predicted from dividing-cell and differentiation models.
why_it_matters: Brca1/Fanci/Rad51/Fanca/Polh and Ccnb1/E2f3 were measured but never FDR-significant, and Cdk5 was also unchanged; the P16 snRNA surface therefore separates the stable mRNA program of Cdk13 loss in mature neurons from the DDR/cell-cycle consequences of stronger CDK12/13 inhibition in proliferating cells.

main_caveats: Defined only over the Cdk13 FDR feature set; exact dual-FDR overlaps were absent or minimal.
summary: The strongest Cdk13 anti-neighbors were not CDK12/13 pathway members and were supported by restricted anti-correlation rather than exact shared FDR genes.
why_it_matters: Gigyf2, Robo2, Oprl1, Gabra3, and Syn1 were the five most negative 221-feature cosine neighbors, yet four had no exact FDR<0.10 overlap with the Cdk13 signature. This makes the negative neighborhood hypothesis-generating and argues against treating the Cdk13 state as the simple inverse of a known synaptic or receptor perturbation.

literature_claim: CDK8/19 Mediator kinases regulate transcriptional outputs in a context-dependent rather than universally basal manner.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not assayed; one dopaminergic group had no Cdk8 rows.
summary: Cdk8 had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 recovered neuronal groups despite measurable target rows and 28 to 192 perturbed nuclei per group.
why_it_matters: The primary phenotype is a broad postnatal neuronal transcriptional zero; the flat self-transcript should be treated as expected in this indel-based Perturb-seq design, not as proof of failed perturbation.

literature_claim: CDK8 kinase activity can be necessary for β-catenin target transcription in β-catenin-hyperactive colon-cancer cells.
main_caveats: The neuronal state was not Wnt-ligand-stimulated and the strongest Wnt evidence came from one thalamic class.

why_it_matters: This refines the CDK8-Wnt relationship by showing that a postmitotic thalamic β-catenin/Tcf7l2 transcriptional state can be CDK8 independent in this basal juvenile-brain setting.

literature_claim: CDK8, MED13, and MED13L are linked through the Mediator kinase module and through overlapping developmental-disorder genetics.
main_caveats: Cdk19, Ccnc, Med12, and Med12l were not represented as perturbation targets, and Med13 self-mRNA was not significantly depleted.
summary: Med13 and Med13l failed to phenocopy the Cdk8 null: Med13 had only 15 DE genes and Med13l only 2 across their surfaces, compared with 0 for Cdk8.
why_it_matters: Same-family comparison rejects a model in which every sampled Mediator kinase-module component yields a common postnatal neuronal transcriptome.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed on full score vectors rather than restricted FDR genes because Cdk8 had no FDR genes.
summary: Data-driven Cdk8 signature neighbors were near-zero correlations; Dctn1, Drd4, Arhgef9, Ppargc1a, Dscam, and Smc1a were kept as measured comparators but rejected as substantive Cdk8 phenocopies.

literature_claim: CDK8 is a transcription-regulating kinase within the Mediator kinase module.
main_caveats: The comparator genes are not all in the CDK8 kinase module and therefore control for assay detectability rather than testing direct biochemical redundancy.
summary: Other transcriptional or chromatin regulators, including Brd4, Phf12, Chd8, and Med23, produced clear postmitotic DE signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Cdk8 remained flat.
why_it_matters: The matched-cell comparison argues that an acute P16-to-P37-44 snRNA-seq assay can detect transcription-regulator loss in this cell class, so Cdk8's zero is gene-specific rather than inherent to the readout.

literature_claim: Cdkal1 is a tRNALys(UUU) ms2t6A methylthiotransferase whose biology should manifest through translation fidelity rather than a receptor-like signaling cascade.
main_caveats: The assay measures RNA, not tRNA modification or mistranslation, and DNA indel fractions were not measured.
summary: Cdkal1 loss-of-function was almost transcriptionally silent in the P16-to-P37/44 neuronal screen, with only two downstream FDR<0.10 gene-cell-group events among 22 recovered cell groups.
why_it_matters: The finding refines the expected Cdkal1 phenotype from a generic tRNA-decoding lesion to a context-limited response: most juvenile postmitotic neurons did not mount a detectable stress, mitochondrial, or translational transcriptome after acute mosaic perturbation.

literature_claim: GGPS1 supplies GGPP, the C20 isoprenoid used for geranylgeranylation of proteins.
main_caveats: Single FDR-significant gene in a 44-cell perturbation group; no other mevalonate genes were significant.
summary: The only significant MH-LH/TH glutamatergic response was Ggps1 induction.
why_it_matters: Ggps1 is the enzyme that produces geranylgeranyl diphosphate for protein prenylation; its isolated up-regulation suggests a very small, cell-restricted isoprenoid-prenylation compensation rather than a broad tRNA or ER-stress program.

direction: Eef1a2 up in Cdkal1 and Uba5
literature_claim: EEF1A2 functions in neuronal translation elongation, whereas UBA5 activates the UFMylation cascade and UBA5 variants can cause encephalopathy.
main_caveats: The shared signal is one gene; Uba5 had hundreds of other DE genes in MB Glut that Cdkal1 did not share.
summary: The sole MB Glut Cdkal1 hit, Eef1a2, converged with Uba5 induction of Eef1a2 but not with the larger Uba5 program.
why_it_matters: EEF1A2 is a neuronal translation-elongation factor, so its up-regulation is the most direct transcriptomic hint that Cdkal1 perturbation touched translation homeostasis; convergence with Uba5 is restricted to this node and therefore remains hypothesis-generating.

direction: expected ISR/UPR absent in Cdkal1; present after Elp1
literature_claim: Cdkal1-deficient beta cells are hypersensitive to ER stress, and Elongator-dependent tRNA modification is linked to stress and neurological biology.
main_caveats: The experiment did not expose neurons to high translation load, high-fat diet, or endocrine secretory demand.
summary: The beta-cell-like ER/ISR response predicted from severe Cdkal1-dependent mistranslation was absent from every measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: Atf4, Asns, Herpud1, Chac1, Hspa5, Xbp1 and related amino-acid-response genes never reached even FDR 0.20 under Cdkal1, while Elp1 perturbation activated Atf4-Asns-Herpud1 in matched 145 MH-LH TH Glut cells. The null is therefore not simply an snRNA-seq readout failure for ISR genes.

literature_claim: Multiple tRNA-modification enzymes, including Elongator, NSUN2, ALKBH8, and TRMT1, are implicated in neurological or neurodevelopmental disease.
main_caveats: The comparator analysis is limited to targets and cell groups recovered in this parquet; several related enzymes were not represented.
summary: Represented tRNA-modification disease relatives did not phenocopy Cdkal1 in matched cell groups.
why_it_matters: Elp1 was a broad ISR responder and drove Eef1a2 down in MB Glut; Elp2 was weaker; Alkbh8 and Nsun2 were completely flat and Trmt1 nearly flat. The screen separates tRNA-modification enzymes by target, complex, and neuronal context rather than collapsing them into one shared transcriptomic syndrome.

main_caveats: Correlation on a nearly flat signature is useful mainly for rejecting phenocopy, not for asserting mechanism.
summary: Cdkal1 had no robust whole-transcriptome signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The strongest non-safe positive and negative score correlations across roughly 0.15-0.37 million matched rows were only +0.039 and -0.030, so the data-driven neighbors nominated before literature were rejected as broad phenocopies.

why_it_matters: The result separates CDKL5's known kinase- and synapse-level biology from a broad autonomous nuclear RNA response: the P16-to-P37/44 sparse knockout can leave essentially every NeuN+ cell group transcriptionally quiet while still not proving that the cells are physiologically normal.

literature_claim: Postdevelopmental Cdkl5 loss alters adult forebrain/hippocampal synaptic physiology, NMDAR signaling, and BDNF/TrkB-associated circuit activity.
main_caveats: A self-transcript drop reports mRNA level, not the rate of frameshift indels or CDKL5 protein depletion.

why_it_matters: This directly demonstrates that self-RNA depletion and downstream transcriptomic output are uncoupled for Cdkl5 in at least one high-cell-count aggregate; the near-flat self-transcript in other groups therefore should not be read as proof that no LoF indels occurred.

literature_claim: CDD is Rett-like and clinically overlaps the developmental and epileptic encephalopathy differential, but the record does not require MECP2-, MEF2C-, UBE3A-, or sodium-channel-like transcriptional consequences after Cdkl5 loss.
main_caveats: Comparators were compared by FDR<0.10 gene counts, not by matched protein, electrophysiology, or behavioral assays.
summary: Cdkl5 did not phenocopy Rett/DEE-neighbor perturbations that were detectable in the same matched cell groups.
why_it_matters: The clinically related gene set is not interchangeable in this acute neuronal snRNA-seq assay: Mef2c and Mecp2 created multi-gene responses, Scn1a/Scn2a created small responses, whereas Cdkl5, Ube3a, and Scn8a were quiet, arguing against one generic DEE transcriptome.

literature_claim: Cdkl5 models implicate aberrant NMDAR signaling, BDNF/TrkB epileptogenesis after dense adult forebrain glutamatergic ablation, and AKT/GSK3β signaling in newborn-neuron dendritic growth and survival.
main_caveats: The adult BDNF/TrkB phenotype is a dense forebrain network manipulation, whereas this screen sparsely perturbs individual neurons and reads nuclear RNA.
summary: Cdkl5 was transcriptionally uncoupled from NMDAR/BDNF-TrkB and AKT/GSK3/mTOR pathway perturbations that were readily measurable in the same analysis universe.
why_it_matters: The result warns against treating Cdkl5 loss as a linear mRNA-level proxy for NMDAR, TrkB, or mTOR signaling: Tsc2, Grin2b, Grin2a, Gsk3b, Mtor, Camk2a, Ntrk2, Rac1, and Pak1 perturbations produced downstream DE in matched groups but Cdkl5 did not recover the corresponding transcript panel.

main_caveats: The ranking uses a restricted, mostly null Cdkl5 score vector; tiny cosines should be treated as rejection of convergence, not as mechanistic similarity.

why_it_matters: Even the best data-driven neighbors had signed-Wilcoxon-score cosines near zero; Kcnb1 and Dstyk were the top positive neighbors and Dlgap4 and Grin2b the top negative neighbors, but the magnitudes were too small to support a shared pathway module.

literature_claim: Lst1 can be part of immune/phagocytosis-associated microglial signatures in plaque-bearing mouse brain regions.
main_caveats: Only one gene passed FDR<0.10 and it did so at FDR=0.09155; the preparation is NeuN-enriched and the Lst1 signal could reflect a rare transcriptomic state or unremoved cell/nuclear contamination rather than a broad Cdkn2a mechanism.
summary: Cdkn2a loss produced an ultra-sparse, cell-group-restricted response: a single up-regulated Lst1 hit in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: Lst1 is more naturally a myeloid/phagocytic immune marker than a neuronal RB/E2F target, so the one FDR<0.10 gene should be treated as an exploratory hippocampal/limbic immune-adjacent sentinel rather than as a canonical Cdkn2a program.

literature_claim: The Cdkn2a locus couples p16INK4a to CDK4/6-RB-E2F control and ARF to the MDM2-p53 arm, so Cdkn2a loss is expected to matter most where G1/S or senescence checkpoints are engaged.
main_caveats: E2f1 and Trp53 CRISPR surfaces also lack DNA indel validation; Cdk4, Cdk6, Rb1, Mdm2, and Mdm4 were not perturbation targets in the parquet and were tested only as Cdkn2a downstream transcripts.
summary: The Cdkn2a perturbation did not derepress RB/E2F cell-cycle genes, suppress p53-effectors, or generate a coherent SASP-like module, and the directly measurable E2f1 and Trp53 perturbations were themselves flat.
why_it_matters: This separates the postnatal neuronal Cdkn2a result from the tumor-suppressor circuitry that makes CDKN2A loss potent in dividing and senescent cells; the absent program is shared by pathway comparators rather than being an isolated Cdkn2a failure.

main_caveats: The cosine calculation is dominated by Cdkn2a null coordinates; Mef2d and Sin3a are retained as measured comparator outcomes, not as mechanistic relatives of Cdkn2a.
summary: The unbiased whole-surface neighborhood of Cdkn2a had no strong attractor: Mef2d was the top positive neighbor but had no downstream FDR<0.10 response, whereas Sin3a was the top negative neighbor and drove thousands of DE genes without reciprocal Lst1 regulation.
why_it_matters: The result rejects both data-driven neighbors as Cdkn2a phenocopies and shows that the same postmitotic neuronal assay can register large transcriptional perturbation signatures when the assayed gene is an active regulator.

main_caveats: The two FDR-supported cell groups have singleton signatures; Cas9 indels and protein loss were not measured.
summary: Acute Cdon loss of function was almost completely buffered in postmitotic NeuN+ neurons: 20 of 22 measured cell groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and the two responding groups each contained only one downregulated gene.
why_it_matters: This converts the screen from a failed search for a Sonic-hedgehog program into a stage- and lineage-specific negative result: broad juvenile neuronal Cdon loss does not launch a large transcriptional state.

literature_claim: CDON promotes Hedgehog signaling with PTCH, BOC and GAS1, and the receptor set is required for Shh-dependent progenitor proliferation and neural patterning.
main_caveats: Boc, Gas1, Gli3, and Shh were not target perturbations in the parquet, so receptor redundancy can be inferred but not directly knocked out in combination.
summary: The expected canonical Hedgehog transcript program was absent after Cdon targeting and after direct perturbation of represented Ptch–Smo–Gli pathway relatives.
why_it_matters: This rejects a Cdon-specific explanation for the flat Cdon surface: the P16 NeuN+ assay is not in a state where acute perturbation of Hedgehog receptor or transcriptional nodes produces a coordinated Gli1/Ptch1/Hhip response.

literature_claim: Human CDON variants cause holoprosencephaly, Cdon mutation synergizes with fetal ethanol during E10 forebrain midline patterning, and Cdon-null mice have embryonic ventral-midbrain dopaminergic progenitor phenotypes.
main_caveats: The screen did not recover Cdon in 215 MB Dopa and did not assay embryos, neural progenitors, or prenatal environmental sensitization.
summary: The neuronal null localizes known CDON forebrain and dopaminergic phenotypes away from P16 postmitotic maintenance and toward embryonic patterning, progenitor, or environmental-modifier windows.
why_it_matters: CDON-linked holoprosencephaly and dopamine-system phenotypes can be severe in development, so the lack of a juvenile NeuN+ transcriptome does not argue that CDON is dispensable in the brain; it says the assayed window is after the susceptible Shh-dependent specification period.

literature_claim: RNF146 promotes Wnt signaling by tankyrase-dependent Axin degradation, and cardiac Cdon deficiency hyperactivates Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
main_caveats: Single gene in one cell group at FDR 0.052805; β-catenin activity was not measured directly.
summary: The only Wnt/tankyrase-adjacent adjusted hit was borderline Rnf146 down in cerebellar GABA neurons, with no Axin2/Lef1/Tcf/Myc/Ccnd1 induction.
why_it_matters: Cdon deficiency can hyperactivate Wnt/β-catenin in heart, but the neuronal P16 Cdon surface does not show the same Wnt-output direction; the Rnf146 hit is best treated as a biomarker hypothesis, not evidence of pathway activation.

literature_claim: HCF-1 is a transcriptional coregulator linked to E2F/cell-cycle transcription, but there is no established CDON–proteasome signature relationship.
main_caveats: Similarity used only the two Cdon FDR<0.10 features; there was no same-direction FDR overlap.
summary: The data-driven robust-overlap search found no positive Cdon neighbor and only Psmc1/Psmb4 as exact anti-neighbors through Hcfc1 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The only recurrent cross-target relationship is a contrast with broad proteasome-subunit stress signatures, arguing that Cdon-downregulated Hcfc1 is not part of a shared proteotoxic or integrated stress module.

why_it_matters: The result rejects a Cebpe-specific guide artifact as the simplest explanation and instead places Cebpe in a larger panel of hematopoietic regulators that are off-axis in NeuN-enriched brain nuclei.

main_caveats: Pearson neighbors were computed on rank-sum score vectors dominated by null genes, so they are useful as a rejection test rather than as a mechanistic map.
summary: Data-driven Cebpe signature neighbors were numerical, not biological: the strongest Pearson correlations were only +0.052889 for Fbxo11 and -0.023915 for Wdr26; Fbxo11 itself had only one downstream hit, whereas Wdr26 generated 3128 FDR<0.10 genes in many of the same groups where Cebpe had zero.
why_it_matters: The absent Cebpe response is not hiding a coherent weak neuronal state, and the Wdr26 contrast shows that the matched Wilcoxon surfaces can detect large perturbation responses when a target is active.

literature_claim: CELSR2 is a PCP adhesion-GPCR family member, whereas GPR137-family lysosomal proteins regulate Rag/mTORC1 and autophagy rather than canonical PCP.
main_caveats: Single downstream gene with FDR 0.0573; GPR137 biology is partly inferred from GPR137-family literature.

why_it_matters: The main L4/5 cortical readout was an endolysosomal/mTORC1-autophagy candidate, not a core Celsr/Fzd/Vangl PCP transcript, suggesting a very small adaptive state marker downstream of Celsr2.

literature_claim: GTF2F1 is a general transcription factor IIF subunit for RNA polymerase II initiation.

why_it_matters: A TFIIF / RNA polymerase II factor, not a PCP or synapse gene, marked the L5 extratelencephalic response, consistent with a restricted transcriptional adaptation rather than a broad re-wiring program.

literature_claim: Celsr2 participates in forebrain wiring and adult cortical synapse maintenance.
main_caveats: The positive signature is only two genes total; cell groups are broad and sparse CRISPR mosaics, not anatomical microdissections.

why_it_matters: The effect map refines adult cortical Celsr2 biology: the P16-P37 neuronal mRNA footprint is not pan-neuronal, not pan-glutamatergic, and not even pan-cortical.

literature_claim: Celsr2 loss is expected to affect ependymal cilia, forebrain axon wiring, adult cortical synapses and dorsal-CA1 NMDA/dendritic physiology.
main_caveats: The assay tests mature neuronal nuclear RNA only; protein localization, axon pathfinding, cilia orientation and spine physiology can change without these transcripts changing.

why_it_matters: This separates Celsr2-dependent wiring, ciliary and synaptic phenotypes from a detectable nuclear mRNA feedback loop over Celsr1/3-Fzd3-Vangl-Dvl or Pla2g4e/NMDA synaptic genes in juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: Celsr2/Celsr3/Fzd3 and Wnt5a-Ror-Dishevelled are genetically related to noncanonical PCP-like developmental signaling.

summary: Neither exploratory data-driven neighbors nor represented Wnt/Ror pathway relatives phenocopied the Celsr2 cortical signature.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation rejection prevents a weak Celsr2 signature from being over-read as a shared Wnt/PCP module and shows that the two Celsr2 hits are idiosyncratic in this assay.

literature_claim: Prior work places CEP112 in sperm RNA granules and centrosomal/basal-foot structures, and also links Macoco/CEP112 to neuronal GABAA receptor surface expression and Cep112-Brca1 mitotic fidelity.

why_it_matters: This is the central result: the acute P16 neuronal perturbation does not convert CEP112's established spermiogenic, centrosomal, basal-foot, mitotic, or GABAA-receptor biology into a durable P37-44 nuclear RNA program.

literature_claim: Macoco/CEP112 was reported to interact with GABAA receptor beta-subunit intracellular domains and to increase surface GABAA receptor levels when expressed in neurons.

why_it_matters: The old Macoco-GABAA literature predicts a receptor-surface trafficking phenotype; the Perturb-seq screen says that removing Cep112 after P16 does not measurably reproduce the transcriptional consequences of directly perturbing GABAA receptor subunits.

literature_claim: CEP112/Macoco binds MAF1 in neurons, and MAF1 is a TORC1-regulated repressor of RNA polymerase III transcription.
main_caveats: This is an indirect pathway contrast because Maf1 itself was not a perturbation target in the parquet.

why_it_matters: Because MAF1 is a Pol III repressor and a reported Macoco partner, this tests an indirect transcriptional route from Cep112/Macoco to RNA-production stress; the route is not engaged by Cep112 in this postnatal neuronal assay.

literature_claim: CEP112 is a centrosomal and basal-foot component, so basal-body and ciliopathy-associated perturbations are the obvious structural comparators in this screen.

why_it_matters: Centrosomal and basal-foot proteins can be structurally important without causing a rapid cell-autonomous nuclear-RNA signature in postmitotic neurons; the related-target surface supports biological buffering or readout displacement rather than a Cep112-specific failure.

main_caveats: Neighbor correlations are genome-wide restricted-signature statistics around a null target and are far below values that would support mechanistic similarity.

why_it_matters: The data-driven search did not uncover a hidden convergent module; it exposed how isolated and flat the Cep112 perturbation is relative to strong caudal/diencephalic programs in the same parquet.

summary: Acute Chd4 loss produced one broad response, concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where 149 downstream genes reached FDR<0.10; every other effect was one to three genes.
why_it_matters: CHD4 is a general chromatin remodeler, but the P16-to-P37/44 neuronal CRISPR surface is not pan-neuronal. The result nominates a postmitotic thalamic vulnerability rather than a global NuRD transcriptional collapse.

main_caveats: Recurrence is only two cell groups per gene; this is a marker hypothesis, not proof of a shared mechanism.
summary: The sparse non-thalamic Chd4 responders mostly appeared as weak echoes of the thalamic program, with Begain, Stxbp2, and Cacnb3 each recurring in 151 plus one additional cell group.
why_it_matters: These three genes are better supported as cross-cell-type Chd4 response markers than isolated hits such as Tnnt2 or Cox7b, which each fired in only one small group.

literature_claim: Chd4 has been shown in cerebellar granule neurons to regulate activity-linked promoters and neuronal connectivity.
main_caveats: The genes are a focused portion of the thalamic DE list; electrophysiology was not measured.
summary: Within 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Chd4 loss up-regulated a channel and calcium/excitability branch including Cacng7, Kcnab3, Cacnb3, Cacna2d2, Kcnt1, Kcna2, Slc8a2 and Ache.
why_it_matters: The strongest response is not limited to generic chromatin or apoptosis genes; it reaches membrane excitability genes that could change thalamic neuron physiology after postmitotic CHD4 disruption.

main_caveats: The gene set is directionally coherent but was inferred from transcript identities; no matrix or adhesion phenotype was measured.
summary: The 151 thalamic signature coupled Bcan/Ndst1/Chst1/B3galnt1 induction with reduced protocadherin-cluster transcripts, indicating cell-surface and extracellular-matrix remodeling.
why_it_matters: CHD4 disruption altered genes that can tune pericellular matrix and adhesion identity, broadening the interpretation beyond nuclear chromatin machinery alone.

main_caveats: The metabolic branch is smaller than the channel/adhesion branches and is transcriptomic only.
summary: A smaller 151 branch shifted metabolic and redox genes, with Pygm, Msra, Acss2, Ddo and Etnk2 up while Gss and Hsd17b4 were down, but canonical UPR/ISR or autophagy markers were absent.
why_it_matters: This suggests a selective adaptive metabolic response rather than a broad ER-stress or lysosomal stress program after Chd4 perturbation in surviving thalamic neurons.

literature_claim: CHD4 was reported to promote mouse embryonic stem-cell neural differentiation by down-regulating p53.
main_caveats: A transient earlier p53 pulse or p53 activation in cells lost before harvest would not be captured.
summary: The broad thalamic Chd4 response did not activate a p53-apoptosis signature: Trp53, Cdkn1a, Mdm2, Bax and Bbc3 all had FDR=1.0, and Phlda3 was nominal only.
why_it_matters: p53 target induction would be visible to snRNA-seq if sustained in survivors; its absence separates the P16 postmitotic thalamic program from CHD4-p53 biology described in embryonic neural differentiation.

literature_claim: ADNP recruits HP1 and CHD4 to form ChAHP and repress lineage-specifying genes in mouse embryonic stem cells.
main_caveats: The neighbor metric used the Chd4 FDR feature set; Huwe1 and Atrx are data-driven neighbors without a direct ChAHP prior, and Setd5 did not pass the FDR-overlap gate.
summary: The data-driven Chd4 signature neighbor was Adnp, and Adnp and Huwe1 shared same-direction subsets of the 151 thalamic Chd4 program.
why_it_matters: ADNP is a known CHD4 partner in ChAHP; its rank-1 convergence argues that the Chd4 phenotype is not just a generic chromatin-remodeler injury signature.

literature_claim: GATAD2B and MBD2 are NuRD-associated proteins, and pathogenic GATAD2B missense variants can disrupt NuRD partner interactions including CHD3/4/5 and MBD2/3.
main_caveats: Only Mbd2 and Gatad2b were represented among canonical NuRD cofactors; Mbd3, Gatad2a, Hdac1/2, Mta and Rbbp subunits were not perturbed here.
summary: Measured NuRD-related perturbations did not phenocopy Chd4: Gatad2b was a restricted-signature neighbor but had zero downstream FDR genes in 151 despite a significant Gatad2b self-transcript drop, and Mbd2 was nearly flat.
why_it_matters: The thalamic Chd4 response is therefore unlikely to be a simple loss of every MBD/GATAD2B-containing NuRD activity; it is more consistent with an ATPase-specific, dosage-threshold, or alternative-CHD4-complex effect.

literature_claim: SWI/SNF/BAF and NuRD remodelers can oppose one another at shared regulatory elements, and BAF genes are heavily implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders.
main_caveats: Overlap was computed on FDR genes in one cell class; it does not identify the chromatin elements where the two remodeler families act.
summary: BAF/PBAF perturbations fired in the same thalamic neurons but often inverted Chd4 genes, especially after Arid2, Arid1a, Smarce1 and Smarcc2 loss.
why_it_matters: The opposite-sign response preserves an expected chromatin logic: SWI/SNF-family perturbations can antagonize NuRD-regulated loci rather than phenocopy CHD4 loss.

literature_claim: CHD3, CHD4 and CHD5 occupy mostly distinct NuRD assemblies and have nonredundant roles during embryonic cortical development.
main_caveats: Chd3 and Chd5 were not themselves perturbation targets in the parquet, so compensation is inferred from transcript induction rather than from epistasis.
summary: Chd4 up-regulated its NuRD ATPase paralog Chd3 in 151, yet Chd2 and Chd8 perturbations produced distinct signatures and Chd7 was almost inert.
why_it_matters: The dataset supports limited interchangeability within the CHD family: a paralog-bounce transcript appears after Chd4 loss, but other CHD perturbations do not reconstruct the Chd4 state.

literature_claim: CHD7 is a haploinsufficient ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler whose strong mouse and human phenotypes arise in embryonic and developmental contexts.
main_caveats: DNA indel status is not measured; the significant neuronal response is limited to one FDR<0.10 gene per responding cell group.
summary: Acute postnatal Chd7 loss produced only two robust downstream transcript changes across 23 neuronal cell groups: Ano8 up in 155 MB Glut and Nfyb up in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: Strong CHD7 developmental phenotypes did not become a broad mature-neuron transcriptional collapse in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR setting.

main_caveats: Neighbor calling used all Wilcoxon-score ranks because Chd7 itself had only two FDR<0.10 downstream genes; the named non-Safe genes should not be read as biological CHD7 partners.
summary: The rank-space Chd7 signature had no convincing positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The flat Chd7 surface is not hiding inside a convergent secondary module shared with another robust perturbation.

literature_claim: CHD8 physically interacts with CHD7 and CHD2/CHD4/CHD8 are CHD chromatin-remodeler relatives.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and postnatal; it does not exclude shared binding or cooperation in progenitors.
summary: CHD-family perturbations Chd8, Chd2 and Chd4 responded where Chd7 was flat, with recurrent Pnisr or Snhg11/Begain-centered signatures and essentially zero overlap with Chd7.
why_it_matters: A direct CHD7-CHD8 protein interaction and shared CHD-family membership did not translate into interchangeable acute postmitotic neuronal phenotypes.

direction: expected programs absent after Chd7 perturbation
literature_claim: CHD7 cooperates with PBAF or SOX factors in neural crest, neural stem/progenitor cells, OPCs, cerebellar granule-cell precursors and developmental GABAergic models.
main_caveats: The tested cells are NeuN-enriched postmitotic neurons; the result is an absence of these programs in this assay, not a failure of the cited developmental programs.
summary: The PBAF/SOX2/neural-stem-cell programs that are most obvious from the CHD7 literature were not recovered in the Chd7 neuronal DE surface.
why_it_matters: The expected CHD7 targets—RA/pro-neural genes, SoxC factors, neural-crest factors and Paqr3—were all FDR-flat, and the represented PBAF/SOX perturbations did not phenocopy Chd7; canonical CHD7 biology is therefore displaced to other stages or unsampled lineages rather than merely weakly visible in mature neurons.

direction: no RA/pro-neural induction or repression at FDR<0.10
literature_claim: In P1 mouse SVZ, Chd7 loss decreased Rarb, Rxrg and Neurod1 expression, and retinoic-acid manipulation modified Chd7-deficient neural-stem-cell and inner-ear phenotypes.
main_caveats: Only steady-state mature-neuron snRNA-seq was assayed; retinoic-acid signaling could still be relevant in progenitors, sensory organs, or earlier treatment windows.
summary: The retinoic-acid/pro-neural rescue axis reported for Chd7-deficient SVZ and inner-ear development did not appear after P16 neuronal Chd7 knockout.
why_it_matters: RA-pathway modulation is therefore a niche- and timing-specific hypothesis; Rarb, Rxrg and Neurod1 were each measured but never significant in this neuronal screen.

literature_claim: CHD8 is a broadly expressed ASD chromatin regulator with pleiotropic developmental functions, so the literature predicts context dependence but not this thalamic/midbrain-enriched acute P16 neuronal signature.
main_caveats: The signature is snRNA abundance only; effect groups with one to three genes are real FDR hits but do not independently define programs.
summary: Acute postmitotic Chd8 loss was a restricted, subcortical-biased perturbation rather than a pan-neuronal transcriptional shock.
why_it_matters: The 10 effect groups contained 148 downstream FDR<0.10 rows, but two groups—151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut—accounted for 123 of them; most cortical and hippocampal groups were flat despite Chd8 being measured.

literature_claim: CHD8 suppression alters H3K36me3 at gene bodies and alternative splicing in neural progenitors, and serine/arginine-rich proteins are RNA-binding splicing regulators.
main_caveats: 10x Flex snRNA-seq cannot test isoform usage directly; the claim rests on abundance changes in RNA-processing genes.
summary: A recurrent PNISR/USP11/DUS3L-down module links the strongest Chd8 responders to RNA-processing and cotranscriptional regulation rather than to a Wnt-only program.
why_it_matters: Pnisr was down at FDR<0.10 in 8 cell groups, Usp11 in 4, and Dus3l in 3; the 151 TH and 155 MB signatures added Luc7l3, Ddx39b, Snrnp70, Rbm6, Matr3, Pan2, and Hexim1/Cdk9-related transcriptional-control genes, consistent with CHD8 biology at elongating, spliced genes.

main_caveats: This is an annotation-level interpretation of gene identities, not a measured proteomic or mitochondrial-functional assay.
summary: The thalamic and midbrain Chd8 signatures also carried an organellar and chromatin-maintenance arm.
why_it_matters: Tmem50a, Man2c1, Slc25a23, Fastk, Ndufb7, Pccb, Samm50, Parl, Dguok, Sirt4, Txndc15, Aaas, Hjurp, Xrcc4, and Mlh3 were significant in the 151 TH and/or 155/191 MB responders, showing that the postmitotic response couples RNA regulation to mitochondrial/ER metabolism and DNA/chromatin homeostasis.

main_caveats: Data-driven neighbor ranking was restricted to the 148 Chd8-significant group×gene loci and should be read as signature convergence, not protein interaction.
summary: Yy1 was the top data-driven positive neighbor of Chd8 and re-used the USP11/DUS3L/PNISR axis in the same subcortical groups.
why_it_matters: Among 1769 measured targets with enough overlap on the 148 Chd8 FDR loci, Yy1 ranked first by signed Wilcoxon-score convergence and had 32 same-direction versus 4 opposite-direction shared FDR hits, making a non-obvious chromatin/transcriptional convergence stronger than CHD paralogs or Wnt-pathway targets.

literature_claim: NRF1 mediates proteasome recovery after proteasome inhibition, and CHD8 can regulate transcriptional elongation and RNA processing.
main_caveats: The Chd8 signature itself did not induce a full NRF1 proteasome-subunit cassette; convergence is partial and restricted-signature-based.
summary: The next Chd8-positive neighbors were proteasome, RNA-processing, or chromatin-corepressor perturbations, nominating a maintenance-state signature downstream of Chd8.
why_it_matters: Psmc1, Cdc40, Nrf1, Sin3a, and U2af2 all landed among the top six same-direction neighbors; their effects were far broader than Chd8, but they overlapped Chd8 on Pnisr/Rsrp1/Snhg11/Luc7l3/Tmem50a/Dus3l/Txndc15-class loci.

literature_claim: SETD1A is an H3K4 methyltransferase pathway gene linked to neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disease, but the literature does not predict that its acute neuronal transcriptome should oppose CHD8.
main_caveats: Zbtb7a is a broad transcriptional perturbation rather than a CHD8 paralog; the contrast is transcriptional, not a direct biochemical antagonism.
summary: Setd1a and Zbtb7a opposed Chd8 even though they are transcription/chromatin regulators with broad neuronal signatures.
why_it_matters: Zbtb7a was the strongest anti-neighbor and reversed Chd8 on Usp11 in four responder groups; Setd1a was the second strongest anti-neighbor and opposed Chd8 on the thalamic Fastk/Foxred1/Glt8d1/Dguok/Csf2ra arm, demonstrating that chromatin regulators in this assay are not interchangeable.

literature_claim: CHD2, CHD7, CHD8 and H3K4/chromatin regulators are all implicated in neurodevelopmental disease, and CHD8 is a beta-catenin-linked chromatin remodeler.
main_caveats: Only perturbation targets represented in the parquet could be tested; absence of convergence in basal snRNA-seq does not rule out shared developmental or protein-level mechanisms.
summary: CHD paralogs, Wnt/beta-catenin targets, BAF components, and other ASD chromatin genes did not phenocopy Chd8 in the P16 neuronal assay.
why_it_matters: Chd7 had only two FDR rows across the full 23-group surface; Chd2, Chd4, Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Kmt2a, Smarcc2, Smarca4, Arid1b, Baz1b, Adnp, Gatad2b, and Kdm5c either had no Chd8 overlap or mixed same/opposite overlap, rejecting simple same-family interchangeability.

literature_claim: In embryonic and neural-progenitor systems CHD8 regulates p53-mediated apoptosis, cortical neural progenitor proliferation, and Wnt/cell-cycle transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: The absence is for basal juvenile NeuN+ nuclei; it does not test embryonic progenitors or p53-dependent survival immediately after a complete knockout.
summary: The expected Wnt/p53/cell-cycle CHD8 program was not recovered after P16 neuronal perturbation.
why_it_matters: A direct search of Wnt/beta-catenin, p53/apoptosis, and proliferative markers found 0 FDR<0.10 hits after Chd8 perturbation, so the juvenile neuronal response cannot be treated as a simple continuation of the embryonic NPC Wnt/cell-cycle phenotype.

literature_claim: L1-CAM/CHL1 Ig-superfamily adhesion molecules regulate neuronal migration, axon guidance, synaptic targeting, and circuit maturation.
main_caveats: The perturbation is mosaic and functional indels were not measured; absence of a nuclear RNA response does not exclude altered axons, dendritic spines, synapses, or behavioral output.
summary: P16 acute Chl1 loss produced a pan-neuronal downstream transcriptional null in every recovered cell group.
why_it_matters: Chl1 is an adhesion and guidance molecule with strong circuit-development priors, yet the P37-P44 snRNA-seq readout found no non-Chl1 genes at FDR<0.10 in 21 neuronal groups; this rules out a broad cell-autonomous stress, differentiation, UPR/ISR, autophagy, or synaptic gene-expression collapse in surviving NeuN+ neurons after postmitotic perturbation.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: CHL1 cooperates with L1/NRP1 in thalamocortical guidance and with Sema3B-NRP2-PLXNA4 signaling in cortical spine pruning.
main_caveats: The queried relatives are not all strict paralogs, Nfasc was not represented as a measured target, and isolated single-gene comparator hits were not interpreted as modules.
summary: The obvious L1-family, NCAM/ankyrin, and semaphorin-receptor comparators fail to define a Chl1-like transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: CHL1 acts with L1cam, Nrp1, Nrp2, and Plxna4 in published guidance and pruning systems, but direct Perturb-seq comparators were flat or had only isolated one-gene hits in the 21 Chl1-matched groups; the data therefore reject a shared adjusted nuclear mRNA signature for this adhesion/semaphorin pathway in the acute postnatal assay.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The correlation used all ranked Wilcoxon scores, so a correlation of a null vector is useful only to reject strong convergence, not to infer mechanism from tiny ranks.
summary: An unbiased cross-perturbation search places Chl1 in near-zero signature space, not in a hidden stress or organelle module.
why_it_matters: The strongest all-21 non-safe positive and negative Chl1 neighbors had |r| < 0.026 over 355046 matched Wilcoxon-score entries; genuine responders such as Rab7 and Opa1 were among weak positive neighbors only because the Chl1 vector is essentially noise-scale rather than because they share Chl1 downstream genes.
