literature_claim: Cx3cr1 encodes the fractalkine/CX3CL1 receptor and Cx3cr1 loss primarily alters microglial development, inflammatory responses, and microglia-mediated synaptic pruning rather than a neuron-autonomous transcriptional pathway.
main_caveats: The screen did not sequence DNA indels and did not recover receptor-positive microglia; the conclusion is restricted to neuron-autonomous snRNA-seq signatures 3-4 weeks after P16 perturbation.
summary: Cx3cr1 loss produced a pan-neuronal zero: all 23 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the Cx3cr1 receptor transcript itself was not a tested expression feature.
why_it_matters: The result is a cell-type refinement rather than a claim that Cx3cr1 is inert in brain. The screen perturbed NeuN-positive neurons after P16, whereas the established CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis is a neuron-to-microglia signaling system driven by receptor-positive microglia.

literature_claim: ADAM10 constitutively and ADAM17 inducibly shed CX3CL1 to tune the amount of membrane-bound versus soluble fractalkine available to CX3CR1.
main_caveats: Adam10 was recovered in only 9 neuronal groups with 20-69 perturbed nuclei, Adam17 and Cx3cl1 were not represented as perturbation targets, and Cx3cl1 was tested only as a transcript downstream of Cx3cr1.
summary: The measured CX3CL1 processing axis did not converge with Cx3cr1: neuronal Cx3cl1 mRNA was unchanged after Cx3cr1 perturbation, and the represented sheddase target Adam10 had 0 FDR<0.10 genes in its 9 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: ADAM10 and ADAM17 regulate ligand shedding upstream of CX3CR1. Their biochemical relation does not translate into a matched cell-autonomous neuronal CRISPR phenotype, consistent with a paracrine ligand-receptor module whose productive receptor side is outside the NeuN-positive sample.

literature_claim: Cx3cr1 is a GPCR with immune and microglial functions, so chemokine, purinergic, cytokine, and interferon-associated perturbations are the represented model-visible immune comparators to Cx3cr1 in this neuronal screen.
main_caveats: The comparators are pathway-class relatives, not the exclusive CX3CL1-CX3CR1 ligand-receptor pair; the Cxcr4 and P2ry12 singleton effects were not recurrent modules.
summary: Other represented neuroimmune targets were also nearly flat in NeuN-positive neurons: Ccr2, Il10ra, Irf5, and P2ry14 had no FDR<0.10 genes, while P2ry12 and Cxcr4 produced only isolated one-gene effects.
why_it_matters: The Cx3cr1 zero is part of a broader pattern in which immune receptor perturbations do not drive recurrent young-neuron nuclear programs, strengthening the interpretation that Cx3cr1 biology is displaced to immune-lineage cells rather than being a missing canonical neuronal pathway.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed over a nearly flat Cx3cr1 score vector, so the top ranks should be interpreted as rejection of convergence, not as mechanistic similarity or antagonism.
summary: All data-driven Cx3cr1 signature neighbors were noise-level, with Adam10 the top positive score neighbor at r=0.0323 and Wdr26 the top negative score neighbor at r=-0.0134 despite Wdr26 producing 3,130 FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: This rejects a hidden Cx3cr1-like module elsewhere in the perturbation universe and shows that the all-null Cx3cr1 surface is not caused by an inability of the Wilcoxon snRNA-seq readout to discover large signatures at comparable cell numbers.

literature_claim: CX3CR1 signaling can restrain microglial neurotoxicity in inflammatory, Parkinsonian, and ALS mouse models, and CNS-penetrant antagonism could increase neuronal vulnerability in those contexts.
main_caveats: The disease-model literature is not matched to a juvenile uninjured mouse Perturb-seq experiment; the finding is a boundary condition on interpretation, not a pharmacology result.
summary: The neuronal null should not be read as evidence that CX3CR1 antagonism is transcriptionally silent in the CNS, because the responsive receptor-positive microglial compartment was largely excluded.
why_it_matters: Cardona and colleagues reported that Cx3cr1 deficiency can increase microglial neurotoxicity and neuronal loss in inflammatory and degenerative mouse models. A NeuN-positive P37-44 null therefore de-risks only direct neuronal nuclear programs, not therapeutic blockade in disease-activated microglia.

literature_claim: PUM1 is a mammalian Pumilio RNA-binding protein that represses target mRNAs post-transcriptionally; a CXCR4-to-PUM1 connection is not established.
main_caveats: Each responder contains a single FDR<0.10 gene; the Zgpat and Pum1 events do not make a replicated pathway module.
summary: Cxcr4 produced a sparse two-island neuronal response: Zgpat was down in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and Pum1 was up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene in each cell group.
why_it_matters: The FDR-supported biology is cell-type restricted and gene-isolated rather than a recurrent CXCL12 module; Pum1 points to a possible RNA-regulatory marker, but that marker is not known to be a direct CXCR4 effector.

literature_claim: CXCL12/CXCR4/ACKR3 signaling governs embryonic interneuron migration and dentate-gyrus neural stem or immature granule-cell positioning.
main_caveats: The tested marker panel is transcriptional and cannot score physical mispositioning or migration history directly.
summary: The canonical CXCL12/CXCR4/ACKR3 neurodevelopmental marker axis was not transcriptionally recovered after postnatal Cxcr4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Naively, loss of a receptor required for neuronal migration would nominate Cxcl12/Ackr3, Dcx, Sox2, Neurod, Dlx, Lhx6, or Reln shifts; all had FDR 1.0 across the 22 Cxcr4-measured groups, arguing that the assay sampled after the morphogenetic program was over or outside the progenitor/interneuron state that carries it.

main_caveats: Full-vector correlations were computed on Wilcoxon scores, so an almost-null target necessarily has small and noise-sensitive nearest-neighbor coefficients.
summary: Across all model-visible perturbations, Cxcr4 sat near a global transcriptional null: its strongest signed-score neighbors had absolute Pearson correlations below 0.027.
why_it_matters: The closest positive and negative signatures, Npy1r/Kcna1 and Grn/Crebbp, were mathematical neighbors of a nearly flat vector rather than robust phenocopies, so convergence with them should be treated as absent rather than mechanistic.

literature_claim: CXCR4 is a Gi-coupled chemokine GPCR and can route extracellular CXCL12 signals into chemotactic cytoskeletal signaling branches.
main_caveats: Ccr2 is only a family comparator and Tiam1/Rac1 are indirect pathway comparators; direct Cxcl12 and Ackr3 perturbations were not represented as targets.
summary: Represented chemokine/Rac-arm comparators did not converge with Cxcr4: Ccr2 and Tiam1 were null in all matched groups, and Rac1 produced a Ranbp1-only Sst response where Cxcr4 was flat.
why_it_matters: This rejects the simple expectation that a generic chemokine GPCR or Rac migration-effector perturbation would reproduce the two isolated Cxcr4 hits in this postmitotic brain readout.

literature_claim: Cxcr4 loss disrupts hematopoiesis in mice and CXCR4 antagonism with plerixafor mobilizes hematopoietic stem cells clinically.
main_caveats: The screen excluded most non-neuronal, immune, vascular, and bone-marrow lineages, and it used CRISPR LoF rather than an acute antagonist.
summary: The sparse NeuN+ Cxcr4 signature is a poor negative predictor for systemic CXCR4 antagonism, because the major hematopoietic and stromal compartments that define plerixafor biology were not part of this neuron-enriched screen.
why_it_matters: CXCR4 is clearly druggable and loss of CXCL12/CXCR4 has strong hematopoietic consequences in vivo; this dataset instead shows that acute postmitotic neuronal LoF rarely induces a cell-autonomous snRNA-seq state change.

literature_claim: GNB1 encodes a heterotrimeric G-protein beta subunit and GNB1 variants cause severe neurodevelopmental disability, hypotonia, and seizures; a CYC1-to-GNB1 transcriptional link was not the mitochondrial prior.

summary: Cyc1 loss produced exactly one robust downstream transcript, Gnb1, and only in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The positive Cyc1 biology in this screen is a narrow midbrain-glutamatergic Gnb1 decrement rather than a broad mitochondrial stress state.

literature_claim: Complex III participates in OXPHOS and ROS signaling, and mammalian mitochondrial stress can activate an ATF4-centered integrated stress response.

literature_claim: CYC1, UQCRFS1, UQCRB, UQCRC2, UQCRH, and UQCRQ are complex-III components, and TTC19 function is linked to UQCRFS1-containing complex-III maturation.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on Wilcoxon score vectors; because Cyc1 has only one downstream FDR hit, even the full-vector metric is dominated by weak ranks.

why_it_matters: This separates the acute postnatal nuclear RNA response from the strong synaptic, actin, and translational phenotypes reported for CYFIP1; the screen does not support a broad cell-autonomous stress or synaptic-transcript collapse after P16 Cyfip1 perturbation.

why_it_matters: CYFIP1 sits in translation control, yet its acute postmitotic loss did not phenocopy Tsc2 loss or produce the sterol/lysosomal/metabolic secondary response that a nuclear assay can capture.

literature_claim: CYLD has neuronal synaptic, autophagy-flux, and cytoskeletal roles, and the reported FTD/ALS allele increased rather than decreased K63 deubiquitinase activity.

literature_claim: TFIIH is a common downstream NER machine with a basal RNA polymerase II transcription-initiation role, whereas DDB2 is an upstream UV-DDB damage sensor for GG-NER.
main_caveats: The Gtf2h5 contrast rests on two FDR<0.10 genes in one cell group; most represented checkpoint comparators were also flat, so the result is a restricted cross-perturbation absence rather than a large differential module.
summary: Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor represented DNA-repair comparators gave Ddb2 a meaningful convergent partner: all Ddb2 score cosines were near zero, and the NER/TFIIH target Gtf2h5 had only a two-gene 191 MB P MY GABA response that Ddb2 lacked.
why_it_matters: The expected pathway-neighbor test converts a flat Ddb2 surface into a directional statement: Ddb2 does not behave like a basal DNA-damage checkpoint or TFIIH transcription-repair perturbation in this neuronal context.

literature_claim: DDHD1 loss is expected to perturb PI/LPI lipid metabolism, while MCL1 is an anti-apoptotic BCL-2-family survival gene.
main_caveats: Only one transcript reached FDR<0.10 and the Mcl1 FDR was 0.063; protein, lipid, and apoptosis readouts were not assayed.
summary: Ddhd1 has a one-gene FDR<0.10 signature restricted to 046 CTX-CGE GABA, where Mcl1 is upregulated.
why_it_matters: The finding prevents the target from being miscalled globally null while preserving that the response is extremely narrow.

literature_claim: MCL1 is an anti-apoptotic BCL-2-family regulator of cell survival.
main_caveats: Single-transcript hypothesis; Mcl1 RNA could be regulated post-transcriptionally and does not itself prove apoptosis.
summary: Mcl1 upregulation is a candidate anti-apoptotic compensation to Ddhd1 lipid-enzyme loss in CTX-CGE GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: A survival-buffer interpretation is more consistent with the lone measured gene than a broad canonical lipid-remodeling transcriptional program.

literature_claim: DDHD1 and DDHD2 are both HSP-associated lipases but affect different lipid pools and show non-identical cell phenotypes.
main_caveats: Most comparator signatures were themselves weak or null, so the contrast is strongest for the absence of shared CTX-CGE Mcl1 upregulation.
summary: The Ddhd1 CTX-CGE Mcl1 response is not shared by Ddhd2 or by assayed HSP/phosphoinositide comparators.
why_it_matters: Directly rejects a simple DDHD-family or generic HSP transcriptional module and supports biochemical non-interchangeability of DDHD1 and DDHD2 in this assay.

009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: DDHD1 loss primarily changes lysophospholipid and phosphoinositide lipid species and can alter recycling-endosome or neurite morphology.
main_caveats: The negative statement is only transcriptional; lipidomics, endosome imaging, and axon maintenance were not measured.
summary: P16 Ddhd1 loss did not elicit a canonical phosphoinositide, lipid-droplet, mitochondrial, UPR/ISR, proteasome, or recycling-endosome DEG program in neuronal nuclei.
why_it_matters: Shows that the primary DDHD1 phenotype in this time window is not a broad nuclear RNA state, even though the same assay could detect a secondary Mcl1 survival transcript in one inhibitory class.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Biallelic DDHD2 loss causes complex SPG54, and full genetic or pharmacologic DDHD2 loss in mice elevates neuronal brain TAGs and lipid droplets.
main_caveats: 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for Ddhd2; DNA indels and neutral lipids were not measured.
summary: Ddhd2 loss of function did not produce a robust whole-transcriptome response in any measured neuronal class.
why_it_matters: SPG54 is a neuronal lipid-metabolism disease gene, so the absence of any downstream FDR<0.10 gene in 22 measured groups is a real context refinement rather than a failure of the screen; it says this P16 mosaic snRNA-seq assay does not convert DDHD2 loss into a juvenile nuclear RNA program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: DDHD2 loss can elevate TAG/lipid droplets, engage ATG8-family lipophagy, and in chronic knockout contexts produce mitochondrial ROS and apoptosis.
main_caveats: The assay measures nuclear RNA, not TAG, cardiolipin, DDHD2 protein, LC3 recruitment, or lipid droplets.
summary: The lipid-droplet, lipophagy, and ROS/apoptosis programs expected from DDHD2 biology were not transcriptionally induced.
why_it_matters: The null is not merely absence of the Ddhd2 self-transcript: RNA markers of lipid storage, ATG8/lipophagy, UPR/ISR, oxidative stress, and apoptosis were also absent at FDR<0.10, arguing that sampled neurons had not entered the downstream stress state described after strong chronic DDHD2 loss.

literature_claim: DDHD1, DDHD2, ATG8/lipophagy factors, and several ER/transport HSP genes are biologically related by lipid metabolism, lipophagy, or spastic-paraplegia biology, but the literature does not require a shared acute RNA signature.
main_caveats: Most related targets were themselves weak in this screen; Pnpla2/ATGL and Sec23ip were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Related lipid/lipophagy and hereditary-spastic-paraplegia perturbations failed to phenocopy Ddhd2 in the matched DE surface.
why_it_matters: Directly measured relatives were sparse or null: the DDHD1 paralog had only one FDR gene, Atg5 had two, Kif1a had eight, Tmem106b had one, and Map1lc3a, Atl1, Reep1, Spast, Kif5a, Tfg, and Ap4s1 had none across the Ddhd2-matched groups. DDHD2 therefore did not sit in a shared HSP or autophagy RNA module in this assay.

main_caveats: Because Ddhd2 had no FDR<0.10 genes, the all-gene neighbor ranking is a bounded QC comparison, not a mechanistic inference.
summary: The data-driven Ddhd2 signature-neighbor search yielded only background-like positive neighbors and no inverted neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top non-safe all-gene neighbors Trappc10, Atr, and Prepl carried 1, 0, and 0 FDR genes across Ddhd2-matched groups, whereas broad proteasome hits Psmc1 and Psmb4 were the least similar but still positively correlated. There is no hidden robust module that ΔDdhd2 joins after leaving canonical lipid biology.

literature_claim: DDX39B/UAP56 is a central TREX-associated RNA helicase required for mRNA processing and export, a function expected to be broadly needed by cells.
main_caveats: The CRISPR screen measured gene-level nuclear RNA abundance, not DNA indels, DDX39B protein, per-cell nuclear export, or isoform-level splicing.
summary: Ddx39b produced a highly restricted postmitotic neuronal abundance response: only 3 of 21 measured cell groups had any downstream gene at FDR<0.10, and the only multi-gene response was in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: A core mRNA-export helicase did not act as a uniformly visible total-RNA liability in juvenile neurons; the screen nominates a small MB/Pons/Myelencephalon GABAergic population as the reproducible responder rather than cortex or hippocampus.

literature_claim: DDX39B functions in pre-mRNA splicing, TREX-dependent mRNP remodeling, and mRNA nuclear export; THOC1 and spliceosome components are pathway-proximal.
main_caveats: Only 26 perturbed MB P MY GABA nuclei are present, so the gene set is interpreted through recurrence with related perturbations rather than by single genes alone.
summary: The 191 MB P MY GABA Ddx39b signature was dominated by up-regulated RNA-processing and chromatin/transcriptional regulators together with a smaller down-regulated RNA-processing set.
why_it_matters: Genes such as Sart1, Dhx9, Dhx37, Rnpc3, Ptbp2, Rsrp1, Polr2a, Kmt2b, Hdac5, Ncor2, Smarca2, and Smarca4 make the strongest Ddx39b responder look like a remodeling reaction to impaired mRNP biogenesis rather than a generic neuronal-activity signature.

literature_claim: THO/TREX and spliceosome factors participate in the same mRNA-biogenesis route as DDX39B/UAP56.
main_caveats: The overlap is restricted to abundance DEGs and is concentrated in 191 MB P MY GABA; several core adaptors such as Alyref and Nxf1 were not perturbation targets in the parquet.
summary: The data-driven positive neighbors of Ddx39b were not random developmental genes: Thoc1, Tpr, and U2af2 were the top three biological same-direction restricted-signature neighbors, while Cdc40, Snrnp70, and Prpf6 provided weaker but directionally consistent spliceosome convergence.
why_it_matters: Direct cross-perturbation convergence validates that the MB P MY GABA Ddx39b response reports a TREX/splicing/nuclear-export axis even though the Ddx39b self transcript was not FDR-depleted.

literature_claim: TREX loss perturbs mRNP biogenesis; the literature does not specifically predict a proteasome-like Psmc1/Psmb4 transcriptional neighbor for DDX39B.
main_caveats: The stress interpretation is based on a subset of the 191 genes and three cerebellar genes; it does not prove direct DDX39B regulation of proteasomes or mitochondria.
summary: Ddx39b also converged with proteasome perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 and carried an autophagy/mitochondrial remodeling tail in 191 MB P MY GABA and 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: Up-regulation of Ulk1, Vps13d, Grpel1, Miga2, and Lancl1, together with same-direction Ddx39b/Psmc1/Psmb4 overlap on many 191-signature genes, suggests compensated organelle/proteostasis stress downstream of RNA-export perturbation rather than a pure spliceosome-only phenotype.

literature_claim: Tpr/Ranbp2 and Prpf6 are RNA-export or splicing neighbors of the DDX39B/TREX route; Psmc1/Psmb4 were empirical neighbors rather than textbook DDX39B partners.
main_caveats: The comparator panel is limited to targets present in the parquet; the closest DDX39B paralog Ddx39a and export adaptors Alyref/Nxf1 were not perturbation targets.
summary: Ddx39b was far flatter than several pathway-proximal perturbations in the same cell groups: for example, in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, Tpr and Prpf6 produced 478 and 368 downstream DEGs whereas Ddx39b produced only Mllt11.
why_it_matters: The weak L4/5 IT, cerebellar, and many null Ddx39b results are target-specific; those neuron groups were capable of strong mRNA-processing or proteostasis responses to other perturbations in the same parquet.

literature_claim: Human DDX39B, DDX3X, and EIF4A2 variants each cause neurodevelopmental disorders linked to RNA-helicase biology.
main_caveats: This comparison only rejects phenocopy of the Ddx39b 005/191/308 abundance features.
summary: Ddx39b did not phenocopy the represented neurodevelopmental RNA-helicase targets Ddx3x or Eif4a2 in its responder groups.
why_it_matters: Although DDX39B, DDX3X, and EIF4A2 all belong to RNA-helicase neurodevelopmental genetics, their postmitotic mouse-brain LoF abundance signatures separate; the DDX39B NDD mechanism should not be inferred from the generic DEAD-box label alone.

main_caveats: Each group has at most three FDR-significant downstream genes, so no pathway-level enrichment is claimed.
summary: The L4/5 IT cortical and cerebellar GABAergic Ddx39b effects were real but isolated: Mllt11 alone in 005, and Miga2/Lancl1 up with Ttc14 down in 308.
why_it_matters: These genes are candidate sentinels of low-level Ddx39b stress in two neuronal classes, but the dataset does not support assigning either cell group to a full TREX, ISR, UPR, or autophagy program.

literature_claim: DDX39A/URH49 is the close DDX39B/UAP56 paralog and forms a distinct AREX mRNA-export assembly.
main_caveats: Ddx39a, Alyref, and Nxf1 were not targeted as perturbations, and the parquet does not measure protein abundance or mRNA-export flux.
summary: Ddx39b perturbation did not transcriptionally induce Ddx39a, Alyref, Nxf1, or the measured export/splicing factors across the 21 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: If DDX39A/AREX helps buffer single-gene Ddx39b loss, the compensation is likely pre-existing or post-transcriptional rather than an FDR-detectable Ddx39a mRNA bounce-back.

literature_claim: DDX3X disease biology is a broad neurodevelopmental RNA-metabolism defect with a major fetal cortical-neurogenesis component.
main_caveats: The screen measured only surviving NeuN+ nuclei 3-4 weeks after sparse P16 AAV-CRISPR and did not assay embryonic progenitors, protein translation, indels, or neuronal abundance losses.
summary: Ddx3x LoF was a narrow postnatal neuronal perturbation: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut crossed FDR<0.10, with 9 and 6 downstream genes, while 20 measured groups had none and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.
why_it_matters: The screen does not reproduce a pan-neuronal DDX3X syndrome state; it isolates two sparse glutamatergic mature-neuron states after P16 editing.

literature_claim: Ddx3x loss perturbs neurogenesis and translation in fetal cortical progenitors and severe DDX3X missense alleles alter RNA-protein granules in progenitors and neurons.
main_caveats: Only nine downstream genes support this program, so it should be read as a compact marker module, not a genome-wide synaptic shutdown.
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response preferentially lowered a small synaptic/neurite-remodeling set, led by Grin2b, Synpo2, Vangl1 and Plekhg1, while Tmsb10 and Ypel3 were induced.
why_it_matters: This is the clearest mature-neuron transcriptional footprint of Ddx3x LoF in the assay and points to a postmitotic thalamic synapse/actin module rather than progenitor cell-cycle arrest.

literature_claim: DDX3 stimulates CK1ε and Wnt/β-catenin signaling, and Wnt signaling has been proposed as one pathogenic branch for DDX3X missense alleles.
main_caveats: The inference is based on five shared genes; Ctnnb1's matched signature was much larger than Ddx3x's, and Gsk3b did not share Ddx3x FDR genes.
summary: Ddx3x and Ctnnb1 converged in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: five of nine Ddx3x downstream genes were significant in the stronger Ctnnb1 signature and every overlap moved in the same direction.
why_it_matters: The overlap keeps the Wnt/β-catenin prior alive in a postmitotic thalamic glutamatergic context, but as a small Ctnnb1-like submodule rather than a full canonical Wnt transcriptome.

literature_claim: DDX3X is an RNA-remodeling DEAD-box helicase involved in translation and mRNA metabolism.
main_caveats: The module is only six genes and Ddx5 itself was not a perturbation target in the library, so compensation is hypothesized from transcript direction rather than tested genetically.
summary: 155 MB Glut showed an RNA-processing-flavored rebound, with Ddx5 increased and Hnrnpl decreased alongside Inha, Ppp2r5b and Bicd2 induction and Thy1 repression.
why_it_matters: The only FDR-significant DEAD-box transcript in the Ddx3x surface was compensatory and cell-restricted, suggesting that midbrain glutamatergic neurons buffer Ddx3x loss through selective RNA-regulatory remodeling rather than an eIF4F-wide collapse.

literature_claim: DDX3X associates with eIF4F/eIF4E/PABP1-containing translation and stress-granule machinery.
main_caveats: A single-gene CRISPR screen cannot test combined translation-factor depletion or acute biochemical helicase inhibition.
summary: Biochemical translation-initiation relatives did not phenocopy Ddx3x: Ddx39b, Eif4g1, Fmr1, Fxr1, Atf6, Eif2ak4 and Tia1 were flat in both responder groups, and Eif4a2, Eif4h and Eif5a produced only one downstream gene each with no Ddx3x-feature overlap.
why_it_matters: The Ddx3x state is not the generic output of reducing a DEAD-box helicase, the eIF4F scaffold, or a stress-granule RNA-binding factor in P16-edited neurons.

literature_claim: DDX3X mutations can impair translation and RNA-protein granules, DDX3 participates in stress-granule and NLRP3 stress decisions, and DDX3 can regulate Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
main_caveats: The assay reads nuclear mRNA, not translation rates, granule formation, inflammasome assembly, or protein stability; a non-transcriptional biochemical phenotype could still be present.
summary: Ddx3x LoF produced no FDR-supported ISR/UPR, heat-shock, stress-granule, Ddx3y-compensation, or canonical Axin2/Lef1 Wnt-target transcriptional program in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: Because secondary stress transcription would have been visible in snRNA-seq, its absence makes the mature-neuron null surface informative rather than merely a readout failure.

literature_claim: DDX3X disease models implicate RNA metabolism, and DDX3X itself is an RNA-remodeling enzyme.
main_caveats: The compared genes are in a broad RNA-regulatory disease-related class rather than one physical complex with DDX3X.
summary: Strong postnatal RNA-binding/NDD comparators, especially Hnrnpu and Hnrnpc, generated hundreds of DE genes in the same two glutamatergic groups but did not align with the 15-gene Ddx3x signature.
why_it_matters: The weak Ddx3x surface is not just a consequence of using mature, sparse neuronal CRISPR: the same assay can detect broad matched-cell responses to other RNA-regulatory perturbations.

literature_claim: Human germline DEAF1 variants and mouse germline or brain knockouts support a broad neurodevelopmental role for DEAF1.
main_caveats: The CRISPR perturbation is mosaic and postnatal; DNA indels and DEAF1 protein loss were not measured.
summary: Acute Deaf1 loss in juvenile postmitotic neurons produced an extremely sparse, mostly down-regulatory signature: 11 downstream FDR<0.10 calls in 5 of 22 tested groups and no significant Deaf1 self-transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: The screen does not reproduce a broad neurodevelopmental transcriptome despite DEAF1 disease genetics; it isolates a narrow maintenance-like response concentrated in thalamic/midbrain groups plus one cortical L4/5 Eif4g3 call.

literature_claim: DEAF1 binds the EIF4G3 promoter and reduced DEAF1 function lowers Eif4g3/eIF4GII in lymph-node stromal cells.
main_caveats: Only three neuronal cell groups crossed FDR<0.10; many other groups showed weaker non-significant Eif4g3 decreases.
summary: Eif4g3 was the clearest direct-target-like Deaf1 output, falling in L4/5 IT cortex, TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, and MB glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: The same EIF4G3 promoter previously bound by DEAF1 in non-neuronal cells is recovered here in neurons, arguing that at least part of the sparse signature is an on-mechanism transcriptional activation program rather than a generic stress artifact.

literature_claim: RAC3 encodes a Rho-family GTPase whose missense dysregulation can cause neurodevelopmental disease, and B4GAT1 initiates functional alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation.
main_caveats: B4gat1, Tmem80, and Pcdh7 have one or two FDR cell-group calls each; they should be treated as markers of the Deaf1 signature before direct binding is demonstrated.
summary: Rac3, B4gat1, and Tmem80 define a midbrain/thalamic negative module under Deaf1 perturbation, while Pcdh7 is the lone up-regulated FDR hit in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The module moves the Deaf1 response from a pure translation story toward Rho-GTPase/cytoskeletal signaling and dystroglycan-linked extracellular glycosylation in the same caudal neuronal classes that carry most of the response.

main_caveats: The neighbor score is restricted to the 11 Deaf1 FDR gene-by-cell features; Psmb4 also showed two opposite-direction overlaps.
summary: The strongest retained FDR-overlap neighbors of Deaf1 were proteasome perturbations rather than DEAF1 pathway members: Psmc1 and Psmb4 shared recurrent Eif4g3/Rac3/B4gat1 decreases but had thousands of additional DEGs in the same groups.
why_it_matters: This makes Deaf1 a small projection onto a protein-turnover-sensitive neuronal state, not a scaled-down copy of proteasome loss.

literature_claim: Deaf1 represses the 5-HT1A autoreceptor axis in raphe cells but can enhance postsynaptic 5-HT1A expression in other neuronal contexts.
main_caveats: Htr1a was assayed at the transcript level, but the screen did not recover serotonin raphe neurons and did not read out receptor physiology.
summary: The canonical Deaf1-Htr1a serotonergic program was absent: Htr1a did not pass FDR under Deaf1 in any sampled group, and Htr1a perturbation itself was transcriptionally flat.
why_it_matters: A well-known Deaf1 target is therefore displaced from this neuronal snRNA-seq surface; the result should not be interpreted as testing raphe 5-HT1A autoreceptor biology, which was not represented as a recovered cell group.

literature_claim: GSK3β can regulate Deaf1 repression at the 5-HT1A promoter, DEAF1 carries a MYND corepressor-interaction domain, and SAND-domain proteins share a conserved DNA-binding family architecture.
main_caveats: Sp110 is a distant SAND-domain comparator and may be weakly expressed in neurons; GSK3B has many Deaf1-independent functions.
summary: Measurable literature-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy Deaf1: Gsk3b produced only an 8-gene 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c signature with no Deaf1-gene overlap, and the SAND-domain target Sp110 was flat.
why_it_matters: The Deaf1 response is not explained by a generic 5-HT1A/GSK3B or SAND/MYND transcription-factor family state in this dataset.

main_caveats: Restricted to three Wdr26 overlaps on Deaf1 FDR features; the inverse relation is hypothesis-generating only.
summary: Wdr26 was the only FDR-level anti-neighbor with more opposite than same Deaf1-feature overlaps, whereas Prpf6 and Yy1 each converged only on Eif4g3 down-regulation.
why_it_matters: This keeps the inverse-neighbor result appropriately weak: the Deaf1 signature is too small to support a full opposing pathway, but the Wdr26 contrast flags Rac3 and Pcdh7 as the features most able to flip sign across perturbations.

literature_claim: Biallelic DENND5A loss causes developmental and epileptic encephalopathy by impairing apical neural-progenitor polarity, spindle orientation, and symmetric division, not primarily by producing a known acute postmitotic neuronal RNA program.
main_caveats: DNA editing was not measured; a vesicle-localization or electrophysiological phenotype could occur without a strong snRNA-seq response.
summary: Dennd5a loss did not trigger a reproducible autonomous nuclear response in any recovered juvenile postmitotic neuronal class.
why_it_matters: DENND5A is a severe neurodevelopmental-disease gene, yet acute P16 mosaic loss in NeuN-enriched P37-44 neurons produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 21 measured cell groups; the result refines the disease model away from a broad postmitotic stress or synaptic-transcription phenotype and toward stages or modalities outside this assay.

009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: DENND5A/Rab6IP1 acts in Rab6-, Rab11-, and Rab39-associated membrane trafficking, and DENND5A/B are annotated Rab39 GEFs in Rab regulation of trafficking.
main_caveats: Most direct nodes, including Dennd5b and Rab39a/b perturbations, were not present as targets; the represented Rab-cycle comparators are same-pathway rather than same-complex controls.
summary: Expected DENND5A trafficking partners were not transcriptionally engaged, and the closest measurable Rab-GEF-cycle perturbations were also flat.
why_it_matters: The literature-nominated direct DENND5A module centers on Rab6/Rab11/Rab39/SNX1 trafficking, but none of the tested module genes or stress sentinels became FDR-significant after Dennd5a perturbation. The direct pathway nodes were mostly absent as perturbation targets, while represented broader Rab-cycle targets Madd, Rab3gap1, Rab3gap2, Rab18, and Rab27a produced only three isolated downstream hits across matched groups; this argues against a shared, easily detected Rab-GEF transcriptional module in juvenile neurons.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The neighbor calculation intentionally used sub-FDR Dennd5a features because no FDR-defined signature existed; only the absence of a strong neighbor is interpretable.
summary: Dennd5a had no interpretable transcriptomic nearest neighbor in the complete parquet.
why_it_matters: The pre-literature restricted-signature search returned only tiny cosines, with a safe-target control as the top hit and null/near-null genes such as Mertk, Figla, and Pex1 among the strongest positive or negative neighbors. A broad responder, Psmc1, appeared in this weak ranking because it perturbed many genes, not because it phenocopied Dennd5a. Dennd5a should therefore be treated as a buffered null in this dataset rather than as a member of a recovered co-regulated module.

literature_claim: DEPDC5 is a GATOR1 mTORC1 repressor whose variants cause focal epilepsies across multiple cortical foci rather than a thalamic-only disorder.
main_caveats: Only 23 downstream genes pass FDR<0.10, and three cell groups were missing rather than true zeros.
summary: Depdc5 produced one robust postnatal transcriptional response, confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The result converts an expected pan-mTOR repressor into a sharply state- and cell-class-restricted response in this P16 sparse neuronal LoF assay.

literature_claim: GATOR1 loss activates mTORC1, mTORC1 can activate SREBPs, and SREBP2 controls cholesterol-biosynthetic and LDLR genes.
main_caveats: SREBP protein cleavage and mTORC1 kinase activity were not directly measured.
summary: The strongest Depdc5-positive module in 151 was sterol synthesis plus LDL uptake.
why_it_matters: Ldlr, Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Dhcr7, and Cyp51 are the transcriptomic arm most clearly coupled to acute GATOR1 loss here and are candidate snRNA biomarkers of Depdc5 engagement in the thalamic responder.

literature_claim: DEPDC5/GATOR1 and TSC2 are both mTORC1 repressors but respond to amino-acid versus growth-factor inputs.
main_caveats: Convergence is restricted to a 23-gene Depdc5 signature in one cell group; Tsc2 is substantially broader.
summary: Tsc2 was the dominant same-direction Depdc5 neighbor and shared the sterol/PI3K 151 signature.
why_it_matters: The data link the GATOR1 amino-acid arm and the TSC growth-factor/energy arm to one neuronal sterol-feedback output, while showing that Tsc2 releases a much broader transcriptional program than Depdc5.

literature_claim: SREBP2 is a positive transcriptional regulator of sterol biosynthesis genes.
main_caveats: The Phf12 relationship is data-driven and not mechanistically resolved by this dataset.
summary: Srebf2 and Phf12 perturbations opposed the Depdc5 sterol axis rather than converging with it.
why_it_matters: The Srebf2 loss signature validates the identity and direction of the Depdc5 cholesterol module; Phf12 emerged as the strongest empirical anti-Depdc5 neighbor, suggesting an unanticipated route that can push the same genes the other way.

literature_claim: mTORC1 core components and upstream PI3K inputs share a pathway with GATOR1/TSC control of anabolic transcription.
main_caveats: The assay measured transcriptomes, not protein depletion of large core complexes; Mtor had five unrelated FDR<0.10 genes, and Rptor was flat.
summary: Mtor, Rptor, Strada, Pik3r1, and Pik3cb did not phenocopy Depdc5 in 151, despite being obvious pathway comparators.
why_it_matters: Same-pathway membership was not interchangeable in this assay: negative regulators that derepress mTORC1 converged, whereas perturbing positive core mTORC1 or PI3K nodes did not produce a clean anti-sterol signature.

literature_claim: Rab7 participates in lysosomal amino-acid control of mTORC1 through an inhibitory route relieved by TBK1, while GATOR1 directly controls Rag-dependent amino acid signaling.
main_caveats: Rab7 caused a much larger signature than Depdc5 and overlapped only part of the Depdc5 23-gene set.
summary: Rab7 loss converged with Depdc5 on the sterol/endolysosomal 151 state.
why_it_matters: Rab7 was not the textbook GATOR1 comparator, but its same-direction induction of Insig1, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Ldlr, Cyp51, Dhcr7, Lamp2, Grn, and Rragd ties the Depdc5 program to lysosomal amino-acid/sterol handling rather than to PI3K alone.

literature_claim: No Depdc5-specific prior predicted this exact small down-regulated RNA-processing arm.
main_caveats: The arm is small and contains only a few recognizable RNA-processing genes.
summary: Depdc5 also contained a small down-regulated RNA-processing arm.
why_it_matters: Rnpc3 and Srrm2 moved down with the host-gene/negative arm rather than with the induced sterol genes, making the 151 response biphasic instead of a simple global mTORC1 upshift.

literature_claim: Depdc5 loss in neuronal models has been linked to dysmorphic neurons, soma enlargement, increased mTOR signaling, and filopodial changes.
main_caveats: No morphology, electrophysiology, or synapse counts were measured in this snRNA-seq assay.
summary: A modest microtubule/synaptic-adhesion arm accompanied mTOR-sterol activation in the thalamic responder.
why_it_matters: Up-regulation of Tubb3, Tubb4b, Clstn3, Sparcl1, and Adgrb1 links the metabolic Depdc5 state to structural or synaptic remodeling genes, but only in a postmitotic thalamic population rather than in the cortical FCD populations emphasized by disease models.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Germline Dgke loss in mouse alters arachidonoyl phosphoinositide/LTP/seizure phenotypes but was not reported to cause a gross brain transcriptional or histologic syndrome.
main_caveats: Engagement was inferred from guide assignment and Dgke RNA shifts rather than indel sequencing; the experiment did not measure lipids, basal synaptic physiology, or evoked activity-dependent transcription.
summary: Postnatal mosaic Dgke loss had no robust steady-state neuronal transcriptional output in any recovered cell group.
why_it_matters: This is a pan-neuronal buffered RNA phenotype, not an isolated low-power miss: all 23 cell groups were measured, including groups with significant Dgke self-transcript depletion, yet every group had 0 non-Dgke genes at FDR<0.10.

main_caveats: This is a whole-score-vector comparison of a nearly flat signature; tiny correlations should be interpreted only as evidence against robust convergence.
summary: Dgke did not belong to a detectable transcriptomic convergence module in this screen.
why_it_matters: The nearest full-surface neighbors of Dgke had Pearson correlations of only 0.028 and 0.027, and the most anti-correlated targets were equally close to zero, so the Dgke surface is dominated by absence of a coherent shared signature rather than a weak version of another target's program.

literature_claim: DGKε acts in the phosphatidylinositol cycle downstream of PLC-generated DAG, can influence DAG/PKC-linked synaptic signaling, and causes aHUS through endothelial VEGFR2/PIP2/Akt/Cox2 signaling rather than complement itself.
main_caveats: Only Dgke, not its DGK paralogs, was directly represented; Kdr and Prkcg hits were isolated single-gene effects rather than broad pathway signatures.
summary: Represented PI-cycle/DAG/PKC and endothelial-disease neighbors also failed to phenocopy Dgke in neuronal snRNA-seq.
why_it_matters: Plcb1, Prkca, Nrp1, and C3 were flat, and Prkcg or Kdr perturbation produced only isolated one-gene effects where Dgke was flat; the canonical DGKε lipid pathway therefore did not map onto a shared constitutive neuronal RNA program in this assay.

literature_claim: DHDDS supplies dolichol for protein glycosylation, a core eukaryotic pathway expected to have broad consequences when sufficiently impaired.
main_caveats: The two one-gene cell groups are exploratory; primary glycosylation chemistry was not measured.
summary: Dhdds produced a strong postnatal neuronal transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, a smaller coherent response in 155 MB Glut, and only single-gene echoes in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 215 MB Dopa.
why_it_matters: The positive surface shows that acute Dhdds loss is not silent, but the effect is restricted rather than pan-neuronal despite DHDDS being a core glycosylation enzyme.

literature_claim: ER folding stress induces UPR chaperones including GRP78/HSPA5 and GRP94/HSP90B1; DHDDS loss should be able to create such stress through dolichol-linked glycosylation defects.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq detects the secondary UPR, not the lipid-linked oligosaccharide defect itself.
summary: Dhdds induced a reproducible ER chaperone and ER-quality-control module centered on Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Sdf2l1, Creld2, Herpud1, Manf, Pdia4, and Pdia6.
why_it_matters: This is the clearest secondary transcriptional consequence predicted by loss of a dolichol-synthesis enzyme: impaired glycoprotein handling is converted into UPR-like homeostasis in susceptible neurons.

literature_claim: The integrated stress response induces ATF4-dependent amino-acid and stress genes, and CHAC1 is an ATF4/ATF3-regulated glutathione-degrading stress effector.
main_caveats: ATF4 protein activity was not measured directly; the assignment is by downstream genes.
summary: The 151 response included a PERK/ATF4-like ISR and amino-acid arm, with Chac1, Ddit3, Sesn2, Asns, Slc7a5, Slc1a4, Slc3a2, Shmt2, Psph, and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases induced.
why_it_matters: Dhdds stress is not limited to luminal chaperones; it crosses into a cytoprotective ISR program that couples ER load to amino-acid import, tRNA charging, and glutathione pressure.

literature_claim: ISR output can include oxidative-stress adaptation, and CHAC1 links ATF-family stress signaling to glutathione degradation.
main_caveats: Aldh1l2 in 215 rests on only 22 perturbed nuclei and one FDR-significant gene; the redox interpretation is indirect.
summary: Cyb5r1 was the strongest 151 hit and Aldh1l2 recurred in 151, 155, and the single-gene 215 MB Dopa response, nominating redox and one-carbon genes as sensitive readouts of Dhdds stress.
why_it_matters: Aldh1l2 and Cyb5r1 are not the canonical dolichol markers, so their recurrence suggests a mitochondrial/redox tail to ER glycosylation stress that may be useful for tracking vulnerable neurons in this assay.

literature_claim: DHDDS and NUS1 variants cause neurodevelopmental, seizure, and myoclonus/movement phenotypes.
main_caveats: The assay measured neuronal nuclei, not firing, synaptic transmission, or organismal myoclonus.
summary: In the coherent Dhdds responders, neuronal function genes were repressed, including Kcnc2, Atp1a3, Nrxn2, Grin2b, Grin2c, Gabrb2, Slc17a6, Kcna2, Syt3, Scg5, Thy1, Stmn3, Kifc2, Tuba1a, and Lrrc7.
why_it_matters: Human DHDDS and NUS1 disorders are neurological; the dataset connects a glycosylation lesion to cell-autonomous down-regulation of ion, vesicle, and synaptic/neurite genes rather than only to generic UPR induction.

literature_claim: The hexosamine pathway supplies UDP-GlcNAc for glycosylation, while DHDDS supplies dolichol carrier lipid for glycoprotein biosynthesis.
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to Dhdds FDR genes and does not mean the full Gfpt1 and Dhdds signatures are identical.
summary: Gfpt1 was the top positive restricted-signature neighbor of Dhdds and shared 126 same-direction FDR overlaps across the Dhdds FDR gene-cell pairs.
why_it_matters: Independent bottlenecks in glycan precursor supply converge in the same vulnerable neurons: DHDDS perturbs the dolichol carrier, whereas GFPT1 controls UDP-GlcNAc production for glycosylation.

literature_claim: HSPA5/GRP78 is a central ER chaperone, SERCA2/ATP2A2 loss can induce ER/SR stress, and SEC63 participates in ER protein handling.
main_caveats: Hspa5 and Sec63 were low-cell perturbations; Vcp was rejected as only restricted-cosine positive.
summary: Atp2a2 and Hspa5 strongly, and Sec63 partially, converged with the Dhdds ER-stress signature; Vcp had a high cosine but too little FDR overlap to keep as a robust phenocopy.
why_it_matters: The Dhdds response sits in a broader ER protein-homeostasis state shared with ER calcium and chaperone perturbations, separating the downstream stress module from the specific dolichol lesion.

literature_claim: NUS1 is the DHDDS complex partner; DPM1 acts downstream on Dol-P-Man synthesis; ATF6 is a canonical UPR arm.
main_caveats: Nus1 was not represented as a target, and Dpm1/Atf6 comparisons are based on the cell groups in which those perturbations were recovered.
summary: The obvious represented relatives Dpm1 and Atf6 did not phenocopy Dhdds: Dpm1 had only two FDR genes in matched 151 and Atf6 had zero FDR genes in all matched Dhdds responder groups.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues against collapsing the Dhdds phenotype into any partial dolichol-pathway or UPR-axis perturbation; the carrier/substrate ER-load state was much closer to Gfpt1 and Atp2a2 than to Dpm1 or Atf6.

main_caveats: The negative ranking used the same restricted Dhdds FDR-pair vector, so it can miss antagonism outside the Dhdds signature genes.
summary: The most anti-correlated Dhdds neighbors, Il6ra, Diaph2, and Tmem63c, had zero FDR-significant opposite-direction overlaps and were rejected as mechanistic antagonists.
why_it_matters: This preserves the directional screen result: Dhdds had strong positive convergence but no robust negative mirror-image perturbation in the measured universe.

literature_claim: DIAPH2 is a diaphanous-related formin regulated by RHO GTPases and implicated in actin assembly, endosome dynamics, and mitotic microtubule control.
main_caveats: Only 23 and 26 Diaph2 cells were recovered, and functional DNA indel engagement was not measured; the result excludes only a large survivor transcriptomic state in the sampled postmitotic neurons.
summary: Diaph2 loss did not elicit a robust nuclear RNA program in either recovered postnatal glutamatergic class.
why_it_matters: The direct result constrains DIAPH2 biology in this screen: the canonical actin, microtubule, endosome, and mitotic-spindle programs either were not engaged in P16-to-P37/44 thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons or did not propagate to a BH-significant snRNA-seq state.

main_caveats: Comparator ranking used all-gene Wilcoxon score correlations from two low-n Diaph2 groups; it is therefore best used to reject a robust module, not to assign function to the tiny positive or negative neighbors.
summary: Diaph2 did not enter a coherent cross-perturbation transcriptomic module; the closest genome-wide score-vector neighbors were near-zero correlations.
why_it_matters: Because the full parquet contains other target surfaces in the same cell groups, the absence of a strong neighbor argues that the Diaph2 rows are residual sampling noise rather than a weak version of a common stress, proteostasis, or neuronal-decline module.

literature_claim: RHO-family GTPases activate diaphanous-related formins, and combined mDia1/mDia3 loss can perturb embryonic neural morphogenesis and axon guidance.
main_caveats: The canonical Diaph1 and Diaph3 perturbations were absent from the parquet, so the strongest paralog test was unavailable; Fmn1 and Fmn2 are formins but not DIAPH paralogs.
summary: The measurable RHO/formin relatives Cdc42, Rac1, Fmn1, and Fmn2 were also flat in the Diaph2-matched cell classes.
why_it_matters: This pathway-level comparison makes the Diaph2 null less likely to be an isolated guide-count artifact: even a Cdc42 perturbation with a significant self-transcript drop in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut yielded no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, supporting buffering or an off-axis cytoskeletal phenotype for RHO/formin signaling in these postmitotic cells.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Dicer processes pre-miRNAs into mature miRNAs and postnatal cortical Dicer deletion primarily depletes mature miRNAs and impairs neuronal morphogenesis rather than specifying a single obligatory stress transcript.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure indels, Dicer protein, mature miRNAs, soma or neurite morphology, or physiology.
summary: Dicer1 loss did not generate a BH-corrected basal mRNA response in any recovered neuronal class 3-4 weeks after P16 AAV-CRISPR perturbation.
why_it_matters: This is an informative negative result: the microRNA-processing enzyme can be hit in postmitotic mosaic neurons without acutely activating a large nuclear stress, apoptosis, immediate-early, or synaptic-loss transcriptome visible by 10x snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: Canonical animal miRISC uses Dicer-derived miRNAs loaded into Argonaute proteins, which recruit GW182/TNRC6 proteins; TNRC6 paralogs can function redundantly in miRNA-mediated repression.
main_caveats: Drosha, Dgcr8, Xpo5, Tarbp2, Prkra, Tnrc6c, Ago3, and Ago4 were not represented as perturbations, so the screen cannot test the entire pathway.
summary: The pathway-neighbor tests point to a broader miRNA/RISC-axis buffering in this assay: Ago2 and Tnrc6b were completely FDR-flat, while Ago1 and Tnrc6a produced only one to two isolated FDR<0.10 downstream hits.
why_it_matters: A Dicer1 null is less likely to be a Dicer1-specific oddity when the represented Argonaute/GW182 effector nodes also fail to phenocopy a broad miRNA-depression state. It also matches the known paralog redundancy of AGO and TNRC6 execution factors.

main_caveats: Correlations were calculated on Wilcoxon scores over all non-Dicer1 genes in matched measured groups and therefore preserve weak global structure; they should not be read as pathway membership.
summary: A full-universe signature-neighbor search found only noise-scale neighbors for Dicer1; the strongest biological Pearson correlations were +0.0346 with Hdac5 and -0.0468 with Wdr26.
why_it_matters: The data did not hide a non-obvious Dicer1-like transcriptional module among 1,772 other targets. Wdr26 and Pura can generate thousands or tens of FDR genes in overlapping neuronal groups, but their weak whole-surface correlations with Dicer1 do not constitute mechanistic convergence or antagonism.

literature_claim: Postmitotic Purkinje-cell Dicer ablation causes progressive miRNA loss followed by cerebellar degeneration and ataxia, and adult dopamine-neuron Dicer ablation causes progressive DA-neuron loss with locomotor phenotypes on a longer post-deletion axis.
main_caveats: CB GABA is a broad recovered group rather than a confirmed purified Purkinje-cell assay; dopaminergic neurons were not tested for Dicer1.
summary: The experiment does not falsify delayed Dicer-dependent survival programs in adult dopaminergic or Purkinje neurons.
why_it_matters: Adult dopamine-neuron Dicer knockout and postmitotic Purkinje-cell Dicer ablation are delayed maintenance or degeneration models; this dataset missed 215 MB Dopa entirely and saw only a 69-cell CB GABA sample at an earlier 3-4 week post-perturbation interval. The safest interpretation is that the relevant phenotype is displaced from this basal juvenile snRNA window, not that the vulnerable neuron classes are Dicer-independent.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Dip2b is expressed broadly in neurons and Dip2b loss in P0 hippocampal cultures or neuralizing mESCs perturbs axon, synaptic, ion-channel, and axon-guidance biology.
main_caveats: True DNA indel engagement was not assayed; the null is an mRNA-state null, not a morphology, electrophysiology, methylation, or axonal-projection null.
summary: Acute postnatal Dip2b loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: Broad adult neural expression and neurodevelopmental genetics do not translate into a broad nuclear mRNA state after sparse P16 CRISPR; the target is transcriptionally buffered in this postmitotic 3-4 week window.

literature_claim: DIP2B regulates axonal outgrowth in hippocampal neurons through alpha-tubulin binding and K40 acetylation.
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptional and restricted to the represented tubulin targets; acetylated alpha-tubulin protein was not measured.
summary: Dip2b did not engage the tubulin-isoform compensation program that was readily visible after Tuba1a perturbation in matched Pvalb and thalamic neurons.
why_it_matters: DIP2B has been linked to alpha-tubulin acetylation during axon outgrowth, but this screen separates that regulatory role from the robust transcriptomic compensation elicited by loss of an alpha-tubulin structural gene.

literature_claim: DIP2B contains a DMAP1-binding domain and is linked to axon-guidance/tubulin biology; CRMP2 mediates class-3-semaphorin axon-pruning and dendritic-spine remodeling.
main_caveats: Dip2a, Dip2c, Dmap1, Dnmt1, Dpysl2, Sema3a, and Sema3f were not assayed as perturbation targets, so the tested comparator set is incomplete and partly pathway-level.
summary: Literature-nominated Dnmt3a, Dpysl5, semaphorin, and plexin perturbations failed to converge with Dip2b as a coherent postnatal nuclear transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Neither the DMAP1/DNA-methylation annotation nor the axon-guidance neighborhood should be treated as a simple adult snRNA-seq module for Dip2b; most represented relatives were flat or produced isolated single-gene events.

main_caveats: The search used score-vector correlation; because Dip2b has no FDR<0.10 downstream genes, any neighbor relation is restricted-signature and was treated as rejected rather than mechanistic.
summary: An unbiased Dip2b signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The nearest Wilcoxon-score correlations were only |r|<=0.0299, and the nominated targets themselves had minimal downstream DE, so the all-null Dip2b surface is not hiding a reproducible cross-target module.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Methylated 5-prime UTR CGG expansions at DIP2B reduce DIP2B mRNA in FRA12A families, and mouse Dip2b loss perturbs neurite/synaptic development in early systems.
main_caveats: The assay does not model CGG-repeat RNA toxicity, repeat methylation, constitutive heterozygosity, DNA methylation state, or behavior.
summary: The FRA12A/DIP2B neurodevelopmental association is not phenocopied as a pan-neuronal juvenile transcriptional collapse by acute coding loss of Dip2b.
why_it_matters: Human DIP2B CGG-repeat disease can involve methylation-sensitive 5-prime UTR repeat alleles, while the screen models sparse postmitotic coding LoF; the flat result points follow-up toward developmental, structural, methylation, or repeat-specific measurements rather than bulk marker-gene panels.

literature_claim: DLAT deficiency is a mitochondrial PDC disease with neurologic and movement-disorder phenotypes, not a thalamic-Prkcd-specific transcriptional syndrome.
main_caveats: Only one downstream DEG reached FDR<0.10; the finding is about the snRNA-seq response, not about absence of metabolic flux defects elsewhere.
summary: P16 Dlat loss produced a sharply restricted neuronal transcriptome: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had a robust downstream DEG, Jarid2.
why_it_matters: A core PDC subunit did not evoke a pan-neuronal mitochondrial-stress response; the screen nominates thalamic Prkcd glutamatergic neurons as the one recovered cell-autonomous transcriptional responder.

literature_claim: PDC can influence chromatin through acetyl-CoA-dependent histone acetylation, and Jarid2 calibrates PRC2 occupancy and activity at developmental genes.
main_caveats: The dataset measured one Jarid2 transcript, not H3K27me3, acetyl-CoA, histone acetylation, or PRC2 target derepression.
summary: Jarid2 down-regulation was the sole FDR<0.10 downstream Dlat marker in the responder.
why_it_matters: Jarid2 is a PRC2 regulator, so this single-gene output points to a narrow chromatin-regulator axis rather than a canonical metabolic-stress transcriptome.

literature_claim: PDC inhibition blocks pyruvate oxidation to acetyl-CoA and can drive lactate/metabolic dysfunction in brain tissue.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq would detect many secondary stress transcripts but cannot rule out lactate, pyruvate, ATP, acetyl-CoA, ultrastructural, or electrophysiologic changes.
summary: The only Dlat responder lacked an ISR, UPR, mitochondrial-chaperone, autophagy, or lactate/pyruvate transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: The strong Dlat and Jarid2 rows were not accompanied by Atf4/Ddit3/Asns, Xbp1/Hspa5, Hspd1/Hspe1, Sqstm1/Map1lc3b, or Pdk/Ldha/Slc16a induction, so PDC impairment was either buffered or displaced to metabolite, protein, or physiology readouts.

literature_claim: DLAT, PDHA1, DLD, DLST, OGDH, and related enzymes sit in the same PDC or mitochondrial 2-oxoacid/carbon-oxidation network and are plausible phenocopy candidates.
main_caveats: Many exact PDC regulators and subunits, including Pdhb, Pdhx, PDKs, PDPs, and Mpc2, were not perturbation targets in the parquet.
summary: Literature-obvious PDC and adjacent mitochondrial-carbon comparators failed to phenocopy Dlat in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Pdha1, Dld, Dlst, Ogdh, Mpc1, Bckdhb, Aco2, Idh3a, Mdh2, and Ndufs4 all had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and did not move Jarid2 in the Dlat responder, showing that the Dlat-Jarid2 result is not a generic pyruvate-oxidation or TCA loss signature.

literature_claim: UBA5 and UFC1 encode the E1 and E2 enzymes of UFMylation, a pathway tied to proteostasis and ER-stress homeostasis.
main_caveats: The Dlat cosine was only 0.089 for Uba5 and only one Dlat downstream gene existed; Ufc1 and Opa1 ranked nearby by full-vector cosine but did not share Jarid2 at FDR<0.10.
summary: The leading unbiased 151 signature neighbor was Uba5, not a PDC component, and only Uba5 shared Dlat's Jarid2-down feature at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This preserves a weak but data-nominated convergence between Dlat and UFMylation/proteostasis perturbation that would have been missed by testing only canonical PDC relatives.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: PDC, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, TCA enzymes, and DLD-dependent 2-oxoacid dehydrogenases share mitochondrial carbon metabolism and are plausible sources of correlated stress programs.
main_caveats: Each comparator response outside 151 was itself very small, usually one downstream gene.
summary: Related mitochondrial enzymes produced singleton effects in several forebrain groups where Dlat was null or weak.
why_it_matters: Dlat flatness in 008, 012, 017, 046, 052, 054, and 145 is not explained by those cell groups being globally unable to register mitochondrial enzyme perturbations, because Dlst, Ogdh, Pdha1, Aco2, or Mdh2 each yielded an FDR<0.10 downstream transcript in at least one of them.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: DLD is a shared mitochondrial E3 enzyme whose deep loss compromises several alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complexes and causes severe recessive metabolic disease.
main_caveats: The screen did not measure DNA indels or DLD enzyme activity; flat self-transcript FDR values therefore do not prove absence of protein knockout in individual nuclei.
summary: Dld loss of function was transcriptionally buffered across every recovered neuronal class: none of the 21 measured groups had a downstream gene at FDR<0.10, despite Dld mRNA being assayed in each group.
why_it_matters: This is an interpretable negative result for an enzyme at the center of PDH, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and BCKDH chemistry: an acute P16 mosaic perturbation did not by itself push juvenile postmitotic neurons into a detectable nuclear stress or identity program by P37-P44.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Mitochondrial dysfunction can activate ATF4/ISR and ATF5-linked UPRmt transcriptional programs containing mitochondrial chaperones, proteases, metabolic, and redox genes.
main_caveats: The tested marker panel is transcriptomic and nuclear; it cannot exclude a subthreshold metabolite or NADH/NAD+ phenotype.
summary: Canonical mitochondrial ISR, UPRmt, ER-stress, and antioxidant transcripts were absent from the Dld surface: Atf4, Atf5, Ddit3, Trib3, Asns, Hspa9, Hspd1, Clpp, Lonp1, Hmox1, Nqo1, Gclc, Gclm, Txnrd1, and Prdx5 were all FDR=1 in every measured group.
why_it_matters: The null is not just lack of cell-identity remodeling; it specifically says that this perturbation did not reach the mitochondrial-to-nuclear signaling threshold that a strong respiratory or matrix-protein insult should have exposed in snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: DLD acts in the same alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase chemistry as PDH, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and BCKDH components.
main_caveats: The comparator overlap is based on the same FDR<0.10 snRNA-seq readout and several comparator responses are only single downstream genes.
summary: Directly measured DLD-pathway perturbations were also sparse: Bckdhb, Bckdk, and Mpc1 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and Dlat, Dlst, Ogdh, Pdha1, Aco2, Mdh2, Sdha, and Suclg1 produced only one or two downstream genes each across the brain-wide panel.
why_it_matters: The Dld result is part of a broader postmitotic buffering of mitochondrial carbon-entry and TCA-enzyme perturbations rather than a unique annotation miss; same-pathway cross-perturbation therefore supports a threshold/reserve interpretation.

main_caveats: Restricted to targets and cell groups represented in the parquet; this is a transcriptomic-neighbor statement, not a protein-interaction statement.
summary: The data-driven full-transcriptome neighbor search found no robust Dld-like target: the strongest positive and negative signed-score correlations were only +0.025 and -0.022, and Safe_target-labeled perturbations appeared in both tails.
why_it_matters: This prevents a spurious pathway assignment from rank-level noise; Tuba1a and Klf7 had their own real restricted signatures, but Dld did not share an FDR-significant module with them.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: PSD-95 biology is centered on excitatory postsynaptic protein complexes, receptor anchoring, and synaptic plasticity rather than on direct transcriptional control.
main_caveats: DNA indels and PSD-95 protein were not measured, so this is a statement about persistent nuclear RNA only.
summary: Dlg4 perturbation was globally flat at the downstream snRNA level: all 22 measured neuronal groups had 0 non-Dlg4 genes at FDR<0.10 despite uniformly negative Dlg4 self-transcript logFC.
why_it_matters: A P16 sparse LoF of a core postsynaptic MAGUK did not create a persistent nuclear cell-state, stress, or compensation program over the 3-4 week assay window.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: PSD-95 belongs to a PSD-MAGUK family that can show redundancy and developmental compensation in AMPAR targeting, but that literature does not require paralog compensation to appear as mRNA induction after single postnatal Dlg4 loss.
main_caveats: Dlg1, Dlg2, and Dlg3 were not themselves perturbation targets, so only their mRNA behavior downstream of Dlg4 could be tested.
summary: Dlg4 loss did not transcriptionally induce MAGUK paralogs or rewrite mRNAs for represented receptor and PSD partners.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues against a stable Dlg1/Dlg2/Dlg3 mRNA compensation program after Dlg4 LoF; any compensation is likely protein-level, pre-existing, or combinatorial.

literature_claim: PSD-95 binds and organizes NMDAR-containing PSD complexes; family-level MAGUK depletion can reduce NMDAR responses.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic; it does not rule out Dlg4 effects on receptor anchoring or plasticity in the same neurons.
summary: NMDAR-subunit perturbations can be transcriptomically active in the same assay, but Dlg4 is not their mRNA phenocopy.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates loss of a PSD scaffold from loss of receptor subunits: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced FDR<0.10 genes in matched neuronal groups, while Dlg4 had zero downstream genes there.

literature_claim: The named genes encode PSD or transsynaptic proteins linked to glutamatergic synapse organization, a biology dominated by protein complexes rather than direct transcriptional regulation.
main_caveats: Convergence here means shared near-zero DE surfaces, not a shared signed DEG module.
summary: Several represented PSD scaffold or adhesion perturbations converged with Dlg4 by remaining close to transcriptionally flat.
why_it_matters: The common flatness of Syngap1, Shank2, Cacng2, Homer2, Magi2, Nlgn3, and Nrxn2 suggests that postsynaptic structural perturbations often displace to synaptic physiology or protein organization rather than to snRNA state in this P16 screen.

main_caveats: The top negative entry included a safe-target control measured in only six matched groups; no functional relationship is inferred from these tiny correlations.
summary: Unsupervised cross-perturbation search found no meaningful Dlg4 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The near-zero genome-wide correlations show that Dlg4 was not silently joining an unexpected stress, mitochondrial, ubiquitin, or developmental module elsewhere in the perturbation universe.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: De novo DLG4 LoF variants cause a human neurodevelopmental synaptopathy, and PSD-95 protein interactions are themselves pharmacologically targetable.
main_caveats: The experiment is mouse, sparse, postmitotic, and NeuN-enriched; it is not a developmental human disease model.
summary: The DLG4-related synaptopathy LoF axis lacks a durable P16-to-young-adult neuronal RNA biomarker in this assay.
why_it_matters: Human DLG4 LoF is pathogenic, but this screen points away from a stable pan-neuronal nuclear transcript as the limiting disease readout and toward PSD protein complexes, receptor physiology, and network function.

literature_claim: DLGAP4/SAPAP4 is a postsynaptic scaffold enriched at excitatory PSDs and expressed in several forebrain and thalamic areas.
main_caveats: The total downstream signature is only 10 genes, and two responder groups have fewer than 100 perturbed cells.
summary: Dlgap4 produced robust downstream RNA responses in only 3 of 23 recovered cell groups: L5 ET corticofugal glutamatergic neurons, CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons, and TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: The result turns an apparently broad postsynaptic scaffold into a highly sparse acute postnatal RNA responder and identifies one GABAergic responder that is not predicted by a purely excitatory-PSD model.

literature_claim: VGF-derived peptides, granins such as SCG2, and PTPRN/IA-2 are associated with regulated dense-core secretory vesicle biology in neurons or neuroendocrine cells.
main_caveats: This module is small and not known as a direct Dlgap4 target; Ptprn is a borderline L5 ET row at FDR 0.0848.
summary: Dlgap4 down-regulated a dense-core vesicle and neuropeptide module in the two glutamatergic responder classes, with Vgf recurring in both and Scg2 plus Ptprn down in L5 ET.
why_it_matters: Vgf is the only recurrent downstream gene and is therefore the cleanest RNA biomarker candidate for a subset of Dlgap4-responsive excitatory neurons, despite the absence of a global Dlgap4 signature.

literature_claim: DLGAP proteins are best known as excitatory postsynaptic-density scaffolds, while SCN1B/Navbeta1 regulates voltage-gated sodium channels and Ig-superfamily adhesive functions.
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes define the CNU-LGE signature; Tacc1 is a singleton microtubule-associated change and was not promoted to a pathway by itself.
summary: The CNU-LGE LSX GABA response consisted of Scn1b and Tacc1 down-regulation despite a flat-to-positive Dlgap4 self-transcript.
why_it_matters: This identifies an inhibitory striatal-like response arm for an excitatory PSD scaffold and links Dlgap4 to a sodium-channel beta subunit with adhesion and excitability roles.

literature_claim: DLGAP4 has an embryonic ventricular-zone role involving adherens-junction and actin organization, and PLEKHA7 is a conserved adherens-junction component.
main_caveats: All three Dlgap4 rows have FDR values between 0.098 and 0.100, and the assayed thalamic neurons are not embryonic radial glia.
summary: In TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, Dlgap4 caused a borderline membrane-adhesion and glycosylation response: Plekha7 and Xylt2 decreased while Igsf8 increased.
why_it_matters: The directionally mixed surface suggests compensatory remodeling of cell-junction or extracellular glycosaminoglycan-associated components rather than a direct reduction of PSD scaffold transcripts.

literature_claim: DLGAP4 interacts with beta-catenin-containing ventricular-zone polarity and junction complexes during cortical development.
main_caveats: The convergence is postnatal and thalamic, based on three exact shared genes embedded in a much larger Ctnnb1 signature.
summary: Ctnnb1 was the top exact shared-direction neighbor of Dlgap4, sharing Vgf down, Xylt2 down, and Igsf8 up in TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.

literature_claim: The Hsp70 proteostasis network cooperates with degradation systems, creating an a priori expectation that chaperone and proteasome perturbations might converge under a global protein-quality-control burden.

summary: The proteasome targets Psmc1 and Psmb4 were the least Dnajb4-like perturbations by whole-logFC correlation and were broad responders where Dnajb4 was flat.
why_it_matters: Chaperones and proteasome subunits are both proteostasis machinery, but the screen resolves an acute Dnajb4 deletion as qualitatively different from direct ubiquitin-proteasome insufficiency.

main_caveats: Whole-logFC correlations are dominated by non-significant genes for a null target and should not be interpreted mechanistically without FDR-supported overlap.
summary: The top positive whole-transcriptome neighbors of Dnajb4 were themselves null or nearly null, so there is no convincing positive Dnajb4 convergence partner in this analysis universe.
why_it_matters: The pre-literature neighbor search is therefore a guardrail: high positive ranks for Unc13b, Washc4, Adgrl2, Uqcrb, and Grik1 reflect flat-signature geometry, not a synaptic, WASH, adhesion-GPCR, or mitochondrial module downstream of Dnajb4.

literature_claim: Hsp90 and Hsp70/J-protein systems form an interconnected folding network rather than a one-gene-one-output linear pathway.
main_caveats: Hsp90ab1 is not a DnaJ paralog, and its on-target transcript depletion does not prove equivalent DNAJB4 protein loss.
summary: Hsp90ab1 mRNA depletion was itself buffered, producing zero downstream DE genes despite strong on-target transcript loss in many neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: This matched chaperone example shows that the screen can observe a chaperone transcript drop yet still report a downstream null, supporting a biological buffering model for constitutive chaperones in basal postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: PCGF3 is a component of PCGF3/5-containing variant PRC1 chromatin complexes, but the literature does not establish a direct Dnajb6-to-Pcgf3 neuronal pathway.
main_caveats: One downstream gene in only 30 perturbed nuclei; the Psmc1 recurrence shows the Pcgf3 marker is not Dnajb6-specific.
summary: Dnajb6 produced a single reproducible-looking chromatin hit, Pcgf3 up-regulation, restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: The only FDR<0.10 Dnajb6 response was not a heat-shock or aggregate-clearance gene; Pcgf3 belongs to a PCGF3/5 variant-PRC1 chromatin module, so this is a low-confidence biomarker hypothesis rather than a canonical chaperone program.

literature_claim: J-domain proteins route specific Hsp70 clients, and DNAJB6 has unusual anti-amyloid activity compared with many other DNAJ proteins.
main_caveats: Only Dnajb4 and several DNAJC genes, not DNAJB8 or DNAJB1, were present as perturbation targets; lack of transcriptomic output does not exclude protein-level chaperone effects.
summary: The expected HSP40/HSP90/CHIP relatives did not phenocopy Dnajb6.
why_it_matters: Dnajb4, Dnajc5, Dnajc19, Hsp90ab1, and Stub1 were all downstream-flat in the same Dnajb6-recovered groups, while Dnajc13 had only one hit; the shared absence argues against a generic J-protein transcriptome and against treating the Dnajb6 Pcgf3 event as a family-wide HSP40 response.
