literature_claim: HSP70/J-protein machines and the ER unfolded-protein response are transcriptionally coupled to proteotoxic and ER stress.
main_caveats: Comparator signatures are not direct Dnajb6 epistasis; Hspa8 and Hspa5 have broader essential chaperone activities than DNAJB6.
summary: The assay could detect HSP70, HSF1, and ER-UPR transcription when those nodes were perturbed, but Dnajb6 loss did not engage that response.
why_it_matters: Hspa8 induced Hsp90aa1 and Dnaja1, Hsf1 loss reduced Hsph1/Hsp90 genes, and Hspa5 induced Hsp90b1/Pdia4/Derl3/Herpud1/Asns in 151 TH Prkcd and other groups; the same genes were absent from Dnajb6, making the heat-shock/UPR null biologically informative rather than a snRNA-seq blind spot.

literature_claim: DNAJB6 biology intersects aggregate handling, including peptides incompletely degraded by the proteasome, but it is not itself a core proteasome particle.
main_caveats: Proteasome subunit loss is far more proximal and pleiotropic than DNAJB6 loss; the comparison is a detectability and pathway-placement contrast, not a claim of the same mechanism.
summary: Central proteasome subunits produced massive stress/neuronal down-regulation surfaces at similar cell counts, whereas Dnajb6 did not.
why_it_matters: Psmc1 and Psmb4 were broad responders in many Dnajb6-matched groups, with Psmb4 responding in 18 of 19; in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA they had 47 or 32 perturbed cells, close to Dnajb6's 30. This rejects a generic low-cell-count explanation for the Dnajb6 profile and places DNAJB6 outside the basal proteasome-stress axis of young neurons.

main_caveats: The comparison deliberately used nominal Dnajb6 rows because the FDR signature contained only Pcgf3; it is hypothesis-generating only.
summary: Unsupervised neighbors of the weak Dnajb6 nominal signature were themselves weak and biologically incoherent.
why_it_matters: The top restricted-profile neighbors were Mdh2, Hsd17b4, and Rgma, and the top anti-neighbors included Safe_target_94, Thra, and Reln; their FDR<0.10 surfaces ranged from zero to a few unrelated genes. Thus the neighbor calculation confirms that Dnajb6 has no robust transcriptomic module to align with, rather than revealing an unexpected pathway.

literature_claim: DNAJB6 suppresses aggregation of disease-associated amyloidogenic clients, and LGMDD1 is caused by dominant missense alleles rather than by a proven simple neuronal haploinsufficiency state.
main_caveats: The screen did not express mutant huntingtin, tau, alpha-synuclein, or Dnajb6 disease alleles and did not measure insoluble proteins.
summary: Acute Dnajb6 loss in healthy postmitotic neurons does not mimic dominant DNAJB6 myopathy or induced polyglutamine aggregation biology.
why_it_matters: LGMD-D1 mutations can behave as toxic Hsp70-gain alleles, and DNAJB6 protection against amyloid becomes most evident with amyloidogenic clients; the absence of heat-shock, UPR, autophagy, or proteasome bounce-back after simple CRISPR LoF redirects interpretation away from a basal neuronal transcriptional requirement and toward allele- and client-load-specific DNAJB6 functions.

literature_claim: Spred1 encodes a negative Ras-MAPK-ERK regulator with documented CNS activity.
main_caveats: Only one downstream DEG was detected from 57 perturbed nuclei; no canonical endosomal genes accompanied Spred1.
summary: Dnajc13 produced a one-gene, MH-LH TH Glut-restricted Spred1 induction.
why_it_matters: Spred1 is a Ras-MAPK-ERK antagonist; its isolated induction suggests a small receptor-signaling feedback event rather than a broad endolysosomal stress state.

literature_claim: RME-8/DNAJC13 is linked to the retromer/SNX/WASH axis and to autolysosome biology.
main_caveats: The comparator contrast is transcriptional; DNAJC13 indels and endosomal morphology were not measured.
summary: Dnajc13 did not phenocopy the Vps35/Rab7 endolysosomal transcriptional state in TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The matched-cell contrast shows that this screen can detect retromer/late-endosomal transcriptional consequences in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, so the Dnajc13 weak result is a selective uncoupling rather than a universal pathway-blind assay failure.

literature_claim: RME-8/DNAJC13 acts with HSC70/clathrin and is associated with retromer, WASH and autophagic lysosome reformation machinery.
main_caveats: Several exact RME-8 interactors, including Snx1 and Fam21/Washc2, were not perturbation targets; total DEG counts do not prove direct complex activity.
summary: Proximal RME-8 pathway comparators were heterogeneous and did not converge on the Dnajc13 surface.
why_it_matters: Vps35, Cltc, Hspa8, Rab7, Becn1, Atg5 and Lamp2 generated detectable but distinct responses, whereas Washc4, Dnm1, Atg16l1, Map1lc3a and Vps35l were flat; RME-8 loss therefore cannot be read as a generic WASH, clathrin, HSC70 or core-autophagy perturbation in this assay.

literature_claim: Cell and neuronal studies predict altered ATG9A trafficking, reduced autophagic flux, and lysosome morphology defects after RME-8/DNAJC13 depletion.
main_caveats: A trafficking or autophagic-flux defect could occur without changing nuclear mRNA; this is a negative transcriptional result only.
summary: The expected Dnajc13 autophagy, lysosomal and HSP secondary program was absent at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The absence of Atg9a, Lamp2, Sqstm1, v-ATPase, cathepsin, calreticulin and HSP/DnaJ induction argues that acute Dnajc13 loss did not create a severe proteostasis or lysosomal-stress state detectable by juvenile neuronal snRNA-seq.

main_caveats: The cosine calculation used the whole weak score surface; it is useful mainly as a rejection test here.
summary: Whole-surface Dnajc13 signature neighbors were numerically tiny and failed an FDR-overlap check.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative cosine neighbors were not biologically meaningful phenocopies or antagonists, preventing over-interpretation of a near-null target by noisy rank similarity.

literature_claim: Loss of DNAJC19 is expected to compromise mitochondrial protein import/cardiolipin homeostasis and severe mitochondrial import stress can drive an ATF4/ISR transcriptional program.
main_caveats: DNA indels and mitochondrial protein import were not directly measured; the result is bounded to sparse postnatal neuronal nuclei and cannot exclude stronger biallelic loss or heart/myeloid phenotypes.
summary: Dnajc19 loss-of-function was globally transcriptome-buffered: none of the 22 recovered neuronal groups had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: DNAJC19 is a mitochondrial inner-membrane import and cardiolipin-remodeling disease gene, so the absence of Ddit3/Asns/Chac1-like stress output is a biological result of this P16 mosaic neuronal assay rather than a single-cell-type oversight.

literature_claim: Mitochondrial inner-membrane dysfunction or perturbed import can signal through DELE1/HRI to an ATF4 integrated-stress transcriptional program.
main_caveats: This is a cross-perturbation inference; Opa1 and Lonp1 perturb different mitochondrial nodes and need not be quantitative surrogates for DNAJC19 import-motor loss.
summary: The Dnajc19 null cannot be explained by inability of this snRNA-seq screen to detect mitochondrial stress, because Opa1 and Lonp1 perturbations in the same parquet induced the expected ATF4/ISR-like genes.
why_it_matters: Opa1 up-regulated Asns, Ddit3, Chac1, Aldh1l2, Shmt2, Slc7a5, Mars1/Cars and down-regulated mt-encoded respiratory transcripts across 10 matched cell groups, while Lonp1 induced Ddit3/Herpud1 in a smaller subset; thus Dnajc19 is specifically uncoupled from that stress threshold in this experiment.

main_caveats: The search used whole-surface Wilcoxon score correlations; a near-zero Dnajc19 vector is intrinsically poorly suited to discovering neighbors.
summary: A model-universe search found no meaningful Dnajc19 signature neighbor: the largest real-gene score correlation was only r=0.041 and the strongest inverse real-gene correlation was r=-0.016.
why_it_matters: The top data-nominated neighbors were statistical near-zeroes rather than a hidden co-regulated module, so downstream biology should be read as a flat Dnajc19 surface rather than as weak convergence with Diaph2, Copg1, Gucy2e, Htr4, Bin1, or Kpna3.

literature_claim: DNAJC19 is a specialized mitochondrial inner-membrane J protein associated with TIM23/PAM and prohibitin-cardiolipin biology, whereas other targeted DNAJ genes and many OXPHOS targets are pathway-adjacent rather than same-complex substitutes.
main_caveats: Most direct DNAJC19 binding partners were not targeted, so this is a neighborhood rejection, not a full same-complex epistasis map.
summary: Represented DNAJ-family and proximal mitochondrial comparators did not phenocopy Dnajc19; the only broad inner-membrane stress phenotype among the checked relatives came from Opa1, while core TIM23/PAM members were not targeted.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting DNAJC19 as interchangeable with generic DNAJ chaperones or with every nuclear mitochondrial gene in the screen; the measurable family/pathway neighborhood was mostly buffered, and the most proximal import-motor partners were absent from the perturbation universe.

main_caveats: Only one downstream transcript reached FDR<0.10, in 52 perturbed nuclei; this should be treated as an isolated candidate response rather than a pathway.
summary: Dnajc5 generated a single downstream FDR<0.10 event: Fndc3a up-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
why_it_matters: The only positive biology in the target surface is a restricted one-gene response, not a pan-neuronal synaptic, heat-shock, ISR, autophagy, or lysosomal program.

literature_claim: CSPα/Dnajc5 is a synaptic-vesicle co-chaperone for the Hsc70-SGT/SNAP-25 axis; mouse CSPα knockout causes presynaptic degeneration and full CSPα knockout cortex can show neuronal synaptic repression with autophagy up-regulation.
main_caveats: The absent program is transcriptomic; this assay cannot directly measure SNAP-25 folding, SNARE assembly, vesicle exocytosis, or CSPα protein remaining after indels.
summary: The Dnajc5 perturbation did not recover the expected CSPα synaptic-maintenance, Hsp70/co-chaperone, ISR, or autophagy nuclear programs.
why_it_matters: Full CSPα loss is sufficient to produce synaptic dysfunction, SNAP-25/SNARE defects, neurodegeneration, and in a full-knockout cortical snRNA context synaptic-pathway repression plus autophagy up-regulation; the acute sparse P16 LoF surface stopped at one FDR gene.

literature_claim: CSPα and Hsc70 cooperate with SGT to maintain SNAP-25 for SNARE-complex assembly.
main_caveats: Hspa8 itself produced only 14 FDR<0.10 genes, and Sgta/Snap25 perturbations were not represented as comparator targets.
summary: Hspa8, the Hsc70 partner in the CSPα chaperone system, showed a small heat-shock/co-chaperone replacement signature that Dnajc5 did not share.
why_it_matters: The direct Hsp70 arm of the chaperone machinery is not transcriptionally equivalent to acute Dnajc5 loss in this dataset; the expected complex relationship does not translate into a matched snRNA signature.

literature_claim: Clathrin and Synj1 act in synaptic-vesicle membrane retrieval and endocytic recycling, pathways adjacent to the presynaptic vesicle cycle served by CSPα.
main_caveats: Cltc is an endocytic coat component, not a CSPα complex member; Stx1b and Synj1 were also downstream-null here.
summary: Cltc, unlike Dnajc5, produced a broad response in eight neuronal groups, including immediate-early, synaptic, and membrane-trafficking genes.
why_it_matters: A presynaptic-vesicle/endocytic target can generate robust nuclear DE in the same screen, so the flat Dnajc5 surface is more specific than a generic failure to detect synaptic-vesicle biology.

literature_claim: CSPα/DNAJC5 is a specialized cysteine-string Hsp40 co-chaperone rather than a generic DnaJ family member.
main_caveats: The true CSP paralogs Dnajc5b and Dnajc5g were not represented as perturbation targets, so the measured contrast is within more distant DnaJ relatives.
summary: Represented DnaJ/Hsp40-family perturbations did not phenocopy the one-gene Dnajc5 signature.
why_it_matters: The screen preserves client and compartment specificity within the Hsp40 family: neither Dnajb4/Dnajc19 null surfaces nor the single Dnajb6 and Dnajc13 hits converged on Fndc3a or the CSPα-expected programs.

main_caveats: The screen did not install CLN4 missense/deletion alleles and did not assay non-neuronal lysosomal storage.
summary: Acute Dnajc5 loss-of-function did not phenocopy DNAJC5/CLN4 adult neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis biology at the neuronal transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: The result argues against using a sparse acute LoF snRNA signature as a direct surrogate for dominant cysteine-string DNAJC5 disease variants; allele-specific palmitoylation, mislocalization, aggregation, lysosomal storage, or complete/longer CSPα loss must be modeled directly.

literature_claim: DNAL1/Dnal1 encodes the conserved LC1 outer-dynein-arm subunit used in motile-ciliated tissues, whereas mammalian brain neurons carry primary cilia rather than multiciliated outer-dynein-arm axonemes.
main_caveats: Outer-dynein-arm biology was not directly assayed in ependymal cells; DNA editing was not measured, so the interpretation rests on downstream flatness and target biology rather than verified indels.
summary: Dnal1 loss produced a near-pan-neuronal negative surface in this P16 acute CRISPR screen: among 22 measured NeuN+ groups only one downstream gene, Nup205 in L5 ET neurons, passed FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result is consistent with Dnal1 being an axonemal outer-dynein-arm component for motile cilia rather than a required postmitotic neuronal primary-cilium transcriptomic regulator.

literature_claim: NUP205 is a nuclear-pore component with experimentally described ciliary roles.
main_caveats: Only one gene crossed the liberal FDR<0.10 threshold, q=0.0957, with 77 perturbed L5 ET nuclei; no broader Nup family or ciliary comparator support was recovered.
summary: The sole robust downstream Dnal1 signal was an isolated Nup205 decrease in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut neurons.
why_it_matters: NUP205 links nuclear-pore biology to cilia, so the L5 ET hit is a plausible but hypothesis-generating sentinel for a cilia-associated nuclear-envelope axis rather than a complete pathway response.

literature_claim: Outer-dynein-arm LC1 is a motile-cilium motor subunit, whereas IFT, BBSome, dynein-2, and RFX genes support the architecture or trafficking of cilia, including neuronal primary cilia.
main_caveats: Most ciliary comparators were themselves very weak in the neuronal DE atlas, so the contrast is an absence of convergence rather than a comparison to a strong primary-cilium signature.
summary: Represented primary-cilium and ciliary-trafficking perturbations did not phenocopy Dnal1; their restricted-signature cosines were near zero and no comparator shared the L5 ET Nup205 hit at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The screen keeps axonemal motility, primary-cilium assembly, dynein-2 retrograde trafficking, BBSome, and ciliogenesis-transcription-factor perturbations as separable weak signatures in neurons instead of one generic ciliopathy transcriptome.

main_caveats: Cosines were computed on the 50 largest absolute-score Dnal1 features per cell group because the FDR signature contained only one downstream gene; the comparison is therefore restricted-signature support only.
summary: The closest data-driven transcriptomic neighbors of Dnal1 were weak and biologically non-obvious; the top cosine was only 0.1307 with Map1lc3a and the strongest anti-neighbor was -0.1125 with Zfp292.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation search did not reveal a hidden robust stress, autophagy, synaptic, or ciliary module behind the Dnal1 surface; the nearest-neighbor structure is consistent with an assay-floor signature.

literature_claim: Dynamin-1 is a neuronal GTPase required for efficient activity-dependent synaptic-vesicle fission, but single-isoform loss can be supported partly by dynamin-independent or other dynamin-isoform mechanisms.

summary: P16 Dnm1 CRISPR produced a pervasive downstream-zero signature: 0 non-Dnm1 genes reached FDR<0.10 in every one of 22 measured neuronal groups, even though the Dnm1 transcript decreased in 21/22 groups and was FDR-significant in 10.
why_it_matters: This separates Dnm1 transcript engagement from a nuclear cell-state program: acute sparse loss in young postmitotic neurons did not trigger the transcriptional stress or synaptic remodeling that a severe vesicle-recycling failure might have produced.

main_caveats: The screen did not introduce patient variants, quantify seizure output, or measure inhibitory synaptic transmission.
summary: The GABAergic Dnm1 surface was also downstream-null, including Pvalb, Sst, CNU-MGE, CNU-LGE, hypothalamic GABA, midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA and cerebellar GABA groups; no immediate-early, stress/proteostasis or synaptic sentinel reached FDR<0.10 anywhere.
why_it_matters: This warns against reading simple postmitotic Dnm1 LoF as a transcriptional surrogate for dominant-negative DNM1 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, whose pathogenic alleles can poison dynamin assemblies and whose GABAergic phenotypes are circuit/allele dependent.

literature_claim: Early cell-specific Dnmt3a deletion blocks neuronal non-CG/CpG methylation maturation and yields synaptic and bidirectional RNA changes.
main_caveats: No DNA-indel or methylome readout was collected, so the data show absence of downstream nuclear RNA response rather than absence of editing or absence of methylation effects.
summary: Dnmt3a loss at P16 produced a transcriptome-wide zero rather than a neuronal mCH-writer signature: no measured neuronal group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The dominant biology is buffering of an acute, sparse perturbation of a cumulative DNA-methylation writer, not a selective Dnmt3a program in one neuronal class. The result sharply separates P16 mosaic loss from embryonic or perinatal Dnmt3a cKOs that erase the methylation landscape before maturation.

literature_claim: In inhibitory-neuron cKOs, MeCP2 is a restricted reader of Dnmt3a-dependent methylation and the two knockouts share a subset of same-direction DE genes.
main_caveats: The comparison is across distinct target cell numbers and uses broad snRNA cell groups rather than purified striatal inhibitory neurons.
summary: The mCH writer and its represented methylation readers uncouple in the P16 screen: Mecp2 had a reproducible DE surface while Dnmt3a, Mbd2 and Mbd5 had only zero or single-gene surfaces and no shared robust DE with Dnmt3a.
why_it_matters: If acute writer loss simply removed the mCH signal read by MeCP2, the Dnmt3a and Mecp2 signatures should have converged. Instead, MeCP2 loss acts immediately on pre-existing methylated chromatin whereas acute Dnmt3a loss does not erase that substrate over 3-4 weeks.

main_caveats: The APP/presenilin/tau connection is indirect relative to the Rac/WAVE/GSK3β Dock3 mechanism, and this assay did not measure APP processing or tau phosphorylation.

why_it_matters: It separates DOCK3's older presenilin/APP/tau associations from an acute RNA phenocopy in postnatal mouse neurons, consistent with those links also acting through protein processing, localization, or phosphorylation endpoints.

literature_claim: DPM1 supplies Dol-P-Man for ER glycosylation pathways and DPM1-CDG is a multisystem neurodevelopmental glycosylation disorder, so loss of function is expected to impair glycoprotein handling rather than behave as a neuronally silent transcription-factor knockout.
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes passed FDR<0.10; DNA indels and glycan occupancy were not measured.
summary: Dpm1 loss produced a detectable but very small response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Pdia6 up and Ttyh3 down at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result shows that postnatal neuronal Dpm1 perturbation can be sensed transcriptionally, but it collapses the expected broad glycosylation-stress program to a two-gene, thalamus-restricted footprint.

literature_claim: DHDDS makes the dolichol carrier backbone, whereas DPM1 consumes dolichol phosphate to make Dol-P-Man; both are expected to influence dolichol-dependent glycosylation.
main_caveats: The argument is based on the two Dpm1 FDR genes; Dhdds has many additional genes that are not robust in Dpm1.
summary: Dhdds, an upstream dolichol-backbone enzyme, reproduced both Dpm1-significant directions in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and did so within a much broader 168-gene response.
why_it_matters: The paired Pdia6/Ttyh3 convergence roots the Dpm1-positive cells in the dolichol/glycosylation axis rather than an unrelated single-gene artifact, while the larger Dhdds response shows that upstream dolichol depletion is a stronger way to breach ER-glycan homeostasis in these neurons.

literature_claim: Hypoglycosylation can create ER folding stress detectable through the UPR, and GFPT1 sits at the rate-limiting entry to the hexosamine pathway that feeds glycosylation and is connected to XBP1-dependent UPR signaling.
main_caveats: Dpm1 nominally moved several UPR genes, but only Pdia6 met FDR<0.10; this finding rests on robust absence of the Gfpt1-like UPR set in Dpm1.
summary: Dpm1 exposed only a Pdia6 edge of the ER-folding/UPR program that Gfpt1 strongly activated in the same thalamic cell group.
why_it_matters: The same assay readily recovered Hspa5, Ddit3, Herpud1, Xbp1, Atf4, Hsp90b1, Manf, Pdia4, and Calr after Gfpt1 perturbation, so the missing full UPR after Dpm1 is an informative thresholded or buffered Dol-P-Man result, not a failure of snRNA-seq to see ER stress.

literature_claim: FKTN acts in alpha-dystroglycan O-mannose glycan maturation and PIGN in GPI-anchor synthesis, two distal Dol-P-Man-dependent branches.
main_caveats: Dpm2 and Dpm3, the same-complex DPM synthase partners, were not available as perturbation targets.
summary: The downstream O-mannosylation and GPI-anchor comparators Fktn and Pign did not phenocopy Dpm1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Although DPM1 supplies mannose to O-mannosylation and GPI-anchor biosynthesis, the branch-specific perturbations that were present in the screen were flat where Dpm1 responded; thalamic Pdia6 induction is therefore coupled to the Dol-P-Man/dolichol-carrier axis rather than to every distal glycosylation disease gene.

main_caveats: A sparse two-gene Dpm1 signature makes global correlation insensitive; Dhdds convergence was found by pathway-aware follow-up, not by high whole-surface correlation.
summary: The unsupervised whole-surface neighbor search found no strong Dpm1-like or Dpm1-opposite perturbation signature.
why_it_matters: The highest signed-score correlations were near zero and the leading non-glycosylation neighbors failed to reproduce the 151 Pdia6/Ttyh3 effect, so Dpm1 should be interpreted through the local glycosylation comparators rather than as a member of a broad global transcriptional module.

literature_claim: DPP6 is a membrane auxiliary subunit of Kv4 A-type potassium channels with electrophysiological effects on dendritic and action-potential excitability.
main_caveats: A null RNA signature is not a null indel assay; Cas9 editing was not sequenced and Kv4 channel gating was not measured.
summary: P16 mosaic Dpp6 loss produced no FDR-defined downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The result separates DPP6's channel-auxiliary biology from a nuclear RNA state: three cell groups showed significant lowering of the Dpp6 transcript itself, yet no non-target gene reached FDR<0.10 anywhere.

literature_claim: DPP6 acts with Kv4.2/Kv4.3 pore-forming channels and KChIP proteins in native neuronal A-type K+ channel complexes.

why_it_matters: Dpp6 and Kcnd3 did not form a same-complex RNA module: both had zero downstream hits in the 22 matched Dpp6 groups and their whole-surface signatures were orthogonal.

main_caveats: Cosines were computed on the Wilcoxon-score surface and are descriptive; they collapse cell groups and genes into one vector.
summary: The all-target signature-neighbor search put Dpp6 at the noise floor rather than in a coherent convergent or antagonistic module.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative whole-surface neighbors, Nr4a1 and Fbxo11, had very small signed cosines and no shared FDR-supported genes with Dpp6, so downstream interpretation should not be transferred from either target.

literature_claim: DPP6 loss or antibody-mediated DPPX dysfunction is expected to perturb Kv4-dependent neuronal excitability and can be associated with CNS hyperexcitability in disease.
main_caveats: Only RNA markers were tested; fast activity, dendritic A-current gradients, and surface Kv4 protein were outside the assay.
summary: Dpp6 loss did not transcriptionally backfill the Kv4 complex or elicit an immediate-early activity program.
why_it_matters: If sparse Dpp6 loss had generated a chronic cell-autonomous hyperactivity or channel-compensation state, Kv4-family, KChIP, or Fos/Junb/Egr1/Npas4/Arc/Bdnf transcripts could have moved; their FDR values were all 1.0 across the Dpp6 surface.

why_it_matters: Dpyd behaves as a transcriptionally isolated, weak responder in this analysis universe rather than clustering with a strong hidden module.

why_it_matters: The lone reproducible FDR hit points to a nuclear RNA-processing factor rather than to a broad immediate-early, stress, proteostasis, autophagy, or synaptic-remodeling program; Zfp326 is therefore a restricted biomarker candidate, not evidence for a pathway-wide DBIRD state change.

main_caveats: The comparator search used all matched Wilcoxon-score rows, and Drd2 itself has only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene; the correlations should be read as a rejection of strong modules, not as mechanistic evidence linking the named genes.
summary: A genome-scale signature-neighbor search found no strong transcriptomic convergence or anti-convergence with Drd2.
why_it_matters: The Drd2 surface lacked both an expected pathway neighbor and an unexpected data-driven module; its one Zfp326 hit was not reused by the closest whole-surface positive or negative neighbors.

summary: The all-target neighbor search placed Drd4 in background rather than in a reproducible co-signature module.

summary: Efemp1 loss produced no robust cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptome in any recovered cell group: all 20 measured groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This makes the main result a pan-measured neuronal null rather than a missed focal responder: under P16 sparse CRISPR in NeuN+ nuclei, Efemp1 did not behave like a postmitotic neuronal transcriptional dependency.

why_it_matters: This is an informative context-specific zero: Egr2 does not behave as a constitutive basal transcriptional dependency in the sampled P16-to-P37/44 neurons, even though it is a strong developmental and peripheral myelination regulator elsewhere.

why_it_matters: Mafb was both the top data-driven neighbor and a literature-obvious r5/r6 comparator, yet its matched response was only one Pvalb DEG; Sox10 was fully flat. This decouples the embryonic/PNS Egr2 network from the postmitotic CNS assay.

main_caveats: Wdr26 and Huwe1 are data-driven comparators, not Egr2 pathway members.
summary: Wdr26 and Huwe1 produced robust DE in the same broad cell classes where Egr2 remained flat.
why_it_matters: This rejects a purely pipeline-wide or cell-count-wide explanation of the Egr2 zero; matched P37-44 neuronal nuclei could yield large Wilcoxon signatures for other targets.

literature_claim: EGR2 variants cause peripheral myelinopathies and Egr2/Krox20 directly regulates Schwann-cell myelination genes.
main_caveats: This does not test Schwann cells, axonal myelination physiology, or human dominant-negative EGR2 alleles.
summary: The Egr2 perturbation did not engage the peripheral myelin gene module most relevant to EGR2-linked CMT and congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy.
why_it_matters: A sparse postnatal CNS neuron assay is not a positive model for therapeutic hypotheses centered on Schwann-cell Egr2/Sox10/NAB control of Mpz or Pmp22 dosage.

literature_claim: GLP/G9a is a broadly important H3K9 repressor in neural development and postnatal forebrain neurons, and EHMT1 haploinsufficiency causes Kleefstra syndrome.
main_caveats: Engagement was inferred only from guide assignment; the self-transcript was not FDR-depleted, which is expected for Cas9 indel perturbations and does not rule out active knockout.
summary: Ehmt1 loss was a very sparse postnatal neuronal transcriptomic perturbation: only thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells and midbrain glutamatergic cells had any downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: A Kleefstra-syndrome chromatin regulator did not create a pan-neuronal snRNA program when edited after neuronal specification; that focuses interpretation on a small responder surface rather than on absent cortical or hippocampal pathways.

literature_claim: Postnatal GLP/G9a deficiency can derepress non-neuronal and progenitor genes in mature forebrain neurons through loss of H3K9-mediated repression.
main_caveats: This is a tiny seven-gene module; non-neuronal identity leakage is an interpretation of gene identity and H3K9 biology rather than a formally enriched pathway.
summary: The main Ehmt1-positive signature was a seven-gene thalamic module dominated by up-regulation of Abhd12b, Endou, Smtn, Stxbp2, Msra, and Atp2a1 with Vwc2 as the only down-regulated hit.
why_it_matters: The direction is compatible with local relief of repressive chromatin at a few lineage-incongruent or homeostatic loci, not with a broad collapse of synaptic or protocadherin expression.

main_caveats: Single-gene FDR support; no second FDR<0.10 gene in this cell group.
summary: The 155 MB Glut response was a singleton Nrip3 up-regulation.
why_it_matters: It preserves the only statistically robust midbrain glutamatergic hit while preventing the one gene from being over-expanded into a pathway.

literature_claim: EHMT1 belongs to an H3K9 transcriptional repression axis; SETDB1 is an indirect H3K9-pathway comparator whereas CHD4 and SIN3A are data-nominated chromatin repressors.
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to Ehmt1 FDR features and the overlap spans only three to four genes.
summary: The Ehmt1 thalamic module converged most strongly with Chd4, Setdb1, and Sin3a, which re-induced Abhd12b/Smtn/Msra in the same direction.
why_it_matters: The best measured positive neighbors were chromatin repressors rather than canonical synaptic genes, supporting the interpretation that the small Ehmt1 TH signature reports a local repressive-chromatin module.

main_caveats: Data-driven contrast only; it does not establish direct regulation between these targets and Ehmt1.
summary: Uba5, Cic, Elp1, Smarcc2, and Yy1 opposed the Ehmt1 TH module despite being strong responders in the same cell group.
why_it_matters: The thalamic genes are regulatable in this assay and are not a generic stress or power artifact; related or strong chromatin perturbations can push the same loci in the opposite direction.

literature_claim: Prior EHMT1 models implicate BDNF-dependent synaptic scaling, NMDAR signaling, hippocampal dysfunction, and embryonically established repression of protocadherins.
main_caveats: Absence is assessed only at the mRNA level and only in NeuN-enriched nuclei; no H3K9me2, electrophysiology, or DNA-indel data were collected.
summary: Ehmt1 did not recover the expected protocadherin, BDNF, or NMDA-receptor transcriptional programs anywhere in the 22 measured groups.
why_it_matters: The result argues that Kleefstra-relevant cortical, hippocampal, and synaptic phenotypes are not reproduced simply by sparse P16 Ehmt1 LoF followed by baseline snRNA-seq at P37-P44.

literature_claim: ZNF644 and WIZ bind G9a/GLP and regulate its chromatin recruitment for H3K9 methylation-dependent gene repression.
main_caveats: Negative for Zfp644 is not definitive because its perturbed-cell counts in matched groups were lower than Ehmt1 and ZNF644 biology is strongest in progenitors.
summary: The measurable G9a/GLP recruitment cofactor Zfp644 did not phenocopy Ehmt1 in the matched thalamic or midbrain responder groups, while Ehmt2 and Wiz were not represented as perturbation targets.
why_it_matters: The closest textbook complex could not explain the observed signature: the main enzymatic paralog was absent from the screen, and the represented recruiter was transcriptionally silent in the cell groups where Ehmt1 responded.

literature_claim: EIF2AK4/GCN2 is an eIF2α kinase that is activated most canonically by amino-acid deficiency and other stresses to initiate the ISR.
main_caveats: DNA indel engagement was not measured, 215 MB Dopa was not recovered, and low-count groups such as 217 P MY Pineal Glut provide weaker individual nulls.
summary: Postnatal Eif2ak4 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream DE in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result makes the absence of a constitutive GCN2-dependent neuronal transcriptome the primary phenotype: the pooled AAV perturbation did not expose a basal ISR, proteostasis, redox, lysosomal, translation, or synaptic mRNA program in juvenile postmitotic neurons.

main_caveats: This dataset did not challenge mice with amino-acid deprivation or another GCN2-activating stress; immediate ISR relatives were features, but not perturbation targets, except Eif2ak4.
summary: No canonical ATF4/amino-acid-starvation or compensatory eIF2α-kinase mRNA program was recovered after Eif2ak4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The null includes the genes that the literature would nominate first—Atf4 targets and other eIF2α kinases—so the absence is informative for an unstressed in-vivo neuronal state rather than a failure to annotate the correct pathway.

why_it_matters: The unbiased comparison rejects the possibility that Eif2ak4 had a hidden recurrent module resembling another assayed perturbation despite failing gene-level FDR thresholds.

literature_claim: Germline GCN2 loss altered hippocampal LTP, memory, ATF4 translation, and CREB activity.
main_caveats: The perturbation was postmitotic and mosaic, the cell groups are broad pooled excitatory classes, and snRNA-seq was not coupled to LTP induction.

why_it_matters: GCN2 can control hippocampal ATF4 translation and CREB activity, but the juvenile sparse Eif2ak4 perturbation had 0 downstream DE in both hippocampal excitatory groups, and direct Creb1 loss itself responded only outside those pools in the matched query.

literature_claim: Biallelic EIF2AK4 mutations cause recessive pulmonary veno-occlusive disease, a pulmonary vascular form of pulmonary hypertension.
main_caveats: Pulmonary endothelial, smooth-muscle, immune, and vascular-wall cells were outside the NeuN-enriched brain assay, so the conclusion is lineage exclusion, not a PVOD mechanism test.
summary: PVOD/PAH genetics did not map to a neuronal Eif2ak4 signature in this screen.
why_it_matters: The biallelic human EIF2AK4 disease axis is pulmonary vascular; the lack of neuronal Eif2ak4 response, together with mostly flat Bmpr/Smad/vascular comparators, argues against treating this brain dataset as a model of that lineage-restricted pathology.

literature_claim: Eif4a2 encodes an eIF4F ATP-dependent RNA helicase with miRNA/Ccr4-Not functions that could change mRNA fate.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; only two downstream genes passed FDR<0.10, so mechanistic interpretation is narrow.
summary: Acute Eif4a2 loss produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured neuronal groups, and the true transcriptional responders were restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The sparse surface argues that Eif4a2 is not a broad postmitotic mRNA-destabilization trigger in this assay, even though its own transcript was significantly reduced in five groups.

literature_claim: Cadm4-mediated axoglial adhesion regulates CNS myelination.
main_caveats: Cadm4 is a single transcript in a neuronal nuclear readout; the experiment did not sample oligodendrocyte or Schwann-cell biology.
summary: Cadm4 was the sole robust non-self gene in the thalamic 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.
why_it_matters: Cadm4 is an adhesion molecule with established axoglial biology, so the single-gene effect points to an adhesion/myelination-adjacent marker rather than to canonical translation-factor mRNA feedback.

literature_claim: Drebrin/DBN1 participates in dendritic-spine actin remodeling and synaptic plasticity.
main_caveats: One DE gene supports a marker hypothesis only; the assay does not measure spine morphology or synaptic physiology.
summary: Dbn1 was the sole robust non-self gene in the 191 MB P MY GABA response.
why_it_matters: Dbn1 encodes drebrin, an actin-associated regulator of dendritic spines, making the brainstem GABA effect more synaptic/cytoskeletal than ISR-, UPR-, or ribosome-gene biased.

literature_claim: eIF4A2 and eIF4A perturbations are expected to act first on translation initiation of selected mRNAs, often with ribosome-loading changes that need not appear as RNA-level stress.
main_caveats: The dataset did not run ribosome profiling or proteomics, so absence of RNA stress is not absence of translational dysregulation.
summary: The Eif4a2 surface did not recover an integrated-stress, unfolded-protein, proteostasis, ribosomal, or eIF4F transcriptional bounce-back program.
why_it_matters: If Eif4a2 loss were causing a secondary RNA-level stress response, snRNA-seq should have recovered stress genes among the FDR<0.10 set; instead every robust downstream transcript was Cadm4 or Dbn1.

literature_claim: eIF4A2 acts with Ccr4-Not, eIF4H stimulates eIF4A helicase activity, mTOR regulates eIF4F availability through the eIF4E arm, and DDX3X is a related post-transcriptional DEAD-box helicase.
main_caveats: Several most-obvious paralogs or cofactors, including Eif4a1, Eif4a3, Eif4e, Eif4b, Ddx6, Cnot7, and Cnot8, were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Represented Ccr4-Not/eIF4F/mTOR comparators did not phenocopy the two Eif4a2 responder signatures.
why_it_matters: Although CNOT1, EIF4H, EIF4G1, MTOR, and DDX3X are pathway or mechanistic neighbors of RNA-helicase translation control, their perturbations either responded in different groups or with different genes, separating Eif4a2 from a generic eIF4F/Ccr4-Not mRNA signature.

main_caveats: The neighbor metric used nominal Eif4a2 features because the FDR<0.10 surface contained only two downstream genes; cosines were small.
summary: The top phenotype-first signature neighbor was Ufc1, not a canonical eIF4F or miRNA-pathway target, and the convergence was concentrated in a shared thalamic Cadm4 decrease.
why_it_matters: This preserves a data-nominated, non-textbook relationship while keeping it exploratory: Ufc1 was rank 1 by restricted nominal Eif4a2 features and also down-regulated Cadm4 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Ufc1 was far broader than Eif4a2.

literature_claim: Human EIF4A2 variants produce neurodevelopmental disorder through both loss- and gain-of-function mechanisms, and EIF4A2 haploinsufficiency can produce dystonia-tremor.
main_caveats: The assay is mouse, juvenile, postmitotic, and LoF-only; gain-of-function missense alleles and protein/ribosome phenotypes are outside scope.
summary: The mouse P16 mosaic Eif4a2 LoF phenotype is compatible with EIF4A2 disease being a selective translation-timing problem rather than a pan-neuronal mRNA-collapse state.
why_it_matters: Human EIF4A2 loss-of-function can cause dystonia and EIF4A2 variants can cause neurodevelopmental disease, but this postmitotic snRNA-seq assay found no large cell-autonomous mRNA program after acute Eif4a2 targeting.

literature_claim: eIF4G1 is the scaffold of the cap-dependent eIF4F complex; mammalian cells also encode a functional eIF4GII/EIF4G3 homolog and alternative eIF4F assemblies.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot read out ribosome occupancy or protein synthesis directly; DNA indels and Eif4g1 protein depletion were not measured.
summary: Eif4g1 loss produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptomic response in any of the 21 recovered postnatal neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: A core eIF4F scaffold would be expected to perturb cap-dependent initiation, yet the P16-to-P37/44 mosaic loss-of-function surface is pan-null at the nuclear mRNA level; this is a biological negative for secondary transcription, not evidence that editing failed.

direction: ISR genes up in Opa1/Elp1 but absent in Eif4g1
literature_claim: The integrated stress response induces ATF4 and amino-acid homeostasis genes, and loss of the cap-binding eIF4E component can secondarily dysregulate amino-acid gene expression.
main_caveats: The positive ISR benchmarks are other perturbation targets, not Eif4g1 rescues; Uba5 was a near-zero full-profile neighbor rather than a mechanistic eIF4F relative.
summary: An ATF4/amino-acid stress program that is readily observed after Opa1 and Elp1 perturbation was absent after Eif4g1.
why_it_matters: The absence of Asns, Cars, Mars1, Chac1, Ddit3 and related ISR genes is an informative Eif4g1 result: overlapping neuronal groups in the same Wilcoxon universe could detect this secondary stress program when it was engaged.

literature_claim: eIF4A and eIF4H act with eIF4G in 5-prime-UTR unwinding, and the TSC/mTORC1/4E-BP axis regulates access of eIF4E to cap-dependent initiation.
main_caveats: Mtor and Rptor single-gene perturbations may be compensated within mTOR complexes; the Tsc2 transcriptional program was not mechanistically decomposed here.
summary: The individually perturbed eIF4F/mTOR cap-initiation arm was flat or extremely weak, whereas Tsc2 loss generated hundreds of DEGs in matched neurons.
why_it_matters: This separates loss of Eif4g1, Eif4a2, Eif4h, Mtor or Rptor from Tsc2 disinhibition in the same assay, arguing that the dataset can see mTOR-adjacent neuronal transcription but that simple postnatal cap-initiation loss is strongly buffered.

literature_claim: Rare EIF4G1 variants were proposed as familial Parkinson mutations, later challenged in large cohorts, and EIF4G1 was reported to interact genetically with VPS35 in alpha-synuclein models.
main_caveats: The Eif4g1 perturbation had no recovered MB Dopa cells, the assay was loss-of-function rather than human missense alleles, and aged dopaminergic-vulnerability phenotypes were outside the screen.
summary: Parkinson-family targets represented in the parquet did not converge with the Eif4g1 acute loss-of-function surface.
why_it_matters: EIF4G1 has a contested PARK18 relationship and a reported genetic interaction with VPS35, but Vps35, Snca, Park7, Uchl1, Atp13a2 and Vps13c did not produce an Eif4g1-like signature in these sampled juvenile neurons; simple Eif4g1 loss is therefore a poor transcriptomic proxy for that disease axis in this context.

main_caveats: The score correlation uses a null-like Eif4g1 vector; it is a rejection of convergence, not a positive mechanistic association with the top-ranked genes.
summary: A full-universe signature-neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Eif4g1 neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top nominal neighbors were not hidden pathway members with high shared-direction overlap; their score correlations were near zero, so the Eif4g1 surface is better interpreted as globally flat than as a weak version of a Uba5, Opa1, Rel or Vps35 program.

literature_claim: eIF4H stimulates the eIF4A initiation helicase and germline Eif4h-null mice have growth, brain-volume, posterior-cortex dendritic/spine, and learning phenotypes.
main_caveats: Sparse CRISPR indels were not measured at the DNA or protein level, and snRNA-seq cannot detect ribosome occupancy or local dendritic translation.
summary: Sparse P16 Eif4h loss did not recreate the broad cortical and growth phenotype expected from germline Eif4h deficiency; the assay recovered only two FDR<0.10 mRNA changes across 22 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: This separates Williams-Beuren-region EIF4H biology from a large cell-autonomous mature-neuron mRNA program and pushes the canonical effect toward earlier organismal development and protein/synapse-level outputs.

literature_claim: HEXIM1 inhibits P-TEFb-dependent RNA polymerase II elongation, while UBA5 and UFC1 act in UFMylation, a pathway linked to ER-ribosome quality control and neurodevelopmental disease.
main_caveats: The Eif4h call is one gene in one cell group; Uba5/Ufc1 convergence is transcriptional co-occurrence and does not prove direct regulation of Hexim1 by UFMylation.
summary: Hexim1 was the sole FDR<0.10 Eif4h hit in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and fell in a recurrent thalamo-hypothalamic module shared in the same direction by Uba5, Ufc1, and Tsc2.
why_it_matters: HEXIM1 is a P-TEFb/7SK transcription-elongation brake; its selective recurrence with UFMylation components suggests that the strongest Eif4h mRNA edge is a small slice of a protein-synthesis or ER-ribosome homeostasis response rather than a broad translation shutdown signature.

literature_claim: Synaptotagmin-1 is a synaptic Ca2+ sensor required for fast synchronous neurotransmitter release.
main_caveats: Syt1 passed only the FDR<0.10 screen threshold and no other synaptic-vesicle gene passed FDR<0.10 in this cell group.
summary: Syt1 was the only FDR<0.10 gene in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and was uniquely up-regulated by Eif4h among all perturbations that significantly changed Syt1 there.
why_it_matters: Syt1 encodes the fast synaptic-vesicle Ca2+ sensor, so this isolated signal nominates a presynaptic vesicle marker, not unfolded-protein stress, as the second measurable mature-neuron readout of Eif4h loss.

literature_claim: No prior claim was needed for the unbiased genome-wide neighbor calculation.
main_caveats: Cosines use all genes, including mostly null features, so they should be read as ranking statistics, not strong phenocopy measurements.
summary: The global Eif4h signature had no strong whole-surface neighbor: the best positive cosine was only 0.0327 and the most negative was -0.0202 across 1772 other perturbations.
why_it_matters: The nearest-neighbor calculation finds real hints, such as Eif4a2 and UFMylation genes near the top, but the numerical effect sizes show that Eif4h is too flat for a robust genome-wide convergence or antagonism call.

literature_claim: eIF4H stimulates eIF4A and associates with the eIF4A/eIF4G helicase module during translation initiation.
main_caveats: Eif4a2 itself had only two downstream FDR<0.10 calls, and Eif4g1 was not recovered in every group, so the contrast is a weak-signature negative.
summary: Eif4h did not phenocopy the literature-obvious cap-dependent initiation comparators Eif4a2 or Eif4g1, even though Eif4a2 was the top unbiased positive neighbor.
why_it_matters: A physical relationship between eIF4H, eIF4A, and eIF4G is detectable only as a weak rank-order effect; acute loss of the accessory factor Eif4h, the helicase Eif4a2, and the eIF4F scaffold Eif4g1 are not interchangeable transcriptomic perturbations in mature neurons.

literature_claim: FMRP and mTOR signaling participate in neuronal translational homeostasis and fragile-X-linked synaptic pathology.
main_caveats: The screen targeted only selected pathway genes; Eif4e, Eif4b and canonical 4E-BPs were not perturbation targets in the model-visible parquet.
summary: Eif4h was also separable from FMRP/mTOR translational-control targets: Tsc2 produced a broad multi-group response, whereas Mtor was small and Rptor, Fmr1, and Cyfip1 were nearly or completely flat.
why_it_matters: The result cautions against treating all neuronal translation regulators as one perturbational class; even within protein-synthesis biology, upstream growth signaling and the eIF4H helicase accessory node occupy different transcriptional dependencies.

literature_claim: Hypusinated eIF5A is an essential elongation/termination factor and Eif5a or Dhps deletion in mouse neurons produces severe developmental or cognitive phenotypes.
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes reached FDR<0.10; DNA indels and hypusinated eIF5A protein were not measured.
summary: Eif5a loss produced a two-gene, two-cell-class response rather than a pan-neuronal translation-failure signature.
why_it_matters: The selective Nrg3-up and Dgkz-down calls show that the target was not completely inert, but also that mature neurons in this P16 mosaic CRISPR setting buffered loss of a canonical hypusine-dependent translation factor at the level of steady-state nuclear RNA.

literature_claim: Nrg3 promotes excitatory synapse formation onto ErbB4-positive hippocampal interneurons.
main_caveats: Nrg3 is a single RNA marker in a broad Pvalb group; ErbB4 signaling, synapses, and NRG3 protein were not directly assayed.
summary: Pvalb interneurons showed a solitary Nrg3 up-regulation after Eif5a perturbation.
why_it_matters: Nrg3 is a synaptogenic neuregulin-family ligand for ErbB4-positive inhibitory interneurons, so this single robust Pvalb call is a plausible circuit-facing marker of Eif5a loss rather than a generic ISR or UPR marker.

literature_claim: Ribosome stalling or amino-acid/ER stress can trigger eIF2alpha-ATF4 transcription and ATF4-dependent autophagy gene induction.
main_caveats: The panel tests nuclear RNA responses, not translation rates, ribosome stalls, hypusine abundance, or autophagic flux.
summary: The expected ISR, UPR, autophagy/lysosomal, and OXPHOS stress transcriptomes were absent.
why_it_matters: Because translation-factor failure can secondarily induce detectable ATF4 and autophagy programs, the absence of Atf4/Ddit3/Trib3/Hspa5/Herpud1/Sqstm1/Atg/Lamp/OXPHOS sentinels argues that most surviving Eif5a-perturbed neurons did not enter a proteotoxic crisis between P16 and P37-44.

literature_claim: eIF5A acts during translation elongation and termination but has a stall-relief role distinct from other elongation factors.
main_caveats: Eef2 and Eif5a were assayed with different guide sets and nuclei; this is a cross-perturbation contrast, not a matched biochemical comparison.
summary: Eif5a did not phenocopy the represented elongation-factor target Eef2.
why_it_matters: Eef2 perturbation generated 1,119 downstream FDR<0.10 calls in 14 measured groups, whereas Eif5a generated two; this shows that postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq can recover translation-factor biology, but the specialized eIF5A hypusine axis is buffered or displaced relative to Eef2 in this assay.

literature_claim: DGKζ is a diacylglycerol kinase linked to synaptic DAG turnover and dendritic-spine maintenance.
main_caveats: The module is based on one shared sentinel gene; no lipid, PKC, or synaptic physiology was measured.
summary: The thalamic Dgkz-down call placed Eif5a on one pole of a recurrent cross-perturbation axis.
why_it_matters: Sin3a, Elp1, and Gfpt1 independently drove Dgkz down in the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group, whereas Rnpc3, Thoc1, and Snrnp70 drove it up; Eif5a therefore tags a reproducible thalamic lipid-signaling transcript even though its own signature is minimal.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

literature_claim: ELF2/NERF is an ETS-domain RNA-polymerase-II transcription factor with established functions in B-cell/RUNX1, vascular hypoxia/Tie2, proliferation, apoptosis, and early lymphoid programs.
main_caveats: DNA indels and ELF2 protein were not measured; low or absent self-mRNA knockdown is expected in this CRISPR-indel readout and does not prove guides failed.
summary: Elf2 loss produced an almost flat neuronal snRNA-seq surface: no cell group lost the Elf2 transcript at FDR<0.10 and only one non-self gene passed FDR<0.10 across all 23 recovered groups.
why_it_matters: A sequence-specific ETS transcription factor can be measurably present yet buffered after sparse P16 CRISPR loss in postmitotic neurons; the result narrows Elf2's strong transcript-regulatory priors to contexts outside the sampled juvenile neuronal compartment.

literature_claim: STXBP2/Munc18-2 binds syntaxins and is required for late cytotoxic-granule exocytosis in immune cells; a direct ELF2-to-STXBP2 link in thalamic neurons had not been the expected program.
main_caveats: Single-gene FDR signal with no supporting FDR-level pathway genes; no protein or vesicle-fusion assay was performed.
summary: The only robust Elf2-dependent neuronal transcript was Stxbp2, up-regulated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: STXBP2/Munc18-2 is a syntaxin-binding vesicle-fusion factor best known from secretory-lysosome exocytosis; its isolated induction nominates a thalamus-restricted trafficking readout rather than a broad ETS regulon.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ELF2/NERF can promote VCP transcription, and Bap31 has been reported to regulate VCP expression through Elf2.
main_caveats: Direct VCP promoter binding was reported in non-neuronal or cell-line systems; this screen cannot assay VCP ATPase activity, BAP31 protein, or proteostasis flux.
summary: Elf2 did not engage the literature-predicted BAP31–ELF2–VCP axis in juvenile neurons.
why_it_matters: Vcp and Bcap31 transcripts were measured throughout the Elf2 surface but never became FDR-significant, Bcap31 perturbation itself had no non-self DE, and Vcp perturbation produced a distinct six-gene signature that excluded Stxbp2; therefore the known VCP promoter relationship is not a dominant cell-autonomous neuronal output here.

literature_claim: NERF/ELF2 belongs to an ETS family that includes ELF and ETS factors, interacts with RUNX1 in B-cell promoter assays, and is linked to Tie2/angiopoietin signaling in endothelial contexts.
main_caveats: True paralogs Elf1/Elf4 and RUNX1/angiopoietin targets were not represented as perturbations, so the comparison uses available ETS-family and receptor proxies.
summary: Measurable ETS and endothelial-receptor comparators failed to phenocopy Elf2.
why_it_matters: Ets1 was completely flat, Etv6 produced only Kdm4c and Adora1 in a signature that omitted Stxbp2, Tek was flat, and Kdr had only one off-program DEG; the Elf2 result is not a generic ETS-family, Tie2, or vascular-receptor signature transplanted into neurons.

main_caveats: Neighbor analysis used Wilcoxon score correlations over shared group×gene features and is intentionally transcriptome-level; it cannot detect non-transcriptional phenotypes.
summary: Unbiased cross-perturbation neighbors did not reveal a hidden Elf2 module.
why_it_matters: The strongest whole-surface score correlations were near zero and the most negative named neighbor, Ctcf, was a broad responder with hundreds of DE genes but essentially no anti-Elf2 structure; this supports reading Elf2 as a buffered target, not as a member of a recurrent perturbational state whose individual FDR calls were missed.

literature_claim: Elongator-dependent wobble-uridine loss perturbs translation and can elicit protein-homeostasis stress, while the ISR induces ATF4 and amino-acid/redox genes.
main_caveats: Pvalb and CNU-HYa HY GABA responses are tiny; DNA indels and ELP1 protein are unmeasured.
summary: Elp1 caused a sharply restricted neuronal response: six of 21 measured groups had downstream FDR<0.10 genes, with 830 of the signal calls concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and smaller same-program fragments in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: The response is not pan-neuronal even though Elongator is a core translation complex; the restriction turns a mostly null screen surface into evidence for cell-state-specific vulnerability after postmitotic Elp1 loss.

literature_claim: ELP1 and ELP2 are subunits of the same Elongator holo-complex, and ELP2 mutations impair Elongator activity and protein homeostasis in neurodevelopmental models.
main_caveats: Elp3-Elp6 were not represented as perturbation targets; the matched Elp2 response was mostly confined to 151.
summary: The same-complex target Elp2 was the top non-safe Elp1 signature neighbor and shared 166 FDR<0.10 calls with Elp1, all in the same direction.
why_it_matters: A direct Elp1-Elp2 phenocopy anchors the stress signature to the Elongator complex rather than to off-target guide behavior or to a generic thalamic stress artifact.

literature_claim: ALKBH8 acts on wobble-uridine tRNA substrates downstream of Elongator-derived cm5U, whereas Elongator itself performs the conserved early wobble-uridine step.
main_caveats: Absence of DNA indel measurements makes flat Alkbh8, Nsun2, and Trmt1 surfaces less definitive than the positive Elp2 convergence.
summary: Acute loss of the represented tRNA-modification enzymes Alkbh8, Nsun2, and Trmt1 did not reproduce the Elp1/Elp2 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.
why_it_matters: The data separate Elongator-core disruption from a generic tRNA-modification-null state in this assay: even the Elongator-substrate methyltransferase Alkbh8 was flat where Elp1 was strong.

literature_claim: The integrated stress response induces ATF4-dependent amino-acid and recovery genes after translation and ER stress.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq reports secondary transcript abundance rather than tRNA modification or translation rates directly.
summary: Elp1 up-regulated an ATF4-linked amino-acid, one-carbon, and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase program: Asns, Slc1a4, Slc3a2, Slc7a1, Slc7a5, Shmt2, Mthfd2, Aldh1l2, Cars, Mars1, Aars, Lars, and Eprs were induced in the thalamic response, with subsets recurring in 145, 155, and 191.
why_it_matters: The main transcriptomic consequence of acute Elp1 loss is an adaptive attempt to rebalance amino-acid supply, redox metabolism, and tRNA charging after a translation-quality defect.

literature_claim: Perturbing Elongator-dependent codon translation speed during cortical neurogenesis can trigger ER stress and UPR signaling.
main_caveats: Xbp1 and Stt3b are not recurrent across all responders; Herpud1 is the clearest ER-stress marker.
summary: Elp1 activated an ER protein-quality-control branch marked by Herpud1 in 151, 145, and 155, plus Xbp1 in 151 and Stt3b in 191.
why_it_matters: This branch connects the Elp1 signature to UPR/ERAD rather than to a pure amino-acid-starvation program, matching the idea that wobble-uridine translation errors can stress co-translational folding.

literature_claim: No Elp1-specific prior was identified for recurrent Srsf5 repression.
main_caveats: Mechanism is not established; Srsf5-alone behavior in 066 should be treated as a boundary signature.
summary: Srsf5 was down-regulated in five Elp1 responder groups and Ddx17 in three, nominating RNA-processing factor loss as a recurrent secondary marker of the Elp1 state.
why_it_matters: Srsf5 is the only gene significant in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and recurs across excitatory and inhibitory responders, so it may mark the weakest edge of the Elp1 response where the ATF4 module is otherwise not recovered.

literature_claim: ELP1-linked familial dysautonomia prominently affects sensory/autonomic neurons, while mouse studies also establish Elongator requirements in the CNS.
main_caveats: The sampled groups are broad neuronal classes; peripheral, enteric, retinal, and non-neuronal compartments were not assayed.
summary: Elp1 can drive a central postmitotic neuronal ISR/UPR within 3-4 weeks, outside the peripheral sensory and autonomic lineages classically emphasized in familial dysautonomia.
why_it_matters: The finding refines disease biology by showing that selected mature brain neurons are capable of mounting a transcriptional proteostasis response to Elp1 loss, rather than all Elp1 vulnerability being restricted to neural-crest derivatives or embryonic fate specification.

literature_claim: Elongator has previously been linked to cytoskeletal regulation of neuronal migration and branching during development.
main_caveats: These are transcript changes in postmitotic nuclei, not direct measurements of tubulin acetylation, neurite structure, or synaptic function.
summary: The dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response paired ATF4/UPR induction with down-regulation of neuronal synaptic, cytoskeletal, and RNA-processing genes.
why_it_matters: This shows that the response is not an isolated protective ATF4 bounce-back; it is accompanied by reduced expression of genes tied to neuronal structure and communication in the same nuclei.

literature_claim: No same-complex or direct pathway-prior relationship was used to nominate Gfpt1, Atp2a2, Dhdds, or Hspa5.
main_caveats: The comparison is signature-based and Hspa5 had high raw cosine but only nine overlapping significant calls.
summary: Beyond Elp2, the strongest positive Elp1 neighbors were Gfpt1, Atp2a2, Dhdds, and Hspa5, all with same-direction raw cosine similarity and same-direction significant overlap on Elp1 coordinates.
why_it_matters: The data independently place Elp1 in an ER/metabolic proteostasis neighborhood rather than restricting interpretation to known Elongator subunits.

literature_claim: No literature-obvious inverse Elp1 comparator was identified among these raw anticorrelates.
main_caveats: This conclusion applies to FDR-supported transcriptomic overlap in this dataset, not to all possible functional interactions.
summary: The strongest raw non-safe anticorrelates to Elp1 failed a robust FDR-overlap test and should not be interpreted as inverse biology.
why_it_matters: This prevents noise from low-cell or flat perturbations from being promoted to a mechanistic antagonist of the Elp1 ISR program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: Germline or patient-like Elp2 defects disrupt brain development, cortical morphogenesis, myelination, and protein homeostasis.
main_caveats: The three non-151 calls are single FDR genes rather than pathway-scale responses; the two missing taxonomy groups were not tested.
summary: Elp2 caused a pathway-scale response almost only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; all other responders were single-gene, marginal surfaces.
why_it_matters: The acute postmitotic CRISPR phenotype is not a generic neuronal Elp2 transcriptome: thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons crossed a stress-response threshold that most cortical, limbic, GABA, and cerebellar groups did not.

literature_claim: ELP1 and ELP2 are both Elp123 scaffold subunits within the six-subunit Elongator complex, so loss of either is expected to impair Elongator function.
main_caveats: Elp3-Elp6 were not represented as perturbation targets, so convergence could only be tested against Elp1.
summary: Elp1, the only assayed alternative Elongator subunit, was the strongest positive Elp2 neighbor and reproduced the 151 ATF4/amino-acid signature in the same directions.
why_it_matters: Same-complex convergence argues that the 151 signal is an Elongator-loss response, not an isolated guide or target-transcript artifact; Elp1 was stronger and extended into 145 and 155, showing non-identical dosage or subunit sensitivity.

literature_claim: ALKBH8 participates in wobble-uridine mcm5U biogenesis downstream of carboxymethyluridine formation, whereas Elongator-dependent modifications represent a broader U34 branch.
main_caveats: The evidence is a negative perturbation comparison; as for Elp2, DNA indels and tRNA chemistry were not measured for Alkbh8, Cdkal1, or Trmt1.
summary: Elp2 did not phenocopy represented non-Elongator tRNA-modification targets in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The strong Elp2/Elp1 signature is therefore not a universal consequence of perturbing any tRNA-modification enzyme in these neurons; it appears tied to the Elongator branch, a stronger multisubunit disruption, or a cell-specific threshold.

literature_claim: Loss of Elp2 impairs tRNA modification and proteostasis, and ATF4 is a canonical induced effector of eIF2α-mediated integrated stress.
main_caveats: The dataset is transcriptomic only; it does not directly measure eIF2α phosphorylation, ribosome pausing, or tRNA hypomodification.
summary: The 151 Elp2 signature contains a high-confidence ATF4/integrated-stress-response program.
why_it_matters: Up-regulation of Atf4, Ddit3, Asns, Chac1, amino-acid importers, and Sesn2/Trib3 turns Elp2 loss into a detectable translational/proteostatic stress state in a defined postmitotic thalamic population.

literature_claim: Elongator-dependent tRNA wobble modifications tune translation efficiency and proteome homeostasis; amino-acid limitation/stress drives ATF4-dependent biosynthetic compensation.
main_caveats: Synthetase induction is inferred as compensation from the transcriptome; tRNA charging was not directly assayed.
summary: Elp2-perturbed 151 cells up-regulated a tRNA-charging and amino-acid supply module.
why_it_matters: Induction of multiple aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases plus LAT1/4F2hc and one-carbon/proline biosynthetic genes is a homeostatic attempt to restore amino-acid and charged-tRNA availability after Elongator loss rather than a simple collapse of gene expression.

literature_claim: Impaired Elongator function can perturb protein homeostasis; ER N-glycosylation and calcium-handling defects are established routes to unfolded-protein stress.
main_caveats: Hspa5 and Opa1 were nominated mostly by restricted-signature cosine with shallow significant overlap; the shared state is strongest for Atp2a2, Gfpt1, and Dhdds.
summary: Non-obvious ER and proteostasis perturbations, especially Atp2a2, Gfpt1, and Dhdds, converged on the Elp2 151 signature, but Elp2 lacked a full BiP/Xbp1 chaperone UPR.
why_it_matters: The neighbor structure connects Elp2 loss to ER/glycoprotein proteostasis while also showing that the Elp2 state is ATF4/Herpud1-biased rather than a generic Hspa5-Xbp1 ER-stress transcriptome.

literature_claim: Elongator has been linked to neuronal cytoskeleton, branching, intracellular trafficking, synapse formation, and altered cortical dendrites in Elp2 mutant mice.
main_caveats: Loss of neuronal transcripts could reflect secondary stress remodeling rather than direct regulation by Elp2.
summary: The stress-positive 151 population also down-regulated neuronal, synaptic-vesicle, calcium-channel, and cytoskeletal transcripts.
why_it_matters: This places Elp2-dependent synaptic/cytoskeletal biology downstream of an acute, cell-autonomous postmitotic stress state in thalamic glutamatergic neurons, extending prior cortical morphology observations into a new neuronal class.

main_caveats: Exploratory transcriptomic module; the dataset does not establish whether these spliceosomal changes are causal.
summary: Srsf5 and a broader RNA-processing/RNP module decreased under Elp2 loss, with Srsf5 recurring as the single significant 155 MB Glut gene.
why_it_matters: The recurrence makes Srsf5 a compact marker of the Elp2/Elp1 stress state outside the main thalamic responder, while the accompanying Ddx5/Ddx17/Luc7l3/Srrm2 repression suggests RNA-maturation machinery is part of the adaptive or degenerative response.

main_caveats: The rejection applies to the Elp2 restricted-signature FDR-overlap gate, not to all possible phenotypes of those targets.
summary: Restricted-signature anti-neighbors of Elp2 were vector artifacts rather than robust inverse perturbations.
why_it_matters: Rejecting Gabra3, Zfp182, Hoxa3, Mtnr1b, and Dlst prevents construction of a false antagonistic pathway from anti-correlation over genes that were not themselves significant in the comparator perturbations.

literature_claim: Established En1 neural biology is concentrated in embryonic midbrain-hindbrain/cerebellar patterning and patterned postnatal cerebellar territories, not in all mature forebrain neurons.
main_caveats: Does not assay DNA indels, embryonic specification, hindbrain, non-neuronal cells, or the missing MB Dopa class.
summary: En1 produced 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 22 recovered P16 postmitotic neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The finding defines the measured phenotype: En1 is a high-confidence global transcriptional null in this surface, so interpretation should focus on timing, lineage, redundancy, and coverage rather than on a hidden responder program.

literature_claim: Engrailed factors support adult midbrain dopaminergic neuron maintenance, mitochondrial stress resistance, and protection from Parkinson-like degeneration.
main_caveats: Other midbrain-enriched non-dopaminergic groups were measured, but they are not a substitute for 215 MB Dopa.
summary: The En1 perturbation surface is missing 215 MB Dopa, the cell class most directly predicted by adult Engrailed dopaminergic-maintenance literature.
why_it_matters: The absence of a dopaminergic response is a coverage limitation, not evidence that En1 is inert in midbrain dopamine neurons.

literature_claim: En2 can compensate for En1 in cerebellar contexts, Pbx proteins cooperate with Engrailed at the midbrain-hindbrain boundary, and Pax/Otx organizer genes sit in the same embryonic patterning space.
main_caveats: Correlations are dominated by an En1 null vector; singleton comparator DE genes are not interpreted as pathways.
summary: En1 has no robust data-driven signature neighbor and does not converge with En2 or other assayed homeobox/Pbx relatives.
why_it_matters: The expected paralog and pathway-neighbor comparison was directly measured rather than assumed: En2 had only one FDR<0.10 singleton in matched groups, several Otx/Foxa/Lmx/Pitx/Pbx comparators were flat, and the strongest whole-surface En1 correlations across 1772 targets were near zero.

literature_claim: Engrailed protects midbrain dopaminergic neurons through complex-I translation, oxidative-stress resistance, DNA-damage/chromatin pathways, and LINE-1 repression.
main_caveats: LINE-1 repeats and enzyme activities are not direct gene-level snRNA-seq analytes; the statement rests on absence of transcriptional proxies.
summary: The assayed En1 loss did not elicit expected dopaminergic mitochondrial, oxidative-stress, UPR/ISR, or organizer-marker transcriptional proxies.
why_it_matters: Engrailed protein therapy and En1 Parkinson-model biology act through adult dopaminergic mitochondrial and genome-stability mechanisms; this En1 CRISPR-null surface lacks the key lineage and shows no secondary stress proxy elsewhere, so it cannot be used to falsify those mechanisms.

literature_claim: Tmem191 is annotated as a protein-coding transmembrane-protein gene with no experimentally supported GO molecular-function or biological-process annotation.
main_caveats: This is a single FDR<0.10 gene at q=0.0652, not a pathway; the CTX-CGE sample has 93 perturbed nuclei and En2 DNA editing was not measured.
summary: En2 produced a one-gene CTX-CGE GABA response, up-regulating Tmem191 and no other transcript at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The only robust En2-positive biology in this acute postnatal screen was not a canonical Engrailed midbrain/cerebellar program but a rare, poorly annotated membrane-gene change in cortical CGE-derived inhibitory neurons.

literature_claim: En1 and En2 jointly control midbrain dopaminergic neuron survival in a dose-dependent Engrailed program.
main_caveats: The assay did not recover En2 rows in MB Dopa neurons, so this is a matched-cell-group contrast, not a test in the canonical dopaminergic population.
summary: The En1 paralog did not phenocopy En2: En1 had zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the 22 matched groups, no CTX-CGE Tmem191 effect, and only a weak global score correlation with En2.
why_it_matters: Engrailed paralogy and shared dopaminergic survival biology should make En1 the first comparator to check; its flat surface argues that the En2 CTX-CGE Tmem191 hit is not a generic Engrailed-homeobox signature in this P16 mosaic assay.

literature_claim: Germline En2 mutants alter forebrain Pvalb/Sst and GABA-receptor expression, while Engrailed factors in midbrain dopaminergic neurons regulate survival, Ndufs1/Ndufs3-linked complex-I activity, and Snca.
main_caveats: Absence is limited to 3-4 weeks after P16 perturbation in recovered neuronal groups; MB Dopa was not measured for En2 and cell abundance was not the endpoint.
summary: En2 loss did not activate the expected Pvalb/Sst/GABA-receptor, Ndufs1/Ndufs3, or Snca programs in any recovered cell group.
why_it_matters: The negative program test separates germline En2 developmental phenotypes from acute postmitotic En2 depletion: the snRNA-seq readout would have detected a secondary GABAergic or mitochondrial transcriptional shift if it were present in surviving NeuN-positive cells, but those genes all remained at FDR=1.0.

literature_claim: No literature relationship was used; these were rank neighbors from the DE matrix.
main_caveats: The correlations were computed over signed Wilcoxon scores after requiring more than 300000 matched gene-by-cell-group pairs; En2 itself has only one FDR<0.10 gene.
summary: The data-driven En2 nearest neighbors were correlations close to zero rather than strong convergent modules.
why_it_matters: Mef2c and Atxn10 produced hundreds of FDR<0.10 genes in several of the same groups where En2 was flat, showing that the En2-null surface is target-specific rather than a global failure of those cell groups to yield DE.

literature_claim: Endoglin is an accessory TGFβ-superfamily receptor with essential endothelial/vascular roles and HHT genetics rather than a known autonomous postmitotic-neuron effector.
main_caveats: No DNA indel or protein measurement is available, and the missing 215 MB Dopa group cannot be interpreted.
summary: Eng loss of function produced a neuronal pan-null: 22 recovered neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the remaining 215 MB Dopa group was not recovered for Eng.
why_it_matters: The screen is almost exactly orthogonal to canonical endoglin biology: it perturbed sparse postmitotic NeuN+ neurons, whereas ENG is a vascular TGFβ/BMP co-receptor whose disease phenotypes arise mainly in endothelial angiogenic circuits. The flat surface therefore refines the model rather than refuting endoglin function.

literature_claim: Endothelial BMP9/10 signaling uses an ENG/ALK1/type-II-receptor complex to activate SMAD1/5/8 and downstream ID1/ID3/EFNB2-like transcription.
main_caveats: Most comparator positives were single-gene signatures; the comparison rejects transcriptomic convergence in neurons but does not test endothelial cells or ligand/flow stimulation.
summary: The ENG pathway did not silently reappear through related TGFβ/BMP receptors: Acvrl1 and Tgfbr3 were completely flat, Smad4 was flat, and 16 represented TGFβ/BMP comparator perturbations produced only seven isolated one-gene hits across 350 matched neuronal tests.
why_it_matters: ENG, ACVRL1/ALK1, BMPR2/ActRII receptors and SMADs are expected to co-operate in endothelial BMP9/10 signaling. Their failure to form a shared neuronal module shows that Eng is uncoupled from this vascular receptor-SMAD circuit in the sampled postmitotic neurons, not merely that the Eng guides were unusually weak.

main_caveats: This comparison used all Wilcoxon scores because Eng had no FDR-level signature; the top ranks are exploratory and biologically uninterpreted.
summary: Whole-universe score-vector neighbors of Eng were near zero, including a safe-target neighbor, and their DE surfaces were absent or one-gene only.
why_it_matters: The absence of a strong positive or negative neighbor argues that Eng did not hide a reproducible stress, proteostasis, synaptic, or developmental module below the FDR cutoff. The ranked neighbors are best treated as a negative control on signature matching, not as biological phenocopies.

literature_claim: Germline Eno1 disruption is early embryonic lethal and ENO1 knockout in proliferative pancreatic cancer cells yields hundreds of DE genes and metabolic rewiring.
main_caveats: Eno1 itself was absent from the expression-feature set and DNA indels were not measured; the finding is restricted to surviving NeuN+ nuclei 3-4 weeks after sparse postnatal CRISPR.
summary: Acute P16 Eno1 loss produced no corrected single-nucleus transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: This sharply restricts ENO1's solo loss-of-function biology in the experiment to something other than a broad postmitotic neuronal stress or metabolic transcriptome; the result is a real negative surface, not a single underpowered cell type.

literature_claim: Alpha- and gamma-enolase are co-regulated during brain development, adult neurons can coexpress alpha and gamma enolase, and ENO2 can maintain enolase function in ENO1-deleted glioma cells until ENO2 or total enolase is inhibited.
main_caveats: ENO2 and ENO3 were readouts but not perturbation targets in this parquet; isoform protein abundance and total enolase activity were not measured.
summary: The Eno1 null is most consistent with pre-existing mature-neuronal enolase buffering rather than transcriptional induction of another enolase isoform.
why_it_matters: Neurons have gamma-enolase/ENO2 biology, and ENO1-deleted glioma cells are tolerated until ENO2 is also inhibited; here Eno2 and Eno3 transcripts did not become FDR-significant after Eno1 perturbation, so any buffering is likely constitutive or enzymatic rather than a detectable RNA compensation program.

literature_claim: ENO1 loss or silencing in proliferative disease models has been linked to Warburg-effect control, AMPK-Akt signaling, extracellular-matrix and ER-lumen DEGs, pentose-phosphate and sugar-metabolism changes, and OXPHOS/lipid-metabolism up-regulation.
main_caveats: The evidence is transcriptomic only; it rules out a detected RNA program, not subtle changes in glycolytic flux or ATP.
summary: ENO1's canonical glycolysis and cancer metabolic-reprogramming priors did not map onto an HIF/MYC, lactate, UPR/ISR, or oxidative-phosphorylation transcriptional program in healthy postmitotic neurons.
why_it_matters: The assay would have seen a secondary stress transcriptome if acute Eno1 loss had generated one: expected markers were present but FDR-negative after Eno1, metabolic regulators Hif1a/Myc/Nfe2l2/Prkaa2/Rptor were flat as perturbations, and Tsc2 produced 636 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the same analysis universe.

main_caveats: Correlation was computed on Wilcoxon scores for matched gene-by-cell-group rows; a target with no robust DE necessarily has limited ability to nominate mechanistic neighbors.
summary: No other perturbation in the directly queried universe converged with or opposed Eno1 in a meaningful way.
why_it_matters: The closest data-driven neighbors were not ENO1's textbook relatives and had absolute Wilcoxon-score correlations of only 0.030 or less, so the Eno1 profile is better interpreted as signature absence than as membership in a hidden recurrent module.
