literature_claim: CBP/p300 are KAT3 coactivators and H3K18/H3K27 acetyltransferases, but single p300 deletion in adult forebrain excitatory neurons is much less disruptive than CBP deletion or combined KAT3 loss.
main_caveats: Cas9 indels, p300 protein loss, H3K27ac loss, and behavior were not measured; two taxonomy groups were missing for Ep300.
summary: Ep300 single-gene loss did not produce a robust steady-state transcriptional response in any of the 21 measured neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The all-cell-group zero is the main phenotype: in this P16-to-P37/44 sparse neuronal CRISPR setting, isolated p300 loss is buffered rather than broadly collapsing a p300/CBP enhancer program.

literature_claim: Adult-forebrain CBP loss, and some p300 manipulations at the behavioral level, implicate KAT3 proteins in activity-dependent plasticity and memory programs.
main_caveats: The screen was unstimulated and steady state; it did not assay learning, seizures, environmental enrichment, or acute activity induction.
summary: Canonical immediate-early and plasticity transcripts were absent from the Ep300 DE surface.
why_it_matters: Arc, Fos/Jun-family, Egr-family, Npas4, Nr4a, Homer1, Bdnf, Cebpb, and Crem would be natural readouts if a basal CREB/KAT3 plasticity module were collapsing, but all 315 tests across the 21 groups had adjusted P=1.0.

literature_claim: CBP and p300 can compensate jointly for H3K27ac and neuronal identity, while adult single-p300 loss can be weaker than CBP loss.
main_caveats: Crebbp was recovered in only eight Ep300-overlapping cell groups, so a broader paralog comparison was not available.
summary: The measurable KAT3 paralog Crebbp did not broadly phenocopy Ep300 in the matched screen universe.
why_it_matters: The expected closest relative generated only a small 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature and an extremely low Ep300-Crebbp whole-profile correlation, arguing against a shared cell-autonomous snRNA module for single KAT3 perturbations in this assay.

literature_claim: Enhancer acetylation, BRD4/KMT2A-linked chromatin disease, and CHD8-associated neurodevelopmental chromatin regulation belong to the same broad regulatory space as Rubinstein-Taybi chromatin disorders.
main_caveats: This is a screen-internal contrast across different genes, not proof that Brd4, Chd8, Kmt2a, or Creb1 signals run through p300.
summary: Other transcriptional and chromatin regulators were FDR-level responders in the same cell groups where Ep300 was silent.

literature_claim: ERBB3 recruits p85 through multiple YXXM motifs and in ERBB2/ERBB3-active systems signals strongly into PI3K survival/proliferation pathways.

main_caveats: Because Erbb3 itself has no FDR-level response, rank-vector correlations are dominated by weak signed ranks; they are informative only for excluding strong convergence.
summary: The unbiased signature-neighbor scan found no robust positive or negative Erbb3 neighbor; all score-vector correlations were near zero.
why_it_matters: This rules out a hidden, noncanonical transcriptomic module that would have been missed by looking only at textbook ERBB targets.

literature_claim: ErbB4 is concentrated in cortical GABAergic interneurons and Nrg1/ErbB4 controls inhibitory-circuit connectivity.

summary: Erbb4 RNA itself fell in the two measured inhibitory groups with FDR-level on-target evidence, but neither group produced a downstream transcriptome at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The guides reached Erbb4-expressing inhibitory neurons, especially Pvalb cells, so the absence of downstream genes is stronger than a simple expression-mismatch null; in this postmitotic juvenile assay, Erbb4 loss looks buffered at the nuclear RNA level after the receptor transcript is reduced.

literature_claim: NRG1/2/3 signal through ERBB receptors including ERBB4 and ERBB3.

why_it_matters: ETS factors share DNA-binding logic and Ras-MAPK inputs, yet Etv6, Elf2, Spi1, Map2k1, Braf, Bmpr and Smad perturbations had zero-to-tiny signatures with near-zero score correlations to Ets1; the Ets1 null is therefore not hiding a generic ETS or MAPK transcriptional state.

literature_claim: Ets1 has been linked to HDAC1/BMP control in neural crest, to HDAC1 in injured primary afferents, and to Lcn2-dependent axon growth in embryonic spinal-cord neurons.
main_caveats: Axon length and sensory-neuron injury physiology are outside the morphology-free, brain-only snRNA readout; Lcn2 was not present as a tested row in 215 MB Dopa.
summary: Previously reported Ets1 effector transcripts from axon-growth and neural-crest programs were absent: Lcn2, Hdac1, Id3, Bmp2, Bmp4, Msx2, and Snai2 never reached FDR<0.10 after Ets1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The negative result is informative rather than a pure readout failure: the snRNA-seq surface contained the relevant transcripts and would have detected a large, shared secondary Lcn2/HDAC1/BMP response if it had been engaged in these P16-perturbed brain neurons.

literature_claim: Low Ets1 or Ets1 knockout promotes B/T-cell activation, antibody-secreting-cell differentiation, and lupus-like autoimmunity, with direct B-cell targets identified by ChIP-seq and expression profiling.
main_caveats: The screen cannot test lymphocytes, endothelial involvement, microglia, or glia directly because those populations were not part of the recovered neuronal DE surface.
summary: The screen did not convert Ets1 into a neuronal autoimmune-risk program: robust B- and T-cell Ets1 biology is displaced to lineages that were absent or strongly depleted from the NeuN-enriched neuronal assay.
why_it_matters: This keeps Ets1 lupus and lymphocyte biology from being over-read as a cell-autonomous role in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Etv6 has strong requirements in embryonic neural/mesenchymal survival and hematopoietic progenitors rather than a well-established role as a maintenance factor for postmitotic juvenile neurons.
main_caveats: The CRISPR indel rate was not assayed at DNA level, so the sparse response cannot be converted to full knockout penetrance.
summary: Postnatal Etv6 loss produced an extremely sparse neuronal transcriptomic surface: 2 of 23 tested cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and each responder contained only one such gene.
why_it_matters: A gene that is essential in embryo and blood did not act as a broad mature-neuron transcriptional maintainer after P16 CRISPR loss; the detectable response was restricted to one thalamic and one NP/CT/L6b/OB glutamatergic group.

literature_claim: Adenosine A1 receptors are inhibitory GPCRs that reduce neuronal excitability and excitatory synaptic transmission.
main_caveats: This is a single-gene transcriptomic marker; receptor protein abundance and adenosine physiology were not measured.
summary: Etv6 loss up-regulated Adora1 as the single FDR-level hit in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Adora1 encodes the inhibitory adenosine A1 receptor; its selective induction nominates adenosine sensitivity, rather than a broad apoptosis or stress pathway, as the cleanest thalamic output of Etv6 perturbation in this screen.

literature_claim: ETV6 functions as a corepressor-associated transcription factor, whereas KDM4C is a histone demethylase acting at chromatin.
main_caveats: Only one chromatin-modifier transcript passed FDR<0.10; histone methylation was not directly profiled.
summary: Etv6 loss up-regulated the chromatin enzyme Kdm4c as the only FDR-level hit in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
why_it_matters: Kdm4c encodes JMJD2C, an H3K9/H3K36 demethylase; its isolated up-regulation links the NP/CT/L6b/OB response to chromatin-state rebalancing rather than to the hematopoietic or inflammatory programs that dominate ETV6 literature.

main_caveats: Comparator selection used a top-500 nominal Etv6 score vector because only two Etv6 downstream genes passed FDR; overlap at FDR level is one gene.
summary: Prox1, a data-driven positive neighbor of the weak Etv6 signature, independently up-regulated Adora1 in the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group.
why_it_matters: The shared Adora1 direction keeps the Etv6 thalamic hit from being a completely private one-off, while the absence of broader overlap shows that Etv6 is not simply a scaled-down Prox1 perturbation.

literature_claim: TEL/ETV6 can contact SIN3/SMRT/NCoR/HDAC corepressors, so shared direct repression would make Etv6 and Sin3a losses move targets in the same direction.
main_caveats: Sin3a produced a much broader signature than Etv6; Adora1 opposition may be indirect.
summary: Sin3a, a measurable corepressor-pathway comparator, down-regulated Adora1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut whereas Etv6 up-regulated Adora1 there.
why_it_matters: A direct-corepressor expectation would predict shared de-repression, so the opposite Adora1 sign argues that the Etv6-Adora1 relationship in thalamic neurons is indirect or embedded in a SIN3A-dominant regulatory architecture.

literature_claim: ETS-family proteins share a conserved ETS DNA-binding domain but use distinct cofactors and family-specific regulatory logic.
main_caveats: Some ETS relatives were not present as screen targets, and Elf2 produced one unrelated Stxbp2 hit in 151.
summary: Other ETS-family targets represented in the parquet, Elf2, Erf, Ets1, and Spi1, did not phenocopy the Etv6 Adora1 or Kdm4c outputs.
why_it_matters: The result separates the sparse Etv6 neuronal phenotype from generic perturbation of GGAA/T-binding ETS factors and from family paralogy alone.

literature_claim: Hematopoietic ETV6 disruption can derepress interferon-response genes and perturb megakaryocyte and HSC biology.
main_caveats: The conclusion is limited to neuronal nuclei that survived 3-4 weeks after P16 perturbation and to genes represented in the expression matrix.
summary: The screen did not recover ETV6-linked interferon, apoptosis, UPR/ISR, or megakaryocyte-marker programs after Etv6 loss in any neuronal cell group.
why_it_matters: Because Etv6 encodes a transcriptional repressor and IFN/stress programs would be transcript-visible if induced, their absence makes the neuronal nulls biologically informative rather than a pure snRNA-seq readout failure.

literature_claim: Ext1 loss has strong embryonic axon-guidance effects and postnatal excitatory-neuron synaptic phenotypes in mouse models.
main_caveats: The result is transcriptional only; DNA indels, heparan sulfate chain loss, AMPA-receptor localization, and electrophysiology were not measured.
summary: P16 acute mosaic Ext1 loss produced no FDR-level downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal class.
why_it_matters: This converts a flat DE table into a positive biological result: after neurons are postmitotic, sparse CRISPR Ext1 disruption is transcriptionally buffered across cortical, hippocampal, thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, pontine/myelencephalic, pineal, and cerebellar neuronal groups rather than selectively activating a hidden stress or synaptic gene module.

literature_claim: EXT1/EXT2 build HS chains, HS biosynthesis can feed back on NDST1 and sulfation, and HSPGs regulate FGF, Hedgehog, WNT, Slit/Robo, and Ephrin-A signaling.
main_caveats: Nuclear RNA reporters are an indirect readout of extracellular glycan function, and some morphogen reporters are weakly expressed in mature neurons.
summary: Ext1 perturbation failed to induce the expected heparan-sulfate feedback, FGF/ERK, Hedgehog, WNT, Slit/Robo, or Eph transcriptional reporters.
why_it_matters: The null was not limited to Ext1 itself: explicitly queried HS-biosynthetic genes and canonical activity reporters were present in the DE tables but uniformly FDR=1, arguing that a P16 neuronal perturbation did not measurably collapse morphogen/axon-guidance transcriptional outputs.

literature_claim: EXT1, EXT2, and upstream/downstream HS biosynthetic enzymes participate in one glycan-synthesis pathway and might have been expected to converge if this screen captured HS-chain depletion transcriptionally.
main_caveats: Ext1 itself has no FDR genes, so similarity was assessed with full signed Wilcoxon-score vectors rather than shared significant genes.
summary: The data-driven Ext1 neighborhood was null-like, and the closest non-safe neighbor, B3gat3, did not mark a coherent heparan-sulfate module.
why_it_matters: B3gat3 is a glycosaminoglycan linker enzyme and was nominated directly from the screen rather than the literature, but its correlation with Ext1 was only r=0.028 and its two significant genes were confined to one striatal GABA group; Ext2, Xylt1, and Hs6st2 were similarly near-orthogonal or flat.

literature_claim: Postnatal deletion of Ext1 from excitatory neurons removes HSPGs and causes impaired glutamatergic transmission and autism-like behavior without obvious brain morphology defects.
main_caveats: The screen did not measure HS abundance or electrophysiology, and the amygdala cell types from the prior model are coarser than the matched taxonomy here.
summary: The postnatal Ext1 phenotype most consistent with this dataset is a silent-to-snRNA synaptic glycan defect rather than an ISR, UPR, or morphogen-transcription phenotype.
why_it_matters: Postnatal excitatory-neuron Ext1 deletion can impair glutamatergic transmission without gross brain morphogenesis defects; the present P16 mosaic screen likewise showed no FDR-level neuronal stress module, so follow-up should assay HS chains, AMPA-receptor localization, or synaptic physiology rather than only RNA-state biomarkers.

literature_claim: EXT2 functions in a Golgi EXT1-EXT2 enzyme complex that builds the heparan-sulfate glycan backbone rather than in a nuclear transcription-factor module.
main_caveats: DNA indels and HS-chain abundance were not measured; the screen cannot determine whether each nucleus had biallelic enzymatic knockout.
summary: Ext2 mRNA could be reduced without producing a corrected downstream neuronal transcriptome.
why_it_matters: The strongest Ext2 self-transcript losses occurred in Pvalb, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c, and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, yet every one of those groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10; the result argues for pathway buffering or a non-transcriptional primary phenotype rather than absence of target sampling.

literature_claim: HSPGs participate in axon guidance, synapse development, and cell-type-specific synaptic specificity.
main_caveats: Each cell group contributed only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene, both at 0.05<FDR<0.10; this should be treated as a restricted-signature hypothesis, not a complete pathway.
summary: The corrected Ext2 signature is two down-regulated neuronal connectivity genes: Epha5 in L2/3 IT cortex and Slc6a17 in CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: Both corrected downstream events are negative and neuronal rather than FGF/Wnt/Hedgehog target genes or generic UPR/stress genes, nominating Epha5 and Slc6a17 as low-confidence, cell-class-restricted sentinels of postnatal Ext2 loss.

literature_claim: Embryonic disruption of HS synthesis alters HS-binding morphogen patterning in mouse brain, and zebrafish ext2 mutants show reduced Fgf target expression and Wnt sensitization.
main_caveats: The tested nuclei were postmitotic neurons after P16 AAV CRISPR, not embryonic neuroepithelium; absence of corrected target-gene changes does not imply intact HS biochemistry.
summary: P16 Ext2 loss did not recover the embryonic FGF/Wnt morphogen-output program predicted from developmental Ext2 and HS work.
why_it_matters: FGF/Wnt/Hedgehog sentinel transcripts were queried in every Ext2 cell group and none reached FDR<0.10, even though several of the same readouts were detectable elsewhere in the parquet; the dominant response in this juvenile neuronal assay is therefore not a canonical morphogen-target collapse.

literature_claim: EXT1 and EXT2 form a 1:1 heparan-sulfate chain-elongation complex.
main_caveats: Both signatures are weak by conventional DE standards, so the contrast is a failure to converge on a sparse snRNA signature, not proof that Ext1 and Ext2 differ at the glycan level.
summary: Ext1, the obligatory same-complex partner of Ext2, did not phenocopy even the sparse Ext2 transcriptional surface.
why_it_matters: A simple HS-polymerase model predicts Ext1 and Ext2 to be the most obvious matched perturbations, but Ext1 produced zero corrected downstream genes in 22 measured groups and did not reproduce Epha5 or Slc6a17 in the Ext2 responder groups.

literature_claim: HS biosynthesis begins with a shared glycosaminoglycan linker, is elongated by EXT copolymerases, and is diversified by HS-modifying enzymes on HSPG core proteins.
main_caveats: The comparator set samples only represented targets and cannot assay unperturbed pathway members such as Ndst genes or every glypican and syndecan.
summary: Other represented HS-linkage, HS-modifying, and HSPG-core perturbations were also decoupled from Ext2.
why_it_matters: Xylt1, Glce, Hs6st2, and Gpc6 were completely flat at FDR<0.10, and B3gat3 produced only two unrelated genes in a striatal GABA group; this argues that the observed Epha5/Slc6a17 events are not a reproducible postnatal HS-biosynthesis module.

main_caveats: Ranking weak signatures by global cosine can elevate arbitrary low-amplitude correlations; the useful conclusion is the lack of robust convergence, not the identities of the top ranks.
summary: The unbiased Ext2 signature-neighbor search found no meaningful global convergence or antagonism.
why_it_matters: After feature-level residualization, the largest positive and negative cosines to Ext2 were near zero, and the named non-safe neighbors did not alter Epha5 or Slc6a17 in matched responder groups; Ext2 therefore behaves as an isolated weak surface in this screen rather than as a member of a large transcriptomic response class.

literature_claim: F2 encodes prothrombin/thrombin, an extracellular coagulation protease that can activate PAR signaling and injury-associated inflammatory transcription in neural and vascular contexts.
main_caveats: The guides were delivered after neuronal specification and only to sparse NeuN+ nuclei; no DNA indel, prothrombin protein, or thrombin-activity measurement was available.
summary: F2 loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null rather than a coagulation, PAR, stress, or synaptic program in juvenile postmitotic neurons.
why_it_matters: The strongest biological statement is the absence of any cell-autonomous F2-regulated neuronal mRNA program under basal conditions: 23 neuronal groups and 388,023 downstream tests yielded zero FDR<0.10 genes.

main_caveats: Correlations used Wilcoxon scores, not FDR-restricted overlap; because F2 has no FDR<0.10 genes, overlap-based convergence is necessarily zero.
summary: F2 had no meaningful positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor; even the extremal whole-universe score correlations were approximately zero.
why_it_matters: This prevents a hidden low-amplitude convergence claim: the data-driven neighbors Fgfr2, Plxnd1, and Pgrmc1 did not share a significant F2 module, and the strongest anticorrelate, Smc1a, responded only in a different thalamic class.

literature_claim: Thrombin can activate PARs and, especially after ischemia, BBB injury, or glial activation, drives MAPK, NF-kappaB/AP-1, cytokine, and matrix-remodeling responses.
main_caveats: The assayed nuclei were mostly neurons in an uninjured 3-4 week endpoint; transient immediate-early changes could have resolved before harvest.
summary: The expected thrombin/PAR receptor and AP-1/NF-kappaB injury readouts were measurable but absent after F2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: snRNA-seq would have registered a durable secondary Fos/Jun/Egr, Nfkbia, cytokine, Mmp9, Serpine1, or Socs3 program if sparse postnatal F2 editing had shifted active PAR/injury signaling; the panel instead stayed at FDR=1.0.

literature_claim: Adult systemic prothrombin depletion causes fatal hemorrhage, F2 20210G>A increases plasma prothrombin as a gain-of-function thrombophilia allele, and thrombin inhibitors act on active extracellular thrombin.
main_caveats: This is an assay-interpretation warning, not a direct pharmacology experiment with dabigatran, warfarin, or a plasma F2 allele.
summary: The neuronal CRISPR null does not model systemic thrombin inhibition or the human F2 20210G>A thrombophilia allele.
why_it_matters: A flat neuron-autonomous signature should not be read as evidence that direct thrombin inhibitors or plasma F2 gain-of-function are brain-transcriptionally inert: those interventions act on circulating or BBB-associated thrombin and on an extracellular protease pool rather than on F2 mRNA inside isolated neurons.

literature_claim: FAM120A can scaffold oxidative-stress Src/PI3K-Akt survival signaling, couple mTORC1-SREBP transcription to lipogenic RNA processing, and buffer Ago2-bound mRNAs.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; the result applies to basal postnatal NeuN+ nuclei, not to oxidatively challenged cancer cells or embryonic stem cells.
summary: Fam120a loss caused an almost fully buffered basal neuronal transcriptome: 23 cell groups were measured, but only Hgs in Pvalb GABA and Luc7l3 in MB glutamatergic neurons reached FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This turns a mostly null surface into a biological statement: FAM120A is not an acute master regulator of steady-state mRNA abundance in juvenile postmitotic neurons under basal in-vivo conditions.

literature_claim: HGS/HRS is an ESCRT-0 endosomal sorting protein that works with STAM to traffic ubiquitinated receptors toward lysosomal degradation.
main_caveats: Only Hgs passed FDR<0.10 and no broader ESCRT, lysosomal, or autophagy gene set was recovered.
summary: Pvalb GABA neurons showed a single FDR<0.10 response, Hgs up-regulation, after Fam120a perturbation.
why_it_matters: HGS is the HRS component of ESCRT-0, so its isolated induction nominates endosomal cargo sorting as the only robust Pvalb-adapted transcript in this perturbation, but it is a one-gene, hypothesis-generating signal rather than a full lysosomal program.

literature_claim: FAM120A can act in SRSF1/U1-70K-coupled RNA processing of lipogenic transcripts, and LUC7L3 is a U1 snRNP-associated regulator of 5-prime splice-site use.
main_caveats: Luc7l3 was the only MB Glut downstream FDR gene for Fam120a; no direct FAM120A-LUC7L3 interaction was measured.
summary: MB glutamatergic neurons showed a single FDR<0.10 response, Luc7l3 down-regulation, after Fam120a perturbation.
why_it_matters: The isolated loss of a U1 snRNP-associated splicing factor is directionally compatible with FAM120A being an RNA-processing protein, yet the absence of additional spliceosome genes keeps this as a restricted biomarker rather than a splicing-collapse phenotype.

literature_claim: FAM120A promotes efficient splicing and stability of SREBP1 lipogenic transcripts downstream of mTORC1 in anabolic cancer-cell settings.
main_caveats: The measured positive comparator is dominated by Srebf2/sterol genes in neurons, whereas the cited FAM120A study emphasized SREBP1-driven fatty-acid synthesis in cancer cells.
summary: Fam120a did not engage the neuronal mTORC1/SREBP sterol module even though the same assay detected it after Tsc2 activation and Srebf2 loss in MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The expected cancer-cell FAM120A-to-SREBP output is not simply invisible to snRNA-seq: Tsc2 and Srebf2 perturbations moved Cyp51, Insig1, Msmo1, Ldlr, Fdft1, Dhcr24, and Acaca in the predicted sterol directions in the same neuronal compartment, whereas Fam120a left that program at FDR=1.

literature_claim: FAM120A/Ossa can activate Src-family kinases and recruit PI3K p85 to support Akt-mediated survival after oxidative stress.
main_caveats: Kinase phosphorylation is protein-level; nevertheless, a sustained stress-survival transcriptional response was not present.
summary: Fyn, Pik3r1, Pik3cb, and Akt3 perturbations did not converge with Fam120a, and none reproduced the Hgs or Luc7l3 singletons.
why_it_matters: This argues that basal Fam120a loss is uncoupled from the Src/PI3K/Akt survival scaffold that made FAM120A stress-protective in cancer cells, at least at the level of secondary steady-state mRNA programs in juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: FAM120A co-binds many Ago2 targets and reduces Ago2-mediated degradation of those mRNAs in mouse embryonic stem cells.
main_caveats: The screen measured steady-state nuclear RNA, not 3-prime UTR occupancy or miRNA repression kinetics.
summary: Ago1, Ago2, and Tnrc6a produced flat or tiny DE surfaces and did not phenocopy Fam120a.
why_it_matters: The mouse embryonic stem-cell model in which FAM120A buffers Ago2-bound 3-prime UTR targets did not translate into a postnatal neuronal Ago-like transcriptome after Fam120a loss.

main_caveats: Cosine was computed on full Wilcoxon-score vectors and is dominated by many subthreshold genes because Fam120a has only two FDR hits.
summary: The top data-driven Wilcoxon-score neighbors of Fam120a were not strong: the best positive cosine was Nefl at 0.0337 and the best negative cosine was Atrn at -0.0179.
why_it_matters: The absence of a sizable positive or inverse neighbor means the two Fam120a singletons do not belong to a recurrent global perturbation module in the available universe.

literature_claim: FAM120A was among genes prioritized by schizophrenia exome/GWAS convergence at FDR<5%, in a study whose top rare-coding risk genes are enriched for neuronal expression and synaptic biology.
main_caveats: Human genetic association does not specify which cell type, age, or molecular modality should respond after acute CRISPR loss in mouse.
summary: Fam120a is much flatter than several represented schizophrenia rare-variant comparators in the same assay, especially Setd1a.
why_it_matters: A postnatal cell-autonomous mRNA response is not a universal property of schizophrenia-risk genes: Setd1a and a few receptor or autophagy-related comparators produced measurable neuronal signatures, while Fam120a did not.

literature_claim: Sin3b encodes a Sin3/HDAC chromatin corepressor involved in E2F repression, cell-cycle exit and differentiation; the literature does not connect it directly to Fam149b.
main_caveats: One downstream gene in a 37-cell perturbed bin; treat as a candidate marker, not a complete program.
summary: Fam149b produced a single FDR-level downstream change, Sin3b down-regulation, confined to 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: The result defines the positive biology in this screen as a narrow chromatin-corepressor response rather than a broad ciliary or SHH signature.

literature_claim: FAM149B1 is a ciliary gene whose deficiency impairs Smoothened-induced GLI1/PTCH1 expression in cultured cells, and primary cilia mediate SHH expansion of cerebellar progenitors.
main_caveats: The screen read out nuclear RNA but not ciliary length, IFT tip accumulation, ligand-stimulated signaling or embryonic progenitor abundance.
summary: Fam149b loss did not recover the expected GLI/PTCH readout or a secondary IFT/cilium RNA module in any assayed neuronal group.
why_it_matters: GLI1 and PTCH1 are transcriptional and were directly assayable; their FDR=1.0 behavior, together with flat ciliary sentinels, argues that the canonical FAM149B1-SHH fibroblast readout was not active in this postnatal NeuN+ context.

literature_claim: FAM149B1/JBTS36 and BROMI/TBC1D32 act in a shared IFT-turnaround module, and multiple ciliary genes converge on Joubert or related ciliopathies.
main_caveats: Most comparator surfaces were themselves one-gene or zero-gene signatures, so this is a rejection of transcriptomic convergence, not a test of cilia morphology.
summary: The represented same-pathway ciliary comparators were nearly flat and did not phenocopy the Fam149b Sin3b response.
why_it_matters: The absence of Tbc1d32/Fam149b convergence argues that the screen context suppresses the FAM149B1-BROMI IFT-turnaround module at a pathway level, rather than producing a Fam149b-specific failure.

main_caveats: The search used Wilcoxon-score cosines across matched group-gene dimensions; because Fam149b has only one FDR-level gene, it is intentionally interpreted as an isolation result.
summary: A whole-transcriptome score-neighbor search gave only near-zero Fam149b neighbors and anti-neighbors.
why_it_matters: This keeps the cross-perturbation calculation from over-interpreting coincidental rank correlations in an almost silent target.

direction: two downstream genes up in two cell groups; nineteen measured groups flat
literature_claim: FAR1 is a rate-limiting fatty-alcohol supplier for ether lipid and plasmalogen synthesis, a pathway whose primary products are lipids rather than transcripts.
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes pass FDR<0.10, so each is a marker rather than a complete pathway by itself.
summary: Far1 loss-of-function produced an ultra-sparse neuronal transcriptional response: exactly two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 21 measured cell groups, Insig1 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and Tial1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The screen argues against a broad cell-body mRNA program after postnatal neuronal Far1 perturbation and confines the positive transcriptomic readout to two marker-like events.

literature_claim: INSIG1 is an endoplasmic-reticulum regulator of SCAP-SREBP and HMG-CoA reductase trafficking in sterol feedback control.
main_caveats: The Far1 arm is supported by one FDR<0.10 gene and lacks a broader SREBP target-gene wave.
summary: The hypothalamic GABA Far1 hit lands on the INSIG/SREBP sterol-feedback node: Far1 and Tsc2 perturbations both increased Insig1 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, whereas direct Srebf2 perturbation decreased Insig1.
why_it_matters: This places the most lipid-interpretable Far1 response in a sterol regulatory circuit and distinguishes it from nonspecific peroxisome disruption.

literature_claim: Tial1/TIAR encodes an AU-rich RNA-binding protein annotated to the nucleus and cytoplasmic stress granules, but a FAR1-to-Tial1 relationship is not established.
main_caveats: A single modest logFC event; Agps did not reproduce it in the same cell group.
summary: Far1 induced the RNA-binding/stress-granule gene Tial1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut without accompanying FDR<0.10 ISR, unfolded-protein, redox, synaptic-vesicle, or peroxisome sentinel genes.
why_it_matters: Tial1 is a candidate thalamic marker of a post-transcriptional response to Far1 loss, but the isolated nature of the hit argues for validation before assigning a full stress-granule program.

literature_claim: FAR1 and AGPS act in the same peroxisome-initiated plasmalogen pathway, and FAR1 protein is subject to plasmalogen-dependent post-translational feedback.
main_caveats: Gnpat, Pex7, Pex5, and Far2 were not represented as perturbation targets, so their surfaces could not be measured.
summary: Canonical ether-lipid and peroxisome perturbations did not phenocopy Far1: Agps had only three non-overlapping thalamic genes, Pex14 had zero downstream genes despite strong self-transcript drops in several groups, and Pex1/Hsd17b4/Abcd3/Acbd5 were essentially flat.
why_it_matters: The positive Far1 Insig1/Tial1 signature is not a generic transcriptional consequence of weakening peroxisomal ether-lipid biogenesis in postmitotic NeuN+ neurons.

direction: expected sentinel programs absent after Far1
literature_claim: Ether-lipid deficiency has been linked to synaptic vesicle/neurotransmitter defects in complete Gnpat knockout mice and to ferroptosis programs in proliferating cancer cells.
main_caveats: Sentinel testing cannot replace lipidomics, electrophysiology, or axonal/synaptic proteomics.
summary: Far1 did not elicit a broad sterol, peroxisome, ISR/UPR-redox, or synaptic-vesicle mRNA program; only Insig1 passed FDR<0.10 among the queried sentinel genes.
why_it_matters: The assay would have captured a secondary soma stress or SREBP program if one were launched broadly, so the null surface is informative about transcriptional buffering even though it does not exclude lipidomic or synaptic physiology.

direction: loss-of-function in dataset; Arg480 disease is feedback-escape gain of ether-lipid synthesis
literature_claim: Biallelic FAR1 variants deplete ether lipid synthesis, while heterozygous Arg480 variants disrupt plasmalogen-dependent FAR1 degradation and increase ether lipids.
main_caveats: No lipid measurements or gain-of-function Far1 perturbations were assayed.
summary: The sparse LoF profile should not be treated as a model of dominant FAR1 Arg480 disease, whose mechanism is feedback escape with elevated ether-lipid synthesis rather than Far1 loss.
why_it_matters: It separates recessive FAR1 deficiency biology from gain-of-function FAR1 disorders when using CRISPR-LoF neuronal signatures for disease interpretation.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: FARS2 loss impairs mitochondrial tRNAPhe aminoacylation and mitochondrial translation, reduces respiratory-chain function, and causes severe neurodevelopmental phenotypes in biallelic disease and deficiency models.
main_caveats: DE is measured only in surviving guide-positive NeuN+ nuclei; DNA indels and target-cell depletion were not assayed.
summary: Fars2 CRISPR did not produce a robust downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal population measured for the target.
why_it_matters: The primary result is an informative absence: a postnatal sparse knockout of an essential mitochondrial tRNA synthetase left 22 recovered neuronal classes with zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes, so the dataset supports survivor/buffering explanations rather than a cell-type-specific Fars2 transcriptional program.

literature_claim: Mammalian inhibition of mitochondrial translation can activate an ATF4-dependent integrated stress response.
main_caveats: Opa1/Lonp1 are mitochondrial comparators, not mt-aaRSs; their positive ISR signatures demonstrate detectability but not that every Fars2-edited cell reached an equivalent biochemical lesion.
summary: The expected ATF4/ISR, mitochondrial chaperone/protease, and mtDNA-encoded OXPHOS RNA programs were absent after Fars2 perturbation even though Opa1 and Lonp1 perturbations show that such genes are detectable in this analysis universe.
why_it_matters: This passes the readout gate for Fars2: the negative result cannot be dismissed as snRNA-seq being categorically unable to see mitochondrial stress; rather, recovered Fars2-edited cells did not enter the secondary ISR-like state expected from a strong mitochondrial-translation block.

literature_claim: mt-aaRSs share the canonical mitochondrial tRNA-charging role, but mt-aaRS diseases can be cell-type selective and different mt-aaRS lesions can trigger distinct compensatory programs.
main_caveats: Rars2 and Lars2 themselves only had one FDR<0.10 singleton each, so the contrast is a family-level absent-signature result rather than pathway-gene overlap.
summary: The represented mitochondrial aaRS relatives Rars2 and Lars2 were also almost flat and did not converge with Fars2.
why_it_matters: The Fars2 null is part of a broader postnatal buffering/survivorship pattern for the represented mt-aaRS family rather than a Fars2-only anomaly; each family member is required for a different tRNA but none produced a shared acute neuronal ISR/OXPHOS RNA signature here.

main_caveats: Neighbor correlations used all rank genes and are therefore interpreted only negatively; no Fars2 FDR<0.10 genes existed for shared-DE overlap.
summary: Whole-universe signature search found no meaningful transcriptional neighbor for Fars2.
why_it_matters: The top data-driven matches, Manf and Limk1, sat at noise-scale signed-score correlations, so the screen did not nominate a hidden stress, ER, cytoskeletal, or synaptic module that simple FDR counting missed.

literature_claim: FAS is a ligand-gated TNFR death-domain receptor that transduces FASL engagement through the CD95 DISC and can also signal toward NFkappaB in protected or non-apoptotic contexts.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured; the observed buffer is for basal sparse CRISPR in juvenile neurons, not for FasL or injury challenge.
summary: Fas loss was globally buffered in recovered juvenile NeuN+ neurons, with only 1 downstream FDR<0.10 row across 22 measured cell groups and no detectable apoptosis, NFkappaB/JNK, or stress-gene program.
why_it_matters: This turns a mostly empty DE surface into an interpretable basal-state result: Fas is not exerting tonic death-receptor transcriptional control in uninjured postmitotic neurons in this assay.

literature_claim: PAFAH1B2 is the alpha2 catalytic subunit of intracellular PAF-AH, whose catalytic subunits modulate Wnt signaling in developing GABAergic neurons.
main_caveats: Single-gene signal at FDR 0.091; no measured Fas literature connects Pafah1b2 directly to CD95 signaling in postmitotic hypothalamic GABA neurons.
summary: Pafah1b2 was the sole Fas-induced FDR<0.10 gene, up in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only cell-class-restricted Fas signal while preventing it from being over-expanded into a Wnt, apoptosis, or migration pathway without companion DE genes.

literature_claim: Death-domain TNFR signaling can share FADD, caspase-8, RIP, NFkappaB, and MAPK components with FAS/CD95 signaling.
main_caveats: The closest ligand and DISC components, including Faslg, Fadd, and Casp8, were not themselves perturbation targets, so the comparison uses reachable relatives rather than the exact DISC.
summary: Measured TNFR/death/NFkappaB/MAPK neighbors failed to phenocopy Fas despite known pathway proximity.
why_it_matters: The absence of convergence with Tnfrsf1a, Traf3, Bcl2, Nfkb1, Mapk1, Mapk9, and other represented TNFRSF perturbations argues that the Fas profile is not a reusable TNF-family death-receptor module in this basal neuronal dataset.

literature_claim: No prior Fas relationship was being tested; this was an unbiased search over all represented target signatures.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from Wilcoxon z-score profiles; a nearly flat target can have unstable nearest neighbors.
summary: Whole-universe signature neighbors of Fas were quantitatively negligible.
why_it_matters: The data-driven pass did not uncover a noncanonical convergent module hidden outside the FAS literature; the top positive and negative neighbors all had |r|<0.04 and should be rejected as biology-level comparators.

literature_claim: FBN1 loss in matrix-rich tissues is expected to disrupt extracellular microfibrils and TGFβ/BMP growth-factor regulation.
main_caveats: The result is strong for the assayed P16-to-P37/44 neuronal nuclei, but it does not test non-neuronal matrix-producing cells.
summary: Fbn1 loss was nearly globally buffered in postnatal NeuN+ neurons, with only 1 downstream FDR<0.10 row across 371796 non-self tests in 22 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: The dominant biological result is absence of a broad neuron-autonomous Fbn1 program; the flat self-transcript is expected in this CRISPR-indel assay and should not be mistaken for proof of failed editing.

literature_claim: DYM participates in Golgi organization and ECM secretion pathways, and Dym deficiency has postnatal neurodevelopmental trafficking consequences.
main_caveats: Single-gene response at FDR 0.0959 in 66 perturbed nuclei; no broader Golgi, UPR or ECM program passed FDR<0.10.
summary: Dym was the sole FDR<0.10 Fbn1-response gene and was upregulated in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
why_it_matters: Dym links the only positive row to a Golgi/ECM secretory-trafficking gene rather than to canonical TGFβ targets, suggesting a very local compensatory trace of Fbn1 perturbation.

literature_claim: Fibrillin-1 microfibrils, LTBPs, ADAMTS/ADAMTSL proteins and TGFβ receptors/SMADs are coupled through extracellular growth-factor storage and connective-tissue disease biology.
main_caveats: The closest structural genes Fbn2, Ltbps, MFAPs and fibulins were not perturbation targets, so only receptor/SMAD, integrin and ECM disease-family comparators could be tested directly.
summary: Fbn1 did not phenocopy represented fibrillin/TGFβ comparators and did not induce a detectable TGFβ/ECM target-gene panel.
why_it_matters: The observed Dym row is uncoupled from the extracellular latent-TGFβ mechanism that dominates Marfan biology; related receptors and SMADs were themselves mostly transcriptionally silent in the neuronal screen.

main_caveats: Neighbor discovery used 101 nominal rows because the FDR<0.10 Fbn1 vector was too sparse for a stable full-signature comparison.
summary: Unbiased Fbn1 signature neighbors computed from nominal p<0.001 rows did not yield an FDR-level convergent module on re-test.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting nominal cosine neighbors as biology when the target’s corrected signature contains only one positive gene.

literature_claim: FBXO11 haploinsufficiency or de novo variants cause neurodevelopmental disease, and experimental FBXO11 deficiency can produce neuronal developmental phenotypes.
main_caveats: The perturbation was sparse P16 CRISPR in NeuN-positive neurons; DNA indels were not measured, and formal signal in the sole responder was one gene.
summary: Fbxo11 loss produced a highly buffered postmitotic neuronal transcriptome: among nine recovered cell groups, only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and that response was a single Ppib decrease.
why_it_matters: The result separates FBXO11 neurodevelopmental disease relevance from an acute, broad P16-to-P37/44 nuclear transcriptional requirement in already specified neurons.

literature_claim: Cyclophilin B family biology is tied to endoplasmic-reticulum redox and folding biology.
main_caveats: The ER-folding interpretation rests on a single FDR-significant transcript; no coordinated UPR module was detected.
summary: Ppib is the sole robust Fbxo11-responsive transcript and is down-regulated only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; canonical UPR/ISR transcripts such as Hspa5, Ddit3, Atf4, and Xbp1 did not reach FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Ppib nominates a narrow thalamic ER-folding readout but argues against a dataset-wide ER-stress or proteasome-bounce-back program after postnatal Fbxo11 loss.

main_caveats: The 46-feature vector intentionally used rank-leading sub-threshold Fbxo11 genes because only one downstream gene passed FDR; the follow-up FDR overlap test was negative.
summary: The top empirical neighbors of the restricted Fbxo11 rank signature were Dscam, B9d1, and Nfib, while En1, Rack1, and Dcaf8 were the strongest anti-neighbors, but their actual FDR<0.10 surfaces did not share the Fbxo11 Ppib hit.
why_it_matters: For this target, nearest-neighbor structure is driven by sub-threshold ranks rather than a reproducible FBXO11 module; it should not be converted into a mechanistic network.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: FBXO11 functions as an SCF substrate receptor coupled to p53 neddylation, BCL6 degradation, CDT2 turnover, TGF-beta regulation, and Snail-family degradation in epithelial, immune, or proliferating systems.
main_caveats: Core SCF members and several direct substrates were not perturbation targets in the screen; this is a same-assay comparison of available pathway-adjacent targets.
summary: Represented literature-obvious comparators in the F-box, p53, TGF/SMAD, and Snail axes were nearly flat in the same nine cell groups and did not reproduce Fbxo11's Ppib response.
why_it_matters: The expected FBXO11 epithelial, cell-cycle, and p53/TGF axes are uncoupled from the P16 neuronal response rather than simply hidden in a related perturbation.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Proteasomal activation ameliorated neuronal phenotypes in FBXO11-deficient human stem-cell and fly models.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot measure proteasome activity, protein ubiquitination, pSMAD2, or p53 neddylation directly.
summary: FBXO11 proteasome biology did not manifest as a persistent postnatal neuronal UPR/ISR transcriptome: Ppib alone changed, while Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Hsp90b1, and Xbp1 were non-significant in the Fbxo11 DE surface.
why_it_matters: Proteasome activation may rescue FBXO11-deficient developmental systems, but this screen gives no support for treating a chronic, cell-autonomous ER-stress transcriptome in surviving P16-perturbed neurons.

main_caveats: The count of DE genes is robust, but true DNA indel engagement was not assayed and the two positive groups have low perturbed-cell counts.
summary: Fbxo38 produced an extremely sparse neuronal response: 2 single-gene responder groups among 22 measured groups, with 20 measured groups lacking downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The dominant phenotype in this P16 postmitotic CRISPR screen is buffering rather than a broad transcriptional program, so the two positive singleton genes must be interpreted against a mostly flat surface.

literature_claim: HDAC2 suppresses neuronal gene expression and negatively regulates synaptic plasticity and memory-associated processes in mice.
main_caveats: Only one HDAC/chromatin gene reached FDR<0.10, and the effect is based on 26 perturbed pineal nuclei.
summary: Fbxo38 loss uniquely up-regulated Hdac2 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: Hdac2 is a chromatin regulator with established neuronal repressive activity, making its isolated induction a candidate marker of a pineal Fbxo38 state rather than evidence for a broad chromatin program.

literature_claim: TRAPPC11 functions in ER/Golgi trafficking and TRAPP-associated vesicle biology, and human TRAPPC11 mutations affect muscle and glycosylation.
main_caveats: Trappc11 was the sole FDR<0.10 gene in this group and its FDR was 0.060, so no larger trafficking program is established.
summary: Fbxo38 loss down-regulated the TRAPP-complex gene Trappc11 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: Trappc11 nominates a vesicle-trafficking/autophagy-linked readout in the only hindbrain-midbrain GABA-like Fbxo38 responder, but the response is a single near-threshold gene.

literature_claim: FBXO38/MoKA can coactivate KLF7, and a motor-neuronopathy FBXO38 variant impairs KLF7-mediated transcription and neurite outgrowth.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and postnatal; DNA indels, FBXO38 protein, and peripheral motor neurons were not assayed.
summary: Direct Klf7 loss was transcriptionally visible in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Fbxo38 loss in the same cell group did not recover a KLF7-like transcriptomic effect.
why_it_matters: Because FBXO38/MoKA is a KLF7 coactivator in prior work, the measured Klf7-versus-Fbxo38 split argues that FBXO38 is not the limiting KLF7 cofactor in this juvenile thalamic neuron state.

main_caveats: Cosine was computed over weak genomewide Wilcoxon scores; singleton Fbxo38 effects limit all signature-neighbor metrics.
summary: The top data-driven perturbation neighbors of Fbxo38 were tiny-amplitude similarities and did not reproduce its responder groups.
why_it_matters: The Fbxo38 signature is not part of a large shared transcriptomic module in the model-visible universe, so apparent neighbors such as H3f3a, Mast1, Oprl1, Snrpb, Cfap69, and Ptprm should be rejected as biological convergence.

literature_claim: SCF-F-box receptors link substrates to ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation, but an adaptor perturbation need not phenocopy a core proteasome perturbation.
main_caveats: The contrast is anchored by a single shared Trappc11 gene; U2af2 is not a proteasome component and serves here as an empirical broad-signature comparator.
summary: Trappc11 moved in the opposite direction under Fbxo38 than under broad Psmc1 and U2af2 perturbations in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: A core proteasome perturbation caused a large stress and synaptic-downshift signature with Trappc11 up, whereas Fbxo38 caused only Trappc11 down; the Fbxo38 result is therefore not simply generic ubiquitin-proteasome overload.

literature_claim: TP53INP2 can promote mammalian autophagosome biogenesis by bridging LC3B and ATG7.
main_caveats: Only one autophagy-linked gene reached FDR<0.10; Atg5, Atg7, Map1lc3a, and Map1lc3b did not, so this is a biomarker-grade candidate rather than a proven autophagy flux response.
summary: Fbxw7 loss-of-function produced a single adjusted-significant downstream gene, Trp53inp2, and only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The one recovered transcript is an autophagosome-biogenesis factor, nominating a narrow proteostasis/autophagy compensation rather than the canonical Notch, MYC, cyclin-E, or mTOR/SREBP program expected from FBXW7 substrate stabilization.

literature_claim: FBXW7 promotes turnover of Notch, c-Jun, cyclin/MYC, SREBP, mTOR, and NFE2L1 substrates and Fbxw7 loss in embryonic neural stem/progenitor compartments activates Notch/c-Jun biology.
main_caveats: The screen measured mRNA in nuclei rather than FBXW7-substrate protein abundance, so absent substrate-gene mRNA is best read as absence of a secondary transcriptome, not absence of all substrate stabilization.
summary: Acute postnatal Fbxw7 knockout did not recover canonical FBXW7 substrate-output transcriptional programs.
why_it_matters: Known FBXW7 biology predicts increased activity of Notch, AP-1, MYC/cyclin-E, mTOR/SREBP, or NFE2L1-proteasome arms after substrate stabilization, but 25 assayed marker genes across 21 neuronal groups produced no adjusted calls; the Trp53inp2 response is therefore not simply the expected cell-cycle or Notch developmental phenotype transposed into juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: SREBP, mTOR, and NFE2L1 are FBXW7-regulated substrate arms that can lead to sterol, growth, or proteostasis transcriptional responses.
main_caveats: The comparator panel perturbs pathway nodes vertically rather than deleting SCF(FBXW7) itself; Rptor and Srebf1 were flat, so convergence is absent for some pathway nodes as well.
summary: Fbxw7 does not phenocopy mTOR/SREBP-axis perturbations that are detectable in the same neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Tsc2 and Srebf2 perturbations generated sterol/metabolic DEG programs in the same analysis universe, including Cyp51, Insig1, Ldlr, Fdft1, Fads6, Dhcr24, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, and Sqle, so the absence of those genes after Fbxw7 loss is a specific FBXW7-to-SREBP/mTOR uncoupling at P16 rather than a generic inability of snRNA-seq to detect lipid-metabolic transcription.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on full Wilcoxon-score vectors and Fbxw7 is nearly flat, so tiny cosines are expected and should not be overinterpreted as mechanistic relationships.
summary: Fbxw7 had no strong data-driven signature neighbor in the full target universe.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive cosine was only 0.039 and the strongest negative cosine was -0.020 across 1772 other targets; even the strong Cdc40 and Wdr26 signatures did not reproduce the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Trp53inp2 call, arguing that the Fbxw7 result is an isolated, sparse signature rather than part of a broad recurrent perturbation module.

literature_claim: Fbxw7-Notch signaling is a neural stem-cell and neuronal-glial differentiation mechanism in embryonic or perinatal progenitor systems.
main_caveats: Adam10 and Psen1 were recovered in fewer matched groups than Fbxw7; a membrane-cleavage pathway could also have faster or protein-level effects that this 3-4 week nuclear RNA endpoint misses.
summary: Available Notch-pathway perturbations were themselves nearly silent in the Fbxw7-matched postnatal neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Notch1, Notch2, Adam10, and Psen1 perturbations lacked a robust matched neuronal transcriptome, so the absence of Hes/Hey and Notch markers after Fbxw7 loss matches a pathway that is transcriptionally quiescent in NeuN-enriched P37-44 neurons rather than a failure uniquely of the Fbxw7 guides.

literature_claim: FBXW7 is a developmental regulator, and human monoallelic deletions plus nonsense, frameshift, splice, and missense variants are associated with a variable neurodevelopmental syndrome.
main_caveats: The screen is mosaic and acute, does not assay DNA indels or protein substrates, and removes Fbxw7 after the developmental window in which much of the human phenotype may originate.
summary: The FBXW7 neurodevelopmental signal is displaced from an acute juvenile pan-neuronal transcriptional phenotype.
why_it_matters: Human FBXW7 variants cause a developmental disorder, but in this P16 mosaic LoF screen almost all specified neuronal classes were flat and the one positive class showed only Trp53inp2. That pattern refines FBXW7 disease biology toward embryonic lineage allocation, progenitor viability, glial fate, substrate-specific alleles, or non-transcriptional substrate accumulation rather than a large shared mRNA state in young postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: FcγRIV is an activating Fc receptor whose established IgG/IgE functions are concentrated in myeloid cells, while microglial FcγRIV is inducible in inflammatory CNS settings.

why_it_matters: The result turns the apparent lack of signal into a lineage statement: a postnatal FcγRIV perturbation is inert across the sampled healthy neuronal nuclei rather than exposing a hidden basal neuronal Fc-receptor program.

main_caveats: The similarity calculation is dominated by a flat Fcgr4 vector; it is useful mainly to reject strong convergence, not to infer biology from the weak ranks.
summary: Fcgr4 had no meaningful signed transcriptomic neighbor in the whole parquet universe.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative neighbors had absolute Pearson correlations no larger than 0.031, so cross-perturbation analysis provides no evidence for a shared Fcgr4 module masked by per-cell-group thresholds.

literature_claim: FcγRIV is part of a γ-chain-dependent activating Fc receptor family with overlapping IgG2a/IgG2b effector functions.
main_caveats: Fyn was measurable and flat, but it is a broad Src-family kinase rather than a FcγRIV-specific receptor subunit.

why_it_matters: Failure of Fcgr4 alone to move neuronal transcripts is not equivalent to loss of a complete Fcγ receptor signaling module or to a test of Fcgr1/Fcgr3/Fcer1g compensation in professional effector cells.

main_caveats: This is a direction-of-interpretation warning rather than evidence for efficacy or safety of FcγRIV modulation in brain disease.
summary: The pan-neuronal null should not be used to deprioritize FcγRIV biology in antibody effector or neuroinflammatory settings.
why_it_matters: Fcgr4 deletion or blockade changes IgG2a/IgG2b effector biology in vivo, and microglial FcγRIV is reported only under inflammatory CNS contexts that this young, unstimulated, NeuN-enriched screen did not sample.

literature_claim: FEZF factors are embryonic transcriptional repressors of Hes5, while DTX3 is a Deltex-family E3 ligase linked to NOTCH2 ubiquitination in non-neural cells.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene passed FDR<0.10; Pde2a is subthreshold; DNA editing was not assayed.
summary: Fezf1 loss produced a single robust transcriptional response, Dtx3 up-regulation in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: The signal is far narrower than Fezf1's developmental literature would suggest and nominates one postnatal corticofugal class as the only detectable responder in this assay.

literature_claim: Fezf1 is embedded in forebrain neurogenesis and GnRH/Kallmann developmental networks that include FEZF paralogs, Notch-Hes output, and multiple axon-guidance or chromatin disease genes.

why_it_matters: The Fezf1 L5 ET response is not a generic consequence of perturbing Notch receptors, deep-layer fate factors, or GnRH-disease genes that happened to be in the screen.

why_it_matters: The non-textbook nearest neighbors show that the Dtx3 response is isolated within the measured perturbation universe rather than part of a broad reusable module.

literature_claim: Fgf1-null mice were reported to lack overt abnormalities, and Fgf1/Fgf2 double-null phenotypes were no worse than Fgf2-null phenotypes in the assayed settings.
main_caveats: Guide-induced DNA lesions were not measured; 215 MB Dopa was missing; the result does not test embryonic, injury, diabetic, vascular, or glial FGF1 biology.
summary: P16 sparse Fgf1 loss produced no robust cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptome in any recovered cell group.
why_it_matters: A pan-FGFR ligand that is active in many developmental, injury, and metabolic contexts is not detectably required as a single endogenous ligand in healthy postmitotic NeuN+ neuronal nuclei over this 3-4 week window.

literature_claim: FGFR activation drives RAS-MAPK signaling, and exogenous central FGF1 can acutely induce ERK-cascade modules including Spry-family regulators in hypothalamic glia.
main_caveats: The tested genes are a marker panel, not phospho-ERK protein readout; they rule out a sustained downstream RNA program rather than a very transient phosphorylation event.
summary: Fgf1 LoF did not produce the canonical FGFR-RAS/MAPK immediate-early or ERK-feedback transcript program.
why_it_matters: The absent Fos/Jun/Egr/Dusp/Spry/Etv response argues that the flat screen is an informative absence of tonic FGFR transcriptional signaling, not a snRNA-seq readout mismatch for a hidden MAPK transcriptional burst.

literature_claim: FGF1 signals through FGFRs to recruit RAS-MAPK and related intracellular pathways.
main_caveats: Some central FGF components, including Fgf2 and Fgfr4, were not represented as perturbation targets; most represented comparators had very sparse one-gene DE surfaces.
summary: Directly measured FGFR/RAS/ERK-neighbor perturbations also failed to converge on a broad Fgf1-like state.
why_it_matters: The expected pathway neighbors Fgfr1, Fgfr2, Fgfr3, Fgfrl1, Sos1, Kras, and Mapk1 were represented and yielded only 0-2 isolated downstream genes per target, with score-cosines to Fgf1 of 0.0175 or lower; the Fgf1 null is therefore part of a screened FGF-axis buffer rather than an isolated ligand outlier.

literature_claim: FGF11-FGF14/FHFs are intracellular proteins that regulate voltage-gated sodium channels and are distinct from secreted canonical FGFR ligands such as FGF1.
main_caveats: The canonical secreted paralog Fgf2 was not a perturbation target, so the closest extracellular redundancy test was unavailable.
summary: The represented Fgf-family paralogs were rejected as Fgf1 phenocopies.
why_it_matters: Fgf12 and Fgf13 belong to the intracellular FHF branch rather than the secreted FGFR-ligand branch, and the data matched that family split: each had only one isolated downstream hit and essentially zero cosine to Fgf1.

main_caveats: Cosines were computed from Wilcoxon scores and are restricted to the genes and cell groups shared with Fgf1.
summary: The data-driven nearest-neighbor search did not nominate a robust Fgf1 module.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive and negative neighbours of Fgf1 were nearly orthogonal and often transcriptomically silent themselves, so no target-agnostic module should be inferred from nominal Fgf1 ranks.

literature_claim: Single intracerebroventricular FGF1 injection can induce sustained diabetes remission in rodents and elicits early hypothalamic transcriptional responses dominated by tanycytes, ependymal cells, astrocytes, and oligodendrocyte-lineage cells, with Agrp neurons the most responsive neuronal subset.
main_caveats: The screen's coarse hypothalamic groups may not contain enough arcuate Agrp neurons, and NeuN enrichment under-samples the glial populations that dominate the pharmacologic response.
summary: Hypothalamic Fgf1 LoF was not a transcriptional mirror of pharmacologic central FGF1 action.
why_it_matters: Central FGF1 agonism in diabetic rodents is a glia-rich, multicellular hypothalamic response; deleting endogenous Fgf1 in sparse healthy juvenile NeuN+ nuclei is not an adequate reverse signature and should not be used to argue against FGF1/FGFR agonism.

literature_claim: Fgf12/FHF1 is an intracellular FHF that regulates neuronal excitability; isolated Fgf12 knockout is much milder than combined FHF loss in mice.
main_caveats: The Nmnat2 signal is a single FDR<0.10 gene, and DNA indel frequency was not measured.
summary: Fgf12 CRISPR loss was almost completely buffered at the snRNA-seq level, with a singleton Nmnat2 response confined to 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
why_it_matters: The surface argues against a broad postnatal transcriptional homeostasis role for Fgf12 in this acute neuronal screen, while preserving one reproducible FDR signal rather than flattening the target to 'all null'.

literature_claim: Nmnat2 protein supply from the soma is needed for axon survival, whereas FHFs are best established as intracellular voltage-gated sodium-channel regulators.
main_caveats: No direct FGF12-Nmnat2 mechanism is established here; the claim rests on one transcript in one cell group.
summary: The sole robust Fgf12 downstream gene, Nmnat2, points to an axon-maintenance transcript rather than to altered Nav-subunit mRNA.
why_it_matters: Nmnat2 is a labile axon survival factor, so its selective down-regulation is a biologically higher-value hypothesis than an arbitrary singleton; it suggests a possible axonal-maintenance readout to test after stronger or combined FHF perturbation.

literature_claim: Nmnat2 down-regulation is an axon-maintenance risk signal.
main_caveats: Hspa5 had only 21 perturbed cells in the matched 145 group, and the convergence is a one-gene overlap.
summary: Hspa5 was the only same-direction FDR-level neighbor of the Fgf12 Nmnat2 coordinate, but its broader ER-stress signature did not accompany Fgf12 loss.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation comparison separates the Fgf12 singleton from a generic Hspa5/UPR state: both can lower Nmnat2 in 145, but Fgf12 did not induce Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Derl3, Herpud1, Asns, or other stress genes.

literature_claim: FHFs and Nav subunits function in a shared excitability apparatus, and FGF13 family biology is cell-type- and isoform-specific.
main_caveats: Fgf11, Fgf14, and several beta subunits were not represented as targets; electrophysiological phenotypes were not assayed.
summary: The measured FHF/Nav relatives did not phenocopy Fgf12 in the MH-LH TH group, so Nmnat2 is not a generic transcriptional consequence of reducing Nav-channel complex activity.
why_it_matters: Fgf13, Scn1b, Scn2a, Scn1a, and Scn8a were directly queryable; even strongly depleted Scn1b and Scn2a in 145 failed to lower Nmnat2, localizing the Fgf12 signal outside a simple shared Nav-subunit knockdown signature.

literature_claim: FGF12 pathogenic variants alter NaV1.2 and NaV1.6 gating through both loss- and gain-of-function kinetic effects, with several reports highlighting gain-of-function FHF1 epilepsy mechanisms.
main_caveats: The screen lacks DNA indel-seq and electrophysiology, so it can delimit transcriptional consequences but not channel-gating engagement.
summary: A sparse postnatal Fgf12 loss-of-function transcriptome should not be read as a negative test of FGF12 channelopathy mechanisms or sodium-channel-blocker logic.
why_it_matters: Human FGF12 epileptic encephalopathy is dominated by missense or copy-number effects on channel gating; a mosaic P16 CRISPR LoF that leaves Nav transcripts unchanged is an allele- and modality-mismatched model for those mechanisms.

literature_claim: Published FGF13 biology emphasizes embryonic forebrain migration, interneuron excitability, MSN excitability, and FHF-NaV channel regulation rather than Rell2 in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene passed FDR<0.10; mechanism of Rell2 repression is not established.
summary: Acute Fgf13 loss produced a single FDR-level downstream marker, Rell2 down-regulation, restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The only positive transcriptomic result is thalamic and one-gene, so it nominates Rell2 as a cell-class-specific marker hypothesis rather than recovering a canonical FGF13 microtubule or NaV program.

main_caveats: Correlation ranking was performed on a nearly null Fgf13 profile; it is best used to reject robust convergence, not to infer weak biology.
summary: The pre-literature whole-surface signature-neighbor search produced only near-zero correlations, and the nearest non-control positive and negative targets failed to reproduce the Rell2-containing thalamic response.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-assigning Fgf13 to a large generic Perturb-seq module; its measured signature is effectively isolated and too small for module-level inference.

literature_claim: FGF13 is an intracellular FGF homologous factor that belongs to FGF11-FGF14 and regulates NaV channels; FGF13 and FGF14 can act concertedly on voltage-gated sodium-channel localization.
main_caveats: Fgf14 was not represented as a perturbation target, so the closest published FHF comparator could not be assayed directly.

why_it_matters: A physical FHF-NaV relationship does not imply identical mRNA consequences after acute P16 LoF, and receptor-FGF targets were appropriately uncoupled from the intracellular FHF Fgf13.

literature_claim: FGFR1 is a receptor tyrosine kinase for FGF developmental and neurogenic signals that can activate FRS2/RAS-MAPK and PI3K cascades.
main_caveats: The assay does not measure DNA indels, phospho-ERK/AKT, morphology, electrophysiology, glia, olfactory bulb, or progenitors; a flat self-transcript is expected for many active indel knockouts.
summary: Fgfr1 loss produced an exceptionally sparse postnatal neuronal transcriptomic surface: only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: Canonical FGFR1 biology is potent, but this acute P16 mosaic loss-of-function experiment shows that most mature NeuN+ neuronal nuclei do not sustain a broad homeostatic, MAPK, stress, or synaptic mRNA response over 3-4 weeks.

literature_claim: HNRNPM is an hnRNP-family RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA processing; it is not an established FGFR1-MAPK transcriptional feedback gene.
main_caveats: Only Hnrnpm reached FDR<0.10 in this group; snRNA-seq did not assay HNRNPM protein or splicing outcomes.
summary: CNU-HYa/HY/MM glutamatergic neurons carried the only negative Fgfr1 downstream call, Hnrnpm down-regulation.
why_it_matters: The hit nominates an RNA-processing transcript as a possible cell-restricted Fgfr1-loss marker, but as a single near-threshold gene it should be treated as a biomarker hypothesis, not a multi-gene splicing program.

literature_claim: NIPA1 encodes a Mg2+ transporter implicated in autosomal-dominant hereditary spastic paraplegia.
main_caveats: Only Nipa1 reached FDR<0.10 in CB GABA; the FDR was 0.0668 and no transporter activity was measured.
summary: Cerebellar GABA neurons carried the only positive Fgfr1 downstream call, Nipa1 up-regulation.
why_it_matters: Nipa1 is a neuronal transporter gene with disease relevance, so its induction is a concrete follow-up marker for the CB GABA Fgfr1 perturbation even though it does not define a broader endpoint in this dataset.

literature_claim: Activated FGFR1 signals through FRS adaptors to GRB2/SOS, PTPN11, RAS-MAPK, and PI3K; sustained FGFR-MAPK output should feed ETS and DUSP/SPRY feedback genes.
main_caveats: Frs2, Frs3, and Grb2 were not direct screen targets; the test relies on represented downstream relays and steady-state RNA rather than phosphoproteomics.
summary: Fgfr1 perturbation did not lower canonical MAPK-feedback transcripts, and core MAPK-relay perturbations did not converge with the two Fgfr1 responder loci.
why_it_matters: The absence of Etv/Dusp/Spry/Fos-Jun responses is informative rather than a pure readout failure: Map2k1 loss generated detectable Vgf, Ptpn5, Unc13a, and Etv5 changes in TH Prkcd neurons, but Fgfr1 loss did not feed that program in any measured group.

literature_claim: FGFR1-3 belong to the same receptor family and can route FGF ligands into overlapping intracellular cascades, whereas FGFRL1 resembles FGFRs extracellularly but lacks the canonical kinase domain.
main_caveats: Only Fgfr2, Fgfr3, and Fgfrl1 were represented; Fgfr4 was absent, and the comparison concerns postnatal neuronal mRNA, not embryonic receptor redundancy.
summary: Fgfr2, Fgfr3, and the receptor-like Fgfrl1 were measurable but did not phenocopy Fgfr1 in the two Fgfr1 responder groups.
why_it_matters: The expected receptor-family comparison separates a shared embryonic FGFR signal-transduction apparatus from this postmitotic neuronal surface: the paralogs were essentially silent too, not redundant sources of the Hnrnpm or Nipa1 responses.

literature_claim: FGF1 is a secreted FGFR ligand, whereas FGF12 and FGF13 are FGF11-family intracellular FGFs rather than canonical extracellular FGFR activators.
main_caveats: Most canonical brain FGFR1 ligands, such as Fgf2, Fgf8, Fgf17, or Fgf18, were not represented as perturbation targets here.
summary: The represented FGF-family perturbations, Fgf1, Fgf12, and Fgf13, did not identify an autocrine FGF module feeding the Fgfr1 two-gene response.
why_it_matters: This rejects a simple matched ligand-receptor interpretation for Hnrnpm and Nipa1 within the measured targets: Fgf1 was entirely flat, and Fgf12/Fgf13 had minimal, non-matching effects consistent with their classification as intracellular FGF homologous factors rather than classic FGFR ligands.

literature_claim: No literature-based relationship to Fgfr1 was used for these data-driven neighbors.
main_caveats: The conclusion is about the computed snRNA-seq signatures; it does not exclude pathway similarity in unmeasured stages or modalities.
summary: The unbiased Fgfr1 signature-neighbor search yielded no robust biological neighbor: the best whole-vector correlations were near zero, and the two-gene restricted neighbors were only nominal at the matched loci.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-reading Cdc40, Dmd, Mc2r, Prkag2, or Flt4 as Fgfr1 pathway partners; the computation instead confirms that the Fgfr1 surface is too sparse for strong cross-perturbation convergence.

literature_claim: CCSAP is a centriole/cilia/spindle microtubule protein, and FGF signaling can regulate primary-cilium behavior in non-neuronal systems.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene crossed FDR<0.10 in this cell group; the 017 result used 60 perturbed nuclei and needs direct cilium or centrosome validation.
summary: Fgfr2 loss produced a single significant CA3-family hit, Ccsap up-regulation in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, suggesting a narrow ciliary or centrosomal response rather than a broad FGF program.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only robust positive target-specific signal and points to a plausible FGFR-cilia interface while preventing over-interpretation of a one-gene signature.

literature_claim: FGFR activation classically signals through FRS2/GRB2/SOS to RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK and induces SPRY/MKP/ETV feedback genes.
main_caveats: Braf and Map2k1 are downstream pathway nodes, not FGFR2-specific receptors; their comparison establishes assay detectability of a MAPK-like transcriptional state, not direct biochemical epistasis.
summary: Fgfr2 did not recover canonical FGF/ERK feedback genes even though Braf and Map2k1 perturbations elicited a MAPK-linked Vgf/Ptpn5/Unc13a/Etv5 program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The null cannot be dismissed as an snRNA-seq inability to detect MAPK output; it places the block at the level of FGFR2 input, receptor redundancy, or ligand availability in P16 neurons.

literature_claim: FGFR1-3 and related FGF-pathway components belong to a shared FGF signaling network with overlapping RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT effectors.
main_caveats: Several core adaptor and feedback genes, including Frs2, Grb2, Plcg1, Sprouty genes, and Etv4/5, were not perturbation targets represented in the parquet.
summary: Measured FGFR-family and nearby FGF-pathway perturbations were sparse singleton/null surfaces and did not phenocopy the Fgfr2 CA3 Ccsap response.
why_it_matters: The expected paralog or receptor-family relationship is rejected in this P16 neuronal loss-of-function context, arguing for either strong upstream buffering or very local receptor-ligand specificity.

literature_claim: Many FGFR2-related craniosynostosis alleles are gain-of-function and FGFR2 dysregulation is associated with cancers.

why_it_matters: FGFR2 is druggable and disease-linked, but acute LoF in P16 neurons is not the inverse of developmental or oncogenic receptor over-activation; this is a guardrail for therapeutic interpretation.

main_caveats: Comparator similarities were computed on the Fgfr2 top-ranked restricted signature because the FDR<0.10 surface has only one downstream gene.

literature_claim: Major Fgfr3 CNS biology is reported in embryonic progenitors, caudal telencephalon, and astrocyte-lineage cells rather than as a ubiquitous mature-neuron transcriptional driver.
main_caveats: Indel formation was not assayed, and a sparse P16 CRISPR loss-of-function perturbation does not test embryonic clonal expansion or astrocytes.

why_it_matters: The dominant biological result is not a broad FGFR transcriptional module but its absence from postmitotic NeuN+ neurons, even though Fgfr3 was represented in 22 cell groups.

literature_claim: FGFRs signal from ligand-activated receptors that traffic through endosomal compartments, and Hook3 is a Golgi/endosome dynein-dynactin cargo adaptor.

why_it_matters: Hook3 encodes an endosomal and Golgi dynein adaptor, making the lone hit most consistent with a very narrow membrane-trafficking adjustment rather than canonical ERK feedback.

literature_claim: FGFR1, FGFR2, and FGFR3 are same-family receptor tyrosine kinases and can compensate substantially for one another during early telencephalic FGF signaling.
main_caveats: The contrast is based on very sparse FDR<0.10 calls for every receptor-family perturbation.
summary: The represented FGFR-family perturbations did not phenocopy each other in P16 neurons.
why_it_matters: Fgfr1, Fgfr2, and Fgfr3 each produced only isolated, mutually distinct FDR<0.10 genes, while Fgfrl1 was flat; family membership therefore did not predict a shared postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic signature.

literature_claim: FGFR tyrosine kinases signal through intracellular RAS-MAPK and ERK-feedback transcriptional effectors.
main_caveats: Only a small MAPK-output module was detected for the downstream comparators; phospho-ERK itself was not measured.

why_it_matters: The assay was capable of recovering Vgf, Ptpn5, Etv5, and Unc13a down-regulation after core MAPK-branch perturbations, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Fgfr3 perturbation in the matched group left the same genes at FDR=1.0.

literature_claim: Human FGFR3 skeletal dysplasias are largely caused by activating FGFR3 mutations in cartilage and bone contexts, whereas FGF receptors drive canonical RAS-MAPK transcription when engaged.
main_caveats: The experiment does not measure protein phosphorylation, indel alleles, chondrocytes, astrocytes, or embryonic brain.

why_it_matters: The absence of Dusp/Spry/Etv, immediate-early, or stress activation in NeuN+ P37/44 nuclei argues against a broad postnatal neuronal transcriptional response to partial Fgfr3 loss, but it does not de-risk FGFR3 inhibition in astrocytes, embryonic progenitors, growth plate chondrocytes, or gain-of-function disease states.

literature_claim: FKBP12 manipulation changes mTOR biochemistry and synaptic plasticity in forebrain neurons and regulates TGF-beta-family receptors and calcium-channel complexes in other systems.
main_caveats: DNA indels and FKBP12 protein depletion were not assayed; a flat mRNA profile does not exclude phosphorylation, translation, calcium, or electrophysiological phenotypes.
