why_it_matters: FKBP12 is a potent biochemical scaffold in mTOR, TGF/BMP, calcineurin, ryanodine-receptor, and synaptic physiology, but acute sparse postmitotic neuronal loss does not impose a persistent steady-state nuclear RNA program.

literature_claim: FKBP12 deletion can alter mTOR phosphorylation and late LTP in forebrain tissue, so loss can have strong protein-level consequences even when assayed weeks after birth.
main_caveats: Self-mRNA FDR is not a DNA-editing assay, and nuclei in a broad cell group may include edited cells with different protein residuals.
summary: Detectable Fkbp1a self-transcript reduction was still locally buffered: L5 ET CTX and TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons showed significant Fkbp1a mRNA depletion, yet each retained 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The two self-positive groups separate target-mRNA knockdown from a downstream transcriptional response; FKBP12 can be measurably depleted at the RNA level without a broad homeostatic, mTOR, stress, or synaptic degeneration signature.

literature_claim: Brain FKBP12 deletion was reported to enhance mTOR phosphorylation, mTOR-Raptor interaction, and S6K phosphorylation.
main_caveats: Tsc2 loss is a stronger and more direct mTORC1 disinhibition than FKBP12 loss; Tsc2 downstream RNAs are not guaranteed to be exclusively mTORC1 direct.
summary: The FKBP12-to-mTORC1 expectation was not recovered: Fkbp1a was uncorrelated with Mtor, Rptor, and the mTORC1 disinhibitor Tsc2, while Tsc2 loss produced 636 downstream genes where Fkbp1a was flat.
why_it_matters: This argues that basal Fkbp1a loss is not equivalent to a sustained Tsc2-like mTORC1 transcriptional activation, even though FKBP12 conditional deletion can increase mTOR-Raptor/S6K biochemistry.

literature_claim: FKBP12 binds and inhibits ligand-free TGF-beta-family type-I receptors, and FKBP12 antagonism can disinhibit TGF/BMP signaling.
main_caveats: This screen assayed differentiated neurons, not embryonic endocardium, repair tissue, or ligand-stimulated receptor systems; absence of SMAD-like RNA does not rule out acute receptor biochemistry.
summary: No FKBP12-dependent TGF-beta/BMP-SMAD transcriptional program appeared; direct Tgfbr1, Bmpr1a, Smad1, Smad3, and Smad4 perturbations were also completely flat, and Tgfbr2, Acvr1, and Smad2 produced only one to two single-gene hits.
why_it_matters: The known receptor-inhibitory role of FKBP12 is therefore largely outside the basal NeuN-positive postmitotic transcriptomic axis sampled here, rather than a hidden broad neuronal SMAD response downstream of Fkbp1a.

literature_claim: FKBP12 complexes with RyR/IP3R and interacts functionally with calcineurin-dependent phosphorylation, including in alpha-synuclein proteotoxicity models.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure calcium flux, channel gating, NFAT localization, protein phosphorylation, or evoked neuronal activity.
summary: The calcium-channel/calcineurin branch also failed to leave a coordinated RNA footprint: Itpr1, Ryr3, Ppp3cc, and Nfatc3 were flat, Ppp3ca returned only six downstream genes, Ryr2 only one, and Fkbp1a returned none.
why_it_matters: The represented FKBP12 partners point to channel phosphorylation and calcium-dependent phosphoprotein control as the likely compartment of action, not a constitutive NFAT-like neuronal snRNA program.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed against an Fkbp1a signature with no FDR-significant downstream genes, so nearest-neighbor ranks should not be interpreted as mechanistic links.
summary: The data-driven nearest-neighbor search found no real Fkbp1a module: the strongest positive score neighbor was only r=0.032 and the strongest negative was r=-0.014 after excluding Safe_target controls.
why_it_matters: This makes the null global rather than selective failure of an expected textbook comparator; even unrelated top neighbors such as Ski, Med15, Nfyc, Bcap31, Ctcf, and Sucla2 converged or diverged from Fkbp1a only at noise-scale correlations.

literature_claim: FKBP12 can regulate calcineurin-dependent phosphorylation and alpha-synuclein toxicity under proteotoxic stress.
main_caveats: The MB Dopa cell count was the smallest Fkbp1a stratum and the experiment lacked alpha-synuclein overexpression, aging, and phosphoproteomic readout.
summary: The MB dopamine result is not a Parkinsonian FKBP12 test: only 20 Fkbp1a-targeted MB Dopa nuclei were recovered and no FDR<0.10 downstream RNA change accompanied Fkbp1a loss.
why_it_matters: FKBP12 has been tied to alpha-synuclein toxicity through calcineurin phosphoproteomics under proteotoxic challenge; the juvenile, unstressed snRNA null should not be used to rule out FKBP12-calcineurin pharmacology in dopaminergic disease models.

literature_claim: Fktn is a ribitol-phosphate transferase for α-dystroglycan matriglycan biosynthesis, while Plxdc2 has been described as a neural-developmental and PEDF-binding cell-surface receptor rather than a known FKTN effector.
main_caveats: Single-gene signal just below the conventional 0.05 FDR threshold but inside the prespecified FDR<0.10 effect threshold; the perturbed population had only 55 cells and Fktn DNA editing was not measured.
summary: Fktn CRISPR produced a single robust downstream event: Plxdc2 induction in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
why_it_matters: The screen did not recover a bulk matriglycan-loss program; it nominated a rare upper-layer excitatory response involving a cell-surface receptor gene that is developmentally active but not an established α-dystroglycan pathway component.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: DPM1, FKTN, RXYLT1 and LARGE1 feed the same functional glycosylation of DAG1/α-dystroglycan, and α-dystroglycan connects the extracellular matrix to dystrophin-glycoprotein-complex components.
main_caveats: Several closest enzymatic comparators, including Fkrp, Pomt1/2, Pomgnt2, B3galnt2, Pomk, B4gat1, Ispd and Gmppb, were not present as perturbation targets; the positive Fktn signature itself contains only Plxdc2.
summary: The Fktn Plxdc2 response was not phenocopied by measured α-dystroglycan/matriglycan or dystrophin-glycoprotein-complex perturbations.
why_it_matters: Sequential enzymes in one matriglycan pathway should often converge if the observed transcriptome were a generic loss of α-dystroglycan ligand binding; the direct contrast argues that the Plxdc2 event is Fktn/context-specific or stochastic rather than a canonical shared-pathway reporter.

literature_claim: α-dystroglycanopathy mechanisms are dominated by defective extracellular-matrix binding, pial basement-membrane integrity, glial endfeet and synapse organization rather than by a defined acute neuronal UPR or ISR program.
main_caveats: This is a transcriptional negative result, not proof that α-dystroglycan glycosylation, ligand binding, neuronal migration, or synapse density were normal.
summary: P16 neuronal Fktn loss did not elicit a broad ECM, glycosylation, stress, proteostasis, autophagy, redox, or synaptic transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: The absence is itself informative: FKTN disease biology is dominated by α-dystroglycan post-translational modification, basement-membrane architecture and synapse organization, so a sparse postmitotic snRNA-seq screen should not be expected to phenocopy congenital cortical dysplasia as a large cell-autonomous mRNA cascade.

literature_claim: In mice, Fktn deletion can deplete functional α-dystroglycan over an approximately 18-day period, and fetal Fktn or Large gene delivery at E12.5 can prevent severe cortical dysplasia in the corresponding brain models.
main_caveats: The experiment did not include embryonic delivery, astrocytes, radial glia, DNA indel calls, α-dystroglycan glycosylation assays, laminin overlays, or histology.
summary: The data reinforce that postnatal NeuN+ neuronal snRNA-seq is a poor standalone pharmacodynamic readout for FKTN brain rescue.
why_it_matters: Embryonic mouse rescue experiments place the structural-brain requirement for Fktn/Large activity in fetal development; the screen perturbed neurons only at P16 and therefore mainly tests residual postmitotic neuronal transcriptional feedback, not the glial-basement-membrane axis that determines congenital malformation.

literature_claim: FLNB is an actin-scaffolding developmental disease gene with strong skeletal/chondrocyte and embryonic neuronal-migration priors, not a known tonic mature-neuron transcription factor.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not assayed; per-group perturbed-cell counts were modest; absence was measured only in NeuN-enriched P16-to-P37/44 neurons.
summary: Flnb produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 21 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: Despite complete coverage of major glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, the postnatal sparse CRISPR LoF did not elicit proteostasis, stress, synaptic, cytoskeletal, BMP/TGF-beta, or other secondary mRNA programs, sharply restricting where a cell-autonomous FLNB loss program can operate.

literature_claim: Chondrocyte literature places FLNB in complexes or pathways with Formin1, integrin/RhoA actin remodeling, and BMP/TGF-beta/Smad/Runx2 differentiation control.
main_caveats: Rhoa and filamin paralogs were not represented; most related perturbations were themselves weak in neurons, so the result rejects convergence in this assay rather than the pathway biochemistry.
summary: The Flnb surface is uncoupled from represented FLNB actin, integrin, Rho-family, and BMP/TGF-beta/Smad pathway neighbors.
why_it_matters: The obvious Fmn1, Itgb1, Rac1, Cdc42, Tgfbr/Bmpr, Smad, and Runx2 comparators were directly represented but had score cosines from -0.002895 to 0.011168 and no shared FDR<0.10 overlap with Flnb, arguing against a latent FLNB-to-BMP/TGF-beta or FLNB-to-actin-integrin transcriptomic module in this neuronal setting.

main_caveats: Signature-neighbor cosines were computed from signed Wilcoxon scores; when Flnb has no robust DE genes, the ranking is useful mostly as a negative control for module strength.
summary: The unbiased Flnb nearest-neighbor signature is effectively random rather than a coherent module.
why_it_matters: The strongest full-overlap positive neighbor reached only cosine 0.025197 and the strongest full-overlap negative only -0.014473; partial-overlap Safe_target and Diaph2 extremes stayed similarly tiny, and the queried algorithmic neighbors had at most one FDR<0.10 gene. This makes Flnb a background-level signature rather than a hidden member of another neuronal program.

literature_claim: Human FLNB mutations and Flnb-deficient mice disrupt vertebral segmentation, joint formation, endochondral ossification, microvascular development, and chondrocyte behavior.
main_caveats: Dominant human missense alleles and recessive truncating alleles are not equivalent to sparse CRISPR LoF in postmitotic neurons.
summary: The screen refines FLNB disease biology away from an acute mature-neuron transcriptomic LoF mechanism.
why_it_matters: FLNB skeletal disorders and Flnb-null mouse phenotypes are severe, but this P16 CRISPR surface is silent in NeuN-enriched brain, indicating that disease-relevant LoF transcriptional programs are more likely in prenatal skeletal/chondrocyte or microvascular contexts, or require alleles and tissues not modeled here.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: FLRT3 is better known as an extracellular FLRT adhesion and repulsive-guidance cue influencing embryonic cortical migration and glutamatergic synapse development.
main_caveats: The two discoveries are near the 10% FDR boundary and have only 50-52 perturbed cells; indel engagement was not directly measured.
summary: P16 Flrt3 loss produced an ultra-sparse nuclear RNA response: only Dapk1 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Odc1 in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: The only reproducible biology in the DE surface is a borderline upper-layer excitatory singleton response, not a broad adhesion, axon-guidance, death, UPR, proteostasis, or synaptic down-regulation program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: Dapk1 and Odc1 have established death/autophagy and polyamine-biosynthetic functions, but they are not established direct FLRT3 effectors.
main_caveats: This is a two-gene, two-cell-class hypothesis; one unrelated spliceosome perturbation also weakly induced Odc1 in 008.
summary: The two Flrt3-regulated transcripts nominate Dapk1 and Odc1 as weak, cell-restricted sentinel genes rather than members of the canonical FLRT adhesion machinery.
why_it_matters: Dapk1 is a death/autophagy-associated kinase and Odc1 is the entry enzyme for polyamine synthesis, so their induction could mark a late calcium-stress or metabolic compensation branch downstream of disrupted surface adhesion.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: FLRT3 can form adhesive and repulsive complexes with latrophilins and UNC5 receptors and participates in glutamatergic synapse and axon-guidance biology.
main_caveats: Flrt1, Flrt2, Unc5b, Tenm1, Tenm2, and Lrrtm2 were not Flrt3-matched measurable targets; the comparison is transcriptomic, not structural.
summary: Represented FLRT3-adjacent adhesion and guidance targets did not phenocopy Flrt3: Adgrl1/2/3, Unc5c/d, Tenm3/4, Lrrtm3, Robo1, and Dcc were completely flat in matched groups, while Lrrtm1, Lrrtm4, and Nrxn1 produced only unrelated singletons.
why_it_matters: The absence of shared Dapk1/Odc1 regulation or a broader adhesion/synapse module separates the P16 Flrt3 RNA phenotype from the textbook FLRT-latrophilin-UNC5 structural complex.

main_caveats: Score-correlation neighbors are a computational result, and Flrt3 itself has only two FDR<0.10 genes.
summary: Global cross-perturbation search did not uncover a robust hidden Flrt3 neighbor: the strongest full-surface signed-score correlations were Pdx1 at r=0.02817 and Calm2 at r=-0.01588.
why_it_matters: The top data-driven neighbors were themselves nearly flat, so the Flrt3 surface behaves as a sparse idiosyncratic signature rather than one member of a recurrent perturbation module.

literature_claim: Flt3 has reported nervous-system roles, while Gak is a clathrin-mediated trafficking kinase rather than a canonical published FLT3 target.
main_caveats: The signature is a single gene at FDR 0.051 with 64 perturbed L5 ET nuclei; it is a candidate marker, not a pathway.
summary: Flt3 loss produced a selective, one-gene Gak-up response in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and nowhere else in the measured neuronal surface.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only FDR<0.10 transcriptomic event as an L5 ET biomarker candidate while preventing over-interpretation as a broad FLT3 pathway.

literature_claim: Ligand-activated and AML-mutant FLT3 signal through PI3K, RAS-MAPK, and STAT5 to regulate growth and survival.
main_caveats: The queried genes are transcript markers of pathway consequences; phosphorylation and receptor trafficking were not assayed.
summary: The Flt3 neuronal DE surface did not recover canonical FLT3 STAT5, PI3K, RAS-MAPK, survival, or inflammatory transcriptional output.
why_it_matters: An RTK immediate-phosphorylation program is not directly measured, but the secondary Socs/Pim/Dusp/immediate-early/cytokine markers that would support pathway engagement were absent, so the weak surface is biologically informative for P16 CNS neurons.

literature_claim: FLT3 is structurally related to class-III RTKs, and NGF/NTRK biology was an expected neural comparison point from the Flt3-NGF survival literature.
main_caveats: Most comparator signatures were themselves weak in matched neuronal groups; failure to converge is robust, but mechanistic opposition is not established.
summary: Neither the top score-vector neighbors nor represented RTK relatives phenocopied the Flt3 L5 ET Gak event.
why_it_matters: The absence of convergence with Kit, Csf1r, Pdgfrb, Ntrk1, Ntrk2, Ntrk3, Stat5b, Pik3r1, and Mapk1 separates the lone Flt3 event from a generic neuronal receptor-tyrosine-kinase or FLT3-downstream signature.

literature_claim: TMEM129 is an ER-resident ubiquitin ligase involved in ER-associated degradation.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene passed FDR<0.10; no broader UPR, ISR, proteasome, or lysosomal program was detected.
summary: Flt4 loss produced a single corrected cerebellar GABA response: down-regulation of the ERAD E3-ligase gene Tmem129.
why_it_matters: The only FDR-supported transcript nominates ER membrane ubiquitination rather than canonical VEGFR lymphangiogenesis as the one detectable neuronal readout; because it is a one-gene module, it should be treated as a candidate marker, not a proven ER-stress program.

literature_claim: VEGFR3/Flt4 has strong endothelial, lymphatic, neural-stem-cell, and developing glial-precursor biology rather than an established broad postmitotic neuronal transcriptional program.
main_caveats: CB GABA had only 80 perturbed cells, and DNA indel formation was not measured.
summary: The Flt4 transcriptional response was restricted to 308 CB GABA and consisted of one gene; all other 22 neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This confines any postnatal NeuN+ neuronal Flt4 effect to a very sparse cerebellar GABA state and argues against a broad pan-neuronal VEGFR3 loss-of-function program in this screen.

literature_claim: VEGFR3 signals with VEGF-C, VEGFR2/KDR, and NRP2 in endothelial and lymphatic contexts, and SOX18 and PROX1 are lymphatic-endothelial fate regulators linked to Vegfr3.
main_caveats: Several ligand and endothelial-marker genes, including Vegfc, Vegfd/Figf, Flt1, Pdpn, and Lyve1, were not represented as perturbation targets and could only be checked as Flt4 DE genes.
summary: Canonical VEGFR3-pathway comparators did not phenocopy Flt4: Kdr, Nrp1, Nrp2, Prox1, Sox18, Notch1, Tek, and Flt3 all failed to regulate Tmem129 in 308 CB GABA, and Prox1 instead produced a separate 64-gene thalamic signature.
why_it_matters: A same-pathway expectation from VEGFR2/NRP2 and SOX18/PROX1 lymphatic biology collapses in the NeuN+ postmitotic screen, showing that the Flt4 hit is not a recovered canonical VEGFR3 module.

literature_claim: Flt4/VEGFR3 loss is expected to affect VEGF-C/VEGF-D lymphangiogenesis and, in neural or glial precursor settings, proliferation, chemotaxis, and neurogenesis.
main_caveats: The assay does not include most lymphatic, vascular, glial precursor, or neural-stem-cell nuclei, so absence in neurons cannot be generalized to those lineages.
summary: Flt4 loss did not induce VEGF receptor, lymphatic-endothelial identity, or neural progenitor marker programs in any measured postmitotic neuronal cell group.
why_it_matters: The result redirects interpretation of the broad null from technical failure toward a target whose main transcriptionally visible biology lies in vascular, lymphatic, stem-cell, or glial precursor compartments absent from this NeuN+ juvenile screen.

main_caveats: Cosine similarity over nearly all measured genes is dominated by a weak, near-null Flt4 vector; it is informative mainly because the nearest values were very close to zero.
summary: Unbiased whole-surface neighbors of Flt4 were essentially zero-correlation and were rejected as biological phenocopies.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative surfaces, Tshr and Npy5r, did not reproduce the 308 CB GABA Tmem129 effect, so the Flt4 surface has no robust convergent or opposing target in the model-visible universe.

literature_claim: Loss or pathogenic variation of FLVCR1 can disrupt erythropoiesis, embryonic viability, choline metabolism, sensory neurons, and embryonic cortical neural progenitors.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation and protein loss were not measured; 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for Flvcr1.
summary: Flvcr1 was a pan-null perturbation across all 22 measured neuronal cell groups, with zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This is the central phenotype: the screen found no cell-type-restricted responder even though the target transcript was detected in every measured contrast.

main_caveats: Signature comparison was dominated by Flvcr1 near-null scores; it is useful as a negative neighbor search, not as evidence of mechanistic relationships to the listed genes.
summary: No strong data-driven signature neighbor emerged for Flvcr1; the best non-safe positive and negative Wilcoxon-score cosines were only +0.0315 for Eef2 and -0.0155 for Auts2.
why_it_matters: The flatness is not hiding a noncanonical matched module elsewhere in the perturbation universe; broad responders such as Eef2 and Wdr26 were detectable but essentially orthogonal to Flvcr1.

literature_claim: FLVCR1 loss impairs choline import, connects to Kennedy-pathway phospholipid synthesis, perturbs mitochondria, and activates HRI-dependent integrated stress in other systems.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq does not measure choline, ethanolamine, heme, or membrane lipids directly; only propagated mRNA responses were tested.
summary: Expected ISR, UPR, heme-stress, Kennedy-pathway, and heme-biosynthesis markers were unchanged after Flvcr1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The assay would have detected a propagated transcriptional stress or lipid/heme compensation program if acute Flvcr1 loss had triggered one in sampled neurons; the absence makes the null biologically informative rather than a pure readout failure.

literature_claim: FLVCR1a interacts with the IP3R3-VDAC complex at mitochondria-associated membranes and loss of Flvcr1a impairs mitochondrial calcium and energy metabolism in embryonic neural progenitors.
main_caveats: Itpr3, Vdac1/2/3, and Mcu were not perturbation targets; Itpr1 is only a represented IP3-receptor-family proxy.
summary: Represented literature-obvious comparators Itpr1, Mcph1, and Tfrc did not reveal a matched postnatal neuronal FLVCR1 module.
why_it_matters: The FLVCR1a MAM and mitochondrial-Ca2+ literature nominates IP3R/VDAC-family and Mcph1-like NPC biology, but acute Itpr1 or Mcph1 loss was also flat in the same neuronal groups, and Tfrc produced only isolated weak effects.

literature_claim: Canonical FLVCR1 and FLVCR-family phenotypes are strongest in erythroid cells, embryonic neural progenitors, retina/posterior-column sensory neurons, and FLVCR2-expressing BBB endothelium.
main_caveats: This is a negative refinement; it does not prove Flvcr1 is dispensable for all mature neurons, all time scales, or metabolite-level physiology.

why_it_matters: It warns against expecting late sparse cortical or subcortical neuronal FLVCR1 knockout to model progenitor-driven congenital hydrocephalus, erythroid heme toxicity, FLVCR2 BBB choline supply, or retina/posterior-column sensory degeneration.

literature_claim: Fmn1 encodes an FH2-domain formin with reported actin/microtubule, dendritogenesis, adherens-junction, and limb-BMP functions.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein depletion were not assayed; the conclusion is restricted to nuclear RNA abundance 3-4 weeks after P16 mosaic CRISPR.
summary: Fmn1 loss of function was transcriptionally buffered in every recovered neuronal class: 22 of 23 groups were tested and none contained a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result is a true measured pan-surface negative result, not a single underpowered slice; even the highest-count groups, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, had zero corrected downstream hits.

literature_claim: Fmn1, Fmn2, and Diaph2 all belong to the formin actin-nucleator family, whereas Cdc42/Rac1/Ral-family GTPases are neighboring actin regulators.
main_caveats: The cross-perturbation interpretation is limited by sparse hits in the comparators and by the absence of several formins from the target list.

why_it_matters: This rejects an obvious expectation that perturbing related actin regulators would create a shared cell-state signature in this assay; for these structural cytoskeletal genes, family membership did not translate into a convergent snRNA-seq program.

literature_claim: Germline Fmn1 disruption in the embryonic limb increases BMP signaling, including Msx1 up-regulation and Fgf4 reduction.
main_caveats: The BMP prior comes from limb bud development, not mature neurons; Fgf4 itself was not in the Fmn1-tested gene universe.
summary: The Fmn1 limb-BMP signature was not redeployed in neurons: BMP sentinels Msx1, Grem1, Id1, Id2, Id3, Bmp2, Bmp4, and Bmp7 all remained FDR=1.0 after Fmn1 perturbation, and BMP receptor targets were flat or isolated single-gene responders.
why_it_matters: Classical Fmn1 knockout biology would nominate BMP output as an expected secondary transcriptional readout; its total absence in postnatal NeuN-positive nuclei makes the null informative rather than simply a failure of genome-wide RNA detection.

literature_claim: Mammalian Formin-1 participates in adherens-junction actin assembly and Fmn1 also physically cooperates with Filamin B in chondrocytes.
main_caveats: Ctnnb1 is a transcriptionally active beta-catenin perturbation rather than the same biochemical node as Fmn1; this is a pathway contrast, not a claim of direct antagonism.
summary: The adherens-junction branch was separable from Fmn1: Ctnnb1 knockout produced a large thalamic glutamatergic signature, whereas Fmn1 was zero-hit in the same 145 and 151 groups and Ctnna2/Flnb gave at most isolated hits.
why_it_matters: Fmn1 can bind alpha-catenin and participate in junctional actin assembly, but the screen shows that postmitotic neuronal Fmn1 loss does not collapse beta-catenin-dependent thalamic transcription.

literature_claim: In cultured mouse hippocampal neurons, Fmn1 is up-regulated by Ngn3, Fmn1-Ib overexpression increases primary dendrites and glutamatergic synaptic inputs, and Fmn1 siRNA blocks Ngn3-induced dendritogenesis/synaptogenesis.
main_caveats: The screen used loss-of-function in already postmitotic P16 neurons and read out nuclear RNA rather than live neurite initiation or synapse counts.
summary: The embryonic Ngn3-Fmn1 dendritogenesis/synaptogenesis axis was absent at the RNA level: Fmn1 did not regulate synaptic or dendritic sentinel transcripts, and Neurog3, Notch1, and Notch2 perturbations were zero- or single-gene responders in the matched postnatal surface.
why_it_matters: The Fmn1 neuronal prior came from E17 hippocampal cultures at 1-5 DIV and predicts dendrite and glutamatergic-input morphology; those phenotypes did not manifest as a durable broad transcriptional state after P16 editing.

literature_claim: FMN2 is a neuronal formin linked to spine density, growth-cone actin, memory, and embryonic Wnt-dependent progenitor proliferation.
main_caveats: DNA indel engagement and cytoskeletal morphology were not measured; a strong non-transcriptional phenotype could coexist with this sparse RNA surface.
summary: Acute P16 Fmn2 loss produced only two FDR<0.10 downstream calls across 22 recovered neuronal groups, with one singleton in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and one in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
why_it_matters: The result argues against Fmn2 driving a broad steady-state nuclear RNA program in juvenile postmitotic neurons and forces the canonical actin/spine biology to be interpreted as mostly structural or temporally displaced.

literature_claim: SS18 is exchanged from neural BAF complexes as cells exit progenitor states, and inappropriate SS18 persistence can impair dendritic outgrowth.
main_caveats: Single-gene signature; no additional BAF-complex or progenitor-state module passed FDR<0.10.
summary: Ss18 was selectively up-regulated after Fmn2 perturbation in L4/5 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: The strongest Fmn2 RNA event involves a BAF chromatin-remodeling subunit, not an actin gene, suggesting a narrow compensatory or chromatin-state marker worth validating in cortical IT neurons.

literature_claim: PIGN encodes an endoplasmic-reticulum enzyme required for GPI-anchor biosynthesis.
main_caveats: The adjusted signal is close to the 0.10 threshold and no other GPI-anchor gene was significant.
summary: Pign was up-regulated after Fmn2 perturbation in CNU-LGE LSX GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: This nominates GPI-anchor biosynthesis as an unexpected, cell-restricted Fmn2-associated transcript, but only as a hypothesis because it is a one-gene FDR=0.0686 event.

literature_claim: Fmn2 participates in Lrp6 endocytosis and Wnt-associated β-catenin/Dvl2 trafficking in embryonic neural progenitors.
main_caveats: Ctnnb1 detection was strongest in thalamic groups rather than the two Fmn2 singleton groups; this tests pathway convergence, not direct biochemical Wnt activity.
summary: The embryonic Fmn2/Wnt/β-catenin axis is uncoupled from the acute postmitotic Fmn2 signature.
why_it_matters: Ctnnb1, Gsk3b, Lrp5, Lrp6, and Mrtfa did not phenocopy Fmn2 in its two responder groups, and Fmn2 was flat even in thalamic neurons where Ctnnb1, Gsk3b, and Lrp6 perturbations produced detectable DE surfaces; the canonical Wnt expectation is therefore a developmental/progenitor prior, not the dominant juvenile neuronal output.

literature_claim: Fmn2 belongs to the formin actin-regulator family and acts in growth-cone actin structures.
main_caveats: Fmn1 may not substitute for Fmn2, and Diaph2 was recovered in only two non-responder groups, so this is a negative phenocopy test rather than a complete formin-family survey.
summary: Formin-family perturbations represented in the screen did not converge with Fmn2.
why_it_matters: Fmn1 was recovered across 22 groups and had no downstream DE, including no Ss18 or Pign response in the Fmn2 responder groups; Diaph2 was only sparsely recovered and also flat. The Fmn2 singleton signature is not a generic formin-family state in this assay.

literature_claim: No literature comparator was used for the pre-literature whole-universe neighbor search.
main_caveats: Because the Fmn2 surface itself contains only two FDR genes, global correlations are dominated by weak Wilcoxon-score structure and should be used to reject strong convergence, not to infer a mechanistic relationship to the ranked neighbors.
summary: No strong data-driven signature neighbor or anti-neighbor of Fmn2 was present in the model-visible target universe.
why_it_matters: The top global correlations were near zero and the top ranked neighbors failed to reproduce Ss18/Pign in matched responder groups, indicating that Fmn2 does not sit on a common, repeatedly induced perturbation axis in this dataset.

literature_claim: UCP4/SLC25A27 is a neuronal mitochondrial uncoupling protein that can reduce ROS production and increase resistance to metabolic or oxidative stress.
main_caveats: Slc25a27 was the sole FDR<0.10 downstream gene; no broader mitochondrial, UPR, ISR, or redox transcriptional module accompanied it.
summary: Acute Fmr1 perturbation produced a singleton Slc25a27/UCP4 induction in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: This nominates mitochondrial proton-leak and oxidative-stress buffering as the only FDR-supported nuclear mRNA response to Fmr1 loss in the screen, but the interpretation is hypothesis-generating because it rests on one FDR<0.10 gene.

main_caveats: The residualized metric is dominated by a near-null Fmr1 vector; the only FDR-overlap test is effectively a one-gene Slc25a27 test.
summary: The whole Fmr1 response is nearly orthogonal to other perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: The data-driven neighbor search did not reveal a strong convergent disease or pathway neighbor; even the best residualized dense-logFC neighbors were close to zero, so the Fmr1 surface is best treated as isolated and strongly buffered on the nuclear transcriptome axis.

literature_claim: FMR1, FXR1, and FXR2 form the FXR family; FMRP can repress translation through CYFIP1/eIF4E, and FMRP counterbalances group-I mGluR-stimulated protein synthesis.
main_caveats: Fxr2, Eif4e, Arc, Rps6kb1, Pten, and Rheb were not recovered as directly testable target perturbations here; Fxr1 and Grm1 were recovered in only subsets of Fmr1-matched groups.
summary: FXR, CYFIP, eIF4G, and group-I-mGluR single-gene perturbations do not phenocopy Fmr1 in this acute snRNA screen.
why_it_matters: Although FXR paralogs, CYFIP1, and group-I mGluRs are literature-obvious FMRP relatives or regulators, Fxr1, Cyfip1, Cyfip2, Grm1, Grm5, and Eif4g1 each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the matched recovered groups, matching Fmr1 more by absence than by a shared effector signature.

literature_claim: Fmr1 loss has been linked to elevated mTOR-dependent translation, and TSC1/TSC2 are upstream inhibitors of mTORC1 in the CNS.
main_caveats: The screen perturbed Mtor itself by loss of function, not activation; Tsc2 is therefore the more directionally comparable mTORC1-activating perturbation.
summary: Tsc2 loss, not Fmr1 loss, is the mTOR-linked perturbation that generates a broad neuronal transcriptome in the same analysis universe.
why_it_matters: This separates FMRP-dependent translational derepression from direct mTORC1 disinhibition: Tsc2 had 636 downstream DEGs in 21 Fmr1-matched recovered groups, whereas Fmr1 had 1 and Mtor loss had 6.

literature_claim: FMRP regulates mRNA translation at synapses and stalls ribosomes on many synaptic and autism-linked target mRNAs; expected loss-of-function consequences are therefore translational and protein-level at many targets.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot score ribosome occupancy, local dendritic translation, synaptic protein abundance, or electrophysiology directly.
summary: Canonical FMRP target mRNAs and secondary stress programs are absent from the Fmr1 nuclear transcriptome.
why_it_matters: The screen would have detected a robust compensatory UPR, ISR, heat-shock, autophagy, proteasome, or large FMRP-target mRNA-abundance program, but none appeared; this supports a model in which acute Fmr1 loss primarily perturbs local translation, protein abundance, excitability, or spine dynamics rather than steady-state nuclear mRNA abundance.

literature_claim: FNTB is the catalytic beta subunit of FTase, and complete FTase loss is essential in embryos but buffered in many adult tissues.
main_caveats: DNA indels and residual FTase activity are unmeasured; sparse effects may miss protein-localization or phosphorylation phenotypes.
summary: Fntb produced a near-pan-neuronal buffered transcriptional surface: only Lhfpl4 and Nefl passed downstream FDR<0.10 across all 23 recovered cell groups, and Fntb itself was never FDR-significant.
why_it_matters: A weak self-transcript is expected in this CRISPR platform; the important observation is that a core protein-prenylation enzyme failed to evoke a broad nuclear RNA stress, mTOR, or Ras/MAPK program in postmitotic juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: LHFPL4/GARLH4 is required for synaptic targeting and clustering of GABA(A) receptors in hippocampal neurons.
main_caveats: Single downstream gene at FDR 0.0888; no broader inhibitory-synapse module was detected.
summary: Fntb up-regulated Lhfpl4 only in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, nominating a focal hippocampal inhibitory-synapse auxiliary response.
why_it_matters: LHFPL4 is a GABA(A)-receptor clustering factor in hippocampal neurons; the Fntb hit points to a synaptic compensation candidate outside the canonical FTase/Ras story.

literature_claim: NEFL forms axonal neurofilaments and contributes to axon caliber, synaptic properties, and organelle trafficking.
main_caveats: Only 27 Fntb-perturbed nuclei supported this cell group and no additional axonal-injury genes passed FDR<0.10.
summary: Fntb up-regulated Nefl in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, a low-count focal neurofilament response.
why_it_matters: NEFL is an axonal structural protein; its isolated increase could mark altered axonal cytoskeleton handling after prenylation disruption, but cannot yet be read as neuronal injury.

literature_claim: FTase substrates feed Ras/MAPK and Rheb/mTOR signaling, while K-Ras can bypass FTase through alternative geranylgeranylation.
main_caveats: Some same-complex processing targets were absent from the parquet, and comparator engagement was not measured by indel sequencing.
summary: Represented FTase substrate and downstream Ras/Rheb pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Fntb in the Fntb responder cell groups.
why_it_matters: The lack of shared Lhfpl4 or Nefl regulation by Hras, Kras, Braf, Raf1, Mapk1, Mtor, Cdc42, Rac1, or Rala argues that P16 Fntb loss does not simply translate into a Ras/MAPK or Rheb/mTOR transcriptional state in wild-type neurons.

main_caveats: A target with only two FDR-significant genes is intrinsically poorly suited for stable nearest-neighbor analysis.
summary: Neither global nor restricted data-driven cross-perturbation rankings yielded a robust Fntb neighbor.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting weak numerical neighbor ranks as biology: the isolated two-gene Fntb surface has no reproducible transcriptional phenocopy among represented perturbations.

main_caveats: DNA indel rates were not measured; low on-target RNA movement is expected in this screen and is not evidence that the CRISPR perturbation failed.
summary: Acute Foxc2 loss of function was pan-null across the 23 recovered NeuN+ neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: FOXC2 is a transcription factor with strong developmental and vascular priors, yet a P16 mosaic CRISPR perturbation in postmitotic neurons produced zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes in 388,023 non-self tests; this makes the neuronal null itself the main phenotype rather than a missed canonical program.

literature_claim: FOXC1/FOXC2 directly cooperate with VEGF and Notch signaling at Dll4 and Hey2, and FOXC2 cooperates with NFATc1 and cytoskeletal regulators during lymphatic-valve maturation.
main_caveats: Some expected genes are rare in neuronal nuclei, so this is a statement about the recovered NeuN+ transcriptomes, not about endothelial or lymphatic cells.

why_it_matters: The absence is not a generic snRNA-seq readout failure: FOXC2's canonical outputs are transcriptional and the expected genes were measured, but their Foxc2 FDR values were uniformly 1.0 in the neuronal surface.

literature_claim: FOXC2 is embedded in Notch, VEGF, NFATc1, BMP/TGF-beta and Foxc1/Foxc2 cooperative developmental networks in non-neuronal systems.
main_caveats: The neighbor analysis is restricted to signed Wilcoxon-score vectors and becomes intrinsically low dynamic range because Foxc2 itself has no FDR<0.10 genes.

literature_claim: FOXC2 loss of function causes lymphatic and venous valve disease through endothelial/lymphatic programs that include valve maturation and cytoskeletal maintenance.
main_caveats: This is a prioritization warning rather than proof of benefit for any FOXC2-directed therapy.
summary: The neuronal null should not be used to discount FOXC2 as a lymphatic or vascular disease target.
why_it_matters: Human FOXC2 disease is dominated by lymphedema-distichiasis and valve failure, and mouse work places the actionable cytoskeletal arm in lymphatic endothelial valves; those cell types are largely absent from this NeuN+ postnatal screen.

why_it_matters: It gives a molecular readout consistent with disinhibition: loss of a postsynaptic inhibitory GABA_A subunit can be converted into Ca2+/activity-dependent nuclear signaling when the circuit and receptor context cross threshold.

literature_claim: GABRA1, GABRB2, and GABRG2 can occupy the same abundant GABA_A receptor class and all carry epileptic-encephalopathy disease alleles, which could have predicted similar perturbation signatures.

why_it_matters: The beta2 response is subunit- and context-specific in this assay rather than a pan-GABA_A receptor or generic GABAergic-transmission signature, warning against assuming exchangeability of disease-associated receptor subunits.

literature_claim: Single GABA_A receptor subunits function in heteropentamers, and β-subunit paralog context can buffer the effect of a single β perturbation.

literature_claim: Gabrd encodes an extrasynaptic GABA_A receptor δ subunit whose primary expected phenotype is altered tonic conductance, not obligatory transcriptional rewiring.

literature_claim: GABA_A receptor subunits form pharmacologically and anatomically specialized pentamers, and immediate-early genes report neuronal activity-dependent transcription.

why_it_matters: The same-family comparison shows that the array can recover activity-linked transcription after GABA_A receptor perturbation, but δ-subunit loss alone is much more transcriptionally silent than beta-2 or gamma-2 loss.

literature_claim: CTTNBP2 regulates cortactin mobility and dendritic spine formation and maintenance.

main_caveats: The verdict depends on the centered-cosine definition used for this report; it rejects these particular whole-vector neighbors, not the existence of all possible context-specific Gabrd relationships.

why_it_matters: The measured target is too sparse for whole-transcriptome nearest-neighbor interpretation; related-target and one-gene recurrence tests are more trustworthy than nominal global cosine ranks.

literature_claim: GABRG2 encodes a gamma2 subunit needed for normal GABA-A receptor pharmacology and synaptic receptor maintenance.
main_caveats: Indels and protein-level receptor loss were not measured, and the two downstream genes do not constitute a broad pathway.

why_it_matters: The dominant phenotype of a GABA-A gamma2 subunit deletion in this system is transcriptomic buffering; the expected primary effects are receptor localization and channel function, not a broad mRNA program.

literature_claim: Bdnf transcription is induced by calcium/neural activity, and Vgf is a BDNF- and activity-responsive neuronal peptide gene.
main_caveats: Each responder cell group has only one significant downstream gene; Bdnf and Vgf were not perturbation targets in this dataset.
summary: Bdnf and Vgf were the only robust Gabrg2-induced downstream genes and nominate activity/neurotrophin sentinel readouts in two glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: The identity and direction of the two hits are compatible with a compensatory response to altered inhibition, while the lack of Fos, Npas4, Nr4a1, Arc, or Egr FDR hits argues against a generalized immediate-early response.

literature_claim: Bdnf is activity regulated, and Kcnq2/Kcnb1 potassium-channel loss can elevate neuronal excitability.
main_caveats: Neighbor scoring was restricted to the two robust Gabrg2 features; Psmb4 was broad and supported by only 41 perturbed cells in this group.
summary: The Gabrg2 Bdnf feature in L4/5 IT neurons converged with Kcnb1 and Kcnq2 perturbations, whereas the proteasome target Psmb4 shared Bdnf within a much broader low-cell-count signature.
why_it_matters: Data-driven convergence with potassium-channel perturbations supports an excitability-linked interpretation of Bdnf up-regulation and identifies Kcnb1 and Kcnq2 as more informative neighbors than same-complex GABA-A paralogs for this feature.

literature_claim: Gamma2-containing receptors and gephyrin-associated inhibitory synapses occupy a common receptor-clustering pathway, and GABRG2, GABRB, GABRA, and GABRD family members are all epilepsy-relevant inhibitory receptor genes.
main_caveats: Only represented relatives could be tested; several GABA-A subunit targets were not in the parquet universe.
summary: Measured GABA-A receptor subunits and inhibitory-synapse neighbors did not phenocopy the two Gabrg2 responder signatures.
why_it_matters: The result argues that receptor-complex membership is insufficient to predict a shared postmitotic snRNA response; gamma2 loss has cell-context-specific transcriptional leakage from an otherwise off-axis synaptic perturbation.

literature_claim: Vgf is inducible by BDNF and participates in neuronal plasticity.
main_caveats: The mechanistic relation between Lrp1, Zbtb7a, Sin3a, and Vgf was not resolved by the two-feature overlap.
summary: Vgf up-regulation in MB Glut was recurrent across Lrp1, Zbtb7a, and Sin3a, with Zbtb7a and Sin3a producing hundreds of additional DE genes.
why_it_matters: Vgf is a real Gabrg2 output in MB Glut, but cross-perturbation recurrence shows it is a generic neuropeptide/activity endpoint rather than a GABA-A-specific module.

main_caveats: The rejection is restricted to the two Gabrg2 FDR features.
summary: Bcl11b and Dlgap4 were the strongest raw opposite-direction restricted-signature candidates but showed no robust inverse Bdnf/Vgf FDR signal.
why_it_matters: This prevents a noisy two-gene projection from being over-interpreted as an anti-Gabrg2 state; the robust Gabrg2 surface has positive one-feature neighbors but no FDR-supported negative neighbor.

literature_claim: GABA_A receptors are ligand-gated chloride channels, γ3-containing receptors are low-abundance relative to γ2 populations, and mice lacking Gabrg3 or Gabrg3 plus Gabra5 were overtly normal.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure DNA indels, inhibitory currents, receptor surface abundance, or drug binding, so the finding is confined to the P16 mosaic snRNA-seq axis.
summary: Gabrg3 loss of function produced a pan-measured transcriptomic null: all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result turns the absence of DEGs into biology: an accessory γ3 GABA_A receptor subunit can be removed sparsely after P16 without a detectable cell-autonomous nuclear stress, receptor-compensation, or activity response.

literature_claim: γ3 can assemble with α and β2/3 subunits, but γ-subunit choice confers distinct native receptor abundance and pharmacology.
main_caveats: The comparator signatures were small: Gabrg2 and Gabrd produced one or two downstream genes, and only Gabrb2 produced more than a handful of FDR<0.10 genes.
summary: Literature-obvious GABA_A relatives did not phenocopy Gabrg3; Gabrg2, Gabrb2, and Gabrd had small, cell-restricted FDR<0.10 signatures where Gabrg3 was flat, while seven other receptor-subunit targets were also flat.
why_it_matters: Direct comparison separates γ3 from γ2 and β2 biology in this assay and shows that the absence of Gabrg3-induced DE is not because all GABA_A receptor perturbations are invisible to the Wilcoxon readout.

main_caveats: Pearson correlations were computed against a nearly structureless Gabrg3 vector; the only conclusion is absence of robust convergence, not mechanistic opposition among the listed neighbors.
summary: The data-driven Gabrg3 signature neighbors were effectively uncorrelated with Gabrg3 and were rejected as biological convergent modules.
why_it_matters: The unbiased search did not reveal a hidden Gabrg3-like transcriptomic state; the strongest positive and negative neighbors had |r|≤0.031 over Wilcoxon-score vectors and were unrelated or near-null targets.

literature_claim: GABRG3 lies in the 15q11-q13 GABRB3/GABRA5/GABRG3 cluster and has been reported in family-based associations with autistic disorder and alcohol dependence.
main_caveats: Human association studies do not establish coding loss of function or the same developmental window; the screen cannot test unsampled olfactory bulb, hindbrain, non-neuronal, or circuit-level phenotypes.
summary: Human GABRG3 disease associations are not mimicked by a simple sparse postnatal coding LoF transcriptional program in the sampled mouse neurons.
why_it_matters: Association signals near GABRG3 in autism or alcohol dependence may reflect regulatory alleles, circuit-level physiology, other 15q11-q13 genes, or developmental/network contexts rather than a large cell-autonomous DEG cascade after acute Gabrg3 loss.

literature_claim: Gabrr2 encodes a rho subunit of a GABA-gated chloride channel whose best-established output is receptor current, especially in retinal bipolar cells, rather than a defined transcriptional program.
main_caveats: DNA indels and receptor currents were not measured; the flat Gabrr2 mRNA row is expected under sparse CRISPR and does not by itself prove or disprove protein knockout.
summary: Gabrr2 produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The screen strongly argues against a broad postnatal nuclear stress, proteostasis, immediate-early, or synaptic-remodeling program after sparse Gabrr2 perturbation in the sampled brain panel; the result is flat across both glutamatergic and GABAergic classes rather than restricted to one low-power group.

literature_claim: Rho subunits sit within the broader GABA_A ligand-gated chloride-channel superfamily but form pharmacologically and physiologically distinct GABA_A-rho/GABA_C receptors rather than the same dominant alpha/beta/gamma brain receptors.
main_caveats: The comparator signatures are themselves sparse, so this is a restricted response-contrast rather than a large shared-module test.
summary: Gabrr2 did not phenocopy the few activity-gene responses elicited by represented classical GABA_A receptor subunits.
why_it_matters: The assay can detect an immediate-early/activity transcriptional echo of inhibitory-receptor perturbation, as Gabrb2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut up-regulated Nr4a1, Vgf, Fos, Npas4 and related genes and Gabrg2 perturbation up-regulated Bdnf or Vgf in two groups. Gabrr2 remained at zero FDR<0.10 genes and had near-zero correlations to all tested alpha/beta/gamma/delta subunits, refining rho2 as not a driver of that sampled brain response.

main_caveats: Correlation over a null Gabrr2 vector reports absence of a stable signature; it should not be interpreted mechanistically for the weak neighboring targets.
summary: The whole-universe signature scan found no meaningful positive or negative Gabrr2 neighbor.
why_it_matters: The nearest targets nominated without literature priors were not hidden phenocopies: the largest Pearson correlations across the full Wilcoxon surface were only +0.025 and -0.015, and those targets had zero to four total downstream DE genes. Gabrr2 therefore lacks both a canonical GABAergic match and an unexpected transcriptomic match in this screen.

literature_claim: GAD2 encodes GAD65, a glutamate decarboxylase that makes GABA and is concentrated in GABAergic neurotransmission.
main_caveats: Gad2 mRNA was significantly reduced in five of eight measured GABAergic groups; DNA indel rates and GAD65 protein were not measured.
summary: Gad2 perturbation produced a target-transcript drop only in inhibitory neuron classes, with robust Gad2 self-DE in five GABAergic groups and no significant self-drop in any glutamatergic group.
why_it_matters: The recovered self-transcript effect is aligned with the GAD65/GABA-neuron axis and separates Gad2 biology from excitatory-cell nulls; the absence of downstream genes means this is an engagement-and-selectivity finding, not a transcriptional effector program.

main_caveats: The metric used all matched Wilcoxon scores, so it is intentionally descriptive rather than a mechanistic pathway test.
summary: Gad2 had no meaningful whole-universe signature neighbor: the best data-driven positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations were |r|≤0.030.
why_it_matters: This rejects the possibility that Gad2 carried a weak but coherent transcriptome program hidden under the FDR threshold; Wdr26, Dstyk, Zhx3, Safe_target_39, Safe_target_81, and B9d1 were numerical nearest neighbors rather than biological phenocopies.

literature_claim: GABA is synthesized presynaptically by glutamate decarboxylase and loaded into synaptic vesicles by the vesicular inhibitory amino-acid transporter; GAD65 has been linked to vesicular GABA filling.
main_caveats: Gad1, the basal GABA-synthesis paralog, was not represented as a perturbation target, and neurotransmitter content or release was not measured.
summary: Gad2 aligned with presynaptic GABA-axis perturbations by being effectively self-only at the transcriptome level; Slc32a1 also produced no downstream DE, and Slc6a1 and Abat produced only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene each.
why_it_matters: The matched comparator surface argues that sparse perturbation of GABA synthesis, vesicular loading, reuptake, or catabolism is not sufficient to trigger a robust nuclear program, even when transporter or enzyme transcripts are detectably reduced.

literature_claim: Reduced GABAergic inhibition can produce activity-dependent neuronal outputs, and GABA acts through ionotropic GABA-A and metabotropic GABA-B receptors.
main_caveats: The receptor signatures were themselves small and cell-type restricted; they show detectability of selected GABA-pathway transcriptional effects, not a broad receptor phenocopy of Gad2.
summary: Postsynaptic GABA receptor subunit loss could produce sparse activity-regulated DE where Gad2 was flat: Gabrb2 induced a Nr4a1/Vgf/Fos/Npas4 module in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons and Gabrg2 induced Vgf or Bdnf in two excitatory groups.
why_it_matters: The GAD2 null is therefore not a universal failure to observe GABA-pathway biology in the screen; postsynaptic receptor perturbations cross a transcriptional threshold in selected cells whereas presynaptic GABA supply perturbations usually do not.

literature_claim: GAD65-deficient mice show stress-sensitive seizures and anxiety-like phenotypes, and GAD65 is a human autoantigen in stiff-person/GAD-antibody spectrum disease.
main_caveats: The assay sampled unstimulated nuclei rather than stressed networks, behavior, GABA release, EEG, or autoimmunity.
summary: The screen did not recover a Gad2-driven seizure or anxiety surrogate: Fos, Npas4, Nr4a1, Vgf, Bdnf, Arc, Egr1, and Homer2 all had FDR=1.0 across measured Gad2 groups.
why_it_matters: Known GAD65 loss phenotypes are circuit- and behavior-level inhibitory defects; a sparse postnatal snRNA null should not be read as evidence that GAD65 inhibition is transcriptionally or clinically inert.

literature_claim: Galanin is a secreted neuropeptide/GMAP precursor acting through GalR GPCRs to regulate neuroendocrine, synaptic, seizure, pain and injury physiology.
main_caveats: This finding is restricted to steady-state snRNA-seq in sparsely edited P16 mouse neurons and does not test peptide abundance, GalR occupancy, electrophysiology, behavior, pituitary, peripheral sensory, or spinal functions.
summary: Gal loss-of-function produced a full-surface downstream transcriptional null across the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: Across 371796 downstream tests there were no FDR<0.10 genes and no robust immediate-early, neuropeptide, Gal receptor, cAMP, or GIRK transcriptional program, so sparse P16 Gal editing did not elicit a broad cell-autonomous nuclear RNA response by P37-P44.

literature_claim: GALR1, GALR2 and GALR3 are the known GPCR receptors for galanin-family peptides, and GALP is a structurally related GalR ligand.
main_caveats: Only Galr1 was represented as a perturbation target; a shared absence of FDR-level DE is a negative comparator result, not evidence of molecular overlap.
summary: The direct receptor perturbation Galr1 mirrors Gal as a 22-group transcriptional null, while Galr2, Galr3 and Galp were absent as perturbation targets.
why_it_matters: The only measurable Gal receptor-family comparator did not phenocopy with a positive RNA module; this converts the Gal null from an isolated target observation into a Gal/GalR-axis readout limitation in this sparse nuclear transcriptomic assay.

literature_claim: GalR1 is a brain galanin GPCR that signals mainly through inhibitory Gi/Go/cAMP pathways and is expressed in discrete forebrain and other CNS regions.
main_caveats: No DNA indel calls are available; broad cell groups can dilute rare Galr1-positive subtypes, and several on-target logFC values are near-zero-expression artifacts despite flat Wilcoxon scores.
summary: Acute Galr1 loss generated a pan-surface basal transcriptional null: no measured neuronal group contained even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10, and the on-target Galr1 row was FDR=1.0 in all 22 represented groups.
why_it_matters: For a sparse, ligand-gated neuropeptide GPCR, this is evidence against a tonic cell-autonomous Galr1 transcriptional maintenance program in juvenile postmitotic neurons, not evidence that Galr1 biology is absent from the brain.

literature_claim: Galanin is the peptide ligand for GalR1, GalR2, and GalR3 and can coexist with classical neurotransmitters in CNS neurons.
main_caveats: Cosine comparisons use weak Galr1 scores because Galr1 has no FDR-significant genes; ligand perturbation in a sparse mosaic design may not remove extracellular galanin supplied by neighboring unperturbed cells.
summary: Neither unbiased signature matching nor the encoded Gal ligand nominated a real Galr1-like transcriptome. The closest score-vector neighbors had absolute cosine <=0.033, and Gal itself had 0 downstream genes and cosine 0.00292 to Galr1.
why_it_matters: The receptor null is internally reproducible at the pathway entry point: mosaic loss of Gal, which would be the most obvious ligand-side phenocopy if a cell-autonomous galanin tone existed, was also flat.

literature_claim: GalR1 activation can inhibit adenylyl cyclase through Gi/o, activate GIRK channels, and in locus coeruleus GalR1 abundance is regulated through cAMP/CREB feedback.
main_caveats: Most signaling comparators were not paralogous receptors, Galr2/Galr3 were unavailable, and CREB targets were queried as a focused absence test rather than inferred from a Galr1 DE signature.
summary: The known GalR1 cAMP/GIRK axis did not appear as a downstream Galr1 response: curated CREB and activity transcripts remained FDR=1.0 after Galr1 loss, Galr2 and Galr3 were not perturbation targets, and represented effectors were mostly self-only or null.
why_it_matters: This separates acute receptor deletion from direct manipulation of PKA/CREB and GIRK signaling; the dataset does not support a chronic CREB feedback loop in the sampled basal cell groups even though Creb1 perturbation itself can create a detectable transcriptome.

literature_claim: Reduction or deletion of GalR1 in C57BL/6J mice increases hippocampal neuronal loss after kainate-induced status epilepticus.
main_caveats: The screened groups are broad, the assay was not a kainate or status-epilepticus challenge, and neuronal abundance loss was not the primary DE readout.
summary: Hippocampal-associated Galr1 perturbation was flat in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut despite seizure and kainate literature implicating GalR1 in hippocampal protection.
why_it_matters: The Galr1 injury literature is therefore better read as a network/excitotoxic-challenge phenotype than as a tonic CA1/CA3/DG survival transcriptome measurable three to four weeks after sparse postmitotic receptor deletion.

literature_claim: GATA1 is primarily an erythroid and megakaryocytic transcription factor rather than a broadly active postmitotic neuronal selector.
main_caveats: The parquet does not measure DNA indels; Git1 and Rab18 were isolated subthreshold hits and are not interpreted as a pathway.
summary: Gata1 loss-of-function was a complete neuronal DE null across all 23 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: For a DNA-binding transcription factor, a real cell-autonomous role in the assayed cells should usually be visible as RNA changes; the lack of any FDR<0.10 downstream gene localizes Gata1's canonical activity away from P16-to-P44 NeuN+ neurons rather than nominating a neuronal target program.

literature_claim: GATA1 partners with erythroid/megakaryocytic regulators including KLF1 and FOG/ZFPM1 to drive blood precursor differentiation.
main_caveats: Several closest blood regulators, including Gata2, Zfpm1, Tal1, Lmo2, and Ldb1, were not perturbation targets, so their absence is inferred from downstream gene tests rather than direct target perturbations.
summary: The expected erythroid/megakaryocytic GATA1 circuit was absent both downstream of Gata1 and across related perturbations represented in the same screen.
why_it_matters: This converts a flat target result into a lineage-specific conclusion: globin, heme, platelet, Klf1, and Zfpm1/FOG-linked transcripts were stable after Gata1 perturbation, and Gata3, Gata4, Gata6, Klf1, Gfi1b, Epor, Mpl, Spi1, Myc, and Zfpm2 did not reveal a masked GATA-like neuronal module.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed from whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon scores; because Gata1 itself has no FDR-defined responders, any neighbor is necessarily a weak, noise-dominated restricted-signature comparison.
summary: Unbiased signature-neighbor search found only near-zero Gata1 correlations in the 1773-target universe.
why_it_matters: The top positive neighbors Fbxo11, Idh3a, and Npy1r had cosine similarities of only 0.043 or less, and the top negative neighbor Wdr26 had a broad real signature that still correlated only -0.023 with Gata1; hence the nominal Gata1 ranks are not a recurrent neuronal module shared with other perturbations.

literature_claim: GATA1 is elevated in MDD dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and is sufficient, when overexpressed in PFC neurons, to repress synapse-related genes.
main_caveats: The assay did not model MDD, chronic stress, adult prefrontal anatomy, or GATA1 overexpression; the result should not be read as disproving a gain-of-function disease-state role.
summary: Baseline Gata1 loss in healthy juvenile mouse neurons did not invert a reported GATA1-overexpression synaptic-repression program.
why_it_matters: The MDD/PFC literature predicts that high neuronal GATA1 can repress synaptic genes; Calm2, Syn1, Rab3a, Rab4b, and Tubb4a all remained FDR=1 after Gata1 CRISPR, arguing that the disease observation requires induced or ectopic GATA1 rather than tonic endogenous Gata1 activity in these neurons.

literature_claim: HECTD2 encodes a HECT-domain E3 ubiquitin ligase; a direct neuronal Gata3-Hectd2 regulatory edge is not established by the cited literature.
main_caveats: Singleton FDR=0.080 result; no other ubiquitin-proteostasis genes reached FDR<0.10, so this is a marker hypothesis, not a pathway call.
summary: The only Gata3 downstream FDR<0.10 event is Hectd2 induction in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: This localizes the measurable P16 postmitotic Gata3 transcriptional output to a single limbic excitatory gene rather than to a canonical serotonergic, noradrenergic, or GABA fate program.

literature_claim: Gata3 and the upstream Gata2 network regulate embryonic sympathetic, dorsal raphe serotonergic/glutamatergic, and midbrain GABAergic differentiation or survival programs.
main_caveats: Engagement was not measured by indel sequencing; the conclusion is restricted to surviving NeuN+ nuclei from broad postnatal cell groups after mosaic AAV CRISPR.
summary: Gata3 loss-of-function is almost completely buffered transcriptionally across the P16-to-P37/44 neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: Gata3 is a transcription factor with strong embryonic and peripheral requirements; the absence of serotonergic, raphe glutamatergic, midbrain GABAergic, catecholaminergic, and apoptosis marker responses shows that those programs are not re-entered by sparse postmitotic CRISPR in the sampled broad neuronal classes.

literature_claim: Gata2/Gata3 and GATA-associated factors such as Tal-family and Zfpm cofactors act in embryonic serotonergic and GABAergic selector networks.
main_caveats: Gata2, Gata5, Tal1, Tal2, Fev, Skor2, Helt, and Nkx2-2 were not perturbation targets in the parquet, so the comparison is limited to represented relatives.
summary: Directly measurable GATA-family and GATA-associated neural comparators do not phenocopy Gata3.
why_it_matters: The absence of shared FDR genes for Gata1, Gata4, Gata6, Isl1, Lmx1b, Slc32a1, and Zfpm2 argues against a generic GATA-family or neurotransmitter-selector signature in this postmitotic screen and preserves a negative pathway comparison rather than assuming paralog interchangeability.

main_caveats: Correlation was computed on Wilcoxon z-score vectors dominated by non-significant genes; the result is best read as a rejection of strong neighbors, not as proof of fine-scale pathway independence.
summary: The full-universe signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Gata3 neighbor.
why_it_matters: Even the best unrestricted Pearson correlations were near zero and the top positive and negative neighbors shared no FDR<0.10 gene with Gata3, so the singleton Hectd2 response is not part of a broader hidden module recovered elsewhere in the screen.

literature_claim: MED1 encodes a Mediator-complex subunit; no prior source predicts that Gata4 loss should induce Med1 in juvenile CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic neurons.
main_caveats: Only one gene reached the permissive FDR<0.10 cutoff and it did not pass FDR<0.05; Gata4 self-transcript was not measured in this group, and DNA indel efficiency is unavailable.
summary: Gata4 produced a one-gene, CA3/CA2-FC/DG-restricted response: Med1 was up-regulated at FDR 0.098 and no other recovered group had an FDR<0.10 downstream gene.
why_it_matters: The only positive signal points to a very small transcriptional perturbation rather than a broad GATA4 developmental module; because MED1 is a general Mediator-complex subunit, the hit should be treated as a seed observation, not as proof of a Mediator pathway switch.

literature_claim: GATA4 is a GATA zinc-finger transcription factor required for embryonic heart and male-gonad development and genetically linked to cardiac septal defects.
main_caveats: The assay intentionally lacked the embryonic cardiac, endodermal, and gonadal lineages in which these programs normally run.
summary: The recovered neuronal nuclei did not activate or repress the canonical GATA4 cardiac, endodermal, or gonadal loss-of-function programs.
why_it_matters: GATA4 is a potent lineage transcription factor, but the expected targets such as Nppa/Nppb/Myh6/Myh7/Tnnt2/Actc1 and developmental partners or gonadal markers never survived FDR correction after P16 neuronal perturbation. The null therefore refines the perturbation to a neuronal, postmitotic context rather than contradicting embryonic heart, liver, and gonad biology.

literature_claim: Cardiogenic GATA factors have partial redundancy but can be non-interchangeable, whereas MEF2C has postnatal neuronal synapse-regulatory activity.
main_caveats: The Gata4 signature contains only one FDR<0.10 gene, so correlation-based neighbors are dominated by weak ranks and are useful mainly as negative controls for convergence.
summary: Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor GATA4's obvious family/partner perturbations phenocopied Gata4; the only robust contrast was that Mef2c generated 109 neuronal DE genes in matched groups where Gata4 was flat.
why_it_matters: The near-zero Gata4 correlations reject a hidden shared GATA4-like neuronal module and the Mef2c contrast shows that the same Wilcoxon/Flex/postmitotic design could detect a TF-loss transcriptional response when the TF is active in these neurons.

literature_claim: GATA4 is high in migrating embryonic GnRH neurons and, in adult Greywick/conditional mice, hypothalamic Gata4 downregulation in subsets of neurons and glia perturbs fertility and food-intake programs; GATA4 also regulates astrocyte growth.
main_caveats: Cell groups are coarse, non-neuronal nuclei are under-sampled, and the screen read P37-P44 nuclei only 3-4 weeks after a mosaic P16 AAV perturbation.
summary: Broad hypothalamic neuronal groups did not reproduce the reported hypothalamic Gata4 fertility/feeding program.
why_it_matters: The CNU-HYa/HY GABA group and the weak CNU-HYa/HY MM Glut group had no FDR<0.10 genes, and Gnrh1, sex-hormone-receptor, feeding-neuropeptide, and astrocyte-marker queries were FDR=1.0. This argues that the central Gata4 phenotypes reported in Greywick/conditional mice are likely carried by rare GnRH or arcuate/ventromedial hypothalamic cells, astrocytes, prolonged neuroendocrine feedback, or a denser perturbation than this sparse juvenile screen provided.

literature_claim: NSUN2-mediated cytosine-5 RNA methylation protects neuronal tRNAs; NSUN2 deficiency can activate stress pathways and neuronal apoptosis.
main_caveats: One FDR<0.10 gene in one cell group; no UPR, ISR, synaptic, or death module was significant, so the compensatory interpretation is hypothesis-generating.
summary: Acute Gata6 loss-of-function produced a single robust neuronal downstream hit: Nsun2 was up-regulated in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and nowhere else.
why_it_matters: The result nominates a highly restricted RNA-methylation/tRNA-stability marker of the rare Gata6 response while preventing over-interpretation as a broad stress program.

literature_claim: GATA6 loss disrupts primitive or visceral endoderm differentiation and can reduce HNF4A or SEMA3C-centered programs in embryonic endodermal and neural-crest-derived smooth-muscle contexts.
main_caveats: Most canonical genes are weakly represented or sparsely detected in neurons; absence of their DE is informative for this assay context, not a contradiction of embryonic knockout biology.
summary: The neuronal Gata6 perturbation uncoupled completely from canonical GATA6 endodermal and neural-crest smooth-muscle targets.
why_it_matters: Genes such as Hnf4a and Sema3c are strong expectations for GATA6 loss in their native embryonic tissues, yet their absence here shows that an acute P16 neuronal knockout is not a miniature endoderm or cardiac-neural-crest assay.

main_caveats: Cosine was computed across all matched tested genes and groups; it is dominated by a mostly null Gata6 vector.
summary: The data-driven Gata6 signature had no meaningful positive or negative model-wide neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top z-score cosine hit was a safe-target control and the top real-gene hit, Zic4, reached only cosine 0.029; the most negative comparator, Cr2, was only -0.011. Thus the single Nsun2 effect is not embedded in a recurrent perturbational module.

literature_claim: GATA4 and GATA6 cooperate in endoderm-derived organogenesis and HNF4A can sit downstream of GATA6 in visceral endoderm; GATA1/2/3 and GATA4/5/6 form related but developmentally biased GATA subfamilies.
main_caveats: The queryable GATA set was incomplete because Gata2 and Gata5 were not perturbation targets in the parquet; the measured family signatures were themselves very small.
summary: Literature-obvious GATA-family and endodermal neighbors did not phenocopy Gata6 in the mouse neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: Gata1, Gata3, Gata4, and Hnf4a were directly queryable, but all were nearly orthogonal to Gata6 and none reproduced the 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA Nsun2 increase; expected family or pathway similarity is displaced to other lineages rather than recovered in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: GATAD2B is a p66 NuRD component, whereas RASGRP2 is a calcium/DAG-regulated Rap1 guanine-nucleotide-exchange factor not previously defined as a NuRD output.
main_caveats: The Gatad2b FDR support is a single robust thalamic group plus one sub-threshold neighboring group; Rasgrp2 alone does not constitute a full Ras/Rap pathway signature.
summary: Gatad2b loss exposes a Rasgrp2-up thalamic glutamatergic signal rather than a broad NuRD release program.
why_it_matters: Rasgrp2 was the entire FDR<0.10 response in 145 MH-LH TH Glut and reappeared just below threshold in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where the same gene was a robust Chd4 target. This nominates a narrow Ras/Rap GEF branch as the most reproducible positive output of postnatal Gatad2b loss.

literature_claim: ERAD clears ER proteins through ubiquitin-dependent steps that use E2 ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes.
main_caveats: Only one ERAD-related gene reached FDR<0.10; neither Chd4 nor Mbd2 reproduced Ube2g1 in Pvalb cells.
summary: Pvalb interneurons showed an isolated Ube2g1 induction after Gatad2b perturbation.
why_it_matters: UBE2G1 is part of ubiquitin transfer biology that can feed ER-associated protein degradation, so this single FDR hit is a candidate proteostasis readout rather than the expected chromatin-wide de-repression response.

009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: GATAD2B haploinsufficiency and inactivating mouse alleles perturb embryonic cortical patterning and developmental transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: Sparse AAV-CRISPR in juveniles cannot exclude developmental effects before P16 or effects in progenitors and non-neuronal cells.
summary: Across postmitotic juvenile neurons, Gatad2b loss was transcriptionally buffered and failed to recover the embryonic cortical-patterning program expected from GAND models.
why_it_matters: Only two downstream genes survived FDR<0.10 among 371,796 downstream tests despite all 22 measured groups containing the target transcript row and two groups showing significant Gatad2b mRNA decreases. The P16 perturbation therefore tests maintenance in specified neurons, not the embryonic progenitor and corticogenesis roles that dominate the prior literature.

literature_claim: GATAD2B/p66β and CHD4 occupy the NuRD remodeling assembly and are linked through MBD2/MBD3-containing NuRD structure.
main_caveats: The global score correlation was very small because Gatad2b was nearly flat; convergence is therefore driven mainly by the restricted Rasgrp2 axis.
summary: Chd4 was the top data-driven Gatad2b neighbor and shared Rasgrp2 directionality, but Chd4 had a much broader thalamic response.
why_it_matters: The same-complex ATPase ranked first by all-score correlation and made Rasgrp2 a strong 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut DEG, validating a NuRD-proximal component of the weak Gatad2b signal. However, Chd4 produced 158 downstream genes and 149 in 151 alone, while Gatad2b produced only two overall, so p66β loss did not phenocopy catalytic CHD4 loss in this postnatal assay.

literature_claim: MBD2 binds p66/GATAD2 proteins and marks one NuRD subcomplex, but MBD2- and MBD3-containing NuRD assemblies can be distinct.
main_caveats: Mbd3 and Gatad2a were not represented as perturbation targets, so the screen could not test the more developmentally ubiquitous MBD3-p66 paralog axis.
summary: The directly measured Mbd2 perturbation did not phenocopy Gatad2b, separating p66β loss from a simple MBD2/NuRD failure mode.
why_it_matters: Mbd2 was present as a same-complex target in all 23 cell groups, yet produced only one downstream hit in CTX-CGE GABA and none in either Gatad2b responder. This rejects Mbd2 as an explanation for the Pvalb Ube2g1 or MH-LH TH Rasgrp2 outputs.

literature_claim: No literature-obvious Zbtb7a-Gatad2b relationship was used; Zbtb7a was nominated solely by the screen-wide score comparison.
main_caveats: The all-score Pearson correlation was close to zero, so only the measured rejection of broad phenocopy is high-confidence.
summary: Zbtb7a was a nominal data-driven neighbor but was rejected as a Gatad2b phenocopy because its response was broad.
why_it_matters: The second-ranked global neighbor produced 2646 FDR<0.10 genes in 22 cell groups, compared with two genes in two groups for Gatad2b. This preserves the computational neighbor while preventing a weak all-score correlation from being over-read as a shared mechanism.

literature_claim: Gcgr loss in mice has strong systemic metabolic phenotypes, dominated by hepatic glucose control and liver-alpha-cell endocrine feedback.

summary: Gcgr was a pan-measured neuronal non-responder: all 22 recovered cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The major biological result is absence of a cell-autonomous juvenile neuronal transcriptomic program after sparse postmitotic Gcgr loss, not a missed focal responder; it separates the strong endocrine phenotypes of whole-body or liver Gcgr loss from this basal NeuN-positive brain assay.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed on full Wilcoxon-score vectors because Gcgr had no FDR-positive genes; the result is a QC-style negative, not mechanistic convergence.
summary: The high-dimensional Gcgr score vector had no meaningful positive or negative neighbor across the target universe.
why_it_matters: The nearest-neighbor calculation nominated Safe_target_96 and only near-zero correlations, showing that subthreshold nominal ranks should be treated as background rather than a hidden GCGR-like module.

literature_claim: In hepatocytes, glucagon-GCGR signaling raises cAMP and engages PKA, CREB, and CRTC2 to drive gluconeogenic transcription.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was assayed; the experiment did not add glucagon, measure cAMP, or sample liver.
summary: The expected glucagon-to-cAMP/CREB transcriptional axis was absent downstream of neuronal Gcgr perturbation and did not phenocopy pathway-node perturbations.
why_it_matters: Hepatic GCGR activation normally signals through cAMP/PKA/CREB/CRTC2 to induce gluconeogenic transcripts, but Gcgr loss in this brain screen neither changed Pck1/G6pc/Ppargc1a nor common cAMP-response genes such as Crem, Fos, Nr4a1, and Sik1; Creb1 itself produced a small Crem-centered response where Gcgr remained flat.

literature_claim: GCGR, GLP-1R, GIPR, and PTH1R are class-B1 peptide GPCRs, and GCGR/GLP-1R/GIPR pharmacology is dominated by agonist-dependent signaling.

summary: Other represented class-B peptide GPCRs were also flat or nearly flat in the same basal neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: Glp1r, Gipr, Pth1r, and Gcgr are ligand-gated class-B receptors, but their CRISPR loss under this unstimulated P16-to-P37/44 neuronal design produced no broad basal downstream transcriptome, consistent with receptor-family buffering without ligand or metabolic provocation.

main_caveats: One FDR gene only; the next-best gene in the same cell group had FDR 0.765, so no pathway-scale program can be inferred.
summary: Gclc produced a single FDR-significant downstream change, Zfp512b down-regulation, and only in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: The only robust transcript-level responder was focal rather than a glutathione, oxidative-stress, ISR, or ferroptosis module; it should be treated as a hypothesis-generating cell-class-restricted marker of the rare Gclc response.

why_it_matters: Strong Gclc loss is a redox-metabolic lesion, yet this sparse P16 Perturb-seq assay did not convert that lesion into a detectable antioxidant or stress transcriptome.

why_it_matters: The screen separates biochemical adjacency from transcriptomic phenocopy: same-enzyme and GSH/GPX4/NRF-axis perturbations were all essentially orthogonal to Gclc in the matched neuronal DE surface.

main_caveats: Cosine similarity was computed on weak Wilcoxon-score vectors; rankings among near-zero correlations are not mechanistically meaningful.
