literature_claim: Complete neuronal disruption of glutathione production or use can cause mitochondrial, ferroptotic, and inflammatory neurodegeneration.
main_caveats: The dataset did not measure edited alleles, protein, glutathione, lipid peroxidation, or lost nuclei.
summary: The juvenile sparse neuronal null should not be read as evidence that inhibiting GCLC is transcriptionally or biologically inert in brain.
why_it_matters: GCLC is the catalytic entry point to glutathione synthesis, and strong neuronal Gclc or Gpx4 loss can kill neurons; a mosaic snRNA-seq survivor assay can miss metabolite depletion, delayed degeneration, and glial inflammation that would matter for systemic or chronic GCLC inhibition.

literature_claim: GCLM is expected to act through glutamate-cysteine ligase and glutathione/redox homeostasis rather than through Fam91a1 or Epha7 regulation.
main_caveats: Only two FDR<0.10 genes were observed over 22 tested groups; no DNA indel readout verifies per-cell Gclm inactivation.
summary: Gclm loss generated an ultra-sparse, noncanonical neuronal footprint: one Fam91a1 increase in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and one Epha7 increase in 308 CB GABA, with no downregulated FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: This makes the positive biology cell-class-restricted and single-gene rather than an NRF2/glutathione stress response; the two hits should be treated as marker hypotheses, not as a rich pathway state.

literature_claim: FAM91A1 is linked to TBC1D23 and endosome-to-Golgi trafficking, with no established role as an NRF2/glutathione marker.
main_caveats: The recurrent module is a one-gene overlap; the stronger comparator signatures contain many other genes that are absent after Gclm perturbation.
summary: The thalamic Fam91a1-up event is rare but recurrent, appearing in 6 of 1773 tested perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and always in the same direction.
why_it_matters: Fam91a1 is not a canonical glutathione target; recurrence with Tpr, Wac, U2af2, Elp1, and Tcf7l2 argues that the Gclm hit lies in a narrow thalamic state shared with strong RNA-processing/nuclear/lineage perturbations, not in a textbook antioxidant module.

literature_claim: EphA7 is a neural Eph receptor best documented in developmental axon-guidance contexts, not as part of glutathione metabolism.
main_caveats: The Gclm side of the contrast is one gene in 54 perturbed cerebellar GABA cells; Wdr26 has a broad CB GABA signature but only the Epha7 edge overlaps this sparse Gclm surface.
summary: The cerebellar Epha7-up hit is also rare and is directionally opposite to Wdr26 loss in the same 308 CB GABA class.
why_it_matters: Epha7 was significant after only two perturbations in 308 CB GABA across the visible universe, making the Gclm/Wdr26 contrast a candidate cerebellar Eph-receptor marker edge rather than a broad antioxidant readout.

literature_claim: GCLC/GCLM form the rate-limiting GCL enzyme, NRF2 regulates glutathione-system genes, and GPX4 uses glutathione downstream to detoxify lipid peroxides.
main_caveats: Comparator engagement is also inferred from guide assignment, not indel measurement; Gpx4 mRNA itself was not in the tested gene universe.
summary: Gclm did not converge with represented canonical relatives: Gclc, Gpx4, Nfe2l2, and Gls were flat in the two Gclm responder groups and did not reproduce Fam91a1 or Epha7.
why_it_matters: The closest biochemical neighbor, Gclc, is the catalytic partner of Gclm, and Nfe2l2/Gpx4/Gls cover antioxidant regulation, glutathione use, and glutamate supply; their lack of phenocopy makes the two Gclm DEGs more likely to be a weak, noncanonical neuron response than a recovered glutathione program.

literature_claim: Gclm-null models reduce glutathione and are sensitized to oxidative stress, and NRF2 activation should induce Gclc/Gclm, Slc7a11, Nqo1, Hmox1, Gsts, Gsr, Txnrd1, Srxn1, ferritin, and related antioxidant genes.
main_caveats: The assay measures RNA, not glutathione, GSSG, lipid peroxidation, or reactive oxygen species; rare cell stress coupled to cell loss would be invisible in surviving nuclei.
summary: The canonical oxidative-stress, glutathione-recycling, NRF2, ferritin/metallothionein, and ATF4/ISR transcriptome was absent after Gclm perturbation.
why_it_matters: This is the major negative result: the screen could query many expected stress markers and saw none, so mature sparse neuronal Gclm loss does not cross a threshold that elicits a cell-autonomous redox-stress transcriptional program over the 3-4 week assay.

why_it_matters: GDI1 is a Rab-cycle disease gene, but in P16-P37/44 postmitotic neurons its loss does not launch a sustained synaptic, lysosomal, UPR/ISR, redox, autophagy, proteasome, or immediate-early RNA program detectable by this snRNA-seq design.

literature_claim: Rab7 is a late-endocytic/lysosomal Rab, and RabGDIs regulate GDP-bound Rab proteins, including delivery and retrieval steps in Rab membrane cycling.

literature_claim: GFI1 cooperates with ATOH1 and POU-family hair-cell factors during inner-ear hair-cell differentiation, while Gfi1b is a functional paralog in blood but not in inner ear.

why_it_matters: Atoh1, Pou4f3 and the paralog Gfi1b were directly measurable as perturbation targets; Atoh1 and Pou4f3 were completely flat and Gfi1b produced only one singleton FDR<0.10 gene, matching the conclusion that the sampled brain neurons are outside the cochlear hair-cell regulatory circuit.

literature_claim: Enhancer hijacking can activate GFI1 or GFI1B in medulloblastoma, where Gfi1 cooperates with Myc and depends on Lsd1 in neonatal cerebellar progenitor-derived tumor models.

main_caveats: Correlations of a null profile are expected to be noise-dominated and should not be over-interpreted gene by gene.
summary: A genome-wide neighbor search found no substantive Gfi1-like or anti-Gfi1 signature.

literature_claim: GFI1B is a hematopoietic SNAG zinc-finger repressor whose LoF causes large erythroid and megakaryocytic phenotypes in the appropriate lineages.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured, and the missing 215 MB Dopa group was not tested for Gfi1b.
summary: Gfi1b loss was almost pan-neuronally buffered: across 371818 tested group-gene rows in 22 recovered cell groups, only one downstream row reached FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: A SNAG-domain transcriptional repressor should create an mRNA phenotype in the cell type that uses it. The absence of a broad response in postmitotic NeuN-enriched brain nuclei argues that the sampled neurons do not deploy canonical GFI1B repression after P16 perturbation.

literature_claim: Ankrd13-family UIM proteins bind ubiquitinated activated EGFR and regulate receptor endocytosis from the plasma membrane.
main_caveats: Only one FDR<0.10 gene was present; the evidence does not support a broader ubiquitin, lysosome, or EGFR program under Gfi1b loss.

why_it_matters: The hit nominates ubiquitin/endocytic trafficking as the sole measurable transcriptional output of Gfi1b LoF in this screen, but because it is a single gene it should be treated as a cell-restricted biomarker rather than a complete pathway.

main_caveats: Correlations are dominated by a largely flat Gfi1b vector; sparse negative neighbors such as Diaph2 have only two overlapping cell groups.

why_it_matters: The top genome-wide score correlations were close to zero, so the Gfi1b surface is not a weak version of a known recurrent perturbation module.

literature_claim: GFI1 is the closest GFI1B paralog and ATOH1/POU4F3 are inner-ear comparators, while GATA1/KLF1/SPI1/MEIS1 sit in hematopoietic TF space.

summary: The represented GFI-family and sensory/hematopoietic TF comparators did not reveal a latent Gfi1b-like neuronal program.
why_it_matters: Gfi1, Atoh1, Pou4f3, Gata1, Klf1, Meis1, and Spi1 each had 0 FDR<0.10 genes, so the closest paralog and the most obvious lineage-neighbor perturbations were rejected as positive phenocopies in this normal neuronal screen.

literature_claim: ZBTB7A/LRF is embedded in erythroid transcriptional control downstream of GATA1, a broader network that also contains lineage determinants such as KLF1.
main_caveats: Zbtb7a is an indirect erythroid-network comparator, not a GFI1B paralog or obligate complex member.
summary: Zbtb7a strongly diverged from Gfi1b despite both being connected to erythroid transcription-factor biology.
why_it_matters: Zbtb7a produced 2639 FDR<0.10 genes across the same 22 cell groups in which Gfi1b produced one, showing that the neuronal assay can expose large signatures from pleiotropic lineage TFs and that the Gfi1b null is not simply a property of all blood-development regulators.

literature_claim: Somatic structural variants can juxtapose GFI1 or GFI1B to active enhancers and activate them as group 3/4 medulloblastoma oncogenes.

why_it_matters: GFI1/GFI1B are implicated in medulloblastoma through enhancer-hijacking gain of expression; knocking out essentially silent Gfi1b in normal P16 cerebellar GABA and other neurons is a different allele, stage, and cell state. This prevents over-reading the 308 CB GABA null as evidence against a tumor-progenitor oncogene role.

literature_claim: GFM2 and NDUFS4 are mitochondrial-disease genes in the OXPHOS axis, and OPA1 is a mitochondrial inner-membrane dynamics gene with energetic consequences.
main_caveats: Most exact GFM2 recycling partners and the GFM1 paralog were absent as perturbation targets, so this is a disease-axis comparison rather than a same-complex epistasis test.
summary: Within represented mitochondrial disease genes, Gfm2 resembled weak core OXPHOS/mitochondrial-translation perturbations more than the strong Opa1 stressor.
why_it_matters: Ndufs4, Fars2, Slc25a46, and Lars2 were flat or near-flat despite their links to mitochondrial respiration or translation, whereas Opa1 produced hundreds of DE genes; this separates the assay's detectable mitochondrial architecture-stress axis from its buffered single-component OXPHOS/translation axis.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: EF-G2mt loss is context-sensitive and can be unmasked by forced oxidative metabolism or statin exposure.
main_caveats: No statin, carbon-source switch, respiration assay, or biochemical OXPHOS protein measurement was present in the Perturb-seq experiment.
summary: The basal neuronal null should not be interpreted as evidence that GFM2 is dispensable under respiratory or toxic stress.
why_it_matters: External EF-G2mt work found little viability loss in glucose despite deep mRNA depletion but clear defects in galactose and atorvastatin contexts; the mouse-brain screen lacked an imposed metabolic challenge, so it reports an unstressed basal state only.

main_caveats: The whole-profile correlation is dominated by a null Gfm2 vector; it is useful for rejection of convergence, not for nominating mechanism.
summary: Unbiased whole-surface neighbors of Gfm2 were numerically near-zero and were rejected as meaningful phenocopies.
why_it_matters: The closest positive and negative Pearson correlations ranged only from 0.0329 to -0.0190, and the neighboring targets were null or tiny-effect perturbations; Gfm2 therefore has no reproducible transcriptomic module to align in this dataset.

literature_claim: GFPT1 supplies UDP-GlcNAc for ER/Golgi glycosylation, and Gfpt1-deficient muscle elevates UPR markers when glycosylation stress creates misfolded proteins.
main_caveats: The assay read nuclei, not UDP-HexNAc, N-glycans, O-GlcNAc, or protein aggregates directly.
summary: Gfpt1 loss produced a thresholded ER chaperone/ERAD response in 7 neuronal groups, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The data nominate protein-folding stress as the dominant post-P16 neuronal consequence of Gfpt1 loss and show that it is not uniform across all GFPT1-measured neurons.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: O-GlcNAc homeostasis is maintained by feedback on OGT and OGA abundance in response to O-GlcNAc levels.
main_caveats: Ogt RNA down-regulation is not an OGT protein or O-GlcNAc measurement; low-HBP feedback has been characterized mainly in cultured non-neuronal cells.
summary: The O-GlcNAc-cycle transcript Ogt was repeatedly repressed by Gfpt1 perturbation, with Oga also repressed in the strongest thalamic group.
why_it_matters: A rate-limiting HBP perturbation fed back onto the O-GlcNAc writer/eraser axis at the RNA level, but in the opposite Ogt direction from the simplest low-O-GlcNAc compensation model.

literature_claim: The PERK branch of ER stress engages ATF4/DDIT3 and amino-acid/redox adaptation programs.
main_caveats: Some redox/one-carbon genes are multifunctional, so the redox interpretation is made at the module level rather than from any single transcript.
summary: Gfpt1-responsive neurons co-induced an ISR/amino-acid module and a redox/one-carbon module rather than a pure chaperone-only UPR.
why_it_matters: The signature couples ER proteostasis to Atf4/Ddit3 stress metabolism, amino-acid transport and charging, glutathione-linked Chac1, and mitochondrial one-carbon transcripts.

literature_claim: HBP/O-GlcNAc and UPR signaling can alter transcription, translation, cytoskeletal function, and cell survival programs.
main_caveats: The direction is transcriptional; no electrophysiology or synapse morphology was measured.
summary: The broad responders down-shifted neuronal excitability, vesicle, and cytoskeletal transcripts while stress transcripts rose.
why_it_matters: This links HBP depletion to a possible adaptive reduction in neuronal operating state after postmitotic ER stress, especially in the 110/151/155 signatures.

literature_claim: DHDDS supports dolichol-dependent protein glycosylation, ATP2A2/SERCA2 preserves ER calcium for folding, and HSPA5/BiP is a core ER chaperone.
main_caveats: Cosine was computed on the Gfpt1 FDR<0.10 restricted signature; Psmb4 and Elp1 are data-driven stress neighbors rather than enzymes in the HBP.
summary: The top data-driven neighbors of Gfpt1 were ER/glycosylation and proteostasis perturbations, led by Dhdds and Atp2a2.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation convergence argues that Gfpt1 loss is read out as ER proteostasis stress in this screen, not merely as an isolated O-GlcNAc signaling defect.

literature_claim: Ogt is downstream of HBP-derived UDP-GlcNAc, Hk1 and Gpi1 feed the fructose-6-phosphate substrate pool, and ATF6/GCN2 are related stress-response nodes.
main_caveats: GFPT2 and most internal HBP enzymes were not represented as perturbation targets, so some closer enzymatic comparisons were not possible.
summary: The represented obvious neighbors Ogt, Hk1, Gpi1, Atf6, and Eif2ak4 did not phenocopy Gfpt1.
why_it_matters: The Gfpt1 signature is not reproduced by direct OGT loss, upstream glycolysis, or single ATF6/GCN2 stress-sensor knockouts, constraining the transcriptional response to the HBP-to-ER-glycosylation axis.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Loss of GFPT1 is expected to perturb glycosylation and, when proteostasis is overwhelmed, induce ER stress.
main_caveats: Only four total downstream genes were present across the two groups; no pathway should be inferred from Dclk1 alone.
summary: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut were real but minimal non-UPR responders.
why_it_matters: These sparse responders show that crossing the FDR threshold after Gfpt1 loss does not automatically mean the full Hspa5/Ddit3 program engaged.

literature_claim: Muscle Gfpt1 deficiency can activate UPR, attenuate autophagy, accumulate protein aggregates, and provoke apoptosis.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot detect protein aggregates or autophagic flux; nuclei lost before harvest would not be profiled.
summary: The neuronal UPR/ISR signature did not extend to a robust autophagy or apoptosis transcriptome in surviving nuclei.
why_it_matters: Postmitotic neurons can show the Hspa5/Ddit3 arm of Gfpt1 loss without the full muscle-like maladaptive aggregate-clearance/apoptosis program being apparent by snRNA-seq at 3-4 weeks.

literature_claim: GFRα1 is not a nuclear transcriptional regulator; it is a GPI-anchored GDNF-family co-receptor with strongest null-mutant phenotypes in developmental GDNF/RET contexts.
main_caveats: Functional indels were not measured and Gfra1 mRNA was not significantly reduced, but weak or flat self-transcript is expected in this platform and does not prove failed editing.
summary: Gfra1 was transcriptionally buffered across the 22 measured brain-neuron cell groups, with zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every tested group and only FDR=1.0 changes in the Gfra1 transcript itself.
why_it_matters: This makes Gfra1 a whole-surface null in the P16-to-P37/44 sparse CRISPR experiment, rather than a cell-type-restricted responder hidden by one large group.

literature_claim: GDNF/GFRα1 can drive NCAM/Fyn and RET-dependent survival pathways, synapse formation or maintenance, CREB-linked dendritic maturation, and dopaminergic trophic/phenotype programs in specialized systems.
main_caveats: Only mRNAs were measured; phosphorylation of ERK, AKT, FAK, CREB or AMPAR subunit trafficking could occur without a detectable nuclear RNA program.
summary: The screen did not recover MAPK/immediate-early, trophic-stress, UPR/ISR, AMPA-synaptic or dopaminergic-identity marker induction after Gfra1 loss.
why_it_matters: The null is not merely a lack of named pathway enrichment: genes that would reveal strong GDNF/RET signaling loss, compensatory stress, synaptic remodeling or DA-state erosion were individually observable but never reached FDR<0.10.

main_caveats: Pearson correlations were calculated on full Wilcoxon-score surfaces; no inference is made from raw logFC correlation because logFC values contain shared low-expression artifacts.
summary: Gfra1 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbor in the 1773-target model-visible universe; the best positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations were only +0.030 and -0.019.
why_it_matters: The top neighbors were not GDNF/RET relatives and were either empty Safe-target surfaces or unrelated perturbations with their own signatures, so the apparent rankings are consistent with numerical noise around a flat vector.

literature_claim: GFRα1 can signal with RET or with NCAM/Fyn, while adult Ret deletion alone can be dispensable for bulk midbrain dopamine-neuron maintenance.
main_caveats: Gdnf and the Gfra2/3/4 paralog receptors were not represented as perturbation targets, so redundancy among GDNF-family ligands or co-receptors could not be measured directly.
summary: Directly represented GDNF/NCAM pathway comparators, Ret, Ncam1, Fyn and L1cam, also lacked downstream FDR<0.10 signatures and were uncorrelated with Gfra1.
why_it_matters: Even Ncam1, which showed significant self-transcript reduction in 10 cell groups, had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes; the absent Gfra1 program therefore extends to the measurable NCAM arm rather than being explainable only by a flat Gfra1 self-transcript.

literature_claim: GDNF is a trophic factor for the nigrostriatal dopaminergic pathway and can modulate dopamine-neuron survival, dopamine release and DA-phenotype regulators, but Ret alone is not universally required for adult dopamine-neuron maintenance.
main_caveats: The cell group was absent for Gfra1 rather than flat, so no direct dopaminergic Gfra1 loss-of-function conclusion is possible.
summary: The Parkinson’s-relevant nigrostriatal GDNF axis was effectively off-axis: 215 MB Dopa had no Gfra1 rows, and DA-identity transcripts were not changed in the other measured groups.
why_it_matters: A flat Gfra1 result in this screen should not be read as evidence against GDNF/GFRα1 biology in substantia-nigra dopaminergic neurons or striatal trophic support, which are rare projection-specific and disease-age contexts outside the recovered Gfra1 surface.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: GH-responsive neurons have been mapped in many mouse brain regions, with the densest populations in hypothalamic nuclei, and CNS GH actions are implicated in metabolic and neuroendocrine homeostasis.
main_caveats: The null is transcriptomic and basal; DNA indel engagement was not measured, and broad cell groups can dilute rare GH-responsive subpopulations.
summary: Ghr loss of function produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome in any of the 19 measured neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: This is a pan-surface negative result for basal, P16-to-P37/44, sparse neuronal Ghr perturbation rather than a selective cortical, hippocampal, hypothalamic, midbrain, or cerebellar response.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Activated GHR uses JAK2 to recruit STAT5A/B and can activate STAT1/STAT3, while SOCS and CIS genes participate in inducible negative feedback on GH/JAK-STAT signaling.
main_caveats: The tested nuclei were not acutely challenged with GH, so absence of these mRNAs does not rule out a rapid pSTAT5 response in ligand-stimulated Ghr+ cells.
summary: The expected GH/JAK-STAT feedback readout was absent after Ghr perturbation.
why_it_matters: If this screen had captured tonic GHR-JAK-STAT activity in the perturbed neurons, SOCS/CIS and related immediate readouts should have been among the most detectable mRNAs; their universal FDR=1 behavior localizes the missing biology to stimulus/subpopulation context rather than to a missed secondary stress program.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: GHR, PRLR, EPOR, and the leptin receptor are class-I-cytokine/JAK-STAT receptors, and GHR also connects to STAT, ERK/MAPK and PI3K/IRS signaling.
main_caveats: Jak2, Stat5a, Socs2, Socs3, and Cish were absent as perturbation targets, so the comparison omits several most-proximal GHR nodes.
summary: Represented GHR-pathway and class-I-cytokine comparators did not phenocopy Ghr.
why_it_matters: The expected relatives—PRLR, LEPR, EPOR, STAT/IGF/insulin/MAPK/mTOR nodes—were directly queried and all had near-zero score-vector cosines to Ghr, showing that the Ghr null is not a hidden cytokine- or growth-factor-like signature in this assay.

main_caveats: The search used continuous Wilcoxon score profiles because Ghr had no FDR-significant genes to support an overlap metric.
summary: A pre-literature whole-universe neighbor search found only noise-level Ghr neighbors.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative neighbors were not textbook GH-axis genes and none reached an absolute cosine of 0.034; therefore downstream interpretation should center the null surface, not a spurious nominal module.

literature_claim: GHSR is a functional ghrelin GPCR whose deletion changes ligand-evoked feeding/arcuate activation and metabolic phenotypes in challenged animals.
main_caveats: Editing was not assayed by indel sequencing; the two FDR genes are singletons near the 0.10 threshold.
summary: Basal postnatal Ghsr loss of function produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 22 measured neuronal groups, despite a Ghsr row being tested in every measured group.
why_it_matters: The dominant result is strong buffering of a neuroendocrine GPCR at the baseline whole-transcriptome level, not a failed experiment inferred from self-mRNA.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: SLC17A5 encodes a lysosomal transporter that exports free sialic acids from lysosomes; no established GHSR-to-Slc17a5 transcriptional link was found.
main_caveats: One gene in 62 perturbed cells with FDR just below 0.10; no companion lysosomal genes reached FDR<0.10.
summary: Ghsr perturbation up-regulated Slc17a5 in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut as a single lysosomal sialic-acid transporter hit.
why_it_matters: This is the strongest positive DE call but it nominates only a low-confidence cortical lysosomal/acidic-sugar transporter biomarker, not a broad lysosomal response.

literature_claim: Cplane1 is a ciliogenesis and planar-polarity effector gene localized to the ciliary transition zone; no prior GHSR-to-Cplane1 transcriptional axis was expected.
main_caveats: The call is a single FDR<0.10 transcript and Cplane1 loss itself had no downstream DE genes in the matched groups.
summary: Ghsr perturbation down-regulated Cplane1 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut as a single cilia/CPLANE-associated hit.
why_it_matters: The result points to a possible weak cortical IT ciliary transcript response while explicitly avoiding a claim of a coordinated ciliogenesis program.

literature_claim: GHSR acts in discrete hypothalamic and hippocampal circuits through ligand-evoked GPCR, Fos, and NMDAR-linked physiology rather than requiring a broad basal transcriptional output.
main_caveats: The hindbrain and MB Dopa axis were incompletely assayed, and no fasting or ghrelin challenge was applied.
summary: Ghsr loss did not recover orexigenic neuropeptide or immediate-early transcriptional programs in hypothalamic or hippocampal candidate groups.
why_it_matters: It separates GHSR physiology from a basal postmitotic snRNA phenotype and shows that the absence is not simply a failure to notice Agrp/Npy/Pomc/Fos-class markers.

literature_claim: GHSR is a GPCR and can be functionally coupled to DRD2 heteromers, suggesting DRD2 and other feeding/neuromodulatory GPCR perturbations as natural comparators.
main_caveats: The Ghsr signature is only two genes, so the global correlations are useful mainly as a rejection of strong convergence.
summary: Neither data-driven signature neighbors nor represented ghrelin/neuromodulatory comparators converged strongly with Ghsr.
why_it_matters: Cross-target measurement rejects both a hidden strong global neighbor and a DRD2/feeding-GPCR phenocopy for this weak Ghsr surface.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: Cplane1 participates in ciliogenesis; the dataset tests whether its own loss creates a matching transcriptome.
main_caveats: Ciliary pathway state is inferred only from one Ghsr-regulated transcript.
summary: The downstream Cplane1 singleton is not reciprocated by Cplane1 knockout.
why_it_matters: A directly tested Cplane1 perturbation had no downstream genes at FDR<0.10 across the same 22 groups, arguing that Ghsr perturbation did not trigger a reproducible ciliary loss-of-function state.

literature_claim: GIGYF1/2 complexes repress translation and can promote co-translational mRNA decay, while GIGYF1 also has a translation-initiation repression mechanism independent of 4EHP.
main_caveats: The assay measures nuclear RNA after mosaic P16 CRISPR, not ribosome footprints or protein synthesis; DNA indel burden is unknown, and the two isolated FDR genes should not be treated as a broad program.
summary: Gigyf1 loss of function was a globally buffered acute neuronal perturbation: all 23 cell groups were recovered, but only two downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across the entire surface.
why_it_matters: A genome-wide snRNA Wilcoxon assay that detected large signatures for other targets found almost no steady-state mRNA consequence of postnatal Gigyf1 editing, so the dominant result is not a missed cell class but a near-pan-neuronal mRNA null.

literature_claim: No GIGYF1-specific literature found predicts isolated Pdhb or Nap1l3 induction in these neuronal classes.
main_caveats: Each effect group contains exactly one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, so the result is a biomarker hypothesis rather than a coherent pathway call.
summary: The only downstream Gigyf1 FDR hits were Pdhb up in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and Nap1l3 up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: These two upward single-gene effects are the only cell-type-restricted positive signals, nominating a metabolic pyruvate-dehydrogenase transcript in limbic glutamatergic neurons and an NAP1-like chromatin transcript in striatal MGE-lineage GABA neurons without a recurrent GIGYF module.

literature_claim: GIGYF1 and GIGYF2 can both bind 4EHP and participate in GIGYF1/2-4EHP mRNA repression/decay, although newer work also describes a GIGYF1-specific eIF3-eIF4G1 initiation-repression mechanism.
main_caveats: Gigyf2 itself was a sparse responder and Eif4e2, Znf598, Grb10, and Ddx6 were not targetable comparators in the parquet.
summary: Gigyf2, the closest GIGYF paralog, did not phenocopy Gigyf1; it produced 42 downstream DE genes in five groups where Gigyf1 had zero.
why_it_matters: The direct paralog contrast separates GIGYF-family capacity from GIGYF1-specific biology: thalamic, midbrain-glutamatergic, hypothalamic GABA, and Pvalb neurons were able to mount a Gigyf2 transcriptomic response even though Gigyf1 was flat.

literature_claim: GIGYF proteins were discovered as GRB10 interactors linked to IGF receptor signaling; GIGYF1 disruption can impair IGF1R recycling, and RACK1 is a proximal ribosome-associated quality-control factor.
main_caveats: GRB10, ZNF598, DDX6, and EIF4E2 were not directly perturbed; IGF1R recycling and ribosome ubiquitylation are protein-level phenotypes.
summary: The tested IGF/insulin receptor and RACK1 RQC nodes did not recreate a Gigyf1-like positive module.
why_it_matters: Insr and Igf1r knockouts were transcriptionally silent in their measured neuronal groups, Rack1 produced only two thalamic genes, and none of these comparators changed the two Gigyf1 marker genes, arguing that the GRB10-IGF1R and ribosome-collision branches are not strong baseline nuclear-RNA programs in this juvenile neuronal assay.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: GIGYF1 disruption has been associated with ASD and impaired IGF1R/ERK signaling, and germline or developmental animal GIGYF1 ablation causes neurodevelopmental and behavioral phenotypes.
main_caveats: The screen perturbed sparse P16 postmitotic neurons and cannot test embryonic progenitor proliferation, neuronal production, or organism-level behavior.
summary: Postnatal Gigyf1 editing did not collapse cortical projection-neuron transcriptomes despite literature linking GIGYF1 loss to autism and cortical neurogenesis.
why_it_matters: The upper-layer and corticofugal zeros move the ASD interpretation away from an acute, three-week, cell-autonomous mRNA toxicity model in already specified neurons and toward developmental progenitor timing, circuit-level outputs, receptor trafficking, or translation-level effects.

main_caveats: The two largest signatures also had the largest Gigyf2 perturbed-cell counts, so biological specificity and power covary; 215 MB Dopa had no Gigyf2 rows.
summary: Acute Gigyf2 loss produced a sparse, anatomically biased transcriptome: 42 downstream FDR<0.10 calls in 5 of 22 measured neuronal groups, dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The response is not a pan-neuronal consequence of losing a general translation-repressor scaffold; it is a postnatal vulnerability that is concentrated in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic classes plus three very small GABA/hypothalamic signatures.

literature_claim: GIGYF2-4EHP represses initiation on defective or paused mRNAs and GIGYF1/2-4EHP complexes couple ribosome pausing to mRNA decay, so RQC stress is a plausible secondary outcome of loss.
main_caveats: The snRNA-seq data measure total nuclear Xbp1, not the spliced Xbp1 isoform, and the FDR<0.10 ER module is only two named genes.
summary: Gigyf2 triggered a narrow ER quality-control response rather than a global proteotoxic-stress program.
why_it_matters: Xbp1 and Selenok induction in 151, 155 and 110 is the transcriptomic echo most consistent with GIGYF2's role at stalled or defective translations, but the absence of Atf4/Ddit3/Hspa5, autophagy genes, and proteasome-subunit induction shows that the cells were buffered rather than in a broad ISR or heat-shock state.

literature_claim: GIGYF1/2 and EIF4E2 act in cytoplasmic co-translational mRNA decay and in translational repression of a subset of NMD targets, rather than being described as spliceosome factors.
main_caveats: Several overlaps with Tpr, U2af2 and Prpf6 are mixed in direction; the finding is a signature-level convergence, not a direct physical interaction.
summary: The thalamic and MB Glut signatures contain a recurrent RNA-processing module that converges with spliceosome and nuclear-pore perturbations.
why_it_matters: Up-regulation of Rsrp1, Luc7l2, Snrnp70 and Sf3b4, together with Hnrnpu down-regulation in 151, extends an mRNA-fate perturbation into a nuclear RNA-processing state not predicted by textbook 4EHP cap competition alone.

literature_claim: Mouse Gigyf2 disruption produces age-related motor impairment and neurodegeneration in spinal and brainstem/cerebellar regions.
main_caveats: The assayed cells were juvenile-to-young-adult and sparse; the experiment was not a survival or aged neurodegeneration assay.
summary: The broadest Gigyf2-positive groups coupled stress/RNA genes to down-regulation of neuronal signaling and structural transcripts.
why_it_matters: Prkcg, Shc3, Fat3, Gpcpd1, Syne1, Sptan1 and Ubr4 fell in 151, and Nptn, Adcy8, Gabrb2 and App fell in 155, linking a post-transcriptional quality-control gene to a young, neuron-intrinsic synaptic/architecture readout before overt aged degeneration is modeled.

main_caveats: One gene defines the effect; it should be treated as a marker for follow-up rather than a pathway claim.
summary: Fndc1 was a Pvalb-selective Gigyf2 biomarker candidate.
why_it_matters: A single extracellular-matrix/adhesion-associated transcript was the whole conventional Pvalb response, separating fast-spiking interneurons from other cortical interneuron groups that were strict nulls.

main_caveats: The result is a boundary condition on interpretation, not a mechanistic module; no additional nominal genes were used.
summary: The CNU-HYa/HY effects were real but too small and heterogeneous to define a GIGYF2 core pathway.
why_it_matters: Zcchc18/Pcgf2/Slc19a2 in 066 and BC005537/Zcchc2/Selenok in 110 show that the FDR<0.10 surface extends outside MB/TH Glut, but their three-gene sizes argue against mining them into nominal pathway stories.

literature_claim: GIGYF2 suppresses new initiation on collided/defective mRNAs and UFMylation is required for ER-localized ribosome-associated quality control.
main_caveats: Psmb4 and Psmc1 caused much broader signatures than Gigyf2; the overlap is a shared stress state, not a claim that Gigyf2 is a proteasome subunit.
summary: Proteasome and UFMylation perturbations were the strongest FDR-level neighbors of Gigyf2.
why_it_matters: Psmb4, Psmc1 and Uba5 are not 4EHP-complex members, yet they recurrently perturbed the same cell-gene dimensions as Gigyf2, placing the Gigyf2 state closer to protein-quality-control stress than to the expected 4EHP or CCR4-NOT single-gene controls.

literature_claim: GIGYF1/2 act with 4EHP/EIF4E2, CCR4-NOT, and collided-ribosome pathways, making Gigyf1, Cnot1, Hbs1l, Eif4e2, Zfp598 and Grb10 obvious comparators.
main_caveats: Eif4e2, Zfp598 and Grb10 were not represented as targets; Cnot1 had only 25-57 perturbed cells in the five matched groups.
summary: Literature-obvious single perturbations did not phenocopy Gigyf2.
why_it_matters: Gigyf1, Cnot1 and Hbs1l were measured where Gigyf2 responded but had no exact FDR-level overlap with the 42 Gigyf2 dimensions; acute Gigyf2 loss in neurons is therefore not reproduced by losing the paralog, a CCR4-NOT scaffold, or a ribosome-rescue factor one at a time.

literature_claim: GIPR is an incretin class-B GPCR whose physiologic effects are ligand gated and concentrated in endocrine cells plus specialized hypothalamic and brainstem GIPR neurons.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure DNA indels, ligand-evoked cAMP, food intake, or rare Gipr+ subtype physiology; flat Gipr mRNA is therefore not evidence of failed editing.
summary: Gipr loss was almost fully buffered at the basal juvenile neuronal transcriptome: only one downstream row reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured groups.
why_it_matters: A gut-hormone receptor with strong endocrine and CNS pharmacology did not behave like a broad cell-autonomous postmitotic transcriptional dependency in this NeuN+ screen.

literature_claim: aPKCλ/PRKCI participates in neuronal polarity complexes; post-differentiation neuronal aPKCλ deletion can disturb polarity-complex proteins without causing overt neuronal loss.
main_caveats: Only Prkci survived FDR control; no Par-complex or morphologic endpoints were measured, and 70 Gipr-targeted nuclei supported the L5 ET test.
summary: The sole robust Gipr downstream event was a L5 ET cortical decrease of Prkci, not a recurrent incretin immediate-early response.
why_it_matters: Prkci/aPKC belongs to the neuronal polarity machinery, so this isolated row nominates a receptor-to-polarity-axis biomarker in L5 extratelencephalic neurons, but only as a single-gene, moderate-confidence hypothesis.

literature_claim: GIPR and related incretin receptors couple peptide stimulation to cAMP/PKA and transcriptional CREB outputs in stimulated endocrine contexts.
main_caveats: Several literature-obvious class-B receptors were not represented as targets, and the represented comparators were themselves mostly weak in L5 ET neurons.
summary: Gipr's L5 ET Prkci decrease was uncoupled from generic class-B GPCR/cAMP perturbation and from a CREB/immediate-early program.
why_it_matters: If the Prkci row reflects real biology, it is not a simple readout of lowering GLP1R/GCGR-like Gs-cAMP tone or CREB-dependent activation in the captured basal state.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation was necessarily restricted to the 200 strongest mostly subthreshold Gipr features because Gipr had only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene.
summary: An unbiased restricted-signature search found no high-confidence positive or negative Gipr neighbor in the target universe.
why_it_matters: The isolated Prkci response should not be folded into a broader inferred module; top nearest and opposite signatures were low-cosine and shared no FDR<0.10 Gipr features.

literature_claim: Dual GIPR/GLP1R agonism can reduce body weight clinically and long-acting GIPR agonism in mice requires specialized central GABAergic circuitry.
main_caveats: The screen does not test agonism, appetite circuits, pancreatic or adipose targets, or area-postrema responses directly.
summary: The P16 CRISPR loss-of-function surface should not be used as a transcriptomic proxy for agonist GIPR/GLP1R co-pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Tirzepatide-like pharmacology is agonist, chronic, peripheral-plus-central, and depends on rare GABAergic GIPR circuits; this screen measured unstimulated sparse neuronal loss and also rejected Glp1r phenocopy of Gipr in the L5 ET Prkci assay.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: GLCE edits heparan sulfate and germline or embryonic perturbation of the pathway can have major developmental consequences.
main_caveats: DNA indels and HS glycan structure were not assayed; the result is transcriptome-only and post-P16.
summary: Acute Glce loss of function produced a zero-FDR cell-autonomous transcriptomic surface across all 22 recovered neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: This is a strong boundary on GLCE biology in juvenile postmitotic neurons: the perturbation did not trigger a detectable nuclear stress, synaptic or morphogen-response program despite broad sampling of excitatory and inhibitory classes.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Glce acts in the same HS-chain modification system as EXT polymerization and HS sulfation enzymes, and Hsepi phenotypes can be masked by compensatory 6-O- and N-sulfation in Drosophila.
main_caveats: Hs2st1, Ndst genes, Sulf genes and Hs6st1/3 were not represented as perturbation targets; Ext2's two genes are isolated and not a coherent Ext2 program.
summary: Represented HS biosynthetic comparators Ext1, Hs6st2 and Ext2 were also weakly responsive or flat, so the pathway-level response is buffered rather than Glce-specific.
why_it_matters: The expected HS relatives did not expose a hidden Glce-like neuronal module: Ext1 and Hs6st2 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and Ext2 had only two singleton downstream rows across 23 groups.

main_caveats: All-gene cosine is useful for bounded neighbor discovery but is uninformative for Glce because the Glce vector contains no FDR-supported component.
summary: The closest data-driven Glce signature neighbors were near-zero residual correlations, not convergent biological modules.
why_it_matters: The strongest whole-surface cosine to Glce was only 0.0246; genuine responders such as Manf and Camta1 carried UPR or neuronal-downregulation signatures that Glce did not share, while the most negative neighbors were likewise mostly null.

literature_claim: HS and Glce regulate ligand availability for BMP, FGF, Wnt/Hedgehog and guidance systems, most prominently in embryonic patterning and extracellular navigation contexts.
main_caveats: The marker test covers transcriptional reporters only; it cannot score ligand gradients, HS sulfation, axon trajectories or synaptic physiology.
summary: HS-linked FGF/Hedgehog/Wnt-axon-guidance transcriptional markers were not mobilized by postnatal Glce perturbation.
why_it_matters: The assay should have detected a robust secondary transcriptional response if active neuronal FGF/Hedgehog/Wnt signaling were being transcriptionally rewired; every queried marker remained FDR 1.0 across the 22 Glce groups.

literature_claim: GLI1 is a Hedgehog-induced transcriptional activator/amplifier, but Gli1-null mice are viable and GLI2 carries much of the initial Shh-response burden.
main_caveats: DNA editing was not measured; the conclusion is limited to a 3-4 week mosaic CRISPR challenge started at P16.
summary: Gli1 loss of function was essentially transcriptionally silent in P16-perturbed postmitotic neurons: all 23 measured cell groups retained Gli1 self-FDR=1.0, and 21 groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The major result is not a failed canonical Hedgehog signature hidden by noisy self-knockdown; it is a context-specific absence of detectable GLI1 transcriptional output in NeuN-enriched juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: MCTP1 has been linked to CNS neuronal vesicle retrieval, and amphiphysin binds dynamin at nerve terminals during synaptic-vesicle endocytosis.
main_caveats: One FDR<0.10 gene in each responder; no recurrence of Mctp1 or Amph across other Gli1 cell groups.
summary: The only two downstream Gli1 FDR hits were negative and cell-restricted: Mctp1 decreased in Pvalb GABA neurons and Amph decreased in CNU-HYa HY MM glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: The two hits point at membrane/synaptic-vesicle-associated transcripts rather than Hedgehog target genes, but each occurs alone in its cell group and should be treated as a biomarker hypothesis, not as a broad synaptic program.

literature_claim: PTCH, SMO, ciliary trafficking regulators and GLI factors operate in the same vertebrate Hedgehog signal-transduction pathway.
main_caveats: Gli3, Sufu, Shh and Kif3a were not represented as tested targets in the parquet.
summary: Canonical Hedgehog/ciliary comparators failed to phenocopy the Gli1 singletons: Gli2, Gpr161, Ptch1, Ptch2 and Kif3b had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes, and Smo or Ift88 each produced only one midbrain-glutamatergic singleton.
why_it_matters: The lack of matched responses separates the P16 neuronal Gli1 phenotype from a canonical PTCH-SMO-cilium-GLI cascade and makes the two Gli1 hits unlikely to be a recovered Hedgehog pathway module.

main_caveats: The Gli1 profile has only two FDR features, so both cosine rankings and two-feature rankings are inherently fragile.
summary: Across-screen signature matching did not reveal a stable Gli1 neighbor: the nearest whole-vector cosines were small, and a two-gene restricted search linked Psmb4 and Psmc1 only through partial Amph co-downregulation.
why_it_matters: This keeps a data-first comparator search from being over-interpreted: Gli1 occupies an isolated, two-gene edge case rather than a shared stress or proteasome module in the measured neurons.

why_it_matters: The main dataset phenotype is a pancellular absence of FDR-supported mature-neuron transcriptional output, despite adequate examples of other responders in the same cell groups.

main_caveats: Extracellular Shh, Gli3, Sufu, and Kif3a were not perturbation targets in the parquet.

why_it_matters: The null is pathway-coherent: the postnatal NeuN+ screen lacks a detectable canonical Hh-GLI transcriptional circuit, rather than missing only Gli2.

main_caveats: Correlation was computed on full Wilcoxon-score vectors, not on shared significant DEGs, because Gli2 had no significant DEGs.
summary: The strongest data-driven Gli2 signature neighbors had score-vector correlations below 0.04 in absolute value.
why_it_matters: This rejects hidden convergence with another perturbation program and identifies the Arx/Rax/Fbxo11 neighbor calls as numerical byproducts of a nearly null signature.

literature_claim: GLI2 loss affects embryonic ventral CNS patterning, cerebellar GCP expansion, and congenital pituitary or midline development, while SIX3, ZIC2, and TGIF1 belong to the broader HPE genetic landscape.
main_caveats: The assayed groups are coarse adult-enriched neuronal nuclei; this is not a direct embryonic or human disease model.
summary: Loss of Gli2 in P16 postmitotic NeuN+ cells did not reproduce embryonic ventral-patterning, cerebellar granule-precursor, or HPE-family transcriptional programs.
why_it_matters: Known GLI2 disease and cerebellar phenotypes are better placed in early progenitors, pituitary/midline, limb/craniofacial, and GCP or glial contexts than in maintenance of mature neuronal transcriptomes.

summary: Glis2 loss of function was transcriptionally buffered across every measured P16-to-P37/P44 neuronal group.
why_it_matters: This is a real brain-wide non-response rather than a missing-cell artifact: all 23 neuronal groups were recovered, and none contained a downstream gene at FDR<0.10.

literature_claim: Renal Glis2 loss derepresses Hedgehog/Wnt-linked Snai1 and Wnt4, with EMT, TGF-beta/fibrosis, apoptosis, and senescence outputs.
main_caveats: Absence is restricted to NeuN-enriched brain neurons; renal tubular epithelium and non-neuronal fibrotic compartments were not sampled.
summary: The kidney Glis2-loss program—Hedgehog release, Snai/Wnt activation, EMT/fibrosis, and senescence/apoptosis genes—was absent from juvenile neuronal nuclei.
why_it_matters: The neuronal null is informative because several canonical downstream transcripts were in the tested gene universe yet remained FDR=1.0 in every Glis2 group; the NPHP7 loss mechanism therefore does not generalize to a pan-neuronal stress or EMT-like program after postmitotic Glis2 editing.

literature_claim: GLIS proteins are a related C2H2 zinc-finger family and Glis2 functions in a Hedgehog-linked renal ciliopathy pathway.
main_caveats: Some obvious relatives, including Glis1, Gli3, Wnt4, Snai1, Kif3a, and Pkd2, were not perturbation targets in the parquet and could only be marked not_tested_missing.
summary: Literature-obvious GLIS/Hedgehog/ciliopathy comparators did not converge on Glis2 in neurons.
why_it_matters: Glis3, Gli1, Gli2, Pkd1, and Snai2 were directly represented as target perturbations and produced at most one or two isolated FDR hits, with no shared Glis2 FDR genes; the screen therefore separates the neuronal Glis2 null from both GLIS-family relatedness and the renal Hedgehog/ciliopathy axis.

literature_claim: Glis2 can repress beta-catenin/TCF output and can recruit a CtBP1/HDAC3 transcriptional silencing complex.
main_caveats: The Ctnnb1/Ctbp1 signatures need not be direct Wnt targets; the conclusion is pathway-neighborhood divergence, not shared target-gene identity.
summary: Core beta-catenin and CtBP perturbations were detectable in thalamic/hypothalamic groups where Glis2 was flat.
why_it_matters: Ctnnb1 caused a large 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response and a smaller 145 MH-LH TH Glut response, while Ctbp1 produced Stxbp2-centered hits in the same region; this rejects a generic inability of these postnatal nuclei to mount a transcriptional response to the beta-catenin/CtBP neighborhood.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on full signed Wilcoxon-score vectors; it is a transcriptome-level metric and insensitive to non-transcriptional phenotypes.
summary: Unbiased signature geometry found no strong positive or negative Glis2 neighbor.
why_it_matters: The nearest non-Glis2 perturbation by signed Wilcoxon-score correlation was only r=0.038 and the most anti-correlated was only r=-0.023, so Glis2 was not hiding a weak coherent module that could be recovered by cross-target aggregation.

literature_claim: CPE is a secretory-vesicle carboxypeptidase with endocrine and hippocampal/neural functions, whereas GLIS3 is best established as an endocrine and epithelial transcription factor.
main_caveats: The 012 group is heterogeneous and the signature contains one FDR-significant gene; Pcsk1, Pcsk2, and Syt4 were not significant, so this is not a coordinated prohormone-processing program.
summary: Glis3 perturbation produced a single robust downstream event, Cpe down-regulation, confined to 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: The result narrows the only positive postnatal neuronal signal to a limbic glutamatergic group and to a regulated-secretory/neuropeptide-processing gene, rather than a broad beta-cell, ciliary, or neuronal stress program.

literature_claim: GLIS3 belongs to the GLIS zinc-finger family, is linked to primary-cilium/SUFU biology, and cooperates with islet transcriptional programs that include NEUROG3, HNF, PAX, and MAF factors.
main_caveats: Several comparators themselves had weak brain signatures, so the claim is absence of phenocopy in this screen rather than biochemical independence.
summary: Represented GLIS-family, Hedgehog-proximal, and pancreatic transcriptional relatives failed to phenocopy the Glis3 Cpe-only brain signature.
why_it_matters: The absent phenocopy rejects the simplest expectation that postnatal neuronal Glis3 loss behaves like a generic GLIS/GLI/ciliary perturbation or like depletion of its beta-cell transcriptional partners.

literature_claim: INS1/PC12 work linked GLIS3 binding with neuronal-function and autophagy genes, while a later GLIS3 review argued that the autophagy evidence was modest and not reproduced in mouse models.
main_caveats: Manf is a detector perturbation for UPR detectability, not a same-complex GLIS3 comparator.
summary: The literature-suggested GLIS3 autophagy/ER-stress axis was not recovered after acute Glis3 loss in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: Because Manf perturbation induced Hspa5/Hyou1/Pdia6-class UPR genes in the same analysis universe, the absence of these genes after Glis3 perturbation is an informative negative result, not an snRNA-seq readout failure.

main_caveats: Cosine similarities are dominated by a very small Glis3 effect vector, so the neighbor list is useful mainly to rule out a strong shared signature.
summary: The unbiased Glis3 signature had only near-zero positive and negative neighbors across 1772 other targets.
why_it_matters: This places Glis3 among buffered or singleton perturbations in the juvenile neuronal screen rather than in a recurrent injury, UPR, proteostasis, or synaptic module.

literature_claim: Agonist-occupied GLP-1R can signal through Gs/cAMP/PKA/EPAC/CREB and induce Fos/c-Fos in appetite and autonomic nuclei.
main_caveats: Engagement was not measured by indel sequencing; the result is a steady-state broad-cell-class snRNA null rather than an agonist challenge of purified GLP-1R+ neurons.
summary: P16 mosaic Glp1r loss-of-function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset fact is not a weak canonical program but a brain-wide steady-state null: even immediate-early, cAMP-CREB, and appetite-neuropeptide transcripts were FDR-flat 3-4 weeks after perturbation.

literature_claim: GLP-1R is a class-B peptide GPCR related to receptors such as GCGR and GIPR and couples canonically to Gs-driven cAMP effectors.
main_caveats: Many comparator responses were themselves very small; absence of convergence is robust for this assay but not a biochemical statement that the receptors cannot use shared signaling proteins.
summary: GLP-1R did not converge with its literature-obvious class-B GPCR or Gs/cAMP/PKA/EPAC/CREB comparators.
why_it_matters: The parquet directly separates loss of the sparse ligand receptor from loss of broadly used cAMP/CREB pathway nodes: Creb1 generated the only multi-gene comparator signature, while Gcgr, Pth1r, adenylate cyclases, PKA, Rapgef4, and most PDE/receptor perturbations were null or single-gene calls.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon scores across overlapping group-gene entries; because Glp1r had no significant genes, the neighbor list should be read as a negative control, not as mechanistic similarity to Mycn or Ranbp2.
summary: The unbiased whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Glp1r signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The strongest biological score correlations were only r=0.029 on the positive side and r=-0.015 on the negative side, so the data nominate Glp1r as an isolated flat profile rather than a member of a recurrent transcriptional module.

literature_claim: Brain GLP-1R neurons are anatomically restricted and GLP-1R agonists act through hypothalamic, lateral-septal/amygdalar/BNST, hindbrain, and mesolimbic circuits with Fos-positive activation after drug exposure.
main_caveats: The warning is inferential because the screen lacks ligand challenge, DNA indel rates, subnucleus sampling metadata, and a measured Glp1r 215 MB Dopa surface.
summary: The Glp1r screen result should not be read as evidence that CNS GLP-1R agonists lack neuronal targets.
why_it_matters: Known GLP-1R pharmacology is ligand/state and nucleus specific, whereas this experiment edited sparse postmitotic neurons without an agonist or feeding/stress challenge and lacked a Glp1r measurement for 215 MB Dopa; the null therefore warns that this Perturb-seq design is poorly aligned to VTA, hindbrain, and challenge-evoked therapeutic GLP-1R mechanisms.

literature_claim: GLRA1 encodes an inhibitory glycine-receptor chloride-channel subunit whose adult textbook biology is strongest in spinal cord and brainstem circuits, not a Slc5a3 nuclear program in rostral MGE-derived GABA neurons.
main_caveats: One FDR-significant gene in 67 perturbed nuclei; receptor indels and glycine currents were not measured.
summary: Glra1 produced a real snRNA-seq response only in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and that response consisted of a single down-regulated gene, Slc5a3.
why_it_matters: The screen did not recover a broad glycine-receptor or excitation/stress transcriptome; it exposed an unexpectedly focal basal-ganglia MGE GABA readout.

literature_claim: SLC5A3 transports myo-inositol with sodium and is required for normal brain inositol metabolism and neonatal respiratory rhythmogenesis in mice.
main_caveats: This is a one-gene marker; no other downstream gene in the Glra1 054 CNU-MGE GABA surface passed FDR<0.10.
summary: The lone Glra1-induced transcriptomic marker, Slc5a3, nominates sodium/myo-inositol transport rather than synaptic-gene remodeling as the detectable state variable in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: SLC5A3/SMIT1 is an osmoregulatory and inositol-uptake transporter; its selective decrease suggests a testable link between GlyR α1 loss and osmolyte/inositol handling, but not a full osmotic-stress regulon.

literature_claim: GlyR α subunits, the GlyR β subunit, SLC6A5, gephyrin/GPHN, and collybistin/ARHGEF9 participate in glycinergic inhibitory transmission or startle-disease genetics.
main_caveats: Several comparator perturbations had fewer than 60 CNU-MGE perturbed cells; the contrast is transcriptomic and does not rule out shared electrophysiological loss of glycinergic currents.
summary: Direct GlyR-family and glycinergic-synapse perturbations did not phenocopy the Glra1→Slc5a3 effect.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a generic consequence of weakening any glycinergic synapse component in this assay; the small Glra1 signature is α1-specific or gRNA/context-specific within the measured CNU-MGE state.

literature_claim: SLC5A3 is an osmoregulatory myo-inositol transporter; no prior source predicts opposite GLRA1 and PSMB4 regulation of Slc5a3 in MGE-derived neurons.
main_caveats: This is a single shared gene; Psmb4 is not a glycinergic component and its own 054 signature is broad.
summary: Psmb4 perturbed the same CNU-MGE GABA Slc5a3 marker in the opposite direction and with a large transcriptomic response, whereas Glra1 down-regulated Slc5a3 alone.
why_it_matters: The opposite Psmb4 signature shows that the screen could move Slc5a3 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and separates Glra1 loss from the broad proteasome-stress programs that Psmb4 evokes.

main_caveats: The Glra1 vector has only one FDR-significant coordinate, so full-score correlations are expected to be dominated by null-surface noise.
summary: Unbiased whole-surface signature matching found no strong Glra1-like or anti-Glra1-like perturbation in the model-visible universe.
why_it_matters: The top cosine similarities were near zero, so the Glra1 phenotype should be interpreted as a singleton Slc5a3 event rather than as a member of a diffuse multi-gene module.

literature_claim: Glra2 is a developmental GlyR alpha2 subunit that can be required for embryonic cortical interneuron migration and projection-neuron generation in germline or embryonic Glra2 models.
main_caveats: The screen measured RNA in surviving P37-44 neuronal nuclei after P16 mosaic CRISPR; indel formation, protein loss, calcium signaling, migration, circuit physiology, and abundance depletion were not measured.
summary: Glra2 CRISPR produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of 22 measured neuronal groups despite a mostly negative self-transcript trend.
why_it_matters: The principal result is a global postmitotic RNA buffer: in this P16-to-P37/44 sparse neuronal loss-of-function assay, eliminating a GlyR alpha2 chloride-channel subunit did not elicit a stress, synaptic, developmental, or compensatory transcriptional program.

literature_claim: Alpha GlyR paralogs form glycine-gated chloride channels, beta-containing GlyRs can be synaptically localized through inhibitory scaffolds, and Slc6a5 participates in glycinergic transmission.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptome-wide but limited to targets represented and recovered in the parquet; Arhgef9 and Glrb had fewer than 22 overlapping groups.
summary: A GlyR-centered comparator panel did not converge with Glra2: Glra1, Glra3, Glrb, Gphn, Arhgef9, and Slc6a5 all had score cosines within +/-0.013 of Glra2 and no shared FDR gene because Glra2 had no FDR genes.
why_it_matters: The flat Glra2 result is not hiding a generic glycinergic-receptor RNA module; several receptor, transporter, and inhibitory-scaffold perturbations were themselves essentially single-gene or no-gene signatures in this postnatal assay.

main_caveats: Cosine ranks are dominated by noise when the query perturbation has no FDR-level genes; the finding is the absence of a robust neighbor, not a mechanistic link to the named targets.
summary: The unbiased nearest neighbors of Glra2 were not biologically interpretable convergent modules: the strongest positive score-cosine was only 0.027 and the strongest negative was -0.0147 across 1772 candidate targets.
why_it_matters: This preserves the pre-literature comparator result: Glra2 is a true isolated flat surface in this dataset rather than a member of an unanticipated stress or lipid-metabolism signature family.

literature_claim: GLRA2 neurodevelopmental disease is linked to disrupted GlyR alpha2 signaling during cortical development and to multiple allele classes, including loss-, gain-, and altered-function variants.
main_caveats: The gene list is a targeted absence check, not an enriched DE module; disagreement here means the expected program was not recovered in this assay context.
summary: The absent developmental-gene response argues that this P16 loss-of-function screen should not be read as a native model of GLRA2 neurodevelopmental alleles, especially gain- or altered-function missense alleles.
why_it_matters: GLRA2 disease variants can reduce function, increase function, change gating, or change trafficking; a sparse postmitotic CRISPR knockout leaves the embryonic migration/progenitor window and allele-specific channel biophysics untested.

literature_claim: Glra3 encodes the alpha-3 subunit of a glycine-gated chloride channel; alpha-3 loss is expected to alter inhibitory currents, and alpha-3-containing GlyRs can support tonic forebrain currents.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; direct currents, synaptic localization, spinal circuits, retina, and inflammatory challenge were not assayed.
summary: Acute Glra3 loss did not produce a sustained cell-autonomous transcriptome in any recovered neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The robust result is a pan-sampled absence of FDR-supported downstream genes, including immediate-early genes that would have reported a persistent excitability response; Glra3 behaves as a membrane-current gene rather than a transcriptional-state regulator in this P16-to-P37/44 brain snRNA-seq assay.

literature_claim: Synaptic GlyRs are alpha/beta chloride channels anchored through the beta subunit to gephyrin, and gephyrin-collybistin also organizes inhibitory GABA-A receptor synapses.
main_caveats: This is a null-overlap comparison; rare one-gene comparator hits should not be treated as pathway programs.
summary: The literature-obvious GlyR and inhibitory-synapse comparators did not reveal a hidden Glra3-like transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: Directly measured relatives rejected the expectation that alpha subunits, the beta subunit, gephyrin/collybistin clustering, or an adjacent GABA-A receptor subunit would phenocopy Glra3 in snRNA-seq: Glra2, Glrb, and Arhgef9 had zero downstream hits; Glra1, Gphn, Slc6a5, and Gabrg2 produced only isolated non-overlapping genes.

literature_claim: No literature comparator was used for the data-driven residual-neighbor search.
main_caveats: Residual correlation uses transcriptome-wide logFC values and is not informative for electrophysiological phenotypes.
summary: Unbiased residual-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Glra3 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: After subtracting gene/cell-group means across the 1,773-target analysis universe, the best residual correlations were near zero and the nominated neighbors were non-responders, arguing that the Glra3 surface is statistically indistinguishable from background rather than a weak version of another target's program.

literature_claim: Glra3 knockout and S346A point-mutant mice implicate alpha-3 GlyRs in PGE2-dependent spinal inflammatory hyperalgesia.
main_caveats: The dataset was acute, mosaic, neuronal brain snRNA-seq rather than a spinal inflammatory-pain experiment.
summary: The Glra3 null is not evidence against alpha-3 GlyR analgesic biology.
why_it_matters: The best-established Glra3 phenotype is PGE2/PKA-dependent reduction of alpha-3 GlyR currents in spinal inflammatory hyperalgesia; this screen omitted spinal nociceptive circuits, inflammatory prostaglandin challenge, and current recording, so a cortical/forebrain snRNA-seq zero should not deprioritize alpha-3 potentiators or phospho-modulation studies.

literature_claim: GLRB is a glycine-gated chloride-channel beta subunit whose canonical action is receptor assembly, conductance and synaptic anchoring rather than direct transcriptional regulation.
main_caveats: Functional indels were not measured; the conclusion is limited to snRNA-seq 3-4 weeks after a P16 mosaic CRISPR perturbation in recovered NeuN+ brain nuclei.
summary: Glrb loss produced no FDR-level downstream transcriptome in any recovered neuronal class, even though the target transcript itself was depleted in three posterior classes.
why_it_matters: This converts an apparently negative screen surface into a specific buffered result: sparse postnatal Glrb loss can lower Glrb mRNA in some nuclei without launching proteostatic, ISR, autophagy, redox, synaptic-down, or activity-regulated RNA programs.

main_caveats: Self-transcript depletion is only an RNA proxy; an indel can be functional without degrading the transcript, and an mRNA drop does not demonstrate loss of surface GlyR currents.
summary: The only FDR-level Glrb self-transcript drops were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, and each remained downstream-null.
why_it_matters: The classes with the clearest RNA engagement are posterior thalamic/midbrain/pons-myelinencephalon groups, refining the null away from a uniform lack of Glrb detection toward a target-positive but transcriptionally buffered subset.

literature_claim: GlyR alpha subunits, the beta subunit, gephyrin, ARHGEF9/collybistin and the glycine transporter SLC6A5 occupy the same inhibitory glycinergic synapse biology, with GLRA1, GLRB and SLC6A5 also linked genetically to hyperekplexia.
main_caveats: Several comparator signatures are themselves tiny, so this is a rejection of robust transcriptomic convergence rather than proof that the proteins are functionally unrelated.
summary: Literature-obvious glycinergic relatives did not converge on a shared RNA module: Glra2, Glra3 and Arhgef9 were downstream-null, while Glra1, Gphn and Slc6a5 each produced only isolated single-class hits.
why_it_matters: The absence of a common Glrb/Glra/Gphn/Slc6a5 program shows that this postnatal snRNA assay is not reading out the glycinergic synapse as a transcriptional pathway in the sampled neurons.

literature_claim: Gephyrin can organize both glycine receptors and subsets of GABA_A receptors at inhibitory synapses through a shared binding surface.
main_caveats: The GABA_A signatures are small and in different receptor subunits; they serve as empirical readout controls, not as evidence that Gabrb2 or Gabrg2 are mechanistic Glrb paralogs.
summary: Glrb did not induce canonical activity-regulated genes, whereas Gabrb2 and Gabrg2 perturbations produced small FDR-level Nr4a1/Vgf/Fos/Npas4 or Bdnf responses in matched groups.
why_it_matters: This gates the readout-mismatch interpretation: the platform can recover activity-regulated immediate-early RNA when an inhibitory receptor perturbation drives it, but a Glrb loss did not measurably disinhibit the sampled nuclei.

main_caveats: Cosines were computed from Wilcoxon downstream-score vectors and exclude target self-genes; because Glrb is close to zero, the neighbor ranks are mathematically well-defined but biologically weak.
summary: Glrb had no meaningful same-sign or opposite-sign target neighbor in the complete parquet signature search.
why_it_matters: The nearest measured perturbations were too weakly correlated to rescue a hidden module by cross-target averaging, keeping the biological interpretation anchored on a true near-flat Glrb surface rather than on a noisy nominal gene list.

main_caveats: Only one downstream gene at FDR 0.062397 with 27 perturbed cells; Abcf3 did not recur in the other measured Gls groups.
summary: Gls produced one FDR<0.10 downstream event: Abcf3 induction in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: This is the only positive cell group in the entire Gls surface, so it nominates a very narrow and low-confidence striatal/MGE GABA response rather than a canonical glutamate-metabolism program.

literature_claim: GLS enzymatically supplies glutamate for neurotransmission and intracellular glutamate metabolism.
main_caveats: The FDR-significant mRNA drop is not DNA indel sequencing and does not prove biallelic enzyme loss; absence of RNA DE does not test glutamate pools or synaptic release.
summary: Two subcortical glutamatergic groups had measurable Gls self-transcript depletion but still no downstream DE.
why_it_matters: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, the target mRNA moved in the expected direction while every non-Gls transcript remained below FDR<0.10, arguing that postmitotic neuronal Gls loss is buffered at the nuclear transcriptome under this sparse 3-4 week assay.

literature_claim: Glutamine-derived glutamate feeds neurotransmitter, TCA/anaplerotic, amino-acid, and glutathione/redox pathways; GLS1 inhibition is therefore important in proliferative glutamine-addicted cells.
main_caveats: The marker test was transcript-only; metabolites, flux, vesicle filling, electrophysiology, and protein abundance were not measured.
summary: The expected glutamate/GABA-cycle, redox, autophagy, and ISR/UPR marker transcripts were absent from the Gls DE surface.
why_it_matters: GLS loss is expected to perturb glutamate pools, GABA production, anaplerosis, and glutathione-linked redox biology, but none of the 30 pre-specified marker transcripts reached FDR<0.10 in any measured cell group, excluding a broad compensatory nuclear program in this experiment.

literature_claim: GABAergic neurons make GABA from glutamate through glutamic-acid decarboxylase, and GLUD/GOT route glutamate to α-ketoglutarate or aspartate in broader glutamate metabolism.
main_caveats: The conclusion is based on transcriptomic overlap, not matched metabolomics; Got1 and Got2 had a few FDR<0.10 genes in one thalamic group.
summary: Perturbations of represented glutamate-metabolism and GABA-branch relatives were also largely flat and did not converge with Gls.
why_it_matters: Glud1, Got1, Got2, Gad2, Abat, Slc6a1, Slc1a1, and Slc1a2 failed to create a shared transcriptomic module with Gls, suggesting that single-gene perturbation of neurotransmitter metabolic flux is usually not read out as a cell-autonomous snRNA-seq program in these postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: GRIN1, GRIN2A, and GRIN2B encode NMDA-receptor subunits mediating glutamatergic synaptic transmission.
main_caveats: The comparator result does not establish the direct electrophysiologic consequence of Gls loss; it only localizes the absent Gls response relative to postsynaptic receptor-gene responses.
summary: Postsynaptic NMDA-receptor perturbations responded where presynaptic Gls was flat.
why_it_matters: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b generated real DE in the same analysis universe while their signatures were nearly orthogonal to Gls, showing that the Gls null is not a general inability of this assay to recover consequences of glutamatergic-gene perturbation.

main_caveats: The cosine is dominated by sub-threshold Wilcoxon-score variation because Gls has only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene.
summary: Whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no robust positive or negative Gls signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top positive and top negative neighbors of Gls were Nfs1 and Prepl with absolute score-cosine values below 0.031 and no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, so Gls is best treated as a near-null signature rather than assigned to a data-driven response module.

literature_claim: Human GLS loss-of-function and deficiency produce severe neurologic disease, while GLS1 is being developed as a target in glutamine-addicted cancers.
main_caveats: This was partial, mosaic CRISPR in juvenile mouse neurons and lacked pharmacologic exposure, glia, metabolomics, and physiology.
summary: The flat neuronal snRNA-seq result should not be read as safety of GLS inhibition at the synaptic or metabolic level.
why_it_matters: GLS1 is a pharmacologic cancer target and inherited GLS deficiency is neurologic, but the assay observed neither a stress program nor a broad neurotransmitter-gene compensation after sparse postmitotic knockout; therapeutic interpretation therefore needs metabolite, electrophysiology, and non-neuronal follow-up rather than relying on this nuclear-RNA negative result.

literature_claim: GDH1 links glutamate to alpha-ketoglutarate/TCA flux; complete CNS Glud1 loss affects astrocytic glutamate oxidation and neuronal GDH becomes important under glucose deprivation or elevated energy demand.
main_caveats: The screen measures basal nuclear RNA 3-4 weeks after sparse P16 CRISPR, not metabolites, enzymatic activity, DNA indels, astrocytes, or stimulated neuronal bioenergetics.
summary: Glud1 loss produced no robust downstream neuronal transcriptional program in 22 measured cell groups despite a consistently negative self-transcript.
why_it_matters: This is a target-specific negative result rather than an assay failure: a mitochondrial glutamate-to-alpha-ketoglutarate enzyme was perturbed in postmitotic neurons, yet glutamate/glutamine, GABA, ISR, UPR, and redox marker transcripts did not pass FDR 0.10.

literature_claim: GDH, glutaminase, alpha-ketoglutarate-linked aminotransferases, and TCA enzymes are biochemically coupled around cerebral glutamate and alpha-ketoglutarate metabolism.
main_caveats: The comparator responses themselves were small, so the contrast is strongest as a failure to find a common robust transcriptional module.
summary: Represented glutamate/alpha-ketoglutarate neighbors did not converge on a shared transcriptomic module with Glud1.
why_it_matters: Mouse neurons in this assay did not treat GLUD1 as an interchangeable transcriptional proxy for glutaminase, cytosolic/mitochondrial aspartate aminotransferases, the alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex, or the astrocytic glutamate transporter target Slc1a2.

literature_claim: GLUD1 hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia is driven by activating, GTP-insensitive GDH mutations that act prominently in pancreatic beta-cell and peripheral nitrogen metabolism.
main_caveats: The screen tested only loss of function in neuronal nuclei and did not assay insulin, ammonia, metabolites, or GLUD1 gain-of-function alleles.
summary: The LoF-null neuronal surface should not be read as modeling GLUD1 gain-of-function hyperinsulinism or ammonia disease.
why_it_matters: Dominant GLUD1 disease alleles increase GDH activity by weakening allosteric inhibition; the perturbation here is sparse mouse neuronal loss of function in a pancreas- and liver-free, astrocyte-poor readout, so a flat neuronal signature mainly argues against an overt LoF transcriptional liability in juvenile neurons.

main_caveats: The neighbor ranking used the 600 Glud1 genes with raw p<0.005 because Glud1 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes; it is therefore an exploratory restricted-signature analysis.
summary: The top data-driven neighbors of the Glud1 surface were only weak nominal correlations and were rejected as robust convergent biology.
why_it_matters: The whole-universe search did not uncover a hidden perturbation module; apparent neighbors were a property of the raw-p nominal tail of an otherwise FDR-null surface.

literature_claim: G alpha olf is expected to couple dopamine D1 and adenosine A2A receptors to adenylyl-cyclase/cAMP signaling most prominently in striatal medium spiny neurons.
main_caveats: The 012 call contains only 33 perturbed cells and a single FDR-significant gene; Muc3a is not a known Gnal effector, and Pde4a was only sub-threshold.
summary: Gnal loss produced only a single robust downstream hit, Muc3a up-regulation, in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: The result argues that P16 sparse Gnal loss is not a broad transcriptional perturbation in juvenile postmitotic neurons; the measurable positive biology is a one-gene limbic glutamatergic event rather than the canonical striatal cAMP program.

literature_claim: PDE10A is enriched in striatal MSNs and its inhibition can increase cAMP-linked striatal gene expression, whereas G alpha olf couples D1/A2A receptors through the AC5 source complex.
main_caveats: The 059 cluster is broad rather than a purified D1- or D2-MSN class; Pde10a had 71 perturbed cells versus 40 for Gnal; receptor ligands were not acutely controlled.
summary: In the striatal/LGE GABA group, Pde10a knockdown activated Scg2 and Crem while Gnal, Adcy5, Gnas, Drd2, Gnao1, and Pde4b were FDR-flat.
why_it_matters: The same assay can detect a cAMP-linked MSN transcriptional output when the cyclic-nucleotide degradation arm is perturbed, so the Gnal null is specific to the receptor-to-adenylyl-cyclase source arm or its basal state rather than a global inability to score striatal cAMP transcription.

literature_claim: GNAL pathogenic variants are loss-of-function causes of mostly adult-onset isolated dystonia through impaired G alpha olf signaling rather than a described neuronal degeneration syndrome.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure proteins, phospho-PKA/ERK, firing, movement phenotypes, olfactory sensory neurons, or chronic adult disease states.
summary: Gnal perturbation did not trigger a neuronal stress, proteostasis, UPR/ISR, autophagy, or synaptic-collapse transcriptome in any measured group.
why_it_matters: DYT-GNAL is therefore better modeled here as a circuit signaling defect than as an acute cell-intrinsic toxicity program; a basal snRNA readout after P16 knockout is unlikely to expose the movement-disorder mechanism without activity or behavioral challenge.

literature_claim: No prior literature claim was used; these were computed neighbors from the DE universe.
main_caveats: The comparator query was restricted to top/bottom Gnal ranks because the FDR signature contained only one downstream gene; all absolute neighbor scores were small.
summary: The top data-driven Gnal restricted-signature neighbors were weak and failed to reproduce the Muc3a event.
why_it_matters: Gnal does not sit inside a large convergent transcriptomic module in this screen; nearest-neighbor calls should be treated as null-noise comparators rather than mechanistic phenocopies.

literature_claim: THAP1-related dystonia is a clinical differential diagnosis for DYT-GNAL rather than a member of the G alpha olf cAMP complex.
main_caveats: This is a restricted cross-target comparison; Thap1 biology itself is not interpreted beyond its measured non-convergence with Gnal.
summary: Thap1, a represented isolated-dystonia differential gene, showed recurrent Prepl/Cuedc2/Fam117a changes in thalamic and midbrain groups but none in the two Gnal-relevant 012 or 059 groups.
why_it_matters: The screen separates the Gnal and Thap1 disease genes rather than merging all dystonia genes into one transcriptional phenotype, consistent with genetically overlapping dystonia syndromes using different cell and molecular mechanisms.

literature_claim: PUF60 is a general splicing factor involved in 3-prime splice-site recognition.
main_caveats: Single downstream gene and single cell group; no coordinated spliceosome module reached FDR<0.10.
summary: Gnao1 produced one robust downstream transcriptomic hit: Puf60 was down-regulated in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The only FDR<0.10 downstream gene is an RNA-splicing factor and it appears in a single cortical intratelencephalic class, so the dataset supports an extremely narrow, noncanonical transcriptional consequence rather than a broad Go/cAMP program.
