literature_claim: Gαo is a GPCR-coupled signaling alpha subunit whose best-established proximal outputs are cyclic-nucleotide and ion-channel/synaptic signaling rather than constitutive transcription-factor activity.
main_caveats: DNA indels, protein depletion, cAMP fluxes, membrane excitability, and synaptic release were not measured.
summary: Postnatal Gnao1 loss is transcriptionally buffered in neuronal nuclei: 21 of 22 measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes even though the Gnao1 transcript was measured and shifted downward in every measured group.
why_it_matters: The screen reads out chronic cell-autonomous nuclear RNA 3-4 weeks after P16 editing; the missing broad signature says that Gαo loss does not lock most surviving neurons into a stable stress, activity, or compensation state on that axis.

literature_claim: Gαo works within neuromodulatory GPCR complexes that converge on cAMP, GIRK, calcium-channel, and presynaptic-release effectors.
main_caveats: Comparator guide engagement is also inferred from RNA and many on-target mRNA rows are weak; the conclusion is restricted to chronic snRNA signatures.
summary: Literature-obvious Gi/o and cAMP relatives represented in the parquet did not phenocopy Gnao1, and none reproduced the L4/5 Puf60 decrease.
why_it_matters: The Gnao1 surface is not the visible member of a larger chronic GPCR transcriptome: Gnas, Gnal, Gnb5, Adcy1, Adcy5, Drd2, Gabbr1, Gabbr2, Grm7, Oprm1, Kcnj6, Cacna1a, and Pde10a were overwhelmingly flat or single-gene responders in the same Wilcoxon universe.

literature_claim: Gαo and PDE10A both impinge on striatal cyclic-nucleotide signaling, and PDE10A regulates cAMP/PKA signaling in striatum.
main_caveats: The Pde10a response itself is only two genes in this cell group; transient activity responses after Gnao1 editing could have been missed at the P37-44 endpoint.
summary: Immediate-early and cAMP-responsive transcripts were absent after Gnao1 perturbation, despite being in principle detectable in this screen.
why_it_matters: Gnao1 loss was expected to alter cAMP or excitability if it produced a sustained large perturbation; the absence of Fos/Jun/Egr/Npas4/Arc/Nr4a1/Crem/Scg2-family responses, plus visible Pde10a-induced Scg2 and Crem in CNU-LGE LSX GABA, argues against a chronic CREB/activity state rather than a blanket inability of snRNA-seq to see second-messenger output.

main_caveats: Neighbor metrics on a nearly null query are dominated by sub-threshold ranks, so this is a rejection of robust convergence, not a biological link to Npy5r or cilia/proteasome biology.
summary: An unbiased signature-neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Gnao1 neighbor; proteasome and nuclear-pore hits seen with a nominal Gnao1 seed set were rejected as exploratory.
why_it_matters: Genome-wide comparison prevents an overfitted single-target story: the top full-profile cosine similarities were only 0.037 and -0.020, and the apparent Psmc1/Psmb4/Tpr overlaps came from nominal Gnao1 rows rather than robust shared Gnao1 DEGs.

literature_claim: Sorting nexins are endolysosomal trafficking and signaling proteins with nervous-system relevance, but a direct Gnas-Snx29 regulatory edge has not been established.
main_caveats: Single downstream gene, FDR 0.0685, only 72 perturbed nuclei; it is a biomarker hypothesis, not a multi-gene endosomal program.
summary: Gnas produced a one-gene, deep-layer IT glutamatergic response: Snx29 was up only in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, while the remaining 22 measured groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The only robust postnatal cell-autonomous transcriptomic consequence was a candidate trafficking/endosomal marker rather than the broad GPCR-cAMP collapse implied by canonical Gsα biochemistry.

literature_claim: Gαs/Gαolf proteins couple activated GPCRs to adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, PKA and nuclear CREB-dependent transcription.
main_caveats: The assay lacked acute GPCR agonist stimulation and measured a steady post-perturbation basal state.
summary: Resting Gnas loss did not induce the expected cAMP/CREB immediate-early transcriptional module, although Creb1 perturbation in the same analysis universe produced strong Crem compensation.
why_it_matters: The null is not because snRNA-seq cannot read CREB-family rewiring: it can. The block is upstream of transcription, consistent with Gnas functioning as a ligand-gated GPCR transducer whose basal loss is buffered without synchronized receptor activation.

literature_claim: In striatal medium spiny neurons, dopamine D1 and adenosine A2A cAMP signaling depends on a specialized Gαolf/Gβ2/Gγ7/adenylyl-cyclase-5 module.
main_caveats: Most comparator signatures were themselves small; the conclusion rests on absence of shared FDR genes plus near-zero flattened-score correlations.
summary: Gnas did not phenocopy Gnal, Adcy5, Pde10a, PKA, Epac or CREB-axis perturbations; all G-protein/cAMP comparator correlations to Gnas were near zero.
why_it_matters: The directly measured related-target surface separates classical Gsα loss from striatal Gαolf/PDE10A and downstream CREB perturbations, arguing for context- and transducer-specific cAMP wiring rather than one interchangeable cAMP transcriptome.

literature_claim: GNAS inactivation disorders are parent-of-origin dependent, and Gsα in CNS/MC4R-expressing neurons is required in mice for melanocortin-linked energy balance and thermogenesis.
main_caveats: The assayed groups are broad, Mc4r itself was not a perturbation target here, and energy expenditure is a systems physiology output.
summary: Hypothalamic-containing groups did not show a Gnas transcriptional response, despite literature tying CNS Gsα and MC4R-expressing cells to energy expenditure and obesity.
why_it_matters: A bulk 066/110/145 hypothalamic-class zero says that GNAS obesity biology is likely carried by rare receptor-defined neurons and acute melanocortin/autonomic physiology, not by a broad constitutive transcriptome across the recovered hypothalamic populations.

main_caveats: Correlation was computed on Wilcoxon-score vectors; because Gnas has only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene, restricted-signature overlap is intrinsically underpowered.
summary: Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found no strong convergent or anti-correlated Gnas module across 1,773 targets.
why_it_matters: The weak Gnas surface is not concealing an obvious shared disease or stress signature: even the top positive gene neighbors had r≤0.0326 and the top negative gene neighbors had |r|≤0.0116.

literature_claim: Gnb5 loss in germline mice and humans affects neuronal signaling and neurodevelopment through Gbeta5-R7 RGS complexes.
main_caveats: DNA indel engagement and protein depletion were not measured; absence of FDR<0.10 genes does not exclude rapid GPCR, GIRK, or firing phenotypes.
summary: Postnatal mosaic Gnb5 loss produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: The major result is negative but interpretable: a GPCR signal-termination scaffold can be perturbed without inducing a snRNA-seq stress, synaptic, or compensation module 3-4 weeks later.

main_caveats: Only one cell group reached on-target FDR<0.10; Gnb5 mRNA is an imperfect proxy for functional indels.
summary: The only FDR-supported on-target RNA decrease was in Pvalb Gaba, where Gnb5 was down by logFC -0.638 without any downstream DEG.
why_it_matters: This separates target-RNA depletion from transcriptional remodeling: even the cell class with the clearest Gnb5 RNA effect did not launch a secondary nuclear program.

literature_claim: Gbeta5 forms obligatory R7 RGS complexes, GPR158 can scaffold an RGS7-Gbeta5 complex, and Gbeta5/R7 signaling acts on Gi/o and GIRK pathways.
main_caveats: Rgs7, Rgs9, and Rgs11 were not represented as target perturbations, and Gpr179 biology is most obvious in retina, outside this screen.
summary: Measurable Gbeta5/R7-adjacent perturbations were also nearly transcriptomically silent: Rgs6, Gpr158, Gnao1, Gpr179, and Kcnj6 generated at most one downstream FDR<0.10 gene apiece in matched groups.
why_it_matters: The flat Gnb5 surface is a pathway-level property in this assay rather than a unique failure of Gnb5 guides; direct perturbation of associated GPCR/RGS/GIRK nodes likewise failed to produce a broad RNA signature.

main_caveats: Neighbor ranks use nonsignificant whole-signature logFC structure because Gnb5 had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
summary: The top data-driven Gnb5 signature neighbors were unrelated targets with absolute feature-centered correlations below 0.09 and zero shared FDR-supported genes.
why_it_matters: The nominal residual shape around Gnb5 should not be elevated to a hidden module: no robust positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor was recovered.

literature_claim: Germline Gnb5 or GNB5 loss causes developmental, motor, dopaminergic, retinal, cardio-autonomic, and epileptic phenotypes.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks retina, heart, olfactory bulb, hindbrain, most non-neuronal cells, and recovered Gnb5-perturbed MB Dopa rows.
summary: The data refine known GNB5 loss-of-function disease toward electrophysiology, development, retina, heart, and dopaminergic systems rather than a persistent postmitotic cell-autonomous RNA state in sampled forebrain, midbrain, and cerebellar neurons.
why_it_matters: A silent juvenile cortical/brain snRNA result should not be interpreted as safety or irrelevance of GNB5; the strongest literature phenotypes live in kinetic GPCR signaling, germline development, and unsampled or incompletely sampled lineages.

literature_claim: Complete GNPTAB deficiency disrupts lysosomal hydrolase M6P tagging and causes mucolipidosis with storage and neurologic disease in germline contexts.
main_caveats: The primary defect is biochemical rather than transcriptional, functional DNA indels were not measured, and glia were largely absent.
summary: Gnptab did not induce any downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 22 recovered neuronal groups, and canonical lysosomal, autophagy, and UPR/ISR genes were all FDR=1.0.
why_it_matters: This is an informative negative result: the acute postmitotic neuronal screen did not recover the lysosomal-storage transcriptional programs expected from complete congenital GNPTAB loss.

literature_claim: GNPTAB alpha/beta and GNPTG gamma subunits act in the same GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase enzyme that generates M6P signals.
main_caveats: A shared flat transcriptome is weaker than a shared active signature and does not establish equivalent biochemical effects.
summary: The direct GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase partner Gnptg was also flat in every Gnptab-matched group and had a near-zero score-Pearson correlation to Gnptab.
why_it_matters: Same-complex comparison shows that the lack of response is shared by the immediate M6P tag-synthesis module rather than being unique to Gnptab guide behavior.

literature_claim: M6P loss affects lysosomal enzymes unevenly across enzymes and cell types, and M6P-independent routes can partially maintain lysosomal hydrolase delivery.
main_caveats: Single hydrolase knockout is not biochemically identical to wholesale loss of hydrolase M6P tagging; several comparator targets also had weak mRNA self-depletion.
summary: Perturbations of representative lysosomal hydrolase or cargo genes Ctsb, Gaa, Manba, Asah1, Ppt1, and Psap were flat across Gnptab-matched neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Direct loss of several hydrolase cargos also failed to produce broad snRNA-seq signatures, supporting a neuronally buffered lysosomal hydrolase axis in this acute window.

literature_claim: Retromer, autophagy-initiation, and M6P-receptor trafficking act in endolysosomal proteostasis but are indirect rather than catalytic GNPTAB partners.
main_caveats: The Vps35 and Rb1cc1 signatures are small and not shared-direction overlaps with Gnptab, whose own FDR signature is empty.
summary: Vps35 and Rb1cc1 generated detectable signatures in Gnptab-matched neurons while Gnptab remained flat.
why_it_matters: The divergence shows that this dataset can observe endolysosomal/autophagy-linked neuronal transcriptional responses, so the Gnptab null is pathway-specific rather than a blanket lysosome-readout failure.

main_caveats: The query was run on full signed Wilcoxon scores, but Gnptab has no FDR-significant downstream genes, so these correlations reflect a weak vector.
summary: Genome-wide data-driven neighbors of Gnptab were all near zero and non-lysosomal.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting arbitrary top-ranked correlations as hidden Gnptab biology; there was no robust convergent or antagonistic signature to carry forward.

literature_claim: GNPTG loss impairs M6P tagging of soluble lysosomal hydrolases and causes mucolipidosis III gamma, but mouse brain retains partial hydrolase phosphorylation and shows much milder pathology than Gnptab loss.
main_caveats: DNA indels and hydrolase activity were not measured; the result is limited to sparse P16-to-P37/44 neuronal snRNA-seq.
summary: Gnptg loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null rather than a lysosomal-storage-like secondary program.
why_it_matters: GNPTG is a canonical lysosomal enzyme-targeting gene, but its acute sparse removal after P16 did not change any downstream transcript at FDR<0.10 in the assayed postmitotic neuronal nuclei.

literature_claim: M6P-tagging failure causes intracellular lysosomal hydrolase loss and storage in susceptible cells, with the strongest chronic mouse pathology occurring after complete Gnptab loss rather than gamma-subunit loss.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq would not measure hydrolase secretion or substrate directly; only the absence of a secondary transcriptional program is tested.
summary: The expected lysosomal, TFEB/autophagy and cathepsin response was absent at FDR level.
why_it_matters: The primary GNPTG defect is biochemical, but a storage burden large enough to engage lysosomal biogenesis or autophagy should have produced mRNA changes in genes that were present in the DE tables.

literature_claim: GNPTG-defective fibroblasts were reported to increase GNPTAB expression.
main_caveats: The fibroblast report was human and in vitro; this dataset measures steady-state nuclear RNA, not enzyme activity.
summary: The fibroblast GNPTAB-compensation motif was not reused by postmitotic neurons.
why_it_matters: Human GNPTG-mutant fibroblasts can raise GNPTAB mRNA, but the assayed mouse neurons did not up-regulate Gnptab, Nagpa, M6pr, Igf2r or Sort1, separating the neuronal mosaic response from a mesenchymal disease-cell compensation program.

literature_claim: GNPTAB and GNPTG encode subunits of one GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase, with GNPTAB carrying catalytic alpha/beta function and producing a more severe mouse and human disease when fully lost.
main_caveats: Gnptab itself had weak on-target mRNA reduction in this screen, and no hydrolase-phosphorylation assay accompanies either perturbation.
summary: Gnptab, the represented same-complex partner, was also flat and did not converge with Gnptg by signed-score similarity.
why_it_matters: The flatness is therefore pathway-level for the sampled P16 neuronal M6P-tagging perturbations in this screen, rather than a unique property of the gamma subunit alone.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed from signed Wilcoxon scores, not protein phenotypes; the strongest positive and negative correlations were effectively noise scale.
summary: Genome-scale signature comparison nominated no credible Gnptg responder neighbor or antagonist.
why_it_matters: The top data-driven neighbors had signed Wilcoxon-score correlations near zero and were rejected on direct DE-surface inspection, so no secondary module should be inferred from nominal Gnptg ranks.

literature_claim: Lysosomal storage therapies exploit cross-correction: enzyme secreted from donor or treated cells is taken up by recipient cells through M6P-receptor pathways.
main_caveats: Cross-correction was not measured directly here; it is a mechanistic explanation for a sparse M6P-pathway null, not an observed enzyme-flux measurement.
summary: The Gnptg null is compatible with rescue by neighboring wild-type cells in a sparse M6P screen.
why_it_matters: Because M6P-bearing enzymes can be secreted and recaptured by M6P receptors, mosaic CRISPR can underestimate a hydrolase-targeting defect that would be exposed by organism-wide or lineage-wide loss.

main_caveats: The effect is a single gene at FDR 0.098 with 51 perturbed nuclei, and the Gnrhr transcript itself was not on the tested-gene list in the responding group.
summary: Gnrhr-targeting CRISPR produced a responder that was both cell-class restricted and one-gene restricted: Sbk1 was induced in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and no other cell group had a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: This nominates Sbk1 as a narrow candidate marker of the only transcriptomic Gnrhr response in the postnatal neuronal screen, but not as a pathway-level GnRHR effector.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed from Wilcoxon score vectors dominated by a Gnrhr-null surface, so the neighbor ranking is useful mainly for falsifying strong convergence.
summary: Full-surface cross-perturbation analysis did not find a robust convergent Gnrhr module; the strongest biological cosines were only 0.0265 to Camta1 and -0.0150 to Csf1r, and the data-driven neighbors did not reproduce Sbk1 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
why_it_matters: The single Sbk1-positive response is isolated rather than a recurrent state shared with another perturbation in the model-visible universe.

literature_claim: GnRH-GnRHR signaling in pituitary gonadotropes couples through Gq/PLC/calcium/PKC and MAPK to regulate immediate-early factors and gonadotropin subunit genes, and GNRHR loss causes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
main_caveats: The assay was not a pituitary or GnRH-pulse challenge and therefore tests only whether that endocrine program appears ectopically as a postnatal neuronal transcriptional response.
summary: The canonical pituitary GnRHR MAPK/immediate-early/gonadotropin transcriptional program was absent from neuronal Gnrhr perturbations, and represented HPG-axis receptors or GnRHR-linked signaling nodes were also essentially flat and non-convergent.
why_it_matters: The result separates a well-established endocrine GPCR program from basal postmitotic brain-neuron transcriptomes: Egr1/Fos/Jun/Dusp1 and Lhb/Fshb/Cga were not induced or repressed, and Kiss1r, Tacr3, Fshr, Lhcgr, Plcb1, Mapk1, Gnas, Prkaca and Nr5a1 did not phenocopy the Gnrhr Sbk1 response.

literature_claim: Strong GOT1 loss can cause redox/metabolic stress in nutrient-limited cancer cells or high-demand photoreceptors.
main_caveats: The one positive signature contains only six FDR<0.10 genes, and direct metabolites were not assayed.
summary: Got1 produced a real but very small DE response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; 21 other measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
why_it_matters: This makes the primary phenotype selective transcriptional buffering rather than a broad neuronal malate-aspartate-shuttle stress signature.

literature_claim: GOT1 and MDH1 are sequential cytosolic reactions of the malate-aspartate shuttle.
main_caveats: Only Spock2 and Zcchc7 were significant in both perturbations; the full Mdh1 signature was broader than Got1.
summary: Mdh1, the cytosolic malate dehydrogenase partner of GOT1, was Got1's top positive six-gene neighbor and partially shared the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.
why_it_matters: The strongest unbiased convergence lands on the cytosolic half of the malate-aspartate shuttle, supporting a biochemical rather than generic-neuronal origin for the tiny Got1 signature.

literature_claim: MAS contains cytosolic, mitochondrial, and transporter components, and congenital defects in several non-GOT1 MAS genes cause neurological disease.
main_caveats: Only the thalamic Got1 responder group was used for restricted six-marker overlap; Slc25a11 was not a perturbation target.
summary: Mitochondrial and carrier MAS comparators Got2, Mdh2, Slc25a12, and Slc25a13 did not phenocopy Got1 in the matched thalamic responder group.
why_it_matters: Closely connected MAS components are not interchangeable in this postmitotic snRNA assay; the screen resolves a cytosolic Got1/Mdh1 transcriptomic branch from the otherwise flat mitochondrial/carrier arm.

literature_claim: ASNS is induced by amino-acid/ATF4 integrated stress signaling.
main_caveats: Asns is a single marker and the measured FDR is near the 0.10 threshold.
summary: Asns upregulation is compatible with a local amino-acid stress trace, but Got1 did not induce a broad ATF4/CHOP integrated-stress program.
why_it_matters: This separates a weak metabolic compensation from a generalized ISR or proteostasis collapse and explains why large Gfpt1/Dhdds stress signatures only partially overlap with Got1.

literature_claim: No specific prior literature predicted an opposition between Got1 and these nuclear or chromatin perturbations.
main_caveats: Restricted to six genes in one cell group; no mechanistic link is inferred.
summary: Tpr and Setd1a were robust anti-neighbors that significantly reversed the Got1 Pcca/Zcchc7/Atp11b branch, whereas raw anti-neighbors Fbxo11, Son, and Brwd1 were rejected as subthreshold for the six Got1 genes.
why_it_matters: Preserving rejected and retained negative neighbors prevents over-interpreting every signed-score hit and shows that the Got1 thalamic branch is directionally opposed by nuclear-pore/chromatin perturbations rather than by a MAS paralog.

literature_claim: GOT1 loss perturbs NADH/aspartate metabolism in photoreceptors and creates glucose-deprivation sensitivity in cancer cells.
main_caveats: No metabolite, protein-activity, retinal, or proliferating-cell readout was present in this neuronal screen.
summary: The screen does not reproduce the strong GOT1-dependent redox liabilities reported in cancer cells or rods, so acute brain-neuron snRNA silence should not be read as systemic GOT1 safety.
why_it_matters: GOT1 inhibition may look transcriptionally quiet in juvenile postmitotic neurons while still changing metabolites, or while harming unassayed high-flux cells such as photoreceptors under complete deletion.

literature_claim: SNAP-25 is a neuronal SNARE-complex protein involved in synaptic vesicle exocytosis and postsynaptic functions.
main_caveats: The effect is a single gene with modest effect size and FDR 0.0903; it is best read as a candidate marker rather than a full synaptic program.
summary: Got2 produced a single weak downstream DEG: Snap25 was up-regulated only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The only recoverable FDR<0.10 transcriptomic consequence of postnatal Got2 loss was a synaptic-vesicle/SNARE marker, not a broad metabolic, redox, p53, or amino-acid stress wave.

main_caveats: Self-transcript depletion does not measure DNA indels or mitochondrial GOT2 protein; absence of downstream DE is transcriptomic only.
summary: Four neuronal groups showed significant Got2 RNA reduction without any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: The self-only pattern in Pvalb, central MGE GABA, midbrain glutamatergic, and midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA cells argues that a detectable drop in the Got2 transcript often failed to propagate to a stable nuclear RNA program in this P16 mosaic assay.

literature_claim: GOT1, GOT2, MDH1, MDH2 and mitochondrial carriers form the MAS, and neuronal Aralar/SLC25A12-MAS flux couples glucose metabolism to mitochondrial respiration.
main_caveats: Comparator signatures were also small and mostly restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; the contrast uses RNA signatures, not metabolite flux.
summary: Core malate-aspartate-shuttle perturbations did not phenocopy Got2, even in the matched thalamic group where Got2 had its only downstream hit.
why_it_matters: Mdh1 and Got1, both in the cytosolic half of the same shuttle, induced small amino-acid/ISR and synaptic-down signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Got2 shared no downstream FDR gene with them and Mdh2/Slc25a12 were essentially self-only there; the postnatal neuronal response is therefore node-specific rather than a generic MAS transcriptome.

main_caveats: Absence of these RNA programs does not exclude altered NADH/NAD+, aspartate, lactate/pyruvate, respiration, or synaptic physiology.

main_caveats: The conclusion is restricted to z-score RNA-profile similarity in the model-visible perturbation universe.
summary: The whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Got2 neighbor or anti-neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top positive z-score neighbor, Cacna1g, correlated with Got2 at only r=0.035, and the strongest named-gene anti-neighbor, Agtrap, at r=-0.017; none reproduced the Snap25 edge, so the weak Got2 surface is not part of a broader measured Perturb-seq module.

literature_claim: GP1BA/Gp1ba encodes platelet GPIbα, the ligand-binding subunit of the GPIb-IX-V receptor complex whose loss disrupts platelet adhesion and produces Bernard-Soulier-like macrothrombocytopenia in the correct hematopoietic lineage.
main_caveats: The screen did not sample megakaryocytes or platelets, DNA indels were not measured, and the Sst Auh hit shows that the surface is not a perfect zero.
summary: Gp1ba was almost completely transcriptionally silent in the postnatal NeuN+ brain assay: 21 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the only exception was one Sst GABA Auh call.
why_it_matters: This is an interpretable lineage-restriction result, not a failed-editing result: GPIbα biology is megakaryocyte and platelet biology, while the screen perturbed postmitotic neuronal nuclei after P16.

literature_claim: AUH is mitochondrial 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA hydratase in leucine catabolism and also has AU-rich RNA-binding activity.
main_caveats: Only one gene passed FDR<0.10, the FDR was 0.0607, only 34 perturbed Sst cells were assayed, and Gp1ba itself was not recovered as a tested transcript in this cell group.
summary: The one FDR<0.10 response to Gp1ba was a down-regulation of Auh in 053 Sst Gaba.
why_it_matters: Auh nominates a single mitochondrial leucine-catabolism/RNA-binding transcript as the only resolved Sst marker, but the absence of shared Auh regulation in platelet-lineage and data-driven comparators argues against a canonical GPIb-IX-V mechanism.

literature_claim: GPIbα acts in a platelet receptor system; GPIb-IX-V and associated platelet receptors are expected to be active in platelets and megakaryocytes rather than NeuN+ neuronal nuclei.
main_caveats: Same-complex targets Gp1bb, Gp9, and Gp5 were not perturbation targets in the parquet, so the directly tested comparator set used other platelet or megakaryocyte genes.
summary: Measurable platelet and megakaryocyte relatives did not phenocopy Gp1ba in neurons: Gp6, Itga2b, Mpl, and Gata1 each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their recovered neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation null makes a hidden neuronal platelet-receptor module unlikely and shows that Gp1ba is part of a broader platelet-lineage exclusion pattern in this neuronal screen.

main_caveats: Pearson correlations used all overlapping group-by-gene Wilcoxon scores and some safe-target labels had fewer recovered cell groups.
summary: Whole-transcriptome signature neighbors of Gp1ba were numerical rather than biological: the largest positive and negative Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon-score profiles were only 0.031 and -0.020.
why_it_matters: The absence of a strong positive or negative neighbor prevents over-interpreting the isolated Auh hit as a convergent perturbation module.

literature_claim: GPVI is a platelet/megakaryocyte collagen receptor in a FcRγ-dependent ITAM pathway, so neuron-intrinsic GPVI loss is not expected to drive a mature neuronal gene-expression program.
main_caveats: The assay did not include megakaryocytes, platelets, vascular cells, or DNA indel sequencing; absence of a self-transcript drop is therefore not a direct engagement readout.
summary: Gp6 loss produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq response in any measured NeuN-enriched postmitotic neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The experiment directly tested 21 neuronal classes after P16 CRISPR perturbation; all were null at FDR<0.10, matching the expectation that GPVI is a platelet and megakaryocyte collagen receptor rather than a neuronal transcriptional regulator.

literature_claim: Human GP6 deficiency affects platelet collagen responses and GPVI blockade is pursued as an antithrombotic strategy, whereas circulating platelets are anucleate derivatives of megakaryocytes rather than NeuN-positive brain nuclei.
main_caveats: AAV-PHP.eB CRISPR in juvenile neurons is not a pharmacology, vascular, platelet, or bleeding assay and cannot rule out effects in vessel-associated or recruited blood cells.
summary: This neuronal CRISPR screen gives no support for a neuron-autonomous transcriptional liability of GPVI inhibition.
why_it_matters: GPVI antagonists are being developed for thrombotic disease; a completely flat NeuN-positive brain response argues that any brain benefit or risk of GPVI blockade should be sought in platelet/vascular biology rather than in direct postmitotic neuronal reprogramming.

literature_claim: GPC6 is a glypican HSPG with developmental morphogen and astrocyte-linked excitatory-synapse functions, but those priors mostly concern embryonic tissues, astrocyte-secreted factors, or receptor trafficking rather than acute cell-autonomous transcriptomes of P16+ neurons.
main_caveats: CRISPR engagement was not measured by indel sequencing, and a flat Gpc6 mRNA does not prove absence of protein loss; the null applies to downstream snRNA-seq DE after sparse P16 perturbation.
summary: Gpc6 has a pan-tested postnatal neuronal null surface: every one of 22 measured NeuN+ cell groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: This confines acute Gpc6 loss to a buffered or off-axis state in already specified juvenile neurons rather than a broad nuclear stress or fate response.

literature_claim: Heparan-sulfate proteoglycans and their sulfation patterns regulate Slit/Robo, Wnt, netrin, and other axon-guidance systems, often with core-protein redundancy and context-specific glycan requirements.
main_caveats: Only targets represented in the parquet could be tested; several glypican paralogs and sulfotransferases were absent as perturbation targets.
summary: Measurable heparan-sulfate biosynthesis and Slit/Robo relatives did not uncover a latent Gpc6-like guidance module.
why_it_matters: If the dominant Gpc6 function in these cells were an acute HS-dependent Slit/Robo nuclear program, perturbing Gpc6, HS-chain enzymes, or Slit/Robo targets should have produced shared DE; instead all of those score correlations were near zero and the targets were flat or only one-to-two-gene responders.

literature_claim: Glypicans can regulate Wnt, Hedgehog, FGF, and BMP signaling, and GPC6 loss in embryos reduces Hedgehog signaling in developing long bones.
main_caveats: Ctnnb1 is a downstream Wnt effector rather than a Gpc6-specific receptor; Shh, Ihh, Gli3, and Sufu were not represented among the queried comparators.
summary: Wnt/Hedgehog/BMP/FGF receptor and effector perturbations did not phenocopy Gpc6, while beta-catenin perturbation demonstrated that this assay could detect a Wnt-linked thalamic transcriptome when it exists.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the Gpc6 zero is not because all morphogen readouts are invisible in snRNA-seq; rather, Gpc6 is not an acute upstream driver of those neuronal morphogen programs in the sampled postmitotic cells.

literature_claim: Astrocyte glypicans 4 and 6 promote excitatory synapse formation through AMPA receptor recruitment, and exogenous GPC6 can increase surface NMDAR function in differentiating human iPSC-derived neurons.
main_caveats: The comparison is to Grin2b loss-of-function, not to an astrocyte Gpc6 gain-of-function or extracellular GPC6 depletion experiment.
summary: The GPC6-NMDAR prior is not recovered as a Grin2b-like cortical DEG signature.
why_it_matters: Direct Grin2b perturbation produced a detectable cortical response, but Gpc6 did not alter the same cortical IT groups, separating astrocyte or soluble GPC6 effects on receptor surface function from cell-autonomous postmitotic Gpc6 transcriptional loss.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on Wilcoxon score vectors from all shared gene-by-cell-group coordinates, so it detects only transcriptional convergence and not shared synaptic physiology.
summary: The apparently closest data-driven neighbors are statistical non-neighbors, not a hidden module.
why_it_matters: The strongest whole-score Pearson correlations to Gpc6 were only about 0.03 and the strongest anti-correlations about -0.014, so the Gpc6 surface should be read as globally buffered rather than as a weak version of a known stress, nuclear-transport, ufmylation, or NMDAR signature.

literature_claim: Human GPC6 loss-of-function causes recessive omodysplasia, and GPC6-null embryos have reduced Hedgehog signaling in growing long bones.
main_caveats: The screen did not sample skeletal tissues or prenatal brain and therefore refines tissue and timing, not the established causality of GPC6 in omodysplasia.
summary: The omodysplasia/Hedgehog disease axis is not phenocopied by acute mosaic Gpc6 loss in juvenile neurons.
why_it_matters: The result separates a validated systemic developmental loss-of-function disease gene from an acute pan-neuronal transcriptional liability, and cautions that a P16 NeuN+ brain null should not be generalized to cartilage, mesenchyme, or embryonic morphogenesis.

main_caveats: DNA indel formation is unmeasured; the target transcript remaining flat is expected in this platform and does not itself prove failure or engagement.
summary: Gper1 loss produced no FDR-supported basal transcriptomic response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
why_it_matters: The biological result is a screen-wide zero: sparse postmitotic removal of this estrogen GPCR did not chronically shift neuronal snRNA states over 3-4 weeks, even though Wilcoxon discoveries were possible in all of the same coarse cell groups for other perturbations.

main_caveats: The similarity calculation intentionally used all Wilcoxon score vectors, because Gper1 had no FDR<0.10 genes from which to construct a restricted signature.
summary: The pre-literature nearest-neighbor search found no meaningful Gper1 expression module.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative score-vector neighbors were all within |cosine|<0.03, so the Gper1 zero is not hiding a reproducible subthreshold program shared with another perturbation.

literature_claim: GPER and ERalpha/ERbeta are all estrogen-responsive receptors connected to MAPK, PI3K and CREB-linked signaling and, for ERalpha/ERbeta, direct estrogen-dependent transcription.
main_caveats: Most related perturbations were themselves sparse or null, so this is a contrast across weak signatures rather than a strong shared-DE overlap test.
summary: Classical estrogen receptors and represented GPER effector genes did not phenocopy Gper1 in the basal neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: Esr1 and Esr2 produced only one to two FDR genes, Gnas only one, and Mapk1/Akt3/Pik3r1/Plcb1/Pgr none; the low cosine to Gper1 argues that the screen is sampling little tonic estrogen-receptor transcription rather than a specific Gper1-only downstream branch.

literature_claim: GPER1 is positioned in the mouse dorsal hippocampus to modulate synaptic plasticity and is linked to rapid kinase, mTOR, BDNF, Arc and CaMKII responses after estrogenic stimulation.
main_caveats: The assayed 012 and 017 groups are coarse and could dilute rare Gper1-expressing subtypes.
summary: Hippocampal Gper1 knockout did not recover the Arc/BDNF/CaMKII/glutamate-receptor program expected from acute GPER1 synaptic-plasticity work.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates GPER1's acute, synaptic role from a requirement for chronic maintenance of the corresponding mRNAs in postnatal hippocampal glutamatergic nuclei.

literature_claim: Published GPER studies place GLT-1 regulation in astrocytes and estradiol/GPER suppression of IL-1beta and TNF-alpha in ischemia-activated microglia.
main_caveats: The screen is NeuN-enriched and uninjured, so non-neuronal cytokine and glutamate-transporter biology is mainly outside the sampled axis.
summary: The neuronal Gper1 null did not engage the astrocyte or microglial injury programs often used to explain GPER neuroprotection.
why_it_matters: Absence of IL-1beta/TNF and GLT-1/GLAST changes is consistent with those effects living in injury-challenged glia rather than in baseline NeuN+ neuronal nuclei.

literature_claim: BARP/CBARP binds Cav beta subunits and suppresses voltage-gated Ca2+ channel activity and Ca2+-evoked secretion.
main_caveats: The finding is one DE gene in one neuronal class; Cbarp has no established direct biochemical connection to gephyrin.
summary: Gphn loss produced a single robust transcriptomic output: Cbarp up-regulation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: CBARP/BARP is a negative regulator of voltage-gated calcium-channel activity and calcium-evoked exocytosis, so the one recovered RNA change points to an excitable-membrane homeostat rather than to a receptor-subunit replacement module; this is a marker hypothesis, not a proven gephyrin mechanism.

literature_claim: Gephyrin and collybistin organize inhibitory postsynapses by clustering glycine and GABA(A) receptors, and gephyrin knockdown or deficiency disrupts those receptor clusters.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot count receptor puncta, distinguish synaptic from extrasynaptic receptor protein, or measure miniature inhibitory currents.
summary: The FDR-level Gphn surface uncoupled gephyrin perturbation from transcription of GABA(A), glycine-receptor, and inhibitory-synapse genes.
why_it_matters: The expected gephyrin phenotype is postsynaptic receptor clustering and inhibitory physiology; the dataset shows that this does not convert into altered nuclear abundance of Gabra1/Gabrb2/Gabrg2/Glra1/Glrb/Arhgef9/Nlgn transcripts after sparse P16 CRISPR in surviving neurons.

literature_claim: GPHN, ARHGEF9/collybistin, and GABA(A)/glycine receptor subunits act in one inhibitory postsynaptic clustering apparatus.
main_caveats: The global cosine values were near zero because Gphn has a one-gene FDR signature; the comparator result is a rejection of strong convergence, not evidence for opposite biology.
summary: Neither data-driven neighbors nor direct inhibitory-synapse relatives phenocopied the Gphn L4-5 Cbarp response.
why_it_matters: Gabrg2 was the third-closest global score neighbor but did not change Cbarp in 005 despite strong Gabrg2 self-depletion; Arhgef9 and Glrb were downstream-null. The comparison turns the weak Gphn signature into a sharper negative result: gephyrin does not sit in a shared snRNA module with its obvious receptor-clustering partners in this assay.

literature_claim: Gephyrin catalyzes the final step in molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis, which is required for molybdoenzymes such as sulfite oxidase and xanthine oxidoreductase.
main_caveats: Moco abundance, sulfite toxicity, and activity of molybdoenzymes were not measured; glial and peripheral Moco biology was outside the NeuN-enriched readout.
summary: Gphn did not trigger a molybdenum-cofactor or canonical ISR/UPR stress RNA response in the recovered neuronal nuclei.
why_it_matters: GPHN has a second enzymatic role in the final step of Moco synthesis, so a severe metabolic failure could have been visible as stress transcription. Its absence narrows the postnatal neuronal phenotype away from an acute cell-autonomous sulfite/UPR-like crisis under these sparse conditions.

literature_claim: Gpi1 catalyzes the glycolytic glucose-6-phosphate/fructose-6-phosphate isomerization and complete mouse Gpi1 loss is embryo-lethal.
main_caveats: The mRNA profile is from recovered NeuN+ nuclei only and does not measure indels, protein, enzyme flux, metabolites, or cell loss.
summary: Sparse postnatal Gpi1 loss yielded an almost origin-centered neuronal transcriptional phenotype: only two downstream genes passed FDR<0.10 over 22 measured groups.
why_it_matters: Gpi1 encodes a central glycolytic enzyme, so the screen separates flux essentiality from a durable nuclear stress response in P16-P37/44 postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: GFPT1 diverts fructose-6-phosphate into hexosamine biosynthesis, UDP-GlcNAc feeds OGT, and neuronal O-GlcNAcylation is important for neuronal maintenance.
main_caveats: The Gpi1 effect is a single small Ogt transcript decrease at FDR 0.0887; no O-GlcNAc proteomics or metabolomics was measured.
summary: Gpi1 exposed a small Ogt-down signal in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut without the Ddit3/Hspa5/Asns/Herpud1/Sdf2l1/Chac1/Pdia6 HBP-UPR program that Gfpt1 loss robustly triggered in the same group.
why_it_matters: Ogt is the O-GlcNAc writer fed by UDP-GlcNAc; the result says a central Gpi1 hit can touch the Ogt transcript in one thalamic class without phenocopying direct hexosamine-pathway collapse.

main_caveats: Full-vector correlations are necessarily noise-sensitive because Gpi1 has only two robust downstream genes.
summary: The data-driven Gpi1 neighbors were numerically near zero and failed matched-cell validation.
why_it_matters: Wdr26 and Alkbh8 were the strongest positive and negative whole-surface neighbors before applying priors, but Wdr26 did not share the Wdr43 or Ogt effects and Alkbh8 had no significant downstream surface; Gpi1 therefore has no robust convergent transcriptomic module.

literature_claim: Inherited human GPI deficiency is primarily a recessive hemolytic anemia with rare neurological impairment, and complete mouse Gpi1 nulls fail during early development.
main_caveats: The experiment did not assay erythroid cells, embryogenesis, glial metabolic support, chronic aging, metabolites, or severe survivor depletion.
summary: The sparse juvenile neuronal Gpi1 perturbation did not recapitulate the high-penetrance erythroid, embryonic, or rare neurological manifestations of GPI deficiency.
why_it_matters: The null surface argues that GPI-linked neurological disease is unlikely to be explained simply by a resting, cell-autonomous snRNA program in already specified neurons; systemic erythroid stress, development, unsampled metabolic partners, or enzyme-flux phenotypes remain plausible off-axis mechanisms.

literature_claim: GPI moonlights as extracellular neuroleukin/autocrine motility factor and AMF/PGI can signal through gp78/AMFR.
main_caveats: Secreted GPI protein and extracellular ligand competition were not measured, and unperturbed cells in the mosaic can provide ligand.
summary: Neither sparse Gpi1 loss nor direct Amfr perturbation revealed a mature-neuronal AMF/neuroleukin transcriptional axis.
why_it_matters: GPI can act extracellularly as neuroleukin/AMF, but a sparse cell-autonomous CRISPR design is buffered by Gpi1-sufficient neighbors; the measured flat Amfr surface further argues that AMFR signaling was not a dominant resting neuronal program in this assay.

literature_claim: GPR156 is a constitutively active class-C orphan GPCR that can drive Gi-linked cellular phenotypes, most dramatically directional hair-cell polarity.
main_caveats: The perturbation was not validated by DNA indel sequencing and the two positive genes are singletons rather than a recurrent module.
summary: Gpr156 loss produced an almost completely buffered postnatal neuronal transcriptome: only Zer1 and Kmt5a passed FDR<0.10 across 22 measured neuronal cell groups, while canonical immediate-early, stress, autophagy/lysosomal and synaptic markers were uniformly FDR-negative.
why_it_matters: This separates GPR156's strong receptor-level and hair-cell phenotypes from the consequence of acute mosaic loss in P16-specified NeuN+ brain neurons: the screen does not show a broad compensatory or injury transcriptome after Gpr156 perturbation.

main_caveats: Each cell group contains one corrected gene; no pathway-level enrichment should be inferred from either singleton.
summary: The only corrected Gpr156 downstream hits were split between two limbic glutamatergic groups: Zer1 was down in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and Kmt5a was up in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut.
why_it_matters: The sparse positive surface is not pan-neuronal and does not define a shared pathway; it suggests at most narrow limbic excitatory sensitivity embedded in an otherwise null brain-wide response.

literature_claim: GPR156/GABABL is homologous to GABA(B) receptor subunits and in hair cells signals through Gαi within a planar-polarity pathway.
main_caveats: The Gpr156 signature has only two FDR genes and Gnai2, Gnai3, Emx2, Gpsm2, Vangl2 and Fzd3 were not represented as perturbation targets in the parquet.
summary: Represented GABA(B), mGluR/CaSR, Gi/o, and PCP/Wnt comparator perturbations did not phenocopy Gpr156: none reproduced Zer1 suppression in 012 or Kmt5a induction in 017, and each had zero FDR<0.10 genes in those two matched Gpr156 responder groups.
why_it_matters: GPR156's two transcriptomic hits are not a generic class-C GPCR, GABA(B)-like, Gi/o, or planar-cell-polarity signature in this juvenile brain assay.

main_caveats: The correlation was computed on Wilcoxon score vectors with a >=100,000-feature overlap filter; it is a screen-internal metric, not a mechanistic association.
summary: Gpr156 had no strong data-driven signature neighbor: the best positive score-vector neighbor was Rxrb at r=0.029, while the strongest negative correlations were only about -0.011 and included safe-target controls.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation analysis rejects the idea that the two-gene Gpr156 response is part of a larger recurrent target module visible to this screen.

literature_claim: GPR156 is localized in the medial habenula; a p.Glu533Asp human variant was associated with depression risk and caused medial-habenula hyperactivity and stress-related behavior in a mouse locus model, while Gpr156-null phenotypes are curated for stress reactivity and tonic medial-habenula neurons.
main_caveats: The dataset cell group is coarse, contains only 54 perturbed nuclei for Gpr156, and does not measure stress-challenge behavior or membrane potential.
summary: The 145 MH-LH TH Glut group was flat for Gpr156 despite curated and humanized-allele evidence that GPR156 can control medial-habenula excitability and stress-related behavior.
why_it_matters: A lack of snRNA-seq DE does not argue against habenula electrophysiology or GPR156 mood genetics; it says that the P16 sparse loss-of-function perturbation did not create a large, cell-autonomous transcriptional state in this broad young brain group.

literature_claim: GPR158 is a CA3 hippocampal osteocalcin receptor and HSPG-dependent mossy-fiber synapse organizer, whereas CCR4-NOT controls post-transcriptional mRNA metabolism.
main_caveats: Single downstream gene at FDR=0.0956; Cnot3 up-regulation is not yet a full CCR4-NOT pathway state.
summary: The only robust downstream event after postnatal Gpr158 perturbation was Cnot3 up-regulation in the CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic group.
why_it_matters: This preserves a real, CA3-enriched signal in an otherwise buffered receptor perturbation and nominates CCR4-NOT-linked RNA turnover as an exploratory responder to Gpr158 loss rather than a generic GPCR readout.

literature_claim: GPR158/mGlyR regulates cAMP and neuronal excitability through RGS7-GNB5, and Gpr158 ablation alters AMPAR synaptic physiology and BDNF protein more directly than BDNF mRNA.
main_caveats: The screen did not measure DNA indels, cAMP, IP3, phosphorylation, electrophysiology, or behavior.
summary: Gpr158 loss was transcriptionally buffered across the juvenile NeuN+ brain: 22 of 23 measured groups had zero downstream DEGs at FDR<0.10 despite negative Gpr158 self-logFC in every group.
why_it_matters: A membrane GPCR/RGS scaffold can have strong cAMP, AMPAR, BDNF-protein, or synaptic effects without producing a standing cell-autonomous nuclear RNA program three to four weeks after sparse P16 CRISPR.

literature_claim: No prior literature nominates these genes as Gpr158 pathway neighbors.
main_caveats: Neighbor scores were computed on whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon-score surfaces and are dominated by a target with almost no FDR-significant downstream genes.
summary: The strongest unbiased positive and negative Gpr158 signature neighbors were essentially zero-correlation signatures rather than a hidden genome-wide module.
why_it_matters: The data-driven comparison rejects a broad convergent module and argues that the CA3 Cnot3 event is the only interpretable downstream transcriptional effect in this assay.

literature_claim: GPR158 and GPR179 are related orphan class-C-like receptors that recruit RGS7-GNB5 complexes controlling Gi/o-cAMP signaling.
main_caveats: Rgs7 itself was not a target in the parquet, and most compared receptor perturbations were also transcriptionally weak.
summary: Represented RGS7-complex, GPR158-paralog, class-C GPCR, and cAMP-pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Gpr158.
why_it_matters: Gpr158 cannot be replaced in this screen by its paralog Gpr179, by the assayed R7 partner Rgs6 or Gnb5, or by nearby canonical metabotropic-glutamate/cAMP genes; the lone CA3 transcriptional event is receptor-specific within a very weak DE regime.

literature_claim: CCR4-NOT is a multi-subunit post-transcriptional regulator in which CNOT1 scaffolds modules containing CNOT2/CNOT3 and CNOT7/CNOT8 deadenylases.
main_caveats: Only one CCR4-NOT component was significant; RNA stability and CCR4-NOT protein assembly were not measured.
summary: Cnot3 induction was isolated from other measured CCR4-NOT subunit transcripts and from direct Cnot1 loss.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-reading Cnot3 as wholesale activation of the CCR4-NOT complex while retaining it as an RNA-turnover hypothesis for CA3 Gpr158 loss.

why_it_matters: Ddx17 nominates a possible Sst-interneuron RNA-processing response to AMPAR perturbation, but as a one-gene, non-recurrent signal it is best treated as a low-confidence biomarker candidate rather than a pathway-level program.

literature_claim: NMDA receptors are major routes for synaptically coupled Ca2+ signaling to immediate-early transcription, whereas AMPARs primarily mediate fast depolarizing current and receptor trafficking.
main_caveats: The comparator programs come from different CRISPR targets, not from simultaneous Gria2/Grin perturbation in the same nucleus.
summary: NMDA-receptor subunits, but not Gria2, produced activity/synaptic transcriptional programs in matched cortical and thalamic glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: The screen can recover ionotropic-glutamate-receptor transcriptional biology when it exists: Grin2a and Grin2b affected L2/3 cortical activity and synaptic genes, and Grin1 generated a 126-gene TH Prkcd Grin2c response, whereas Gria2 was flat in the same groups.

literature_claim: GluA1-GluA4 form AMPAR tetramers and stargazin/CACNG2-class TARPs are AMPAR auxiliary proteins.
main_caveats: Gria4, Cnih2, Cnih3, Shisa6, and Shisa7 were not represented as targets, so only a subset of the AMPAR assembly could be tested.
summary: Represented AMPAR-core and TARP/scaffold comparators were rejected as strong Gria2 phenocopies because Gria1, Gria3, Cacng2, Cacng3, and Dlg4 were all nearly downstream-null.
why_it_matters: Flatness was not unique to GluA2: the AMPAR postsynaptic complex as sampled here behaved as a buffered electrophysiological/trafficking module rather than a module that drives steady-state nuclear RNA remodeling under basal conditions.

main_caveats: Correlations use all matched Wilcoxon-score entries; with a near-zero Gria2 vector they mainly quantify absence of a distributed signature.
summary: The full-universe Gria2 signature had no meaningful model-wide positive or negative neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top correlations, Tbx19 at r=0.0293 and Lhx4 at r=-0.0146, were tiny and themselves had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the matched surface, showing that Gria2 does not belong to a reusable transcriptomic module in this screen.

literature_claim: Human GRIA2 disease alleles can act by haploinsufficiency, altered gating/pharmacology, or rare gain of function, and Q/R hypoediting is a distinct mechanism that increases GluA2-linked Ca2+ permeability and neurodegeneration.
main_caveats: The assay omitted spinal motor neurons and non-neuronal compartments and did not measure Ca2+ flux, receptor rectification, dendritic spines, seizures, or cell loss.
summary: Sparse postnatal Gria2 loss did not recapitulate the transcriptional footprint one would expect from GRIA2 neurodevelopmental alleles or from Q/R-editing-driven Ca2+-permeable AMPAR toxicity.
why_it_matters: The null transcriptome is a warning against treating this assay as a GRIA2 disease model: much of the disease literature concerns development, altered channel gating, or unedited GluA2(Q), whereas this perturbation removes Gria2 after neuronal specification and reads survivor nuclear mRNA.

literature_claim: Jmjd1c encodes a Jumonji-family epigenetic regulator with H3K9 demethylase activity described outside neurons.
main_caveats: Single FDR<0.10 gene, no FDR<0.05 genes, and only 37 perturbed nuclei in the responding group; no recurrent Jmjd1c induction across AMPAR relatives.
summary: Gria3 loss produced a one-gene Jmjd1c-positive response restricted to 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
why_it_matters: The only FDR<0.10 downstream event preserved by the screen is not a canonical AMPAR trafficking or immediate-early gene; it nominates Jmjd1c as an exploratory marker of a small habenula/thalamic glutamatergic response rather than a broad GluA3 program.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed from Wilcoxon-score vectors over measured gene-by-cell-group entries; Gria3 has only one significant downstream gene, so neighbor ranks are driven by a restricted, low-amplitude signature.
summary: The full Gria3 transcriptional signature lies at the perturbational noise floor and has no strong positive or negative neighbor.
why_it_matters: A whole-surface search returned only tiny score-cosine similarities, including safe-target neighbors on the positive and negative sides and a broad Wdr26 responder as the strongest negative gene-neighbor; the data therefore do not support a reproducible Gria3-centered transcriptional state to cluster with another perturbation.

literature_claim: AMPAR subunits and auxiliary proteins form a trafficking-gated fast-excitatory-receptor system, whereas NMDARs are a related ionotropic glutamate-receptor class with different activity gating.
main_caveats: Several canonical AMPAR interactors, including Gria4, Cacng8, Cnih2/3, Shisa6/7/9, Grip1/2, and Pick1, were not perturbation targets in the parquet.
summary: AMPAR-core and AMPAR-trafficking relatives are buffered like Gria3, whereas NMDAR subunits Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produce detectable DE in the same universe.
why_it_matters: The expected paralogs Gria1 and Gria2 and auxiliary/scaffold targets did not phenocopy a larger Gria3-like program; conversely, the Grin1/Grin2a/Grin2b responses show that juvenile CRISPR perturbation of glutamate receptors can be captured by snRNA-seq when it triggers nuclear remodeling.

main_caveats: The tested gene set establishes absence at FDR<0.10, not absence of electrophysiological plasticity, receptor surface trafficking, or stimulus-evoked transcription outside the harvested basal state.
summary: Acute Gria3 loss does not activate a detectable immediate-early, CREB/BDNF, ISR/UPR, or autophagy transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: GluA3 is positioned at synaptic plasticity, but the P16-to-P37/44 mosaic loss-of-function did not propagate into canonical nuclear activity or stress-compensation transcripts; the primary missing axis is therefore receptor physiology and activity-gated trafficking, not an unobserved broad stress transcriptome.

literature_claim: GRIA3 encodes the X-linked GluA3 AMPAR subunit and rare GRIA3 variants can be receptor gain-of-function or loss-of-function variants with distinct neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
main_caveats: The screen does not assay human missense alleles, X-linked mosaicism, embryonic development, network-level seizures, serotonin/dopamine endpoints, or electrophysiology.
summary: The flat LoF surface refines GRIA3 disease biology toward variant- and physiology-specific channel dysfunction rather than a generic postmitotic transcriptional injury state.
why_it_matters: Human GRIA3 disease alleles include both gain- and loss-of-function receptor defects, so an acute mouse CRISPR LoF that leaves juvenile nuclear RNA mostly unchanged cannot be used as a universal GRIA3 biomarker or as a proxy for gain-of-function alleles.

literature_claim: GluD1 is broadly expressed and controls cerebellar, cortical, and hippocampal synapse structure and glutamate receptor signaling, with behavioral and human neurodevelopmental links.
main_caveats: The perturbation was acute and mosaic, DNA indels were not measured, and snRNA-seq cannot assay synapse number or electrophysiology.
summary: Grid1 loss produced no downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The dataset distinguishes GluD1 synapse and receptor physiology from a cell-autonomous nuclear stress or receptor-compensation program; a flat snRNA-seq profile should not be interpreted as absence of known GluD1 synaptic biology.

literature_claim: GluD1 and GluD2 have ionotropic-receptor architecture but act in neurexin-cerebellin trans-synaptic signaling that is mechanistically distinct from conventional AMPA/NMDA receptor pore subunits.
main_caveats: Comparator signatures come from separate perturbations in the same screen; the analysis establishes convergence or divergence, not direct biochemical epistasis.
summary: Delta/neurexin comparators were transcriptionally flat like Grid1, whereas NMDA receptor subunits Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced detectable cell-type-restricted signatures.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that the screen can detect some postsynaptic glutamate-receptor perturbations, but GluD1/GluD2 and neurexin organizer perturbations remain below a nuclear-transcriptome threshold.

main_caveats: The correlation screen used all shared gene-by-cell-group Wilcoxon scores; restricted comparisons are not meaningful because Grid1 has no FDR<0.10 downstream signature.
summary: Unbiased Grid1 signature neighbors had negligible whole-surface correlations and no reproducible significant signatures.
why_it_matters: This rejects the top nominal neighbors as mechanistic comparators and prevents over-reading the hundreds of nominal but FDR-flat Grid1 genes as a coherent module.

why_it_matters: The broad null surface is not a generic assay failure: most recovered groups are outside the cell and circuit context in which GluD2 is expected to organize Cbln1-neurexin synapses.

literature_claim: Grid2 loss perturbs Purkinje-cell parallel-fiber synapse formation, adult maintenance, and climbing-fiber competition, but those endpoints were measured anatomically or electrophysiologically rather than by snRNA-seq.
main_caveats: Only 36 Grid2-perturbed 308 CB GABA nuclei were recovered, the group is broader than purified Purkinje cells, and CB GABA does not assay the presynaptic granule-cell compartment.
summary: Even in 308 CB GABA, Grid2 loss did not induce a detectable GluD2/Cbln1/neurexin or AMPA-receptor transcript program.
why_it_matters: The expected biology is local synaptic adhesion and heterosynaptic competition, so the absence of Cbln1, Nrxn1/2, Grid1, Grm1, Dlg4, Gria1/2/3, and Shank2/3 RNA responses points to a morphology/electrophysiology phenotype rather than a broad nuclear program.

why_it_matters: If Grid2 loss had activated a stress, mitochondrial, or excitability module detectable by this screen, substantially larger correlations or FDR genes should have appeared; instead, the nearest stress-like comparator, Lonp1, induced a matched Ddit3 response that Grid2 lacked.

literature_claim: GRIK1/GluK1 is a kainate-family ligand-gated cation-channel subunit whose main known actions are synaptic and excitability modulation rather than direct transcriptional control.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation and receptor current were not assayed; a flat Grik1 mRNA row does not prove absence of protein knockout.
summary: Grik1 loss produced a pan-measured null surface: zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every recovered cell group.
why_it_matters: For a ligand-gated kainate receptor, the absence of a basal nuclear RNA program separates Grik1's established electrophysiology from steady-state cell-autonomous transcription in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic CRISPR assay.

main_caveats: The correlation was computed on continuous Wilcoxon score vectors; no strict FDR overlap exists because Grik1 itself had no FDR<0.10 genes.
summary: Grik1 had no substantive data-driven transcriptomic neighbor; the largest whole-surface score correlation was only r=0.030.
why_it_matters: The nearest mathematical neighbors should be read as null-profile noise rather than pathway convergence, preventing over-interpretation of unrelated comparators.

main_caveats: Grik2, Neto1, and Neto2 were not represented as perturbation targets; the Grik3 signal was only three genes and should not be treated as a full signature.

why_it_matters: The expected GluK paralogs and heteromeric partners did not reveal a hidden Grik1-like RNA state, pointing to KAR signaling that is either electrophysiological, developmentally buffered, or dependent on unmeasured GluK2/NETO combinations in this design.

literature_claim: KARs are structurally related to other ionotropic glutamate receptors but have distinct pre/postsynaptic and network roles relative to AMPA and NMDA receptors.
main_caveats: The comparison is at the level of transcriptomic response, not ion conductance or synaptic physiology.
summary: The screen could detect glutamate-receptor biology where it was transcriptional: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced FDR-significant activity/synaptic programs in Grik1-matched groups, whereas Grik1 did not.
why_it_matters: This is a gene-family contrast, not a global assay failure: NMDA-receptor subunits drove Nptx2/Scg2/Bdnf- and Vgf/Kcnv1/Npas4-containing signatures in cortical and thalamic/midbrain groups that were flat for Grik1.

literature_claim: GluK1-containing KARs have disease and therapeutic relevance and can control hippocampal GABAergic network synchrony and amygdala PV-interneuron maturation.
main_caveats: The conclusion concerns this sparse postnatal LoF/single-nucleus setting and should not be extrapolated to acute antagonist pharmacology or unresolved BLA PV subclusters without electrophysiology.
summary: A Grik1 CRISPR LoF allele gives no robust basal snRNA biomarker for the GluK1 programs pursued in epilepsy, pain, anxiety, or PV-interneuron biology.
why_it_matters: Small-molecule GluK1 antagonism or disease alleles may act acutely through channel gating in defined microcircuits; this screen warns that a negative whole-brain single-nucleus RNA signature cannot be used alone to infer pharmacodynamic inactivity or safety.

literature_claim: GluK3-containing kainate receptors are glutamate-gated cation channels with prominent neocortical/dentate expression and predominantly electrophysiological synaptic functions.

summary: Grik3 loss produced only a three-gene, cortex-restricted thresholded transcriptomic response: Amy1 down in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and Gdpd5/Kcng3 up in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The real recovered phenotype is a sparse marker response in two cortical glutamatergic groups, not a broad kainate-receptor or stress program.

literature_claim: Kainate receptors belong to the ionotropic glutamate receptor family, whereas NMDA-receptor calcium influx can drive immediate-early-gene transcription.
main_caveats: Absence is transcriptomic only; it does not test receptor current, gating, surface trafficking, or subcellular localization.
summary: The Grik3 response was uncoupled from canonical receptor compensation and from activity-regulated immediate-early/plasticity transcription.
why_it_matters: The assay could have reported compensatory Grik/Gria/Grin/Neto/scaffold or Bdnf/Nptx2/Vgf/Npas4/Egr/Fos/Jun changes, but none reached FDR<0.10 after Grik3 loss.

literature_claim: GluK1-3 can form functional kainate receptors and GluK4/GluK5 require co-assembly with a GluK1-3 subunit, so Grik1/4/5 were literature-obvious Grik3 comparators.
main_caveats: Grik2 and Neto1/2 were not represented as perturbation targets, and transcriptome similarity cannot exclude shared electrophysiological effects.
summary: Measured kainate-family relatives did not phenocopy Grik3. Grik1, Grik4, and Grik5 each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their recovered groups and no Amy1/Gdpd5/Kcng3 overlap in the Grik3 responder groups.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a shared postnatal transcriptional module downstream of individual kainate-receptor subunit knockouts in this mosaic screen, despite subunit co-assembly in the receptor family.

literature_claim: NMDA-receptor calcium influx is a well-established route to MAPK/ERK-dependent immediate-early-gene transcription in cortical neurons.
main_caveats: Grin2a/Grin2b are not kainate subunits; their large signatures are mechanistic contrasts, not expected one-to-one phenocopies of Grik3.
summary: The same dataset detects ionotropic-glutamate-receptor transcriptional output for NMDA subunits: Grin2a and Grin2b perturbations induced Bdnf/Nptx2/Scg2/Vgf/Npas4/Egr3/Kcnv1-rich cortical programs that Grik3 did not induce.
why_it_matters: This rejects the blanket explanation that postsynaptic receptor perturbations are intrinsically invisible to snRNA-seq; the Grik3 null is receptor-family-specific, not a universal readout failure.

why_it_matters: The sparse Grik3 signature should not be assigned to a confident shared pathway on the basis of cross-perturbation similarity; the top neighbors were weak and failed direct DE-surface validation.

literature_claim: Kainate receptors can act through synaptic ion-channel and non-canonical mechanisms whose primary effects are on transmission rather than on immediate mRNA abundance.
main_caveats: A self-transcript drop does not measure DNA indel structure or surface GluK3 protein loss.
summary: Sst GABA nuclei showed a significant Grik3 self-transcript decrease but no downstream FDR<0.10 response.
why_it_matters: This separates target RNA knockdown from downstream state change: measurable depletion of the Grik3 transcript was still transcriptionally buffered in an interneuron class.

literature_claim: Grik4/GluK4 encodes a kainate-selective ionotropic glutamate receptor subunit active at the hippocampal mossy-fiber-to-CA3 synapse.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not assayed; the flat Grik4 mRNA is therefore an engagement caveat, not proof of an inactive guide.
summary: Acute postnatal Grik4 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result separates GluK4 receptor biology from a broad cell-autonomous snRNA-seq program: even groups containing CA1, CA3 and dentate-gyrus glutamatergic neurons were flat after a P16 mosaic perturbation.

literature_claim: High-affinity GluK4/5 subunits require low-affinity GluK1-3 partners to make functional kainate receptor channels.
main_caveats: Grik2, the canonical GluK2 partner, and Neto auxiliary subunits were not represented among perturbation targets.
summary: The expected kainate receptor relatives did not expose a hidden Grik4-like transcriptome: Grik1 and Grik5 were completely flat, and Grik3 produced only three idiosyncratic FDR hits outside the hippocampal groups.
why_it_matters: GluK4 is an obligate high-affinity subunit that works in heteromeric kainate receptors, so Grik1/3/5 were the first comparators to test. Their matched null shows that this receptor module is largely uncoupled from the Wilcoxon snRNA-seq readout used here.

main_caveats: The neighbor search necessarily used sub-threshold Grik4 features because the FDR<0.10 signature was empty; it is a rejection test, not a source of mechanistic positives.
summary: Data-driven Grik4 neighbors were numerical only: the best restricted positive cosine was Kit at 0.183 and the best biological negative was Kcna1 at -0.116, with no shared Grik4 FDR genes.
why_it_matters: A top-500 nominal signature search failed to recover a coherent positive or inverse module, supporting the interpretation that Grik4 is an empty robust signature rather than a member of an unrecognized transcriptional cluster.

literature_claim: GRIK4 variation is linked to antidepressant response, and mouse Grik4 dosage or germline deletion alters affective, memory and excitotoxic phenotypes.
main_caveats: The screen did not model human SNPs, forebrain overexpression, germline compensation, antidepressant exposure, seizures or hypoxic-ischemic injury.
summary: The postmitotic LoF surface provides no transcriptomic biomarker for GRIK4-linked mood or neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
why_it_matters: Human pharmacogenetic variants and mouse Grik4 overexpression or germline knockout have behavioral effects, but their biology is likely allele-, dosage-, circuit-, or electrophysiology-dependent rather than a large acute nuclear RNA program after sparse neuronal LoF.

literature_claim: GluK5/KA2 is a kainate-receptor subunit with established synaptic and behavioral functions in mouse knockout physiology rather than a known transcription-factor-like regulator.
main_caveats: Functional DNA indels were not measured, and snRNA-seq does not assay synaptic currents or receptor localization.
summary: Acute P16 Grik5 loss was globally transcriptionally buffered: every one of the 22 recovered neuronal groups had zero non-on-target genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.
why_it_matters: The primary phenotype is a strong absence of a somatic nuclear RNA program, not a hidden cell-class-restricted response; this constrains GluK5 biology in postmitotic neurons after 3-4 weeks of sparse CRISPR perturbation.

literature_claim: Kainate receptors are tetrameric assemblies; GluK5 is a high-affinity subunit that functions in heteromeric receptors, with GluK2/GluK5 forming a 2:2 assembly and GluK4/GluK5 contributing to synaptic ionotropic KAR signaling.
main_caveats: The major GluK2 partner, Grik2, and Neto auxiliary subunits were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: The represented kainate-receptor paralogs did not form a shared Grik5-like transcriptional module: Grik1 and Grik4 were fully flat, Grik3 produced only three isolated FDR<0.10 genes, and all three had near-zero score correlations with Grik5.
why_it_matters: GluK5 acts as a heteromeric kainate-receptor subunit, yet acute perturbation of the measured kainate family did not converge at the cell-state RNA level; the receptor family is therefore not a single transcriptomic response module in this assay.

literature_claim: NMDA receptor and calcium signaling regulate neuronal activity-response genes such as NPAS4, whereas kainate receptors are often synapse- and microcircuit-restricted modulators of excitability and release.
main_caveats: The NMDA contrasts are target-level comparisons, not co-perturbations in the same nuclei.
summary: Grik5 was flat in cell groups where NMDA-receptor subunit loss produced robust activity/synaptic transcriptional signatures, including Grin1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Grin2a/Grin2b in upper-layer cortical IT neurons.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that the Wilcoxon universe can detect a glutamate-receptor-induced nuclear program, but this capacity is engaged by NMDA-receptor perturbations and not by the kainate GluK5 perturbation.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on signed Wilcoxon-score vectors and the Grik5 vector itself is almost entirely FDR-null.
summary: A blind nearest-neighbor search found only vanishingly small Grik5 correlations: the best positive neighbors were Drd4 and Notch2 with r≈0.04 and the strongest negative neighbors were Fbxo11 and Atp6v1e1 with r≈-0.04.
why_it_matters: The top neighbors do not rescue a latent Grik5 module; after FDR filtering, Drd4 and Notch2 were fully flat in the matched groups and the negative neighbors had unrelated sparse hits.
