literature_claim: GluK5 knockout changes mossy-fiber physiology and mouse behavior, and kainate receptor antagonists are an active therapeutic chemistry area.
main_caveats: No electrophysiology or drug perturbation was performed in this dataset.
summary: The Grik5 snRNA-seq null should not be read as a negative pharmacology result for GluK5/KAR antagonism.
why_it_matters: Kainate receptors are druggable ion channels with circuit-level physiology; a sparse nuclear transcriptome can be silent while synaptic transmission, plasticity, or behavior remains altered.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: Every conventional NMDA receptor contains obligatory GluN1 subunits, so receptor function should be Grin1-dependent wherever functional NMDARs are present.
main_caveats: Downstream DE is an unchallenged snRNA-seq endpoint and does not measure NMDA currents; the 151 group dominates the gene count.
summary: Acute postmitotic Grin1 loss produced an FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptome in only 5 of 23 measured neuronal groups, and 126 of the 131 significant downstream group-gene entries occurred in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The obligatory GluN1 receptor subunit can be detectably perturbed without forcing a uniform basal nuclear transcriptome; the dominant phenotype is a thalamic-Prkcd-restricted response rather than a pan-neuronal NMDA-loss program.

literature_claim: NMDA-receptor calcium influx activates MAPK/ERK-dependent immediate-early-gene transcription and calcium/CREB-dependent BDNF transcription.
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes passed FDR<0.10, with Bdnf just at the threshold; no protein or evoked-activity assay was performed.
summary: The midbrain glutamatergic Grin1 response was a two-gene activity module, Bdnf and Egr1, both down-regulated.
why_it_matters: Bdnf and Egr1 are canonical calcium/activity-responsive transcripts, so their selective reduction in 155 MB Glut provides the cleanest transcriptional readout of reduced NMDA-to-nucleus signaling in this screen.

literature_claim: NMDAR calcium entry couples synaptic activity to synapse maturation, dendritic remodeling, and plasticity.
main_caveats: Functional synapse number and channel physiology were not measured; pathway labels are inferred from a transcript subset of the 126-gene signature.
summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Grin1 loss suppressed a presynaptic, postsynaptic-scaffold, and ion-channel program while also decreasing the clade-associated Prkcd transcript.
why_it_matters: The strongest Grin1 state is not just an immediate-early-gene deficit; it includes coordinated attenuation of Erc2, Homer2, Lrrc7/Grid2ip, Vamp1/Unc13a, Kif17, Gabrd, and potassium/calcium-channel genes, consistent with remodeling of synaptic output and excitability.

literature_claim: NMDAR signaling can couple calcium entry to activity-regulated transcription, synaptic structural remodeling, and survival pathways.
main_caveats: Eif2ak3 and Jun alone do not establish a full integrated-stress-response cascade; this is a transcriptomic stress/growth hypothesis.
summary: The same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature up-regulated growth/plasticity and stress-linked genes, including Stmn4, Gpm6a, Tspan7, Scg2, Jun, Igf1, Deptor, and Eif2ak3.
why_it_matters: This mixed direction argues for an adaptive state rather than simple shutdown: NMDA loss in this thalamic class adds Jun/PERK-like stress and IGF/mTOR-associated transcripts on top of synaptic down-regulation.

literature_claim: SLC6A17/NTT4 is a neuronal synaptic-vesicle neutral amino-acid transporter, and postnatal interneuron GluN1 loss can have circuit phenotypes.
main_caveats: Single-gene downstream signature; the dataset does not show whether Slc6a17 loss changes vesicle content or Pvalb firing.
summary: Pvalb GABA neurons showed a single robust downstream effect, down-regulation of the synaptic-vesicle amino-acid transporter Slc6a17.
why_it_matters: The Pvalb result links Grin1 loss to presynaptic amino-acid-vesicle biology without a broad stress or IEG program, suggesting a narrow synaptic adjustment in fast-spiking interneurons.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Each cell type contributed one downstream gene near the 0.10 FDR boundary.
summary: 008 L2-3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP Glut and 145 MH-LH TH Glut each had only one non-target hit, Mfsd4a up and Bbx up, respectively.
why_it_matters: These singleton FDR<0.10 effects mark two possible low-amplitude responder classes but do not support a pathway-level interpretation.

literature_claim: Functional NMDARs contain GluN1 plus GluN2/GluN3 subunits, and GluN2 subunits differ by developmental expression, spatial expression, trafficking, and channel properties.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic; Grin2a and Grin2b were not measured in every group, and Grin2c was not represented as a perturbation target.
summary: NMDA-receptor subunit perturbations did not phenocopy Grin1: Grin2a and Grin2b were mainly upper-layer cortical responders, whereas Grin1 was dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and had no exact FDR overlap with Grin2a, Grin2b, Grin2d, or Grin3a.
why_it_matters: Same-receptor membership is not enough to predict the cell class or transcriptomic direction in this acute postmitotic assay; GluN2-containing receptors behave as gated, context-specific comparators rather than interchangeable Grin1 surrogates.

main_caveats: The cosine metric used only the 131 Grin1 FDR<0.10 downstream entries; Ptprd and Scn1b had high cosine but little exact FDR overlap, so the robust claim rests on Rab7, Vps54, and Wdfy3.
summary: Cross-perturbation ranking linked the 151 Grin1 signature to a data-driven trafficking/stress axis: Vps54 was strongly same-direction, Rab7 had the largest exact shared FDR overlap, and Wdfy3 was the strongest opposite-direction neighbor.
why_it_matters: The closest measured neighbors were not the textbook NMDAR subunits, indicating that the dominant thalamic Grin1 signature is shared with perturbations outside the receptor itself and may report a generic membrane-trafficking or neuronal stress state.

literature_claim: GRIN1 disease is clinically heterogeneous, and pathogenic GRIN missense variants can be gain- or loss-of-function at the receptor level, motivating functional classification for therapy.
main_caveats: A Cas9 LoF mosaic in juvenile mouse neurons is not a patient-specific missense model and cannot assign GoF versus LoF for variants.
summary: The sparse Grin1 LoF transcriptome and the Grin-subunit non-phenocopy caution against collapsing GRIN disorders into one basal transcriptional signature.
why_it_matters: Variant- and subunit-specific functional classification is likely a safer therapeutic guide than assuming that all receptor reductions produce the same cell-autonomous gene-expression state.

literature_claim: GluN2A is a postnatally increasing NMDAR subunit implicated in forebrain development and excitability, but prior work did not predict this exact upper-IT transcriptomic restriction.
main_caveats: The signature was sparse in L4-5 and based on 59 perturbed L2-3 nuclei; electrophysiologic responses in other groups could be invisible to snRNA-seq.
summary: Grin2a loss produced a real transcriptional response only in upper cortical IT excitatory neurons, strongest in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and weaker in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The DE surface maps a GluN2A perturbation to a narrow postnatal cortical excitatory compartment rather than to every forebrain NMDAR-expressing neuron.

literature_claim: Synaptic NMDAR and nuclear-calcium signaling can positively regulate activity genes such as Inhba and Ptgs2, and NPTX2/Narp is a secreted immediate-early synaptic protein; the direct expectation for NMDAR loss is therefore not transcriptional induction of the same module.
main_caveats: The experiment is chronic mosaic CRISPR, not acute receptor blockade or evoked stimulation, so the up-regulation is interpreted as a 3-4 week adaptation.
summary: The L2-3/L4-5 responder program was dominated by up-regulated activity-dependent secreted and peptide genes, especially Nptx2 and Scg2 in both responders and Bdnf, Ptgs2, Penk and Inhba in L2-3.
why_it_matters: A loss-of-function hit on an excitatory NMDAR subunit induced, rather than suppressed, several genes normally associated with synaptic activity and calcium-to-nucleus signaling, consistent with a compensatory rebound rather than a simple activity-off signature.

direction: mixed; mostly up with Plch2/Ptprd/Nyap2/Osbpl1a down
literature_claim: Activity-induced NPTX2 can remodel excitatory synapses through AMPAR clustering, but the specific Pcdh15/Cadm4/Sema4a/Rimbp2/Plch2 pattern has not been established as a Grin2a-loss program.
main_caveats: Several genes in this small module have broad membrane or adhesion annotations; no morphology or connectivity readout was taken.
summary: Grin2a loss in L2-3 IT cells coupled the activity gene increase to a smaller synaptic-organization and membrane-remodeling signature.
why_it_matters: The FDR<0.10 genes extend beyond one immediate-early marker and include candidates for altered input/output wiring and lipid or phosphoinositide remodeling.

literature_claim: NMDAR signaling is connected to BDNF through the eEF2/eEF2K translation branch, and MEF2 proteins are activity-regulated synapse-control transcription factors.
main_caveats: The Eef2 signature was much broader than Grin2a and the Mef2c/Kcnb1 overlaps were restricted-signature overlaps, not whole-surface equivalence.
summary: The top positive neighbors of the Grin2a signature were not NMDAR subunits: Eef2 shared 16 same-direction L2-3 coordinates, Mef2c shared 6 coordinates across 005/007, and Kcnb1 shared Nptx2/Scg2 in 005.
why_it_matters: The comparison ties Grin2a to an activity/translation/transcriptional state discovered from the screen itself and separates that state from textbook same-receptor membership.

literature_claim: NMDARs co-assemble from GluN1 and GluN2 subunits with GluN2 paralog-specific spatiotemporal and channel properties, and Grin2a-deficient cortical rat neurons did not compensate by increasing GluN2B protein.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and restricted to represented targets; GluN2C was not represented as a perturbation.
summary: The same-complex benchmark rejected a simple NMDAR-subunit phenocopy: Grin1 was flat in both Grin2a responder groups, Grin2b responded but was an inverse neighbor in L2-3, and other ionotropic glutamate/PSD comparators were flat or discordant.
why_it_matters: A GluN2A-null transcriptome should not be inferred from receptor membership alone; the closest measured paralog, GluN2B, did not substitute for Grin2a in this assay.

literature_claim: NPTX2/Narp is a secreted immediate-early protein regulated by synaptic activity and able to cluster AMPA receptors.
main_caveats: Secreted protein abundance was not measured; Nptx2 was read out only as a nuclear RNA change in two IT groups.
summary: Nptx2 was the strongest recurrent downstream marker of Grin2a loss, independently significant in both cortical IT responder groups.
why_it_matters: Because NPTX2/Narp is secreted and activity-regulated, it is the cleanest RNA candidate in this screen for tracking a cortical Grin2a-loss rebound state.

literature_claim: GluN2B is a glutamate-binding NMDA-receptor subunit with strong roles in developing forebrain synapses and calcium-dependent plasticity.
main_caveats: The screen perturbed postmitotic P16 neurons and measured resting snRNA-seq, so it cannot capture embryonic circuit wiring or evoked electrophysiology.
summary: Grin2b loss generated a real but sharply restricted response: 78 downstream FDR<0.10 group-gene calls across the 22 recovered Grin2b cell groups, with 76/78 in neocortical excitatory projection groups and only two singleton noncortical hits.
why_it_matters: The result localizes the postmitotic, 3-4 week transcriptional consequence of GluN2B loss to a narrow set of juvenile cortical excitatory neurons rather than to every cell in which Grin2b mRNA was detectable.

literature_claim: Neuronal Ca2+ entry and activity drive plasticity-linked transcription; Npas4 is activity inducible, Vgf is neurotrophin inducible, and KvS-family K+ channel subunits tune excitability through Kv2 heteromers.
main_caveats: Vgf and Kcnv1 were recurrent, whereas several immediate-early genes were significant only in L4/5 IT cells.
summary: The main neocortical Grin2b signature was a down-regulated activity/excitability module: Vgf decreased in L4/5 IT, L2/3 IT and L5 ET neurons; Kcnv1, Rph3a and Diras2 decreased in both IT cortical groups; and Npas4/Nr4a1/Egr3 decreased in L4/5 IT cells.
why_it_matters: These genes are precisely the kind of calcium- and activity-linked transcriptional effectors expected to move when a GluN2B-containing NMDAR input is removed, making the cortical response biologically coherent rather than generic CRISPR stress.

literature_claim: NMDAR signaling is not the main carrier of basal fast excitation but shapes functional and structural synaptic plasticity through Ca2+-dependent pathways and postsynaptic signaling partners.
main_caveats: The data are nuclear RNA; presynaptic active-zone transcript changes in the same nuclei are interpreted as secondary network or cell-autonomous maintenance responses, not direct localization of GluN2B to presynaptic terminals.
summary: In L2/3 IT CTX neurons, Grin2b loss repressed a synaptic release, active-zone and postsynaptic organization module containing Unc13a, Unc13b, Rims1, Erc2, Ppfia2, Rph3a, Dlgap2, Cttnbp2, Adgrb1, Igsf9b, Cabp1, Cacnb3, Nptxr and Sorcs3.
why_it_matters: The strongest single cell group therefore coupled the immediate activity deficit to a broader synaptic-maintenance program, consistent with NMDAR control of synapse maturation and plasticity.

main_caveats: Only Adamts2 was recurrently up-regulated across more than one cell group; other up genes are single-group observations.
summary: The up-regulated arm of the Grin2b response was sparse and led by recurrent Adamts2 induction in L2/3 IT and L5 ET neurons, with smaller cell-type-limited increases in Brd9, Arpp21, Sfpq, Mast1, Echdc2, Tbkbp1 and Gpr137c.
why_it_matters: This separates the dominant synaptic/activity down-shift from a much smaller candidate remodeling or compensation arm, and it argues against a broad neuronal ISR/UPR/proteasome program within the Grin2b responder cells.

main_caveats: The comparison was restricted to Grin2b FDR<0.10 genes; Psmb4 itself had much broader signatures and low perturbed-cell counts in several groups.
summary: A restricted 78-feature all-target search nominated Psmb4 as the top same-direction neighbor of Grin2b; it shared seven significant same-direction Grin2b signature genes, including Kcnv1/Rph3a/Egr3/Tyro3 in L4/5 IT cells and Cbarp/Pianp in the singleton noncortical responses.
why_it_matters: The top data-driven positive neighbor was a proteasome target rather than an NMDA-receptor gene, showing that the shared module is a small stress-sensitive activity/synaptic subprogram and not a wholesale receptor-complex phenocopy.

main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic contrast over the Grin2b signature genes, not evidence that Eef2 and Grin2b act in the same biochemical pathway.
summary: Eef2 was the top opposite-direction Grin2b neighbor: it significantly reversed 18 Grin2b signature features, including induction of Vgf, Igsf9b, Sorcs3, Diras2, Rph3a, Slc9a5, Kcnv1 and Unc13a where Grin2b repressed them in L2/3 IT cortex.
why_it_matters: A translation-elongation perturbation can push the L2/3 activity/synaptic module opposite to GluN2B loss, demonstrating that the Grin2b signature is directional and not just a generic vulnerability signature shared by all stressful perturbations.

literature_claim: NMDARs assemble from an obligate GluN1 plus regulatory GluN2/GluN3 subunits, and GluN2 identity changes channel kinetics and coupling to downstream signaling partners.
main_caveats: Grin2c was not represented as a perturbation target in this parquet; absence of shared FDR genes does not exclude shared electrophysiological effects.
summary: Loss of the represented NMDA-receptor relatives did not recapitulate the Grin2b cortical state: Grin1 had no significant overlap with the 78-feature Grin2b signature and concentrated its own hits in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Grin2a had a smaller L2/3 signature with two opposite shared genes and Grin2d/Grin3a were flat.
why_it_matters: The expected same-receptor relatives are therefore experimentally separable in this screen; the Grin2b phenotype is subunit- and cell-state-specific rather than a generic NMDAR-LoF signature.

literature_claim: GluN2B is embedded in postsynaptic signaling assemblies that include CaMKII and PSD-95/SynGAP-linked Ras-MAPK signaling.
main_caveats: Several PSD comparators had small or null signatures themselves, so this rejects transcriptomic phenocopy under this assay rather than biochemical pathway membership.
summary: Represented PSD/CaMKII-pathway targets, including Dlg4, Shank2, Shank3, Syngap1 and Camk2a/b/g, did not produce significant overlap on the Grin2b 78-feature signature.
why_it_matters: Directly measuring the obvious postsynaptic-density comparators prevents over-assigning the Grin2b response to a generic PSD scaffold program; the cortical signature is more specific to GluN2B loss than to every perturbation near NMDARs.

literature_claim: Human GRIN2B pathogenic variants cause neurodevelopmental disorders through multiple mechanisms, including gain- and loss-of-function channel effects, and objective target-specific treatment response remains unsettled.
main_caveats: The data come from acute mosaic mouse LoF and should not be equated to patient-specific missense gain-of-function alleles or germline haploinsufficiency.
summary: The measured LoF-like Grin2b state was cortical, activity-gene-decreasing and synapse-gene-decreasing rather than a pan-neuronal toxicity program.
why_it_matters: GRIN2B disease alleles include functionally diverse gain- and loss-of-function mechanisms; a LoF allele should not be assumed to benefit from additional GluN2B/NMDAR inhibition, and the relevant transcriptional biomarkers in this juvenile LoF context point instead to cortical activity/synaptic output.

main_caveats: Each claim rests on a single downstream gene, so no broader pathway should be inferred.
summary: Pianp in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Cbarp in 155 MB Glut were the only FDR<0.10 noncortical downstream responses to Grin2b loss.
why_it_matters: These isolated decreases are useful as candidate sentinels that a weak noncortical effect exists, but they also show that the high-cell-count thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic groups did not activate the multi-gene neocortical program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: GluN2D is an NMDA-receptor pore subunit with developmentally and regionally restricted expression; its best-established consequences are changes in receptor kinetics, Mg2+ sensitivity, synaptic current decay, and circuit excitability rather than an obligate cell-autonomous steady-state mRNA program.
main_caveats: True indel editing was not assayed; broad cell groups could dilute a rare Grin2d-dependent subnucleus or interneuron subtype.
summary: Grin2d produced no downstream transcriptional response in any measured neuronal group in this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic loss-of-function assay.
why_it_matters: The only adjusted Grin2d hit was the target transcript itself in Pvalb neurons, showing that a measurable target-row decrease can coexist with complete downstream buffering; this makes the result an informative electrophysiology-biased channel-subunit null rather than a pathway activation signature.

literature_claim: Functional NMDA receptors contain obligatory GluN1 plus GluN2/GluN3-family subunits; GluN2 identity gives receptors distinct spatial expression and physiological properties.
main_caveats: Contrasts are based on whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon signatures, not receptor currents; Grin2c and Grin3b were not represented as targets.
summary: Grin2d did not phenocopy the responsive NMDA-receptor subunits Grin1, Grin2a, or Grin2b, even where those targets produced thalamic or upper-layer cortical signatures.
why_it_matters: The same receptor complex was directly measured in the same analysis universe: Grin1 produced 126 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Grin2a and Grin2b produced 29 and 78 mostly cortical genes, but matched Grin2d groups had zero. The contrast argues for subunit- and context-specific NMDAR transcriptional coupling rather than generic NMDA-receptor haploinsufficiency.

literature_claim: GluN2D-containing NMDARs are present in PV/SOM interneurons, and PVI-specific Grin2d loss in medial prefrontal cortex can remodel inhibitory-synapse and schizophrenia-associated transcripts.
main_caveats: The screen pools Pvalb neurons across brain regions and perturbs sparsely; it does not isolate medial-prefrontal PV interneurons or delete Grin2d from every PVI in a circuit.
summary: The Pvalb group did not recover the published PVI GluN2D-to-GABAergic/schizophrenia molecular program after Grin2d perturbation.
why_it_matters: Conditional deletion of GluN2D from mPFC PV interneurons has been reported to down-regulate GABA synthesis, vesicular release, uptake, inhibitory-synapse organizers, and Nrg1/ErbB4/Disc1-related networks; in the broad 052 Pvalb Gaba screen group, Grin2d itself decreased but Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, Grid1, Cbln4, Nlgn2, Nrg1, Erbb4, and Disc1 all stayed non-significant after FDR correction.

literature_claim: Reported pathogenic GRIN2D-DEE alleles are missense variants that alter GluN2D-containing NMDAR function, frequently in early-onset epileptic encephalopathy, and recurrent gain-of-function mutations can show sensitivity to channel blockade.
main_caveats: A flat transcriptome does not rule out electrophysiological defects, seizure susceptibility, or effects of disease-specific missense variants.
summary: The screen gives little support for a simple juvenile sparse Grin2d loss-of-function transcriptome as a model of GRIN2D developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
why_it_matters: GRIN2D-DEE is dominated by de novo missense channel variants with altered receptor function and infantile-onset epilepsy; the absence of an IEG, GABAergic, or stress response here says that acute P16 CRISPR loss does not reproduce the transcriptional consequences expected from a constitutive or gain-of-function DEE allele.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Functional indels were not sequenced; 215 MB Dopa had no Grin3a rows and is missing rather than null.
summary: Grin3a CRISPR loss of function was a pan-measured-class transcriptional null: none of the 22 recovered cell groups had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result separates a lack of stable basal snRNA-seq response from knockout failure: the target transcript was measured but always non-significant, which is expected in an indel-based Perturb-seq assay where mRNA knockdown is modest and DNA editing was not directly assayed.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on a null query vector, so the important result is the absence of a high-magnitude neighbor rather than the identities of tiny rank leaders.
summary: The pre-literature signature-neighbor search found no convincing Grin3a module: the best positive and negative Wilcoxon-score cosines were near zero.
why_it_matters: The Grin3a surface behaves like noise around zero rather than like a weak member of a recurrent stress, translation, or synaptic module; data-driven neighbors such as Dap3, Eng, Manf, Hras, Pik3r1 and Mga were therefore rejected as biological phenocopies.

literature_claim: GluN1 and GluN2 form classical NMDARs, whereas GluN3-containing receptors are rarer, biophysically non-conventional members of the same receptor family.
main_caveats: The screen compared basal RNA consequences of acute mosaic LoF, not channel currents or evoked plasticity.
summary: Grin3a did not phenocopy classical NMDAR subunit loss: Grin1, Grin2a and Grin2b perturbations produced FDR-level signatures in matched neuronal groups whereas Grin3a produced none.
why_it_matters: This confines the negative result to the atypical GluN3A subunit rather than the receptor family as a whole; the assay can register disruption of core GluN1/GluN2 signaling, especially in cortical IT neurons and the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class.

literature_claim: GluN3A restricts GIT1/Rac1 and GIT1/mTORC1 signaling and can regulate activity-induced MEF2C-dependent transcription in stimulated developing neurons.
main_caveats: The screen did not stimulate neurons immediately before harvest and did not measure synaptic protein synthesis or phosphorylation.
summary: The expected GluN3A/GIT1/mTORC1 and activity-regulated IEG biology did not appear as a durable nuclear RNA program after P16 Grin3a editing.
why_it_matters: Arc, Fos, Egr1, Npas4, Bdnf, mTOR/GIT1 and UPR transcripts were all FDR-null, while represented pathway comparators such as Mef2c, Manf, Map2k1 and Mtor produced their own signatures; the Grin3a effect predicted by prior work is therefore likely local, translational, stimulus-dependent or completed earlier rather than a chronically altered whole-nucleus transcriptome.

literature_claim: GluN3A subunits can gate synapse maturation and long-term memory through synaptic mechanisms that remain relevant in selected adult circuits.
main_caveats: Disease models with aberrant GluN3A reactivation, behavioral training, or pharmacologic receptor modulation could still generate signatures absent from this unstimulated mosaic LoF screen.
summary: The flat normal-brain phenotype warns that basal neuronal snRNA-seq will be a poor pharmacodynamic biomarker for Grin3a lowering.
why_it_matters: GluN3A has been proposed as a therapeutically relevant brake on synaptic maturation and memory-related protein synthesis, but the normal P16-to-P37/44 CRISPR loss produced no persistent stress or plasticity RNA marker across forebrain and caudal neuronal classes.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Germline and Purkinje-cell mGluR1 biology predicts strong synaptic and motor phenotypes, especially in cerebellar Purkinje cells.
main_caveats: The assay did not sequence DNA indels and did not assay evoked calcium, TRPC3 current, LTD, or behavior.
summary: Grm1 produced no downstream DEGs at FDR<0.10 in any of its 20 recovered neuronal cell groups; even the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group, where the Grm1 self-transcript was significantly reduced, had zero downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This separates on-target RNA movement from downstream transcription and establishes the main phenotype as a broad basal-RNA null rather than a missed single responder.

literature_claim: Group-I mGluR activation can regulate ARC, c-fos, Egr1, BDNF, and FMRP-linked transcription through PLC/Ca2+, CaMK, MAPK, and CREB-related pathways.
main_caveats: The literature mainly measures agonist-evoked signaling; a baseline P37-P44 nucleus can miss short IEG pulses after synaptic stimulation.
summary: Grm1 loss did not alter activity-regulated group-I mGluR transcriptional targets or mGluR1-effector transcripts: Arc, Fos, Egr1, Bdnf, Fmr1, Homer1-3, Itpr1, Trpc3, Prkcg, and Grm5 all had adjusted P=1.0 across the 20 measured groups.
why_it_matters: A sustained basal CREB/MAPK/IEG or receptor-effector compensation would have been visible by snRNA-seq; its absence makes the null informative rather than merely a failed readout.

literature_claim: mGluR1 is physically and functionally linked to Homer/IP3 receptor and Shank/PSD-95 complexes, and Grm5 can operate through the same Purkinje-cell pathway when substituted for Grm1.
main_caveats: Several canonical genes, including Homer1, Homer3, Trpc3, Gnaq, and Gna11, were not represented as perturbation targets in the queried comparator set.
summary: Most represented mGluR1 pathway relatives and postsynaptic-scaffold targets were also flat in the Grm1-matched groups; Prkcg and Shank3 showed only isolated single-gene effects rather than a shared mGluR1-like module.
why_it_matters: Direct cross-perturbation measurement rejects a simple model in which acutely perturbing any member of the mGluR/Homer/Shank/IP3R/PKC assembly produces a common basal RNA state.

main_caveats: Cosines were computed from Wilcoxon score vectors and are useful for ranking, not for mechanistic inference when the query signature has no FDR genes.
summary: The strongest data-driven positive and negative Grm1 signature neighbors had near-zero cosine similarity and did not produce a shared FDR module; Wdr26, the only strong responder among them, responded in seven groups while remaining weakly anti-correlated with Grm1.
why_it_matters: The pre-literature neighbor scan behaves as expected for a null target: it supplies contrasts and rejects convergence rather than nominating a hidden pathway.

literature_claim: GRM1 disruption causes cerebellar ataxia through mGluR1-dependent Purkinje-cell signaling, and mGlu receptors are pharmacologically modulable.
main_caveats: The 308 CB GABA cluster is broader than purified Purkinje cells, had only 45 Grm1-perturbed nuclei, and the LoF screen does not model gain-of-function SCA44 alleles.
summary: Sparse postnatal Grm1 LoF did not trigger a persistent cerebellar nuclear transcriptome resembling mGluR1 pathway failure.
why_it_matters: For GRM1 ataxia and mGluR1 allosteric-modulator development, this warns that stable bulk or single-nucleus RNA biomarkers in broad juvenile neuronal classes may be insensitive compared with Purkinje electrophysiology, Ca2+ imaging, synapse-refinement assays, or evoked IEGs.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: mGluR5 loss or modulation strongly affects synaptic plasticity and behavior in germline, pharmacologic, and fragile-X contexts.
main_caveats: This is a basal neuronal-snRNA result; it does not assay DNA indels, receptor protein, electrophysiology, ligand-evoked signaling, or behavior.
summary: Grm5 loss was pan-null at the basal nuclear transcriptome: 22 measured neuronal groups each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.
why_it_matters: This establishes that the primary result is a bounded negative on the P16-to-P37/P44 snRNA axis, not a missed cell-type-restricted program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Stimulated mGluR5 can couple Ca2+, ERK, CaMK, and SRF to immediate-early and plasticity genes, including Arc.
main_caveats: Kumar et al. studied stimulated striatal neurons; the perturb-seq assay was basal CRISPR loss without an agonist challenge.
summary: Grm5 loss did not reduce an mGluR5-induced immediate-early or synaptic-plasticity mRNA program; Arc, Fos, Jun, Egr1, Npas4, Nr4a1, Bdnf, Dusp6, Homer, Shank, PLC/IP3, and mTOR/FMRP-axis transcripts were all FDR=1.0.
why_it_matters: The expected transcriptional arm of stimulated mGluR5 signaling was explicitly queried and absent, focusing the null on basal unstimulated loss rather than on failure to check canonical genes.

literature_claim: mGluR5 sits in a GRM receptor family and couples through PLC/calcium with Homer-Shank postsynaptic scaffolding.
main_caveats: This is a cross-perturbation count comparison, not shared-direction DEG overlap, because Grm5 had no FDR-supported DEGs.
summary: Most measured metabotropic glutamate receptor, PLC/IP3, PKC/CaMK, and postsynaptic scaffold perturbations were also basal-snRNA buffered, with Grm1, Grm6, Grm7, Grm8, Homer2, Itpr1, Plcb1, Prkca, Dlg4, and Shank2 each producing zero downstream hits.
why_it_matters: The expected family and pathway neighbors were measured and did not reveal a hidden Grm5-like module; flatness is a recurrent property of single receptor/scaffold perturbations in this assay.

literature_claim: mGluR5, FMRP, and TSC2 intersect at synaptic protein-synthesis control and fragile-X/TSC pathophysiology.
main_caveats: The Tsc2 program should not be treated as the missing Grm5 mechanism; it only demonstrates that related translational control can become transcriptionally visible.
summary: Tsc2, an mTOR-axis disease comparator, produced 636 downstream DEGs in nine groups where Grm5 remained flat; Fmr1 and Mtor themselves were close to flat.
why_it_matters: The Grm5 null is not explained by a universal inability of the dataset to see postnatal translation/growth consequences; sustained Tsc2 loss crossed a threshold that Grm5 receptor loss did not.

main_caveats: Neighbor statistics used Grm5 nominal p<0.01 rows because no FDR-supported Grm5 signature existed; all such comparisons are exploratory and were rejected as mechanistic evidence.
summary: The top data-driven Grm5 signature neighbors were all weak: the largest positive restricted cosine was 0.155 and the largest negative non-control cosine was -0.091.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation search failed to nominate a robust hidden phenocopy, preserving the target as a genuine transcriptomic null instead of forcing a pathway from nominal genes.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: mGluR5 negative allosteric modulators are a mature therapeutic chemistry area with multiple compounds advanced into CNS clinical trials.
main_caveats: CRISPR loss in mouse neurons is not the same as systemic reversible NAM dosing in humans; the finding applies only to transcriptomic biomarkers.
summary: Basal neuronal snRNA DE is unlikely to be a sensitive standalone readout for mGluR5 negative allosteric modulation.
why_it_matters: mGluR5 is a clinical CNS drug target, but this dataset says receptor loss can be biologically real while leaving no juvenile cell-body mRNA fingerprint.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: mGluR6 is the feed-forward metabotropic glutamate receptor of retinal ON bipolar cells and GRM6 mutations primarily cause ON-pathway night blindness.
main_caveats: The screen did not sample retina; indel formation was not measured, and the Grm6 self-transcript was flat as expected for this sparse CRISPR/snRNA design.
summary: Grm6 loss produced no FDR-level downstream transcriptional response in any recovered non-retinal neuronal class; 21 groups were null and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was only weak because Mbd2 stopped at FDR 0.119.
why_it_matters: This is a cell-scope result: the P16 mosaic CRISPR perturbation did not uncover a basal Grm6-dependent program in sampled brain neurons, consistent with the gene’s dominant retinal ON-bipolar role rather than a widespread forebrain or midbrain transcriptional role.

literature_claim: Retinal mGluR6 signals through Go and a GPR179/RGS/GNB5/TRPM1 postsynaptic complex, and Grm1, Grm5, Grm7, and Grm8 are mGluR-family members.
main_caveats: Several exact retinal partners, including Grm4, Trpm1, Gnb3, Gng13, Rgs7, Rgs11, Nyx, and Lrit3, were readout genes but were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: The represented mGluR-family and ON-bipolar signalplex comparators failed to phenocopy Grm6: Grm1, Grm5, Grm7, Grm8, Gnb5, and Gpr179 each had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and Gnao1 had only one.

main_caveats: The self-transcript decrease does not quantify functional indels; downstream buffering is measured only at the snRNA level.
summary: Significant Gtf2i self-transcript reduction can coexist with a downstream zero.
why_it_matters: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba demonstrate that the absence of FDR downstream genes is not simply absence of measured target RNA shift; these postmitotic classes are buffered at the transcriptomic readout.

literature_claim: GTF2IRD1/GTF2I act at promoters in embryonic tissues and the developing brain; Gtf2ird1 mutations can mildly affect bulk brain transcriptomes despite protein-level and behavioral consequences, and GTF2IRD1 can be autoregulated so mRNA abundance is not a direct engagement readout.
main_caveats: CRISPR indels were not measured; the result is strong for acute postnatal snRNA output, not for embryonic function or protein loss.
summary: Postnatal mosaic Gtf2ird1 loss produced an almost flat neuronal transcriptome: only 9 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 3 of 22 measured cell groups, and no cell group showed FDR-significant reduction of the Gtf2ird1 transcript itself.
why_it_matters: This converts the dominant observation from a generic negative into a timing- and biology-linked buffered response: a TFII-I transcription factor with embryonic brain and craniofacial roles left little acute P16-to-P37/P44 snRNA footprint in most postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Embryonic GTF2IRD1-bound genes are enriched for chromatin and ubiquitination mediators, and shared GTF2I/GTF2IRD1 targets include synaptic and reactive-oxygen-species-responsive genes.
main_caveats: Only seven genes passed FDR<0.10; several are not canonical neuronal-effector genes, so the module could mark a rare thalamic state rather than direct GTF2IRD1 binding.
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only multi-gene Gtf2ird1 responder, with 6 up-regulated genes, F11r, Sparcl1, Rab30, Abca3, St3gal5, and Gkap1, and one down-regulated gene, Cit.
why_it_matters: The thalamic response is small but selective and is dominated by membrane/extracellular and vesicle-lipid-associated genes rather than a broad TFII-I promoter program, nominating this thalamic population as the only place where Gtf2ird1 loss consistently exceeded the dataset FDR gate.

literature_claim: Developing-brain GTF2IRD1 targets are enriched for transcriptional and chromatin regulators.
main_caveats: Each cell group has exactly one FDR<0.10 gene with adjusted P values of 0.084 and 0.088; the singletons should be validated before being treated as pathways.
summary: Two additional Gtf2ird1 responder groups consisted of one up-regulated marker each: Cckbr in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and Smarcc2 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: These singletons are the only cortical projection-neuron and striatal/pallidal MGE GABA outputs in the screen; Smarcc2 links weakly to the chromatin-regulator class highlighted in embryonic GTF2IRD1 binding studies, whereas Cckbr is a cell-state biomarker candidate with no strong prior as a GTF2IRD1 effector.

literature_claim: GTF2I and GTF2IRD1 are paralogous TFII-I family members in the Williams-Beuren critical region, and atypical deletions implicate distal WBSCR genes such as GTF2IRD1 and GTF2I in behavioral and cognitive components of Williams syndrome.
main_caveats: Gtf2ird2 and several WBSCR genes, including Clip2 and Stx1a, were not represented as perturbation targets, so the comparison covers only represented paralog/disease neighbors.
summary: The represented TFII-I/Williams-Beuren comparators did not phenocopy Gtf2ird1: Gtf2i had a distinct 151 TH signature with no overlap among the seven Gtf2ird1 TH genes, Baz1b was nearly flat, and Limk1 was flat in every matched group.
why_it_matters: A related-target contrast is informative because Williams syndrome is a 7q11.23 copy-number disorder; this screen argues that acute neuronal LoF of individual WBSCR genes is not interchangeable with the embryonic, multi-gene dosage state.

main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to the nine Gtf2ird1 FDR vertices; the global Gtf2ird1 profile had no strong Pearson neighbor.
summary: The small thalamic F11r/Sparcl1/Cit sub-signature was reused but with different signs by unrelated perturbations: Zeb1 and Zmym2 also up-regulated F11r, whereas Brd4 and Rnpc3 inverted key Gtf2ird1 TH genes.
why_it_matters: This is a data-nominated convergence rather than a textbook pathway: it reframes F11r and Sparcl1 as markers of a recurrent 151 TH transcriptional state that several perturbations can enter from different directions, rather than as Gtf2ird1-specific readouts.

literature_claim: GUCY2C is a guanylin/uroguanylin receptor linked to cGMP-CFTR signaling, whereas Cacng3 encodes a TARP/AMPA-receptor auxiliary subunit.
main_caveats: Single downstream gene at FDR 0.086 in 47 perturbed nuclei; marker-like rather than pathway-scale.
summary: Gucy2c loss produced a single FDR-controlled downstream hit: Cacng3 was down in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, while every other recovered group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: CACNG3 is a neuronal TARP/AMPA-receptor auxiliary subunit, so the one recovered Gucy2c RNA phenotype points to a weak excitatory synaptic marker rather than recovery of the canonical intestinal CFTR or broad cGMP program.

literature_claim: Receptor guanylyl cyclases generate cGMP in localized signaling microdomains, and cyclic nucleotide abundance is shaped by PDE and cyclase enzymes.
main_caveats: Comparator signatures were themselves sparse; the conclusion is restricted to transcriptional convergence in this assay.
summary: Represented guanylyl-cyclase and cyclic-nucleotide comparators did not phenocopy Gucy2c in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: The Cacng3 decrease is not a generic consequence of perturbing receptor guanylyl cyclases or cyclic-nucleotide regulators in the same pooled assay.

main_caveats: The neighbor metric used all signed Wilcoxon scores and is dominated by weak, near-null signatures for this target.
summary: Gucy2c had no high-confidence global convergent module; its nearest whole-universe neighbors had cosine magnitudes near zero and included safe-target controls.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting weak score correlations as biology and shows that the one-gene Gucy2c surface is not embedded in a reproducible cross-perturbation module.

literature_claim: GC-C/GUCY2C acts in PMV hypothalamic and SN/VTA dopaminergic circuits; activation can promote anorexigenic Pomc signaling, and GUCY2C loss sensitizes nigral dopamine neurons to mitochondrial/ROS toxicity.
main_caveats: Broad recovered groups can dilute rare PMV cells; the dopaminergic cell group had no Gucy2c rows; no MPTP or metabolic challenge was applied.
summary: Postmitotic Gucy2c perturbation did not recover hypothalamic Pomc/Lepr or nigral mitochondrial-stress marker programs in the measured broad hypothalamic and non-dopaminergic midbrain groups.
why_it_matters: The negative surface refines neuronal GUCY2C biology to PMV and SN/VTA dopamine contexts and warns that this screen cannot adjudicate Parkinson-relevant dopaminergic protection because the Gucy2c 215 MB Dopa test was missing.

literature_claim: Cacng2 and Cacng3 encode TARP-family AMPA-receptor auxiliary subunits expected to act close to synaptic receptor trafficking and gating.
main_caveats: Flat Cacng2/Cacng3 self-transcripts do not prove absent indels; their null surfaces are still sparse CRISPR transcriptional readouts.
summary: Direct perturbation of the data-nominated Cacng3 target, and of its TARP paralog Cacng2, was transcriptionally flat and did not reproduce the Gucy2c-linked 012 signature.
why_it_matters: The result separates Cacng3 as a candidate downstream RNA marker from a Cacng3-loss state: lowering Gucy2c and directly perturbing Cacng3 were not equivalent in this postnatal snRNA readout.

why_it_matters: This is a robust negative result for acute single-locus H2ac8 loss in P16-perturbed, P37-44 NeuN-enriched postmitotic neurons; the absence extends to targeted S-phase, histone-locus, and p53-response genes that would have reported a secondary transcriptional stress response.

why_it_matters: This is a broad, dataset-level negative result, not a single low-powered zero: the assay tested cortical, hippocampal, thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain-adjacent and cerebellar neuronal classes and found no robust acute postnatal H3f3a loss-of-function mRNA program.

literature_claim: H3f3a/H3f3b provide the H3.3 protein pool and HIRA and DAXX/ATRX are the two major H3.3 deposition routes.
main_caveats: The screen measured mRNA, not H3.3 protein replacement, chromatin occupancy, or chaperone activity.

why_it_matters: If H3f3a-only editing is buffered in these postmitotic neurons, the buffer is not a detectable induction of the other H3.3 gene or of the major HIRA/DAXX deposition machinery in the 3-4 week snRNA-seq window.

literature_claim: ATRX acts with DAXX to deposit H3.3 at heterochromatic regions such as telomeres and pericentric repeats.
main_caveats: Atrx itself had only 11 downstream FDR<0.10 rows, and Daxx/Hira/H3f3b were not perturbation targets, so this is a restricted same-pathway contrast.
summary: Atrx, the only represented H3.3-deposition comparator, created a small FDR-level signature but did not phenocopy H3f3a.
why_it_matters: The ATRX/DAXX pathway can move neuronal transcripts in this dataset, yet the single-gene H3f3a perturbation did not move the same Limd2/Resp18/Csf2ra-centered response, separating H3f3a dosage from ATRX loss under the assay conditions.

summary: Data-driven signature search found no meaningful H3f3a neighbor: the strongest positive score correlation was Ndufb9 at r=0.033 and the strongest overall negative was a four-group Safe_target_58 at r=-0.017.
why_it_matters: A nominal H3f3a gene list is not recapitulated by another perturbation; the top computational neighbors are rejected as biology because their correlations are near zero and their FDR-level overlap with H3f3a is necessarily empty.

literature_claim: Pediatric-type high-grade gliomas carry H3F3A/H3.3 K27M or G34 mutations that dominantly rewire H3K27/H3K36 chromatin states rather than simply deleting one H3.3 gene.
main_caveats: The screen sampled NeuN+ neurons, not proliferating glioma-like progenitors or glia, used loss-of-function rather than precise K27/G34 missense editing, and did not measure histone methylation.
summary: Loss of H3f3a in postmitotic neurons did not model H3F3A oncohistone biology.
why_it_matters: H3K27M and H3G34R/V are dominant missense histone alleles in pediatric-type glioma; the absence of a neuronal H3f3a-loss response warns against treating H3F3A disease as simple haploinsufficiency or expecting H3F3A inhibition to phenocopy allele-specific chromatin poisoning.

literature_claim: HERC2 is a large E3 ligase with developmental and neurological phenotypes, but most prior phenotypes come from germline organisms or stressed cultured cells rather than acute P16 mosaic neuronal loss.
main_caveats: Each responding group has only one downstream FDR<0.10 gene; DNA indel engagement is not measured, and weak self-transcript depletion neither verifies nor falsifies knockout.
summary: Herc2 loss produced an extremely sparse but real P16-to-P37/44 neuronal transcriptome: Rack1 was induced in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and Dlat was induced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 20 other measured groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: This converts the screen from a simple null into a two-locus, two-cell-class response: HERC2 can be sensed transcriptionally in selected postmitotic neurons, but the acute response is not pan-neuronal.

literature_claim: RACK1 is a multifunctional scaffold at PKC/MAPK/Src signaling complexes and at the 40S ribosome with roles in protein synthesis.
main_caveats: The evidence is a single transcript in 60 perturbed nuclei; the dataset does not establish direct HERC2-to-RACK1 regulation or a full ribosomal stress program.
summary: Rack1 up-regulation was a private L5 ET marker of Herc2 perturbation: in that group Rack1 reached logFC 0.866 and FDR 0.0247, and no other tested perturbation made Rack1 significant at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: RACK1 is a ribosome- and kinase-scaffold protein, so this singleton points to a translation/signaling sentinel rather than to a broad DNA-damage or proteasome-collapse program.

literature_claim: DLAT encodes the E2 acetyltransferase component of the mitochondrial pyruvate dehydrogenase complex linking pyruvate to acetyl-CoA production.
main_caveats: Dlat is the only Herc2-significant transcript in the group; Uba5 and Cic have much broader thalamic signatures, so the comparison supports recurrence of the Dlat node, not global convergence.
summary: Dlat up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut nominated a mitochondrial pyruvate-dehydrogenase node as the thalamic Herc2 readout.
why_it_matters: Dlat was regulatable in this same group by only five perturbations at FDR<0.10 and changed in both directions—up in Herc2, Uba5, and Cic and down in Esrra and the Dlat self-perturbation—so the Herc2 hit is not an analytic orphan even though it is a singleton within the Herc2 signature.

literature_claim: HERC1 and HERC2 form the large-HERC subfamily, and HERC2 can allosterically activate E6AP/UBE3A through physical interaction.
main_caveats: This is a restricted endpoint comparison in two cell groups, not a complete protein-level test of HERC1-HERC2 or HERC2-UBE3A complex function.
summary: Herc1 and Ube3a failed to phenocopy the two Herc2 endpoint genes in matched responder groups.
why_it_matters: HERC1 is the other large HERC and UBE3A/E6AP physically and functionally interacts with HERC2; their flat 022/151 endpoint tests argue that the L5 ET Rack1 and thalamic Dlat signals are not generic consequences of crippling a large HERC ligase or the HERC2–UBE3A axis.

literature_claim: HERC2 regulates DDR and p53/MDM2 proteins under genotoxic stress, XPA turnover after cisplatin damage, FBXL5-dependent iron homeostasis, and germline neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
main_caveats: The conclusion is negative only for basal snRNA-seq in surviving NeuN-positive neurons; it does not rule out damage-induced repair-foci defects or embryonic HERC2 requirements.
summary: Acute Herc2 knockout did not activate the canonical DNA-damage, p53, UBE3A/HERC-compensation, FBXL5/iron, UPR/ISR, proteasome, or autophagy marker set at transcriptional FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: HERC2 is linked to RNF8-dependent double-strand-break signaling, XPA turnover, MDM2-p53 signaling, FBXL5/iron regulation, and severe developmental disease; their absence here argues that basal juvenile neurons are buffered against a broad secondary stress response for 3-4 weeks after mosaic Herc2 loss.

literature_claim: No prior literature comparator nominated by the Herc2 signature-neighbor calculation.
main_caveats: Whole-rank cosine over a nearly flat signature is intentionally conservative and is influenced by rank noise in the zero groups.
summary: Herc2 did not have a strong transcriptome-scale neighbor: the top same- and opposite-direction whole-rank neighbors were Tsc2 and Wdr26, but their cosines were only 0.0376 and -0.0266 and neither reproduced Rack1 or Dlat at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The lack of a high-cosine neighbor prevents a pathway assignment from being driven by the broad Tsc2/Wdr26 midbrain signatures and preserves Herc2 as a sparse, mostly private response.

summary: Hesx1 loss at P16 was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null across the recovered cell groups: zero downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 in 22 measured groups spanning cortex, hippocampus, thalamus, hypothalamus, midbrain/pineal-labeled groups, and cerebellar GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: The dominant result is not a local failed hit; it is a broad absence of postmitotic neuronal transcriptional dependence on an embryonic forebrain/pituitary homeobox repressor.

literature_claim: Active HIC1 is a BTB/POZ C2H2 zinc-finger sequence-specific transcriptional repressor whose loss should de-repress target mRNAs in a permissive cell.
main_caveats: DNA indels and HIC1 protein were not measured; the conclusion is limited to sustained snRNA-seq effects after sparse postnatal neuronal loss of function.
summary: Acute P16 Hic1 loss was transcriptomically buffered across every recovered NeuN+ neuronal class.
why_it_matters: A sequence-specific repressor should reveal direct de-repression if it is active and limiting; instead all 22 measured groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and no Sirt1 or Atoh1 de-repression, refining Hic1 biology away from a broad maintenance role in juvenile postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: HIC1 directly represses SIRT1, and HIC1 inactivation can increase SIRT1 to attenuate p53-dependent DNA-damage apoptosis.
main_caveats: The experiment did not impose DNA damage or aging stress, so it tests basal neuronal maintenance rather than the stressed cancer-cell state.
summary: The canonical HIC1-SIRT1-p53 DNA-damage loop did not fire in the young neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: Loss of a HIC1 repressor state can up-regulate SIRT1 and blunt p53-dependent apoptosis in stressed normal or cancer cells, but Hic1 perturbation left Sirt1, Trp53, and p53-response candidates nonsignificant in the neuronal DE surface, and Trp53 perturbation itself was flat in matched groups.

literature_claim: Hic1 cooperates with Ptch1 in medulloblastoma and directly represses Atoh1 in the cerebellar granule-neuron-progenitor tumor context.
main_caveats: Granule-neuron progenitors and medulloblastoma initiation were not sampled, so absence in CB GABA should not be read as absence in the SHH-responsive lineage.
summary: The Hic1-Ptch1-Atoh1 medulloblastoma axis is absent from the sampled postmitotic neuronal compartment.
why_it_matters: Hic1 loss did not de-repress Atoh1, the only cerebellar group was CB GABA rather than granule-neuron progenitors, and Atoh1/Ptch1/Smo/Gli1 perturbations were null or singleton in matched groups; the tumor-suppressor circuit therefore maps to an earlier SHH-responsive progenitor lineage, not to young NeuN+ neurons.

literature_claim: HIC1 can attenuate Wnt output through TCF-4/beta-catenin and can use CtBP or NuRD corepressor complexes on target genes.
main_caveats: These are pathway neighbors and cofactors, not Hic1 paralogs; divergence need not mean biochemical independence at all loci.
summary: Wnt/chromatin perturbations were detectable where Hic1 was flat, rejecting a simple phenocopy with Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Chd4, Arid1a, or Ctbp1.
why_it_matters: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed hundreds of DE genes for Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, and Chd4 and smaller Arid1a/Ctbp1 responses, whereas Hic1 had zero; the absence of Hic1 signal is therefore not because beta-catenin/TCF or NuRD-like transcriptional programs are generically invisible in this analysis.

main_caveats: Because Hic1 itself is flat, nearest-neighbor ranking is inherently noise-dominated and was used only to reject convergence.
summary: Hic1 had no meaningful data-driven signature neighbors beyond other null-like perturbations.
why_it_matters: The strongest whole-surface correlations were only r≈0.03 or weaker and the nearest neighbors had no coherent DE surface, so cross-perturbation comparison did not reveal a hidden Hic1 downstream module.

why_it_matters: A direct HIF1A partner did not reveal a hidden postmitotic neuronal ARNT-dependent state, supporting stimulus gating rather than a Hif1a-only anomaly.

main_caveats: The comparison used whole-surface Wilcoxon-score correlations even though Hif1a itself had no robust FDR<0.10 genes.

why_it_matters: The best positive and negative neighbors were all near r=0, so there is no data-driven alternate pathway hiding under the canonical HIF prior.

why_it_matters: This turns a screen-wide flat profile into a biological boundary: the HIVEP1 transcription factor is not sufficient to drive a cell-autonomous basal neuronal program 3-4 weeks after P16 perturbation.

literature_claim: HIVEP1 loss amplifies TLR/NF-κB cytokine expression in monocytes/macrophages, while germline Schnurri-2/Hivep2 deficiency in mouse brain is associated with GFAP, complement, MHC, and other inflammatory signatures.
main_caveats: The glial markers test for a program contaminating or secondarily induced in NeuN+ nuclei; astrocytes and microglia themselves were largely not sampled.
summary: The expected NF-κB, cytokine, complement/MHC, and glial-inflammatory readouts were absent after Hivep1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Because the expected output of HIVEP1 loss is transcriptional and these sentinel transcripts were tested, their complete FDR failure indicates contextual uncoupling of Hivep1 from inflammatory NF-κB in this neuronal assay rather than a snRNA-seq readout mismatch.

literature_claim: HIVEP1, HIVEP2, and HIVEP3 are related ZAS-family transcription factors; HIVEP2 loss is a neurodevelopmental-disease mechanism and germline Schnurri-2 deficiency perturbs inflammatory and neuronal markers in mouse brain.
main_caveats: Hivep3 had only singleton hits, and equivalent DNA editing across the three HIVEP paralogs was not measured.
summary: The two measured HIVEP paralogs did not phenocopy Hivep1 in matched neurons: Hivep2 was fully flat and Hivep3 yielded only two isolated singleton DE genes.
why_it_matters: A κB/ZAS family prior would have made Hivep2 and Hivep3 the obvious comparators, yet their score-vector correlations to Hivep1 were approximately zero; the postnatal neuronal HIVEP-family surface is therefore dominated by non-convergence, not interchangeable single-gene paralog activity.

literature_claim: The reported HIVEP1 phenotype is coupled to TLR2/TLR4 agonists and MyD88/TRAF6-driven NF-κB activation.
main_caveats: Only Tlr2, Tlr4, Chuk, Nfkb1, and Rel among the obvious pathway nodes were represented; Tlr4 was recovered in 20 of the 22 Hivep1-matched groups.
summary: Perturbing represented TLR/NF-κB neighbors also failed to reveal a Hivep1-like response.
why_it_matters: The flat Tlr2, Tlr4, Chuk, Nfkb1, and Rel surfaces argue that the pathway containing HIVEP1's canonical immune targets is largely quiescent in unstimulated postmitotic neurons in this screen.

main_caveats: Correlations used Wilcoxon score vectors over matched tested genes and groups; they should not be interpreted as mechanistic links.
summary: The unbiased cross-perturbation search found no meaningful positive or negative Hivep1 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top score-vector neighbor across 1,772 other target profiles correlated with Hivep1 at only r=0.0319, putting quantitative support behind the visual conclusion that Hivep1 is a near-zero vector rather than an unrecognized member of another strong transcriptomic module.

literature_claim: Human HIVEP2 loss of function causes neurodevelopmental disease and germline Shn-2 knockout mice have broad brain molecular and behavioral phenotypes.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured and the assay was acute, sparse, NeuN-enriched, and postmitotic.
summary: Hivep2 produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes across all 22 measured neuronal cell groups despite one significant on-target mRNA decrease in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: This is a strong acute neuron-autonomous negative result: the canonical disease gene is not an immediate basal transcriptional regulator in these postmitotic P16-edited nuclei.

literature_claim: MIBP1/HIVEP2 represses NF-κB targets, and germline Shn-2 knockout brain up-regulates NF-κB-responsive, complement, MHC, and astrocytic genes.
main_caveats: Sparse NeuN+ nuclei cannot test whether edited neurons would recruit astrocytes or microglia in a tissue-wide knockout.
summary: The NF-κB, complement, MHC, and astrocyte-response program expected from germline Schnurri-2 deficiency was absent from Hivep2-perturbed neuronal nuclei.
why_it_matters: The result separates a chronic glial/tissue inflammatory consequence of full Shn-2 loss from the direct transcriptional output of acute Hivep2 loss inside single neurons.

literature_claim: MIBP1 regulates Sstr2 and Myc in prior molecular studies, and Shn-2 knockout mice show altered DG maturation, Arc induction, parvalbumin/GAD67, and CNPase phenotypes.
main_caveats: The screen used basal snRNA-seq rather than immunostaining, electrophysiology, or activity induction.
summary: Sstr2, Myc, Arc, dentate granule-cell maturation markers, and inhibitory markers were all flat after Hivep2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Direct MIBP1 target candidates and the strongest Shn-2 KO neuronal markers are not acutely reset by P16 Hivep2 editing, arguing against a rapid cell-autonomous version of the immature-dentate phenotype.

literature_claim: HIVEP proteins are κB-site-binding ZAS transcription factors connected to NF-κB regulation.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic only and does not test stimulus-evoked NF-κB signaling.
summary: Hivep1, Hivep3, Nfkb1, and Chuk did not converge with Hivep2: the two paralogs and two NF-κB-side perturbations were flat or nearly flat with score correlations from 0.0005 to 0.0066 for the main flat comparators.
why_it_matters: The family/pathway relation was directly measurable and rejected; κB-binding membership alone is not sufficient to create a shared acute neuronal transcriptome in this dataset.

literature_claim: OGT modulates MIBP1 repression of NF-κB targets, and Shn-2 germline KO shares immature-dentate features with other kinase/phosphatase mouse models.
main_caveats: These are pathway or phenotype neighbors rather than same-complex members; lack of convergence is therefore directional but not a biochemical contradiction.
summary: Ogt and immature-dentate comparators such as Camk2a, Ppp3ca, Ppp3r1, and Ntrk2 did not phenocopy Hivep2; Ogt was a broad responder with 2154 FDR<0.10 genes whereas Hivep2 remained flat.
why_it_matters: A molecule reported to modulate MIBP1 and genes belonging to phenotypically related iDG models can be active in the same analysis universe without converging on Hivep2.

main_caveats: Neighbors were ranked by global Wilcoxon-score correlation over a flat Hivep2 vector, so they are useful mainly as negative controls for convergence.
summary: The data-driven top Hivep2 neighbors were near-zero full-vector correlations; the positive neighbors Unc5c, Erbb4, and Mbd5 and the negative neighbors Safe_target_81, Fbxo11, and Eef2 did not share any FDR genes with Hivep2.
why_it_matters: The pre-literature nearest-neighbor calculation found no hidden convergent module and showed that a strong responder, Eef2, can be recovered with comparable cell counts.

literature_claim: HIVEP3 is a κB-binding HIVEP/ZAS transcription factor and an ASD candidate, but the prior record does not predict that acute P16 loss should specifically up-regulate Sorbs2 in hypothalamic GABA cells and R3hdm2 in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells.
main_caveats: Both responding groups contain only a single FDR<0.10 downstream gene, and the Hivep3 transcript itself was not depleted at the RNA level.
summary: Hivep3 loss produced only two downstream FDR<0.10 genes across 23 measured neuronal groups: Sorbs2 was up in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and R3hdm2 was up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: This converts an otherwise near-null transcription-factor perturbation into a sharply restricted neuronal response, and separates the two real responders from the 21 groups with no corrected downstream signal.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation was necessarily restricted to the two Hivep3 significant coordinates; only R3hdm2, not a multi-gene program, overlaps at FDR<0.10.
summary: The R3hdm2-up coordinate in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut recurred in Tm2d1, Huwe1, Lrrtm1 and Gabrb2 perturbations; Tm2d1, Huwe1 and Lrrtm1 were the top three positive neighbors of the restricted Hivep3 two-gene signature.
why_it_matters: Direct cross-perturbation overlap shows that the stronger Hivep3 hit lies on a repeatedly inducible thalamic axis, but not on a Hivep3-specific or HIVEP-family-specific module.

main_caveats: The two broad negative comparators have much larger signatures than Hivep3, so the contrast is coordinate-level rather than a full phenocopy.
summary: The restricted Hivep3 signature is opposed by Sin3a, Wdr26 and Ogt: Sin3a and Wdr26 significantly down-regulate R3hdm2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Ogt significantly down-regulates Sorbs2 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: The negative-neighbor result indicates that the two Hivep3 marker coordinates can move in both directions in the screen, so the Hivep3 singleton hits should not be dismissed as invariant marker-gene artifacts.

literature_claim: HIVEP1/2/3 are a κB-binding ZAS family, while SHN3/HIVEP3 connects to BMP/Runx2 osteoblast biology; these relationships nominate same-family and BMP-pathway targets as obvious comparators.
main_caveats: TRAF2 and WWP1, two direct literature interactors, were not present as perturbation targets and therefore could not be tested.
summary: Hivep1, Hivep2, the recovered NF-κB perturbations Nfkb1, Rel and Chuk, and the BMP/Runx2 perturbations Runx2, Bmpr1a, Smad1, Smad4 and Smad9 did not reproduce the Hivep3 Sorbs2/R3hdm2 response.
why_it_matters: This rejects the most obvious HIVEP paralog and canonical pathway phenocopies inside the same DE universe, making the Hivep3 neuronal response look idiosyncratic rather than a generic HIVEP, NF-κB or BMP effect.

literature_claim: HIVEP3/KRC participates in TNF-receptor signaling and SHN3/HIVEP3 controls Runx2 and Alg2-linked osteoblast/chondrocyte differentiation in non-neuronal systems.
main_caveats: Very lowly expressed cytokine or matrix genes are not individually informative, but the expressed immediate-response and BMP/Id checks were also FDR-flat.
summary: Hivep3 loss did not induce or repress the expected NF-κB/TNF, Runx2/Alg2/BMP, Id or chondrogenic ER-response genes at FDR<0.10 anywhere in the neuronal surface.
why_it_matters: The absence is mechanistically interpretable: the two neuronal Hivep3 hits are not a hidden osteoblast-like differentiation signature and are not accompanied by a detectable inflammatory NF-κB program.

literature_claim: Sorbs2 encodes neuronal nArgBP2, which colocalizes with F-actin at dendritic spines and growth cones and is required for dendritic complexity and excitatory synaptic transmission in mouse neurons.
main_caveats: The association to Hivep3 is based on one borderline FDR=0.051 gene and should be used as a marker hypothesis rather than a mechanism.
summary: Sorbs2 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA nominates a hypothalamic GABAergic actin-synaptic scaffold marker after Hivep3 loss.
why_it_matters: Sorbs2/nArgBP2 is a neuronal dendritic-spine and growth-cone scaffold, so its isolated induction is the most biologically legible Hivep3-positive gene even though it is not sufficient to call a broad cytoskeletal program.

literature_claim: HK1 phosphorylates glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, is prominent in brain, and localizes to the outer mitochondrial membrane through VDAC-associated biology.
main_caveats: No DNA indel, HK1 protein, ATP, glucose-6-phosphate, or apoptosis readout was made; the average CRISPR mRNA effect in this platform is partial, and target transcript remaining in a nucleus is not evidence that no frameshift occurred.
summary: Hk1 loss-of-function was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null in the assayed postmitotic brain: no measured cell group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: HK1 is the canonical brain glucose-phosphorylating, VDAC-associated hexokinase, so the screen strongly argues against a chronic glycolytic, ISR/autophagy, mitochondrial-apoptosis, or synaptic mRNA program in P16-edited neuronal survivors; the claim is limited to transcript abundance, not ATP, glucose-6-phosphate, or indel status.

literature_claim: Dominant HK1 neurodevelopmental disorder is caused by recurrent monoallelic missense variants that likely perturb product inhibition and cause gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, while truncating alleles are seen in population data.
main_caveats: The screen did not install the disease missense alleles and did not assay embryonic brain, retina, CSF metabolites, or progressive degeneration.
summary: The Hk1 LoF surface does not support simple haploinsufficiency as a strong postnatal neuronal transcriptional mechanism for dominant HK1 neurodevelopmental disease.
why_it_matters: The only group with robust Hk1 self-transcript reduction, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, still had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes; that agrees with clinical genetics placing NEDVIBA variants at recurrent regulatory hot spots with likely gain-of-function behavior rather than ordinary truncating loss.

why_it_matters: The contrast separates buffered early glucose phosphorylation from a transcriptionally visible hexosamine/O-GlcNAc effector: Gpi1, Tpi1, Pfkm, Eno1, and Slc2a1 were flat or nearly flat like Hk1, but Ogt produced 2,154 FDR<0.10 downstream genes across matching groups.

main_caveats: Cosines were computed on mostly null Hk1 Wilcoxon scores; they are useful for rejecting convergence, not for assigning mechanism.

literature_claim: HK1 mutations cause severe red-cell hexokinase deficiency, and monoallelic recurrent HK1 variants cause a neurodevelopmental syndrome with visual defects and brain anomalies.
main_caveats: The dataset was not a drug-exposure experiment and did not sample erythrocytes, retina, astrocytes, olfactory bulb, hindbrain, or non-neuronal brain cells.
summary: A quiet neuronal snRNA-seq surface does not de-risk HK1 inhibition.
why_it_matters: The screen excludes blood and retina and measures mRNA in surviving NeuN+ nuclei, while HK1 deficiency is a severe erythroid enzyme disease and dominant HK1 brain disease is allele-specific. Therapeutic strategies that reduce HK1 activity should therefore be judged with metabolic, retinal, and hematologic assays rather than by this neuronal null alone.

literature_claim: HLCS loss impairs multiple biotin-dependent carboxylases and can also perturb chromatin-associated gene regulation, causing severe multiple-carboxylase deficiency under global loss.
main_caveats: DNA editing, protein biotinylation, enzyme activity, and metabolites were unmeasured; the result is restricted to sparse postnatal neuronal nuclei.
summary: Hlcs perturbation is pan-null across the 23 recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups, with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and no FDR-significant induction of monitored carboxylase, ISR, or UPR transcripts.
why_it_matters: A severe canonical mitochondrial/biotin-carboxylase defect would have been expected to create a secondary stress or compensation program if it were acutely cell-autonomous in these P16 neurons; the assayed transcriptional axis stayed buffered.

literature_claim: PCC is a direct biotin-dependent carboxylase activated by HLCS-dependent biotinylation.
main_caveats: Pcca was not measured as a perturbation in 215 MB Dopa, and Pcca tests one substrate branch rather than full HLCS loss.
summary: Pcca, the represented direct propionyl-CoA-carboxylase substrate gene, did not phenocopy a hidden Hlcs program; both perturbations were flat and their DE-score vectors correlated only weakly.
why_it_matters: The direct HLCS-to-PCC arm appears transcriptomically silent in this acute neuronal assay, arguing against a missed strong propionyl-CoA catabolism response downstream of Hlcs.

literature_claim: No prior HLCS pathway claim was used for the data-driven neighbor ranking.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on noisy non-significant Hlcs Wilcoxon scores, so the conclusion is the absence of a strong neighbor, not a biological link to the ranked genes.
summary: All-universe signature ranking found no convergent Hlcs module: top positive and negative Pearson correlations were below 0.05 in absolute value, and the strongest anti-neighbor Wdr26 had thousands of FDR-significant genes where Hlcs had none.
why_it_matters: This rejects the idea that the weak nominal Hlcs ranks conceal a reusable disease module shared with another perturbation in the parquet.

literature_claim: Loss of HMGCR output should reduce mevalonate-derived sterols and can feed back through the SREBP pathway that regulates HMGCR and other cholesterol-biosynthesis enzymes.
main_caveats: The assay measures RNA in surviving NeuN+ nuclei, not mevalonate, sterols, protein prenylation, or DNA indel burden.
summary: Acute Hmgcr loss produced an almost flat neuronal transcriptional surface rather than a sterol-feedback signature.
why_it_matters: HMGCR is the gatekeeper of mevalonate synthesis, so the dominant result is not a positive sterol program but buffering: only 2 downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across 21 measured neuronal groups, and a 26-gene sterol/mevalonate/SREBP marker panel was completely absent.

main_caveats: Each effect group contains one FDR<0.10 downstream gene; no recurrence makes mechanistic assignment low confidence.
summary: The only real Hmgcr downstream hits were two isolated up-regulated transcripts: Hdac11 in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Hnrnpul1 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The sparse positives define the measured biology more faithfully than a forced pathway enrichment: Hmgcr did not cause recurrent DE, and neither gene marked a multi-gene module within its cell group.

literature_claim: SREBP2 is the main transcriptional activator of cholesterol synthetic genes, so Srebf2 loss should suppress this module.
main_caveats: Most core mevalonate enzymes were measured only as readout genes, not as perturbation targets.
summary: Srebf2, but not Hmgcr, recovered a cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptional module in the same parquet.
why_it_matters: The expected cholesterogenic genes were detectable in neuronal nuclei: Srebf2 loss down-regulated Dhcr24, Insig1, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Fdft1, Sqle, Fdps, and Ldlr in several Hmgcr-matched groups, whereas Hmgcr loss left the same panel at FDR 1.0 throughout.

literature_claim: SREBP1 is related to the SREBP transcription-factor family, whereas FNTB acts downstream of mevalonate-derived farnesyl diphosphate in protein prenylation rather than in sterol transcription.
main_caveats: Only Fntb, not the full prenyltransferase family, was represented as a directly queryable target.
summary: The other queryable Hmgcr relatives, Srebf1 and Fntb, did not phenocopy Hmgcr.
why_it_matters: Srebf1 was flat in all 23 groups and Fntb produced only two single-gene effects, so the Hmgcr Hdac11/Hnrnpul1 blips are not a generic cellular response to manipulating a nearby lipid regulator or a downstream farnesylation enzyme.

main_caveats: Because the Hmgcr signature is only two genes, full-vector neighbor calls are dominated by weak rank structure; they are useful mainly as rejected strong phenocopies.
summary: The strongest data-driven neighbors of Hmgcr were very weak proteasome/ER-associated signatures, not sterol-pathway perturbations.
why_it_matters: Psmb4, Psmc1, Atp2a2, Ranbp2, and Atp6v1e1 were the top positive full-signature neighbors, but the best correlation was only r=0.0965 and proteasome perturbations had hundreds to thousands of DEGs where Hmgcr had one, arguing against a shared proteotoxic-stress module.

literature_claim: Acute genetic Hmgcr loss can deplete non-sterol isoprenoids and induce ER-stress biology in mouse liver.
main_caveats: The positive UPR comparator is an ER-calcium perturbation, not a second mevalonate enzyme.
summary: Hmgcr did not induce the UPR/ISR-like stress program that the same assay recovered after Atp2a2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Strong HMGCR-pathway loss can trigger ER stress in sensitive cells, and UPR/ISR transcripts were easy to see here under Atp2a2 loss; their absence under Hmgcr makes the Hmgcr null informative rather than simply a snRNA-seq readout failure.

literature_claim: Hmgcr-null mice die early in embryogenesis, brain cholesterol handling shifts toward glial supply as neurons mature, and partial human HMGCR impairment is sufficient to cause a progressive myopathy.
main_caveats: The parquet does not assay skeletal muscle, hepatocytes, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, secreted lipoproteins, or metabolites.
summary: The screen separates Hmgcr muscle/liver essentiality from buffered postmitotic neuronal RNA phenotypes.
why_it_matters: Germline Hmgcr loss is embryonic lethal and human HMGCR impairment causes progressive muscle disease, yet mosaic postnatal neuronal Hmgcr perturbation was nearly silent; HMGCR biology is therefore displaced toward developmental, peripheral metabolic, glial, or chronic cell-nonautonomous contexts relative to this assay.

literature_claim: HNF1A is enriched in pancreas, liver, kidney, and intestinal or related epithelial lineages, including beta-cell and hepatocyte contexts where it regulates direct transcriptional targets.
main_caveats: The dataset has no DNA indel readout and did not sample the canonical pancreas, liver, kidney, or intestine lineages.
summary: Hnf1a loss of function had no FDR-level whole-transcriptome response in any of the 23 recovered postnatal neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: This converts a flat screen result into a lineage statement: Hnf1a is a potent transcription factor in epithelial metabolic organs, but its acute removal after neuronal specification does not expose a latent cortical, thalamic, midbrain, dopaminergic, or cerebellar neuronal program.

literature_claim: HNF1A belongs to an HNF1 family that can dimerize with HNF1B and to an HNF4A/HNF1A-centered pancreatic-hepatic transcriptional network.
main_caveats: Some canonical comparators, including Foxa1, Onecut1/2, Rfx6, Gck, and Ins1/2, were not represented as perturbations; the tested relatives showed at most isolated one-gene hits, not shared programs.
summary: The neuronal Hnf1a null was shared by its directly represented HNF/MODY transcription-network comparators rather than selectively rescued or phenocopied by one paralog.
why_it_matters: Hnf1b can heterodimerize with HNF1A and HNF4A/HNF1A form overlapping pancreas-liver regulatory loops; querying those relatives showed that the network itself is absent or insulated in this NeuN+ neuronal assay rather than that Hnf1a alone is anomalously buffered.

main_caveats: This comparison used Wilcoxon score-vector correlations; because Hnf1a had no FDR-level genes, no overlap statistic can nominate a convergent regulated gene set.
summary: Whole-universe signature search did not reveal a robust Hnf1a-associated neuronal module.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive neighbor of Hnf1a was a safe-target control and the best non-safe and anti-correlated neighbors had absolute correlations below 0.04, so the apparent neighborhood is a null/noise neighborhood rather than evidence for Cd3e-, Fbxo11-, or immune-like biology.

main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured; Hnf1b mRNA was FDR=1 in every group, but weak self-transcript depletion is expected in this platform and is neither proof of failure nor proof of complete knockout.
summary: Hnf1b produced no corrected downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured juvenile neuronal groups after P16 sparse CRISPR loss of function.
why_it_matters: The dominant result is not a missed responder but a complete all-cell-class absence: in this postmitotic NeuN-enriched brain readout, Hnf1b does not acutely drive a detectable neuronal transcriptomic program.
