literature_claim: Human HNF1B intragenic variants and especially 17q12 microdeletions have been reported with neurodevelopmental disorders, while recurrent 17q12 deletions confer autism and schizophrenia risk.
main_caveats: The mouse screen removes Hnf1b mosaically after P16 and cannot test embryonic haploinsufficiency, contiguous 17q12 deletion genes, or human-specific neurodevelopment.
summary: The 17q12/HNF1B neurodevelopmental association is not phenocopied by acute Hnf1b loss in sampled P16 postmitotic neurons.
why_it_matters: Sparse neuronal knockout after fate specification failed to evoke either a general NDD-like stress program or the known HNF1B developmental programs, supporting a model in which neurodevelopmental risk is earlier, deletion-wide, or in unsampled developmental compartments rather than an ongoing Hnf1b requirement in juvenile sampled neurons.

literature_claim: CacyBP/SIP is expressed in brain neurons and can participate in SIAH-dependent ubiquitin-mediated beta-catenin degradation, but it has not been established as an HNF4A neuronal target.
main_caveats: Only one FDR-significant gene was recovered; the effect was not a recurrent program and cannot establish direct HNF4A binding or protein-level beta-catenin changes.
summary: Hnf4a perturbation produced a single robust downstream change, Cacybp down-regulation, in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: Cacybp is brain-expressed and connected to SIAH/SKP1 ubiquitin biology, so this singleton may mark a small Hnf4a-sensitive protein-turnover or beta-catenin-adjacent axis in a hindbrain GABA population, but it is not a full multi-gene pathway response.

literature_claim: HNF4A is a nuclear-receptor transcription factor required for visceral-endoderm and hepatic programs and mutated in MODY1 pancreatic endocrine disease.

summary: Postnatal Hnf4a loss does not recover the canonical HNF4A hepatocyte, visceral-endoderm, intestinal, or pancreatic transcriptional program in any sampled neuronal class.
why_it_matters: This turns the broad null surface into an interpretable out-of-lineage result: the assay perturbed postmitotic NeuN+ brain neurons, whereas the known high-amplitude HNF4A circuitry controls unsampled endoderm-derived metabolic epithelia.

why_it_matters: Direct measurement rejects an untested-paralog explanation: Hnf4g, Hnf1a, Hnf1b, Foxa2, and Sox17 each had zero downstream genes across the matched groups, while related but brain-relevant Prox1 remained capable of producing a thalamic response.

main_caveats: A near-zero signature can only reject large shared transcriptomic programs; it cannot rule out subtle protein-level HNF4A biology in an expressing tissue.
summary: Unbiased whole-surface signature comparison did not find a convincing positive or negative Hnf4a neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top mathematical neighbors have absolute Pearson correlations below 0.052, and the nominal top positive Wdr26 has a large transcriptomic footprint not shared by Hnf4a, so Hnf4a does not sit in a detectable neuronal perturbation module.

main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not assayed; 215 MB Dopa lacked Hnf4g rows; the result is a postmitotic neuronal transcriptional negative, not an organism-wide Hnf4g knockout.

why_it_matters: Hnf4g is a DNA-binding HNF4-family nuclear receptor, so a broad primary or adaptive transcriptional program should have been visible if HNF4G were active in these NeuN-enriched postmitotic neurons; none was recovered.

main_caveats: Hnf4a, Hnf1a, and Hnf1b are literature comparators rather than required Hnf4g complex members in neurons; the lone Hnf4a Cacybp hit in 191 MB P MY GABA is not enough to define a program.
summary: The HNF comparison set was also nearly flat in the same brain groups: Hnf1a and Hnf1b had no FDR hits, and Hnf4a had only a single Cacybp decrease.
why_it_matters: Directly measuring the obvious paralog and HNF-named comparators rejects the possibility that Hnf4g alone was anomalously flat while a closely related HNF perturbation drove a large postmitotic neuronal program.

main_caveats: Restricted to Wilcoxon score-vector cosine over the model-visible parquet; the top and bottom values were intentionally kept only as rejected exploratory neighbors.
summary: Unbiased score-space neighbors were rejected: the best Hnf4g cosine similarities were only +0.026 and -0.024, and the strongest apparent responder, Tsc2, had hundreds of FDR hits while Hnf4g had none.
why_it_matters: The all-gene rank vectors do not hide a coherent Hnf4g module below the FDR cutoff; nearest-neighbor biology derived from this flat signature would be driven by low-amplitude rank noise.

literature_claim: HNRNPA2B1 is a broadly expressed hnRNP involved in RNA processing and transport.
main_caveats: Responder counts were small and the two broadest signatures also had the largest perturbed-cell counts.
summary: Hnrnpa2b1 produced only 25 downstream FDR<0.10 calls across 6 of 21 measured cell groups, with the largest signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The target is not a global postnatal neuronal gene-abundance regulator in this assay; its measurable output is sparse and state-restricted.

literature_claim: HNRNPA2B1 belongs to the hnRNP/RNA-processing network and can couple m6A-marked RNAs to DGCR8-dependent pri-miRNA processing.
main_caveats: The inference is from mRNA abundance only; HNRNPA1 was not itself a perturbation target, so reciprocal epistasis could not be measured.
summary: The strongest Hnrnpa2b1-responsive RNA/RNP genes point to compensatory RNP-family rebalancing: Hnrnpa1 was up in both main glutamatergic responders, Hnrnpu was down in two responders, and Rbm25, Tcerg1, and Drosha were up in the thalamic responder.
why_it_matters: The cells do not simply lose RNA-processing transcripts; they alter other nuclear RNA regulators, nominating Hnrnpa1 up-regulation as the main mRNA biomarker of Hnrnpa2b1 loss in this dataset.

literature_claim: HNRNPA2B1 promotes DGCR8-dependent pri-miRNA processing and can amplify TBK1-IRF3 interferon signaling after DNA-virus sensing.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq does not quantify mature miRNAs; the IFN prior was defined after viral stimulation rather than at baseline.
summary: The expected m6A/pri-miRNA and antiviral IFN outputs were largely uncoupled from the measured neuronal response: Drosha was significant only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Dgcr8, Dicer1, and assayed IFN/TBK1 markers were never FDR-significant.
why_it_matters: A single Drosha increase should not be overread as global Microprocessor activation, and Hnrnpa2b1 loss did not launch a DNA-sensing interferon program in uninfected NeuN+ neurons.

literature_claim: Several hnRNPs and nuclear RBPs are linked to neuronal RNA processing and neurological disease.
main_caveats: The comparators are same-family or same-phenotype-class RBPs, not subunits of one obligate complex.
summary: Hnrnpa2b1 was far weaker than related nuclear RBP perturbations: Hnrnpu, Tardbp, Matr3, and Hnrnpc generated 2096, 670, 555, and 260 matched downstream FDR calls, respectively.
why_it_matters: The flat Hnrnpa2b1 groups cannot be dismissed as an assay-wide inability to detect RBP biology; multiple RNA-binding targets were readily visible under the same P16 AAV and snRNA-seq workflow.

main_caveats: The cosine calculation used all matched Wilcoxon scores, so with such tiny magnitudes it is useful mainly to reject strong convergence.
summary: Hnrnpa2b1 had no robust whole-transcriptome signature neighbor: the top positive and negative cosine similarities were only +0.0358 and -0.0226, and the nominated neighbors shared no same-group FDR hits with Hnrnpa2b1.
why_it_matters: This prevents post-hoc assignment of the sparse signature to a strong hidden module such as Unc5c/Plxnd1/Sall1 or Ptprc/Fbxo11/Dscam signaling.

literature_claim: Neurological HNRNPA2B1 disease is linked to RNA-processing dysfunction and low-complexity-domain mutations rather than only reduced gene dosage.
main_caveats: Protein-level aggregation and long-term adult degeneration were not measured.
summary: Acute Hnrnpa2b1 loss did not induce a broad stress, interferon, or proteinopathy-like gene-abundance program despite HNRNPA2B1 being an ALS/MSP protein.
why_it_matters: The result argues that a juvenile mosaic LoF allele is a poor transcriptional model of the toxic prion-like HNRNPA2B1 variants that alter RNP granules in ALS/MSP.

main_caveats: Most genes occur in only one or two groups; Col4a2 is unusual in a NeuN-enriched neuronal dataset and should be validated.
summary: Outside the RNA/RNP genes, recurrent FDR hits were limited to empirical markers such as Hmgn3 up in 005 and 155, Atp11b up in 066 and 151, and Fam193b down in 151 and 155, with singletons such as Mapk1ip1, Abhd8, Cep131, Ppcdc, Peg3, and Col4a2.
why_it_matters: These recurrent genes are practical readouts of the sparse Hnrnpa2b1 state but do not define a canonical pathway, correctly preserving the noncanonical tail of the measured DE surface.

literature_claim: HNRNPC and other hnRNPs are ubiquitous RNA-processing proteins with major consequences in the nervous system when dosage is altered.
main_caveats: Gene-level snRNA-seq does not report alternative splicing directly, and the 217 P MY Pineal Glut call has only 32 perturbed cells.
summary: Hnrnpc loss of function generated a gene-level response in only 8 of 22 measured cell groups, concentrated in thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, hindbrain/pineal, and Pvalb GABA neurons rather than broadly across telencephalic projection neurons.
why_it_matters: The effect of a ubiquitous pre-mRNA-binding protein was not ubiquitous in this P16-to-P37/44 neuronal screen; the observed biology is a region- and cell-state-restricted postmitotic response.

literature_claim: HNRNPC packages U-rich pre-mRNAs and regulates alternative exon inclusion, m6A-accessible binding, and alternative cleavage/polyadenylation.
main_caveats: The assay quantifies gene abundance, not splice junctions or poly(A)-site isoforms, so these are compensatory factor-level changes, not direct isoform events.
summary: The strongest Hnrnpc responders rewired RNA-processing genes: Ddx39b, Ddx17, Pabpn1, Son, Prpf39 and Cpsf7 rose in selected groups, whereas Luc7l2, Rbm25, Srsf2, Tia1 or Hnrnpu fell in major thalamic/midbrain responders.
why_it_matters: The perturbation read out as a secondary splicing/export/3-prime-end compensation state, exactly the class of process controlled by hnRNP C, rather than as a simple drop of the Hnrnpc mRNA row itself.

literature_claim: ZFAND1 recruits p97/VCP and the proteasome for stress-granule clearance, and TXNL1 is a redox-active proteasome cofactor.
main_caveats: The data show transcript induction of proteostasis-associated genes; they do not measure stress granules, proteasome flux, or TXNL1/ZFAND1 protein activity.
summary: Hnrnpc-responsive groups induced a proteostasis/stress-granule-clearance flank marked by recurrent Txnl1 and by Zfand1, Anapc5, Ube2f, Rbx1, Josd1 and ubiquitin-pathway genes.
why_it_matters: Loss of a nuclear RBP was coupled to protein-quality-control circuitry, suggesting that affected neurons adapt to RNP stress by increasing proteasome- and ubiquitin-linked capacity.

literature_claim: MTERF3 represses mammalian mitochondrial DNA transcription initiation, and SLC25A36 transports pyrimidine nucleotides into and out of mitochondria.
main_caveats: The causal link to hnRNP C is inferential; mtDNA transcription, respiration, and metabolites were not assayed.
summary: A mitochondrial nucleotide/mtRNA module accompanied Hnrnpc loss: Mterf3 was up in six responders, Slc25a36 in five, and Slc25a3, Atp5d, Ppm1k or Mff in selected major responders.
why_it_matters: This recurrent module links an RBP perturbation to mitochondrial transcription and inner-membrane nucleotide exchange, a secondary program not obvious from the canonical hnRNP C literature.

literature_claim: Human HNRNPC haploinsufficiency affects neurodevelopment and neuronal morphology through altered alternative splicing.
main_caveats: Gene-level changes may be downstream of mis-splicing and are cell-group-specific; they are not direct evidence of changed channel or synaptic protein abundance.
summary: Major responders also changed neuronal effector genes, including Cacna1a up in 151/191/217, vesicle or endomembrane genes Scamp5, Stx3 and Stx1b, and down-regulation of Dst, Syne1, L1cam, Syt7, Shank3 or Gpm6a in selected groups.
why_it_matters: The postmitotic signature connects Hnrnpc dosage to mature excitability, trafficking and cytoskeletal transcripts rather than only to progenitor migration or generic RNA-processing factors.

literature_claim: HNRNPC controls splice-site outcomes, PRPF6 and SNRNP70 act in the major spliceosome, RNPC3 acts in the minor spliceosome, and CDC40 is an activated-spliceosome factor.
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor statistics compare gene-level DE over Hnrnpc FDR coordinates, not direct physical interactions.
summary: Prpf6, a U4/U6-U5 tri-snRNP spliceosome perturbation, was the top robust Hnrnpc signature neighbor; Snrnp70, Rnpc3 and Cdc40 produced broader spliceosome-related signatures that only partly overlapped Hnrnpc.
why_it_matters: The data-driven neighbor was a core spliceosome factor, confirming that the Hnrnpc transcriptional state is spliceosome-adjacent, while also showing that Hnrnpc loss is a weak, restricted branch rather than a full core-spliceosome-collapse state.

literature_claim: HNRNPC directly competes with U2AF65/U2AF2 to prevent cryptic Alu exonization in human cells.
main_caveats: The screen cannot score Alu or splice-junction inclusion; a true isoform-level antagonism could be present even without an inverse gene-abundance signature.
summary: The expected U2AF2 antagonist did not form a clean opposite Hnrnpc gene-expression mirror: U2af2 was broad in the same neuronal groups but its Hnrnpc-overlapping calls were nearly balanced in direction.
why_it_matters: The famous HNRNPC-U2AF65 competition at human Alu splice sites is not recapitulated as a simple inverse gene-level LoF relationship in postmitotic mouse neurons; it is likely an isoform- and repeat-context mechanism here.

literature_claim: HNRNPC, HNRNPA/B and other hnRNPs are related nuclear RNA-binding proteins involved in pre-mRNA maturation and neurological disease biology.
main_caveats: The assay measured only four hnRNP-family comparators, not the full family or all paralogs.
summary: Measured hnRNP-family members were not interchangeable with Hnrnpc: Hnrnpa2b1, Hnrnph2 and Hnrnpdl were almost flat, whereas Hnrnpu was broad but directionally mixed relative to Hnrnpc.
why_it_matters: Family membership alone was a poor predictor of mouse neuronal perturbation state; this argues for target-specific RNP biology rather than a generic hnRNP response.

literature_claim: HNRNPC repression, particularly with ADAR deficiency, can generate endogenous dsRNA and type-I-interferon signaling in cancer-cell contexts.
main_caveats: Olfactory bulb, hindbrain, and non-neuronal innate-immune cells were depleted or absent from the assay; DNA editing and dsRNA itself were not measured.
summary: Hnrnpc loss did not activate a detectable interferon/dsRNA response in the 22 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: A cancer-cell HNRNPC vulnerability mechanism was absent in juvenile mouse neuronal nuclei, warning against assuming that HNRNPC depletion universally exposes immunostimulatory dsRNA.

literature_claim: GCLC functions in glutathione synthesis and RUBCNL is an autophagy-related Beclin/Rubicon-like regulator; no HNRNPC-specific prior predicts this exact pineal branch.
main_caveats: Only 32 perturbed nuclei support this group, and many genes sit close to the FDR 0.10 threshold.
summary: The 217 P MY Pineal Glut responder carried a low-count, exploratory tail with Gclc and Rubcnl induction plus Jund, Tle2 and Gtf3c5 down-regulation.
why_it_matters: This separates a possible redox/autophagy/AP-1 branch from the recurrent RNA and mitochondrial core and prevents overfitting the 217 signal to the canonical splicing story alone.

literature_claim: HNRNPDL is an hnRNP RNA-binding protein whose closest D-family circuitry and shRNA studies point to alternative splicing and RNA-processing regulation.
main_caveats: The Wilcoxon matrix is gene-level snRNA abundance; isoform changes, NMD-coupled isoform ratios and protein solubility were not measured.
summary: Hnrnpdl loss in P16 sparse postmitotic neurons produced an almost fully buffered gene-abundance surface: only Hnrnpu in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Sh3bp5 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured classes.
why_it_matters: A classical splice/RNA-binding gene can be active yet leave very little total-mRNA response in juvenile neurons; the flat self-transcript is expected for indel-based CRISPR and does not invalidate the result.

literature_claim: hnRNP proteins act in interconnected but structurally divergent RNA-processing networks.
main_caveats: This is a singleton gene-level response; a direct Hnrnpdl-Hnrnpu regulatory edge was not demonstrated.
summary: The strongest Hnrnpdl-dependent transcript was Hnrnpu up-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and the same Hnrnpu row moved in the opposite direction after Hnrnpa2b1, Hnrnpc or Wdr26 perturbation.
why_it_matters: This nominates Hnrnpu as a sensitive, thalamus-enriched RNA-binding/homeostatic marker rather than a generic consequence of perturbing any hnRNP-family target.

literature_claim: SH3BP5/SAB participates in mitochondrial JNK-ROS signaling in stress and cell-death pathways.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10, so this is not evidence for a full JNK transcriptional program.
summary: Hnrnpdl perturbation selectively increased Sh3bp5 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
why_it_matters: Because SH3BP5/SAB is tied to mitochondrial JNK stress signaling, the hit is a hypothesis-generating marker for a small signaling-brake response restricted to deep corticothalamic/OB-related glutamatergic neurons.

literature_claim: hnRNP proteins share pre-mRNA/RBP biology, while HNRNPDL and other prion-like hnRNPs have isoform- and low-complexity-domain-specific regulation.
main_caveats: The closest Hnrnpdl paralog, Hnrnpd/AUF1, was not a screen target and therefore could not be measured directly.
summary: Measurable hnRNP-family perturbations did not phenocopy Hnrnpdl: Hnrnpu and Hnrnpc altered 2140 and 294 downstream genes in matched groups, whereas Hnrnpdl altered 2, and their whole-surface correlations with Hnrnpdl were near zero.
why_it_matters: The flat Hnrnpdl surface is not a generic inability of the screen to detect loss of an RNA-binding hnRNP; it is specific to Hnrnpdl biology, timing, or assay modality.

main_caveats: The correlations use rank-score vectors over all matched gene-by-cell-group entries; they intentionally summarize total-mRNA DE, not splicing.
summary: The top model-visible neighbors of Hnrnpdl were not convincing biological convergers: the best positive non-safe correlation was Wdr26 at r=0.0446 and the best negative was Fbxo11 at r=-0.0469.
why_it_matters: Genome-wide cross-perturbation search did not reveal a coherent upstream module hidden behind the two singleton Hnrnpdl hits.

literature_claim: HNRNPDL loss or mutation has been linked to broad RNA-processing changes, myofiber disruption, altered phase separation and reduced solubility in muscle, endothelial sprouting defects and proliferative cell-cycle control.
main_caveats: The assay lacks skeletal muscle, endothelial cells, cancer-cycle states, long aging, and an explicit D378N/H missense allele.
summary: The P16 neuronal CRISPR perturbation did not recover broad muscle-dystrophy, phase-separation/proteostasis, endothelial-sprouting, or proliferative cell-cycle programs described for HNRNPDL in other systems.
why_it_matters: The negative result redirects HNRNPDL disease modeling toward muscle, isoform/solubility and allele-specific aggregation assays rather than treating juvenile neuronal total-mRNA silencing as a faithful LGMDD3 model.

literature_claim: HNRNPH2 is a broadly used RNA-processing factor and an HNRNPF/H paralog-family member, but Hnrnph2 knockout can be buffered by Hnrnph1 in mouse.
main_caveats: The significant signature is small; 215 MB Dopa was not measured for Hnrnph2.
summary: Hnrnph2 loss produced only seven downstream whole-gene FDR<0.10 calls, concentrated in four caudal neuronal groups and absent from the other 18 measured groups.
why_it_matters: The response is real but narrow: postnatal Hnrnph2 single-gene LoF is not a pan-neuronal whole-gene expression shock in this assay.

literature_claim: RSRP1 is a spliceosome-associated arginine/serine-rich protein.
main_caveats: The screen measures whole-gene abundance, not whether Rsrp1 isoforms or splicing targets changed.
summary: Rsrp1 down-regulation was the recurrent RNA-processing readout of Hnrnph2 perturbation, appearing in 145, 151, and 155, while no other downstream gene recurred in more than two groups.
why_it_matters: RSRP1 is itself annotated as a probable spliceosomal factor, so it is a compact reporter of the RNA-processing branch that survives whole-gene correction after acute Hnrnph2 LoF.

literature_claim: IDH3G and OGDH encode mitochondrial TCA-cycle components, and TIMM44 functions in mitochondrial protein import.
main_caveats: Only three mitochondrial genes were FDR-significant, so this is a module-level hypothesis rather than evidence for a measured respiration phenotype.
summary: Idh3g, Ogdh, and Timm44 were induced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Idh3g also induced in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The second Hnrnph2 program is a small mitochondrial/TCA and mitochondrial-import bounce rather than a broad ISR or unfolded-protein response.

literature_claim: HNRNPU is an hnRNP-family neurodevelopmental-disease gene with loss-of-function pathogenicity.
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to seven Hnrnph2 significant coordinates; it is a convergence test, not proof of a direct Hnrnph2-Hnrnpu complex.
summary: Hnrnpu was the top positive restricted-signature neighbor, matching five of seven Hnrnph2 downstream coordinates including Rsrp1 down in three groups and Idh3g up in two.
why_it_matters: A different hnRNP-family neurodevelopmental gene recapitulates both the RNA-processing and Idh3g arms, arguing that the tiny Hnrnph2 signature is not random noise.

literature_claim: HNRNPH1/H2 can cooperate with snRNPs during splice-site regulation, and U2AF2, SNRNP70, PRPF6, and CDC40 are annotated spliceosomal factors.
main_caveats: Restricted signature with only a few shared genes; Matr3 is an RNA/nuclear-matrix neighbor rather than a core snRNP component.
summary: U2af2, Cdc40, Prpf6, Snrnp70, and Matr3 converged with Hnrnph2 on Rsrp1 down-regulation but did not consistently share the Idh3g/Ogdh/Timm44 branch.
why_it_matters: The screen separates an RNA-spliceosome stress reporter from the caudal mitochondrial branch; expected splicing neighbors phenocopy only part of Hnrnph2.

main_caveats: This is data-driven and restricted-signature based; only two opposite significant coordinates defined each negative neighbor.
summary: Proteasome/autophagy/translation-adjacent neighbors such as Psmb4, Huwe1, Gigyf2, and Rab7 opposed the Hnrnph2 Rsrp1 or Idh3g directions.
why_it_matters: The opposite neighbors show that Rsrp1 loss and Idh3g induction are not a generic response to any strong neuronal CRISPR stressor.

literature_claim: Frameshift Hnrnpu haploinsufficiency in mouse cortex and human organoids produced only partial RNA/protein lowering, consistent with transcript buffering or adaptation.
main_caveats: DNA indels and HNRNPU protein were not measured in the Perturb-seq nuclei.
summary: Hnrnpu-targeted nuclei up-regulated Hnrnpu RNA across all measured groups rather than showing a simple knockdown signature.
why_it_matters: The positive self-transcript makes the target transcript an adaptive or indel-insensitive readout; it should not be mistaken for absence of functional CRISPR loss.

literature_claim: Hnrnpu haploinsufficiency causes modest, cell-type-specific transcriptomic dysregulation in developing neocortex and hippocampus, with strong subiculum vulnerability.
main_caveats: Perturbed-cell count covaries with discovery power, and 10x snRNA detects survivors only.
summary: The acute Hnrnpu transcriptome was broad but concentrated in thalamic and midbrain groups, with 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA carrying 80.8% of all downstream FDR<0.10 events.
why_it_matters: This shifts the recoverable postnatal response away from a purely cortical/subicular expectation and identifies the neuronal classes in which P16 Hnrnpu LoF most strongly surfaces as steady-state DE.

literature_claim: HNRNPU and the hnRNP family act in pre-mRNA/splicing and broader RNA-metabolism processes.
main_caveats: 3-prime snRNA measured gene abundance, not alternative isoforms.
summary: Hnrnpu induced a compensatory RNA-processing module and converged with spliceosome/RNA-processing perturbations.
why_it_matters: This is the positive molecular link that best matches HNRNPU’s canonical hnRNP biology in the postmitotic CRISPR setting.

main_caveats: The module is a downstream state; no direct HNRNPU binding to these mRNAs was measured.
summary: Amino-acid starvation and ISR-like genes were induced in the largest Hnrnpu responders.
why_it_matters: The response is not limited to nuclear RNA factors; postmitotic Hnrnpu loss secondarily taxes translation and amino-acid homeostasis.

literature_claim: NRF1-dependent transcriptional feedback induces proteasome synthesis after proteasome inhibition.
main_caveats: Hnrnpu itself is not known to encode a proteasome factor; convergence supports a secondary proteotoxic state.
summary: Hnrnpu triggered ubiquitin, lysosome, autophagy, and proteasome-quality-control genes and converged with direct proteasome-subunit perturbations.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation convergence with Psmc1 and Psmb4 makes the proteostasis module load-bearing rather than a hand-picked gene list.

literature_claim: Hnrnpu haploinsufficiency down-regulates neuronally expressed genes enriched for neuronal migration and axon guidance in neocortex and hippocampus.
main_caveats: Specific P0 subiculum genes such as Mef2c were not recovered.
summary: Hnrnpu loss paired compensatory transport/cytoskeletal up-regulation with down-regulation of synaptic, axonal, and ciliary/neurite genes.
why_it_matters: The module partially recovers the migration/axon-guidance direction predicted from germline disease models but in a postmitotic remodeling form.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: HNRNPU contributes to chromatin organization and transcriptional gene regulation.
main_caveats: The transcription factor causal chain upstream of Dmtf1 and Hdac3 was not measured.
summary: Chromatin and transcriptional regulators headed by Dmtf1 and Hdac3 were induced across the Hnrnpu surface.
why_it_matters: Hnrnpu perturbation recruits a second nuclear regulatory layer beyond splice factors, consistent with HNRNPU’s chromatin-scaffold role.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: NeuN+ snRNA cannot fully exclude sparse non-neuronal ambient nuclear RNA contributing to this module.
summary: An ECM/secretory-matrix module, including Col4a1, Col4a2, Colgalt1, Adam15, and Vldlr, rose in several neuronal Hnrnpu responders.
why_it_matters: This preserves a noncanonical secondary program that would be lost if Hnrnpu were summarized only as an RNA-splicing hit.

literature_claim: hnRNP proteins share RNA-metabolism functions but differ structurally and functionally; HNRNPC LoF is a distinct NDD mechanism.
main_caveats: Only Hnrnpc, Hnrnpa2b1, and Tardbp were represented among the considered hnRNP-like targets; Hnrnpul1/2 were not measured as targets.
summary: Measured hnRNP-family perturbations did not phenocopy Hnrnpu even though RNA-processing perturbations did.
why_it_matters: This separates Hnrnpu biology from a generic abundant-hnRNP LoF state and rejects Hnrnpc, Hnrnpa2b1, and Tardbp as interchangeable postnatal neuronal comparators.

literature_claim: HNRNPU, DEPDC5/GATOR1, and TSC/mTOR perturbations are all linked to epilepsy, with DEPDC5 and TSC complexes acting as mTORC1 repressors.
main_caveats: Phospho-S6/mTOR activity was not measured; inference is from transcriptomic overlap only.
summary: Depdc5 was an Hnrnpu-induced gene, but the mTOR/DEE comparator landscape split: Tsc2 converged while Depdc5, Mtor, Scn2a, and Grin1 were rejected as phenocopies.
why_it_matters: The result argues for compensatory induction of an mTOR brake within the Hnrnpu stress state rather than a primary Depdc5/GATOR1-like transcriptome.

literature_claim: HNRNPU has chromatin-organizing functions in addition to RNA-processing functions.
main_caveats: Opposition was based on restricted Hnrnpu significant features rather than full-transcriptome correlations.
summary: Setd1a and Zbtb7a were robust opposite-overlap comparators for the Hnrnpu signature.
why_it_matters: An opposite related-regulator contrast prevents the Hnrnpu signature from being collapsed into a generic chromatin-perturbation response.

literature_claim: Cell-type-specific Hnrnpu disease signatures have been proposed as inputs for transcriptomic reversal; proteasome stress can itself drive a compensatory transcriptional signature.
main_caveats: The screen has no drug data; the warning follows from cross-perturbation identity of the acute signature.
summary: The acute P16 Hnrnpu signature is a survivor stress signature, not a clean embryonic HNRNPU-NDD disease signature for direct transcriptomic reversal.
why_it_matters: Compounds selected to reverse this screen signature could suppress RNA/proteasome compensation rather than rescue the developmental HNRNPU program.

main_caveats: Biomarker value is defined for this mouse P16 CRISPR snRNA dataset, not yet for patient tissue or protein assays.
summary: Dmtf1, Atxn2l, Gpr180, Ahi1, Rsrp1, Macf1, Depdc5, and Hdac3 form recurrent marker genes for acute neuronal Hnrnpu perturbation.
why_it_matters: These genes report the response across multiple cell groups and are more robust assay biomarkers than one-off single-cell-type hits.

literature_claim: Homer2 is a long Homer postsynaptic scaffold in an EVH1/coiled-coil family that organizes group-I mGluR, calcium-store, and Shank/PSD protein complexes rather than a transcription factor.
main_caveats: DNA indels and Homer2 protein were not measured; single-nucleus RNA cannot assay receptor localization, phosphorylation, calcium transients, or spine morphology.
summary: Homer2 loss produced a pan-measured, FDR-level null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: This converts a flat DE surface into a biological constraint: in basal P37-44 neurons, acute mosaic Homer2 loss does not launch a large cell-autonomous RNA program, including no detectable proteostasis, ISR/UPR, autophagy, redox, translation, or synaptic-downregulation module.

literature_claim: Homer proteins physically tether group-I metabotropic glutamate receptors to IP3 receptors and are cross-linked to PSD-95 complexes through Shank scaffolds; Shank3 deficiency is known to perturb mGluR5-Homer scaffolding.
main_caveats: Homer1/Homer3 were not perturbation targets, and the comparison is restricted to RNA-level outputs.
summary: Direct Homer-complex perturbations did not reveal a shared transcriptomic module that Homer2 failed to match.
why_it_matters: The expected physical neighbors—Grm1, Grm5, Itpr1, Ryr2/Ryr3, Shank2/Shank3, and Dlg4—were measurable and were themselves essentially flat in Homer2-matched neuronal groups, so Homer2's null is the local behavior of this postsynaptic scaffold class in the assay rather than a unique outlier.

main_caveats: The correlation calculation uses the full subthreshold score vector because Homer2 has no thresholded genes; it is useful mainly for rejecting convergence.
summary: The all-target, data-driven nearest neighbors of Homer2 were too weak to support a hidden convergent signature.
why_it_matters: Pearson correlations over matched Wilcoxon-score surfaces never exceeded 0.044; the strongest nonrestricted neighbor, Fbxo11, had only one FDR-level downstream gene, and the strongest broad neighbor, Dhdds, generated a TH/MB ER-stress program absent from Homer2. Thus Homer2 is best treated as a true flat signature, not as a member of a low-amplitude module.

literature_claim: Repeated ethanol and nucleus-accumbens manipulations implicate mGluR5-Homer2-PI3K protein signaling in binge-like alcohol consumption and ethanol-induced neuroplasticity.
main_caveats: The screen was juvenile, unstimulated, and whole-brain cell-grouped; nucleus-accumbens subtypes and alcohol exposure were not isolated.
summary: The addiction-linked mGluR5-Homer2-PI3K axis is not reproduced as a basal juvenile neuronal RNA state.
why_it_matters: Adult nucleus-accumbens studies tie Homer2b, mGluR5, and PI3K activity to binge alcohol intake, but represented PI3K/AKT/MAPK/MTOR perturbations showed no Homer2-like module in the same screen. The disease-relevant Homer2 mechanism therefore reads out as receptor scaffolding, kinase activity, and circuit plasticity rather than a broad basal transcriptome.

literature_claim: Hoxa1 acts mainly in early embryonic hindbrain, otic, neural-crest and cardiac patterning rather than as a broad juvenile neuronal maintenance factor.
main_caveats: True indel formation was not measured; the conclusion is limited to an acute, sparse P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ snRNA-seq endpoint.
summary: P16 Hoxa1 loss was pan-cell-type flat at the robust DE threshold: all 23 recovered neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This makes postmitotic Hoxa1 unlike a sustained neuronal identity regulator in the sampled juvenile brain; the absence of an Hoxa1 mRNA drop is expected for sparse CRISPR indel readout and is not sufficient to call the perturbation failed.

literature_claim: Embryonic Hoxa1 loss alters Hoxb1/Egr2-linked hindbrain segmentation genes and downstream neural-crest and otic targets such as Foxd3, Zic1, Pax8, Fgfr3 and Lhx5.
main_caveats: Hoxb1 itself was absent from the Hoxa1 feature lists, so the absent program is inferred from represented pathway members rather than from Hoxb1 RNA.
summary: The embryonic Hoxa1 retinoic-acid and rhombomere program was not re-induced or derepressed after P16 Hoxa1 loss.
why_it_matters: If the postnatal cells retained an active Hoxa1-dependent RA/Hox circuit, snRNA-seq should have captured coordinated shifts in its transcriptional members; instead every queried expected-program gene remained FDR=1.0.

literature_claim: Hox proteins act with Pbx/Meis cofactors and retinoic-acid signaling in an embryonic hindbrain patterning network.
main_caveats: The strongest family members Hoxb1, Hoxa2 and Hoxb2 were not perturbation targets; the assayed Hox comparators are only partial proxies for the embryonic Hoxa1 circuit.
summary: Represented HOX-family and Hox-cofactor/retinoic-acid comparators also failed to produce a broad postnatal neuronal Hoxa1-like signature.
why_it_matters: The Hoxa1 null is therefore not an isolated outlier: retinoic-acid receptors, TALE cofactors and other represented Hox genes were similarly buffered in this assay, with only isolated singleton or doubleton DE events.

main_caveats: The result is a restricted signed-score comparison over represented genes and cell groups; it is useful for rejecting strong convergence, not for inferring biology from r≈0.03 neighbors.
summary: Phenotype-first global neighbors of Hoxa1 were at noise-scale correlations, so Msx2, Wwox and Mbd5 were rejected as convergent positives and Lgals3, Wnk3 and Or51e2 were rejected as meaningful anti-neighbors.
why_it_matters: With no FDR<0.10 Hoxa1 genes, the continuous score vector contains only weak rank fluctuations; the cross-perturbation search therefore supports a buffered surface rather than a hidden shared module.

literature_claim: Biallelic pathogenic HOXA1 variants cause congenital syndromes dominated by horizontal gaze palsy, deafness, cerebrovascular malformations, central hypoventilation and cranial-nerve/heart involvement.
main_caveats: The dataset does not sample embryonic otic epithelia, cranial neural crest, vascular cells or heart, so it cannot localize the primary disease transcriptome.
summary: The screen refines HOXA1-related disease biology toward congenital patterning in embryonic and non-neuronal derivatives, not ongoing Hoxa1 dependence of broad sampled juvenile neurons.
why_it_matters: A postmitotic P16 brain perturbation did not recapitulate cranial motor, otic, carotid or heart-linked transcriptional programs, matching the idea that HOXA1 disease phenotypes are laid down during early development in lineages mostly absent from this NeuN+ assay.

literature_claim: Acp6 encodes lysophosphatidic acid phosphatase type 6 and Slc49a4 encodes solute carrier family 49 member 4; neither is an established Hoxa13 Bmp, Fgf, or Eph morphogenesis effector.
main_caveats: Only two genes pass FDR<0.10, both at FDR 0.0816, with 48 perturbed cells; no larger pathway can be inferred.
summary: Hoxa13 produced a narrowly cell-class-restricted 217 P MY Pineal Glut response consisting only of Acp6 and Slc49a4 up-regulation at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The only reproducible transcriptional trace of Hoxa13 loss in the assayed juvenile neuronal brain is a two-gene signal outside established Hoxa13 embryonic patterning circuits; this constrains any mechanistic interpretation to a small, hypothesis-generating P MY/Pineal module rather than canonical Hox morphogenesis.

literature_claim: Hoxa13 and Hoxd13 act partially redundantly in distal limb development, and Hox proteins commonly use TALE cofactors of the Pbx and Meis/Prep families.
main_caveats: Most comparator signatures are as small as Hoxa13 or smaller; Hoxd10, Pbx1, and Meis2 each had one isolated FDR hit in a different gene or cell group, so the conclusion is non-convergence, not proof of no biology.
summary: The 217 Acp6/Slc49a4 signature was not shared by represented Hox-family targets or by assayed Pbx, Meis, and Pknox2 Hox cofactors.
why_it_matters: The Hoxa13 signal is not a generic consequence of perturbing Hox-family or Hox-TALE transcriptional machinery in this screen. Hoxd13, the literature-obvious posterior paralog, had no FDR<0.10 genes in 22 measured groups and did not regulate either Acp6 or Slc49a4 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.

literature_claim: Embryonic Hoxa13 loss disrupts Fgf8 and Bmp7 in genital tubercle, Epha7/Epha4 in limb and umbilical-artery mesenchyme/endothelium, and Gata3-associated lower urogenital patterning.
main_caveats: Most canonical effectors are lowly expressed or sporadically represented in neuronal nuclei; absence here should not be extrapolated to embryonic Hoxa13-positive tissues.
summary: Embryonic Bmp/Fgf/Eph/Gata3/vascular Hoxa13 effectors were absent from the postnatal neuronal DE surface.
why_it_matters: Loss of Hoxa13 in limb, genital tubercle, urogenital, and placental settings down-regulates morphogen, cell-adhesion, apoptosis/proliferation, and vascular programs; the P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ brain assay showed no FDR-supported movement of Bmp7, Fgf8, Nog, Epha7, Epha4, Gata3, Tek, Foxf1, Gli3, Hoxd13, or Ar, arguing that the screen did not recover a hidden canonical Hoxa13 program.

literature_claim: Hox genes pattern the embryonic hindbrain and spinal cord, whereas Hoxa13/Hoxd13 functions are best established in embryonic distal limb and urogenital morphogenesis.
main_caveats: No indel sequencing is available; the target transcript was usually absent from the tested gene set, so the result is a postnatal neuronal buffering statement, not a DNA editing efficiency readout.
summary: Hoxa13 was transcriptionally buffered across 22 of 23 measured neuronal cell groups, with only one sub-threshold weak group.
why_it_matters: A homeobox factor whose major biology is embryonic positional specification did not trigger a broad secondary stress, UPR, proteostasis, autophagy, redox, translation, or synaptic-collapse signature when acutely perturbed after neurons were born. The null surface is therefore biologically interpretable rather than a generic perturbation failure.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation was restricted to the two Hoxa13 FDR genes; the positive non-self neighbors did not pass FDR for either gene, and Thap11 shared only the Acp6 locus at FDR<0.10.
summary: The strongest data-driven anti-neighbor was Thap11, which robustly down-regulated Acp6 in 217 P MY Pineal Glut rather than reproducing the Hoxa13 up-signature.
why_it_matters: Acp6 is detectably regulated in the same cell class by another perturbation, so the Hoxa13 Acp6 increase is not simply an undetectable locus; however, the opposite Thap11 direction also shows that this two-gene signature should not be treated as a general perturbation-stress marker.

literature_claim: Mouse Hoxa3 loss causes strong embryonic pharyngeal neural-crest/endodermal organogenesis phenotypes rather than a documented postnatal brain-neuron maintenance phenotype.
main_caveats: DNA editing was not measured, but Hoxa3 self-mRNA was also not expected to be informative; the conclusion is restricted to postmitotic neuronal nuclei recovered 3-4 weeks after P16 AAV-CRISPR.
summary: Hoxa3 is a pan-measured neuronal null in this P16-to-P37/P44 brain CRISPR screen.
why_it_matters: The dataset refines Hoxa3's potent embryonic transcription-factor biology away from a maintenance role in the sampled juvenile NeuN+ neuronal classes: all 23 recovered groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite 388046 Hoxa3 DE tests in total.

literature_claim: Embryonic third-pharyngeal-pouch studies place Hoxa3 upstream of altered Tbx1/Bmp4/Fgf8 regional timing and of parathyroid/thymus differentiation programs, and a hESC 3PPE model connects HOXA3 to PAX9, SIX1, BMP4, PBX1 and EPHB2/Wnt behavior.
main_caveats: These expected genes are sparse in neurons; the test is useful as an absence-of-program control, not as evidence for direct regulation in brain.
summary: Canonical third-pharyngeal-pouch and thymus/parathyroid marker genes were not mobilized by Hoxa3 loss in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: Gcm2, Foxn1, Pax1, Pax9, Tbx1, Six1, Bmp4, Fgf8, Ephb2 and Pbx1 are the genes that the embryonic Hoxa3 literature makes worth checking; their complete absence at FDR<0.10 argues that the P16 neuronal assay did not merely miss a nontranscriptional endpoint, but sampled a cell state in which the embryonic Hoxa3 cis-regulatory program is closed.

literature_claim: Hoxa3 has partially overlapping group-3 paralog functions with Hoxb3/Hoxd3 in pharyngeal-organ migration, and Hox transcription factors commonly use Pbx and Meis/Prep TALE cofactors for DNA-site selection.
main_caveats: Hoxb3 and Hoxd3, the closest group-3 paralogs, were not perturbation targets in the parquet; the represented comparators test a broader, not identical, Hox/TALE network.
summary: Perturbations of represented Hox/TALE/pharyngeal relatives did not phenocopy Hoxa3; most were as flat as Hoxa3.
why_it_matters: If juvenile neurons retained an active Hox-Pbx-Meis developmental module, Hoxa3 could have converged with Hoxa1 or with Pbx/Meis cofactors. Instead the signed-score correlations were near zero and Hoxa1, Foxn1, Meis1 and Pbx3 had no FDR<0.10 groups, while Tbx1, Pbx1 and Meis2 each produced only one isolated significant gene.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed over many null features; they are useful chiefly for rejecting hidden convergence, not for assigning weak nominal genes to biology.
summary: The de novo Hoxa3 signature neighbors are random-like rather than a hidden convergent pathway.
why_it_matters: The strongest biological positive neighbor was Pax4 at r=0.028722 and the strongest negative neighbor was Lrpprc at r=-0.015797 across the signed Wilcoxon profile; querying Pax4, Cit, Tgfbr2, Chmp4b, Lrpprc, Bmpr1b, Chrm3 and Purg found only 0-2 significant groups per target and no possible shared Hoxa3 FDR genes.

literature_claim: Hoxb8 loss-of-function phenotypes are established in germline mice and in posterior spinal or microglial contexts, not by acute sparse loss in juvenile forebrain and midbrain neurons.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation was not measured, and a flat Hoxb8 RNA row is not proof that individual edited alleles were uncut.
summary: Acute P16 Hoxb8 perturbation produced no robust neuronal transcriptional response in any of the 23 recovered brain cell groups.
why_it_matters: This clean pan-surface zero constrains Hoxb8 loss-of-function biology away from broadly cell-autonomous effects in the surveyed postmitotic neurons; the known Hoxb8 grooming and sensory defects must be sought in other stages or lineages rather than in a hidden FDR-significant program in this dataset.

main_caveats: Metric is whole-surface rank-score correlation of a null target; it is useful for rejecting convergence, not for interpreting the nominal neighbor identities.
summary: The Hoxb8 score vector had no meaningful transcriptomic neighbor: even the most positive and most negative genome-wide comparators had |r| ≤ 0.032.
why_it_matters: Because the nearest neighbors are essentially zero-correlation null signatures, no alternative target nominates a masked Hoxb8-like response module for follow-up.

literature_claim: Hox transcription factors act in AP-patterning niches and often use Pbx/Meis cofactors, with HoxB8-Pbx coupling documented in myeloid differentiation models.
main_caveats: The true group-8 paralogs Hoxa8, Hoxc8, and Hoxd8 were not perturbation targets; comparator responses were mostly single-gene and therefore rejection of convergence is stronger than any positive contrast among them.
summary: Represented Hox genes and the Pbx/Meis TALE cofactors did not converge with Hoxb8 in this postnatal neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: The absence of a shared Hox/Pbx/Meis program argues that the null is context-wide for the assayed developmental Hox axis, rather than a Hoxb8-only accident.

literature_claim: Hoxb8 mutant grooming/anxiety phenotypes have been linked to Hoxb8-lineage microglia and to downstream corticostriatal circuit defects, while spinal sensory phenotypes map to posterior Hoxb8 domains.
main_caveats: A mosaic transcriptome screen cannot distinguish failure to perturb the correct Hoxb8-expressing cells from a real absence of adult neuronal requirements within rare unsampled nuclei.
summary: The neuronal all-null surface is most consistent with Hoxb8-linked grooming and anxiety phenotypes being microglial or developmental-circuit phenomena, not acute transcriptional defects of the sampled neurons.
why_it_matters: A neuronal CRISPR strategy against Hoxb8 at juvenile stages would be a poor phenocopy of the pathological-grooming model; Hoxb8-lineage microglia and spinal/posterior developmental compartments are better-justified mechanistic targets.

main_caveats: Only 25 perturbed nuclei supported the call, and a single up-regulated gene does not establish a pathway-level Hoxd10 response.
summary: The only reproducible Hoxd10 call was Tut1 up-regulation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with no broader FDR<0.10 cascade.
why_it_matters: This preserves the lone positive signal without inflating it into a canonical Hox program; Tut1 is a hypothesis-generating marker of the rare cell group in which the screen detected any Hoxd10-dependent RNA change.

literature_claim: Hox proteins act as sequence-specific developmental transcription factors, often with Pbx/Meis cofactors; Hox10 paralogs are known to cooperate in lumbar motor-neuron patterning.
main_caveats: The exact Hox10 partners Hoxa10 and Hoxc10 were not perturbation targets; represented Hox13/Hox1/Hox3/Hox8 family members are only family-level comparators.
summary: Represented Hox-family targets and Pbx/Meis Hox cofactors did not phenocopy Hoxd10 in the matched P16 brain groups.
why_it_matters: The expected Hox regulatory neighborhood was measurable for several family members and cofactors, but all were null or private one/two-gene responders; the Hoxd10 zero is therefore a local absence of a postnatal Hox/TALE module rather than a hidden signature shared with a related perturbation.

main_caveats: The cosine calculation is dominated by a null Hoxd10 vector, so it is useful mainly to reject robust convergence, not to nominate mechanism.
summary: Unbiased whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no strong Hoxd10 signature neighbor or anti-neighbor.
why_it_matters: Because the closest gene-coded score-vector cosines were only +0.0277 to -0.0211 and the top neighbors themselves had at most two FDR<0.10 genes, the measured Hoxd10 surface is best treated as a near-null surface rather than as a weak sample of a known module.

literature_claim: Hoxd10 is deployed in embryonic lumbosacral spinal cord and, with Hoxc10, controls lumbar motor-column, divisional, and motor-pool identity.
main_caveats: The assay would not capture embryonic changes in unsampled spinal motor neurons; the marker test is a negative check that those markers were not secondarily induced in the sampled brain groups.
summary: The perturbation did not ectopically reveal the embryonic lumbar motor-neuron program expected from Hoxd10 biology.
why_it_matters: Lumbar LMC and motor-neuron markers such as Lhx1, Isl1, Isl2, Lhx3/Lhx4, Mnx1, Foxp1, Etv1/Etv4, and Aldh1a2 were FDR-flat, arguing that forebrain, midbrain, and pineal-associated P16 neurons never entered the Hoxd10-responsive spinal developmental state.

literature_claim: Hoxd13 biology is concentrated in embryonic posterior Hox programs such as distal limb/autopod patterning and caudal neural-tube patterning, not in specified postnatal forebrain, thalamic, midbrain, or cerebellar neurons.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured; the result is a high-confidence transcriptomic null only for recovered neuronal cell groups.
summary: Hoxd13 targeting produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every one of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups; 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset finding is a broad negative result in postmitotic P16-to-P44 brain neurons, not a missed single-cell-type response.

literature_claim: HOXD13 and HOXA13 regulate embryonic distal-limb/autopod and skeletal genes, including HOXD13-linked Sfrp1, Barx1, and Fbn1 and HOX13-associated BMP/WNT/FGF/SHH signaling programs.
main_caveats: Only genes expressed and retained in the snRNA-seq DE gene set could be checked; the true limb mesenchymal target cells were absent.
summary: Expected HOX13 embryonic limb and skeletal-patterning readouts were not induced or repressed by Hoxd13 in the brain screen.
why_it_matters: The absent limb-patterning genes show that the flat surface is not hiding a weak canonical Hox13 program; the sampled nuclei are outside the HOXD13 target-gene competence window.

main_caveats: Cosine comparison used all Wilcoxon-score directions and is descriptive; the top negative raw labels included Safe_target controls and were not interpreted biologically.
summary: Hoxd13 had no strong data-driven signature neighbors; top unbiased cosine similarities were near zero.
why_it_matters: A whole-universe comparison failed to reveal a noncanonical Hoxd13-like neuronal module, so positive interpretation should not be built from nominal Hoxd13 genes.

literature_claim: Hoxa13 is partly redundant with Hoxd13 in distal limb patterning, and PBX proteins act as HOX cofactors in spinal motor-neuron fate programs.
main_caveats: Most compared perturbations were themselves null; the only Hoxa13/Hoxd10 differential expression occurred in low-count 217 P MY Pineal Glut signatures.
summary: Represented HOX paralogs and PBX/MEIS cofactors did not converge with Hoxd13 in matched postnatal brain groups.
why_it_matters: The expected Hox13 and HOX/PBX relationships are developmentally gated: Hoxa13/Hoxd13 limb redundancy and Pbx-dependent spinal patterning do not translate into a postnatal neuronal HOX network in this assay.

literature_claim: Hras and Nras are individually and jointly dispensable for gross mouse growth and neuronal development when Kras is retained.
main_caveats: No DNA indel data were available, 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for Hras, and this does not test activating HRAS alleles or Ras-family combinations.
summary: Single Hras perturbation produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The dominant biological signal is buffering: acute loss of one classical Ras isoform after neuronal specification did not impose a corrected RNA state across cortex, hippocampal/amygdalar, thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain-adjacent, and cerebellar neuronal classes.

literature_claim: Canonical Ras signaling couples HRAS-family GTPases through RAF, MEK, and ERK to ERK-feedback transcriptional outputs.
main_caveats: The comparator signatures were sparse, Nras was not represented as a perturbation target, and Hras itself had no FDR genes for a shared-DE overlap test.
summary: Hras failed to phenocopy represented Ras/MAPK neighbors, even in the thalamic cell class where Braf and Map2k1 both down-regulated Vgf, Ptpn5, and Unc13a.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates canonical pathway membership from measured postnatal neuronal LoF phenotypes: RAF/MEK perturbations could be detected, but their sparse signatures were not upstreamed to Hras.

literature_claim: Ras/ERK signaling induces nuclear transcription and negative feedback, and hyperactive HRASG12V increases ERK signaling in mouse brain.
main_caveats: The assay measured basal post-perturbation RNA, not acute growth-factor- or activity-evoked ERK transcription.
summary: The expected basal Ras/ERK feedback and immediate-early module was not recovered after Hras loss.
why_it_matters: DUSPs, Spry, ETV factors, Fos/Jun/Egr genes, Arc, and Npas4 are transcriptional readouts that snRNA-seq should be able to detect if basal HRAS loss collapsed ERK-output transcription; their corrected absence makes this a pathway-level negative result rather than a pure readout failure.

main_caveats: Cosine similarity was calculated on Wilcoxon scores from largely null Hras vectors; the result is most useful as a rejection of strong convergence, not as a mechanistic link to the named neighbors.
summary: A whole-universe score-cosine search found no strong positive or negative Hras signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: This rejects the possibility that Hras was secretly part of a broad, recurrent stress or perturbation-quality module; the null signature remained near-orthogonal to all other represented targets.

literature_claim: Germline Hs6st2 knockout in adult mice alters hippocampal RNA-seq and only mildly affects cortex.
main_caveats: DNA indels and HS 6-O-sulfation were not assayed; the screen was sparse, postmitotic, and acute relative to germline KO.
summary: Hs6st2 had no robust downstream transcriptional response in any measured cell group.
why_it_matters: The central dataset result is a complete FDR-controlled downstream null, not a cell-type-restricted positive signature hidden in nominal genes.

literature_claim: Adult whole-animal Hs6st2 knockout down-regulates dendrite and glutamatergic synapse genes and up-regulates ribosome and protein-translation genes in hippocampus.
main_caveats: The assay groups aggregate hippocampal subfields and do not isolate CA1 pyramidal neurons; no spine or glycan endpoint was measured.
summary: The published hippocampal dendrite/synapse-down and ribosome/translation-up programs were absent from the two hippocampal excitatory groups.
why_it_matters: The expected secondary transcriptional phenotype should be visible in RNA-seq if it were reproduced, so its absence argues that the germline CA1 phenotype is not an immediate P16-onset cell-autonomous snRNA-seq program.

literature_claim: HS modification genes and FGFR1 can act in one pathway; Hs6st1 and Fgfr1 knockdown in mouse neuronal cells converge on ECM-up and chromatin-down transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: Hs6st1 and Hs6st3 paralogs were not target perturbations; available Ext/Fgfr comparators were single knockouts rather than combinatorial HS edits.
summary: Measurable HS-chain and FGF-receptor perturbations did not phenocopy Hs6st2, and Hs6st1/Hs6st3 were absent as targets.
why_it_matters: The literature-obvious HS/FGFR pathway failed as a convergent acute neuronal transcriptional module; Ext1, Ext2, Fgfr1, Fgfr2, and Fgfr3 produced at most singleton DE genes and near-zero score correlations to Hs6st2.

main_caveats: A correlation of noise-level signatures is a computational negative, not evidence that Hs6st2 has no glycan or morphological function.
summary: Hs6st2 sits near the origin of cross-perturbation signature space.
why_it_matters: The top data-driven neighbors were not strong biological neighbors: the strongest positive and negative correlations to the Hs6st2 Wilcoxon-score vector were only 0.0312 and -0.0171, consistent with a target whose measured signature is dominated by noise-level ranks.

literature_claim: HS6ST2 is linked to X-linked neurodevelopmental disease, Hs6st2 KO affects memory and CA1 dendritic spines, and HSPG sulfation participates in developmental axon and synapse biology.
main_caveats: A loss-of-function screen cannot test whether gene replacement or glycan modulation would rescue established extracellular or spine defects.
summary: The screen separates HS6ST2-linked disease biology from an acutely reversible postnatal neuronal DE cascade.
why_it_matters: Human variants and mouse germline KO establish nervous-system relevance, but the Perturb-seq null warns that a 3-4 week postmitotic mosaic loss does not recreate the hippocampal KO transcriptome; disease mechanisms may be displaced to early wiring, whole-tissue glycan remodeling, or non-transcriptional spine phenotypes.

literature_claim: HSD17B4/MFP2 deficiency disrupts peroxisomal beta-oxidation and causes organismal neurologic disease in humans and mice.
main_caveats: DNA indels, protein loss, lipid-metabolite accumulation, and non-neuronal responses were not measured.
summary: Hsd17b4 loss of function produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptional null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 21 recovered cell groups.
why_it_matters: This separates acute sparse postmitotic neuronal Hsd17b4 editing from the severe metabolic and neurologic phenotypes produced by germline or broad neural MFP2 deficiency.

literature_claim: ABCD3 participates with HSD17B4 in peroxisomal fatty-acid oxidation, ACBD5 controls peroxisome-ER lipid handling, and PEX1/PEX14 act upstream in peroxisomal matrix import.
main_caveats: Shared-direction overlap is necessarily zero because Hsd17b4 itself has no significant downstream genes; Pex1 singleton hits were not pathway-coherent.
summary: Directly measured peroxisomal relatives did not phenocopy Hsd17b4; Abcd3, Acbd5, and Pex14 were flat and Pex1 had only two isolated singleton FDR hits.
why_it_matters: The null is broader than a single enzyme: perturbing represented transporter and import arms of the peroxisome system still failed to reveal a coherent acute neuronal RNA module.

main_caveats: The comparison used all raw Wilcoxon scores after Hsd17b4 had no FDR-defined signature, so it is useful mainly as a rejection of robust convergence.
summary: The Hsd17b4 raw full-transcriptome surface had no robust data-driven signature neighbor; the top positive and negative Pearson correlations were only 0.029 and -0.020.
why_it_matters: This rejects the possibility that Hsd17b4 had a reproducible but unannotated weak signature shared with other perturbations in the model-visible universe.

literature_claim: Severe MFP2 loss can induce liver PPARalpha/SREBP2 lipid feedback and neural MFP2 loss alters Purkinje function and integrity; HSD17B4 is also part of a broader Perrault disease family.
main_caveats: The PPAR/SREBP prior is liver-derived, and the Purkinje prior includes electrophysiologic and axonal phenotypes that need not appear as soma snRNA changes.

why_it_matters: The null extends beyond total DEG counts to programs predicted by severe MFP2 deficiency; there was no detectable neuronal PPAR/SREBP rebound or stress response within 3-4 weeks of P16 editing.

literature_claim: HSF1 is the stress-activated transcription factor for mammalian HSP genes, and Ahsa/Stip proteins function in the HSP90-HSP70 chaperone system.
main_caveats: The signature is only 12 cell-gene calls across four groups, and Hspa1a/b or Dnajb1 were not FDR-significant in this unstressed snRNA-seq assay.
summary: Postnatal Hsf1 loss reproducibly depresses a small HSP90/HSP110 co-chaperone module rather than activating a large mixed stress program.
why_it_matters: The only robust Hsf1-positive biology is the expected direct transcription-factor output: Hsph1, Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Ahsa2 and Stip1 fall in selected neuronal classes, all in the perturbed-versus-control down direction.

literature_claim: HSF1 controls heat-shock targets but is latent and context regulated in basal cells.
main_caveats: The four effect groups include the two largest Hsf1 samples, so weak groups with 63-112 perturbed cells could contain the same program below the q-value threshold.
summary: Basal HSF1 dependence is sharply cell-type restricted in this P16-P44 neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: Only four of 22 measured cell groups had downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for Hsf1; therefore the screen nominates Pvalb, thalamic, hypothalamic, and midbrain glutamatergic neurons as the populations with detectable constitutive HSF1 output.

literature_claim: Proteasome impairment can drive HSF1-dependent heat-shock induction and Nrf1-dependent replacement proteasome transcription.
main_caveats: The screen was not a heat-shock or proteasome-inhibitor challenge, so it tests basal buffered loss rather than the maximum HSF1-inducible response.
summary: Hsf1 loss did not itself produce a proteotoxic-stress, UPR/ISR, proteasome-bounce-back, redox, apoptosis, or mitochondrial stress transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Genes that would mark a secondary stress cascade, including Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Atf3, Atf4, Ddit3, Xbp1, Chac1, Ppp1r15a, Bax, Ubc and proteasome subunits, were not significant, so the direct chaperone decrease appears buffered over 3-4 weeks in young postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Loss of ubiquitin-proteasome function causes HSF1-dependent heat-shock induction.
main_caveats: The proteasome signatures were much broader than Hsf1 and arose from individual subunit perturbations, not pharmacologic proteasome inhibition.
summary: Proteasome-subunit perturbations run the Hsf1 HSP signature in the opposite direction.
why_it_matters: Psmc1 and Psmb4 were the top opposite FDR-overlap neighbors: they increased several of the same Hsph1/Hsp90/Ahsa2/Stip1 genes that Hsf1 decreased, indicating that Hsf1 CRISPR removes a downstream transcriptional effector whereas 26S proteasome damage creates an upstream proteotoxic load that activates compensatory chaperones.

literature_claim: HSP90 and HSP70 chaperones are negative feedback regulators of HSF1 activation.
main_caveats: Hspa8 support comes from a restricted 12-dimension cosine and one robust thalamic chaperone up-regulation; Hsp90ab1 may be buffered by the remaining HSP90 alpha isoform, which was not a represented perturbation.
summary: Chaperone loss is not equivalent to Hsf1 loss: Hspa8 partially anti-phenocopies Hsf1, and Hsp90ab1 knockdown is almost exclusively on-target.
why_it_matters: The strongest raw negative Hsf1 neighbor was Hspa8, which increased Dnaja1 and Hsp90aa1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, matching the Hsp70/Hsp90 literature in which these chaperones repress HSF1; by contrast, direct Hsp90ab1 loss showed strong Hsp90ab1 mRNA depletion in many groups without recreating the Hsf1 downstream program.

literature_claim: No direct HSF1-Sin3a-Prpf6-U2af2 convergence was used as a prior; these neighbors were nominated by the parquet.
main_caveats: The comparator signatures are much larger than Hsf1 and only overlap a restricted HSP/Rsrp1 subset.
summary: The leading non-Hsp same-direction neighbors were Sin3a, Prpf6, and U2af2, not other heat-shock factors.
why_it_matters: These broad chromatin and RNA-processing perturbations repeatedly decreased Rsrp1 and subsets of the Hsp90/Hsph1/Ahsa2/Mat2a module, so the Hsf1 signature is also a node of a neuronal RNA/chromatin vulnerability program rather than a fingerprint unique to HSF1.

literature_claim: The heat-shock, Nrf1 proteasome-bounce-back, ER-UPR, and oxidative-stress branches are related proteostasis pathways but have distinct upstream transcription factors.
main_caveats: Atf6 and Nfe2l2 were themselves null in this assay, so their rejection as Hsf1 phenocopies is stronger for the measured basal screen than for a stress-inducible experiment.
summary: Nrf1, Atf6, Nfe2l2, and Vcp were measured stress-branch comparators but did not phenocopy Hsf1.
why_it_matters: This rejects a generic stress-factor interpretation: Nrf1 produced a broad, Rsrp1-containing signature, Atf6 and Nfe2l2 were transcriptionally flat, and Vcp had only six hits, none of which reproduced the Hsf1 Hsp90/Hsp110 co-chaperone pattern.

literature_claim: No established Rsrp1-HSF1 relationship was required for this nomination.
main_caveats: Rsrp1 is not specific to Hsf1; it is also down-regulated by Nrf1 and several RNA-processing perturbations.
summary: Rsrp1 is the most recurrent non-classical transcript in the Hsf1 neuronal signature.
why_it_matters: Rsrp1 fell in three of the four robust Hsf1 responders and is also the dominant shared gene in U2af2, Sin3a, Prpf6, and Nrf1 comparisons, making it a practical hypothesis marker for a postnatal neuronal chaperone/RNA-processing state even though it is not a textbook HSP.

literature_claim: Hsp90ab1 encodes the constitutive cytosolic Hsp90β chaperone, and mouse Hsp90β is essential in germline developmental models.
main_caveats: The screen did not sequence on-target indels or assay Hsp90 protein/client abundance; Hsp90β embryonic essentiality is not directly tested by sparse postnatal neuronal perturbation.
summary: Acute Hsp90ab1 loss was transcriptionally buffered across every assayed neuronal class: all 23 groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite a negative Hsp90ab1 snRNA logFC in every group.
why_it_matters: The result separates DNA-level CRISPR engagement from a downstream stress phenotype; in this P16 postmitotic mosaic context, reducing the constitutive cytosolic Hsp90β isoform alone did not make a detectable neuronal heat-shock, UPR or synaptic state.

literature_claim: Hsp90 participates in HSF1 regulation, and activated HSF1 transcribes Hsp90, Hsp70, Hsp40 and small-HSP genes.
main_caveats: The literature expectation is strongest for heat shock or pharmacological/pan-Hsp90 inhibition, not for sparse single-Hsp90ab1 CRISPR.
summary: The canonical HSF1 heat-shock output expected after strong Hsp90 blockade, and broader ISR/UPR/autophagy stress reporters, were absent after Hsp90ab1 CRISPR.
why_it_matters: The null is mechanistic rather than merely low-powered: a cytosolic-chaperone stress program should be visible by snRNA-seq if single-isoform Hsp90β editing had collapsed proteostasis.

literature_claim: Hsp90/Hsp70 chaperones and the ubiquitin-proteasome system are linked through client triage, including CHIP-mediated degradation of chaperone-bound clients.
main_caveats: Psmb4 and Psmc1 perturb core proteasome activity rather than the Hsp90 foldase itself, so their signatures are a positive assay control and contrast rather than a same-complex phenocopy.
summary: The same assay readily detected proteotoxic remodeling when the 26S proteasome was hit: Psmb4 and Psmc1 generated 14008 and 11089 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, respectively, and in 155 MB Glut they shared 1823 same-direction DE genes while Hsp90ab1 had none.
why_it_matters: FDR-supported induction of Hsph1, Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Ubc and proteasome transcripts, with concurrent depression of Atp1a3, Slc17a6 and Scn1a, shows that snRNA-seq would have captured a large proteostasis-to-neuronal-function state change if Hsp90ab1 loss had produced one.

literature_claim: Hsp70, Hsp40/J proteins, HSF1 and Hsp90 form the cytosolic proteostatic response machinery, but they are not all obligate unstressed transcriptional state regulators.
main_caveats: Several canonical Hsp90 partners, including Hsp90aa1, Cdc37, Stip1, Ahsa1 and Ptges3, were not perturbation targets in this parquet.
summary: Measured Hsp90-neighborhood perturbations did not phenocopy Hsp90ab1 or the core proteasome program: Hsf1, Hspa5, Hspa8 and Vcp produced only 6-24 downstream DE genes in total, and represented DnaJ perturbations were essentially flat.
why_it_matters: The Hsp90ab1 null sits in a broader pattern in which single heat-shock/chaperone nodes are buffered in unstressed juvenile neurons, whereas proteasome subunits are not.

literature_claim: No prior biological neighbor was implicated by this de novo near-zero cosine search.
main_caveats: Neighbor scoring used the full signed-score surface because Hsp90ab1 had no FDR<0.10 downstream signature to overlap.
summary: Hsp90ab1 had no meaningful whole-surface signature neighbor: full signed-score cosines were only +0.0275 for the top positive gene Psmb4 and -0.0126 for the top negative gene Npy1r, with safe-target signatures among the extreme negative and positive ranks.
why_it_matters: The nominal vector should not be over-interpreted; most top Hsp90ab1 neighbors were themselves null, so the data-driven search rejects a hidden convergent module.

literature_claim: Hsp90 inhibitors are druggable proteostasis modulators, including in neurodegeneration models where HSF1/Hsp70 induction is often part of the desired mechanism.
main_caveats: No disease-associated aggregates, tumors, pharmacological inhibitor exposure or protein-client measurements were present in this screen.
summary: A single Hsp90β hypomorph in normal postmitotic neurons did not reproduce the biology usually sought with Hsp90-directed drugs—HSF1/Hsp70 induction and proteotoxic client triage—so this negative result should not be read as a negative pan-Hsp90-inhibitor test.
why_it_matters: For neurodegeneration or cancer logic, pan-Hsp90 ATPase inhibition, isoform-selective Hsp90β inhibition, and sparse CRISPR of Hsp90ab1 are different perturbations; this dataset only supports the third in a healthy juvenile neuronal background.

literature_claim: HSPA5/BiP is a broadly required ER chaperone; complete mouse loss is embryonic lethal and conditional neuronal loss can kill Purkinje cells.
main_caveats: The DE test conditions on recovered NeuN+ nuclei and does not measure edited-cell abundance or DNA indels; 145 and 308 have very small signatures and low perturbed-cell counts.
summary: Hspa5 loss was not pan-neuronal: 16 of 19 measured groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream gene, whereas 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut carried a 20-gene ER-stress signature and 145 MH-LH TH Glut and 308 CB GABA carried only 3- and 1-gene tails.
why_it_matters: BiP is a ubiquitous ER chaperone, so the dataset refines an apparently essential pathway into a high-threshold, cell-class-restricted transcriptional response after P16 sparse CRISPR in surviving neurons.

literature_claim: BiP restrains ER stress sensors, and ER stress induces chaperone, folding, and ERAD genes to restore ER proteostasis.
main_caveats: The branch assignment is transcript-based; Xbp1 was not significantly induced by Hspa5, and IRE1 splicing was not measured by 3-prime snRNA-seq.
summary: The main 151 response was induction of an ER folding and ER-associated degradation module, with Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Derl3, Creld2, Sel1l, and Herpud1 among the corrected up-regulated genes.

Thus the screen would have reported a broad secondary nuclear aftermath if one had persisted for 3-4 weeks, but none was detectable.

literature_claim: The strongest HTR2C loss-of-function phenotypes map to appetite and arousal/excitability circuits, POMC neurons, and highly Htr2c-expressing choroid plexus, not to a ubiquitous neuronal transcription factor function.
main_caveats: The assay did not resolve arcuate POMC neurons, measure choroid plexus, stimulate serotonin receptors, or read out membrane excitability.
summary: The flat Htr2c DE surface should not be read as a loss-of-function phenocopy of HTR2C obesity biology failing to exist.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse HTR2C loss of function affects appetite, body weight, behavior, and network excitability, whereas this experiment samples unstimulated postmitotic nuclei and largely excludes choroid-plexus epithelium. The dataset therefore warns that a basal whole-transcriptome null underestimates ligand-gated GPCR targets whose actionable biology is rare-cell physiology and circuit state.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The neighbor metric used score Pearson over broad cell-group matched genes; a different readout such as DNA indels or electrophysiology was not compared.
summary: A data-driven search found no meaningful positive or negative Htr2c signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Before applying serotonin priors, the all-target Wilcoxon-score scan placed Htr2c on the noise/null manifold: even the best non-safe positive and negative neighbors had |r|<0.03 and no shared FDR-significant response with Htr2c. Downstream interpretation should therefore be anchored on the absence of a reproducible Htr2c signature rather than on a weak nominal-gene pattern.
