literature_claim: MANBA encodes lysosomal β-mannosidase; full β-mannosidase deficiency causes progressive β-mannosidosis with neuronal oligosaccharide storage and anatomically selective vacuolation in mouse brain.
main_caveats: No DNA indel, MANBA enzyme-activity, or oligosaccharide-storage measurement is available, so the result is a transcriptional absence rather than proof that edited neurons retained normal lysosomal chemistry.
summary: P16 mosaic Manba loss produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 22 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and queried lysosomal, autophagy, unfolded-protein, and integrated-stress markers also had no FDR signal.
why_it_matters: The canonical MANBA lesion is lysosomal storage, so the absence of even a secondary TFEB/autophagy/ISR program is informative: sparse postnatal Manba loss did not generate an acute cell-autonomous lysosomal-stress transcriptome in juvenile neurons.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Many soluble lysosomal enzymes traffic through M6P-dependent sorting and can enter neighboring cells through M6P-receptor-mediated secretion-recapture; GNPTAB/GNPTG initiate the M6P tag on lysosomal enzymes.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure enzyme cross-correction directly, GNPTAB/GNPTG perturbations also had weak target-transcript depletion, and the represented panel lacks closer modeled targets such as Aga, Man2b1, Hexa, Hexb, Glb1, Gba1, and Neu1.
summary: The flat Manba phenotype was shared by represented lysosomal hydrolase and M6P-trafficking targets: Gaa, Ppt1, Ctsb, Gnptab, and Gnptg each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in Manba-matched groups, despite strong self-transcript depletion for several of them.
why_it_matters: A class-level flat soluble-hydrolase surface argues against treating Manba as an isolated failed guide set; it is consistent with a mosaic system in which secreted, M6P-tagged lysosomal enzymes can be recaptured from WT neighbors and with a short assay window that does not accumulate storage burden.

literature_claim: No specific prior literature predicted convergence between Manba and these data-driven neighbors.
main_caveats: Cosines were computed from whole signed Wilcoxon-score vectors; because Manba had no FDR genes, the comparison can reject convergence but cannot nominate shared driver genes.
summary: The genome-scale signed-score search found no meaningful Manba signature neighbor: the best positive cosine was Kif1a at 0.02460 and the strongest negative was Fbxo11 at -0.01694, and these top neighbors failed to share an FDR-supported Manba program on re-query.
why_it_matters: For a null target, nearest-neighbor analysis can otherwise overinterpret noise; the near-zero extrema show that Manba is best modeled as an unstructured flat signature rather than as a member of an unexpected transcriptional module.

literature_claim: V-ATPase subunits acidify lysosomes; impaired lysosomal acidification is predicted to disrupt degradative and autophagic flux in neurons.
main_caveats: Atp6v1e1 affected only 10 genes and two responsive groups had fewer than 30 perturbed nuclei, so this is a restricted, comparator-only contrast rather than a robust V-ATPase program.
summary: V-ATPase perturbations did not phenocopy Manba: Atp6v0a1 was flat across all 22 matched groups, while Atp6v1e1 produced only 10 FDR<0.10 downstream genes concentrated in 308 CB GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: Loss of a proton-pump subunit should be a more cell-autonomous route to lysosomal dysfunction than loss of one soluble glycosidase; its different, still weak surface reinforces that Manba's negative result is not simply a generic lysosome signature falling below the FDR cutoff.

literature_claim: MANF is an ER-resident BiP/IRE1-linked regulator whose loss or mutation increases UPR signaling.
main_caveats: Xbp1 splicing, PERK phosphorylation, and MANF protein loss were not measured; Hspa5 up-regulation is a downstream stress readout, not a direct indel assay.
summary: Manf loss elicited a recurrent, adaptive ER-chaperone/ER-protein-processing module rather than a broad neuronal identity program.
why_it_matters: Hspa5/BiP was the dominant corrected hit, with Hyou1, Pdia6, Dnajb9, Sdf2l1, Ppib, Rpn1, Txndc5, and Sec11c appearing in the deeper responder groups, directly tying the screen phenotype to MANF's ER quality-control function.

literature_claim: Whole-region Manf knockouts activate UPR in cortex, striatum, hippocampus, substantia nigra, and cerebellum, while MANF/CDNF effects are tissue-specific.
main_caveats: Cell groups are broad neuronal classes; the absence of glia and the mosaic design can make regional literature and this single-nucleus surface non-equivalent.
summary: The Manf UPR was strongly cell-group restricted: 10 of 23 measured groups had any corrected downstream hit and only CNU-MGE GABA, CNU-HYa/HY GABA, MB Glut, and MB/Pons/My GABA carried multi-gene chaperone signatures.
why_it_matters: Sparse postnatal Manf loss did not cause a pan-neuronal stress state; it crossed the transcriptional ER-stress threshold only in selected inhibitory, midbrain, thalamic, and NP/CT-related populations.

literature_claim: Gfpt1 deficiency can provoke ER stress, Sec63 feeds ER translocation through BiP, and CDNF is MANF's ER-neurotrophic paralog.
main_caveats: The neighbor score was restricted to 34 significant Manf feature hits and therefore detects convergence on the observed Hspa5 module rather than full-transcriptome equivalence.
summary: The most robust positive signature neighbors were ER-load perturbations, especially Gfpt1 and Dhdds, not the textbook MANF paralog CDNF or the measured upstream branch target Atf6.
why_it_matters: The screen places Manf with glycosylation, protein-translocation, and ER-calcium stressors by measured output, implying that acute loss of the BiP/IRE1 modulator is sensed as impaired ER client handling.

literature_claim: UPR signaling can either restore ER homeostasis or progress to unresolved, pro-apoptotic stress; beta-cell Manf loss is terminal whereas Manf-deficient neurons can sustain UPR without dopamine neuron loss.
main_caveats: Gene-level snRNA-seq does not measure Xbp1 splicing or eIF2α phosphorylation, so branch assignment is inferred from corrected downstream transcripts.
summary: Manf activated chaperone genes without the severe ATF4/CHOP-like ISR module that appeared after Gfpt1 and Atp2a2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The distinction separates a buffered ER-homeostatic response from a stronger terminal-stress trajectory: Ddit3, Chac1, and Asns were absent from Manf while they were prominent in Gfpt1 and Atp2a2 surfaces.

literature_claim: MANF can regulate autophagy/lysosome or stimulate autophagy in non-neuronal toxic-proteostasis settings.
main_caveats: Autophagic flux is a protein/organelle phenotype; the conclusion is limited to absence of a corrected autophagy-lysosome RNA module and to represented autophagy guide targets.
summary: Manf loss did not recover an autophagy-lysosome transcriptional program and did not phenocopy core autophagy knockouts; Rb1cc1 instead induced the opposite chaperone direction in a subset of Manf feature genes.
why_it_matters: MANF has been tied to autophagy and lysosome function in worm and kidney proteinopathy contexts, but the P16 neuronal loss-of-function state here was dominated by ER folding genes and was transcriptionally separable from Rb1cc1/Becn1/Atg5/Atg16l1 perturbation.

literature_claim: MANF interacts functionally with BiP/HSPA5 and UPR signaling centered on IRE1, PERK, and ATF6.
main_caveats: Atf6 and Hspa5 target engagement was judged only from transcriptomics; Hspa5 is essential and its own transcript did not show corrected knockdown.
summary: Atf6 and Hspa5 perturbations were rejected as Manf phenocopies in matched neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Although MANF is mechanistically tied to UPR sensors and BiP, simply targeting Atf6 or Hspa5 did not reproduce the Manf Hspa5/Hyou1/Pdia6 module, indicating that the Manf signature is not a generic consequence of weakly perturbing any UPR-axis component.

main_caveats: Each of these non-core genes was significant in only one Manf cell group; the pineal/P-MY Snd1-only response had just 34 perturbed cells.
summary: Several corrected Manf hits were cell-specific singletons outside the core Hspa5 module.
why_it_matters: Mtor up-regulation was unique to L4/5 IT cortex, Kcna1 up and Agpat4 down occurred only in CNU-MGE GABA, Mia3/Copa up and Cacna2d2 down were restricted to MB/Pons/My GABA, and P/MY/Pineal Glut had only Snd1; these events should be treated as local secondary hypotheses, not as universal MANF biology.

literature_claim: MAP1B biology is dominated by microtubule, axon-branching, and dendritic-spine phenotypes rather than by a defined transcriptional cascade.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation and MAP1B protein abundance were not measured; the conclusion is limited to nuclear RNA 3-4 weeks after P16 perturbation.
summary: Map1b produced a transcript-self-only response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut: the Map1b transcript was significantly lower, but no non-Map1b transcript reached FDR<0.10 in either group or anywhere else.
why_it_matters: Detectable suppression of the target mRNA can coexist with a complete absence of downstream nuclear DE, arguing that postmitotic Map1b loss is buffered at the snRNA-seq state level rather than that every weak self-transcript group is automatically a failed guide.

literature_claim: MAP1B participates in axon guidance and in a GSK3β-regulated tubulin-tyrosination pathway that changes cortical axon interstitial branching.
main_caveats: Only nuclear mRNA was assayed; tyrosinated tubulin, phosphorylated MAP1B, EB3 dynamics, axon branches, and spines were not measured.
summary: Map1b loss failed to regulate the literature-nominated tubulin-tyrosination, axon-growth, neuronal-migration, and GSK3/MAP1B marker set at RNA level in all 22 measured groups.
why_it_matters: The GSK3β/MAP1B branch phenotype is mediated through post-translational tubulin code and axon morphology, so the absence of Ttl, Vash1, Vash2, Svbp, Tuba1a/Tubb, Gap43, Stmn2, or Reln/Dab1 RNA changes is a negative result for a nuclear compensatory program, not evidence that those structural phenotypes would be absent under an imaging or proteomic readout.

main_caveats: The comparison was based on Wilcoxon-score correlations across matched assayed features; the Safe_target numerical extrema reinforce that the Map1b profile is nearly flat.
summary: The full-universe signature search found no meaningful Map1b neighborhood: the largest named-gene Pearson correlations were only +0.0308 to Syn1 and -0.0154 to Sipa1l3.
why_it_matters: A target with an undiscovered compensatory module would usually pull a coherent cross-perturbation neighborhood; here the nearest neighbors are effect-size noise with zero shared FDR-level Map1b downstream genes.

literature_claim: MAP1B, Tau, and MAP2 are developmentally important neuronal MAPs with synergistic or overlapping microtubule roles in knockout mice.
main_caveats: Map1a and Map2 were not perturbation targets, so the most textbook MAP1B paralog and dendritic MAP2 could not be measured directly.
summary: Mapt, Map6, Map1lc3a, and Mapre2 did not phenocopy Map1b, each producing 0 downstream DE genes at FDR<0.10 across the 22 Map1b-matched groups and Pearson r values from -0.0037 to 0.0173.
why_it_matters: The expected MAP-family relationship collapses in this acute postnatal snRNA assay: Tau/MAP1B or MAP2/MAP1B synergy described in germline development does not translate into a single-gene nuclear RNA state for Mapt or Map1b.

literature_claim: Dynactin is a microtubule-based axonal-transport component required for initiation of retrograde transport from the distal axon.
main_caveats: The sterol program was observed after Dctn1 perturbation, not Map1b perturbation; the mechanistic bridge from dynactin disruption to cholesterol-gene induction is inferred from the DE signature.
summary: Dctn1, unlike Map1b, triggered a broad sterol/SREBP-like response in the same analysis universe, with 450 downstream DE genes across 12 Map1b-matched groups and strong up-regulation of Insig1, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Fdps, Ldlr, Hmgcr, Fdft1, and Sqle.
why_it_matters: The Dctn1 contrast shows that postmitotic neurons in this dataset can convert a microtubule-transport perturbation into a robust nuclear homeostatic program; Map1b's absence of such a program is therefore biologically informative and not a blanket limitation of Wilcoxon snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: Human truncating MAP1B variants are associated with intellectual disability/cognitive phenotypes and extensive white-matter deficits, while experimental MAP1B loss alters axons and synapses.
main_caveats: The screen excluded most non-neuronal nuclei and did not sample olfactory bulb or peripheral sensory neurons; mosaic P16 loss cannot reproduce congenital MAP1B haploinsufficiency.
summary: The Map1b null refines MAP1B disease biology toward developmental wiring, white-matter integrity, and subcellular cytoskeletal mechanisms rather than a stable postnatal neuronal transcriptomic state.
why_it_matters: For MAP1B truncating-variant disorders, these data warn that postnatal neuronal RNA biomarkers may be sparse: a therapy or model readout may need axon-tract, myelination, spine, or tubulin-code assays rather than expecting a large cell-autonomous DEG panel in surviving neurons.

literature_claim: Severe Atg5 or Atg7 loss shows that neurons require basal autophagy, but mammalian LC3/GABARAP paralogs can act differentially and redundantly, so loss of a single LC3A paralog need not mimic core autophagy collapse.
main_caveats: The dataset measured nuclear RNA, not LC3 lipidation, autophagic flux, or DNA indels; a primary autophagosome phenotype without secondary transcription remains possible.
summary: Map1lc3a loss produced a pan-panel downstream null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 22 recovered neuronal groups, despite measurable negative self-transcript shifts in many groups.
why_it_matters: For a neuronal ATG8-family autophagy effector, this says that acute single-LC3A loss was buffered in juvenile postmitotic neurons rather than launching a p62/ubiquitin-stress transcriptional state over the 3-4 week assay window.

literature_claim: MTORC1 regulates autophagy initiation, LC3 lipidation, autophagosome maturation, and lysosomal transcription, while LC3A acts downstream as an ATG8-family effector.
main_caveats: Most represented core-autophagy comparator perturbations were themselves weak in this assay, and direct ATG8 paralog perturbations Map1lc3b/Gabarap/Gabarapl1/Gabarapl2 were not target perturbations in the parquet.
summary: The represented autophagy/lysosome/mTOR comparators did not phenocopy Map1lc3a: their score-profile correlations with Map1lc3a were approximately zero, and Tsc2 was strongly divergent with 636 downstream genes where Map1lc3a had none.
why_it_matters: This separates single LC3A removal from the broader mTOR-autophagy regulatory surface visible to the same screen, especially from TSC2/mTORC1 perturbation effects in hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, pontine/myelencephalic, and cerebellar neurons.

main_caveats: Pearson scores were calculated over all matched Wilcoxon z-score features, so a null target's ranks are sensitive to noise; they are used only to reject strong convergence.
summary: A target-agnostic signature-neighbor search found no hidden convergent module for Map1lc3a; even the largest Pearson correlation was only 0.061 and the strongest negative neighbor was only -0.039.
why_it_matters: The flat Map1lc3a surface is not rescued by continuous, subthreshold similarities to another perturbation module: the nearest profiles were essentially null-like, while a broad Wdr26 response merely served as a weak anti-neighbor.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: LC3/GABARAP proteins and SQSTM1 carry selective cargo into autophagosomes, and MTORC1-TFEB signaling can regulate autophagy and lysosome gene expression.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot measure LC3 lipidation or turnover of the corresponding proteins; absence of transcript induction does not prove absence of protein-level compensation.
summary: The Map1lc3a null did not contain transcriptional replacement of LC3A by alternative ATG8s or a TFEB/SQSTM1 autophagy-lysosome bounce-back: 22 expected transcripts were all FDR=1.0 in all 22 measured groups.
why_it_matters: If LC3A is buffered here, the compensation is more likely pre-existing ATG8 paralog capacity or protein-level flux control than induced Map1lc3b/Gabarap-family mRNA up-regulation.

direction: downstream response restricted to 2 of 22 measured groups
literature_claim: Raf-MEK-ERK is a central neuronal signaling cascade, but MEK1 and MEK2 are partially redundant and many ERK functions are stimulus gated rather than constitutive.
main_caveats: MB Dopa was not recovered for Map2k1; snRNA-seq measures chronic basal RNA rather than acute phospho-ERK or evoked transcription.
summary: Map2k1 loss produced a sparse neuronal steady-state RNA response, with FDR<0.10 downstream genes in only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA among 22 measured groups.
why_it_matters: The screen does not support a pan-neuronal MEK1 transcriptional requirement at P37-P44; basal MEK1 dependence is concentrated in two posterior neuron groups even though the target transcript often trends down elsewhere.

literature_claim: Neuronal BDNF/Trk and synaptic inputs can use MEK/ERK to activate Elk/CREB-dependent transcription, including Vgf induction, and STEP/PTPN5 and UNC13A act in ERK-linked synaptic signaling.
main_caveats: Only four genes pass FDR<0.10; classic immediate-early genes such as Fos, Egr1, Arc, and Dusp6 remain sub-threshold after multiple-test correction.
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c response is a down-regulated ERK-linked neuropeptide and synaptic program anchored by Vgf, Etv5, Ptpn5, and Unc13a.
why_it_matters: Vgf and Etv5 connect the signature to activity/neurotrophin-responsive MAPK transcription, while Ptpn5 and Unc13a place the output in ERK feedback and presynaptic machinery rather than in a generalized stress, proteasome, or UPR program.

literature_claim: BRAF and SHOC2 act upstream of MEK/ERK in the RAS/MAPK pathway and are RASopathy or RASopathy-like genes expected to modulate ERK output.
main_caveats: Etv5 was directionally down after Braf loss but did not reach FDR<0.10; Shoc2 shared only Vgf at FDR<0.10.
summary: Braf perturbation validates the 151 Map2k1 module by down-regulating Vgf, Ptpn5, and Unc13a in the same group; Shoc2 shares the Vgf arm more weakly.
why_it_matters: This cross-perturbation overlap distinguishes a real Raf-to-MEK transcriptional edge from an isolated four-gene Map2k1 artifact and made Braf a stronger FDR-level neighbor than the noncanonical rank-1 Pearson neighbor Mapt.

literature_claim: MEK1/2 share ERK1/2 substrates, and BRAF, KRAS, MAP2K1, MAP2K2, SOS1, RAF1, LZTR1, and PTPN11 are genetically connected through RAS/MAPK signaling and RASopathies.
main_caveats: Several obvious pathway nodes, including Araf, Mapk3, Nf1, Nras, Rasa1, Dusp6, and Etv5, were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Most expected Ras/MAPK neighbors did not phenocopy Map2k1 in its responder groups: Map2k2, Mapk1, Ptpn11, Raf1, Hras, Kras, and Rasa2 were flat in 151 and 191, Sos1 produced only Cul7, and Lztr1 changed Vgf in 191 without matching the Las1l/Uso1 pair.
why_it_matters: The data separate a narrow Braf-Map2k1 axis from the broader RASopathy gene set and show that same-pathway membership was insufficient to predict basal postnatal neuronal RNA phenotypes.

main_caveats: Continuous logFC correlations are not mechanistic by themselves; this comparison was used only to reject strong transcriptomic convergence.
summary: The full-universe signature search found no meaningful Mapre2 convergence partner.
why_it_matters: The strongest centered positive and negative neighbors had absolute correlations below 0.017, and the top positives were nearly null themselves; apparent anti-neighbors such as Psmc1 and Psmb4 were strong perturbations but not inverse Mapre2 programs.

literature_claim: MAPRE2/TUBB variants cause circumferential skin creases Kunze type and MAPRE2 mutations perturb microtubule binding and cranial neural crest migration in early development.
main_caveats: The screen did not include embryonic neural crest or epithelial lineages and did not engineer the disease missense alleles.
summary: The postnatal Mapre2 null does not model the embryonic, allele-specific MAPRE2 disease mechanisms reported for CSC-KT.
why_it_matters: Human MAPRE2 disease alleles change microtubule binding and embryonic craniofacial neural-crest migration; acute sparse P16 loss in already specified mouse neurons yielded no stress or fate response. Interpreting this screen as disease rescue or as evidence that MAPRE2 is irrelevant to development would be the wrong direction.

literature_claim: Mapt encodes tau, a microtubule- and protein-kinase-binding neuronal protein; tau-deficient mice can be viable and grossly normal despite subtle axonal or maturation phenotypes.
main_caveats: Indel formation and tau protein depletion were not measured; single-nucleus RNA cannot rule out local cytoskeletal or synaptic protein-localization phenotypes.
summary: Mapt loss produced no FDR-resolved downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The strongest dataset fact is a pan-measured zero: two groups showed significant Mapt self-transcript reduction, yet every group stayed at 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10. In P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic neurons, endogenous tau loss is therefore buffered at the nuclear mRNA level rather than launching a stress or fate program.

literature_claim: Tau, MAP1B, MAP2 and related MAPs have overlapping activities in neurite outgrowth, neuronal migration and microtubule organization.
main_caveats: Map1a, Map2 and Map4 were measured as Mapt-response genes but were not perturbation targets; the assay tests mRNA compensation, not redistribution or phosphorylation of existing MAP proteins.
summary: The expected MAP-family/tubulin compensation was not an mRNA program after Mapt perturbation.
why_it_matters: Tau redundancy is usually discussed through other microtubule-associated proteins, but the screen directly shows that acute Mapt loss did not transcriptionally induce Map1a, Map1b, Map2, Map4, Map6, Stmn2 or assayed tubulin genes; directly perturbing Map1b, Map6 and Mapre2 was also flat across the same matched cell groups.

literature_claim: Pathogenic MAPT variants and amyloid-beta models act through tau deposition, tau protein aggregation and tau-dependent postsynaptic Fyn signaling.
main_caveats: The screen has no amyloid, no mutant tau aggregation, no aging interval and sparse neuronal sampling, so absence of this axis is context-specific.
summary: A MAPT-APP-Fyn/tauopathy transcript axis was absent from young wild-type neurons after Mapt loss.
why_it_matters: Human tauopathy and Aβ-toxicity literature point to tau aggregation, postsynaptic Fyn routing and disease-age protein pathology. In this dataset, Mapt loss left App, Fyn, Gsk3b and Mark3 unchanged, and App, Fyn and Sorl1 perturbations were themselves flat or near-flat, arguing that the disease axis is not a constitutive, cell-autonomous transcriptional module triggered by lowering Mapt.

main_caveats: Computed on a null Mapt Wilcoxon-score vector; by construction it has no FDR<0.10 Mapt genes to support shared-direction overlap.
summary: Full-universe rank-neighbor analysis found no robust positive or negative Mapt signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The data-driven top neighbors of Mapt were not MAPT textbook partners: the largest non-safe signed-score cosines were only 0.027 for Spast, 0.027 for H4c11 and 0.027 for Sorl1, and the most negative non-safe cosine was -0.0145 for Cspp1. Even negative neighbors such as Thoc1 and Atxn10 had real DE surfaces where Mapt was flat, so the nearest-neighbor calculation is best read as another null rather than a hidden module.

literature_claim: MAPT lowering is being pursued clinically with antisense oligonucleotides and can reduce CSF tau biomarkers in human Alzheimer disease.
main_caveats: Guide-induced indels and tau protein were not assayed, target reduction was mosaic and sparse, and the experiment was in young wild-type mouse neurons rather than diseased adult human brain.
summary: The screen is compatible with neuronal tolerance of tau lowering but is not an efficacy model for tau-lowering ASOs.
why_it_matters: A therapy that lowers MAPT would hope not to create a broad acute stress program. The P16 mouse mosaic knockout surface satisfies that safety-like criterion in NeuN+ neurons, but its lack of tauopathy, Aβ challenge, aging and non-neuronal sampling means it cannot test whether tau lowering reverses pathological tau biology.

literature_claim: MARCHF6 is an ER E3 ligase and an endogenous brake on the SREBP-regulated cholesterol-biosynthesis pathway through substrates that include SQLE and HMGCR.
main_caveats: Three of the five responding groups contained only a single FDR<0.10 sterol-feedback gene; the strongest interpretation rests on the 151 and 155 signatures.
summary: Marchf6 loss induced a compact SREBP2/cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptome in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with one-gene Fdps or Insig1 outposts in 066, 110, and 308.
why_it_matters: The positive biology is not generic ERAD stress; the only multi-gene Marchf6 program recovered by this P16 mosaic neuronal assay is de novo sterol synthesis plus SREBP feedback and LDLR uptake.

literature_claim: SREBPs activate lipid-synthesis and uptake genes, and loss of MARCH6 increases SREBP-regulated cholesterol gene expression.
main_caveats: The comparison used a restricted 30-coordinate Marchf6 signature and cannot prove direct SREBP2 binding in the assayed neurons.
summary: Srebf2 perturbation was the matched pathway inverse of Marchf6: it was the second strongest negative neighbor and drove 12 downstream Marchf6 sterol genes in the opposite direction at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The inversion turns the Marchf6 signature from a gene list into a directional pathway readout: Marchf6 loss releases an Srebf2-shaped sterol program, while Srebf2 loss collapses the same program.

literature_claim: MARCHF6 controls flux through cholesterol synthesis at multiple ERAD substrates, including SQLE and HMGCR, while SREBP-family transcription factors regulate lipid synthesis genes.
main_caveats: Hmgcr and Srebf1 showed weak self-transcript depletion in many groups, so absence of a phenocopy is an informative but engagement-limited negative comparison.
summary: The obvious sterol relatives Hmgcr and Srebf1 were measured but did not phenocopy Marchf6 in its responder groups.
why_it_matters: Marchf6 behaves as a multi-node ER sterol regulator rather than as a simple Hmgcr-loss surrogate, and the response is aligned with Srebf2 rather than the Srebf1 branch.

main_caveats: The biological path from each neighbor to SREBP activation is not established here; Far1 was rejected because it lacked FDR-level overlap despite a high sign-based cosine.
summary: Mib1, Dctn1, Tsc2, and Htt unexpectedly converged on the same sterol coordinates as Marchf6, whereas Far1 fell out after FDR-level overlap testing.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation neighborhood says that the neuronal SREBP/sterol module is a recurrent compensatory endpoint of several unrelated perturbations, not a private Marchf6 artifact.

main_caveats: Exploratory restricted-signature result; Phf12 has a broad 151 response, and this analysis does not distinguish direct repression from secondary cell-state effects.
summary: Phf12 was the strongest data-driven antineighbor after returning to the parquet, opposing 11 downstream Marchf6 sterol coordinates at FDR<0.10; Kifbp, Pi4kb, and Opa1 did not pass that overlap gate.
why_it_matters: The analysis preserves a non-obvious negative sterol regulator nominated by the dataset while rejecting antineighbors whose cosine came mostly from sub-threshold signs.

literature_claim: In POMC neurons, Marchf6 prevents cytosol-retained POMC from causing ER stress and ferroptotic cell death.
main_caveats: The assay did not isolate POMC neurons and measured snRNA rather than lipid peroxidation, so it rules out only a coordinated secondary transcriptional stress program in the assayed groups.
summary: The POMC-neuron ER-stress/ferroptosis expectation did not generalize: Marchf6 induced Acsl4 in 151, but not a coordinated Hspa5, Ddit3, Herpud1, Asns, Chac1, or Trp53 stress program.
why_it_matters: This is an informative absence, not a readout failure: Hspa5 and Opa1 perturbations triggered UPR/ISR genes in matched groups, so postnatal Marchf6 loss can release sterol synthesis without a broad transcriptional ER-stress or ferroptosis state.

literature_claim: FAME3 is caused by noncoding TTTTA/TTTCA expansions in intron 1 of MARCH6; similar repeat expansions in unrelated genes suggest a repeat-dependent mechanism independent of the recipient gene's normal function.
main_caveats: FAME is human and adult-onset, and CRISPR coding loss cannot model expanded-repeat RNA or repeat instability.
summary: Simple postnatal Marchf6 loss-of-function did not create a broad cortical, cerebellar, or pan-neuronal disease-like transcriptome, consistent with FAME3 being a specific intronic repeat-expansion mechanism rather than ordinary MARCHF6 haploinsufficiency.
why_it_matters: The disease allele linked to MARCHF6 sits outside the coding sterol-E3 mechanism; the Perturb-seq negative surface warns against interpreting FAME3 as a uniform loss of Marchf6 enzymatic function in juvenile postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: MARCKS is primarily a PKC/CaM-regulated membrane, actin, and PIP2 effector in neurites and dendritic spines rather than a primary transcriptional regulator.
main_caveats: DNA indels and MARCKS protein depletion were not measured; weak nominal genes were ignored because all downstream calls failed FDR.
summary: Marcks loss was transcriptionally buffered across the recovered postmitotic neuronal atlas: none of 22 measured cell groups had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result is a broad negative biology call, not a failed screen: within a P16-to-P37/44 sparse CRISPR snRNA readout, single-cell Marcks loss did not launch detectable stress, proteostasis, synaptic, or compensatory transcriptional modules in any neuronal class that was recovered.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Marcks germline and embryonic studies implicate the gene in perinatal viability, forebrain commissure formation, cortical lamination, and radial progenitor placement and proliferation.
main_caveats: The assay cannot test embryonic radial glia directly because perturbation starts at P16 and nuclei were NeuN-enriched.
summary: The embryonic MARCKS requirement for forebrain construction did not reappear as a postmitotic cortical or hippocampal snRNA program.
why_it_matters: Germline Marcks phenotypes arise during neurulation, radial-progenitor organization, and cortical lamination; the zero-DE result in recovered cortical and hippocampal neuronal groups refines those effects to an earlier progenitor-rich window rather than a persistent autonomous transcriptomic defect after P16.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation used all signed Wilcoxon scores and is intentionally treated as a coherence diagnostic, not as a nominal-gene biological module.
summary: Marcks had no convincing data-driven signature neighbor: the strongest positive and negative gene-target correlations were all near zero.
why_it_matters: A real shared transcriptional state would be expected to recruit a recurrent neighbor in a 1,773-target DE universe; instead, Ext1, Tomm40, Wdr37, Ptprn, Gria3, and Cyld aligned with signed Marcks ranks only at |r|<=0.027 and were themselves mostly flat.

literature_claim: MARCKS is controlled by PKC and calmodulin, interfaces with PIP2/actin and CDC42/RAC-linked neurite machinery, and has a MARCKSL1 paralog with overlapping developmental functions.
main_caveats: The direct paralog Marcksl1 was not present as a perturbation target, and pathway comparators were scored by transcriptomic overlap rather than by protein localization or morphology.
summary: Acute Marcks knockdown did not phenocopy represented PKC, calmodulin, or small-GTPase cytoskeletal perturbations.
why_it_matters: The literature-nominated axis around MARCKS contains PKC/CaM regulation and CDC42/RAC-linked actin control, yet Prkca, Calm2, Cdc42, Limk1, Myo5a, and Mapk9 were flat, Prkcg/Calm3/Rac1/Actg1 produced only 1-3 total FDR calls, and the clearest comparator, Calm1, responded mainly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where Marcks had no robust downstream gene. Thus MARCKS is not a transcriptomic proxy for this pathway under P16 sparse LoF.

literature_claim: Rai1 is a promoter-associated, dosage-sensitive transcriptional activator whose loss in selected neuronal populations yields Smith-Magenis-like motor, learning, and metabolic phenotypes.
main_caveats: The finding is a one-gene FDR signal in only 39 perturbed nuclei; canonical Rai1 effectors Clock and Bdnf were not differentially expressed.
summary: Mark3 loss produced a restricted Rai1-down response in MH-LH TH Glut and no broader Rai1 effector module.
why_it_matters: Rai1 is a dosage-sensitive neuronal transcriptional regulator; its isolated loss from a habenular/thalamic glutamatergic class nominates a noncanonical MARK3-to-RAI1 connection rather than a general MARK/tau stress response.

literature_claim: MARK/PAR kinases phosphorylate tau/MAP substrates and lie in an LKB1 AMPK-related kinase family, whereas GSK3B is a tau kinase through a distinct pathway.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot score phospho-tau, ARHGEF2 localization, RHOA activity, or Hippo kinase activity; Mark1/2/4 and Stk11 were not represented as tested targets.
summary: The Mark3 response was uncoupled from the canonical MARK tau/MAP and ARHGEF2-Hippo polarity axes at the mRNA level.
why_it_matters: The best-established MARK3 substrates are regulated by phosphorylation and localization, so the absence of Mapt, Map2, Map4, Arhgef2, Dlg5, Stk3/4, or Lats1/2 transcriptional changes prevents over-reading the Rai1 signal as a tau or Hippo program.

main_caveats: The data-driven comparison is limited by Mark3 having only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene; cosine magnitudes were therefore treated as rejection evidence, not as mechanistic similarity.
summary: Genome-scale score-neighbor analysis did not reveal a robust Mark3 transcriptional phenocopy.
why_it_matters: The top named positive and negative neighbors had near-zero whole-surface cosine scores and failed to reproduce Rai1 at FDR<0.10 in the responsive cell group, indicating that Mark3 has no strong shared snRNA-seq module in this assay.

literature_claim: VPS41 participates in HOPS-dependent cargo delivery to lysosomes and in mTORC1-TFEB/TFE3 regulation.
main_caveats: The signature is one gene with FDR 0.0917 in 57 perturbed nuclei; it should be treated as a sentinel, not a full autophagy module.
summary: Mast1 loss produced a single lysosomal trafficking hit, Vps41 up-regulation, specifically in CTX-CGE GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: Vps41 is a HOPS-complex lysosomal and autophagy trafficking component, so this nominates an endolysosomal rebound as one rare transcriptional output of acute postnatal Mast1 perturbation rather than a broad canonical cytoskeletal program.

literature_claim: DnaJ/Hsp40 proteins specify Hsp70 chaperone folding/degradation cycles, and a separate cancer-cell study showed that MAST1 protein abundance is controlled by chaperone/E3 ubiquitin/proteasome machinery.
main_caveats: The link between Dnaja2 and Mast1 was not directly tested; the observed program is a single transcript at FDR 0.0848.
summary: Mast1 loss induced the Hsp40 co-chaperone Dnaja2 in CNU-MGE GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: Dnaja2 points to Hsp70-client proteostasis as a second sparse compensatory axis, compatible with MAST1 being a kinase whose stability can be chaperone-controlled rather than with direct MAST-family transcriptional feedback.

literature_claim: MAST1 is a nervous-system, postmitotic-neuron microtubule-associated kinase implicated in cortical and cerebellar developmental malformations.
main_caveats: P16 mosaic CRISPR interrogates survivor nuclei and mRNA, not prenatal axon anatomy, neuronal migration or phosphoprotein output.
summary: The Mast1 transcriptional response was almost completely buffered and confined to two inhibitory populations.
why_it_matters: Only two of 21 measured groups carried any FDR<0.10 downstream gene, both were GABA groups, and each had one induced quality-control or membrane-trafficking gene; no cortical excitatory or cerebellar GABA population showed a robust snRNA-seq response.

literature_claim: MAST kinases share a conserved kinase-PDZ architecture, MAST proteins interact with PTEN and beta-2-syntrophin-associated complexes, and other MAST kinases could compensate for Mast1 deletion.
main_caveats: The result excludes mRNA induction, not compensation by pre-existing proteins, altered kinase activity or altered localization.
summary: Mast1 perturbation did not transcriptionally induce MAST-family paralogs or the PTEN/syntrophin/nNOS axis.
why_it_matters: Germline Mast1 deletion can be viable and has been interpreted as potentially compensated by other MAST kinases, but this postnatal snRNA-seq surface shows no Mast2, Mast3, Mast4, Pten, Nos1, Sntb2, Dmd or Utrn mRNA feedback across 21 groups.

literature_claim: Syntrophins and ERK-pathway components are literature-adjacent to MAST proteins, though the MEK relation was shown in cisplatin-resistant cancer rather than neurons.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed on a very weak Mast1 vector; absence of Mast2, Mast3, Mast4, Pten, Nos1 and Sntb2 targets prevented direct same-family and core-interactor perturbation tests.
summary: Neither the data-driven nearest neighbors nor testable literature-neighbor perturbations converged with Mast1 in the responder groups.
why_it_matters: The strongest whole-surface neighbors were near zero, and Fgf13, Wdfy3, Nhs, Fzd2, Kif2a, Zbtb21, Snta1, Map2k1 and Raf1 all failed to reproduce Vps41 or Dnaja2 at FDR<0.10 in 046/054, arguing that the Mast1 effect is an isolated weak signature rather than a member of an obvious shared perturbation module.

literature_claim: MAST1 patient alleles are mainly de novo missense or in-frame changes; L278del mice had enlarged corpus callosum and cortical apoptosis whereas Mast1 deletion was viable.
main_caveats: DNA-level indel formation was not measured, and a sparse CRISPR LoF screen cannot model a dominant-negative in-frame allele.
summary: The acute LoF null refines, rather than contradicts, MAST1 disease genetics.
why_it_matters: A P16 indel perturbation failed to recover Cdkn1b, broad cytoskeletal, apoptosis or MAST-paralog programs, supporting the interpretation that human MAST1 malformations are driven by prenatal, allele-specific protein dysfunction rather than by a large autonomous postmitotic mRNA cascade after simple loss of one copy.

literature_claim: S85C knock-in mice show selective vulnerability rather than pan-neuronal loss, including motor-neuron, Purkinje-cell and CA1-related pathology.
main_caveats: n_pert varies across groups and lower motor neurons are outside the dissected tissue; the readout is a short postnatal gene-abundance signature, not a survival assay.
summary: Matr3 loss was broad but not uniform: 18 of 21 measured neuronal groups had FDR<0.10 downstream signal, with the largest signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The response is not an all-or-none RBP toxicity state. The strongest postnatal gene-abundance response is concentrated in thalamic and midbrain classes rather than in CA1-containing hippocampal neurons or two telencephalic GABA groups that were completely flat.

literature_claim: MATR3 regulates alternative and cryptic splicing and participates with PTBP1, HNRNPK and SUGP2 on repeat-derived LINE substrates.
main_caveats: The 10x gene-count matrix cannot prove cryptic exon inclusion or direct MATR3 binding of the induced transcripts.
summary: The most target-proximal-looking abundance change was an RNA-processing rebound: Sugp2 was up in 12 groups while Rsrp1 and several splicing factors were recurrently down.
why_it_matters: SUGP2 is a known LINE-associated RBP that works in MATR3-containing splicing assemblies, so its induction is a plausible compensatory marker of lost Matrin3 RNA surveillance rather than an unrelated stress gene.

literature_claim: UGGT2 functions in ER glycoprotein quality control, whereas ZKSCAN3 represses an autophagy/lysosomal transcriptional program in cultured cells.
main_caveats: This is a transcript-level secondary signature; protein folding load, autophagic flux and ER stress were not measured directly.
summary: Matr3 perturbation repeatedly induced ER quality-control and stress-adaptation genes, including Uggt2 and Sec11a, together with Zkscan3 and redox or mitochondrial quality-control markers.
why_it_matters: This maps the RNA-binding perturbation onto a secondary proteostasis/autophagy-gating response that standard Matrin3 annotations would not predict, but that the snRNA-seq screen robustly recovered in many neurons.

literature_claim: DDHD1 and ATP9B-family proteins are lipid-remodeling or flippase factors linked to organelle biogenesis and membrane trafficking, but they are not established canonical Matrin3 outputs.
main_caveats: The module is inferred from transcript recurrence; organelle trafficking and electrophysiology were not assayed.
summary: A membrane/lipid-trafficking module headed by Ddhd1 and Atp9b was the most recurrent positive component of the Matr3 signature and coupled to synaptic or ion-channel changes such as Kcnq2 upregulation.
why_it_matters: The response suggests that postmitotic neurons rebalance membrane handling and excitability after an RNA-scaffold perturbation, with the broadest remodeling in 155 MB Glut where App, Gls and Atp1a3 were simultaneously downregulated.

literature_claim: GPT2 is a mitochondrial alanine transaminase required for neuronal glutamate/anaplerotic metabolism, growth and motor function.
main_caveats: Gpt2 induction is a marker of adaptation, not evidence that Matr3 directly binds Gpt2 RNA or that alanine/glutamate flux changed.
summary: Gpt2 defined a subcortical metabolic branch of the response, rising in Pvalb/MGE/HY GABA and in thalamic or midbrain neurons but not in cortical IT neurons.
why_it_matters: Matr3 loss therefore does not only elicit an RBP/splicing module; in selected neuronal classes it induces mitochondrial glutamate-pyruvate transamination machinery, pointing to a cell-type-specific metabolic adaptation.

literature_claim: U2AF2, PRPF6 and CDC40 are curated major-spliceosome factors, providing an indirect spliceosome expectation but no specific Matrin3 phenocopy prediction.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed on the restricted 555-feature Matr3 signature; Tpr and Ascc3 may converge through nuclear or protein-homeostasis stress rather than a direct Matrin3 complex.
summary: The unbiased nearest positive neighbors of Matr3 were U2af2, Tpr and Ascc3; U2af2, Prpf6 and Cdc40 splicing-factor perturbations shared a significant subset of the Matr3 module but were far broader than Matr3.
why_it_matters: The convergence ties Matrin3 loss to spliceosome/RNA-processing stress in this dataset without reducing it to a generic consequence of any splicing perturbation: U2af2 was nearest on the restricted signature, whereas Prpf6 and Cdc40 caused thousands of DEGs and only partially overlapped.

literature_claim: MATR3, TDP-43 and FUS are ALS-linked RNA-processing proteins with overlapping interaction biology, while other ALS genes act through proteostasis, autophagy or axonal mechanisms.
main_caveats: FUS, HNRNPA1, C9orf72, TBK1 and OPTN were not represented as perturbation targets in the parquet and therefore could not be tested.
summary: Among measurable ALS-family perturbations, Tardbp was the only partial Matr3 phenocopy; Hnrnpa2b1, Atxn2, Tia1, Kif5a, Sqstm1 and Vcp were essentially divergent or flat.
why_it_matters: This separates the Matrin3 abundance state from a generic ALS-gene state and preserves a related-target negative result: even ALS-linked RBPs did not reproduce the recurrent Ddhd1/Atp9b/E2f4/Gpt2 Matr3 module in juvenile mouse neurons.

literature_claim: MATR3 disease alleles include S85C knock-in pathology and cryptic-splicing defects, while MATR3 also supports RNA and differentiation programs in other cell systems.
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic warning, not a dose-response or rescue experiment; true indel engagement and protein depletion were not measured.
summary: Because acute neuronal Matr3 depletion itself triggered broad RNA-processing, proteostasis and metabolic signatures, pan-Matr3 lowering is unlikely to be neutral even if allele-specific suppression of toxic MATR3 variants remains conceptually attractive.
why_it_matters: ALS-linked S85C can impair MATR3 solubility rather than simply eliminating RNA binding; a non-allele-specific loss strategy could remove residual wild-type Matrin3 functions in many postmitotic neuronal populations.

main_caveats: The response is a single gene in 57 perturbed nuclei; no binding or indel data prove that Uhrf1bp1l is a direct MBD2 target.
summary: Mbd2 produced a real FDR-level signature only in 046 CTX-CGE GABA, where the entire response was Uhrf1bp1l down-regulation.
why_it_matters: The dataset nominates a narrow CGE-derived interneuron context rather than a pan-neuronal chromatin-collapse phenotype; because Uhrf1bp1l was a CTX-CGE hit for Mbd2 only, it is also the cleanest measured biomarker of Mbd2 engagement in this screen.

literature_claim: MBD2 binds methylated DNA and participates in MBD2/NuRD-mediated transcriptional repression, predicting derepression of methylated targets after effective loss of function.
main_caveats: Direct MBD2-bound targets were not assayed by ChIP or methylome profiling, and DNA indels were not measured.
summary: The screen did not recover the textbook MBD2 loss-of-repression program: no Mbd2 cell group contained an FDR<0.10 up-regulated downstream gene.
why_it_matters: If postnatal MBD2 were the limiting NuRD recruiter at many methylated promoters, this snRNA-seq assay should have seen a positive derepression signature. Instead the only FDR hit was down-regulated, so acute P16 loss of a single MBD2 reader is transcriptionally buffered in nearly all neuronal classes.

literature_claim: MBD2 is one methyl-CpG reader linked to NuRD, whereas MECP2, MBD5, CHD4, and GATAD2B have distinct MBD/NuRD or NuRD-related neurodevelopmental genetics.
main_caveats: Mbd3, Mbd1, Mbd4, Chd3, HDAC, MTA, and RBBP paralogs were not targeted, and the comparison is transcriptomic rather than biochemical.
summary: Mbd2 did not phenocopy MBD-family or NuRD-family perturbations represented in the parquet.
why_it_matters: Mecp2 produced a distinct thalamic/midbrain-weighted response, Chd4 was dominated by 149 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Gatad2b and Mbd5 were nearly flat, and Dnmt3a was wholly flat; this separates Mbd2 from both neurodevelopmental MBD-family genes and the represented NuRD ATPase/bridge subunits in the same experimental universe.

main_caveats: Cosine values are dominated by sub-threshold Wilcoxon scores because Mbd2 has only one FDR-level downstream gene; this finding is useful mainly as a rejection of strong convergence.
summary: The unbiased Mbd2 signature had no strong recurrent neighbor; its largest all-vector cosine was only 0.031598 and the top six positive or negative neighbors did not share the CTX-CGE Uhrf1bp1l hit.
why_it_matters: This rejects a hidden high-confidence co-perturbation module: the sole Mbd2 response was idiosyncratic rather than a member of an Sv2a-, Mycn-, Atp1a3-, Meox1-, Ephb1-, or Nhs-like state.

literature_claim: Mbd2-deficient mice show cognitive, social, emotional, hippocampal expression, and ASD-risk-gene phenotypes.
main_caveats: The mapped cell groups are broad hippocampal/amygdala glutamatergic aggregates and the screen did not assay morphology, behavior, methylation, or DNA indel load.
summary: The germline hippocampal Mbd2-deficiency program reported in mice was not recovered by acute P16 mosaic Mbd2 loss in hippocampal-like glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: Mbd2 can be behaviorally relevant in chronic whole-animal models, but this screen argues that any corresponding hippocampal transcriptome either requires earlier or more complete perturbation, a non-sparse circuit perturbation, or both.

literature_claim: Bulk Mbd5-hypomorphic mouse brain and human CRISPR neuronal models showed modest, context-dependent transcriptional consequences rather than a single invariant MBD5 loss program.
main_caveats: Indels were not measured and the P16 AAV setting samples mosaic surviving neurons only.
summary: Acute postmitotic Mbd5 loss produced a near-flat snRNA-seq response across 21 neuronal groups, with only one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The screen rules out a large, uniform cell-autonomous transcriptional collapse after P16 Mbd5 perturbation and reframes MBD5 biology as subtle, delayed, or context restricted in this assay rather than as an immediate pan-neuronal chromatin failure.

literature_claim: MAP2K4 encodes MKK4, a dual-specificity kinase that regulates JNK and p38 MAPK signaling.
main_caveats: Single-gene signal at FDR 0.0609 in 35 perturbed cells; no phospho-JNK/p38 protein readout was collected.
summary: Map2k4 was selectively increased in 001 L5-6 IT Glut and was the only Mbd5 downstream transcript passing the FDR<0.10 threshold.
why_it_matters: MAP2K4/MKK4 links the otherwise flat Mbd5 surface to a stress-activated JNK/p38 kinase branch that can be followed up as a narrow L5-6 IT candidate rather than as a broad MBD5 signature.

literature_claim: MBD5 and MBD6 interact with and stabilize mammalian BAP1/PR-DUB complexes through ASXL scaffolds, which also connect the complex to FOXK1/2 and OGT-associated machinery.
main_caveats: Mbd6, the closest MBD5 PR-DUB paralog, was not represented; Ogt has many BAP1-independent functions.
summary: Represented BAP1/PR-DUB-associated perturbations did not phenocopy Mbd5: Bap1 and Ogt were far broader, whereas Asxl3 and Foxk2 were flat, and none shared the L5-6 Map2k4 hit.
why_it_matters: Endogenous MBD5 can be a BAP1-complex subunit through ASXL proteins, but acute neuronal signatures in this atlas are not determined simply by membership in that biochemical complex.

literature_claim: MBD5/MBD6 differ from methyl-DNA readers such as MBD2 and MeCP2, while GATAD2B/CHD4 and SETD5 represent separate chromatin neurodevelopmental disorders.
main_caveats: The comparison is DE-surface based and does not measure shared chromatin occupancy or protein-complex biochemistry.
summary: Mbd5 was not interchangeable with represented MBD-family, NuRD, or chromatin-NDD controls in the matched groups.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation used an exploratory 220-feature nominal signature because Mchr1 had only one FDR downstream gene; conventional FDR overlap found no shared robust gene.

Ligand-evoked GPCR assays, calcium/cAMP, electrophysiology, circuit-state and ependymal-cilia readouts are therefore better matched to this target.
