literature_claim: MFSD6 is an orphan neuronal major-facilitator-family protein whose mRNA changes with altered energy availability, and Mfsd6/MMR2 also has an immune MHC-I receptor annotation.
main_caveats: True DNA indel formation and protein loss were not measured; the assay used resting NeuN+ nuclei rather than diet challenge, viral challenge, or allogeneic macrophages.
summary: Mfsd6 loss was buffered across the postnatal neuronal atlas: 22 of 23 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the whole target yielded only one downstream hit.
why_it_matters: MFSD6 is a neuronal atypical MFS membrane protein, so a basal transporter failure might have produced ER, metabolic, lysosomal, immune, or neuronal-state secondary transcription; the screen instead shows that most young postmitotic neurons tolerate mosaic Mfsd6 perturbation without a large snRNA-seq state change.

literature_claim: TMTC1/TMTC2 are ER-resident membrane proteins involved in calcium homeostasis, and TMTC1-4 form a pathway for cadherin/protocadherin O-mannosylation.
main_caveats: The effect is one FDR<0.10 gene in 66 perturbed nuclei; no ER-stress or glycosylation program accompanied the Tmtc1 mRNA change.
summary: The only significant downstream response was Tmtc1 down-regulation in L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: Tmtc1 encodes an ER membrane protein linked to ER calcium handling and cadherin/protocadherin O-mannosylation, raising an exploratory hypothesis that Mfsd6 loss touches ER membrane or adhesion-glycosylation biology only in corticofugal projection neurons.

literature_claim: MFSD6, MFSD8, MFSD10 and MFSD11 are phylogenetically related atypical MFS/SLC-like proteins, and Mfsd6 and Mfsd10 mRNAs change with nutrient status in mouse brain.
main_caveats: Absence of mRNA compensation does not exclude shared substrates, protein-level compensation, or acute changes in transporter flux.
summary: Mfsd6 perturbation did not transcriptionally induce related MFSD transporter genes, and MFSD8/MFSD10/MFSD11 were not available as reciprocal perturbation targets.
why_it_matters: This rejects an obvious compensation model at the mRNA level: neither the lysosomal MFSD8 branch nor the energy-responsive MFSD10/MFSD11 branch showed detectable rebound after Mfsd6 loss in any measured neuronal group.

literature_claim: Mfsd6/MMR2 is annotated in mouse as an MHC class-I-binding receptor, and Mfsd6 knockout mice fail to reject selected H-2K(d)/H-2D(d) allogeneic skin grafts.
main_caveats: The screen used C57BL/6J H-2b mice and did not sample monocytes/macrophages or allograft stimulation.
summary: The macrophage MHC-I receptor annotation of Mfsd6 did not translate into a neuronal H2-K1/B2m/Tap/Psmb or interferon transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: It separates the allograft/MMR2 literature from unchallenged NeuN+ brain nuclei: the relevant MHC-I and IFN-response transcripts were measured and stayed below FDR<0.10 after Mfsd6 loss.

literature_claim: No target-specific literature nominated these data-driven neighbors as MFSD6 partners.
main_caveats: The comparison is dominated by weak Mfsd6 signatures, so it is best interpreted as rejecting strong transcriptomic convergence rather than defining a negative molecular interaction.
summary: Cross-perturbation matching found no robust Mfsd6 phenocopy: the strongest non-safe positive and negative neighbors had score-vector correlations between −0.011 and 0.031.
why_it_matters: The lone Mfsd6/Tmtc1 event is not part of a recurrent atlas-wide perturbation module, and top nominal neighbors such as Litaf, Dhdds, Purg and Atl3 failed to share the L5 ET Tmtc1 effect when directly queried.

literature_claim: MGA/PRC1.6 represses context-dependent lineage-inappropriate germline and differentiation genes; Obscn encodes a muscle sarcomeric scaffold rather than a canonical neuronal marker.
main_caveats: Only four significant gene-by-cell-type calls support the positive surface, and Obscn is a single-cell-group event.
summary: Mga perturbation generated a tiny up-only response restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The abrupt contrast between two glutamatergic responder groups and 17 measured null groups makes the response a cell-state-specific derepression leak rather than a pan-neuronal consequence of losing a MAX-network transcription factor.

literature_claim: MGA-containing PRC1.6 binds and represses meiotic genes including STAG3, and STAG3 is induced after MGA loss in cancer and organoid settings.
main_caveats: The broader meiotic/piRNA program did not follow Stag3 in postmitotic neurons.
summary: Stag3 was the repeated MGA-loss marker, rising in both thalamic/midbrain glutamatergic responder groups.
why_it_matters: STAG3 is a known PRC1.6-repressed meiotic target, so its selective derepression is the clearest molecular bridge from this neuronal screen back to MGA/PRC1.6 biology.

literature_claim: SETDB1 participates in germline-gene repression alongside PRC1.6, and TASOR is the central HUSH subunit that enables SETDB1/H3K9me3 deposition at repetitive targets.
main_caveats: This rests on one shared transcript; Mga did not induce a full HUSH-component or retroelement program.
summary: Tasor connected the Mga and Setdb1 signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Because TASOR nucleates HUSH and HUSH recruits SETDB1/H3K9me3 silencing, Tasor upregulation after perturbing two repressive-chromatin nodes is a candidate compensatory chromatin-defense readout.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Strong MGA/PRC1.6 loss in ESCs and epithelial cancer models derepresses germline/meiotic, EMT, and E2F/cell-cycle programs.
main_caveats: The result excludes robust transcriptional induction in this P16 neuronal assay but not embryonic, germline, tumor, or full conditional PRC1.6 loss contexts.
summary: Mga loss did not derepress the expected broad germline, EMT, or E2F/cell-cycle programs in postnatal neurons.
why_it_matters: This converts 0-DE cell groups and silent panels into a mechanistic refinement: the broad MGA-loss programs are not automatic outputs of acute postmitotic neuronal perturbation.

literature_claim: MGA belongs to the extended MYC/MAX network but MGA-PRC1.6 repression is mechanistically distinct from MNT/SIN3-HDAC and from MYC activation.
main_caveats: The most direct partners, Max, Pcgf6, L3mbtl2, and E2f6, were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Represented MAX/MYC and E2F-side perturbations failed to phenocopy Mga in the responding groups.
why_it_matters: The direct data reject a generic MAX-network or E2F-family explanation for the Stag3/Tasor/Obscn signature and keep the interpretation tied to MGA-specific PRC1.6 biology.

main_caveats: This is a restricted-signature rejection rather than a mechanistic relationship among these genes.
summary: The top unbiased positive and negative signature neighbors of the near-null Mga surface were rejected by overlap.
why_it_matters: This preserves a data-driven negative result: global correlation over noisy null coordinates can nominate neighbors, but direct FDR overlap showed that Npsr1, Pi4kb, Setd1a, Trp63, Sipa1l3, and Grin3a do not share the Mga responder signature.

literature_claim: SREBP2 is a master transcriptional activator of cholesterol and sterol-biosynthesis genes.
main_caveats: The assay measures RNA, not SREBP2 cleavage, cholesterol mass, or Mib1 protein; 007 contributes only Hmgcs1 to the sterol list and 217 P MY Pineal Glut has only 23 perturbed nuclei despite a coherent signature.
summary: Mib1 loss activates a recurrent SREBF2-like sterol/cholesterol-synthesis module in 8 strong neuronal groups, with an additional Hmgcs1-positive branch in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The screen does not primarily read out the textbook Notch fate-specification defect; it exposes a postnatal neuronal lipid-homeostasis state in which Mib1 restrains cholesterogenic transcription.

direction: Notch comparators flat; Mib1 sterol genes up
literature_claim: MIB1 ubiquitinates Delta-like/Jagged ligands and is required for productive Notch signaling in mammalian development.
main_caveats: Notch activity was inferred from RNA targets and related CRISPR perturbations, not from ligand endocytosis or NICD protein.
summary: The Mib1 sterol response is uncoupled from canonical Notch transcription in this postmitotic neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: Mib1 is a Notch-ligand E3 ligase by prior biology, but the measured post-P16 neuronal phenotype does not collapse onto Dll1, Notch, ADAM10 or presenilin perturbation and lacks HES/HEY/Nrarp/Dtx1 induction or repression.

literature_claim: Rab7 late-endosomal trafficking, dynein-dynactin transport, mTORC1 signaling and MARCHF6-dependent ER degradation of cholesterol enzymes all regulate membrane or cholesterol homeostasis.
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to the 172 significant Mib1 features; convergence is transcriptional and does not prove a direct physical interaction between Mib1 and Dctn1/Rab7.
summary: Dctn1 was the strongest positive signature neighbor of Mib1, and Rab7, Htt, Marchf6 and Tsc2 also aligned in the same sterol genes.
why_it_matters: The unbiased neighbor search points to endolysosomal/dynein, mTOR and ER sterol-control perturbations rather than to Notch receptors as the closest functional neighborhood of the Mib1 response.

literature_claim: Loss of SREBP2 is expected to reduce cholesterol-synthesis gene expression.
main_caveats: Phf12, Zbtb7a and Uba5 are empirical inverse neighbors; their mechanistic route to sterol repression is not established here.
summary: Direct Srebf2 perturbation is the top inverse signature neighbor of Mib1.
why_it_matters: Opposite regulation by the pathway transcription factor validates that the repeated Hmgcr/Fdft1/Sqle/Cyp51/Msmo1/Dhcr24 block is bona fide SREBF2 output and not a generic stress artifact.

literature_claim: Mib1 can regulate ciliogenesis through centriolar satellites, and RFX3 is a ciliogenic transcription factor.
main_caveats: Only six genes pass FDR<0.10 in 47 perturbed nuclei; this is a restricted signature, not a reconstructed cilia pathway.
summary: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut carries a small cortical Mib1 response enriched for Pde4a, Ptprf, Rfx3, Gde1 and Fst rather than the broad subcortical sterol battery.
why_it_matters: The Rfx3 call provides a limited bridge to Mib1 centriolar-satellite/ciliogenesis biology, but the absence of Pcm1 and Ccdc14 transcriptional changes argues that the screen did not recover a full ciliary proteostasis state.

direction: absent except isolated Nfe2l1 in 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: snRNA-seq would miss transient protein-level stress, but persistent secondary stress transcription was not present at harvest.
summary: Mib1-responsive cells did not mount a broad nuclear UPR, ISR, autophagy, lysosomal or proteasome-bounce-back program.
why_it_matters: The sterol signature is therefore interpretable as specific lipid-homeostatic transcription rather than as part of indiscriminate E3-ligase or organelle damage stress.

literature_claim: MIC13/QIL1 loss is expected to disrupt MICOS/crista-junction architecture rather than to induce a known Zfp687 or Ppm1f module.
main_caveats: Each responder contained only one FDR<0.10 gene and the two FDR values were just below 0.10.
summary: Micos13 produced a two-hit, GABA-restricted nuclear response: Zfp687 up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and Ppm1f down in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, with no other FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the other 21 measured groups.
why_it_matters: The measured consequence is not a pan-neuronal mitochondrial stress signature; the only robust RNA changes are singleton regulatory-signal genes in two GABA-rich classes.

literature_claim: MICOS13, MICOS, OPA1, and YME1L control crista organization, and MICOS13 loss can reduce mitochondrial respiration.
main_caveats: Absence of nuclear stress genes does not exclude cristae-junction defects, because the screen did not measure mitochondria by EM, proteomics, or respirometry.
summary: The postnatal Micos13 transcriptome did not recover a canonical mitochondrial ISR, OXPHOS, or lipid-stress program in the responder cells; Opa1 and Dctn1 induced those programs in the same 054/066 groups, but Micos13 did not.
why_it_matters: This separates a primary crista-junction assembly factor from downstream nuclear stress readouts and argues that Micos13 loss did not impose an Opa1-like energetic crisis on these survivor nuclei.

literature_claim: MICOS subunits, OPA1, and YME1L all regulate crista architecture or dynamics.
main_caveats: The closest same-complex comparators were absent from the target universe, so the contrast is with adjacent cristae/dynamics genes rather than another measured MICOS core subunit.
summary: Represented cristae and mitochondrial-dynamics relatives were not interchangeable with Micos13: Opa1 gave a broad amino-acid/ISR signature, Yme1l1 and Mff were flat, and the direct MICOS subunits were not perturbation targets.
why_it_matters: The comparison prevents collapsing all cristae regulators into one transcriptional phenotype; in this assay, Opa1 has a nuclear stress-coupled mode that Micos13 and Yme1l1 lack.

main_caveats: Full-vector z-score similarity is dominated by non-significant ranks for such a sparse target, so the accepted conclusion is the measured failure to share FDR<0.10 markers rather than the identity of the low-cosine neighbors themselves.
summary: The full-signature data-driven neighbors of Micos13 were numerically weak and did not reproduce the two Micos13 singleton markers in matched cells.
why_it_matters: The highest whole-transcriptome cosine was only 0.038, and the top positive and negative neighbors were rejected as phenocopies; the Micos13 response is therefore best treated as a sparse idiosyncratic surface, not a member of a large convergent module.

literature_claim: Published MICOS13 studies identify cristae-junction and MICOS-assembly phenotypes, not Zfp687 or Ppm1f as established downstream markers.
main_caveats: Both markers are single-gene FDR<0.10 calls; they need guide-level replication or orthogonal validation before use as biomarkers.
summary: Zfp687 and Ppm1f are exploratory, cell-group-specific sentinels of Micos13 perturbation because no other target in the parquet changed the exact same gene/cell-group feature at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: If these singleton hits validate, they would mark separable GABA responses to MICOS13 loss rather than generic CRISPR, mitochondrial, or stress responses.

literature_claim: Complete MICU1 loss disinhibits MCU-dependent mitochondrial calcium uptake, causes calcium overload/ROS or ATP phenotypes, and produces brain-muscle or neuronal disease phenotypes.
main_caveats: Cas9 indel formation was not measured; weak self-transcript depletion is expected in this AAV Perturb-seq design; live mitochondrial calcium, ATP, ROS, and survival were not assayed, and 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
summary: Micu1 was transcriptionally silent by the study threshold: every one of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for this target.
why_it_matters: This sharply bounds the interpretation of acute P16 mosaic Micu1 loss: the surviving juvenile-to-young-adult NeuN+ neurons did not mount a stable autonomous nuclear DE program, even though complete MICU1 loss is a strong mitochondrial calcium phenotype in other systems.

literature_claim: Severe MICU1 deficiency can cause mitochondrial calcium overload, ROS, ATP defects, and excitotoxic death; severe inner-mitochondrial perturbation can feed forward into stress and quality-control programs.
main_caveats: Opa1 is an inner-membrane quality-control comparator, not a uniporter subunit; absence of FDR-significant marker transcripts cannot rule out acute calcium flux or metabolite abnormalities.
summary: The Micu1 null was not hiding a canonical stress module: ISR, UPR, redox, heat-shock, mitophagy, and proteostasis markers were all absent at FDR<0.10, whereas Opa1 perturbation in the same analysis produced a recurrent ISR/amino-acid response.
why_it_matters: This turns the null into a biological refinement: basal postnatal Micu1 perturbation did not progress to chronic mitochondrial damage signaling detectable by snRNA-seq, and the assay was capable of detecting such a program when a mitochondrial comparator elicited it.

main_caveats: The calculation used Wilcoxon-score cosine over shared Micu1-tested gene/cell-group rows; a flat target makes even rank-level neighbor calls intrinsically low-information.
summary: Data-driven Micu1 signature neighbors were numerically near zero and were rejected as biological convergence: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score cosine was 0.037 and the strongest negative was -0.024.
why_it_matters: Neighbor analysis did not nominate a hidden robust module for Micu1; its nearest profiles were either safe/flat or unrelated targets with very small whole-transcriptome correlations.

literature_claim: The MICU proteins are MCU calcium sensors and MICU3 is a brain-enriched MICU1 partner; OPA1 marks a distinct mitochondrial inner-membrane quality-control axis.
main_caveats: The strongest comparator, Opa1, is not in the MCU complex; direct MCU-complex convergence remains unmeasured because those targets are absent from the parquet.
summary: The screen could not test true MICU1 same-complex or paralog epistasis because Mcu, Mcub, Micu2, Micu3, Smdt1, Ccdc90a, Slc8b1, and Letm1 were absent as targets; a broader mitochondrial panel was mixed, with Opa1 strong but Ndufs4, Ppargc1a, Park7, and Yme1l1 flat.
why_it_matters: The Micu1 result should not be generalized to MCU biology as a whole, but it also is not simply a failure of neuronal snRNA-seq to see mitochondrial perturbations.

literature_claim: MIF is a cytokine/tautomerase-family protein that can signal through CD74/CXCR4-family receptors, activate MAPK/NF-kB-like inflammatory responses, and antagonize p53 in responsive systems.
main_caveats: Engagement is inferred from transcript shifts rather than DNA indel sequencing; the negative result is limited to uninjured, postnatal neurons and does not test glial or immune responses.
summary: Mif is downstream-silent across the entire recovered neuronal surface: no cell group had a non-Mif FDR<0.10 gene despite recurrent negative self-transcript shifts.
why_it_matters: This converts a broad zero into an interpretable result: in juvenile postmitotic NeuN+ neurons, basal Mif loss does not by itself launch inflammatory, stress, trophic, or apoptotic transcriptional programs expected from many MIF disease models.

literature_claim: MIF and D-DT/MIF-2 are related cytokines with overlapping CD74/CD44 signaling functions.
main_caveats: Only Mif, not Ddt, was perturbed; this is evidence against transcriptional Ddt induction, not against protein-level or ligand-level redundancy.
summary: The only corrected Mif event was a self-decrease in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, not a downstream module or Ddt-family compensation.
why_it_matters: A corrected self-transcript drop shows that the assay could register direct Mif depletion, yet Ddt and canonical inflammatory or stress-response genes remained FDR-flat; the hypothalamic/mammillary glutamatergic cell class therefore buffers acute postnatal Mif loss at the mRNA level.

literature_claim: MIF-family ligands and CD74/CXCR4 receptors can drive MAPK signaling, inflammatory transcription, survival signaling, and p53 antagonism in responsive cells.
main_caveats: Many direct extracellular receptors were not perturbation targets, and the represented intracellular comparators are generic pleiotropic genes rather than one-to-one MIF complex members.
summary: Represented receptor and effector perturbations from the MIF literature failed to form a robust neuronal Mif-like module.
why_it_matters: Mif was not hiding within a shared CD74/CXCR4-MAPK-NF-kB-p53 transcriptional axis in this assay: Cxcr4 produced only two isolated downstream genes, Mapk1 showed only self-depletion, and Nfkb1, Rel, Mapk9, Hif1a, and Trp53 were downstream-flat, while Ddt/Ddtl/Cd74/Cd44/Cxcr2/Ackr3 were unavailable as targets.

summary: The pre-literature signature-neighbor search nominated only restricted, sub-FDR alignments with mostly flat targets.
why_it_matters: Kalrn, Plcb1, Gpr161, Eif4g1, Prkca, and Gria3 were the strongest positive or negative neighbors over 113 nominal Mif features, but their FDR surfaces did not overlap Mif; the calculation rejects a hidden robust convergent module and places Mif among the many transcriptome-mute targets in the screen.

literature_claim: PGBD5 is a neural-enriched piggyBac-derived gene, but no published Minar2-PGBD5 regulatory link was found.
main_caveats: One downstream gene only and 46 perturbed L5 ET nuclei; this is a restricted-signature result.
summary: Minar2 has a single robust downstream response: Pgbd5 up-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The only FDR<0.10 hit is in a defined corticofugal excitatory class and is not a broad whole-brain Minar2 program; it nominates a narrow neuronal hypothesis rather than confirming canonical hair-cell, mTORC1, or Notch biology.

literature_claim: No literature-predicted relationship was tested for these data-driven neighbors.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed on a near-null Minar2 signature, so the main inference is rejection of a strong neighbor, not positive mechanistic convergence.
summary: Pre-literature whole-signature neighbors were almost orthogonal to Minar2 and failed to reproduce the L5 ET Pgbd5 event.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting the lone Pgbd5 hit as part of a recurrent perturbation module; the nearest positive and negative neighbors look like noise-level full-transcriptome matches rather than meaningful Minar2 biology.

literature_claim: Minar2 interacts with Raptor and negatively regulates mTORC1 in adipocytes; loss of Minar2 hyperactivates mTOR signaling in that lineage.
main_caveats: mTOR activity is often phosphorylation-based; absence of an RNA signature does not exclude subtle local mTORC1 biochemical changes.
summary: Minar2 loss in postnatal neurons did not generate a Tsc2-like mTORC1 transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: The screen contained an mTORC1-activating comparator that produced hundreds of neuronal DE genes, including sterol and lysosomal genes, yet Minar2 remained flat; the adipocyte Minar2-Raptor mechanism therefore does not generalize as an acute neuronal RNA program in these conditions.

literature_claim: MINAR2 and the paralog MINAR1 are linked to NOTCH2 binding or interaction in non-screen contexts.
main_caveats: The direct paralog Minar1 was not represented as a perturbation target, and Notch receptor knockdowns were also weak in this neuronal assay.
summary: Notch receptor perturbations did not converge with Minar2.
why_it_matters: The named NOTCH2 association was an obvious prior, but Notch2 loss was itself a transcriptomic null and Notch1/Notch4 were sparse; acute Minar2 LoF in surveyed neurons should not be summarized as a Notch transcriptional phenotype.

literature_claim: Minar2 controls cholesterol distribution and homeostasis in sensory hair bundles, whereas SREBPs regulate transcription of cholesterol and fatty-acid synthesis genes.
main_caveats: The assay did not sample inner-ear hair cells and cannot measure membrane cholesterol localization directly.
summary: Minar2 did not activate or suppress an Srebf2-like sterol-biosynthetic transcriptome.
why_it_matters: The screen could detect a coordinated cholesterol-biosynthesis program after Srebf2 perturbation, so the flat Minar2 result argues that hair-bundle cholesterol redistribution is not recapitulated as broad SREBP2 target-gene regulation in P16 postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Adult global Minar2 knockout mice were reported to have motor deficits, loss of tyrosine-hydroxylase-positive pars compacta neurons, and alpha-synuclein protein up-regulation, whereas human recessive MINAR2 disease was described as nonsyndromic deafness.
main_caveats: Broad MB and CB GABA groupings are not a one-to-one test of substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons or adult neuronal survival.
summary: Young midbrain and cerebellar neuronal groups did not recover the adult Minar2 knockout Parkinson-like phenotype, and 215 MB Dopa was missing.
why_it_matters: The adult mouse phenotype points to a specific late nigrostriatal and protein-abundance axis; the P37-44 NeuN+ assay should not be interpreted as disproving that phenotype because the matching dopaminergic group was not recovered for Minar2.

literature_claim: Mkx is an Iroquois-related transcription factor whose established mammalian loss-of-function phenotypes are tendon and periodontal/mesenchymal rather than postmitotic neuronal.
main_caveats: The result is a strong negative only for the assayed P16-to-P37/P44 NeuN+ brain setting; DNA indels and unsampled mesenchymal tissues were not measured.
summary: Mkx loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal null: 21 measured cell groups each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut were not tested for Mkx.
why_it_matters: The complete absence of a robust neuronal transcriptional response is itself the main phenotype and is consistent with Mkx biology being displaced to tendon, ligament, periodontal, and other mesenchymal lineages rather than juvenile NeuN+ brain neurons.

literature_claim: Mkx promotes type I collagen and tendon ECM genes, participates in TGFβ2-linked tenogenesis, and restrains Runx2/Sp7/Alpl-associated osteogenic drift in periodontal ligament fibroblasts.
main_caveats: Bglap, a PDL osteogenic marker reported in literature, was not present in the Mkx neuronal DE rows queried here and is therefore not included as a dataset-tested marker.
summary: Canonical Mkx-regulated tenogenic ECM, tendon, TGFβ, and PDL/osteogenic readouts were present in the DE gene universe but were uncoupled from Mkx perturbation in neurons.

main_caveats: Cosine was computed on a null Msl2 signature, so these are exploratory restricted-signature checks rather than mechanistic pathway assignments.

why_it_matters: The required cross-perturbation scan rejected the possibility that a coherent but sub-threshold Msl2 module was hiding in the continuous scores; the closest apparent neighbors were weak or unrelated when their matched FDR-level surfaces were re-queried.

literature_claim: Msx genes are embryonic cerebellar neuroepithelial transcription factors, whereas SBF2/MTMR13 is known for MTMR2-associated endomembrane and peripheral-neuropathy biology rather than as an MSX2 target.

why_it_matters: Sbf2 nominates an endomembrane/phosphoinositide gene as the only reproducible postnatal neuronal readout of Msx2 loss, but the one-gene signature makes it a marker hypothesis rather than a pathway call.

literature_claim: MSX factors act in embryonic BMP-responsive neural progenitor programs, including cerebellar neuroepithelium and Msx1/Msx2-dependent Atoh1 activation in the dorsal spinal cord.
main_caveats: The assay observes only surviving NeuN+ postmitotic nuclei and does not test embryonic progenitors directly.

why_it_matters: The screen directly argues that acute Msx2 loss at P16 is not maintaining a broad canonical developmental transcriptome in juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: Canonical BMP signaling through type I/II BMP receptors and Smad1/5/8 is a major route to BMP-dependent neural developmental transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: Several comparator perturbations were weak in this fixed-dose CRISPR assay, so non-phenocopy is strongest for the absence of Sbf2 movement rather than for all possible BMP outputs.
summary: BMP-receptor and Smad perturbations represented in the screen did not phenocopy the Msx2-to-Sbf2 cerebellar GABA event.
why_it_matters: Although MSX genes are classical BMP effectors, the measured P16 neuronal BMP-SMAD perturbations were themselves nearly flat and did not reproduce Sbf2 induction, so the Sbf2 event should not be assigned to a canonical BMP-SMAD module in this dataset.

main_caveats: Cosines were computed on the 500 most nominal Msx2 entries, not on a multi-gene FDR-controlled Msx2 program.
summary: Restricted-signature neighbors of Msx2 were computational but not FDR-convergent; Wdr26 and Ranbp2 showed large opposing CB GABA signatures without sharing the single Sbf2 hit at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The top-neighbor exercise prevents over-reading Msx2 as part of a robust Wdr26/Ranbp2 cerebellar module: the apparent similarity used nominal Msx2 ranks, whereas the corrected Msx2 signature remained one gene.

literature_claim: MSX2 binds DNA as a transcriptional repressor; gain-of-function MSX2 causes Boston-type craniosynostosis and loss-of-function MSX2/ALX4 alleles cause parietal foramina through skull-vault developmental mechanisms.
main_caveats: No craniofacial lineage was sampled and the screen did not assay skull morphology.
summary: The postnatal neuronal LoF surface does not model human MSX2 skull phenotypes or Boston-type gain-of-function craniosynostosis.
why_it_matters: MSX2 disease genetics point to dosage- and allele-sensitive cranial ossification; a sparse P16 neuronal CRISPR LoF with almost no downstream transcription is therefore best interpreted as lineage and window restriction, not as absence of MSX2 biology.

literature_claim: Germline Mt3-null mice have reduced total brain zinc but normal basal growth, brain gross morphology, and hippocampal learning unless challenged by aging or kainate.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not assayed, so the RNA self-row is engagement context rather than proof that every nucleus carried a loss-of-function allele.
summary: Mt3 perturbation showed a pan-measured buffered basal phenotype: the Mt3 self-row shifted negative in every recovered cell group, with FDR-significant self-depletion in 3 groups, but no downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in any of 22 measured groups.
why_it_matters: This converts an apparently flat screen target into a biologically interpretable steady-state negative: neuronal Mt3 mRNA can be reduced in a juvenile acute CRISPR setting without launching a detectable basal transcriptional compensation program.

literature_claim: MT3 has been linked to oxidative-stress zinc release, lysosomal function, and autophagy, particularly in cultured astrocytes and challenged cells.
main_caveats: A no-challenge neuronal screen cannot refute stress- or astrocyte-specific MT3 functions; it only rules out an autonomous basal neuronal induction of these sentinels.
summary: Mt3 loss did not activate metallothionein compensation, Nrf2/glutathione redox genes, heat-shock/ISR genes, or lysosomal/autophagy sentinels in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: MT3 is frequently framed as a zinc/oxidative-stress/lysosome gene; the dataset shows that acute basal neuronal loss is not sufficient to trigger that secondary transcriptome, even though other perturbations in the same parquet can recover Ddit3, Herpud1, Hsph1, and Hsp90aa1 responses.

literature_claim: MT3 is abundant in zincergic hippocampal neurons and Mt3-null mice show enhanced kainate-linked CA3 injury.
main_caveats: The DE group aggregates CA3, CA2 and dentate/fasciola-cinerea neurons; a narrow CA3-only or seizure-time transcriptional response could be diluted or absent from this steady-state assay.
summary: Hippocampal Mt3 perturbation was flat in both recovered hippocampal glutamatergic groups, including the CA3/CA2-FC/DG group.
why_it_matters: The kainate literature points to CA3-selective vulnerability when MT3 is absent, but this screen places that vulnerability downstream of seizure or zinc-mobilizing challenge rather than in a tonic P16-to-P37/44 CA3 transcriptional state.

literature_claim: Metallothionein and redox biology nominates Mt1, Mt2, Mt4, Mtf1, and stress-response genes as obvious comparators for Mt3.
main_caveats: Because Mt3 itself has zero FDR<0.10 downstream genes, all-neighbor statistics are restricted-signature diagnostics rather than evidence for a mechanistic partnership with the ranked neighboring targets.
summary: Neither phenotype-first nor literature-obvious cross-perturbation queries found a convergent Mt3 module in the parquet.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation comparison prevents over-reading of isolated nominal Mt3 rows: the strongest non-control score-neighbors had near-zero correlations, top neighbors had only one robust row apiece, same-family metallothionein targets were absent, and represented redox comparators did not phenocopy Mt3.

literature_claim: KIF21A is a kinesin-4 microtubule-growth inhibitor with cytoskeletal roles relevant to neuronal morphology, but it is not a canonical MT2/melatonin target gene.
main_caveats: Single FDR-significant gene in 60 perturbed cerebellar GABA nuclei; Kif21a up-regulation should be treated as a candidate readout, not a resolved module.
summary: Mtnr1b loss produced a single robust downstream event, Kif21a up-regulation, and it was restricted to 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: This turns an otherwise flat MT2 perturbation into a narrow cerebellar GABA result and nominates Kif21a as a single-gene cytoskeletal readout rather than a broad melatonin, cAMP, stress, or clock program.

literature_claim: MT2 is a high-affinity melatonin GPCR that signals largely through Gi/o to inhibit adenylyl cyclase, and MT2 contributes to melatonin modulation of CREB signaling in the SCN.
main_caveats: The literature expectation comes from ligand-stimulated or germline settings; this screen used unstimulated, sparse, postnatal CRISPR in a melatonin-deficient strain.
summary: The FDR surface uncoupled Mtnr1b from the expected MT2 Gi/cAMP/CREB and circadian-clock transcriptional programs.
why_it_matters: If postnatal MT2 loss created a sustained ligand-dependent disinhibition of cAMP/CREB or clock-gene transcription, snRNA-seq should have captured downstream immediate-early or clock RNAs; their absence makes the null informative under the C57BL/6J no-high-amplitude-melatonin context rather than merely a readout failure.

main_caveats: Restricted by Mtnr1b having only one robust downstream gene; full-score Pearson correlations are dominated by weak, non-FDR structure.
summary: Data-driven signature neighbors did not validate a recurrent Mtnr1b-like program.
why_it_matters: The strongest whole-profile correlations were near zero and the nearest broad responder, Wdr26, did not make Kif21a significant in 308 CB GABA, arguing that the Mtnr1b Kif21a event is not a generic cerebellar stress or high-DE artifact.

literature_claim: Common and rare MTNR1B variants are linked to altered insulin secretion and type 2 diabetes, and MT1/MT2 heteromers act in retina, neither of which is recreated by neuronal MT2 CRISPR in this assay.
main_caveats: The result is a scope refinement, not evidence that MTNR1B is irrelevant to beta cells, retina, or ligand-stimulated CNS physiology.
summary: The screen argues against treating unstimulated juvenile neuronal MT2 loss as a proxy for MTNR1B diabetes alleles or melatonergic drug exposure.
why_it_matters: Human MTNR1B risk involves pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion and coding variants with distinct signaling defects; this NeuN-enriched brain screen, with beta cells, retina, olfactory bulb, and pituitary pars tuberalis absent or outside scope, mainly tests baseline neuronal receptor removal in a melatonin-deficient mouse.

literature_claim: mTOR signaling has broad neuronal functions in growth control, translation, gene expression, autophagy, and metabolic balance rather than a known restriction to these two adult cell classes.
main_caveats: The two positive signatures are small: five downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and one in 155 MB Glut.
summary: Mtor loss-of-function produced an FDR-supported RNA response in only 2 of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The selective TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and MB Glut response is the central phenotype; the absence of FDR-supported genes in the other 21 groups is not missing data because Mtor was queried in every group.

literature_claim: Strong mTORC1 loss is expected to alter translation, autophagy, lipid synthesis, mitochondrial metabolism, and neuronal homeostasis, not this exact five-gene module.
main_caveats: Each functional submodule is represented by one or a few FDR-supported genes, so it should be treated as a responder marker set, not as a fully resolved pathway.
summary: The TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Mtor signature is a five-gene mixed module, with Rims3, Comt, and Pink1 up and Tmed8 and Kndc1 down.
why_it_matters: Pink1 and Tmed8 place the weak TH response near mitochondrial and secretory/ER trafficking stress edges, while Rims3, Comt, and Kndc1 make the module neuronal rather than a clean global ribosome, lysosome, or SREBP program.

literature_claim: UBA5 and UFC1 are core enzymes in the UFM1 post-translational modification pathway, which supports ER-associated ribosome quality control and ER protein homeostasis.
main_caveats: The Mtor signature is only six genes; Uba5 is the strongest overlap, Ufc1 and Ufsp2 contribute weaker same-direction evidence, and Tbl1xr1 was rejected because it did not reproduce any of the six responder genes at FDR<0.10.
summary: The top positive Mtor neighbors were enriched for UFMylation factors: Uba5 was the #1 global neighbor and Ufc1 was #2, with Uba5 reproducing four of the six Mtor responder genes at FDR<0.10 in the same directions.
why_it_matters: This was not the textbook-obvious mTORC1 complex; it nominates ER/ribosome quality-control biology as the closest measured transcriptomic neighbor of the small Mtor signature.

literature_claim: TSC2 inhibits Rheb-mTORC1, whereas DEPDC5 is part of GATOR1, a Rag-GTPase GAP complex that suppresses amino-acid signaling to mTORC1.
main_caveats: Only Stmn4 gives a clean opposite FDR-supported overlap with Mtor; most Tsc2 and Depdc5 genes are not present in the tiny Mtor signature.
summary: Tsc2, an upstream mTORC1 brake, was the strongest anti-neighbor of Mtor and reversed the MB Glut Stmn4 effect.
why_it_matters: The sign is directionally consistent with the pathway: loss of a repressor should activate mTORC1 and oppose loss of the Mtor kinase; it also shows that MB Glut and several Mtor-null groups can mount a large mTOR-pathway-adjacent RNA response.

literature_claim: Raptor is the scaffold essential for mTORC1, PI3K/AKT is a growth-factor input to mTOR, and FKBP12 is the rapamycin-binding, non-obligate mTORC1 inhibitor cofactor.
main_caveats: Flat transcriptomes do not prove absent protein-level pathway effects, especially for Rptor whose self-transcript was not measurably depleted.
summary: Canonical same-pathway perturbations did not phenocopy Mtor loss: Rptor and Fkbp1a were FDR-flat across all 23 groups, and Akt3/Pik3cb/Pik3r1/Pik3r2 were flat wherever measured.
why_it_matters: A simple wiring diagram would predict Rptor loss to share mTORC1-loss outputs, but the sparse postnatal RNA surface instead separates the kinase target from same-complex and upstream-node perturbations.

why_it_matters: The negative result distinguishes a constitutive cell-autonomous mRNA response from a MuSK role that may require cholinergic drive, learning, or electrophysiological readout.

why_it_matters: MuSK is kinase-like and pharmacologically conceivable, but congenital and autoimmune myasthenic biology makes peripheral antagonism a mechanistic risk that this NeuN+ whole-brain-minus-OB/hindbrain dataset cannot test.

literature_claim: Mouse and neural conditional studies place essential Myc-family loss-of-function phenotypes in embryonic development and Nestin-positive neural stem or precursor populations.
main_caveats: The actual indel load was not measured, and the Myc mRNA row was not reduced; in this platform a flat self-transcript is expected and does not rule out functional indels.
summary: Acute Myc loss of function is a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null in the P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ screen: zero downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 in the 22 recovered cell groups.
why_it_matters: MYC is a potent transcriptional growth regulator, so the absence of any adjusted DE argues that these already specified juvenile neurons do not maintain a basal MYC-dependent mRNA program comparable to proliferative Myc biology.

literature_claim: MYC coordinates expression of ribosome-biogenesis, protein-synthesis, metabolism, and cycling genes; c-/N-myc loss in cerebellar precursors weakens nucleolin and disrupts precursor cycling.
main_caveats: The hand-tested panel is finite, and canonical ribosomal-protein reads were not all visible in the model-visible DE universe; the global zero prevents gene-set-level confirmation.
summary: The expected MYC growth, ribosome-biogenesis, translation, and cell-cycle transcript panel was completely absent from the Myc DE surface.
why_it_matters: A MYC-driven secondary transcriptional collapse should be visible to snRNA-seq if present; all queried growth genes had adjusted P=1.0, making the null informative rather than a membrane, morphology, or electrophysiology readout mismatch.

literature_claim: MYC, MYCN, MNT, and MGA sit in a MAX-linked bHLHZip network, and c-Myc/N-Myc can show additive or redundant precursor roles during cerebellar development.
main_caveats: Max, Mycl, and MXD targets were absent from the parquet, and the retained network-member DE signatures were themselves small.
summary: The represented MYC/MAX-network relatives Mycn, Mnt, and Mga did not phenocopy Myc.
why_it_matters: Same-network membership was not enough to predict transcriptomic convergence in these postmitotic neuronal nuclei: Mycn, Mnt, and Mga each produced only sparse, cell-restricted DE while Myc stayed flat in the same groups.

main_caveats: Whole-surface correlations over a null Myc vector can be noise dominated; the result is useful mainly to show that there was no hidden strong Myc-like perturbation in the screen.
summary: A blind search across all other perturbations found no strong positive or negative Myc signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The leading correlations were only r=0.035 to r=-0.0166; therefore Sp7, Dlx6, Grin3a, Uqcrq, Cisd2, Sacs, Agk, Cltc, Mff, and Setd2 are best read as a data-driven rejection set rather than a biologically convergent Myc module.

literature_claim: MYCN is best established as a driver of embryonic and early postnatal neural precursor proliferation, whereas SST interneurons are differentiated inhibitory neurons that can express somatostatin receptors.
main_caveats: The Sst signature has only five genes, a 72-cell perturbed sample, and FDR values of 0.057-0.091 rather than <0.05.
summary: Acute Mycn loss produced a small but FDR-supported signature only in 053 Sst Gaba neurons.
why_it_matters: This moves Mycn from a purely progenitor/proliferation prior to a detectable, postmitotic Sst-interneuron transcriptional response, while preserving the fact that the response is modest and restricted.

literature_claim: Mouse SST interneurons can express multiple somatostatin-receptor subtypes, including SSTR1, and receptor distribution varies across interneuron subtype and layer.
main_caveats: Single-gene biomarker; no peptide, receptor trafficking, or electrophysiology was measured.
summary: Sstr1 was the largest Mycn-responsive transcript in Sst neurons and nominates somatostatin-receptor remodeling as the clearest marker of this response.
why_it_matters: Sstr1 gives the otherwise tiny Mycn Sst signature a receptor-level readout that could be followed by targeted validation, but the dataset does not prove altered SST ligand responsiveness.

literature_claim: MYC/MAX-family activity promotes cell growth through cell-cycle, ribosome-biogenesis, protein-synthesis, and metabolic transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: A fixed snRNA-seq snapshot cannot exclude protein-only MYCN functions or responses in dividing progenitors missing from this assay.
summary: The screen did not recover the canonical Myc/MYCN proliferative growth program after Mycn perturbation.
why_it_matters: The absence of cell-cycle, ribosome-biogenesis, translation, and metabolic MYCN targets is informative because many of these transcripts were tested and completely flat; canonical MYCN biology is displaced to proliferative developmental or tumor states rather than reproduced in P16 postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Myc, MNT, MLXIP/MondoA and regulators such as FBXW7 sit in or near the MYC/MAX/MLX network, and Atoh1 and MYCN both participate in SHH-responsive cerebellar granule-neuron precursor biology.
main_caveats: Several comparators had fewer Sst perturbed nuclei than Mycn, and MAX, MYCL, and MXD-family targets were not represented.
summary: Measured MYC-family, MYC-regulator, SHH-GNP, and neuronal developmental comparators did not phenocopy the Sst Mycn signature.
why_it_matters: Mycn's five-gene Sst response is not a generic readout of perturbing any MYC/MAX-network or cerebellar-developmental target in this assay; even expected relatives were flat or produced tiny, nonoverlapping signals.

main_caveats: The all-vector cosine is dominated by Mycn's near-null surface; this finding rejects the neighbors rather than assigning them mechanism.
summary: A target-agnostic genome-wide neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Mycn signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top whole-surface cosine similarities were close to zero and failed a direct FDR-overlap check, so downstream interpretation should not be borrowed from the nominal Arid1b/Auts2/Chmp4b or Dld/Ago2/Hnrnpu neighborhoods.

summary: Canonical NFAT5 osmolyte and heat-shock targets were absent while Slc38a2 was recovered.
why_it_matters: The Nfat5 effect is not a miniature version of a full hypertonic program; basal CRISPR loss in unchallenged neurons selectively exposed a Slc38a2 arm and left SMIT, TauT, BGT1, aldose reductase, Hsp70-family, Sgk1, and Aqp4 targets flat.

literature_claim: NFAT5 is mechanistically distinct from conventional NFAT1-4 factors such as NFATc3.
main_caveats: Only Nfatc3, not all NFATc paralogs, was represented as a perturbation target in the parquet.
summary: Nfatc3 does not phenocopy the Nfat5 Slc38a2 response.
why_it_matters: The directly measured NFAT-family comparison supports NFAT5-specific tonicity biology rather than a generic effect of deleting an NFAT-related transcription factor in the same cell groups.

literature_claim: No NFAT5 prior nominated these data-driven neighbors as same-pathway osmotic comparators.
main_caveats: The neighbor search used only the two significant Slc38a2 coordinates because Nfat5 had no larger FDR signature; it is hypothesis-generating.
summary: Two-coordinate data-driven neighbors do not define a robust same-direction Nfat5 module, but Elp1/Gfpt1/Elp2 oppose Nfat5 on thalamic Slc38a2.
why_it_matters: The strongest same-direction candidates were weak or one-cell-type-only, whereas several unrelated perturbations significantly increased Slc38a2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; this makes Slc38a2 a bidirectional homeostatic node rather than a broad NFAT5-specific signature cluster.

literature_claim: NFATc3 participates in calcium/calcineurin- and AP-1-gated transcription in stimulated neurons, neural precursor cells, embryonic axon growth, and deprivation-induced cerebellar granule-neuron apoptosis.
main_caveats: Engagement is inferred only from gRNA assignment rather than indel sequencing; negative result is restricted to basal P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ neuronal CRISPR.
summary: Acute Nfatc3 loss produced no durable downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 measured juvenile neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: This is a strong context-specific negative result: Nfatc3 is not acting as a constitutive postmitotic maintenance transcription factor in the assayed basal NeuN+ neuronal nuclei, even though NFATc3 can be activated in neuronal and precursor systems in the literature.

literature_claim: Calcineurin dephosphorylates conventional NFATc proteins, including NFATc3, but also participates broadly in neuronal signaling.
main_caveats: The comparator signatures are narrow; the dataset did not perturb Nfatc1, Nfatc2, or Nfatc4, so redundancy cannot be epistatically resolved.
summary: Calcineurin-subunit perturbations scored where Nfatc3 was flat, especially Ppp3r1 and Ppp3ca in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Because Ppp3r1 and Ppp3ca are upstream calcineurin components, their non-overlap with Nfatc3 shows that the detectable acute calcineurin-subunit signatures in this dataset are not simple Nfatc3-loss signatures.

literature_claim: NFAT5 is an outlying NFAT-family transcription factor that is constitutively nuclear and does not cooperate with Fos/Jun like conventional NFAT1-4 proteins.
main_caveats: Nfat5 was itself a weak two-gene-surface responder; the true conventional paralogs Nfatc1, Nfatc2, and Nfatc4 were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: The assayed NFAT-family outlier Nfat5 did not phenocopy Nfatc3; it produced only Slc38a2 down-regulation in two groups.
why_it_matters: This keeps Nfat5 from being over-read as a functional substitute for missing NFATc paralogs; the measured divergence matches NFAT5's known calcineurin-independent regulatory logic.

literature_claim: No literature-obvious relationship was used for these data-driven neighbors.
main_caveats: Cosine comparison used all ranked genes, not a significant Nfatc3 signature, because Nfatc3 had no FDR<0.10 genes.
summary: Whole-profile signature-neighbor analysis found no robust convergent or opposing Nfatc3 module.
why_it_matters: The top positive Nfatc3 neighbors had near-zero cosines and no FDR hits of their own, so the globally ranked Nfatc3 surface is indistinguishable from null-like noise rather than a weak version of a known gene program.

literature_claim: Calcineurin/NFAT signaling has context-dependent beneficial and detrimental roles in adult and developing nervous-system disease, with contributions from neurons, astrocytes, microglia, vascular cells, and injury conditions.
main_caveats: The screen lacked aged disease models, exogenous injury, pharmacologic pathway blockade, and most non-neuronal lineages.
summary: Basal juvenile neuronal Nfatc3 loss does not recapitulate the glial, injury, aged, or pharmacological calcineurin/NFAT programs emphasized in disease literature.
why_it_matters: The result argues that a calcineurin/NFAT inhibitor effect in neurodegeneration should not be interpreted as direct Nfatc3 inhibition in otherwise unchallenged maturing neurons without testing the relevant older, injured, glial, or activity-stimulated context.

literature_claim: Brain-wide Nfe2l1 loss impairs proteasome gene expression and causes neurodegeneration.
main_caveats: The 151 group also had the largest Nfe2l1 perturbed-cell count, and the 191 signature contained only one downstream transcript.
summary: Nfe2l1 produced a very narrow neuronal response: 5 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 1 in 191 MB P MY GABA, with no downstream FDR signal in the other 19 measured groups.
why_it_matters: Complete neural Nfe2l1 loss is known to compromise proteasome expression and neuronal health, so the sparse P16 CRISPR result localizes the basal cell-autonomous transcriptome to two tiny responder windows rather than a broad pan-neuronal proteasome state.

literature_claim: After proteasome dysfunction, NFE2L1 is processed by VCP/DDI2 and up-regulates proteasome genes and aggrephagy genes such as SQSTM1 and GABARAPL1.
main_caveats: The screen was not proteasome-inhibitor challenged and did not assay NFE2L1 protein cleavage.
summary: The canonical NFE2L1 proteasome-bounce-back and aggrephagy transcriptional programs were not recovered after Nfe2l1 loss in the two FDR-positive groups.
why_it_matters: The strongest prior predicted coordinated 20S/19S proteasome and autophagy target-gene changes; their absence shows that acute basal Nfe2l1 LoF did not push these postmitotic neurons into the classic proteasome-insufficiency state.

literature_claim: Ubc is a stress-inducible polyubiquitin gene; OGT can post-translationally regulate NFE2L1; METTL17 is mitochondrial-ribosomal; TSPAN7 and PLPPR4 participate in synaptic biology.
main_caveats: Each noncanonical subprogram is represented by one or two genes, so this is a restricted-signature interpretation.
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature combined Ubc up-regulation with Ogt and Mettl17 down-regulation plus Tspan7 and Plppr4 induction.
why_it_matters: The mixture of a stress-inducible polyubiquitin transcript, O-GlcNAc and mitochondrial-ribosome factors, and neuronal membrane/synaptic genes indicates a small compensatory adjustment rather than direct reduction of proteasome-subunit mRNAs.

literature_claim: No literature in scope predicted Snhg11 as a direct NFE2L1 response gene in this neuronal context.
main_caveats: Single-gene signature with no canonical target genes; treat as hypothesis-generating.
summary: The 191 MB P MY GABA response was restricted to Snhg11 down-regulation and did not carry a recognizable NFE2L1 proteostasis, redox, chaperone, or aggrephagy module.
why_it_matters: Keeping this as a one-gene response prevents over-interpreting an FDR-supported cell group as a full pathway activation event.

literature_claim: UBA5 and UFC1 drive UFM1 conjugation in a pathway linked to ER stress, UPR, autophagy, and proteostasis.
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to the two Nfe2l1 responder groups and does not prove direct regulation between NFE2L1 and UFMylation.
summary: The strongest positive signature neighbors were Uba5 and Ufc1, UFMylation E1/E2 targets that partially shared the Nfe2l1 thalamic Ubc-up and Ogt-down pattern.
why_it_matters: This data-driven convergence nominates ER-proteostasis and UFMylation stress circuitry as closer to the observed Nfe2l1 signature than the textbook CNC paralog, while preserving the fact that Uba5 and Ufc1 were much broader perturbations.

literature_claim: Proteasome dysfunction activates NFE2L1-dependent compensatory transcription; direct proteasome loss should therefore be a stronger proteotoxic stimulus than loss of the latent regulator alone.
main_caveats: Psmb4 and Psmc1 have direct proteasome structural functions, so divergence does not imply they are downstream-only sensors of NFE2L1.
summary: Direct proteasome hits Psmb4 and Psmc1 induced hundreds to thousands of DE genes in the same matched groups where Nfe2l1 produced only 5 and 1 downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This contrast shows that proteotoxic transcriptional stress was detectable in this assay and that Nfe2l1 loss alone did not phenocopy proteasome insufficiency.

literature_claim: NFE2L1 and NFE2L2 are related ARE-binding CNC factors, NFE2L1 uses small-MAF partners including MAFG, VCP participates in NFE2L1 processing, and HSF1 can induce UBC.
main_caveats: Most upstream-processing genes known from the literature, including Ddi2 and Ngly1, were not represented as target perturbations in the parquet.
summary: Nfe2l2, Mafg, Vcp, and Hsf1 failed to phenocopy Nfe2l1 in the matched responder groups.
why_it_matters: ARE-family membership, a measured small-MAF partner, VCP-dependent NFE2L1 maturation, and HSF1-linked Ubc induction each suggested a possible comparator; the measured surfaces reject simple interchangeability in basal juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: NFE2L1-mediated bounce-back can limit proteasome-inhibitor efficacy and requires ERAD/VCP/DDI2-regulated activation after proteasome insufficiency.
main_caveats: The assay did not apply a proteasome inhibitor or a DDI2 inhibitor, so the therapeutic inference is directional rather than a drug test.
summary: The Nfe2l1 LoF transcriptome in unchallenged postmitotic neurons lacked the biomarkers expected for pharmacologic blockade of NFE2L1 during proteasome inhibition.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic strategies that inhibit DDI2/NFE2L1 to potentiate proteasome inhibitors should be profiled under proteasome stress or with direct proteasome and ubiquitinated-protein readouts; sparse Nfe2l1 LoF alone is not enough to report bounce-back failure.

literature_claim: NRF2 regulates inducible antioxidant and xenobiotic-defense transcription, while Nrf2-null mice can be grossly viable until challenged or aged.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured, and the result applies to basal juvenile neuronal nuclei rather than oxidative challenge, aged brain, or non-neuronal cells.
summary: Acute postnatal CRISPR loss of Nfe2l2 was transcriptionally silent across the 22 neuronal cell groups in which it was measured.
why_it_matters: NRF2 is a canonical ARE transcription factor, but this juvenile, unchallenged, NeuN-enriched assay found no basal neuronal dependence on Nfe2l2 at whole-transcriptome FDR<0.10.

literature_claim: NRF2-small-Maf complexes induce ARE-bearing cytoprotective genes such as Nqo1, Hmox1, Gclc, Gclm, glutathione-transferase, thioredoxin, and stress-defense genes after NRF2 activation.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq may miss protein oxidation or glutathione-pool defects, but it should have detected a sustained secondary Hspa5-like UPR if one were present.
summary: Canonical NRF2 antioxidant, glutathione, thioredoxin, ferritin, SQSTM1, UPR, and ISR transcripts were all absent from the corrected Nfe2l2 surface.
why_it_matters: The null is not merely a lack of novel genes: the exact mRNAs that should fall if basal NRF2 were sustaining an ARE program, or rise if NRF2 loss created redox/ER stress, were measured but never reached FDR<0.10.

main_caveats: Cosines are intrinsically unstable for a perturbation with zero FDR<0.10 genes; the conclusion is limited to rejecting strong convergence.
summary: Full-vector signature search placed Nfe2l2 next to only near-zero neighbors, including flat Safe_target labels, and opposite to Wdr26 only weakly.
why_it_matters: The nearest-neighbor landscape independently says the Nfe2l2 vector is essentially noise-scale; there is no hidden broad module that failed an individual-gene threshold.

literature_claim: NFE2L1 is a related CNC-bZIP factor with a proteasome-bounce-back role, and NRF2 uses small-Maf proteins such as MafG to bind AREs.
main_caveats: Most comparator surfaces were weak, and several obvious pathway nodes, including Keap1, Cul3, Bach1, Maff, Mafk, and Nfe2l3, were not target perturbations.
summary: The measured NRF2-network perturbations, including Nfe2l1 and Mafg, did not phenocopy Nfe2l2.
why_it_matters: A CNC-bZIP paralog or small-Maf partner relationship did not translate into a shared postnatal neuronal LOF transcriptome; Nfe2l2 was flatter than weak Nfe2l1, Mafg, Sqstm1, and Hspa5 stress-axis responses.

why_it_matters: This establishes that Nfia does not maintain a broad P37 juvenile neuronal transcriptome in this sparse P16 CRISPR setting, and it prevents nominal single genes from being over-read as pathway biology.

literature_claim: NFIA, NFIB, and NFIX have overlapping neural developmental programs, and SOX9 physically cooperates with NFIA during gliogenic initiation.
main_caveats: Comparator interpretation uses DE-count and restricted-signature summaries; the assay does not sample the astrocytes or progenitors in which NFI overlap was originally described.
summary: The Nfia signature was isolated rather than part of a detectable neuronal NFI/Sox9 module: Nfib and Sox9 were also flat in Nfia-matched groups, while Nfic and Nfix produced only 3 and 1 adjusted genes, respectively, and raw-score cosines to Nfia were all <=0.01750.
why_it_matters: The failure of literature-obvious paralogs and the Sox9 partner to phenocopy within neurons argues that the whole gliogenic transcription-factor module is displaced out of the sampled postmitotic neuronal compartment, not just that one Nfia guide set was unusually weak.

literature_claim: NFIA loss or haploinsufficiency disrupts embryonic CNS morphogenesis and gliogenesis, whereas forced NFIA expression can drive astrocyte derivation in human stem-cell cultures.
main_caveats: The inference is temporal and lineage-based; the screen cannot rule out subtle neuronal physiology, axon guidance, or morphology phenotypes without a transcriptional correlate.
summary: The NFIA haploinsufficiency program is not reproduced by deleting Nfia after neurons are born: no adjusted DE was detected for Nfia genome-wide or for astroglial targets Apcdd1, Mmd2, Zcchc24, and Gfap.
why_it_matters: NFIA-related CNS malformation is therefore more consistent with a developmental progenitor/astroglial requirement than with an acute, broadly cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional crisis; postnatal neuronal rescue screens may miss the disease-relevant window.

main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; the result applies to mosaic P16 neuronal perturbation, not to embryonic germline or glial loss.

why_it_matters: NFIB is a developmental transcription factor, but in this acute sparse postmitotic setting no measured neuronal class mounted a robust secondary state change; this is an informative stage-context negative, not a failed-assay call from the weak self-transcript.

literature_claim: Embryonic NfiB-null cortex misregulates 1844 genes enriched for cell cycle, neuronal differentiation, axon guidance, Notch signaling and neuronal migration.
main_caveats: The tested literature gene list is a marker subset from embryonic bulk or tissue-level knockout, not a formal gene-set enrichment statistic in the P16 screen.
summary: The embryonic E15.5 NfiB-null cortical program—cell-cycle, Notch, axonogenesis and migration genes—was not recapitulated after P16 Nfib editing.
why_it_matters: Genes such as Hes1, Hes5, Dll1, Notch1, Notch3, Neurog2, Ntn1, Nrp1 and Reln should report a cortical developmental NFIB response if that program were re-entered; their complete FDR-level absence argues that the screen missed an earlier fate-and-axon construction window rather than an acute maintenance program in already specified neurons.

literature_claim: NFIA, NFIB and NFIX have overlapping developmental CNS expression and NFIA/NFIB can heterodimerize and act additively during cortical development.
main_caveats: Double or triple NFI perturbations were not measured; flat single perturbations are consistent with, but do not prove, combinatorial buffering.
summary: The three NFI paralogs represented in the screen, Nfia, Nfic and Nfix, also lacked any Nfib-like single-gene signature.
why_it_matters: Because NFI factors can dimerize and Nfia/Nfib dosage acts additively in embryonic cortex, the near-zero Nfib-Nfia/Nfic/Nfix correlations and the 0-3 FDR genes per paralog keep the single-NFI postnatal null from being misread as proof that NFI biology is absent from brain development.

summary: The NFIB haploinsufficiency disease axis is not phenocopied by a 3-4 week partial mosaic P16 neuronal perturbation.
why_it_matters: The result cautions that NFIB-associated intellectual disability and macrocephaly are more likely to depend on developmental dosage, progenitors, glia and tissue morphogenesis than on an acutely required NFIB-maintained transcriptome in young mature neurons.

literature_claim: NFI factors regulate neural progenitor differentiation and astrocytic marker gene expression in gliogenic contexts.
main_caveats: The absence of astrocyte markers is expected from NeuN+ enrichment and does not test Nfib loss in astrocytes or glial precursors.
summary: NFIB-linked astrocyte and gliogenic marker output is absent from the NeuN-enriched neuronal screen surface.
why_it_matters: All tested glial marker rows, including Gfap, Fabp7, Aqp4, Aldh1l1 and Sparcl1, stayed at FDR=1, matching the sampling design: astrocyte differentiation is a lineage program largely outside a neuronal-nuclei FACS readout.

literature_claim: BAMBI is a TGFβ/BMP-family pseudoreceptor, DBN1/Drebrin participates in postsynaptic actin spine biology, and SEPT5 is a neuronal presynaptic septin, but prior work did not predict this NFIC-regulated combination in Prkcd thalamic/midbrain glutamatergic neurons.
main_caveats: Only three downstream genes passed FDR<0.10 and two were near-threshold, so the module should be read as restricted, not broad.
summary: Acute Nfic loss produced a real but very small three-gene module only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Bambi and Septin5 increased while Dbn1 decreased.
why_it_matters: The only robust downstream signal in 23 neuronal groups is thalamic/midbrain and mixes a TGFβ/BMP pseudoreceptor with synaptic actin and septin genes, so the screen nominates a narrow postmitotic neuronal module rather than NFIC's known tooth-root program.

literature_claim: In odontoblasts, Nfic deficiency elevates TGFβ1/TGFβRI and Smad2/3 phosphorylation, and NFI-C can antagonize phospho-Smad2/3.
main_caveats: SMAD phosphorylation is not assayed by snRNA-seq; the inference is restricted to mRNA-level pathway recovery.
summary: The Bambi increase is uncoupled from a canonical TGFβ/BMP receptor-SMAD loss-of-function signature.
why_it_matters: NFIC is tied in odontoblasts to TGFβ1/Smad2/3 feedback, but in this postnatal neuronal assay Bambi was a singleton pathway gene: Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4, Smad7, Smurf1, Smurf2, and Nedd4l were not robust Nfic targets, and receptor/SMAD perturbations failed to reproduce the Bambi-Septin5-Dbn1 module.

literature_claim: UBA5 acts in the UFM1 cascade and THOC1 in THO/TREX mRNA export; neither is a known NFI-family component.
main_caveats: The neighbor call used only the three Nfic FDR genes because the genome-wide Nfic vector had no high-cosine neighbors; Uba5 and Thoc1 have much broader signatures, so convergence could be indirect.
summary: The top data-driven restricted-signature neighbor was Uba5, whereas Thoc1 was the strongest restricted anti-neighbor.
why_it_matters: Nfic's three-gene 151 signature was not aligned with an NFI paralog; it sat inside Uba5's broad UFMylation/ER-stress response and was inverted most strongly by an mRNA-export perturbation, nominating a stress/RNA-processing axis as an exploratory comparator for this tiny NFIC module.

literature_claim: NFI factors share a family architecture and NFIA/NFIB/NFIX have overlapping neurodevelopmental roles, with some NFI-C activity described in astrocyte differentiation in vitro.
main_caveats: The assay compares acute single-gene CRISPR mosaics, not embryonic combined knockouts; Nfia and Nfib were not recovered in 215 MB Dopa.
summary: Nfia, Nfib, and Nfix did not phenocopy Nfic in the responding 151 group or elsewhere in the matched screen surface.
why_it_matters: Despite shared NFI-family DNA-binding biology and known dosage interactions among Nfia/Nfib during cortical development, single postmitotic perturbation of the represented paralogs was essentially silent and did not drive Bambi, Septin5, or Dbn1, arguing that the Nfic 151 module is paralog-selective in this assay.

main_caveats: Indel formation was not measured; the result is an mRNA/downstream decoupling, not direct proof of inactive NFIC protein in every edited nucleus.
summary: 155 MB Glut showed significant Nfic mRNA depletion without any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: The MB Glut self-only response demonstrates that target-transcript drop and downstream NFIC biology are separable: self depletion can be transcriptionally buffered, while 151 had the opposite pattern—downstream genes despite nonsignificant Nfic FDR.

literature_claim: NFIX loss perturbs neural stem/progenitor differentiation in forebrain and hippocampus, SVZ neuroblast behavior, astrocyte maturation, and postnatal cerebellar programs.
main_caveats: This is a post-P16 sparse CRISPR snRNA-seq assay enriched for NeuN+ surviving neurons; it does not test embryonic progenitors, astrocytes, abundance phenotypes, or DNA editing efficiency.
summary: P16 mosaic Nfix loss of function produced a nearly pan-null transcriptional surface in P37-P44 NeuN+ neurons: only 1 of 388,023 downstream tests passed FDR<0.10, and no canonical astroglial, neural-progenitor, intermediate-progenitor or neuroblast marker did.
why_it_matters: The result sharply separates NFIX developmental/stem-cell biology from acute maintenance of most young postmitotic neuronal transcriptomes in this assay; the absence of GFAP/NSC/IPC marker regulation is informative because those marker transcripts were measured but remained FDR=1.000.

literature_claim: CWC27 functions as a spliceosome-associated splicing factor in vivo, but no NFIX-CWC27 regulatory relationship has been established.
main_caveats: Single cell group, 75 perturbed cells, singleton transcript, FDR just below 0.10, and Nfix mRNA itself was not decreased in this group.
summary: The only adjusted Nfix downstream hit was lower Cwc27 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA nuclei.
why_it_matters: CWC27 is a spliceosome-associated factor, so RNA processing is the only annotated axis that survives FDR for Nfix; however the effect is a singleton at FDR 0.097 and should be treated as hypothesis-generating, not as evidence for a coordinated splicing program.

literature_claim: NFIA, NFIB and NFIX are related NFI-family transcription factors with shared regulatory targets reported in postnatal cerebellar development, and the NFI family shares conserved DNA-binding/dimerization architecture.
main_caveats: The comparison is based on very small adjusted signatures, so it rejects a strong shared transcriptional module but not subtle NFI paralog compensation.
summary: The represented NFI paralogs did not phenocopy Nfix: Nfia and Nfib were completely flat, while Nfic produced a separate three-gene 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature and did not regulate Cwc27 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: Although NFI proteins can be structurally related and have shared developmental targets, acute loss of one paralog in mature neuronal nuclei did not unmask an interchangeable NFI-family module.

literature_claim: NSD1, SETD2 and FBN1 are genes in the differential diagnosis of NFIX-related Malan syndrome or phenotypic overgrowth/Marfanoid syndromes.
main_caveats: These are clinical differentials rather than a single biochemical pathway; Setd2 was measured in only 15 of 23 cell groups.
summary: Malan/Sotos-overgrowth differential genes represented in the screen did not converge with Nfix: Nsd1, Setd2 and Fbn1 had near-zero all-score cosines to Nfix and no Cwc27 overlap.
why_it_matters: Overgrowth/intellectual-disability genes can be clinically grouped, but acute perturbation in P37-P44 NeuN+ neurons did not reveal a common Malan/Sotos-like transcriptional end state.

main_caveats: Cosine similarity was computed on Wilcoxon z-score surfaces and, because Nfix is almost null, is dominated by weak background rather than a large coherent effect.
summary: The data-driven whole-surface neighbors of Nfix were numerically negligible and failed direct overlap tests.
why_it_matters: The closest positive and negative neighbors were not hidden pathway relatives; they had absolute cosine ≤0.028 and did not reproduce the 054 Cwc27 event, so the Nfix surface should not be forced into an apparent convergent module.

summary: The unbiased Nkx6-2 signature search produced only tiny whole-transcriptome cosines, with safe targets among the closest positive neighbors and no shared FDR<0.10 downstream genes for the top non-safe neighbors.
why_it_matters: It prevents assigning a pathway to a random low-amplitude signature: Nkx6-2 has no meaningful convergent or anti-convergent module in this universe.

why_it_matters: The absence of an Nkx6-2 response is part of a broader context mismatch for developmental and glial transcription-factor biology in postmitotic NeuN+ nuclei, rather than an isolated Nkx6-2 anomaly.

literature_claim: Nlgn3 is a brain-expressed postsynaptic cell-adhesion molecule whose established functions are mainly circuit- and synapse-specific rather than large cell-body transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: DNA indels and NLGN3 protein were not measured; this is a transcriptomic null in NeuN+ nuclei, not an electrophysiology or synapse-number assay.
summary: Nlgn3 loss produced a pan-surface downstream transcriptomic null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result rules out a broad cell-autonomous stress, UPR/ISR, proteostasis, autophagy, redox, translation, or synaptic mRNA-remodeling state 3-4 weeks after sparse P16 Nlgn3 CRISPR in these neuronal nuclei, even though self-transcript depletion was measurable in several groups.

literature_claim: Nlgn3 physically and functionally participates in neurexin-based trans-synaptic adhesion and in input-specific alphaNrxn1+AS4 signaling at hippocampal VGT3+/CCK inhibitory synapses.
main_caveats: The screen lacks Nlgn1/Nlgn2/Nlgn4 targets and does not resolve neurexin splice isoforms or CCK/VGT3 connectivity; the contrast is restricted to measured gene targets.
summary: Literature-obvious Nlgn3 neighbors did not phenocopy Nlgn3, and most were themselves transcriptionally sparse.
why_it_matters: The expected neurexin-neuroligin/synaptic-scaffold neighborhood was directly queried rather than assumed: Nrxn1, Nrxn2, Nrxn3, Dag1, Lrrtm1, Adam10, Dlg4, Shank2, Shank3, and Cntnap2 all had near-zero score correlations to Nlgn3 and 0-2 downstream FDR<0.10 genes each.

literature_claim: No prior literature comparator was required for the unbiased neighbor search.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on whole Wilcoxon-score vectors; when the seed signature is a biological null, nearest neighbors quantify absence of convergence more than mechanism.
summary: The unbiased Nlgn3 signature-neighbor search found no real convergent or inverse module.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive neighbors had Wilcoxon-score correlations only 0.026-0.027, and the strongest non-safe-target inverse neighbors were only -0.014 to -0.018; candidate positives Kmt2c, Atcay, Dpm1, and Vps13c were rejected because they were also null or one-to-two-gene responders.

summary: Nlgn3 was uncoupled from transcriptional programs elicited by NMDA-receptor and mTOR-pathway perturbations in the same screen universe.
why_it_matters: Grin1, Grin2b, and Tsc2 generated 131, 78, and 636 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, respectively, but Nlgn3 generated none; the assay can detect neuronal receptor or growth-signaling responses when present, so the Nlgn3 null is not a universal failure of synaptic or ASD-relevant perturbations to produce snRNA-seq DE.

why_it_matters: The CRISPR perturbation removes Nlgn3 function in otherwise normal postmitotic neurons; the best-characterized ASD allele is R451C with gain-of-function or mutation-specific synaptic behavior, and the high-grade-glioma mechanism acts through ADAM10-dependent NLGN3 shedding onto tumor cells that are absent from this NeuN+ dataset.

literature_claim: ATP2A2/SERCA2 is an endoplasmic-reticulum calcium pump with documented neuronal calcium-homeostasis roles.
main_caveats: The signature is a single gene at FDR 0.072 with 58 perturbed nuclei; no calcium-stress module accompanied it.

why_it_matters: The brain readout is nearly flat; the only reproducible coordinate touches SERCA2-mediated ER calcium handling rather than the canonical NOBOX oocyte program.

literature_claim: Nobox is preferentially expressed in primordial and growing oocytes, required for early folliculogenesis, and directly or genetically controls oocyte genes including Gdf9, Pou5f1, and Padi6.
main_caveats: The experiment did not assay oocytes; Pou5f1 and H1foo were absent from the Nobox DE rows, so only the represented canonical genes could be tested.
summary: Postnatal neuronal Nobox loss did not engage the oocyte and early-folliculogenesis regulon.
why_it_matters: The expected NOBOX output is transcriptional, so its absence in this snRNA-seq assay is informative: these P16 NeuN+ neurons do not execute the oocyte-specific Gdf9/Padi6/zona-pellucida program that explains the ovarian knockout phenotype.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation necessarily used Nobox rows below FDR<0.10 because the robust Nobox signature contained only Atp2a2.

why_it_matters: Because the nearest positive and negative cosine neighbors were supported only by a nominal 27-gene shoulder and had no FDR-level overlap, the Nobox L5-ET phenotype should be treated as an isolated singleton rather than as a member of a recurring cross-perturbation signature.

literature_claim: SERCA2/ATP2A2 controls neuronal ER calcium handling, and loss of this calcium pump is expected to have consequences beyond a single isolated transcript change when the perturbation is functionally strong.
main_caveats: This is a cross-perturbation inference from matched DE tables, not a calcium-imaging measurement.
summary: The Atp2a2 singleton under Nobox is uncoupled from the stress response seen after direct Atp2a2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: It prevents over-reading the Nobox hit as a functional Atp2a2 knockout: direct Atp2a2 perturbation can elicit a Ddit3/Chac1/Xbp1/Hspa5 UPR-ISR state in other neurons, whereas Nobox L5-ET nuclei changed Atp2a2 alone and left that secondary program non-significant.

literature_claim: NOD2 senses muramyl dipeptide in innate immune and glial cells and has a narrower MDP-sensing role in a subset of hypothalamic inhibitory neurons.

why_it_matters: This establishes Nod2 as a basal postmitotic neuronal non-responder in this experiment, while separating that fact from unmeasured DNA editing and from NOD2 biology in glia, immune cells, gut barrier tissue, and ligand-challenged states.

literature_claim: Ligand-activated NOD2 can signal via NF-kB/MAPK and can recruit ATG16L1 for antibacterial autophagy in bacterial response contexts.
main_caveats: The panel tests transcriptional recovery of the pathways, not NOD2-dependent recruitment events or kinase activity.
summary: Nod2 perturbation did not induce or repress the expected MDP/NF-kB, cytokine, interferon, inflammasome, or autophagy panel in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: The absence of Il1b/Il6/Tnf/Ccl/Cxcl/Nfkbia/Tnfaip3 and autophagy-gene responses argues against a hidden inflammatory or xenophagy stress response that the snRNA-seq assay could have captured if broadly induced in neurons.

literature_claim: NOD2, ATG16L1, XIAP/RIPK2, TLR, NF-kB, MAPK, and core autophagy components participate in bacterial sensing or autophagy pathways in immune and infection models.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on only 18 subthreshold Nod2 coordinates because Nod2 had no FDR<0.10 genes.
summary: The apparent top data-driven Nod2 neighbors were rejected as subthreshold restricted-signature artifacts rather than biological convergence or divergence partners.
