why_it_matters: The direction and gene content make the positive result look like loss of chromatin restriction on an inappropriate state, which partly matches prior Nsd1 projection-neuron results but appears in a new thalamic postnatal context.

literature_claim: ZMYND8 can recognize H3.1K36me2/H4K16ac chromatin marks, but thalamic convergence with Nsd1 had not been an obvious prior expectation.
main_caveats: The Zmynd8/Kdm5c link is based on a restricted 26-coordinate signature and must not be read as physical interaction.
summary: Zmynd8 and Kdm5c were the main same-direction FDR-overlap neighbors of Nsd1, with Zmynd8 sharing 11 and Kdm5c sharing 5 Nsd1 significant coordinates.
why_it_matters: The shared module nominates a chromatin-reader / H3K4-demethylase neighborhood rather than the NSD paralog as the closest measured transcriptomic context for Nsd1 loss.

main_caveats: Cross-perturbation opposition is measured at RNA level only and Sin3a has many more 151 DE genes than Nsd1.
summary: Sin3a opposed the Nsd1 thalamic module more than any other FDR-overlap comparator, reversing 8 Nsd1 151 signature genes while sharing only 2 in the same direction.
why_it_matters: The contrast turns a broad Sin3a chromatin response into a directional signpost: Myo5c, Kcnk4, Rasgrp2, Nrsn2, and extracellular-state genes move opposite to Nsd1.

main_caveats: Myo5c is a single gene in the 005 group and a reporter candidate, not a mechanistic proof.
summary: Myo5c was the only repeated Nsd1 downstream gene, rising both in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and Zmynd8 reproduced both same-direction Myo5c events.
why_it_matters: Myo5c is a compact reporter candidate for the shared Nsd1/Zmynd8 ectopic module that can be tested by targeted in situ methods.

literature_claim: NSD2, SETD2, and ASH1L are established H3K36 methyltransferases and NSD1-dependent H3K36me2 is linked to DNMT3A-dependent neuronal non-CG methylation.
main_caveats: Setd2 was recovered in only 15 of 20 Nsd1-matched groups and had low perturbed-cell counts.
summary: H3K36-pathway relatives Nsd2, Ash1l, Setd2, and the NSD1-linked methylation effector Dnmt3a did not converge with the Nsd1 signature in matched cell groups.
why_it_matters: The expected same-pathway comparators were directly tested and rejected, arguing that the Nsd1 phenotype is not a generic K36MT or DNA-methyltransferase perturbation surface in this P16 assay.

main_caveats: Only one gene passed FDR<0.10 and it did so at FDR 0.053.

why_it_matters: This preserves a real measured inhibitory-neuron hit while keeping it at the proper single-gene, hypothesis-generating scale.

why_it_matters: The lack of canonical stress sentinels keeps the ectopic thalamic signature from being misread as generic sick-cell or proteostasis compensation.

why_it_matters: Same-pathway nonconvergence argues that postmitotic H3K36 maintenance is not a simple interchangeable NSD-family output in this assay.

main_caveats: Cosines were computed on a near-null signature and are a quality-control contrast, not a mechanistic similarity claim.

why_it_matters: Nominal genes around a zero target do not form a recurring perturbation module, lowering the risk that a real pathway was hidden below FDR.

literature_claim: NSD2-driven H3K36me2 rewires transcription in cancer, and NSD-family inhibitors are being pursued as cancer therapeutics.
main_caveats: CRISPR LOF is not a catalytic inhibitor, and the screen did not sample tumors, immune cells, glia, or developmental progenitors.

why_it_matters: The zero argues that this exact neuronal context is buffered, while also warning that tumor, immune, progenitor, and pharmacological inhibitor responses remain off-axis.

literature_claim: XPO1/CRM1 is a broadly acting export receptor for protein and RNA cargoes, but it is not an established direct NSF-SNARE effector.
main_caveats: Single FDR<0.10 gene, no recurrence across the other 22 cell groups, and no direct mechanistic bridge to NSF in this dataset.
summary: The only robust Nsf downstream hit was Xpo1 down-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
why_it_matters: Instead of a pan-neuronal SNARE-recycling transcriptome, the screen exposes a single nuclear-export transcript as a possible local marker of chronic NSF stress in superficial cortical/entorhinal glutamatergic neurons.

literature_claim: Complete or dominant-negative NSF dysfunction is expected to disrupt SNARE recycling, neurotransmission, AMPAR trafficking, and in DEE variant models autophagy/mTOR signaling.
main_caveats: This is a negative single-nucleus mRNA result; surface receptors, vesicle pools, electrophysiology, DNA indels, and edited-cell depletion were not assayed.
summary: Postnatal Nsf loss did not elicit the transcriptional programs expected from a strong chronic SNARE/vesicle-trafficking failure.
why_it_matters: Gria1/2/3, SNARE-cycle, ISR/UPR, autophagy, apoptosis, and mTOR-axis transcripts remained FDR-flat even though the target mRNA was measured in every cell group, separating acute synaptic trafficking biology from a detectable cell-state program in surviving nuclei.

literature_claim: NSF is a membrane-fusion ATPase in SNAP/SNARE recycling, so direct SNAP/SNARE genes were the obvious comparators.
main_caveats: Cosines were small and the strict FDR overlap with the lone Nsf Xpo1 hit was absent; the result is a weak full-signature relationship only.
summary: The nearest Nsf signature neighbors were weak proteostasis and vesicle-trafficking stresses rather than direct SNARE-complex members.
why_it_matters: All-feature scoring ranked Psmb4, Cltc, Psmc1, Atp6v1a, Atp6v1e1, and Atp2a2 as the six most positive neighbors of Nsf, whereas the best negative neighbors were essentially zero; this places Nsf in a faint endomembrane/proteostatic tail, not in a transcriptomic module shared with Napb or Stx1b.

literature_claim: Munc18/STXBP1, Munc13, complexin, SNAREs, SNAPs, NSF, and AMPAR trafficking interfaces participate in synaptic vesicle or postsynaptic receptor trafficking pathways, and STXBP1 is a DEE disease gene.
main_caveats: Several canonical partners such as Napa, Snap25, Vamp2, and Syt1 were not perturbation targets, and many represented partners had sparse cell recovery.
summary: Nsf did not phenocopy STXBP1, AMPAR-subunit targets, or most assayed SNARE-cycle perturbations.
why_it_matters: The matched screen separates NSF from Munc18/STXBP1: Stxbp1 produced 140 FDR<0.10 genes across 8 groups, including large signatures in 005, 052, and 155 where Nsf had zero, whereas Napb, Stx1b, Dnm1, Synj1, Cplx2, Unc13c, and Gria1/2/3 were themselves flat or singleton perturbations.

literature_claim: DEE-associated heterozygous NSF variants impair vesicular-membrane recycling through a dominant-negative mechanism and can cause defective autophagy with mTOR overactivation.
main_caveats: The screen did not introduce patient missense alleles, did not measure phospho-S6/LC3 flux, and could miss rare dying cells.
summary: NSF-related DEE variant biology, including mTOR/autophagy activation, is not reproduced by sparse postnatal Nsf loss-of-function.
why_it_matters: Human NSF DEE alleles have been argued to act dominantly, and a later cell model connected those variants to mTOR overactivation and defective autophagy; the absence of Atf4/Ddit3/Hspa5/Xbp1/Sqstm1/Map1lc3b/Mtor/Tsc1/Tsc2 responses after CRISPR LoF warns that variant-bearing NSF hexamers may need to be modeled directly rather than inferred from simple allele loss.

literature_claim: NSMCE2/MMS21 is an SMC5/6 SUMO ligase whose loss impairs DNA repair and sensitizes cultured human cells to DNA-damage-induced apoptosis.
main_caveats: Indel formation and protein loss were not measured; absence is confined to NeuN-enriched P16-to-P37/44 neurons.
summary: Nsmce2 loss did not produce a BH-significant downstream transcriptional response in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: The complete 20-group surface is the biological result: an acute P16 CRISPR loss of a genome-maintenance SUMO ligase is buffered at the snRNA-seq level in juvenile postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Strong NSMCE2 loss in proliferating or DNA-damaged cells is expected to perturb replication-fork repair and ATM/ATR/CHK signaling, producing stress and apoptosis when damage is unresolved.
main_caveats: FDR absence of secondary markers cannot test primary molecular lesions such as unresolved fork structures, recombination intermediates, or SUMOylated repair proteins.

literature_claim: OCRL acts with clathrin/AP-2, APPL1, Rab proteins, and PI(4,5)P2 5-phosphatase logic that overlaps partly with synaptojanin-family endocytic uncoating.
main_caveats: Inpp5b and Clcn5, the most direct mouse paralog and Dent-disease comparator, were not represented as perturbation targets.

why_it_matters: Directly measured relatives or pathway neighbors—Inpp5k, Synj1, Appl1, Dnm1, Clcn3, and Clcn4—were also FDR-flat in the Ocrl-matched neuronal groups, making the Ocrl zero part of a broader transcriptionally buffered endocytic/phosphoinositide module rather than a failure unique to one guide set.

literature_claim: OGDH is the E1 component of the 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase step of the TCA cycle, and strong OGDH dysfunction is expected to perturb mitochondrial energy/redox metabolism and cause severe neurological disease.
main_caveats: Functional indels were not measured; this is a single-nucleus RNA phenotype in recovered neurons 3-4 weeks after a sparse postmitotic perturbation.
summary: Ogdh knockdown produced an almost completely buffered neuronal nuclear transcriptome: only two downstream genes passed FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups despite a negative Ogdh self-transcript in every measured group.
why_it_matters: A TCA E1 enzyme can show directional target depletion in this P16 mosaic CRISPR setting without a matching pan-neuronal mitochondrial-stress RNA state; the weak surface should therefore be read as buffering or survival of metabolically compensated cells, not as proof that Ogdh is dispensable.

literature_claim: α-Ketoglutarate dehydrogenase is both sensitive to ROS and capable of generating ROS, and mitochondrial peroxiredoxins buffer peroxide stress.
main_caveats: Prdx5 was a singleton; companion NRF2, ISR, OXPHOS, and autophagy markers were not FDR-significant.
summary: The strongest positive Ogdh downstream hit was Prdx5 induction in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: Prdx5 is a peroxide-detoxifying mitochondrial/peroxisomal antioxidant, so its selective induction is the one robust cell-autonomous redox compensation that matches α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase ROS biology.

literature_claim: BORC regulates lysosome positioning and, with ARL8 and kinesin adaptors, lysosome movement into axons; no prior OGDH-specific Borcs7 induction was identified.
main_caveats: Borcs7 passed FDR<0.10 but not FDR<0.05; other BORC or autophagy/lysosome genes were not a robust module.
summary: Ogdh perturbation up-regulated Borcs7 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, pointing to a restricted lysosome-positioning or axonal cargo response rather than a generic mitochondrial program.
why_it_matters: BORCS7 is part of BORC, a lysosome and axonal vesicle transport complex; its isolated induction nominates endolysosomal transport as a secondary reporter to test after OGDH stress in medial/lateral habenula-thalamic glutamatergic neurons.

literature_claim: OGDH, DLST, and DLD catalyze sequential reactions within one 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex, and related 2-oxoacid dehydrogenases share cofactors and redox chemistry.
main_caveats: Most comparators were themselves weakly engaged by single-nucleus RNA; lack of phenocopy is stronger than any one comparator signature.
summary: Same-complex and neighboring mitochondrial enzyme perturbations did not phenocopy the Ogdh Prdx5/Borcs7 signature.
why_it_matters: The result uncouples OGDH E1 loss from a generic α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, pyruvate dehydrogenase, or TCA-cycle nuclear RNA response in this assay: Dlst, Dld, Dlat, Pdha1, Sdha, Aco2, Mdh1, Mdh2, Idh3a, and Sucla2 were null, singleton, or in Mdh1 a different TH-specific responder.

main_caveats: The marker test was targeted and transcriptomic; metabolite flux, ROS, and protein-state changes were not measured.

why_it_matters: The absence of ATF4/DDIT3/ASNS/TRIB3, ER-UPR, OXPHOS, and broad lysosomal induction makes the two positive genes narrow reporters, not the visible tip of an unresolved global mitochondrial stress response.

literature_claim: OGFRL1 is an OGFr-like, poorly annotated gene whose published phenotypes center on human craniofacial inflammatory bone disease and bone-marrow/monocyte-driven fibrotic liver regeneration rather than on autonomous mature neuronal transcription.
main_caveats: The screen does not measure jaw, bone marrow, liver, microglia, vascular or glial lineages, and DNA indel formation was not directly measured; flat self-transcript FDR is therefore not a failed-editing call.
summary: Ogfrl1 loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any of the 22 measured postmitotic neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a broad cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional requirement for Ogfrl1 three to four weeks after P16 loss, while leaving its reported myeloid, jawbone and liver-regeneration biology outside this NeuN+ brain assay.

literature_claim: The unfolded-protein response is a transcriptional ER-proteostasis program; Hspa5 perturbation exposes that the assay can recover an ER-chaperone-rich program when it is present.
main_caveats: The comparator ranking is computed from a null Ogfrl1 signature; numerical neighbors are therefore used only as rejected controls, not as mechanistic relatives.
summary: A row-centered whole-universe neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Ogfrl1 signature neighbor; even the numerical top residual correlations were only +0.0165 and -0.0172.
why_it_matters: This rejects a hidden shared module: top numerical neighbors either had no robust DE themselves or produced real Hspa5/Polr3b/Ddx39b thalamic-midbrain signatures that were absent from Ogfrl1.

literature_claim: OGT is the single mammalian O-GlcNAc writer and is essential in development and in mature neurons.
main_caveats: Sparse editing and survivor bias can hide the most severe null alleles; the very small 1- to 3-gene signatures should be interpreted as formal effects, not as rich pathway evidence.
summary: Ogt loss produced a real but highly uneven postnatal neuronal transcriptomic response: 18 of 21 measured groups had FDR<0.10 downstream genes, with the bulk of the 2,154 downstream calls concentrated in MB Glut, MB P MY GABA, CNU-HYa HY GABA, Pvalb, L4-5 IT and CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: This separates initiation of O-GlcNAc deficiency from the cells that mount a detectable nuclear response 3-4 weeks after P16 editing; Ogt was not simply a pan-neuronal stress knockout in this sparse juvenile assay.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: O-GlcNAc levels feed back onto OGT and OGA mRNA maturation/abundance, and OGA inhibition is a druggable way to increase O-GlcNAc.
main_caveats: Oga itself was not a perturbation target in the parquet, so only its behavior as an Ogt-responsive transcript could be tested.
summary: Ogt perturbation repeatedly decreased the opposing eraser Oga, most strongly in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and across six additional responders.
why_it_matters: The sign is the one expected for a feedback circuit that tries to preserve O-GlcNAc when writer activity falls; it also puts the endogenous response in the same direction as pharmacologic OGA inhibition, not OGT inhibition.

literature_claim: O-GlcNAc is abundant in chromatin/nuclear pores and loss of O-GlcNAc can perturb the nuclear pore.
main_caveats: Most named RNA-processing genes are effect markers, not proven direct OGT substrates in these neurons.
summary: The most recurrent Ogt module was nuclear RNA processing plus nucleocytoplasmic transport: Rsrp1/Snhg11/Srrm2/Rbm14/Srsf5/Snrnp70 and related splicing genes went down while Xpo1 went up, and the nearest positive perturbation neighbors included Tnpo3, Ranbp2, Tpr, U2af2 and Prpf6.
why_it_matters: The data-driven neighbors are nuclear-transport and spliceosome perturbations rather than the textbook OGA enzyme; this argues that postnatal neuronal OGT loss is read out through an RNA/nuclear logistics state.

literature_claim: The 26S proteasome and OGT are functionally linked, and OGT can control cell viability through a proteasome/mTOR/mitochondrial axis.
main_caveats: The snRNA-seq data show adaptive transcripts, not proteasome flux or O-GlcNAc occupancy.
summary: Psmc1 and Psmb4 perturbations were the strongest FDR-overlap neighbors of Ogt, and Ogt responders carried a smaller direct proteostasis module with Lamp1, Sec62, Gnptg, Psma3, Syvn1 and Stub1.
why_it_matters: This ties the Ogt signature to the proteasome rather than to a generic damage response and is consistent with OGT viability biology passing through proteasome/mTOR/mitochondrial coupling.

literature_claim: OGT regulates mature excitatory synapses and AMPA-receptor GluA2/GluA3 synaptic abundance in neurons.
main_caveats: Accessory-gene transcript loss is an indirect proxy for synaptic physiology; the experiment did not assay synaptic protein localization.
summary: Ogt loss down-regulated synaptic and excitability genes including Iglon5, Kcnab3, Cacng7, Adam22, Prrt1, Ache and Slc6a1, yet did not measurably alter Gria1-4 mRNAs.
why_it_matters: The result refines a known OGT synapse phenotype: this assay recovered a transcriptional synaptic-maintenance response in selected interneuron, hypothalamic and midbrain groups, but not the previously described AMPA-receptor subunit effect, which is likely post-transcriptional or compartmental.

literature_claim: O-GlcNAc acts as a nutrient-sensing modifier, and CYP46A1 is the major enzyme for cholesterol turnover/removal in brain.
main_caveats: Brain cholesterol metabolites were not measured; the claim is based on transcripts.
summary: Cyp46a1, Tecr, Far1 and Srebf2 formed a recurrent down-regulated lipid/cholesterol module, with Lypla2 up-regulation in the same broad responders.
why_it_matters: Cyp46a1 down-regulation is a compact candidate marker for Ogt-sensitive neuronal cholesterol-turnover stress in Pvalb, hypothalamic and midbrain neurons.

literature_claim: O-GlcNAc is present on mitochondrial proteins and OGT-dependent viability can involve mitochondrial dysfunction downstream of proteasome/mTOR imbalance.
main_caveats: Mitochondrial activity and cell death were not measured directly.
summary: The large Ogt signatures selectively depressed mitochondrial and organic-acid metabolism genes, including Mdh1, Pcca, Acadvl, Cox7b, Samm50 and Slc25a carriers.
why_it_matters: This aligns the proteasome neighbor result with a bioenergetic collapse arm and indicates that the MB/HYa/Pvalb Ogt response is not purely nuclear.

literature_claim: UDP-GlcNAc synthesized by the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway supplies OGT, and OGT can associate with mSin3A/HDAC chromatin complexes.
main_caveats: Gfpt1 self-transcript was not detectably reduced; Hcfc1, Tet1-3 and Oga were not available as perturbation targets.
summary: The upstream HBP enzyme Gfpt1 and the OGT-associated chromatin regulator Sin3a failed to phenocopy Ogt strongly in matched cell groups.
why_it_matters: This rejects a simple linear model in which any HBP or OGT-chromatin perturbation reproduces Ogt loss: the only writer produced a proteostasis/RNA signature, whereas Gfpt1 and Sin3a had weak or displaced overlap.

main_caveats: Anti-neighbor scoring was restricted to Ogt-significant gene×cell pairs and does not test all possible phenotypes.
summary: No perturbation in the model-visible universe was a high-overlap inverse Ogt phenocopy; Huwe1 was only a shallow anti-neighbor.
why_it_matters: The absence of a strong opposite signature makes the Psmc1/Psmb4/Tnpo3/Tpr convergence more load-bearing and prevents overinterpreting Huwe1 or Mib1 as functional antagonists.

literature_claim: Embryonic Ogt loss perturbs Wnt/Notch-linked neurogenesis, and OGT can regulate AMPA-receptor abundance or ER stress in other systems.
main_caveats: Absence is transcriptomic only; Wnt, AMPAR or UPR proteins were not assayed.
summary: Expected embryonic Wnt/Notch targets, Gria1-4 AMPA-receptor mRNAs, and a broad Atf4/Hspa5/Xbp1 UPR were absent from the Ogt FDR<0.10 surface.
why_it_matters: The screen should have detected these if they had become dominant nuclear programs in P16-edited neurons; their absence localizes the recovered response away from progenitor specification and away from a pan-UPR.

literature_claim: OPA1 is broadly required for mitochondrial fusion and retinal-ganglion-cell survival but OPA1 disease is strikingly vulnerable-cell selective.
main_caveats: Retina, optic nerve glia, non-neuronal brain cells, olfactory bulb, and hindbrain were outside or depleted from the assay; the finding is a transcriptomic threshold at one juvenile time point, not proof that silent cells have normal mitochondrial morphology.
summary: Opa1 loss generated a FDR-resolved response in 10 of 22 measured neuronal groups and was silent in a large forebrain/cerebellar surface under the P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic CRISPR window.
why_it_matters: OPA1 is a ubiquitous inner-mitochondrial fusion factor, but the response was not ubiquitous; the dataset nominates a thresholded, cell-class-selective mitochondrial stress program rather than a uniform loss-of-function phenotype.

literature_claim: Mitochondrial dysfunction in mammals activates eIF2α/ATF4 through mitochondrial stress relays and induces ISR genes rather than requiring a C. elegans-like canonical mtUPR.
main_caveats: ATF4 protein and eIF2α phosphorylation were not measured; Atf4 mRNA itself did not pass FDR, which is compatible with translational ISR control but leaves the regulator inferred from target genes.
summary: The dominant Opa1-positive module is an ATF4/ISR-like amino-acid stress program.
why_it_matters: Asns, Slc7a5, Chac1, Ddit3, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and one-carbon genes are exactly the nuclear genes expected when mitochondrial stress is relayed to eIF2α/ATF4, connecting loss of inner-membrane fusion to a cytosolic stress-adaptation state in specific brain neurons.

literature_claim: ATF4-centered mitochondrial ISRs reprogram translation and metabolism, including amino-acid handling, under mitochondrial stress.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq measures transcript abundance only; amino-acid flux, charging, and one-carbon flux were not assayed directly.
summary: Opa1-responding neurons up-regulated amino-acid import, aminoacyl-tRNA charging, and serine/one-carbon metabolism as a compensation layer.
why_it_matters: The response is more than generic stress: Slc7a5/Slc7a1/Slc3a2/Slc1a4 transporters, Cars/Mars1/Aars/Eprs/Lars synthetases, and Shmt2/Mthfd2/Aldh1l2/Psph/Phgdh reroute nitrogen, one-carbon, and translational capacity, a metabolic attempt to survive impaired mitochondria.

literature_claim: OPA1 deficiency compromises mitochondrial morphology and respiratory capacity, and mitochondrial stress coordinates nuclear metabolic adaptation.
main_caveats: Mitochondrial RNA abundance in nuclei is an indirect respiratory readout and need not equal oxidative phosphorylation flux.
summary: The broadest midbrain and hypothalamic responses coupled nuclear ISR induction to loss of mitochondrial genome-encoded respiratory-chain transcripts.
why_it_matters: Down-regulation of mt-Co2, mt-Cytb, mt-Nd5, mt-Nd1, mt-Atp8 and related transcripts localizes Opa1 damage to oxidative-phosphorylation output and distinguishes the broad MB Glut/MB P MY GABA/HY GABA states from the sparse Asns-only surfaces.

literature_claim: Mitochondrial stress activates an ISR, but ATF4/ISR is a final common path for many cellular stresses.
main_caveats: Neighbors were found by a restricted Opa1-DE-feature cosine; Hspa8 was high by cosine but had no FDR-level Opa1-feature overlap, and Lonp1 had only five shared FDR overlaps.
summary: Opa1's closest FDR-confirmed neighbors were mostly non-canonical stress perturbations rather than OPA1-processing factors.
why_it_matters: Hnrnpu, Elp1, Gfpt1, Atp2a2 and Psmb4 re-used the same Asns/Chac1/Ddit3/Cars/Mars/Slc7a5 signature, showing that the Opa1 program is a convergent neuronal ISR state that multiple upstream insults can enter.

literature_claim: YME1L, OMA1, and m-AAA proteases regulate OPA1 cleavage, whereas MFF controls the mitochondrial fission side of the fusion-fission balance.
main_caveats: Oma1 itself was not a represented perturbation target, and Mff loss is expected to affect fission rather than to copy inner-membrane Opa1 loss.
summary: Direct OPA1-processing and mitochondrial fission comparators represented in the screen did not phenocopy Opa1 loss.
why_it_matters: Yme1l1, Afg3l2, Mff and Clpp were measurable but flat or off-module, so Opa1 removal is not interchangeable with perturbing OPA1 proteases, a fission receptor, or the CLPP protease in this postnatal neuronal snRNA readout.

literature_claim: No specific inverse Opa1 transcriptional comparator was an a priori expectation.
main_caveats: This is restricted to the target and cell groups recovered in the parquet and to a 245-feature Opa1 signature; it does not exclude non-transcriptional or unscreened antagonists.
summary: The Opa1 signature had no robust inverse transcriptional target among represented perturbations.
why_it_matters: The most negative restricted-cosine neighbors had essentially no FDR-confirmed opposite-direction overlap with Opa1 features, arguing that the screen does not contain a clean antagonist that turns off the Opa1 ISR module.

literature_claim: Human OPA1 disease is dominated by retinal ganglion-cell/optic-nerve degeneration, with some alleles causing multisystem mitochondrial disease.
main_caveats: The tissue excluded retina and was harvested after only 3 to 4 weeks, so absence of the disease-defining endpoint is expected and not therapeutic rescue.
summary: A postmitotic juvenile brain Opa1 knockout recapitulated stress and respiratory compensation, not the retinal-ganglion-cell loss that defines dominant optic atrophy.
why_it_matters: The screen separates an early, cell-autonomous mitochondrial stress transcriptome from later or lineage-specific optic-neuropathy biology; this matters when using brain CRISPR readouts to prioritize OPA1 modifiers.

literature_claim: Several mammalian mitochondrial insults induce ATF4/ISR without inducing the canonical HSP60/HSP10/CLPP mtUPR seen in invertebrate models.
main_caveats: Absence is transcript-level only and does not exclude altered mitophagic flux or mitochondrial protease activity at the protein level.
summary: Opa1 activated Lonp1 in a few groups but did not induce a canonical Hspd1/Hspe1/Clpp mitochondrial UPR or Pink1/Prkn mitophagy transcriptome.
why_it_matters: The FDR surface points to ATF4-linked amino-acid stress as the mammalian neuronal output of Opa1 loss, not to a wholesale chaperone/protease mtUPR or a transcriptional mitophagy program.

literature_claim: Delta, mu, kappa, and nociceptin opioid receptors are homologous GPCRs that couple to inhibitory Gi/o signaling and regulate neuronal firing or transmitter release.

literature_claim: Central endogenous opioids and selective DOR agonists can acutely increase Bdnf mRNA through opioid receptors.
main_caveats: The tested expectation is indirect because the literature perturbed receptors with agonists in rats, whereas the screen used receptor loss in unchallenged mouse nuclei.
summary: Oprd1 LOF did not produce the Bdnf or immediate-early transcriptional outputs that opioid agonist studies make worth checking.

literature_claim: No literature comparator was being tested; these were phenotype-first nearest neighbors across the parquet.
main_caveats: Cosine scores were computed from unthresholded Wilcoxon scores because Oprd1 had no FDR<0.10 DE genes, so the result is useful mainly as a rejection of strong convergence.
summary: A whole-universe signature-neighbor search rejected strong hidden convergence for the Oprd1 nominal vector.
why_it_matters: The top score-cosine neighbors among 1755 targets were only 0.027, 0.0268, and 0.0259, while the strongest negative values were safe controls or approximately -0.011 for real genes; this is a noise-scale similarity profile, not a pathway-level Oprd1 module.

literature_claim: DOR agonists are pursued for disorders such as chronic pain and mood disorders, and different DOR agonists can produce distinct signaling, trafficking, and behavioral consequences.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay receptor occupancy, peptide tone, acute kinase activity, calcium or potassium currents, synaptic release, behavior, or chronic agonist adaptation.
summary: The screen is a poor negative proxy for delta-opioid agonist pharmacology.
why_it_matters: DOR is druggable and biased agonists can drive ligand-specific signaling and longer-term adaptations, whereas this experiment removed Oprd1 sparsely and read out basal nuclear RNA without a pain, stress, peptide, or drug challenge; the null therefore should not be read as evidence that DOR agonists are transcriptionally or behaviorally inert.

literature_claim: KOR activation is ligand-gated, Gαi/o-coupled inhibition of adenylyl cyclase with GIRK/Ca2+ effects and agonist-dependent ERK, p38 and JNK signaling.
main_caveats: DNA indels and receptor function were not measured; the readout was basal snRNA-seq after P16 perturbation and cannot exclude acute phospho-signaling or electrophysiology.
summary: Sparse postnatal Oprk1 loss did not produce a robust downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups; even CREB/MAPK- and dynorphin-related candidate genes stayed at FDR=1 across the Oprk1 surface.
why_it_matters: This turns the apparently flat target into a mechanistic result: the canonical KOR output is not a tonic, cell-autonomous nuclear program in unstimulated P37-44 neurons.

literature_claim: MOR, KOR and DOR are the classical opioid receptors, while Oprl1 encodes the NOP opioid-like receptor; these are related opioid GPCRs with overlapping but distinct signaling contexts.
main_caveats: Null-null convergence does not establish that every paralog is silent in ligand-challenged or behaviorally engaged neurons.
summary: The opioid-receptor paralogs Oprm1, Oprd1 and Oprl1 also lacked FDR<0.10 downstream signatures, with near-zero Oprk1 score correlations, so Oprk1 belongs to a receptor-family-wide basal null rather than being an isolated failure.
why_it_matters: A same-family comparison prevents over-interpreting Oprk1 alone: multiple Gi/o opioid receptors are transcriptionally buffered in this sparse unstimulated neuronal assay.

main_caveats: The neighbor metric used all Wilcoxon-score dimensions because Oprk1 had no FDR<0.10 genes; it is useful only to reject, not nominate, neighbors.
summary: A whole-parquet Wilcoxon-score neighbor search found no meaningful Oprk1 signature neighbor: the strongest positive score correlation was Cit at r=0.0339 and the strongest negative was Fgfr2 at r=-0.0321.
why_it_matters: The absence of a data-driven neighbor is a quality-control result for interpretation: cross-target analyses cannot legitimately attach Oprk1 to another perturbation module by nominal rank noise.

literature_claim: KOR signals through Gαi/o inhibition of adenylyl cyclase, Gβγ regulation of GIRK/Ca2+ channels, and agonist-dependent MAPK kinases.
main_caveats: Most significant comparator rows were on the comparator transcript itself rather than broad downstream programs, so this is a restricted cross-perturbation contrast.
summary: Perturbing Oprk1 did not phenocopy measurable intracellular Gi/o-cAMP/PKA/MAPK targets: Gnao1, Adcy3, Prkaca and Mapk1 showed target-transcript FDR signals in selected groups, whereas Oprk1 remained flat and had |r|≤0.0175 to these pathway perturbations.
why_it_matters: The screen could register perturbations of some expressed signaling effectors; the receptor-level Oprk1 null is therefore more consistent with missing ligand/circuit state than with a universally invisible cAMP pathway.

summary: Literature-driven relatives did not reveal an Otx2-like response: Otx1 was absent as a target, Crx/En1/Lmx1b/Pax6/Pitx3 were themselves completely flat, and En2/Rax/Six3/Rarb produced only 1-3 total FDR<0.10 genes with near-zero correlations to Otx2.
why_it_matters: The result rejects an obvious Otx/retina/midbrain homeobox phenocopy in this P16 neuronal assay and turns the family comparison into evidence for a shared developmental-window or lineage mismatch.

summary: Otx2 had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor across the complete parquet: the strongest Pearson score-vector correlations were Erbb3 at 0.029 and Cspp1 at -0.012.
why_it_matters: The global cross-perturbation geometry confirms that the Otx2 vector is dominated by null noise rather than by a hidden recurrent transcriptional state shared with another screened target.

literature_claim: Oxtr encodes the oxytocin receptor, a neuronal GPCR required for multiple mouse social, maternal, aggression, and lactation phenotypes.
main_caveats: True indel engagement was not measured; three positives are single genes, and the screen did not challenge cells with oxytocin or a social/physiological stimulus.
summary: Oxtr loss after P16 produced a nearly flat steady-state neuronal transcriptome: only three downstream FDR<0.10 genes across all 23 measured cell groups and no BH-significant Oxtr self-transcript drop.
why_it_matters: The principal biological output captured here is buffering, not a failed perturbation: a sparse GPCR knockout did not create a cell-autonomous stress, immediate-early, or synaptic-state transcriptome in basal P37-44 neuronal nuclei.

literature_claim: Mouse OXTR is expressed in VTA dopamine/glutamate neurons and in glutamatergic prefrontal cortical neurons that influence social-recognition circuitry.
main_caveats: The significant genes are one per broad class; 215 MB Dopa has only 24 perturbed cells, and the taxonomy does not resolve VTA subtypes or projection targets.
summary: All Oxtr FDR-level positives localized to three broad subcortical classes—CNU-HYa/HY GABA, MB/P/MY GABA, and MB dopamine—while all cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic groups were null.
why_it_matters: The distribution fits a neuromodulatory receptor whose detectable chronic RNA consequences appear only in a few subcortical populations, with the MB Dopa hit landing in a class that contains VTA dopaminergic neurons previously shown to express OXTR.

literature_claim: ATP-citrate lyase links citrate metabolism to cytosolic acetyl-CoA pools used for lipid synthesis and histone acetylation.
main_caveats: The biology is supported by a single significant Oxtr gene; Dctn1 and Sin3a converge only on Acly, not on the full three-gene Oxtr signature.
summary: The 066 CNU-HYa/HY GABA response was Acly-only: Oxtr increased the acetyl-CoA enzyme Acly, and data-driven neighbors Dctn1 and Sin3a converged on the same Acly-up feature, but Oxtr did not induce the broader sterol/SREBP lipid module seen under Dctn1.
why_it_matters: This isolates a metabolic/acetyl-CoA sentinel rather than a full lipid-biogenesis state, preventing the Acly hit from being over-read as wholesale SREBP activation after Oxtr loss.

literature_claim: WDR83OS/Asterix is part of an ER chaperone for multipass membrane proteins, and ODR4-family proteins are GPCR-trafficking orthologs; OXTR itself is a seven-transmembrane GPCR.
main_caveats: No direct OXTR-Wdr83os or OXTR-Odr4 relationship was tested; each cell group had only one significant gene, and Odr4 in MB Dopa was measured in only 24 perturbed nuclei.
summary: Wdr83os and Odr4 were isolated, Oxtr-selective hits in 191 MB/P/MY GABA and 215 MB Dopa, respectively, suggesting but not proving a weak multipass-membrane/GPCR-biogenesis compensation arm.
why_it_matters: OXTR is a seven-transmembrane GPCR; the only two non-Acly hits point toward ER multipass-membrane insertion or GPCR trafficking, so they are plausible candidate sentinel genes for rare Oxtr-edited neurons even though they do not constitute a multi-gene module by themselves.

literature_claim: OXTR belongs to the oxytocin/vasopressin GPCR family, can cross-talk with AVP receptors, and canonically signals through G proteins to PLC/Ca2+, kinase, MAPK, and CREB pathways.
main_caveats: Some canonical components, including Oxt, Gnaq, and Gna11, were not represented as perturbation targets; the negative comparison is restricted to targets and cell groups present in the parquet.
summary: Oxtr did not phenocopy its receptor-family and downstream signaling relatives: Avpr1a, Avpr1b, Plcb1, Gnao1, Camk2a, Camk2b, Creb1, Mapk1, and Prkca failed to reproduce any Acly/Wdr83os/Odr4 hit in matched responder groups.
why_it_matters: The measurable cross-perturbation contrast shows that Oxtr's tiny residual RNA signature is not a generic Gq/PLC, CaMK, CREB, MAPK, or vasopressin-receptor program; even close GPCR-family priors are the wrong comparator for this basal CRISPR readout.

literature_claim: Ligand-bound OXTR can couple to calcium- and kinase-dependent pathways that converge on MAPK/CREB and neuronal activity-dependent transcription.
main_caveats: This does not test acute oxytocin stimulation; nuclei were collected weeks after editing under basal conditions.
summary: An oxytocin-linked activity/immediate-early transcriptional program was absent: Fos, Egr1, Arc, Npas4, Nr4a1, Bdnf, Crem, and Srf were all FDR=1.0 under Oxtr across every measured cell group.
why_it_matters: The assay would have detected a sustained CREB/AP1-like secondary program, so its absence separates receptor loss in basal nuclei from acute ligand-evoked calcium/MAPK signaling and argues against chronic autonomous activation or stress after sparse Oxtr editing.

literature_claim: The OT receptor is an approved-drug GPCR target and mouse Oxtr mutants have curated social, maternal, aggression, and lactation phenotypes.
main_caveats: Pooled CRISPR did not measure behavior, ligand responses, receptor binding, or DNA indels.
summary: The sparse Oxtr LoF signature should not be used to infer that OXTR is inert or transcriptionally safe as a CNS drug target.
why_it_matters: OXTR is pharmacologically addressable and genetically required for mouse behavioral and lactation phenotypes, but this dataset only tests mosaic postmitotic receptor loss without ligand challenge; a flat basal transcriptome is therefore compatible with strong circuit and behavioral pharmacology.

literature_claim: P2RY12 biology in brain is dominated by microglial nucleotide sensing and motility, not by ELAV-like RNA-binding programs in neuronal GABA classes.
main_caveats: Single gene, n=40 perturbed nuclei, FDR just below 0.10, and no recurrence among directly measured comparators.
summary: P2ry12 produced only a CNU-MGE GABA singleton: Elavl3 was up-regulated at FDR 0.051 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and no other measured cell group had a robust downstream DEG.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only BH-supported neuronal transcriptomic change without over-treating it as a P2RY12 pathway; the effect is narrow, near the FDR boundary, and unsupported by comparator recurrence.

literature_claim: P2ry12 is a homeostatic microglial signature receptor that supports ADP/ATP-dependent process extension and is down-regulated during inflammatory activation.
main_caveats: Microglia were not themselves profiled; marker-gene absence is inferred from NeuN-enriched neuronal DE outputs.
summary: The expected microglial homeostatic and activation transcript sets were absent from the P2ry12 DE surface.
why_it_matters: P2ry12 loss in this dataset is not a weak version of a microglial activation/DAM response; the relevant lineage was largely removed by NeuN enrichment, so the missing program is interpretable rather than an assay-wide failure.

literature_claim: P2ry12 is a microglial homeostatic receptor and P2ry14 is a related P2Y-family nucleotide-sugar GPCR associated with immune biology.
main_caveats: These comparators are lineage/pathway controls, not necessarily redundant receptor subunits; Cx3cr1 and P2ry14 target transcripts themselves were not detected as genes in the P2ry12 DE surface.
summary: Loss of other microglia-lineage receptors represented in the screen was likewise flat in neuronal groups: P2ry14, Cx3cr1, Csf1r, Ccr2, Axl, and Mertk had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes across their recovered surfaces, while Sall1 had one isolated Rgs11 hit.
why_it_matters: The P2ry12 null surface is part of a broader lineage-mismatch pattern among microglial receptors and is not rescued by testing the P2Y-family neighbor P2ry14 or homeostatic comparators such as Cx3cr1/Csf1r.

main_caveats: The neighbor search used sub-threshold P2ry12 rank features because the FDR-supported signature contained only Elavl3.
summary: The strongest data-driven P2ry12 neighbors were only nominal: Atxn1 and Tbx6 had restricted-feature cosines of 0.136 and 0.134, Camta1 and Grm8 had -0.122 and -0.100, and none reproduced Elavl3 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: Even the best whole-universe neighbors do not define a recurrent P2ry12 transcriptional module; broad neuronal responders such as Camta1 are anti-neighbors of weak P2ry12 rank noise rather than mechanistic phenocopies.

literature_claim: P2Y12 has established platelet functions and approved antagonists, and microglial P2Y12 mediates chemotaxis and specialized microglia-neuron contacts.
main_caveats: Sparse CRISPR indels, 3-4 week postnatal timing, and snRNA-seq do not model systemic P2Y12 inhibitor exposure or microglial motility assays.
summary: The neuronal CRISPR surface gives little evidence for a broad cell-autonomous neuronal liability of P2ry12 loss, but it is not evidence against microglial or platelet P2Y12 pharmacology.
why_it_matters: P2Y12 is a druggable ADP receptor; this screen redirects interpretation of the P2ry12 zero toward unsampled microglia and non-neuronal platelets rather than toward neuronal target inactivity.

why_it_matters: The nearest non-safe targets to Pax4 had absolute cosine similarities of only 0.015-0.029 and zero robust shared DE genes, so the weak Pax4 rank-sum pattern is best treated as background rather than convergence on an unannotated pathway.

literature_claim: Pax7 is a paired-box/homeodomain developmental transcription factor with strong roles in embryonic dorsal neural tube, neural crest, superior-colliculus, and skeletal-muscle satellite-cell biology.

why_it_matters: This converts the dominant absence of signal into biology: the screen perturbed postmitotic NeuN-positive neurons after Pax7-dependent embryonic and early-postnatal patterning programs had largely run, so absence of a broad stress, fate, or myogenic program is an informative timing and lineage result rather than an assay-wide failure.

why_it_matters: The only robust Phactr2 response is not a shared PHACTR-family, MRTF, or generic actin-perturbation state; cross-perturbation evidence makes the Lrfn4 event target- and cell-class-restricted.

literature_claim: PHF12/Pf1 has established roles in embryonic viability, proliferative fibroblast ribosome biogenesis, neural crest EMT, and human NDD risk, but prior work did not map juvenile postmitotic brain cell-type selectivity.
main_caveats: Cell groups are coarse aggregates and the apparent caudal bias could hide finer subtype effects.
summary: Phf12 loss was not pan-neuronal: the FDR<0.10 response was concentrated in caudal thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic and pons/myelencephalon-associated neuronal classes, with the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c group dominating the surface.
why_it_matters: This converts many zeros from assay failure into a spatially patterned postmitotic vulnerability map: 711 of 759 downstream Phf12 hits came from 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.

literature_claim: Pf1/PHF12 recruits Sin3/TLE HDAC corepressor machinery and acts as a transcriptional repressor.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot distinguish direct de-repression from fast indirect compensation without chromatin occupancy.
summary: The active Phf12 signatures were strongly up-biased: 341/544 genes in 151, 94/121 in 155, 39/46 in 191, and 29/31 in 066 were up-regulated.
why_it_matters: The sign is consistent with removing a chromatin-associated repressor, while the substantial down arm marks secondary neuronal adaptation rather than simple global de-repression.

literature_claim: Pf1-deficient MEFs show transcript changes affecting ribosome-biogenesis pathways; neuronal Phf12 loss was therefore expected to perturb RNA production or processing, although not necessarily spliceosome mRNAs specifically.
main_caveats: Gene labels nominate RNA-processing stress but this dataset did not measure splicing isoforms directly.
summary: Phf12 perturbation induced a nuclear RNA-processing and spliceosome module, including Dhx38, Sf3b2, Snrnp70, Srsf11, Srsf5, Sfswap and U2af1.
why_it_matters: This was the most repeated molecular module and explains why spliceosome/RNA-binding perturbations were among the nearest cross-screen neighbors.

literature_claim: Phf12 was previously tied to nucleolar/ribosome-biogenesis homeostasis in proliferative cells; the neuronal data broaden the compensatory output to ER/Golgi and ubiquitin-proteostasis genes.
main_caveats: The response is transcriptional; protein folding, organelle flux and proteasome activity were not directly assayed.
summary: A secretory-proteostasis module was induced across Phf12 responders: ER membrane complex, glycosylation, Golgi-trafficking, lysosomal and ubiquitin-system genes all rose.
why_it_matters: This places the response downstream of chromatin loss into a cell-biological compensation axis that is shared with direct proteasome-perturbation signatures.

literature_claim: Prior Pf1 knockout work emphasized ribosome biogenesis rather than a defined neuronal mitochondrial module.
main_caveats: Mitochondrial function was inferred from nuclear mRNAs; mitochondrial transcripts and respiration were not measured.
summary: Ptcd3-centered mitochondrial and oxidative-metabolism genes were repeatedly up-regulated, with Ptcd3 significant in six of ten responder groups and Idh3b/Nduf/Timm/Tomm genes induced in the large thalamic and midbrain signatures.
why_it_matters: The most recurrent single downstream gene is mitochondrial, showing that Phf12 loss does not only alter nuclear chromatin or splicing factors but also engages an organellar metabolic arm.

literature_claim: PHF12 haploinsufficiency causes neurodevelopmental disease, but direct neuronal effector programs have not been defined.
main_caveats: Reduced synaptic mRNAs are a transcriptional proxy and require physiology or anatomy for functional validation.
summary: The negative arm of the strong Phf12 signatures was neuronal: Gls, Syt7, Snap25, Sv2a, Ntng1, Grm1, Gabrg2, Nrxn1 and cytoskeletal genes such as Tuba1a and Tubb3 were reduced.
why_it_matters: This argues that the down-regulated genes are not the direct output expected from losing a repressor, but a secondary loss of synaptic/neurite maintenance accompanying RNA-proteostasis induction.

main_caveats: This is a submodule of the larger TH/MB signatures and was not directly measured at the lipid level.
summary: Srebf2, Dhcr24, Sqle, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcs1, Fdps, Insig1 and Cyp46a1 formed a smaller down-regulated sterol/cholesterol module.
why_it_matters: Coupling sterol-gene loss to synaptic and vesicle-gene loss suggests that Phf12-responsive neurons may remodel membrane lipid programs while mounting ER and mitochondrial compensation.

main_caveats: Cosines were restricted to the 759 Phf12 significant features and therefore test convergence on the Phf12 program, not whole-transcriptome identity.
summary: The top positive Phf12 neighbors were proteasome and RNA-processing perturbations, not SIN3 components: Psmb4, Prpf6, Hnrnpu, Yy1, Psmc1 and U2af2 were the strongest same-direction matches.
why_it_matters: The data-driven neighborhood nominates a proteotoxic/RNA-processing attractor downstream of Phf12 rather than a canonical chromatin-only state.

literature_claim: PHF12/Pf1 binds SIN3A-containing complexes, and PHF12 disease validity is partly supported by this biochemical connection.
main_caveats: Most SIN3 catalytic/core subunits were not target perturbations in the parquet, so Sin3a was the principal directly measurable same-complex test.
summary: Sin3a, the literature-obvious scaffold partner, did not phenocopy Phf12 despite being a broad responder; it had a near-zero/slightly negative Phf12-query cosine with nearly balanced same- and opposite-direction overlaps.
why_it_matters: This distinguishes loss of the PHF12 adaptor from loss of the larger SIN3A scaffold and warns against assuming that one subunit reports the whole HDAC corepressor complex.

main_caveats: The anti-neighbor statistics summarize a restricted query signature; they are not proof of direct antagonism.
summary: The strongest anti-neighbors were Arid2, Setd5 and Nrf1, showing that some chromatin-like or stress-related perturbations invert the Phf12 RNA/proteostasis signature rather than merely fail to match it.
why_it_matters: Opposite neighbors make the Phf12 state directional: the same query genes that rise after Phf12 can fall after other perturbations, especially in the strong thalamic signature.

literature_claim: In premigratory chick neural crest, PHD12 knockdown prevents Sin3A/HDAC-mediated Cad6b repression and blocks neural crest EMT.
main_caveats: Cdh6 is not Cad6b in chick nomenclature, and neural crest cells were not sampled.
summary: The neural-crest Cad6b/Cdh6-Snail2 program expected from embryonic PHD12 biology was absent: Cdh6 and Snai2 were tested in every Phf12 cell group and never reached FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This is an informative negative control on context: the P16 neuronal assay can see Phf12-dependent transcriptional stress, but it does not replay an embryonic EMT target program.

literature_claim: Clinical PHF12 loss-of-function is linked to autosomal dominant complex neurodevelopmental disorder, while experimental Phf12 studies emphasized embryonic viability, MEF senescence and neural-crest EMT.
main_caveats: The screen models acute mosaic postnatal indels, not heterozygous germline human development.
summary: A postmitotic juvenile Phf12 loss-of-function can perturb mature neuronal RNA, proteostasis, mitochondrial and synaptic mRNAs without embryonic cell division.
why_it_matters: PHF12 is a haploinsufficient NDD gene; these data show a plausible cell-autonomous neuronal maintenance component, concentrated outside the cortical groups that dominate many NDD models.

literature_claim: A competitive Tat-SID strategy and PF1 knockdown disrupt SIN3A-PF1 in TNBC cells and suppress EMT/stem-cell tumor programs.
main_caveats: Tat-SID is not a brain-exposure drug and the screen perturbed Phf12 genetically rather than acutely blocking the interface pharmacologically.
summary: Experimental SIN3A-PF1 inhibition proposed for cancer would be expected to intersect neuronal RNA/proteostasis programs if achieved in PHF12-dependent neurons.
why_it_matters: The same protein interface can be therapeutically attractive in proliferating tumor cells yet measurably coupled to synaptic and organellar mRNAs in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: PHF21A/BHC80 is a neuronal chromatin regulator in an LSD1/CoREST-linked H3K4me0 repression system, with neuron-specific isoform biology tied to synaptogenesis.
main_caveats: The signature is small and DNA indel rates were not measured, so absent groups cannot be interpreted as protein-intact cells.
summary: Phf21a loss produced a real but narrow P16-postmitotic transcriptional response: 18 FDR<0.10 downstream events in 5 of 22 measured cell groups, with the largest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The result refines PHF21A from a pan-neuronal chromatin disease gene into an acutely cell-state-selective regulator under juvenile sparse CRISPR conditions.

literature_claim: RREB1 is a Ras-responsive zinc-finger transcription factor that can act as a transcriptional regulator downstream of RAS/MAPK signaling.
main_caveats: Rreb1 was a transcriptomic sentinel only; RAS/MAPK activity was not assayed directly.
summary: Rreb1 induction was the dominant recurrent Phf21a downstream event, appearing in every responder and often as the only FDR-supported gene.
why_it_matters: A Ras-responsive zinc-finger factor, not a textbook REST target, is the most reproducible basal nuclear marker of acute Phf21a loss in this screen.

literature_claim: no PHF21A-specific prior predicted this exact adhesion and Wnt-ligand-trafficking gene set.
main_caveats: The module is gene-poor; Col4a5 recurred in two groups but the other genes were single-cell-group events.
summary: The 151 thalamic and 191 posterior GABA signatures added an induced local membrane/extracellular module around Col4a5, Cdh13, Jam2, Adam15, Tapbp, and Wls.
why_it_matters: The non-Rreb1 genes argue that the strongest Phf21a response was not simply a single transcription-factor spike but included subtype-restricted cell-adhesion and ligand-trafficking genes.

literature_claim: PHF21A is itself an H3K4me0 chromatin reader in an LSD1-linked repressive complex.
main_caveats: L3mbtl3 is a singleton FDR hit and no chromatin occupancy or histone-methylation measurements were made.
summary: L3mbtl3 was induced with Rreb1 in 155 MB Glut, giving a one-gene hint of chromatin-reader compensation rather than a broad generic chromatin program.
why_it_matters: It points to possible replacement by a different methyl-lysine reader in a midbrain glutamatergic context, but the compensation is much weaker than the Rreb1 axis.

literature_claim: No established PHF21A-ZBTB7A functional relationship was required to nominate this comparison.
main_caveats: Zbtb7a had a much broader 2646-gene surface, so this is convergence on a submodule, not a phenocopy.
summary: Zbtb7a was the chief FDR-overlap neighbor of Phf21a, sharing Rreb1 up-regulation in 4 matched responder groups while also opposing 3 weaker Phf21a events.
why_it_matters: The best robust overlap came from a broad transcription-factor perturbation rather than a known PHF21A complex member, nominating Rreb1 as a reusable stress or transcriptional state reachable from multiple repressor perturbations.

literature_claim: PHF21A/BHC80 and REST/Sin3-associated systems are chromatin-repressive frameworks that can regulate neuronal gene expression.
main_caveats: YY1 and SIN3A are not PHF21A paralogs, and opposition was evaluated on the small Phf21a FDR gene set.
summary: Yy1 and Sin3a opposed pieces of the Phf21a 151-thalamic signature, including Rreb1 down after both Yy1 and Sin3a perturbation, while Phf21a drove Rreb1 up.
why_it_matters: Related or broadly repressive chromatin perturbations do not collapse to one shared direction in postmitotic thalamic neurons; PHF21A acts in a specific regulatory state rather than as a generic HDAC-corepressor loss.

literature_claim: PHF21A sits in an H3K4me0/LSD1/CoREST repression axis whose effect could have been expected to align with REST or H3K4-methylation perturbations.
main_caveats: KDM1A, RCOR1/2/3, HDAC1/2, and PHF21B were not represented as targets, so the closest complex-level phenotypes remain untested.
summary: The obvious REST and H3K4 comparators failed to phenocopy Phf21a: Rest, Phf6, Phf8, Kdm5b, and Kdm6b were FDR-flat, whereas Setd1a, Kmt2a, and Sin3a responded but did not share Phf21a's FDR signature.
why_it_matters: Acute Phf21a loss is not the same as turning off REST, all PHD-finger intellectual-disability genes, or H3K4 methylation writers in postnatal neurons.

literature_claim: Human PHF21A haploinsufficiency causes a complex neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual disability, craniofacial anomalies, and variably epilepsy, hypotonia, and autism-related neurobehavioral features.
main_caveats: The screen assayed sparse CRISPR in surviving NeuN+ neurons only; it did not test embryonic progenitors, craniofacial lineages, evoked cAMP transcription, or synapse morphology.
summary: The dataset supports PHF21A haploinsufficiency as a disease gene but redirects the major causal biology away from a broad pan-neuronal basal transcriptome at P16-P44.
why_it_matters: Most human alleles are germline or early de novo loss-of-function events; the sparse juvenile mosaic response warns that a late, basal snRNA-seq knockout is an incomplete model for PHF21A neurodevelopmental disorder and for postnatal therapeutic rescue screens.

literature_claim: Human BFLS genetics and neural loss-of-function models implicate PHF6 in neurodevelopmental transcription, cortical migration, neurite outgrowth, and fetal cortical gene regulation.
main_caveats: CRISPR indels and PHF6 protein loss were not measured; rare cells and state-dependent programs could be diluted in the 23 broad cell groups.
summary: Phf6 loss after P16 produced a globally buffered neuronal nuclear transcriptome: all 21 recovered cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and Phf6 itself had FDR=1 in every group.
why_it_matters: The central result is negative but biological: Phf6 is not a broad basal transcriptional dependency once neurons in this juvenile whole-brain assay are already specified and postmitotic.

literature_claim: Embryonic PHF6 acts with PAF1 during cortical migration, and fetal cortical Phf6 loss changes Reln, Nr4a2, Slc12a5, Phip, and Zic-family expression.
main_caveats: The assay perturbed heterogeneous postnatal cortical populations, not E14-E16 migrating neurons.
summary: The canonical fetal cortical PHF6-PAF1/migration program was not reactivated by postmitotic Phf6 editing: Cspg5 and the fetal-cortical genes Reln, Nr4a2, Slc12a5, Phip, and Zic1-Zic4 all had FDR=1 in every measured Phf6 group.
why_it_matters: This separates the strong embryonic migration mechanism of PHF6 from the basal juvenile transcriptional state sampled here.

literature_claim: PHF6 is a PHD-like chromatin-associated protein, but PHF proteins are not established as a single interchangeable paralog family.
main_caveats: The comparison is family/domain-level rather than same-complex; genes driving Phf12 or Phf21a signatures were not assumed to be PHF6 targets.
summary: PHF/PHD-domain targets did not phenocopy Phf6: Phf8 was flat, Phf21a had only 18 downstream FDR genes, Phf12 had 754, and their Phf6 all-feature score correlations were 0.004-0.010.
why_it_matters: The null is not a generic property of all PHD-finger chromatin factors in the screen; PHF6 behaves as a buffered adaptor rather than like the more responsive PHF12 program.

literature_claim: PHF6 co-purifies with multiple NuRD-complex constituents, including CHD4, HDAC1, and RBBP4.
main_caveats: HDAC1 and RBBP4 were not represented as perturbation targets, and the published PHF6-NuRD interaction was mapped biochemically rather than by matched neuronal CRISPR.
summary: The PHF6-NuRD physical interaction did not translate into a matched neuronal loss-of-function signature: Chd4 produced 158 downstream FDR genes in the same groups, while Mbd2 and Gatad2b produced only 1 and 2, and all three correlated with Phf6 at |r|≤0.0024.
why_it_matters: A same-assembly interaction is therefore not enough to predict a PHF6-like postnatal neuronal transcriptome; CHD4-dominant NuRD loss is measurably different from PHF6 loss here.

main_caveats: Because Phf6 has no FDR-supported signature, all-feature correlations are useful as a rejection of strong convergence, not as positive pathway discovery.
summary: The data-nominated Phf6 signature neighborhood collapsed to noise: the strongest non-safe positive neighbor was Ror1 at r=0.027, and the strongest negative neighbor was Psmb4 at r=-0.022.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-reading Phf6 nominal genes as a reproducible module; even the best cross-target alignments across 355k matched features were essentially zero.

literature_claim: PHF8 loss can alter transcription of H4K20/H3K9-, rDNA-, neuronal-differentiation-, and cytoskeleton-linked genes in developmental or proliferative systems.
main_caveats: AAV-CRISPR was delivered after neuronal specification; indels and PHF8 protein loss were not assayed; snRNA-seq does not measure histone methylation, rRNA precursor synthesis, phosphorylation, or electrophysiology.
summary: Phf8 was a pan-neuronal transcriptional non-responder in the P16-to-P37/44 mosaic loss-of-function assay: 22 assayed neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and even FDR<0.20 returned zero genes across 371,796 downstream tests.
why_it_matters: The result shifts interpretation away from an acute, broad cell-autonomous Pol-II mRNA role for PHF8 in already specified juvenile neurons and toward developmental, chronic, or lineage-restricted PHF8 biology.

literature_claim: Global Phf8 deficiency in mouse hippocampus hyperactivates mTOR signaling and impairs LTP and learning/memory.
main_caveats: Rps6ka1/RSK1 was not in the tested feature set, and mTOR phosphorylation and LTP are protein/electrophysiological readouts outside snRNA-seq.
summary: The hippocampal Ras/mTOR expectation from Phf8-deficient mice was not recovered after sparse P16 Phf8 loss: both hippocampal glutamatergic groups were FDR-null, and model-visible Mtor/Ras sentinels remained uncorrected.
why_it_matters: A published germline mouse phenotype maps PHF8 to hippocampal mTOR and LTP; the screen shows that this pathway is not acutely re-induced as a cell-autonomous neuronal mRNA program within 3-4 weeks of P16 editing.

literature_claim: The direct KDM7 comparison would be to PHF8/KDM7B paralogs KDM7A/KIAA1718 and PHF2/KDM7C, with related PHD-JmjC architecture and substrate preferences.
main_caveats: Direct KDM7 paralogs Phf2 and Kdm7a were absent from the perturbation target set, so redundancy with those paralogs could not be measured.
summary: Phf8 lacked a meaningful positive or inverse signature neighbor, and represented PHF/JmjC or neurodevelopmental chromatin comparators did not phenocopy it.
why_it_matters: The result prevents attributing the flat Phf8 surface to a generic failure to detect chromatin regulators: Setd1a, Mecp2, and Kdm5c produced corrected DE in the same analysis universe, whereas Phf8 and several represented demethylases were flat or unrelated.

literature_claim: PHF8 loss-of-function variants cause X-linked neurodevelopmental disease with craniofacial dysmorphology, and experimental PHF8 loss disrupts embryonic brain/craniofacial, neuronal-differentiation, and astrocyte-differentiation programs.
main_caveats: The screen cannot distinguish absence of indels from buffered chromatin after indels; direct craniofacial, progenitor, astrocyte, and oligodendrocyte lineages were outside the FACS-enriched neuronal dataset.
summary: The Phf8-null surface separates PHF8 loss-of-function disease biology from acute neuronal knockdown in the juvenile brain.
why_it_matters: Human PHF8-XLID is a developmental disorder; the absence of robust DE after P16 editing argues that the molecular lesions most relevant to disease are more likely established during prenatal/perinatal lineage construction, chronic hippocampal adaptation, or glial/craniofacial programs than by a large immediate transcriptomic collapse in every mature neuron.

literature_claim: PHKA1 functions in glycogenolysis as the muscle alpha regulatory subunit of phosphorylase kinase, whereas the dominant brain glycogen store is astrocytic rather than neuronal.
main_caveats: DNA editing was not measured, the mean mRNA knockdown expected in this platform is modest, and 215 MB Dopa was absent for Phka1.
summary: Phka1 is transcriptionally silent after acute postmitotic neuronal loss-of-function across every recovered cell group in this screen.
why_it_matters: The data exclude a broad juvenile neuronal stress, proteostasis, synaptic or metabolic transcriptional response to Phka1 disruption, even though the target transcript itself was tested in 22 cellular contexts.

literature_claim: PhK is an alpha-beta-gamma-delta holoenzyme in which PHKA1/PHKB are regulatory subunits and CALM1-3 encode the delta calmodulin subunit.
main_caveats: PHKA2 and PHKG1/2 were not represented as perturbation targets, and the few Calm1/Calm3 DE genes may reflect PhK-independent calcium biology.
summary: The phosphorylase-kinase complex does not behave as one neuronal transcriptional module: Phka1 and Phkb were both null, while Calm1 and Calm3 had small non-overlapping responses.
why_it_matters: This rejects a simple same-holoenzyme phenocopy model in postnatal neurons and implies that any weak calmodulin signatures are more likely broader calcium/calmodulin effects than a Phka1-like glycogenolysis program.

main_caveats: Correlation was computed on signed Wilcoxon scores and is descriptive; a completely flat target makes nearest-neighbor ranks dominated by nominal noise.
summary: A dataset-wide signature scan could not assign Phka1 a robust convergent or inverse neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative correlations were close to zero and vanished under FDR-overlap testing, so the Phka1 surface is best interpreted as a buffered null rather than a weak member of another perturbation module.

literature_claim: PHKB encodes the regulatory beta subunit of phosphorylase kinase, a glycogenolysis activator whose inherited deficiency primarily compromises liver and muscle glycogen metabolism, while brain glycogen flux is concentrated in astrocytes.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured; acute mosaic CRISPR in NeuN-enriched postmitotic nuclei tests basal neuronal transcription, not liver, muscle, or astrocyte glycogen flux.
summary: Phkb loss of function was FDR-flat in every recovered neuronal cell group.
why_it_matters: A canonical glycogenolysis enzyme can be present in the ranked neuronal transcriptome without producing an ISR, lysosomal, proteostasis, synaptic, or metabolic transcriptional state over the P16-to-P37/44 window.

literature_claim: PhK contains alpha, beta, catalytic gamma, and calmodulin delta subunits; CALM1, CALM2, and CALM3 encode calmodulin and are not established GSD IX genes.
main_caveats: Phka2, Phkg1, and Phkg2 were not target perturbations in the parquet; Calm genes also serve many non-PhK calcium-signaling functions.
summary: Same-holoenzyme PhK comparators did not phenocopy Phkb.
why_it_matters: The absence of Phkb response is not hiding a broader phosphorylase-kinase transcriptional module: Phka1 and Calm2 were also downstream-flat, whereas Calm1 and Calm3 produced only sparse, cell-restricted genes not shared with Phkb.

literature_claim: GAA loss causes lysosomal glycogen accumulation in Pompe disease through a storage mechanism distinct from cytosolic PhK-dependent glycogen phosphorylase activation.
main_caveats: Gaa is a disease-family comparator rather than a PhK-complex member; the assay did not quantify lysosomal glycogen or autophagic flux.
summary: The represented lysosomal glycogen-storage comparator Gaa was strongly self-repressed but downstream-flat in neurons, paralleling Phkb's flatness on the output axis.
why_it_matters: Directly knocking down a Pompe-disease glycogen hydrolase produced no FDR-resolved neuronal stress program, supporting the interpretation that short postnatal neuronal snRNA-seq is poorly coupled to baseline glycogen-storage enzyme biochemistry unless a secondary transcriptional threshold is crossed.

why_it_matters: The top positive score-space neighbor, Cckar, and the top negative neighbor, Safe_target_28, were themselves FDR-flat, and their cosine scores were only +0.039 and -0.023. The Phkb signature is therefore dominated by near-null rank noise rather than a hidden convergent or opposing module.

literature_claim: Phox2a is best established as an embryonic determinant of locus-coeruleus noradrenergic, autonomic/sensory, and cranial motor development.
main_caveats: The assay did not genotype edited alleles and did not sample hindbrain or peripheral autonomic tissues; the one CNU-MGE GABA hit prevents calling the target completely silent.
summary: Phox2a loss of function was nearly silent across the recovered P16-edited neuronal taxonomy: 22 of 23 groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and the remaining group had only one.
why_it_matters: This turns the dominant null surface into interpretable biology: in this juvenile, hindbrain-depleted, NeuN-enriched assay, Phox2a is not a broad postmitotic maintenance factor for cortical, basal-ganglia, thalamic, midbrain dopamine, pineal, or cerebellar transcriptional state.

main_caveats: Only one gene was significant at FDR 0.0668, with no corroborating pathway-level signature.
summary: A single CNU-MGE GABA gene, Itfg1, decreased after Phox2a perturbation.
why_it_matters: This is the only FDR-supported downstream event in the entire Phox2a surface; because it is a lone gene rather than a module, it should be treated as a restricted biomarker candidate rather than a mechanistic Phox2a program.

literature_claim: Phox2 factors promote catecholaminergic/noradrenergic identity genes including Th, Dbh, and Slc6a2 in the appropriate LC or catecholaminergic contexts.
main_caveats: The absent direction is interpreted in a lineage-mismatched screen; most sampled nuclei were not noradrenergic LC neurons.
summary: Canonical catecholaminergic and autonomic Phox2a-associated genes were not detectably altered in the Phox2a perturbation surface.
why_it_matters: Dbh, Th, Slc6a2, Ddc, Gch1, Gata3, Ret, and Ntrk1 all had FDR=1.0 in all 23 groups, so the screen observed no LC/noradrenergic identity collapse in the recovered nuclei despite measuring those symbols.

literature_claim: Phox2b is a close Phox2a paralog and Rnf220/Zc4h2 modifies Phox2a/Phox2b to support LC noradrenergic differentiation.
main_caveats: Zc4h2 itself and several direct catecholaminergic effector genes were not perturbation targets; broad taxonomy can dilute rare subtypes.
summary: Phox2-pathway comparators represented in the parquet did not converge with Phox2a.
why_it_matters: The Phox2b paralog, the Phox2 modifier Rnf220, and Ret/Ntrk1/Isl1 pathway comparators were flat across their measured surfaces and had Itfg1 FDR=1.0 in CNU-MGE GABA, arguing that the expected Phox2 noradrenergic-developmental module is absent from this assay rather than selectively missed only by Phox2a guides.

main_caveats: Because Phox2a has only a one-gene FDR signature, neighbor rankings are dominated by very weak full-vector correlations and should be read as a negative result.
summary: The data-driven whole-surface neighbor search found no strong positive or negative Phox2a signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top score-vector correlations were near zero and did not reproduce the sole Itfg1 hit, so the Phox2a profile lacks a reproducible cross-target transcriptional module in this dataset.

main_caveats: No DNA indel calls are available, and 215 MB Dopa was not tested for Phox2b.
summary: Phox2b had no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured neuronal cell groups; 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut was only weak by a single Rasgef1a near-miss at FDR=0.130.
why_it_matters: The main measured phenotype is a robust absence of a Phox2b-dependent program in the sampled postnatal NeuN+ brain classes, not an interpretable stress or fate-switch module.

literature_claim: Phox2b, together with Phox2a, Gata factors, Hand factors, and Ascl1, regulates autonomic noradrenergic and RTN-associated transcriptional programs including Th and Dbh in the appropriate developmental lineages.
main_caveats: Hand2 and Slc18a2 were not in the Phox2b DE output, and broad cell groups could dilute very rare caudal Phox2b-positive neurons if any were recovered.
summary: The canonical Phox2b autonomic/noradrenergic output was absent: Th, Dbh, Ret, Gfra1, Gata2, Gata3, Phox2a, Ascl1, Atoh1, Sox10, Egr2, Lbx1, and Slc6a2 all had min FDR=1.0 in Phox2b-perturbed groups, and Phox2a/Ret/Sox10/Gfra1/Atoh1/Gata3/Egr2/Lbx1 perturbations were themselves flat or single-gene in the same taxonomy.

literature_claim: Semaphorin-plexin signaling is cytoskeletal and small-GTPase centered; KIF21A regulates microtubule growth and ARHGAP35/p190RhoGAP participates in plexin-to-actin signaling.
main_caveats: Each responder group contained only one downstream DEG, so this is a semaphorin-adjacent marker hypothesis rather than pathway enrichment.
summary: Plxna1 loss yielded only two downstream FDR<0.10 transcriptional hits, Kif21a up in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and Arhgap35 up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: Both genes sit near microtubule/Rho cytoskeletal biology, fitting semaphorin receptor logic, but the response is single-gene and cell-restricted rather than a multigene axon-guidance module.

literature_claim: Class-3 semaphorin signaling uses neuropilin/plexin-A receptor assemblies, and PLXNA1 can cooperate with PLXNA3 in Sema3A-dependent developing axon scaffolds.
main_caveats: Sema3a and Plxna3 themselves were absent from the target universe, and convergence was measured at the mRNA-signature level rather than by ligand challenge or indel sequencing.
summary: Measured plexin, neuropilin, and semaphorin relatives did not phenocopy Plxna1 in the matching responder groups and had near-zero full-signature correlations.
why_it_matters: This rejects a simple interchangeable semaphorin-receptor transcriptional state in the postnatal neuronal screen; Plxna1, Plxna2, Plxna4, Nrp1, Nrp2, Sema5a, and Sema6a were either flat or acted on different single genes in different groups.

main_caveats: Full-transcriptome correlations on a near-null query are most useful for rejection; they are not evidence that these targets share biology with Plxna1.
summary: Genome-wide data-driven Plxna1 signature neighbors were all too weak to keep as biological comparators.
why_it_matters: The best positive and negative neighbors had absolute Wilcoxon-score correlations below 0.03, showing that the two-gene Plxna1 footprint does not anchor a robust cross-perturbation module.

why_it_matters: Human PLXNA1 phenotypes and mouse Plxna1 wiring defects can be severe even though this P16 acute LoF screen mostly sees no nuclear transcriptomic response 3-4 weeks later.

summary: The P16 postmitotic Plxna2 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered: 22 of 23 groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and Pvalb, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c, and MB Glut groups showed significant Plxna2 mRNA decreases without any downstream DE.
why_it_matters: A functional CRISPR indel can be present without strong self-mRNA loss, but the on-target-only rows show that even detectable transcript depletion was not sufficient to trigger a stable mRNA program; this separates postnatal neuronal mRNA state from the developmental wiring phenotypes that dominate Plxna2 biology.

literature_claim: Plxna2, Plxna4, Sema5A, Sema6A, and neuropilin/plexin signaling occupy related semaphorin receptor pathways during neuronal guidance and dentate development.

summary: Represented plexin, neuropilin, and semaphorin perturbations did not converge with Plxna2 in this assay.
why_it_matters: Plxna2 shares ligands and developmental phenotypes with Plxna4/Sema6A and participates in Sema5A signaling, but direct parquet queries showed only near-zero cosine similarity and no shared 009 Med15 response, arguing against a generic P16 semaphorin-plexin mRNA module.

literature_claim: No prior biological neighbor claim was used; this was the pre-literature data-driven comparison across the parquet.
main_caveats: Because Plxna2 itself has only one FDR-level downstream gene, whole-surface cosine values are dominated by weak ranks and should be interpreted for their near-zero magnitude, not as mechanistic links to the listed genes.
summary: The unbiased signature-neighbor search found only near-zero global neighbors for Plxna2.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive real-gene neighbor, Robo4, had a cosine of only 0.0326, and the strongest negative real-gene neighbor, Uqcrb, was -0.0122, so neither known semaphorin biology nor the full dataset revealed a hidden recurrent Plxna2-like transcriptional state.

literature_claim: No prior Plxna4 semaphorin literature evaluated here predicted Zfp384 induction as a downstream marker.
main_caveats: One DEG in 50 perturbed cells; Zfp384 has no demonstrated mechanistic placement downstream of Plexin-A4 in this dataset.
summary: Acute Plxna4 loss produced a singleton Zfp384 up-regulation in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and no other FDR<0.10 downstream gene in any measured cell group.
why_it_matters: The only robust transcriptional output is an unexpected candidate marker of Plxna4 sensitivity rather than a recognizable semaphorin pathway, so the positive phenotype should not be overexpanded into a multi-gene program.

literature_claim: The Srebf1 and Tlr8 relationships were nominated by the dataset rather than by prior Plxna4 biology.
main_caveats: The scan is necessarily weak because Plxna4 has a singleton FDR signature.
summary: The unbiased centered whole-transcriptome surface had no strong positive or negative Plxna4 neighbor: Srebf1 and Tlr8 were the top non-safe MEA-measured neighbors but had cosine_z values of only +0.0106 and -0.0130 and did not reproduce Zfp384 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: This rejects a hidden broad module behind the single Zfp384 point and shows that Plxna4 is isolated even before imposing literature expectations.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Plexin-A4 participates in semaphorin receptor complexes with other Plexin-A proteins, neuropilins, Sema3 ligands, and Sema6A/Sema6B-dependent guidance pathways.
main_caveats: Comparators were assessed only where represented in the parquet; Plxna3 and many other semaphorin ligands were not available as perturbation targets.
summary: Represented semaphorin/plexin relatives were disjoint from Plxna4: none phenocopied the 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut Zfp384 response, and their own significant DEGs were isolated in other groups.
why_it_matters: Plexin-A receptor family membership and shared ligand/co-receptor logic are insufficient to predict the acute nuclear phenotype; in this assay, Plxna4 behaves as a cell-context-specific singleton rather than as an interchangeable member of a semaphorin module.

literature_claim: Plexin-A4 signals through semaphorin receptor complexes and post-translational FARP2/Rac1 or other cytoskeletal mechanisms rather than a simple transcription-factor cascade.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq would miss Rac1 activation, CRMP phosphorylation, growth-cone collapse, dendritic arbors, axon trajectories, and tau phosphorylation.
summary: Plxna4 loss did not transcriptionally regulate assayed semaphorin co-receptors or canonical intracellular signaling nodes, including Nrp1, Nrp2, Plxna1, Plxna2, Plxnd1, Sema4d, Sema5a, Sema6a, Farp2, Rac1, Fyn, Dpysl2, Dpysl5, Cdk5, Cdk5r1, Rasa1, and Rras.
why_it_matters: The expected post-receptor biology is local, ligand-gated phosphorylation and cytoskeletal remodeling; the absence of RNA feedback argues that the juvenile mosaic knockout did not trigger a detectable secondary stress or compensatory nuclear program.
