why_it_matters: The absence of broad stress, DNA-repair, splicing, or cryptic-transcription secondary programs refines the interpretation of SETD2 loss: in this juvenile postmitotic assay the major effects are likely earlier developmental or non-transcriptional rather than bulk mRNA-abundance states.

literature_claim: Setd5 loss is expected to perturb embryonic neural development, neural-progenitor proliferation, rDNA output, and Pol II/cell-cycle programs in susceptible proliferating systems.
main_caveats: A direct rDNA assay and DNA indel measurements are absent; the negative result applies to recovered NeuN+ postmitotic nuclei after P16 perturbation.
summary: Acute Setd5 loss produced only two FDR-positive cell-group responses and did not recover progenitor, E2F/cell-cycle, Hox/Pax6/Nes, RNA polymerase I, or ribosomal-protein programs anywhere in the 21 recovered neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: This is a sharp context refinement: the P16 sparse postmitotic neuronal assay largely bypasses the embryonic and progenitor settings in which SETD5 biology is strongest.

literature_claim: Loss of a SETD5-associated HDAC/NCoR scaffold could derepress selected target genes, but the specific TH Prkcd/Grin2c neuronal module was not a canonical published Setd5 output.
main_caveats: The signature is 13 genes in one cell group; protein and electrophysiologic consequences were not measured.
summary: Setd5 perturbation selectively up-regulated a TH Prkcd/Grin2c neuronal-signaling module, with 12 of 13 significant genes going up and Kat6b going down.
why_it_matters: The main Setd5 signal in this screen is not a broad chromatin-fidelity collapse; it is a localized thalamic program enriched for GPCR, calcium/kinase, synaptic, neurite, and RNA-editing genes.

main_caveats: Single-gene result at FDR 0.05296; it needs validation at protein or transporter-function levels.
summary: The Pvalb response was limited to a single FDR-supported Slc6a1 up-regulation.
why_it_matters: Slc6a1 nominates altered GABA reuptake capacity as a Pvalb-specific marker hypothesis while also showing that Setd5 does not impose a large GABAergic transcriptional state.

literature_claim: SETD5 and ANKRD11 are independently implicated chromatin regulators in neurodevelopment, but no represented same-complex SETD5 partner was available to predict this exact convergence.
main_caveats: The convergence is transcriptomic and restricted to the FDR-positive TH signature.
summary: Ankrd11 was the strongest same-direction data-driven neighbor of the Setd5 responder signature and reproduced seven Setd5 TH up-genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This preserves an unexpected chromatin/NDD convergence: the Setd5 postmitotic TH module aligns with Ankrd11 rather than with the obvious SET-domain methyltransferase comparators.

main_caveats: The comparison is defined over the small Setd5 FDR signature; it should not be read as a direct biochemical relationship.
summary: Cic and Psmb4 drove the Setd5 responder signature in the opposite direction, with Psmb4 inverting 12 of 14 Setd5 FDR coordinates and Cic inverting seven TH coordinates.
why_it_matters: Opposition by a strong proteasome perturbation and by Cic shows that the Setd5 state is not a nonspecific stress artifact or any generic transcriptional repressor response.

literature_claim: SETD5 belongs to the SET-domain chromatin regulator landscape and can act through histone-acetylation control, making SET-domain and CBP/p300-related chromatin genes obvious comparators.
main_caveats: Core HDAC3/NCoR and PAF1-complex members were not represented; exact-overlap rejection can miss weaker pathway-level similarity.
summary: Represented SET-family, MLL/COMPASS-related, CBP/p300, and chromatin-NDD comparators failed to phenocopy the exact Setd5 FDR signature despite several being active in the same TH group.
why_it_matters: Setd5's P16 postmitotic output is not interchangeable with nearby chromatin regulators; a broad SET-domain or chromatin-disease label would have predicted the wrong target neighbors.

literature_claim: Setdb1 has essential H3K9me3-dependent effects during early mouse brain development.
main_caveats: Engagement at the DNA and H3K9me3 levels was not measured; several responder groups contained only 31 to 45 perturbed cells.
summary: Acute postnatal Setdb1 loss produced a sparse coding-gene response: only 9 of 22 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 genes, with the strongest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: SETDB1 is a broadly used chromatin silencer, but in this P16-to-P37/44 neuronal assay its detectable RNA output was sharply cell-type restricted.

literature_claim: Neuronal Setdb1 conditional loss reduces H3K9me3 at the clustered Pcdh superTAD, increases CTCF binding, and derepresses Pcdh isoforms.
main_caveats: The screen measured mature nuclear mRNA, not Pcdh chromatin loops, protein isoforms, or cell-surface adhesion.
summary: Gamma-protocadherin variable exons were the clearest Setdb1-repressed coding module: 15 significant Pcdhga/Pcdhgb cell-gene calls were all up across six responder groups.
why_it_matters: This is the expected sign for releasing a SETDB1/H3K9me3 brake at clustered Pcdh promoters, and it places the effect in Pvalb, thalamic, midbrain, deep-layer cortical, and pontine/myelencephalic neurons in this acute mosaic assay.

literature_claim: HUSH uses TASOR, MPP8, Periphilin, ATF7IP, SETDB1, and MORC2 to deposit H3K9me3 and silence retroelements; ATF7IP stabilizes nuclear SETDB1.
main_caveats: Atf7ip and Tasor were not themselves perturbed targets, so feedback is inferred from their mRNA induction.
summary: Setdb1 perturbation up-regulated Atf7ip and Tasor, components of the SETDB1/HUSH silencing machinery, in thalamic and midbrain responders.
why_it_matters: Induction of a SETDB1-stabilizing partner and a HUSH scaffold is consistent with a compensatory attempt to rebuild H3K9me3 repression after losing the catalytic SETDB1 node.

literature_claim: SETDB1 loss can desilence retrotransposable elements, produce dsRNA, induce type-I interferon genes, and cause apoptosis in AML cells.
main_caveats: The parquet did not quantify repeat families directly, and NeuN enrichment under-sampled glia and immune cells that can amplify interferon signaling.
summary: The cancer-like ERV-to-type-I-interferon viral-mimicry program was not recovered after neuronal Setdb1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: SETDB1 inhibition is often framed as a way to unmask retroelements and stimulate innate immunity; these postmitotic neurons instead showed Pcdh/HUSH coding effects with no robust ISG induction.

literature_claim: SETDB1 shields Pcdh promoters from excess CTCF binding, whereas CTCF/cohesin loops are required for clustered-Pcdh transcription.
main_caveats: The comparison is limited to shared FDR<0.10 coding-gene features and cannot prove direct CTCF occupancy changes in the screen.
summary: Ctcf, the strongest negative Setdb1 signature neighbor, opposed Setdb1 on the gamma-protocadherin axis.
why_it_matters: Although Setdb1 loss and CTCF both converge on the clustered-Pcdh locus in prior chromatin models, the matched Perturb-seq readout separates them into an H3K9 repressor arm that releases Pcdhg transcription and a CTCF arm required to maintain expression of many of the same genes.

literature_claim: EHMT1/GLP is an H3K9me1/2 methyltransferase and SMCHD1 antagonizes CTCF at Pcdh promoters, so both were plausible same-axis comparators.
main_caveats: EHMT2, TRIM28, TASOR, and ATF7IP were not represented as perturbation targets; Ehmt1 overlap was restricted to three non-Pcdh genes.
summary: Setdb1 did not phenocopy measurable neighboring methylation and Pcdh regulators: Ehmt1 shared only a three-gene TH submodule, whereas Dnmt3a and Smchd1 were flat across Setdb1-matched groups.
why_it_matters: The Setdb1 Pcdh/HUSH signature is not a generic response to perturbing H3K9 or DNA-methylation-associated repressors, and the expected Pcdh repressor Smchd1 was buffered in this acute P16 assay.

main_caveats: The relationship is data-driven and restricted to a few shared significant genes; Sin3a had thousands of DE calls not shared with Setdb1.
summary: The unbiased positive neighbors Sin3a and Chd4 met Setdb1 only on a small 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut submodule rather than on a global chromatin-repression signature.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation convergence nominated NuRD/SIN3-like chromatin repression as a local thalamic modifier of Setdb1 output, but their much larger DE surfaces distinguish broad co-repressor failure from Setdb1 loss.

main_caveats: Recurrence is only two cell groups per gene, and no direct Setdb1 literature was identified for either marker.
summary: Ccdc84 and Zmym6 recurred as noncanonical Setdb1-upregulated markers in small responder subsets.
why_it_matters: These genes may be useful readouts of the thalamic and deep-layer cortical Setdb1 state even though they do not explain the canonical Pcdh or HUSH mechanisms.

main_caveats: Single-gene response in 42 perturbed nuclei; it should be treated as a candidate rather than a pathway-level synaptic program.
summary: Setdb1 had a one-gene negative synaptic-release output in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, where Unc13a was the only FDR<0.10 downstream gene and was down-regulated.
why_it_matters: The sign and isolated active-zone identity of Unc13a distinguish this GABAergic effect from the gamma-protocadherin and HUSH-cofactor responses seen elsewhere.

literature_claim: SETX dysfunction can perturb R-loop handling and transcription in AOA2-relevant human cells and in chronic disease settings.
main_caveats: DNA indel status and SETX protein loss were not measured; 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
summary: Setx produced a uniform measured transcriptional null: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 across 22 tested neuronal groups and 371796 downstream gene-group tests.
why_it_matters: The dominant screen phenotype is the absence of an acute steady-state mRNA program, not a restricted positive pathway. The flat Setx self-transcript does not prove failed editing because weak mRNA knockdown is expected in this CRISPR-indel design.

literature_claim: SETX loss can cause R-loop-associated DNA damage, autophagy impairment, proteostasis defects, micronucleus/cGAS inflammation, and ALS4-linked TGFbeta changes in stressed or disease systems.
main_caveats: The screen cannot measure R-loops, protein aggregation, or autophagic flux directly; cGAS markers were tested only through neuronal nuclear transcripts that were represented in the DE table.
summary: No Setx-tested neuronal group activated the expected DDR, ISR/UPR, interferon, autophagy/mitophagy, proteostasis, or Bambi/TGFbeta marker programs at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: R-loop and autophagy defects can generate stress transcription in other SETX-deficient systems, so their absence here localizes the acute postmitotic phenotype away from a strong secondary stress state.

literature_claim: ALS4 SETX pathology can intersect TDP-43 localization, and MATR3 is an ALS-linked RNA/DNA-binding protein that interacts with TDP-43.
main_caveats: The comparison is at the level of gene-level DE counts; Setx has no FDR genes, so there is no responder signature for a shared-direction overlap test.
summary: Setx did not phenocopy the ALS/RNA-binding targets Tardbp or Matr3, which generated hundreds of FDR-scale downstream genes in the same screen.
why_it_matters: This keeps a related-target divergence as first-class biology: acute loss of a ubiquitous ALS-linked nuclear RNA factor can be highly visible in this dataset, but SETX is buffered or displaced from the steady-state mRNA axis.

literature_claim: Dominant ALS4 SETX mutations are linked to reduced R-loops, reduced BAMBI and activated TGFbeta signaling, whereas recessive SETX loss causes AOA2.
main_caveats: The screen did not introduce ALS4 missense alleles and did not assay promoter R-loops or TDP-43 localization.
summary: The Setx LoF surface did not reproduce the dominant ALS4 Bambi/TGFbeta or TDP-43-linked axis.
why_it_matters: A sparse CRISPR loss-of-function result should not be used as evidence that reducing all SETX activity models, or fails to model, ALS4 dominant alleles; those alleles can act through mutation-specific R-loop redistribution and TDP-43 localization phenotypes.

literature_claim: SGCD is a sarcoglycan/DGC component with mouse annotations in sarcolemmal, calcium, cardiac, and muscle biology, whereas PORCN controls Wnt acylation and SIK2 belongs to a kinase family that regulates CRTC/CREB and class IIa HDAC transcriptional outputs.
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes pass FDR<0.10, both at borderline FDR values; the target indel rate was not measured.
summary: Acute Sgcd loss produced a very small, cell-class-restricted response: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut only Sik2 and Porcn increased at FDR<0.10, while every other measured group had zero downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The responder is thalamic and transcriptionally Wnt/kinase-like rather than sarcolemmal, so the screen does not recover the canonical skeletal-muscle or cardiomyopathy SGCD program.

literature_claim: The DGC contains dystroglycan, sarcoglycan, dystrophin, dystrobrevin, and syntrophin subcomplexes, and brain DGC-like assemblies contain dystrophin, dystroglycan, Dp71, syntrophins, and epsilon/delta/zeta sarcoglycans.
main_caveats: Alpha-, beta-, gamma-, zeta-sarcoglycan, dystrobrevin, beta-syntrophin, utrophin, sarcospan, and laminins were not represented as perturbation targets, so the measured contrast covers only the related targets present in the parquet.
summary: Sgcd did not behave like an acute neuronal knockdown of the core DGC or related sarcoglycan/ECM receptors: Dmd, Dag1, Snta1, Sgce, Itga7, and Itgb1 each had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and did not reproduce Sik2 or Porcn in 151 TH.
why_it_matters: Delta-sarcoglycan's two-gene thalamic signature should not be read as generic DGC collapse; matched same-pathway perturbations were flatter than Sgcd in this neuronal assay.

literature_claim: TPR is a nuclear-pore basket protein and UBA5 is the UFM1 E1-like activating enzyme; no prior SGCD-TPR-UBA5 relationship was used to nominate them.
main_caveats: The Sgcd seed contains only two genes; Tpr and Uba5 share only the opposite Porcn direction robustly, while Sik2 is not FDR-significant in those comparators.
summary: Data-driven Sgcd-neighbor searches did not reveal a robust positive phenocopy, but they placed the Sgcd Porcn increase opposite Tpr and Uba5 perturbations, which strongly downregulated Porcn in the same 151 TH class.
why_it_matters: This preserves the non-textbook comparator result: Sgcd sits outside the broad nuclear-pore/UFMylation stress signatures that dominate Tpr and Uba5 in 151 TH, rather than converging with them.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The 215 MB Dopa group had no Sgce rows; DNA indels and epsilon-sarcoglycan protein loss were not measured, and NeuN enrichment undersampled non-neuronal compartments.
summary: Sgce was transcriptomically silent by FDR in every measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: This is a strong negative result for persistent postmitotic cell-state conversion after sparse CRISPR Sgce loss of function: the screen measured the target transcript in 22 groups and found zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite 25-199 perturbed nuclei per group.

literature_claim: Ubiquitous and brain-specific epsilon-sarcoglycan isoforms copurify from brain with delta-sarcoglycan, beta-dystroglycan, and dystrophin Dp71, and brain epsilon/zeta sarcoglycan can be partly preserved independently of the beta/delta sarcoglycan core.
main_caveats: Only Sgcd, Dag1, and Dmd among the obvious DGC neighbors were perturbation targets; Sgcd had two isolated thalamic DE genes that Sgce did not share.
summary: Sgce did not join a coherent dystrophin/sarcoglycan-complex transcriptomic module.
why_it_matters: Epsilon-sarcoglycan is a brain dystrophin-associated protein, but directly measured DGC neighbors were either fully flat or nearly flat, and their whole-surface correlations with Sgce were essentially zero rather than a shared same-complex signature.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Several myoclonus-dystonia SGCE missense mutants are retained in the ER, ubiquitinated, and degraded by the proteasome, without evidence for a dominant-negative block of wild-type epsilon-sarcoglycan trafficking.
main_caveats: The screen assayed LoF gRNAs, not patient missense alleles; absence of a UPR in nuclei does not exclude acute protein handling below FDR detection.
summary: A clean Sgce CRISPR LoF did not induce ERAD, UPR, autophagy, or sarcoglycan-transcript compensation.
why_it_matters: The proteostatic branch of SGCE biology is allele-specific: ER-retained missense proteins are ubiquitinated and degraded, whereas this frameshift-style LoF readout produced no corrected nuclear Hspa5/Atf4/Ddit3/Xbp1/Herpud1/Sel1l/Sqstm1 response and no DGC-gene compensation.

main_caveats: The similarity calculation used all matched Wilcoxon score entries, so it can rank very small random correlations when the query signature itself has zero FDR-significant genes.
summary: The unbiased nearest neighbors of Sgce were rank-order noise, not a biological convergence class.
why_it_matters: The two highest correlations belonged to Safe_target controls and the strongest gene targets, Rax and Syngap1, correlated only r=0.036-0.037; the strongest anticorrelations, Dock3 and Crebbp, were only r=-0.027 and r=-0.025. Thus there is no hidden cross-perturbation module to rescue a nominal Sgce phenotype.

literature_claim: ADCY5, PRKCG, RELN, TOR1A, and additional genes are listed as genetic differential diagnoses for SGCE myoclonus-dystonia, reflecting phenotypic rather than necessarily molecular similarity.
main_caveats: This is a restricted, negative cross-perturbation comparison and many differential-diagnosis genes, including Tor1a and Kctd17, were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Represented myoclonus-dystonia differential genes also failed to form an Sgce-like nuclear state.
why_it_matters: ADCY5, RELN, NKX2-1, and PRKCG perturbations were measurable in the parquet, but ADCY5 had zero FDR<0.10 genes and the others had only isolated single-gene events, matching the idea that clinically overlapping dystonias need not converge on one juvenile snRNA program.

literature_claim: SH3KBP1/CIN85 is an endocytic and signaling adaptor rather than a known Apmap transcriptional regulator.
main_caveats: Single FDR<0.10 downstream gene from 58 perturbed nuclei; no broader APMAP pathway can be inferred from nominal genes.
summary: Sh3kbp1 LoF produced one robust downstream event, Apmap up-regulation, confined to 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
why_it_matters: A target best known as an endocytic adaptor did not trigger a broad postnatal neuronal stress or synaptic transcriptional program; the only BH-controlled response was a precise MH-LH/thalamic glutamatergic Apmap increase.

literature_claim: APMAP is brain-expressed, interacts with gamma-secretase/APP-processing machinery, and its interactome includes autophagy-lysosome modulators.
main_caveats: The dataset measures Apmap mRNA only; it does not measure APP processing, gamma-secretase activity, APMAP protein, or amyloid-beta.
summary: Apmap is a hypothesis-generating positive marker of the Sh3kbp1 response in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
why_it_matters: APMAP has independent brain biology at APP/gamma-secretase and autophagy-lysosome interfaces, so its selective rise after Sh3kbp1 loss nominates a membrane-protein processing readout to validate by protein or imaging assays.

literature_claim: CIN85 binds CBL/CBLB and endophilins to regulate ligand-induced EGFR/MET endocytosis, and CD2AP is a related adaptor.
main_caveats: EGFR, CBL, CBLC, SH3GL1/2/3, DAB2, DNM2, and DNM3 were not target perturbations represented in the parquet, so only Cblb, Cd2ap, Cltc, Dnm1, and Synj1 were directly scored.
summary: Sh3kbp1, Cblb, and Cd2ap were flat while Cltc generated broad DE, separating receptor-specific CIN85 family scaffolding from core clathrin disruption.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation contrast argues that an absence of Sh3kbp1 DE is not because the screen cannot ever detect endocytic damage; it specifically fails to see the CBL/CIN85/CD2AP adaptor tier under basal postmitotic neuronal conditions.

literature_claim: No literature comparator was being tested in this data-driven neighbor calculation.
main_caveats: Correlation was calculated on mostly null signed Wilcoxon scores; therefore it is useful mainly for rejecting strong convergence.
summary: The Sh3kbp1 vector had no robust positive or negative signature neighbor in the full model-visible target universe.
why_it_matters: Top genome-wide signed-score neighbors were all near zero and did not recapitulate Apmap in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, making the focal Apmap hit target-specific rather than part of a reusable multi-target module.

literature_claim: CIN85 loss impairs dopamine-stimulated D2 receptor endocytosis in striatal neurons and BCR-induced NF-kB/CD86 signaling in B cells.
main_caveats: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA is a broad GABAergic aggregate, not purified Drd2-positive striatopallidal medium spiny neurons, and protein trafficking was not assayed.
summary: The expected D2-receptor and BCR/NF-kB outputs were absent from neuronal Sh3kbp1 nuclei.
why_it_matters: SH3KBP1 biology recovered in whole animals and B cells is displaced toward receptor trafficking, dopamine-stimulated striatal physiology, and antibody-lineage activation rather than a juvenile pan-neuronal mRNA program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Germline Shank2 loss causes strong synaptic, NMDAR, and behavioral phenotypes in mice.
main_caveats: DNA indels and SHANK2 protein loss were not measured; absence of RNA DE does not exclude local PSD dysfunction.
summary: Shank2 mRNA decreased in the expected direction across the measured surface but acute P16 Shank2 perturbation produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 22 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: A significant self-transcript decrease in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut without downstream DE separates target-RNA perturbation from a nuclear transcriptional response and argues for buffering under this sparse postmitotic design.

literature_claim: SHANK scaffolds organize PSD-95/GKAP, Homer, mGluR, and NMDAR-associated complexes and Shank2 mouse models perturb NMDAR/ionotropic glutamate receptor physiology.
main_caveats: The queried genes test mRNA abundance only; PSD protein localization and receptor currents were not measured.
summary: The canonical SHANK-Homer-GKAP-NMDA/mGluR mRNA panel was entirely absent from the Shank2 downstream surface.
why_it_matters: The expected disease pathway was not recovered as altered transcript abundance, refining the readout to local synaptic protein organization rather than Grin, Gria, Grm, Homer, Dlg, or Shank-family mRNA compensation.

literature_claim: Shank scaffolds are coupled to NMDAR-associated PSD complexes and Shank2-mutant phenotypes can be improved by restoring NMDAR function.
main_caveats: Cross-perturbation contrast is transcriptional; receptor currents after Shank2 sgRNAs were not assayed.
summary: NMDAR subunit perturbations produced activity-linked transcriptomic signatures in matched groups where Shank2 was flat.
why_it_matters: The dataset could detect glutamatergic receptor perturbation responses, so Shank2's null is a specific scaffold-versus-receptor divergence rather than a blanket failure to recover excitatory-synapse biology.

literature_claim: Shank family and PSD-associated proteins participate in interrelated postsynaptic assemblies, and combined Shank2/Shank3 loss can reveal stronger phenotypes than single perturbations.
main_caveats: Shank1, Homer1, Homer3, Dlgap1, Dlgap2, and Dlgap3 were not represented as perturbation targets and pairwise or double Shank perturbations were not tested.
summary: The closest represented PSD scaffolds and synaptic adhesion genes did not converge on a common Shank2-like transcriptional phenotype.
why_it_matters: Shank2, Shank3, Dlg4, Dlgap4, Homer2, Nrxn and Nlgn3 perturbations were separable or weak despite being literature-near synaptic targets; this argues against replacing missing Shank2 RNA biology with a generic PSD signature.

main_caveats: Correlation used genome-wide Wilcoxon scores and is dominated by a flat Shank2 profile; it does not test protein-level convergence.
summary: The unbiased all-target neighbor search found only near-zero positive and negative correlations with Shank2.
why_it_matters: With maximum absolute correlation only 0.032 across the full signed-score surface, none of the data-driven neighbors should be treated as a hidden Shank2 module.

literature_claim: SHANK3 loss is expected to perturb excitatory synapse organization and striatal or hippocampal physiology in mouse models, with adult re-expression able to rescue selected synaptic and behavioral phenotypes.
main_caveats: The two downstream genes are singletons; DNA indel rates and SHANK3 protein occupancy at synapses were not measured.
summary: The Shank3 transcriptional response was essentially a two-cell-group, two-singleton surface: Uba5 up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Zfp810 up in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with no other downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 20 measured groups.
why_it_matters: SHANK3 is a potent synaptic disease gene, so this result refines the acute postmitotic phenotype: in this sparse CRISPR snRNA assay, loss rarely propagates into a cell-autonomous nuclear program.

literature_claim: UBA5 encodes the E1-like enzyme that activates the ubiquitin-like modifier UFM1.
main_caveats: Single-gene event; Ufm1, Ufc1, Ufl1, and Ddrgk1 were not significant under Shank3 in this cell group.
summary: Uba5 was the only downstream Shank3 DEG in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and was up-regulated.
why_it_matters: UBA5 initiates UFM1 conjugation, so this singleton nominates a proteostasis-adjacent response to Shank3 loss in thalamic excitatory neurons without proving a full UFMylation program.

literature_claim: Zfp810 is annotated as a mouse protein-coding zinc finger protein gene, with no established connection to SHANK3 biology.
main_caveats: Only 57 perturbed cells supported this FDR<0.10 call, and the target transcript itself was flat in the same cell group.
summary: Zfp810 was the only downstream Shank3 DEG in 217 P MY Pineal Glut and the only Zfp810 hit among 1306 targets tested in that group.
why_it_matters: The response is highly specific within the measured target universe but currently points to an unconnected zinc-finger gene rather than a named SHANK3 pathway.

literature_claim: SHANK proteins organize Homer/GKAP/PSD-95 assemblies and Shank3 mutant striatal synaptosomes show altered Homer1b/c and AMPAR subunit protein abundance.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot test receptor localization, PSD stoichiometry, dendritic spine morphology, or synaptic currents directly.
summary: Shank3 loss did not significantly move the core postsynaptic scaffold, AMPAR, NMDAR, mGluR, neurexin-neuroligin, Fmr1, or Cyfip1 transcripts in any measured Shank3 cell group.
why_it_matters: The expected synaptic biology was therefore absent at the mRNA level, arguing that the acute phenotype is not a simple transcriptional relabeling of the PSD protein complex.

main_caveats: Neighbor computation used signed Wilcoxon score vectors because raw log-fold changes for nonsignificant sparse genes contain large dropout-driven values.
summary: The pre-literature score-vector neighbors of Shank3 had absolute correlations below 0.03 and did not share the Uba5 or Zfp810 singleton hits.
why_it_matters: The nearest neighbors are best interpreted as a near-null background check, not as a convergent Shank3 module.

literature_claim: SHANK family proteins cooperate with Homer and GKAP/DLGAP scaffolds at glutamatergic postsynapses, and Shank2/3 double knockout can uncover cortical-region phenotypes.
main_caveats: Only Dlgap4, not Dlgap1-3, was represented among DLGAP targets; overall comparator response magnitudes were small.
summary: Literature-obvious PSD partners did not phenocopy Shank3: Shank2, Dlg4, Homer2, Grm5, Nlgn3, Nrxn1/2/3, Fmr1, Cyfip1, Gria1/2, Grm1, and Syngap1 were flat or nearly flat, whereas Dlgap4 produced its own 10-gene response in L5 ET, CNU-LGE, and thalamic glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: Membership in the postsynaptic scaffold is not sufficient for interchangeable acute transcriptional effects; a SAPAP/DLGAP perturbation can be visible where Shank3 is not.

literature_claim: Shank3 mutant mice show altered NMDA/AMPA physiology and region-specific regulation of AMPAR subunit localization and NMDAR function.
main_caveats: This is a cross-target contrast, not evidence that Shank3 leaves NMDAR currents unchanged.
summary: Direct NMDAR-subunit perturbations were readily detected but diverged from Shank3, with Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b producing tens to hundreds of DEGs where Shank3 had zero or one.
why_it_matters: The absence of an NMDAR/AMPAR mRNA program under Shank3 is not because this screen cannot detect glutamate-receptor perturbations; it is specific to losing the downstream scaffold in this acute context.

literature_claim: SHOC2 is a positive RAF/ERK scaffold and VGF is induced by neurotrophin signaling in neurons.
main_caveats: Single downstream gene; no DNA indel or pERK measurement.
summary: Shoc2 loss produced a single robust downstream DEG, Vgf down-regulation, restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The result shows that acute postmitotic Shoc2 loss can reach a neurotrophin-responsive neuropeptide precursor, but only in one thalamic class in this dataset.

literature_claim: BRAF and MEK1 lie downstream of SHOC2-regulated RAF activation, and TrkB can couple neurotrophin input to ERK-regulated VGF expression.
main_caveats: The shared FDR-level overlap with Shoc2 is Vgf only; Ptpn5, Unc13a, Etv5, and Atp2a2 support Braf/Map2k1/Ntrk2 but are subthreshold in Shoc2 cells.
summary: Braf, Map2k1, and Ntrk2 converged with Shoc2 on Vgf down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Uba5 drove Vgf in the opposite direction.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation recurrence makes the solitary Shoc2 Vgf hit more biologically credible and aligns it with RAF-MEK and neurotrophin signaling rather than nonspecific neuronal stress.

literature_claim: SHOC2 and multiple assayed targets are members of the RAS/MAPK or Noonan-syndrome gene network.
main_caveats: MRAS, PP1 catalytic subunits, SCRIB, ARAF, MAPK3, NRAS, NF1, KSR1, and KSR2 were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Most measurable RASopathy and RAS-MAPK relatives did not phenocopy the Shoc2 thalamic Vgf response.
why_it_matters: The result rejects a blanket same-pathway expectation and refines the active postmitotic Shoc2 output to a BRAF/MEK1-like branch in this assay.

literature_claim: SHOC2 affects RAF/ERK dynamics, which can regulate immediate-early and ERK-feedback transcription.
main_caveats: The assay was not stimulated immediately before harvest, so lack of IEG induction does not exclude stimulus-evoked pERK defects.
summary: Shoc2 did not recover a broad canonical ERK immediate-early or feedback transcriptional program at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The Vgf hit should be interpreted as a narrow biomarker of reduced trophic/ERK tone, not evidence that basal ERK signaling collapsed across thousands of genes at harvest.

literature_claim: SHOC2 depletion is a candidate strategy to sensitize RAS-driven cancers to MEK inhibition, and VGF is coupled to neurotrophin-dependent neuronal plasticity.
main_caveats: Single-cell mouse CRISPR data do not establish drug exposure, reversibility, behavior, or human CNS toxicity.
summary: The only neuronal Shoc2 LoF signal, Vgf down-regulation, is aligned with Braf and Map2k1 suppression and therefore flags a focused CNS pharmacodynamic endpoint for SHOC2-axis inhibitors.
why_it_matters: SHOC2 is therapeutically attractive in RAS-driven cancers; if inhibitors reach brain, VGF/neurotrophin outputs may be a more sensitive neuronal readout than a broad stress signature.

literature_claim: No literature claim is needed for the measured pan-null itself.
main_caveats: CRISPR engagement was inferred only from the mRNA-level guide effect and remains unmeasured at the DNA/protein level; absence is limited to basal P16-to-P37-44 neuronal nuclei.
summary: Sigmar1 loss was a pan-cell-type nuclear-transcriptome null across all 23 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The null is not a missing-data artifact: every taxonomy group had Sigmar1 rows, on-target transcript values, and genome-wide downstream tests, yet no cell group produced a gene at FDR<0.10.

literature_claim: Sigma-1 receptor loss or inhibition can destabilize IP3R/MAM calcium signaling and can be accompanied by IRE1-XBP1, ER-stress, mitochondrial-dynamics/transport, and autophagy phenotypes in stressed cells and motor-neuron models.
main_caveats: The assay does not measure MAM contact geometry, calcium flux, XBP1 splicing, autophagic flux, or mitochondrial transport directly; it rules out a robust accompanying nuclear mRNA program in the sampled nuclei.
summary: Sigmar1 perturbation did not recruit the UPR/ISR, ER-mitochondria calcium, mitochondrial-dynamics, or autophagy/lysosomal transcriptional programs that are the canonical secondary readouts of strong sigma-1-receptor loss.
why_it_matters: The expected stress genes were directly present in the ranked surfaces and had no FDR<0.10 signal, so the result is a biological uncoupling in this in-vivo postnatal brain context rather than merely a failure to name the right genes.

literature_claim: Sigma-1 receptor interacts functionally with ER chaperone and IRE1/IP3R stress pathways at the mitochondria-associated ER membrane.
main_caveats: Comparator coverage was not complete for every target and Hspa5 had only 24 total FDR genes; this is a restricted cross-perturbation contrast, not a protein-interaction assay.
summary: ER-stress and MAM-neighbor perturbations were themselves mostly buffered, while the one responsive chaperone node, Hspa5, produced a thalamic ER-proteostasis signature that Sigmar1 did not share.
why_it_matters: The expected HSPA5/BiP-IRE1-IP3R neighborhood is not a single interchangeable transcriptomic module under basal sparse CRISPR in brain neurons: Atf6, Itpr1, Bcl2, and Eif2ak4 were flat, Hspa5 was modestly active in a subset of groups, and Sigmar1 was flat in all groups.

literature_claim: Sigmar1-dependent motor-neuron degeneration has been tied to mitochondrial dynamics or transport, ER stress, MAM integrity, and autophagy changes.
main_caveats: Opa1 and Tsc2 are pathway-level comparators rather than sigma-1-receptor complex members, and their signatures are alternative perturbations, not downstream markers of Sigmar1 activity.
summary: Opa1 and Tsc2 elicited broad ISR, amino-acid, sterol, lysosomal, and neuronal-remodeling signatures in matched groups where Sigmar1 remained silent.
why_it_matters: If Sigmar1 loss had collapsed mitochondrial homeostasis or mTOR-autophagy signaling strongly in these nuclei, the screen could register such programs; robust Opa1 and Tsc2 responses show that the absence after Sigmar1 is pathway specific.

literature_claim: SIGMAR1, TARDBP/TDP-43, MATR3, ATXN2, HNRNPA-family genes, VCP, KIF5A, and SETX are ALS or motor-neuron-disease genes, with RNA-binding proteins forming a prominent ALS/FTD mechanistic class.
main_caveats: Disease-family membership alone does not predict identical transcriptional signatures; spinal motor neurons and chronic degeneration were not sampled.
summary: Sigmar1 did not phenocopy broad ALS/FTD RNA-binding-protein perturbations even though Tardbp and Matr3 were strong responders in the same thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: SIGMAR1 belongs to a motor-neuron disease genetics landscape, but acute Sigmar1 loss in brain neurons did not converge with the large Tardbp/Matr3 RNA-processing signatures; this separates MAM/calcium Sigmar1 disease biology from generic ALS RNA-binding-protein transcriptional injury in this assay.

literature_claim: No prior literature claim nominated Tmem126a or Mff as close Sigmar1 co-perturbation neighbors.
main_caveats: The neighbor calculation used a flat Sigmar1 Wilcoxon-score vector, so the numerical ranks are exploratory and should not be interpreted as pathway membership.
summary: Sigmar1 lacked a meaningful high-dimensional signature neighborhood: its top positive and negative data-driven neighbors had near-zero correlations and no robust downstream signatures themselves.
why_it_matters: The pre-literature neighbor search did not reveal a hidden convergent module; any mechanistic interpretation therefore rests on expected programs being absent rather than on a weak but coherent alternative set of co-responding perturbations.

literature_claim: No SIL1/BiP-loss literature tested here predicts isolated Rsrp1 induction; RSRP1 is annotated as a nuclear spliceosomal-complex-assembly gene.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene passed FDR<0.10, the logFC was small, and no RNA-splicing program should be inferred from additional subthreshold genes.
summary: Sil1 produced a one-gene FDR<0.10 response: Rsrp1 was up only in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The target's measurable postnatal transcriptional footprint is not a canonical ER-stress wave; it is a sharply restricted, weak RNA-processing hit that should be treated as a hypothesis rather than a full pathway activation.

literature_claim: Sil1 deficiency perturbs BiP nucleotide exchange and, in woozy/Sil1-null mice, UPR markers, protein aggregates, autophagosomes, and Purkinje-cell death are the expected downstream biology.
main_caveats: The assay measured whole-transcriptome nuclear RNA, not Xbp1 splicing, ATF6 cleavage, eIF2α phosphorylation, protein aggregates, or neuron abundance; however, chaperone-stress mRNAs were detectable after other perturbations.
summary: Acute Sil1 loss was uncoupled from the expected BiP/UPR, ERAD, and autophagy transcriptional programs across all measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Mouse and human SIL1 biology would nominate Hspa5/BiP, Hyou1/GRP170, Ddit3/CHOP, Xbp1-axis, protein-quality-control and autophagy genes; none became FDR-supported after P16 sparse Sil1 perturbation, so the main result is a buffered ER-proteostasis phenotype, not a missed single marker.

literature_claim: HSPA5/BiP is the ER HSP70 that uses nucleotide-exchange factors SIL1 and GRP170 and ERdj co-chaperones; HYOU1/GRP170 modifies Sil1-null neurodegeneration.
main_caveats: The Hspa5/Sec63/Manf responses occur in selected cell groups and are cross-perturbation inference rather than double knockout of Sil1 with Hyou1.
summary: The same dataset detects a BiP/UPR-like module after Hspa5, Sec63, and Manf perturbation, but Sil1 does not join that module.
why_it_matters: This rejects a generic readout failure: Hspa5 and Sec63 perturbations converged on Hsp90b1/Pdia4 or Hspa5/Hyou1 induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Sil1 had zero FDR genes there despite more perturbed nuclei.

main_caveats: Neighbor computation used Wilcoxon-score correlations over all matched measured genes; a different restricted or pathway-weighted metric could rank weak null signatures differently, but would not create shared FDR-supported genes here.
summary: Phenotype-first nearest neighbors of Sil1 were essentially random and were rejected by FDR overlap.
why_it_matters: The maximum positive and negative score correlations had |r|≤0.050, and neither biologic nor safe-target neighbors reproduced the L5 ET Rsrp1 hit; therefore there is no latent multi-target Sil1-like transcriptomic module to overinterpret.

literature_claim: Prior work established embryonic cortical and postnatal hippocampal roles for Sin3a, but did not predict this thalamic-midbrain-Pvalb-biased basal response after P16 sparse CRISPR.
main_caveats: Cell groups are coarse; responder strength partly tracks perturbed-cell count, although several low-count groups still produced FDR-supported genes.
summary: Sin3a loss produced a broad but selective P16 neuronal response, with 3761 downstream FDR<0.10 calls across 14 of 21 measured cell groups and the dominant burden in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
why_it_matters: The result localizes the acute postmitotic response to particular thalamic, midbrain, and Pvalb populations rather than uniformly across all Sin3a-expressing neurons.

direction: up; convergent with proteasome loss signatures
literature_claim: Psmc1-dependent 26S proteasome activity is required for neuronal homeostasis, and ERAD is coupled to proteasome-mediated protein quality control.
main_caveats: ER stress was inferred from snRNA-seq target genes rather than direct protein-folding or proteasome-activity assays.
summary: A recurrent ER protein-quality-control program was induced by Sin3a and was most similar to proteasome-subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4.
why_it_matters: This converts a chromatin-scaffold perturbation into a proteostasis phenotype and warns that postnatal SIN3A inhibition can engage stress pathways in neurons.

literature_claim: SRRM2 is a nuclear-speckle scaffold needed for alternative-splicing organization.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq reports transcript levels, not splice-isoform changes; the finding nominates an RNA-processing state but does not prove altered splicing.
summary: Sin3a loss repeatedly down-regulated nuclear-speckle and splicing factors, including Srrm2, Pnisr, Ddx17, Srsf5, Srsf6, Rnpc3, Snrnp70, and Leng8.
why_it_matters: A repressor scaffold generated a sizable negative RNA-processing arm, so the downstream network cannot be interpreted as simple direct derepression of SIN3A targets.

literature_claim: CYP46A1 is the neuronal cholesterol 24-hydroxylase that controls a major route of brain cholesterol turnover.
main_caveats: The module mixes several metabolic branches; metabolite and sterol flux were not measured.
summary: Sin3a responders induced a lipid, cholesterol, mitochondrial, and redox metabolic arm marked by Cyp46a1, Mboat7, Gcdh, Pcx, Acly, Cyb5r3, Qdpr, Aldh6a1, and Gsto1.
why_it_matters: The recurrent Cyp46a1 up-regulation links Sin3a loss to neuronal sterol turnover, a key neuronal homeostatic process outside the canonical SIN3/HDAC complex.

literature_claim: Progranulin has established links to lysosomal function and neural homeostasis.
main_caveats: Lysosomal transcript induction could reflect adaptation to stress rather than direct control by SIN3A.
summary: An endolysosomal clearance branch rose in broad Sin3a responders, including Grn, Pld3, Dpp7, Hdac6, Tmem9, Mcoln1, and Wipi1.
why_it_matters: Together with ERAD induction and proteasome-neighbor convergence, lysosomal gene induction points to a broader protein/organelle-clearance response after Sin3a loss.

literature_claim: Primary cilia act as signaling organelles in brain development and neuronal function.
main_caveats: The evidence is transcriptional only; cilium number, morphology, and signaling were not measured.
summary: Sin3a loss induced a ciliary and basal-body transcript module, with Odf2 up in 12 responder groups and recurrent increases of Alms1, Ift57, Dzip1, Cep192, Cep152, Cfap69, and Dnah9.
why_it_matters: Primary-cilium and centrosome genes were not the textbook SIN3A readout, yet they were among the most recurrent positive transcripts, suggesting a postmitotic signaling-organelle remodeling axis.

literature_claim: Postnatal neuronal Sin3a deletion increases Homer1 and changes mGluR1α/mGluR5-dependent hippocampal plasticity.
main_caveats: The assay sampled basal transcriptomes rather than learning-evoked CA1 physiology.
summary: The prior Homer1/mGluR hippocampal program was only partly recovered: Homer1 rose in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic responders, Grm1 but not Grm5 was significant, and CA3/CA2-FC/DG was weak.
why_it_matters: This refines the postnatal SIN3A plasticity model by showing that the basal P16 whole-brain response is not a uniform reproduction of the CA1 Homer1/mGluR5 phenotype.

literature_claim: In-utero Sin3a knockdown altered cortical progenitor abundance, Brn2-marked identity, and callosal axon elongation.
main_caveats: The postmitotic remodeling interpretation is inferred from transcript markers and not from axon morphology.
summary: Embryonic cortical layer and progenitor targets were absent, while axon-guidance, adhesion, and actin-remodeling genes were induced after P16 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The P16 screen preserves a structural-remodeling echo of Sin3a cortical biology but shows that the acute postmitotic response is shifted away from progenitor proliferation and Brn2/Ctip2 identity shifts.

literature_claim: SIN3A and SIN3B are paralogous SIN3/HDAC complex scaffolds and SIN3B haploinsufficiency also causes an ID/ASD syndrome.
main_caveats: Sin3b was not present as a perturbation target, so compensation was observed only at the downstream transcript level.
summary: Sin3a perturbation weakly induced its paralog Sin3b and several Sin3-associated corepressor transcripts in the strongest cell groups.
why_it_matters: The feedback suggests neurons sense SIN3A-complex disruption, but the small and restricted induction is insufficient to buffer thousands of downstream DE genes in the same groups.

literature_claim: SIN3A is recruited by REST during neuronal-gene silencing in pluripotent cells and interacts with MeCP2 in cortical disease biology.
main_caveats: REST may be too low or inactive in these postmitotic neurons; the screen tests perturbation of each gene separately, not biochemical complex occupancy.
summary: The literature-obvious recruiter perturbations Rest and Mecp2 did not converge with Sin3a in the measured postnatal neurons.
why_it_matters: This isolates the P16 Sin3a response from REST-mediated neural induction and from a simple MeCP2-SIN3A equivalence, forcing interpretation toward other SIN3A-containing assemblies or indirect homeostatic stress.

literature_claim: BAP1, KDM5C, and ZMYND8 encode chromatin regulators with deubiquitinase, H3K4-demethylase, or chromatin-reader functions.
main_caveats: The anti-neighbor call is based on a restricted score-vector metric; FDR-overlap counts were small for these comparators.
summary: Bap1, Kdm5c, and Zmynd8 were the three strongest negative Sin3a restricted-signature neighbors.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that broad chromatin regulators in the same neuronal CRISPR assay can oppose, rather than phenocopy, the Sin3a basal stress/remodeling state.

main_caveats: The assay measures nuclear RNA 3-4 weeks after P16 mosaic CRISPR and does not measure DNA indels, Rap-GTP loading, protein localization, or spine morphology.
summary: Sipa1l3 loss-of-function produced no robust whole-transcriptome response in any recovered neuronal cell group.
why_it_matters: This establishes a broad postnatal neuronal transcriptional null rather than a cell-type-restricted positive response; the largest near-threshold signals, Ccnl1 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and Ccny in 052 Pvalb Gaba, still missed the prespecified FDR<0.10 cutoff.

literature_claim: SIPA1L3 variants or depletion disrupt lens/eye development, epithelial polarity and cytoskeletal organization, and Epha4-Sipa1l3 loss up-regulates the Wnt target axin2 while reducing rax and pax6 in embryonic Xenopus eye assays.
main_caveats: The tested tissue excludes lens and most retina; absence of Axin2/Rax/Pax6 activation here should not be read against embryonic ocular morphogenesis.
summary: The embryonic SIPA1L3 eye-development/Wnt program was absent from postmitotic P16 brain neurons.
why_it_matters: Human and vertebrate disease work points to lens epithelial polarity and Epha4-Sipa1l3 control of Wnt, Axin2, Rax, and Pax6 during embryonic eye formation; none of those transcripts moved after Sipa1l3 perturbation in recovered brain neurons, sharpening cataract biology as an early ocular-lineage mechanism rather than a generic young-neuron transcriptional state.

literature_claim: Sipa1l3/SPAR3 is an excitatory-postsynaptic RapGAP that binds the Fezzin ProSAPiP1/Lzts3, and SPAR-family RapGAPs are linked to PSD-95/NMDA-receptor postsynaptic organization.
main_caveats: Lzts3 and Sipa paralogs were not perturbation targets, and snRNA-seq cannot test RapGAP activity or PSD protein localization directly.
summary: A postsynaptic Sipa1l3 prior did not translate into a PSD transcriptional module in the young adult neuronal nuclei assayed here.
why_it_matters: Sipa1l3/SPAR3 has been localized to excitatory postsynaptic specializations through its C-terminus and Fezzin ProSAPiP1/Lzts3 binding, but Lzts3, Dlg4, Shank3, Syngap1, Rap1a, and Rap1b transcripts were flat downstream of Sipa1l3; Dlg4, Shank2, and Syngap1 perturbations were themselves null, whereas Shank3 produced only two singleton genes. This supports a local protein-organization or electrophysiologic role that is buffered at the cell-body RNA level.

main_caveats: Correlations are computed from mostly sub-threshold ranks because Sipa1l3 had no FDR<0.10 genes.
summary: The unbiased Sipa1l3 signature had no meaningful same-direction or opposite-direction neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The strongest non-safe Pearson correlations on all Wilcoxon-score vectors were only 0.032 and -0.017; Ndufa4, Esrrb, Irf8, Ift81, Tnrc6b and Map1b were also null, demonstrating that Sipa1l3 sits on the background/noise surface rather than in a convergent transcriptional module.

literature_claim: Rodent/vertebrate SIPA proteins form a conserved family with shared RapGAP, PDZ, and C-terminal coiled-coil/leucine-zipper modules.
main_caveats: Transcript-flat paralogs do not exclude protein-level redundancy or compensation by non-SIPA Rap regulators.
summary: There was no transcriptional bounce-back by other measured Sipa-family transcripts.
why_it_matters: Sipa1, Sipa1l1, and Sipa1l2 share the RapGAP-PDZ-C-terminal SPAR domain architecture with Sipa1l3, so paralog induction would have been a plausible RNA-level homeostatic response; all three were present in every recovered Sipa1l3 DE surface with FDR=1.000.

literature_claim: SLC6A6 encodes the sodium- and chloride-dependent taurine/beta-alanine transporter TAUT; it is not a known canonical Six3 embryonic target.
main_caveats: Single downstream gene from 72 perturbed nuclei; the SLC6A6 transporter annotation does not by itself prove a taurine or osmotic stress program.
summary: Six3 loss induced only Slc6a6 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and the edge was unique for Slc6a6 within that cell group across 1742 tested perturbations.
why_it_matters: The result preserves the one FDR-supported positive Six3 phenotype without inflating it into a broad stress pathway; Slc6a6 is a selective hypothesis-generating marker of the postnatal L2/3 Six3 state.

literature_claim: Embryonic Six3 represses anterior Wnt signaling and activates ventral forebrain Shh; human HPE mutations largely act through loss of SIX3 function.
main_caveats: The perturbation was sparse and postmitotic, and DNA indels were not measured; the conclusion is restricted to juvenile neurons, not embryos or retina.
summary: P16 Six3 perturbation failed to move canonical embryonic Wnt/BMP/SHH/FGF sentinels or anterior forebrain/eye transcription factors in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: Six3 is a transcriptional patterning factor, so a real reactivation of its embryonic program should have been visible in snRNA-seq; the absence of Wnt1/Wnt8b/Axin2/Lef1 derepression or Shh loss localizes the textbook SIX3 disease mechanism to an earlier developmental window rather than broad maintenance of specified juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: Six3 belongs to a SIX/homeobox anterior-development network that functionally intersects Wnt, SHH, BMP and eye/forebrain TF programs in embryos.
main_caveats: Score correlations were near zero because Six3 itself was nearly flat; most comparators were also sparse responders in the matched L2/3 group.
summary: Unbiased signature neighbors and represented SIX/homeobox/Wnt-Hh relatives did not converge with the Six3 Slc6a6 signature.
why_it_matters: Testing the comparator surface prevents the single L2/3 Slc6a6 call from being misassigned to a generic L2/3, Wnt, SHH, BMP, FGF or SIX-family module.

literature_claim: Six5 biology is dominated by organogenesis and by lens, spermatogonial, and cardiac-conduction phenotypes rather than by a defined postmitotic neuronal maintenance phenotype.
main_caveats: This is a context-specific transcriptomic negative in P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ brain nuclei; DNA indels and unsampled lens, retina, testis, and heart lineages were not assayed.
summary: Six5 loss of function produced a pan-neuronal transcriptional null: every one of the 23 measured mouse-brain neuronal groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result argues that acute sparse Six5 CRISPR at P16 does not impose a maintenance program on juvenile postmitotic neurons, even though Six5 is a DNA-binding developmental transcription factor.

literature_claim: SIX5 binds the ATP1A1 ARE/MEF3 sequence class and active Six5 can directly activate Igfbp5 in experimental developmental and fibroblast systems.
main_caveats: Only three literature-nominated sentinels were tested here; absence of their mRNA response does not exclude other direct SIX5 targets in lens or mesodermal tissues.
summary: The canonical SIX5/MEF3-ARE target readout was absent: Igfbp5, Atp1a1, and Myog were never FDR-significant after Six5 perturbation.
why_it_matters: A responsive SIX5 transcription-factor knockout should have been visible as altered target mRNA in snRNA-seq; the absence of these genes separates postnatal neurons from the P19, fibroblast, muscle, and promoter-binding contexts in which those targets were nominated.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed over matched Wilcoxon z-score vectors; because Six5 itself was flat, the ranked neighbors should be read as a negative module-discovery result, not as mechanistic partners.
summary: No latent Six5 response module was recovered by cross-perturbation: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score neighbor reached only r=0.0349 and the strongest anti-neighbor only r=-0.0314.
why_it_matters: The Six5 surface is not merely a weak member of a recognizable molecular module; its closest profiles include safe-target controls and nearly flat biological perturbations.

literature_claim: SIX proteins are embryonic developmental regulators that act with Eya coactivators and Dach repressors; Six3/Pax6/Dach1 mark the broader eye/retinal-determination network but are context-specific.
main_caveats: Six3 and Pax6 are not direct Six5 paralog/cofactor substitutes; Six4 and Eya genes were absent from the measured target universe.
summary: Represented SIX/retinal-determination comparators failed to phenocopy or diverge from Six5: Six3, Dach1, and Pax6 all had near-zero correlations with Six5 and no broad DE where Six5 was null.
why_it_matters: The assay directly rejects an active postnatal neuronal SIX/EYA/DACH/PAX eye-development-like module, while also showing that the most obvious missing tests are the same-subfamily Six4 and Eya cofactors that were not recovered as perturbation targets.

literature_claim: Reduced SIX5 expression occurs at the DM1 locus, but Six5-knockout mice chiefly reproduce cataract and other non-neuronal or conduction phenotypes, with Six5 alone not explaining the full multisystem disease.
main_caveats: This screen did not model toxic CUG RNA, splicing defects, multinuclear muscle, heart, eye, or aged tissue; it only tests acute Six5 loss in NeuN-enriched brain nuclei.
summary: Six5 deficiency alone did not elicit a DM1-relevant neuronal transcriptional stress or IGF-target response in young brain neurons.
why_it_matters: This narrows reduced SIX5 dosage toward lens/cardiac/germ-cell arms and away from being sufficient, by itself, to drive a mature neuronal snRNA-seq phenotype.

literature_claim: Ski is an embryonic developmental regulator and a Ski/SnoN-family SMAD corepressor whose loss could have been expected to expose widespread TGF/BMP transcriptional output.
main_caveats: The assay reads surviving NeuN+ nuclei after sparse postnatal indels; DNA editing and SKI protein were not measured.
summary: Ski loss produced a narrow, postmitotic neuronal response: 27 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and 4 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with no FDR-supported downstream gene in the other 21 measured groups.
why_it_matters: The cell-selective surface argues that acute Ski loss is not a pan-neuronal TGF/BMP-SMAD derepression event in this P16-to-P37/44 assay; it is largely an upper-layer cortical IT phenotype with a smaller thalamic echo.

literature_claim: CHD3/NuRD and RFX3 have documented roles in mouse cortical specification and corticothalamic/thalamocortical or cilia-dependent forebrain development, but they had not been placed downstream of postnatal Ski loss.
main_caveats: Only three genes define this interpretive module; the direction is transcript abundance, not direct SKI binding.
summary: The strongest L2/3 IT cortical component was an up-regulated chromatin/RFX module centered on Chd3, Rfx3 and Macroh2a1.
why_it_matters: Ski perturbation did not merely move terminal synaptic markers; it increased regulators with established roles in cortical chromatin remodeling and ciliary/axon-tract development, nominating chromatin-cilia coupling as a postmitotic Ski-sensitive axis in upper-layer IT neurons.

main_caveats: The genes cohere as neuronal adhesion/projection markers but were not validated by morphology or connectivity measurements in this assay.
summary: Ski loss up-regulated an L2/3 IT neuronal adhesion and projection-remodeling gene set including Wscd2, Begain, Igsf11, Dok6, Fat3, Ncam1, Ptprf and Sidt1.
why_it_matters: The most populated portion of the L2/3 signature points to cell-surface and neurite/synaptic remodeling rather than to TGF/BMP immediate-response genes.

main_caveats: This is an RNA signature only; Penk and Chgb decreases were not assayed at peptide or secretion level.
summary: L2/3 IT Ski loss also carried a smaller decreased neuropeptide/secretory arm, with Penk, Chgb and Plk5 reduced while most significant genes were up.
why_it_matters: The mixed-sign response suggests a rebalancing of the L2/3 identity or activity state rather than a single-direction activation program.

main_caveats: Conventional support is FDR-significant but effect sizes are small, with only four genes.
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had a weak but real all-up Ski signature: Cck, L1cam, Spock2 and Ywhah.
why_it_matters: The thalamic response shows that Ski sensitivity is not exclusive to neocortical IT neurons, but its four small logFC hits are qualitatively different from the 27-gene L2/3 cortical program.

literature_claim: Loss of a Ski/SnoN SMAD corepressor can be expected to permit SMAD-dependent TGFβ/BMP target-gene output when ligand-activated receptor-SMAD signaling is present.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure phospho-SMAD occupancy or ligand levels, and SKIL/SnoN was not directly perturbed.
summary: Ski phenotypes were uncoupled from the canonical TGF/BMP receptor-SMAD signature: Id1/2/3/4, Smad7, Serpine1, Cdkn1a, Ccn2, Msx1, Msx2 and Junb never reached FDR<0.10, and 16 represented pathway receptors/SMADs generated only two isolated hits in Ski-responsive cell groups.
why_it_matters: Although SKI is a textbook SMAD corepressor, the postnatal neuronal phenotype is not explained by simple de-repression of tonic TGFβ/BMP target genes or by phenocopy of individual receptor/SMAD loss.

literature_claim: SKI can repress SMAD target output by recruiting transcriptional repressor proteins such as mSin3A and HDAC1.
main_caveats: Only Sin3a itself, not HDAC1 or the full SKI complex, was represented as a perturbation target.
summary: Ski did not phenocopy the represented corepressor neighbor Sin3a: Sin3a had 3761 FDR<0.10 downstream genes across 14 groups and regulated thalamic Spock2 opposite to Ski.
why_it_matters: This rejects a simple model in which postnatal neuronal Ski loss acts as a diluted Sin3A-corepressor loss; SKI's sparse output is a selective regulatory branch, not the broad chromatin-corepressor collapse seen after Sin3a perturbation.

literature_claim: Mib1 is a Notch-ligand E3 ubiquitin ligase with developmental roles in neurogenesis and gliogenesis; a direct postmitotic Ski-Mib1 relationship was not the literature-obvious expectation.
main_caveats: The comparison uses the 31-gene Ski restricted signature and three shared FDR genes; it is a convergence hypothesis, not a biochemical interaction.
summary: The unbiased top positive FDR-backed neighbor of Ski was Mib1, which shared same-direction L2/3 up-regulation of Pde4a, Ptprf and Rfx3.
why_it_matters: The strongest measured convergence emerged from Notch-ligand endocytosis biology rather than from SMAD receptors or SMADs, reinforcing that the observed response is a dataset-nominated L2/3 remodeling module.

literature_claim: GRIN2A and GRIN2B encode regulatory NMDA-receptor subunits whose disruption can cause neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
main_caveats: This is a restricted-signature relationship; only four Ski FDR genes overlap an NMDA-subunit perturbation at FDR<0.10.
summary: Ski's L2/3 program was directionally opposed by Grin2a at Penk, Plch2 and Atp8a2, while Grin2b converged only at Tbkbp1.
why_it_matters: Two NMDA-receptor subunit perturbations bracket the Ski L2/3 signature differently, linking Ski-responsive neurons to excitatory synaptic homeostasis without reducing the phenotype to generic NMDA-receptor loss.

literature_claim: Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome is caused by clustered exon-1 SKI variants, and later biochemical work showed that SGS mutations can stabilize SKI and attenuate TGFβ responses rather than acting as simple nulls.
main_caveats: The screen did not carry patient alleles and did not sample fibroblasts, vascular cells, neural crest, or skeletal tissues.
summary: The P16 neuronal Ski loss-of-function surface does not resemble Shprintzen-Goldberg SKI pathobiology: it lacks canonical neuronal TGFβ/BMP de-repression and is generated in NeuN+ postmitotic lineages rather than the embryonic craniofacial, connective-tissue and vascular contexts emphasized in disease.
why_it_matters: A sparse CRISPR LoF in juvenile neurons is therefore a poor proxy for dominant exon-1 SKI alleles, including alleles that alter SKI stability and phosphorylated-SMAD binding; disease interpretation should focus on allele class, developmental window and non-neuronal lineages.

literature_claim: NKCC1/SLC12A2 is a chloride importer that helps set the developmental NKCC1-to-KCC2 chloride gradient controlling GABA_A polarity.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure DNA indels, chloride flux, or electrophysiology, and the modest on-target mRNA shifts neither prove nor exclude functional knockout in any single nucleus.
summary: Slc12a2 loss of function was a pan-neuronal FDR-level transcriptomic null in this P16-to-P37/44 acute CRISPR screen.
why_it_matters: The result restricts NKCC1 biology in postmitotic young mouse neurons to ion-transport or pre-P16 functions rather than a broad nuclear RNA program: all 23 recovered neuronal classes had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite several well-powered classes.

literature_claim: WNK kinases signal through SPAK/OSR1 to regulate cation-chloride cotransporters, including activation of NKCC1 and reciprocal inhibition of KCC cotransporters.
main_caveats: Only Wnk1, Wnk3, Stk39, Strada, and Prkca were represented; Oxsr1 and the SLC12 paralogs were not tested as perturbation targets.
summary: Represented WNK/SPAK/OSR1/PKC chloride-cotransporter regulators did not converge on a Slc12a2-like program.
why_it_matters: The WNK-SPAK axis is the literature-obvious NKCC1/KCC regulatory module, yet Wnk1, Stk39, and Prkca were also FDR-level nulls, Wnk3 and Strada produced only isolated genes, and their score-vector correlations to Slc12a2 were near zero; the cotransporter phosphorylation pathway is therefore not represented as a shared postnatal neuronal transcriptomic module here.

literature_claim: NKCC1 and KCC2 set the chloride gradient through which GABA_A receptors depolarize immature neurons and hyperpolarize mature neurons.
main_caveats: The GABA_A comparator signatures are small and cell-group restricted, so this is a contrast against detectable receptor-subunit transcriptional consequences, not proof that all GABAergic physiology is absent.
summary: Small GABA_A-receptor activity signatures exist in the same universe, but Slc12a2 does not phenocopy them.
why_it_matters: Gabrb2 and Gabrg2 perturbations elicited restricted immediate-early or neuropeptide responses in thalamic, midbrain, and L4/5 glutamatergic groups, whereas Gabra1, Gabra2, and Slc12a2 were flat; changing the chloride importer at P16 is not equivalent to perturbing major GABA_A receptor subunits at the transcriptome level.

main_caveats: The comparison used full Wilcoxon-score vectors; it is intentionally stringent and no shared FDR-level Slc12a2 genes exist for overlap tests.
summary: A whole-universe signature search found no meaningful Slc12a2 transcriptomic neighbor.
why_it_matters: The nearest Slc12a2 correlations were tiny and included safe-target signatures; top biological neighbors such as Kremen1, Alkbh8, Bmal2, Auh, and Cdin1 had zero or one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, indicating that the apparent neighbors are null-like rank noise rather than hidden pathway convergence.

why_it_matters: The only robust cell-autonomous transcriptional consequence of post-P16 Slc22a17 disruption in this neuronal dataset is an L4/5 IT sterol-enzyme signal, not the broad iron or apoptosis program expected from the canonical LCN2-receptor model.

literature_claim: Rab7 activation controls late-endosomal/lysosomal trafficking and NPC1-dependent cholesterol export.
main_caveats: Rab7 is not a known Slc22a17 complex member and the convergence is one shared gene in one cortical class.

why_it_matters: The convergence connects the otherwise isolated Slc22a17 hit to endolysosomal cholesterol handling, because active Rab7 is a known license for NPC1-dependent lysosomal cholesterol export.

literature_claim: LRP2 is an alternative LCN2 endocytic receptor; SREBF2 activates sterol-biosynthetic genes; TP53 regulates transcription of cell-death genes.

why_it_matters: This separates Slc22a17's L4/5 Msmo1 induction from generic loss of LCN2 endocytosis, transferrin iron uptake, p53 apoptosis, or direct Srebf2 loss.
