main_caveats: Pearson correlations over null signatures are useful only to reject strong convergence; they should not be read mechanistically.
summary: The unbiased whole-surface neighbor search found no interpretable positive or negative Slc52a2 neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top signed Wilcoxon-score correlations were close to zero, and the named neighbors had zero to two FDR<0.10 genes, arguing that the residual Slc52a2 rankings are noise-like rather than a reusable module.

literature_claim: SLC6A1/GAT1 loss reduces GABA reuptake and alters tonic/phasic inhibition in circuits.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation was not measured; a flat Slc6a1 RNA row cannot prove lack of protein loss.
summary: Acute Slc6a1 loss was almost completely transcriptionally buffered: only one downstream gene passed FDR<0.10 across 22 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The dataset mostly tests whether a postmitotic, sparse GAT1 lesion creates a cell-autonomous nuclear compensation program; the answer is no, even in several inhibitory groups with a significant Slc6a1 mRNA decrease.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: YIF1A functions in ER-Golgi recycling and neuronal dendritic membrane delivery, not as an established GAT1-regulated gene.
main_caveats: The adjusted p value was just below 0.10 and no second gene in the same group supported a coherent FDR-level trafficking module.
summary: Yif1a induction in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut was the sole FDR<0.10 downstream event for Slc6a1.
why_it_matters: Yif1a marks a candidate ER-Golgi trafficking response, but it is a single-gene, response-cell-group-restricted signal and should be treated as exploratory rather than as a GAT1 pathway.

literature_claim: GAT1 deficiency primarily perturbs GABA uptake; some pathogenic missense variants additionally impair GAT1 trafficking rather than simply lowering the transcript.
main_caveats: Absence is at snRNA resolution 3-4 weeks after P16 perturbation; earlier or denser perturbations could still drive secondary transcription.
summary: Slc6a1 loss did not induce activity-regulated, GABA-receptor/metabolic, or UPR/ER-stress transcriptional programs.
why_it_matters: The expected GAT1 phenotype is altered extracellular GABA and receptor activation; this screen would have detected a large Fos/Jun/Npas4/Nr4a1-type activity program or an Hspa5/Ddit3/Atf4-type protein-stress program, but neither appeared.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: SLC6A1, GABA receptors, GAD2/SLC32A1, and GABA-transporter paralogs all operate in inhibitory transmission and extracellular GABA handling.
main_caveats: SLC6A11/SLC6A12/SLC6A13 were not perturbation targets, so the strict same-substrate GABA-transporter phenocopy could not be tested.
summary: Literature-obvious GABA and epilepsy comparators did not phenocopy the Slc6a1 Yif1a event, while Gabrb2 and Stxbp1 showed that related neuronal perturbations can be transcriptionally visible in the same universe.
why_it_matters: The Slc6a1 null is target-specific rather than a blanket failure of GABAergic or epilepsy-gene perturbations to register in the assay.

main_caveats: The conclusion is restricted to transcriptomic similarity metrics on weak Slc6a1 vectors; it does not compare electrophysiology.
summary: The pre-literature whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no meaningful positive or negative Slc6a1 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top absolute Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon-score vectors were below 0.026, so the lone Yif1a hit was not embedded in a reproducible cross-target module.

literature_claim: Human SLC6A1 disease variants reduce GAT1 function, and GAT1-deficient mice display extracellular-GABA/receptor physiology phenotypes.
main_caveats: The screen did not measure seizures, tonic inhibition, extracellular GABA, or GAT1 protein at the membrane.
summary: The transcriptional null should not be read as evidence that further GAT1 inhibition is benign in SLC6A1 disease.
why_it_matters: SLC6A1 disorders are driven by reduced GABA uptake/haploinsufficiency, so the assay’s flat nuclear readout is a readout limitation for transporter physiology rather than support for loss-of-function therapy.

direction: Ythdf1, Jun, Stmn4, and Kctd16 up in the two responder groups; no FDR<0.10 down-regulated downstream gene
literature_claim: SLC6A17 is a neuronal synaptic-vesicle neutral amino-acid/glutamine transporter implicated in dendritic-spine, synaptic-vesicle, learning, and intellectual-disability phenotypes.
main_caveats: DNA indels and SLC6A17 protein loss were not measured; sparse basal RNA signal cannot exclude vesicle-metabolite or electrophysiological phenotypes.
summary: Slc6a17 loss produced a very sparse basal nuclear RNA response: only four non-target genes reached FDR<0.10 across 22 recovered cell groups, and all four were confined to CTX-CGE GABA and TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The perturbation decreased Slc6a17 RNA in nearly every recovered group, so the main readout is not lack of guide expression but strong transcriptional buffering of a synaptic-vesicle amino-acid transporter at rest.

direction: up after Slc6a17, Grin1, and Vps54; down after Wdfy3 and Uba5
literature_claim: SLC6A17 acts presynaptically on synaptic-vesicle neutral amino-acid/glutamine handling; no prior evidence predicted the particular TH Jun/Stmn4/Kctd16 signature or its relationship to Vps54, Wdfy3, or Uba5.
main_caveats: Restricted to three Slc6a17 FDR<0.10 genes in one thalamic cell group; direction is transcriptomic, not a measured electrophysiological state.
summary: In TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the full Slc6a17 three-gene response, Jun/Stmn4/Kctd16 up, was recapitulated by Grin1 and Vps54 and inverted by Wdfy3 and Uba5.
why_it_matters: This converts a tiny Slc6a17 signature into a screen-resolvable TH state axis: a presynaptic amino-acid transporter and a core NMDA-receptor perturbation push the same markers in coherent or opposite directions from additional non-Slc6a17 targets.

literature_claim: YTHDF1 promotes m6A-dependent translation of neuronal transcripts after stimulation and supports hippocampus-dependent learning and memory.
main_caveats: Single-gene FDR signal; no other m6A writer, reader, UPR, ISR, or proteostasis gene was significant in this cell group.
summary: Slc6a17 perturbation isolated Ythdf1 up-regulation in CTX-CGE GABA as the only cortical GABA FDR<0.10 downstream event.
why_it_matters: Ythdf1 is an m6A reader linked to neuronal translation, so its solitary induction is a candidate RNA-translation compensation rather than a broad synaptic or stress cascade.

direction: mostly nonconvergent; Grin1 selectively convergent in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
literature_claim: SLC6A17 is a member of the SLC6A15-SLC6A20 neutral amino-acid transporter subfamily and functions as a vesicular neutral-amino-acid transporter.
main_caveats: Closest neutral-transporter paralogs Slc6a15 and Slc6a16 were not represented as perturbation targets; nonconvergence is restricted to the two Slc6a17 responder groups.
summary: Most literature-obvious transporter and glutamate-receptor neighbors did not phenocopy Slc6a17 in the two responder groups; the exception was Grin1 in TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: SLC family membership or neurotransmitter-transporter annotation was a poor predictor of the postnatal single-nucleus response: Slc6a1, Slc6a5, Slc32a1, Gls, AMPA subunits, and most NMDA subunits were flat where Slc6a17 had FDR hits.

literature_claim: No literature claim was used to nominate these genome-wide neighbors.
main_caveats: Cosine scores were computed after excluding Slc6a17 itself but across many near-zero features, which makes the ranking useful mainly as a negative control.
summary: There was no strong whole-transcriptome signature neighbor for Slc6a17 across the perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative cosine neighbors were near zero and failed to reproduce the Ythdf1 or Jun/Stmn4/Kctd16 FDR signatures, so Slc6a17 should be treated as a near-null target with two focal exceptions rather than as part of a broad recurrent screen module.

literature_claim: GlyT2/SLC6A5 is a presynaptic glycinergic transporter, whereas FOXG1, PPAT, and LTK map to cortical transcriptional, purine-biosynthesis, and ALK-family receptor-tyrosine-kinase biology.
main_caveats: Only three FDR-supported genes were detected, Slc6a5 itself was not reduced at the RNA level, and no DNA indel readout is available.
summary: Slc6a5 had one real downstream response: a three-gene, L2/3 IT cortical signature with Ppat and Foxg1 up and Ltk down.
why_it_matters: The only FDR-supported phenotype is statistically real but noncanonical for a GlyT2 transporter, so it should be interpreted as a narrow cortical hypothesis rather than as recovery of the expected glycinergic-vesicle phenotype.

literature_claim: SLC6A5, GLRA1, GLRB, GPHN, and ARHGEF9 belong to the human startle-disease glycinergic neurotransmission axis, and GlyT2 cooperates with VIAAT/VGAT to establish vesicular glycine release.
main_caveats: Most related perturbations were themselves transcriptionally sparse, so the contrast rules out a shared RNA signature in this assay but not shared electrophysiology in glycinergic neurons.
summary: The Slc6a5 L2/3 response did not converge with glycine-receptor, gephyrin/collybistin, VGAT, or related SLC6 transporter perturbations.
why_it_matters: Genes in the hyperekplexia/glycinergic synapse pathway were measurable in this parquet, and their failure to share the Ppat/Ltk/Foxg1 response argues that the only Slc6a5-positive signal is not a generic glycinergic-synapse program.

main_caveats: The rejection is strong for shared FDR genes but does not exclude low-amplitude correlations.
summary: The data-driven Slc6a5 neighbors were rank artifacts rather than phenocopies.
why_it_matters: Whole-surface positive neighbors Stat4, Klhl7, and Idh3a had no FDR-supported downstream genes, and the three-gene 007 nearest neighbors had FDR 1.0 for Ppat, Ltk, and Foxg1; both tests reject apparent correlation as mechanistic convergence.

main_caveats: Psmb4/Psmc1 are not Slc6a5-pathway genes; they are detectability controls for broad RNA responses, not mechanistic comparators.
summary: Proteasome comparators responded broadly where Slc6a5 was flat.
why_it_matters: Psmb4 and Psmc1 produced thousands of DE genes in matched neuronal groups, demonstrating that this Wilcoxon/snRNA-seq surface can detect large stress and synaptic-remodeling transcriptomes; Slc6a5 lacks such a secondary program rather than being hidden by a globally insensitive readout.

literature_claim: Moderate GlyT2 inhibition is discussed as a way to modulate glycinergic inhibition in spinal pain states, with GlyT1 providing primarily glial glycine reuptake around caudal glycinergic synapses.
main_caveats: The conclusion is about assay scope, not about whether GlyT2 inhibitors are efficacious or safe in spinal cord.
summary: This screen should not be used to de-risk GlyT2 inhibition in spinal pain circuits.
why_it_matters: GlyT2 analgesic hypotheses center on glycinergic dorsal spinal cord inhibition and on GlyT2/GlyT1 handling of extracellular glycine, whereas this dataset profiles NeuN+ brain nuclei, omits spinal cord and most glia, lacks Slc6a9 as a measured target, and shows no Slc6a5 response in sampled broad neuronal groups.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: SLC7A14 loss most clearly affects photoreceptors and inner hair cells, and pinealocytes are photoreceptor-related sensory-neuroendocrine cells.
main_caveats: Only 21 perturbed nuclei supported the 217 P MY Pineal Glut result; the two telencephalic effects were single-gene signatures.
summary: Slc7a14 produced only five downstream FDR<0.10 DEGs in 22 measured groups, and the only multi-gene response was in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: A sparse pineal-labeled response aligns better with SLC7A14 sensory-cell biology than with a ubiquitous neuronal amino-acid-transporter stress program.

literature_claim: DMXL2, EFR3, and GABBR2 participate in membrane or synaptic signaling modules not previously established as SLC7A14 transcriptional targets.
main_caveats: Restricted to three DEGs in a low-n cell group; the genes do not prove one unified pathway.
summary: The 217 P MY Pineal Glut response combined up-regulation of Efr3a and Dmxl2 with down-regulation of Gabbr2.
why_it_matters: Although only three genes passed FDR, their functions nominate membrane phosphoinositide scaffolding, V-ATPase or ribbon-synapse trafficking, and metabotropic GABA tuning rather than a generic lysosomal stress state.

literature_claim: SLC7A14 sensory-cell loss and hepatic lysosomal GABA accumulation can perturb autophagy, trafficking, or mTOR signaling.
main_caveats: DNA indels and SLC7A14 protein loss were not measured; FDR-significant self RNA reduction is not identical to complete knockout.
summary: Pvalb neurons showed significant Slc7a14 transcript reduction without any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: The result uncouples detectable target mRNA lowering from a neuronal transcriptional phenotype and argues that Pvalb cells buffer partial acute Slc7a14 loss at the RNA level.

literature_claim: SLC7A14 has been connected to lysosomal autophagy, lysosomal GABA transport, mTORC2, and POMC-neuron mTORC1 signaling.
main_caveats: Some canonical SLC7 transporter paralogs were not represented as perturbation targets; the assay compared transcriptional outputs, not lysosomal flux or phospho-mTOR proteins.
summary: Represented lysosome, autophagy, GABA, and TSC/mTOR comparators failed to share Slc7a14's five significant downstream hits, while Tsc2 produced hypothalamic DEGs where Slc7a14 was null.
why_it_matters: This rejects a simple TSC2-like or autophagy-gene-like neuronal phenocopy and refines SLC7A14 as context-dependent rather than a broad postnatal mTOR transcriptional regulator.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Neighbor ranking was intentionally restricted to the five Slc7a14 downstream DEGs; broader all-gene correlations were near zero for Wilcoxon scores because the Slc7a14 surface is mostly flat.
summary: The top data-driven positive and negative restricted-signature neighbors, Ptf1a and Arid1b, were rejected after matched FDR lookup.
why_it_matters: It prevents an overinterpretation in which a sparse five-gene signature is treated as cross-perturbation convergence when the comparator changes are only subthreshold signs.

literature_claim: Iwr1/SLC7A6OS-family proteins participate in Pol II nuclear import or Pol II biogenesis-associated networks, and SON/SRRM2/PRPF8/SNRNP200 sit in nuclear-speckle or spliceosome RNA-processing machinery.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq measures mRNA abundance, not Pol II localization or splicing chemistry; most Polr2 subunits and GPN factors were not perturbation targets.
summary: Slc7a6os loss produced recurrent Polr2a up-regulation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Son/Snrnp200/Dhx37/Cpsf1 gains and Srrm2/Pnisr losses concentrated in 110 and 151.
why_it_matters: The most target-proximal transcriptomic signal points back to Pol II and RNA-processing homeostasis rather than to SLC7 amino-acid transport; it argues that at least part of the CRISPR perturbation engaged the Iwr1/SLC7A6OS axis even though the Slc7a6os mRNA itself did not fall significantly.

literature_claim: Prior vertebrate and human data argue that SLC7A6OS loss can affect the CNS, but they do not predict which P37-P44 postmitotic mouse neuron classes should show an acute transcriptional phenotype.
main_caveats: The response ranking is transcriptomic and survivor-biased within the recovered NeuN-positive neuronal nuclei; 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for this target.
summary: The postmitotic Slc7a6os response was sharply selective: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained 95 of the 116 FDR<0.10 downstream calls, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut had 15, 155 MB Glut had 3, and three other groups had only single-gene responses.
why_it_matters: SLC7A6OS is broadly expressed and genetically neurological, but acute loss after P16 was not a pan-neuronal transcriptional insult; thalamic and hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons were the principal responder states in this assay.

literature_claim: SLC7A6OS loss of function causes progressive myoclonus epilepsy, a clinically and genetically heterogeneous neuronal disorder; the literature does not define a thalamic transcriptional program for EPM12.
main_caveats: The branch assignment is by gene identity within a 95-gene signature; electrophysiology, protein localization and survival were not assayed.
summary: In the dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response, synaptic and excitability genes were preferentially down-regulated while chaperone, lysosomal and metabolic genes rose.
why_it_matters: Down-regulation of Gabbr2, Grm1, Slc4a10, Kcna4, Dpp6, Syt7, Cacna-family and Grin2c transcripts links a Pol II-import gene to a thalamic neuronal-state program rather than to a uniform collapse of all mRNAs; the countervailing Cct8/Dnaja1/Atp6v1b2/Chchd2/Acadvl branch suggests a buffered stress or remodeling state.

literature_claim: PSMB4/PSMC1 encode proteasome subunits, whereas SNRNP70/PRPF6/U2AF2 encode spliceosome factors; no prior literature made these the expected closest Slc7a6os perturbation neighbors.
main_caveats: The neighbor calculation was restricted to the Slc7a6os FDR<0.10 coordinates; convergence should be read as a shared downstream module, not a direct physical interaction.
summary: The Slc7a6os 116-gene signature most strongly converged with proteasome perturbations Psmb4/Psmc1 and spliceosome perturbations Snrnp70/Prpf6/U2af2 rather than with a textbook SLC7-family neighbor.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation overlap turns a small Slc7a6os signature into a recognizable module: many thalamic genes suppressed by Slc7a6os loss were also suppressed after proteasome or spliceosome disruption, consistent with a shared vulnerable-neuron stress module rather than a Slc7a6os-only effector list.

literature_claim: GPN-loop GTPases and Polr2 subunits are closer Pol II-biogenesis partners for Iwr1/SLC7A6OS than the generic nuclear-transport factors represented in this screen.
main_caveats: The strongest canonical comparators were absent as perturbation targets, and Tnpo3 imports SR splicing factors rather than RNA polymerase II itself.
summary: Direct Pol II-import relatives were absent from the target set, and the represented nuclear-transport factor Tnpo3 converged with Slc7a6os in 151 whereas Ranbp2 did not.
why_it_matters: This bounds the cross-perturbation claim: the assay could compare Slc7a6os with broad nuclear-import and splicing targets, but not with Gpn1/Gpn2/Gpn3/Rpap2 or Polr2 subunits themselves; consequently the observed proteasome/spliceosome neighborhood is data-nominated, not a failure to test the canonical complex.

literature_claim: Progressive myoclonus epilepsies are genetically heterogeneous, and SLC7A6OS was added as an EPM12 locus by a human biallelic loss-of-function splice variant.
main_caveats: The family comparison is at the RNA phenotype level only; a shared excitability phenotype with little transcriptomic output would not be detected.
summary: Progressive-myoclonus-epilepsy family perturbations did not phenocopy the Slc7a6os responder signatures in the matched cell groups.
why_it_matters: Kcnc1, Epm2a, Scarb2, Atp6v0a1, Serpini1, Tbc1d24, Prnp, Sacs and Afg3l2 are disease-neighbor controls rather than pathway controls; their flat matched signatures indicate that EPM12 has an acute transcriptional footprint distinct from ion-channel, lysosomal and other PME genes in this juvenile neuronal assay.

literature_claim: Pld3 is an endolysosomal nuclease; no cited literature links Slc7a6os to Pld3 or Nicn1 in postnatal neurons.
main_caveats: Each cell group contributed exactly one robust downstream gene, so this is a placeholder hypothesis rather than a pathway claim.
summary: The hippocampal Nicn1 and 191 MB P MY GABA Pld3 calls were isolated sentinels, not broad ER, Nodal, lysosomal or inflammatory programs.
why_it_matters: The FDR<0.10 surface contains real single-gene changes outside thalamic and hypothalamic glutamatergic cells, but their isolation prevents pathway expansion; keeping them as singletons avoids inflating a null/weak Slc7a6os surface into unsupported biology.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: NHE7 resides in TGN/post-Golgi membranes and regulates luminal pH and exported-cargo glycosylation, but a transcriptional direction after acute neuronal loss of function was not established.
main_caveats: True DNA indel rates were not measured, and snRNA-seq does not assay Golgi pH, glycans, surface cargo, or synaptic physiology.
summary: Slc9a7 perturbation was buffered at the nuclear-transcriptome level: all 20 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream Wilcoxon DE genes at FDR<0.10, even though three groups showed FDR-level reduction of the Slc9a7 transcript.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a broad UPR, ISR, autophagy, proteostasis, or synaptic mRNA program after acute postmitotic Slc9a7 loss; the likely primary biology remains organelle pH and cargo processing rather than a secondary nuclear program.

literature_claim: V-ATPase, CLC transporters, and endomembrane NHEs jointly set secretory and endolysosomal pH, and NHE6/NHE7/NHE9 defects are connected to neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
main_caveats: The only directly represented NHE paralog was Slc9a9; Slc9a6 and Slc9a8 were not tested in the parquet.
summary: Literature-obvious acidification relatives did not share a Slc9a7 signature: Slc9a9, Atp6v0a1, Clcn3, and Clcn4 were flat in matched groups, while Atp6v1a, Atp6v1b2, and Atp6v1e1 produced only sparse, non-overlapping FDR<0.10 responses with near-zero Slc9a7 score cosines from -0.0053 to 0.0114.
why_it_matters: Endomembrane pH membership did not translate into interchangeable postmitotic snRNA phenotypes; a perturbation can touch the same organellar axis yet remain transcriptionally orthogonal.

main_caveats: A whole-transcriptome cosine over a flat target is intentionally a weak similarity metric; the conclusion is absence of meaningful convergence, not mechanistic opposition to the named neighbors.
summary: The all-target, data-driven neighbor search found no hidden Slc9a7-like transcriptional module: the strongest positive and negative score cosines across 1772 other targets were only +0.0224 and -0.0145.
why_it_matters: The Slc9a7 surface looks like a true transcriptional singleton/null rather than a weak member of an unanticipated co-regulated perturbation class.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Human SLC9A7 p.Leu515Phe is a recurrent XLID missense allele with GOF-like TGN alkalinization and abnormal N-glycosylation, and cancer-cell NHE7 knockdown can compromise cytosolic pH homeostasis and viability.
main_caveats: The perturbation was LoF, mosaic, and postnatal; it did not install the human missense allele and did not measure glycans, pH, cell-surface cargo, or tumor-cell fitness.
summary: The null Slc9a7 LoF surface is most consistent with SLC9A7 biology being off-axis and allele-sensitive: the published XLID allele perturbs TGN/post-Golgi pH and N-glycosylation, whereas acute CRISPR LoF in postmitotic neurons did not induce a detectable secondary stress transcriptome.
why_it_matters: The screen should not be read as evidence that NHE7 is irrelevant to neurons; rather, it narrows what this assay can test and warns that a p.Leu515Phe-like or glycosylation phenotype needs pH, glycoproteomic, cargo-trafficking, or surface-proteomic readouts.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: SLC9A9/NHE9 encodes an endosomal Na+/H+ exchanger implicated in ASD/ADHD; mouse and cell studies predict endosomal pH, synaptic, and cargo-trafficking consequences of NHE9 loss.
main_caveats: This is a steady-state snRNA result, not DNA indel sequencing, endosomal pH imaging, protein-localization imaging, or electrophysiology; several groups have tens rather than hundreds of perturbed nuclei.
summary: Postnatal Slc9a9 perturbation produced a pan-neuronal FDR-zero snRNA signature: every one of the 23 recovered neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This is a strong negative transcriptional result in the sampled P16-to-P37/44 neuronal context. It argues that acute mosaic NHE9 loss is buffered at the level of steady-state nuclear RNA even in hippocampal and cortical glutamatergic groups where NHE9 biology was expected to be relevant.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: Endosomal Na+/H+ exchangers counter V-ATPase-driven acidification and participate in endosomal cargo trafficking.
main_caveats: The comparator lesions are not NHE9 paralogs and can be more disruptive than loss of an endosomal proton leak; overlap was assessed from restricted DE signatures rather than from pH measurements.
summary: Severe endolysosomal and V-ATPase perturbations were transcriptionally detectable in this screen, whereas Slc9a9 was not.
why_it_matters: The comparison separates NHE9 from core endolysosomal failure: Rab7, Vps35, and some V-ATPase subunit perturbations produced corrected lysosomal/stress or trafficking signatures in selected neuronal classes, so the Slc9a9 null is not simply a failure of these cell groups or the Wilcoxon assay to report endolysosomal injury.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: NHE9 and NHE7 are intracellular SLC9 cation/proton exchangers but occupy different endomembrane compartments, with NHE9 biased to recycling endosomes and NHE7 to the trans-Golgi network.
main_caveats: Slc9a7 was not recovered in three Slc9a9 groups and generally had fewer perturbed cells; shared flatness does not prove biochemical redundancy.
summary: The only represented SLC9A endomembrane paralog, Slc9a7/NHE7, also lacked downstream FDR genes in its 20 recovered groups.
why_it_matters: This keeps an expected family comparison explicit: organellar Na+/H+ exchange can be related to disease and organelle pH, but in this juvenile neuronal snRNA assay neither the endosomal NHE9 lesion nor the Golgi-biased NHE7 lesion generated a broad corrected transcriptional state.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: No literature comparator was used for this pre-prior, data-driven neighbor test.
main_caveats: Cosines were computed on signed Wilcoxon scores over matched rows; a low-amplitude spatially or temporally restricted phenotype would be invisible if it did not recur in the assayed nuclei.
summary: Unbiased whole-surface signature search found no meaningful Slc9a9 convergence or anticorrelation with any other perturbation.
why_it_matters: Because Slc9a9 had no FDR genes, a hidden weak program should have appeared as a repeated signed-rank pattern across genes and cell groups; instead the strongest cosine neighbors in 1,772 other targets were near zero.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: NHE9 loss or disease variants are expected to acidify endosomes and change receptor/transporter trafficking, glutamate uptake, and presynaptic calcium entry.
main_caveats: The tested sentinel genes cover transcripts rather than receptor surface abundance, GLAST/GLT-1 protein trafficking, vesicle pH, or calcium influx.
summary: Known NHE9 cargo and synaptic-trafficking readouts were absent at the mRNA level after Slc9a9 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The genes most directly nominated by NHE9 literature--transferrin receptor, astrocytic glutamate transporters, AMPA/TrkB cargo, calcium-channel, and lysosomal sentinel transcripts--were all FDR-null. The dataset therefore refines the expected NHE9 phenotype toward pH, surface localization, and physiology rather than a cell-autonomous nuclear-RNA replacement of those cargo programs.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: SLF2-SMC5/6 biology is dominated by replication-coupled genome stability, and SLF2/SMC5 loss causes fork stress, chromosome mis-segregation, and apoptosis in proliferating patient cells, zebrafish embryos, and Smc5-deficient neural progenitors.
main_caveats: DNA indels and SLF2 protein were not measured; the only positive Slf2 DEG came from 26 perturbed nuclei in one cell group.
summary: Slf2 loss was nearly transcriptionally silent after P16 neuronal CRISPR, producing only one downstream FDR<0.10 gene across 21 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: A genome-maintenance factor with strong S-phase genetics did not trigger a broad DNA-damage, p53, ISR, UPR, or apoptosis program in postmitotic juvenile neurons; this makes the negative surface biologically interpretable rather than a failed-knockdown result.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: Protein phosphatase 5 is required for ATR-mediated checkpoint activation in DNA-damaged proliferating cells.
main_caveats: Single-gene FDR event in 26 Slf2-perturbed nuclei; Nsmce2 and Atr perturbations did not reproduce the Ppp5c hit in the same cell group.
summary: Ppp5c was the lone robust Slf2-dependent transcript and was up-regulated specifically in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
why_it_matters: PP5 can support ATR checkpoint signaling, so Ppp5c is a plausible checkpoint-compensation marker if Slf2 loss creates low-level DNA-repair pressure in a restricted upper-layer glutamatergic population.

literature_claim: Nsmce2 is the SMC5/6-associated SUMO ligase, and ATR is a master replication-stress checkpoint kinase; both act in replication-coupled genome-integrity pathways.
main_caveats: Most direct SLF2 recruiters and SMC5/6 core components, including Slf1, Simc1, Rad18, Smc5, and Smc6, were not perturbation targets in the parquet.
summary: Nsmce2 and Atr converged with Slf2 by being flat, not by sharing an induced repair transcriptome, in the same postnatal neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: The same-complex Nsmce2 and checkpoint-kinase Atr controls show that the missing Slf2 phenotype is a shared postmitotic uncoupling of replication-fork machinery rather than an idiosyncratic Slf2-only anomaly.

literature_claim: Cohesin, built around SMC1/3, and SMC5/6 are distinct structural-maintenance-of-chromosomes complexes with different genome-maintenance roles.
main_caveats: Smc1a is a family-level, not same-complex, comparator; the mechanistic source of its thalamic transcriptomic phenotype is not resolved here.

why_it_matters: The only Slf2 signal is not part of a reproducible multi-target transcriptional module in this dataset, so the isolated Ppp5c event should be read as restricted and hypothesis-generating.

literature_claim: In adult mouse neocortex, BMP2 acts through SMAD1 in PV interneurons to regulate glutamatergic synapse proteins, perineuronal-net components, PV-cell excitability, and excitation-inhibition balance.

why_it_matters: This is the most literature-predicted postmitotic neuronal context for Smad1, yet Smad1 perturbation yielded 0 downstream FDR genes in 108 Pvalb cells and left Id1, Id3, Bcan, and Smad7 at FDR 1.0.

main_caveats: The neighbor search is based on nominal Smad1 rank structure because Smad1 had no FDR-supported genes; these are negative validation results, not biological links between Smad1 and the named targets.

why_it_matters: Top correlations on the restricted Smad1-ranked feature set were only |r|≤0.137, and Rho, Fmn2, Mif, Ago1, Ryr2, and Usf1 showed at most one or two isolated FDR<0.10 genes, arguing against a reproducible noncanonical Smad1-like module.

literature_claim: Acetylcholinesterase acts at cholinergic synapses by hydrolyzing acetylcholine; this is an indirect functional annotation rather than a prior claim about Smad2 regulation.
main_caveats: Each responsive group contains a one-gene signature; Cpne7 has limited prior annotation in this context, and true indel formation was not measured.
summary: Postnatal Smad2 loss produced an ultra-sparse, negative response: Cpne7 decreased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Ache decreased in 155 MB Glut, with no other Smad2 cell group containing a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: This turns an apparently flat canonical transcription-factor perturbation into a restricted marker hypothesis: two high-control-count thalamic/midbrain glutamatergic populations crossed FDR, but each did so through only one downregulated transcript.

literature_claim: Psmc1 and Psmb4 encode proteasome components, whereas Tpr and Tnpo3 encode nuclear-transport machinery; this machinery is not the textbook receptor-SMAD branch of TGFβ signaling.
main_caveats: The Smad2 side of the comparison is only two FDR-significant genes; apparent opposite neighbors were nominal and were rejected.
summary: The two Smad2 marker genes were recurrent downstream endpoints of non-SMAD perturbations: Cpne7 fell after Chd4, Adnp, Tpr, Tnpo3, Zbtb7a, Wac, and Psmc1 in 151, while Ache fell after Ranbp2, Psmc1, Ogt, Ascc3, Wac, Psmb4, Tnpo3, Tpr, and Zbtb7a in 155.
why_it_matters: The nearest real neighbors of the restricted Smad2 signature were nuclear-transport, proteasome, chromatin, and transcriptional regulators rather than TGFβ receptors, arguing that Cpne7 and Ache are reusable neuronal vulnerability readouts rather than a private SMAD2/3/4 target program.

literature_claim: Ligand-activated TGFβ and activin receptors phosphorylate Smad2 and Smad3, promote Smad4-containing complexes, and drive nuclear transcriptional responses.
main_caveats: Comparator nulls also lack DNA-level indel measurements, and several receptor perturbations have modest perturbed-cell counts.
summary: Smad2 did not phenocopy the directly measured TGFβ/activin/BMP SMAD pathway relatives Smad3, Smad4, Smad1, Smad6, Smad9, Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Tgfbr3, Acvr1, Acvr2a, Acvr2b, Acvrl1, Bmpr1a, Bmpr1b, Bmpr2, or the Smad corepressor Ski.
why_it_matters: The failure of same-pathway perturbations to recover the two Smad2 outputs makes the restricted Smad2 phenotype unlikely to be a simple basal readout of the canonical receptor→SMAD2/3→SMAD4 transcriptional cassette.

literature_claim: TGFβ/SMAD signaling uses SMAD2/3-SMAD4-driven feedback genes such as Smad7 and Ski/SnoN-family regulation, and neuronal Smad2 has been placed upstream of the Cdh1-APC/SnoN axon-growth pathway.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance in surviving NeuN+ nuclei was assayed; ligand-stimulated or injury-evoked SMAD2 activity was not imposed.
summary: Smad2 perturbation did not recover a canonical TGFβ/SMAD feedback program or the neuronal Cdh1-APC/SnoN-axis transcripts queried here: Smad7, Skil, Fzr1, Id2, Ccn2, Serpine1, and Junb had zero FDR<0.10 events across the 21 measured Smad2 groups.
why_it_matters: The snRNA-seq readout would have seen a transcriptional feedback burst if basal Smad2 loss were rewiring this pathway; its absence makes the blank surface biologically informative rather than merely technically flat.

literature_claim: Canonical TGFβ-Smad signaling regulates gene expression, and neuronal or astroglial Smad3 can influence dendrite growth and synaptogenesis when stimulated or knocked down in culture.

why_it_matters: Smad3 is a receptor-activated transcription factor, so the complete absence of BH-supported direct or secondary RNA changes argues that baseline P37-44 NeuN+ neurons do not run a strong tonic Smad3-dependent transcriptional program after P16 loss of function.

main_caveats: The comparison intentionally uses the whole subthreshold Smad3 score vector because Smad3 has no FDR-supported responder genes.

why_it_matters: A real perturbation program should recruit correlated targets with shared FDR-supported genes; here the top neighbors are best read as the floor of a nearly featureless Smad3 vector rather than as Trp63, Ephb1, Fbxo11, or Npy1r pathway biology.

literature_claim: Smad2, Smad3, and Smad4 are core TGFβ signal transducers, while Smad1 is a receptor-regulated Smad in the related BMP branch.

why_it_matters: The absence of a related-target module argues that the screen is seeing a quiescent or buffered TGFβ-family transcriptional axis in juvenile neurons, not just one silent guide set for Smad3.

literature_claim: BMP-SMAD1/5/8 signaling is most prominent in embryonic and stem/progenitor neural patterning, and Smad8/9 single loss is buffered by overlapping BMP R-SMADs.

why_it_matters: A BMP receptor SMAD can be genetically removed after neuronal specification without eliciting even a conventional secondary stress, synaptic, or canonical BMP target module, arguing that single-gene Smad9 activity is transcriptionally buffered in this assay context.

literature_claim: BMP type I/type II receptors activate SMAD1/5/8/9, often with overlapping R-SMAD function.
main_caveats: Smad5 was not represented as a perturbation target, and several receptor perturbations were missing one or two of the 23 cell groups.

why_it_matters: If the postnatal neuronal zero were simply a failed Smad9 guide class, related BMP nodes might still expose a receptor-SMAD transcriptional program. Instead, Smad1, Smad4, Smad6, Bmpr1a, Acvr2a, and Acvr2b were also FDR-flat in matched neuronal groups, while Acvr1, Bmpr1b, and Bmpr2 produced only singleton downstream calls.

literature_claim: No prior BMP-SMAD9 literature nominates these off-pathway genes as expected postmitotic neuronal Smad9 phenocopies.
main_caveats: The comparison used residual logFCs, not an FDR-backed Smad9 signature; it supports only a negative statement about lack of robust convergence.
summary: The strongest unbiased Smad9 neighbors were extremely weak and off-pathway rather than BMP relatives.
why_it_matters: Cell-group/output-gene-centered correlations nominated Maf, Myod1, and Lhx3 on the positive side and Adam10, Crebbp, and Npy1r on the negative side, but absolute correlations were only about 0.09-0.12 and the neighbors were themselves null or focal. The apparent manifold position therefore behaves like null-neighborhood noise, not a convergent SMAD9 effector program.

literature_claim: SMAD9/Smad8 can be nonredundant for BMP-induced miR-21, miR-27a, and miR-100 processing in pulmonary vascular cells and Smad8 mutant mice develop pulmonary vascular remodeling.

why_it_matters: Human and mouse SMAD9 disease biology centers on pulmonary vascular cells and a noncanonical Smad8-dependent microRNA-maturation branch. The all-neuronal Smad9 zero, and the absence of Tnc/Prrx1 or canonical Id/Msx activation, therefore refine the null as a lineage and phenotype mismatch rather than a contradiction of PAH genetics.

literature_claim: Liprin-α2 participates in presynaptic RIM1/CASK recruitment and synaptic transmission.

why_it_matters: This is the only non-self transcriptome change strong enough to distinguish Smarca2 perturbation from background in the screen, and it points to a synaptic active-zone scaffold rather than a broad chromatin-remodeling program.

literature_claim: Neuronal BAF complexes contain alternative BRM/SMARCA2 or BRG1/SMARCA4 ATPases plus core and accessory subunits, and SMARCA2 and SMARCA4 can show reciprocal compensatory behavior.
main_caveats: Comparator correlations were computed on sparse FDR surfaces; Smarcb1, Actl6b, Dpf1 and Dpf3 were not represented as perturbation targets in the parquet.
summary: Perturbing core nBAF members was transcriptionally visible in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, but Smarca2 and its ATPase paralog Smarca4 did not phenocopy that response.
why_it_matters: The same dataset can detect BAF-complex disruption, so the near-zero Smarca2 surface is not simply a blind spot for chromatin regulators; the result separates an ATPase-specific, likely redundant perturbation from loss of shared BAF structural subunits.

main_caveats: Correlation over all rank-score rows is a global metric and is conservative for very small signatures.
summary: The unbiased signed-score neighborhood of Smarca2 is essentially empty: the top positive and negative non-safe neighbors were Nr1h4 and Fbxo11 with correlations of only 0.0366 and -0.0278.
why_it_matters: The top neighbors being weak, non-BAF and themselves flat rejects a hidden convergent program elsewhere in the perturbation universe.

literature_claim: SMARCA2-Nicolaides-Baraitser pathogenic variants cluster in the ATPase domain and are inferred to act by dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanisms; a separate schizophrenia study reported that siRNA and Smarca2-knockout prefrontal-cortex signatures can be transcriptomically visible.
main_caveats: CRISPR indels, protein loss and allele dosage are unmeasured; enhancer accessibility and neuronal morphology were not assayed.
summary: A postnatal Smarca2 loss-of-function perturbation does not reproduce the broad gene-dysregulation expectation created by SMARCA2 Nicolaides-Baraitser alleles.
why_it_matters: The screen supports a distinction between simple Smarca2 insufficiency in specified neurons and dominant ATPase-domain missense SMARCA2 disease mechanisms.

literature_claim: SMARCA4-mutant cancer cells depend on residual SMARCA2-containing SWI/SNF complexes, and mature-rat Smarca2 ablation was reported to be phenotypically mild over a short toxicity window.
main_caveats: The screen contains neurons rather than SMARCA4-mutant tumor cells, covers 3-4 weeks after P16 delivery, and does not measure protein depletion or pathology.
summary: Smarca2-only inhibition in Smarca4-intact juvenile neurons is transcriptionally quiet in this screen, whereas published synthetic-lethal SMARCA2 dependencies are concentrated in SMARCA4-deficient cancer contexts.
why_it_matters: The neuronal null de-risks neither developmental exposure nor all cell states, but it argues that strong SMARCA2-pathway toxicity should be sought in SMARCA4-deficient or dual-ATPase contexts rather than inferred from BRM loss alone.

literature_claim: SMARCA4 and these ARID and SMARCC/SMARCD/SMARCE proteins are paralogous or associated mSWI/SNF subunits with shared relevance to neurodevelopmental disorders.

summary: Smarca4 was flat in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut precisely where multiple mSWI/SNF accessory subunits converged on a recurrent thalamic module.
why_it_matters: Arid1a, Arid2, Smarcc2, Smarce1, and weaker Smarcd1/Arid1b perturbations gave FDR<0.10 genes in 151, including recurrent Ptpn3, Begain, Reep2, Prkcd, Abhd12b, Lrrc7, Prkcb, and Rasa4, whereas Smarca4 had 146 perturbed 151 nuclei and zero downstream genes. The thalamic BAF response is therefore subunit-selective and cannot be inferred from BRG1 alone.

main_caveats: Residual SMARCA2-containing complexes were not biochemically measured in neurons; the inference rests on paralog biology and the lack of single-ATPase DE.
summary: The BRG1 paralog Smarca2 also failed to generate a broad matched response, including in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where Smarcc2 and Arid2 were active.
why_it_matters: SMARCA4/BRG1 and SMARCA2/BRM are alternative catalytic ATPases. In this dataset neither single ATPase perturbation phenocopied the thalamic accessory-subunit module, supporting catalytic-ATPase buffering or subunit-threshold specificity after postmitotic single-gene loss.

main_caveats: Neighbor scores were computed over whole Wilcoxon-score surfaces; with a zero-FDR query signature, the ranking is dominated by weak residual score noise.
summary: The unbiased full-parquet neighbor calculation found no robust convergent or anti-convergent Smarca4 signature.
why_it_matters: The best positive neighbors had cosine scores near zero and were themselves null or one-gene surfaces, while the top negative neighbor, Psmb4, had a broad proteasome-like response but only -0.017 cosine to Smarca4. This rejects data-driven neighbors as biological Smarca4 comparators in this screen.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Smarcad1/SMARCAD1 regulates early embryonic chromatin, ERV silencing in ESCs, DNA-end resection, and a skin-specific disease isoform.
main_caveats: The perturbation's true DNA indel rate is unmeasured, and the assay does not directly quantify DNA repair or repetitive-element RNAs.
summary: Smarcad1 perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across all 20 measured neuronal groups, with 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes and no corrected self-transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: The result confines acute Smarcad1 loss to a basal postmitotic-neuron null surface and prevents over-assigning its ESC, skin, or DNA-repair biology to juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: SMARCAD1 cooperates with KAP1 at ERVs in ESCs, and SETDB1/H3K9me3 is a core retroelement-silencing pathway.
main_caveats: Setdb1 is a pathway neighbor rather than a SMARCAD1 subunit; ERV reads themselves were not quantified.
summary: Setdb1, the represented H3K9/retroelement pathway neighbor, responded where Smarcad1 did not: Setdb1 produced 45 downstream FDR<0.10 genes across Smarcad1-matched groups versus 0 for Smarcad1.
why_it_matters: Shows that the absence of a Smarcad1 signature is not explained by an assay-wide inability to capture Setdb1/KAP1/heterochromatin-proximal consequences in neurons.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: BAF/SWI-SNF and related chromatin remodelers regulate neural chromatin programs in stage- and subunit-specific ways.
main_caveats: These are broad disease-family comparators, not SMARCAD1 paralogs or direct complex members.
summary: Multiple represented SWI/SNF, BAF, CHD, and ATRX chromatin-remodeler comparators produced FDR<0.10 neuronal signatures, most strongly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Smarcad1 remained flat in the same matched groups.
why_it_matters: Rules out the simple explanation that all chromatin-remodeler perturbations are invisible in the P16 juvenile-neuron assay and makes the Smarcad1 null a target-specific uncoupling.

main_caveats: This calculation used the full weak signed-score vector because Smarcad1 had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes.
summary: Whole-universe neighbors of the Smarcad1 signed-Wilcoxon profile were essentially uncorrelated, with r values between -0.025 and 0.043 for the strongest positive and negative neighbors.
why_it_matters: Avoids assigning a spurious subthreshold module to a target whose own DE surface lacks FDR-level genes.

literature_claim: SRPK1 is a kinase for SR-family splicing factors that regulate constitutive and alternative splicing.
main_caveats: One downstream gene only; no co-significant splicing program was detected, and the Ogt comparison is opposite-direction and exploratory.
summary: Smarcc1 produced a single adjusted downstream hit, Srpk1 up-regulation in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This is the only positive Smarcc1 biology in the screen and points to an RNA-processing kinase rather than to a multi-gene BAF-collapse response.

literature_claim: SMARCC1 and SMARCC2 are BAF core/scaffold-family subunits, and BAF complexes are assembled and destabilized through regulated interactions among subunits.
main_caveats: Transcriptomic comparisons do not prove which BAF subcomplex is present in these thalamic neurons; several comparator signatures are small.
summary: Smarcc1 failed to phenocopy a thalamic BAF/SWI-SNF module driven by Smarcc2, Arid2, Arid1a, and Smarce1.
why_it_matters: The same cell class that was flat for Smarcc1 carried strong related-subunit signatures, so the result separates BAF155 from BAF170-, ARID-, and SMARCE1-dependent postnatal thalamic transcription rather than dismissing the cell class as unresponsive.

main_caveats: Whole-vector similarity can underweight one-gene signatures; this is a screen-internal negative result only.
summary: Smarcc1 had no robust global positive or negative signature neighbor across the target universe.
why_it_matters: The isolated MB Glut Srpk1 signal was not part of a reproducible same-direction cross-perturbation module, and the strongest whole-vector neighbors had near-zero cosine similarities.

main_caveats: Engagement was inferred from gRNA assignment and nuclear RNA, not directly from DNA indels or protein loss.
summary: Smarcc2 produced a 263-gene downstream response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; the other 21 recovered groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes and 215 MB Dopa was missing.
why_it_matters: The result makes regional selectivity the first-order phenotype: SMARCC2 is competent to drive a postnatal neuronal transcriptomic program, but that program is not pan-neuronal in this assay.

literature_claim: SMARCC2, SMARCE1, SMARCD-family, and ARID-family proteins are components or specificity subunits of mammalian BAF-family chromatin-remodeling complexes.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and restricted to genes significant in Smarcc2; Smarce1 itself had only 16 downstream DEGs and Arid1b only one.
summary: Smarce1 and Arid1a were the top two positive restricted-signature neighbors of Smarcc2 in 151, and all of their FDR-controlled overlaps with the 263-gene Smarcc2 signature were same-direction.
why_it_matters: A pure phenotype-first calculation recovered same-complex BAF subunits, supporting the 151 transcriptional signature as an on-pathway BAF response rather than a one-off guide artifact.

literature_claim: SMARCC1 is the paralogous BAF155 scaffold, SMARCA2/4 are ATPase-family BAF subunits, and BICRA/ARID2/SMARCD1 are BAF-family disease or subcomplex genes.
main_caveats: A flat mRNA self-row does not prove absence of indels for Smarcc1, Smarca4, or Bicra; disease alleles for some CSS genes are not simple LoF.
summary: Smarcc1, Smarca2, Smarca4, and Bicra did not phenocopy Smarcc2 in the matched 151 group; Arid1b and Smarcd1 were nearly flat, while Arid2 was only partially overlapping.
why_it_matters: Same-family membership was insufficient for a postnatal thalamic LoF phenotype, refining BAF biology toward subunit- and allele-specific dependencies.

literature_claim: Neuronal BAF complexes regulate gene-expression programs in postmitotic neurons after an npBAF-to-nBAF subunit switch.
main_caveats: The thalamic marker Grin2c itself was not FDR<0.10 and is not part of this claimed module.
summary: The strongest Smarcc2-negative genes in 151 included Ptpn3, Reep2, Tiam1, C1qtnf4, Prkcd, Ptprz1, Pdp1, and Adarb1, with additional down-regulation of receptor and signaling genes Grin2b, Grm1, Prkcb, Gabra4, Gabbr1, Cacnb2, Kcnk9, Cnih3, and P2rx4.
why_it_matters: These transcripts define the proximal measurable loss-of-state program for acute Smarcc2 disruption in the only responding neuronal population.

literature_claim: BAF170-containing BAF complexes are known to regulate neural developmental programs, including cortical and dentate-gyrus processes tied to progenitor behavior and morphogenesis.
main_caveats: No morphology, migration, or connectivity was assayed, so the matrix/adhesion interpretation rests on transcript identities.
summary: Smarcc2 loss in 151 significantly down-regulated adhesion and extracellular-interface genes including L1cam, Sdk2, Itga3, Serpine2, Agrn, Adamts16, Adamts19, Col15a1, Fbln5, and Col4a1.
why_it_matters: A chromatin-remodeling perturbation converged on a structural neurite-interface program, providing a postmitotic thalamic counterpart to developmental BAF effects on morphogenesis.

main_caveats: The data identify a transcriptional arm but do not establish whether it is adaptive compensation, subtype mixing, or a direct de-repression program.
summary: The 151 response included a large positive arm, with Syt4, Clstn1, Clstn2, Epb41l1, Ndrg1, Pth2r, Gfra1, Tafa1, Sertm1, and Grin3a up-regulated.
why_it_matters: Smarcc2 loss did not merely repress neuronal genes; the mixed up/down program is compatible with a compensatory or alternative-state shift within the same thalamic class.

main_caveats: The gene set is small and heterogeneous; snRNA-seq alone cannot distinguish neuronal cell-cycle re-entry from chromatin-state or RNA-composition shifts.
summary: A small FDR-controlled but heterogeneous cell-cycle, histone, microtubule, and ciliary-gene arm accompanied the 151 response.
why_it_matters: Postmitotic neurons rarely use canonical cell-cycle transcripts as a simple proliferation program; this arm is therefore a hypothesis-generating marker of chromatin or cytoskeletal compensation after BAF perturbation.

main_caveats: Only transcriptomic stress readouts were tested; protein-level stress was not measured.
summary: Canonical ISR/UPR and proteasome sentinel genes were absent from the only Smarcc2 responder, even though the data-driven neighbor Dhdds produced a strong 151 response and known stress-like genes.
why_it_matters: The absence of Atf4, Ddit3, Chac1, Sdf2l1, Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Xbp1, Herpud1, Psma7, and Psmd1 prevents mislabeling the Smarcc2 signature as a generic injured-neuron or ER-stress state.

main_caveats: The rejection applies to FDR-controlled DE in this cell group; weak expression-vector anti-correlation still exists over the restricted gene set.
summary: The strongest negative restricted-signature neighbors of Smarcc2 did not yield robust FDR-controlled anti-phenotypes in 151.
why_it_matters: This protects the analysis from overinterpreting a cosine tail driven by subthreshold fold-changes; Gfra1, Klf12, Idh3a, Snta1, and Dnajc13 should not be used as validated reversal comparators.

literature_claim: BAF complexes regulate postmitotic neuronal maturation and memory, and the SMARCD1 fly ortholog Bap60 is needed for context-dependent neuronal gene regulation during a juvenile circuit-forming window.
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes reached FDR<0.10, and neither DNA indels nor chromatin occupancy were measured.
summary: Acute Smarcd1 loss of function produced a real but very sparse response confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with Ankrd40 up and Ptpn3 down as the only downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The only robust postnatal neuronal transcriptomic effect of Smarcd1 in this screen is not a pan-neuronal BAF-collapse signature; it is a narrow thalamic signature that nominates Ptpn3 and Ankrd40 as sentinels for the one cell group that crossed the FDR gate.

literature_claim: SMARCD1, SMARCC2, SMARCE1, ARID1A/ARID1B, ARID2, and SMARCA2/SMARCA4 are related mSWI/SNF or Coffin-Siris-associated chromatin regulators, but BAF/PBAF/ncBAF assemblies are modular rather than equivalent.
main_caveats: The overlap is one gene, Ptpn3; Smarcd2 and Smarcd3 were not represented as perturbation targets, so direct SMARCD paralog compensation was not testable.
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut effect was shared only partially across BAF relatives: Ptpn3 was also down after Smarcc2, Smarce1, and Arid1a perturbation, whereas Arid2 had a larger thalamic signature without Ptpn3 and Smarca2, Smarca4, and Smarcc1 were flat in this same group.
why_it_matters: Smarcd1 behaves like a weak member of a thalamus-biased BAF-sensitive module rather than like a generic proxy for every mSWI/SNF subunit; the shared Ptpn3 repression preserves a same-direction molecular overlap, while the different signature sizes reject simple one-complex-one-phenotype interchangeability.

main_caveats: The cosine scan used Wilcoxon score vectors dominated by nonsignificant genes because Smarcd1 itself had only two FDR-significant downstream genes.
summary: Smarcd1 had no strong transcriptome-wide signed-score neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The best whole-signature cosines were small and were not accompanied by matching FDR-level downstream surfaces, so the two-gene Smarcd1 phenotype should not be over-interpreted as part of a broad recurrent perturbation module.

literature_claim: SMARCD1 is required in SMARCD1-mutant neurodevelopmental disease, fly memory-forming neurons, postmitotic mammalian BAF biology, and embryonic stem-cell differentiation.
main_caveats: The screen measures nuclear RNA rather than chromatin accessibility, morphology, or memory, and true DNA editing efficiency was not assayed.
summary: A P16 mosaic Smarcd1 loss-of-function perturbation does not recapitulate a broad Coffin-Siris or neural-BAF transcriptional state in young postmitotic mouse neurons.
why_it_matters: SMARCD1 is a congenital neurodevelopmental-disease gene, but its acute postnatal deletion was mostly buffered in this screen; that separates human CSS11 and early chromatin-specification biology from a simple mature-neuron haploinsufficiency model.

literature_claim: SMARCE1 is a common BAF subunit and nBAF complexes can regulate neuronal dendritic transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; the negative surface cannot exclude earlier developmental requirements.
summary: Smarce1 generated a robust downstream signature only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 16 FDR<0.10 genes versus zero in 21 other measured groups.
why_it_matters: A core chromatin-remodeling subunit did not behave as a pan-neuronal dependency after P16 loss; the responsive biology is concentrated in one thalamic state.

main_caveats: The marker claim is transcriptomic and limited to one thalamic cell group.
summary: The core 151 Smarce1 signature down-regulated Prkcd, Prkcb, Ptpn3 and Rasa4.
why_it_matters: Loss of Prkcd in a Prkcd-named thalamic group makes these kinase, phosphatase and Ras-regulatory transcripts candidate readouts of successful Smarce1 perturbation in this state.

direction: mixed; scaffold genes down and Dagla up
literature_claim: nBAF can regulate dendritic outgrowth programs, BEGAIN is postsynaptic-density associated, and endocannabinoids regulate synaptic transmission.
main_caveats: Only six FDR<0.10 genes support this program and no dendrite or synapse morphology was measured.
summary: Smarce1 loss in 151 suppressed a postsynaptic and membrane-lipid gene subset, including Begain, Lrrc7, Sdk2, Abhd12b and Serinc2, while increasing Dagla.
why_it_matters: The measured genes connect the BAF57 response to synaptic scaffold and endocannabinoid/lipid biology rather than only to chromatin machinery itself.

literature_claim: REEP2 is associated with ER membrane shaping and SLC25A37 with mitochondrial iron transport, but a SMARCE1-to-ER or SMARCE1-to-mitoferrin axis is not established.
main_caveats: The module is small and should not be over-read as a full ER stress, ISR or mitochondrial failure response.
summary: A small mixed ER, mitochondrial and redox module accompanied the 151 signature: Reep2, Slc25a37 and Msra decreased, while Ndufv3 and Acat1 increased.
why_it_matters: This suggests a candidate secondary organelle/metabolic adjustment to BAF57 loss in the responder, distinct from the primary down-regulation of Prkcd and synaptic genes.

literature_claim: SMARCE1, SMARCC2, ARID1A and ARID2 act in related mSWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling assemblies.
main_caveats: ARID1A and ARID2 convergence was partial; the comparison is restricted to the single Smarce1-responsive group.
summary: Smarcc2 was the top unbiased positive neighbor of Smarce1 and reproduced 12 of the 16 Smarce1 151 DEGs in the same direction; Arid1a and Arid2 reproduced smaller same-direction subsets.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation convergence ties the restricted Smarce1 phenotype to the BAF/PBAF chromatin-remodeling family instead of treating the 16 genes as an isolated list.

literature_claim: These genes encode BAF-family ATPase, core or subtype-associated subunits and were therefore plausible Smarce1 comparators.
main_caveats: Non-phenocopy may reflect paralog compensation, context-specific expression, or insufficient functional loss for individual comparator targets.
summary: Several represented BAF relatives failed to phenocopy Smarce1 in 151: Smarca2, Smarca4, Smarcc1 and Bicra had zero downstream genes there, whereas Smarcd1 and Arid1b had only two and one.
why_it_matters: The expected same-complex relationship is split into BAF nodes that converge with Smarce1 and BAF nodes that are buffered or dispensable in this postnatal thalamic context.

literature_claim: CHD4 is a catalytic CHD-family ATPase in the NuRD nucleosome-remodeling/deacetylase complex, a chromatin regulator distinct from BAF.
main_caveats: Only four Smarce1 FDR genes were significantly reversed by Chd4; this is a restricted-signature contrast.
summary: Chd4 was the strongest negative neighbor of the Smarce1 151 signature and reversed Begain, Abhd12b, Ccdc141 and Msra.
why_it_matters: The result separates two chromatin-remodeling directions in the same thalamic state: BAF57 loss lowers a subset of genes that NuRD/Chd4 loss raises.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: SMARCE1 is linked to Coffin-Siris syndrome through BAFopathy variants and to clear cell meningioma through loss-of-function mutations in a non-neuronal lineage.
main_caveats: Disease inference is indirect; the screen did not assay embryogenesis, patient missense alleles, meninges, chromatin accessibility, or tumorigenesis.
summary: Acute Smarce1 CRISPR loss after P16 spared most NeuN+ postmitotic neuronal transcriptomes and therefore did not mimic broad SMARCE1 developmental disease in this assay.
why_it_matters: The negative result warns against mapping SMARCE1 Coffin-Siris or meningioma mechanisms onto uniform mature-neuron loss-of-function; human pathology is likely earlier, allele-specific or meningeal-lineage displaced.

literature_claim: Cohesin depletion in immature postmitotic neurons changes neuronal transcription, synaptic, adhesion and connectivity programs.
main_caveats: Only one responding group was recovered; MB Dopa was not tested for Smc1a and several null groups had fewer than 50 perturbed nuclei.
summary: Smc1a loss produced a downstream transcriptomic response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: 34 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 20 other measured groups had 0 and 155 MB Glut had only target-transcript reduction.
why_it_matters: The screen recovers a highly restricted postnatal thalamic SMC1A-cohesin dependency rather than a pan-neuronal cohesin collapse.

literature_claim: Mouse neuronal cohesin depletion has been reported to reduce synaptic-transmission, adhesion, connectivity and neuronal-signaling genes and to impair synapse maturation.
main_caveats: Assignments are gene-set interpretation from Wilcoxon DE genes, not chromatin-contact measurements or electrophysiology.
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c response was dominated by down-regulation of adhesion, extracellular-matrix/guidance and excitability genes, including Ptprm, Spon1, Sema5a, Slit3, Adamts2, Adamts19, Dner, Atp2a2, Atp2b1, Grin2c, Grin2a, Pcp4, Necab2, Kcns2 and Lrrc7.
why_it_matters: These genes point to a postmitotic neuronal identity/connectivity output of cohesin rather than to sister-chromatid cohesion in dividing cells.

literature_claim: Somatic cohesin contains SMC1A-SMC3-RAD21 plus either STAG1 or STAG2, and STAG paralogs and HDAC8 have documented but context-specific cohesin functions.
main_caveats: SMC3, RAD21, NIPBL, WAPL and several other direct cohesin comparators were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Literature-obvious cohesin relatives diverged: Stag2 was the strongest same-direction Smc1a neighbor in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, sharing 14 of 34 Smc1a genes all in the same direction, whereas Stag1 shared none and Hdac8, Pds5a and Ncapd3 were flat in the same cell group.
why_it_matters: The result makes SA2/STAG2 the relevant variable cohesin subunit in this postnatal thalamic module and warns that cohesin regulators cannot be assumed to be interchangeable in neurons.

literature_claim: Cohesin and CTCF cooperate at loop boundaries but can have different effects on chromatin architecture and expression.
main_caveats: Inference is from RNA overlap only; the screen did not measure loop extrusion or CTCF occupancy.
summary: Ctcf perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut recovered only a partial Smc1a subset: 7 of the 34 Smc1a downstream genes, 6 in the shared direction and Sirt5 in the opposite direction.
why_it_matters: The overlap supports a CTCF-anchored loop component to the Smc1a module, but the limited intersection rejects a simple one-to-one CTCF phenocopy.

main_caveats: This comparator was computed only on the 34-gene Smc1a restricted signature in the responding thalamic class; some broad responders overlap many signatures.
summary: The data-driven 151 signature search nominated non-cohesin neighbors: Ctnnb1 and Psmb4 had the largest same-direction FDR overlap with Smc1a, Uba5 was high-overlap but mixed, and Sin3a was the clearest inverse neighbor.
why_it_matters: The Smc1a genes include a thalamic vulnerability/identity module that can be pushed by unrelated β-catenin, proteasome, UFMylation and chromatin-repressor perturbations, so the signature is not a private cohesin fingerprint.

literature_claim: Core SMC1A-cohesin loss in proliferating cells is tied to chromosomal instability, survival and checkpoint defects.
main_caveats: Absence was checked with sentinel transcripts and the FDR<0.10 signature, not with a formal genome-wide enrichment test.
summary: Only six Smc1a FDR<0.10 genes were up-regulated and they were heterogeneous; the sole downstream signature also lacked FDR<0.10 p53, integrated-stress, unfolded-protein, autophagy, or proteasome bounce-back sentinels such as Trp53, Cdkn1a, Bbc3, Atf4, Ddit3, Hspa5, Xbp1, Sqstm1, and Psmb7.
why_it_matters: Acute P16 Smc1a editing in NeuN+ neurons is read out as a selective gene-regulatory/excitability defect, not as the proliferative S-phase checkpoint or generic stress response expected from catastrophic cohesin loss.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Smchd1 loss can derepress inactive-X, imprinted, Pcdh, and Hox targets in developmental or engineered systems; FSHD2 arises from SMCHD1-dependent D4Z4 relaxation on a permissive human allele, and BAMS is driven by ATPase-domain SMCHD1 missense alleles.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not assayed; self-transcript depletion was weak as expected for this screen; cells were mixed-sex NeuN+ brain nuclei without human D4Z4, skeletal muscle, or nasal developmental lineages.
summary: Acute P16 Smchd1 loss was pan-null across the measured neuronal surface: every one of 22 tested groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the expected Pcdh, Hox, and imprinted-cluster candidates were also absent at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This separates a well-established developmental chromatin repressor from acute juvenile neuronal transcriptional maintenance: if Smchd1 was derepressing established clustered-protocadherin or imprinted loci in these postmitotic neurons, gene-level snRNA-seq should have recovered at least the Pcdh arm.

literature_claim: SMCHD1 and SETDB1/H3K9me3 intersect clustered-protocadherin regulation by restraining CTCF-dependent promoter-enhancer action.
main_caveats: Setdb1 and Ctcf are not in a linear one-to-one complex with Smchd1, so this is a pathway-level contrast rather than a strict epistasis test.
summary: The missing Smchd1 Pcdh phenotype is not a Pcdh detectability failure: Setdb1 loss up-regulated 15 Pcdh calls in 6 groups and Ctcf loss changed 48 Pcdh calls, mostly downward, while Smchd1 had no FDR-level Pcdh call among 1,496 Pcdh tests.
why_it_matters: Setdb1 and Ctcf perturbations show that the same nuclei, gene models, and Wilcoxon pipeline can register protocadherin superTAD disruption; Smchd1 therefore sits outside the acutely required Pcdh-maintenance node in this P16 neuronal assay or needs a different developmental/chromatin state.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: LRIF1/HP1 can load SMCHD1 onto H3K9me3 chromatin, and SMCHD1 and LRIF1 converge at D4Z4 while somatic loss of either factor can be transcriptionally buffered.
main_caveats: Lrif1 was compared only at gene-level snRNA-seq; D4Z4 itself is not present in the mouse-brain assay.
summary: The direct SMCHD1 recruitment partner Lrif1 phenocopied the Smchd1 nullity, with 0 FDR<0.10 genes in 22 groups and essentially no score-level correlation to Smchd1.
why_it_matters: The only directly measured SMCHD1-LRIF1 module member did not reveal a hidden LRIF1-only neuronal program; the pair behaves as a buffered somatic heterochromatin module in this system rather than as an acute transcriptional switch.

main_caveats: The correlation was intentionally computed on Wilcoxon scores because logFC values for genes near zero expression share dropout artifacts.
summary: The genome-wide signature-neighbor search did not nominate a meaningful convergent or antagonistic module for Smchd1; the strongest non-self Wilcoxon-score correlation was only r=0.027.
why_it_matters: The null signature is not merely being missed by canonical SMCHD1 priors; across 1,765 measurable perturbation profiles, both the nearest positive and negative neighbors were near zero and had sparse DE surfaces.

literature_claim: SMCHD1 contains an SMC hinge but is a noncanonical GHKL-ATPase homodimer, unlike cohesin SMC1/SMC3-family complexes.
main_caveats: The cohesin comparison is family-level rather than same-complex biology.
summary: Smchd1 was not interchangeable with canonical chromosome-architecture factors: Ctcf, Smc1a, and Stag2 produced robust DE, particularly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Smchd1 remained at 0 FDR<0.10 genes despite 152 perturbed Smchd1 nuclei.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues against a generic failure to perturb chromatin architectural proteins in postmitotic neurons and reinforces that noncanonical SMCHD1 is deployed differently from cohesin/CTCF in this acute setting.

literature_claim: RNF220, stabilized by ZC4H2, modulates Shh/Gli signaling during ventral spinal-cord patterning.
main_caveats: Single gene at FDR 0.099 with modest logFC; no canonical GLI target ensemble accompanied it.
summary: Smo loss produced a lone Rnf220-up transcript in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: RNF220 is positioned in Shh/Gli developmental regulation, so the only Smo-positive neuronal transcript is an E3/Gli modulator rather than a full Gli1/Ptch1/Hhip feedback ensemble.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Smoothened is the obligate transducer downstream of Patched and primary-ciliary GLI regulation, and active canonical Hedgehog signaling induces feedback genes including Gli1, Ptch1, and Hhip.
main_caveats: The assay measures acute sparse CRISPR in neuronal nuclei, not chronic ligand withdrawal, indel genotypes, astrocytes, or proliferating neural precursors.
summary: The expected canonical GLI feedback program was absent after Smo perturbation in all recovered neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: SMO loss in Hedgehog-competent cells should lower GLI activator output and reduce GLI1/PTCH/HHIP-type feedback transcripts; the complete absence of those markers argues that these P16-postmitotic NeuN+ neurons are not maintaining an active, cell-autonomous canonical Hedgehog transcriptome.

literature_claim: Ptch receptors, CDON-family co-receptors, GLI effectors, ciliary GPR161/cAMP regulators, and intraflagellar transport components all control Hedgehog signal transduction around SMO in Hh-responsive cells.
main_caveats: Some canonical relatives, including Sufu and Gli3 as perturbation targets, were not represented; Adcy3 is a ciliary marker but is not the dominant Hedgehog-repressive adenylyl cyclase in every tissue.
summary: Perturbing measurable Hedgehog neighbors did not reveal a coherent Smo-like or opposite module.
why_it_matters: Ptch1/Ptch2, Gli1/Gli2, Gpr161, Cdon, Ift88, Adcy3, and Rnf220 are expected to converge or oppose SMO when a Hedgehog circuit is active; their near-zero Smo cosines and lack of shared Rnf220 regulation show that the sparse Rnf220 hit is not a pathway-wide postnatal neuronal Hh signature.

main_caveats: Cosine was computed on signed Wilcoxon scores, and any whole-surface similarity is intrinsically unstable for a one-gene Smo signature.
summary: The unbiased Smo signature has no strong positive or negative neighbor in the model-visible perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The top score-cosine neighbors were absolute values below 0.04 and failed to share the 155 MB Glut Rnf220 hit, so the response is best treated as near-null rather than as a member of an unanticipated stress, proteostasis, or synaptic module.

literature_claim: ELFN2 is a postsynaptic cell-adhesion molecule involved in group III mGluR organization in brain.
main_caveats: The response consists of one downstream gene in 49 perturbed nuclei; SMS literature did not specifically predict Elfn2.
summary: Sms perturbation produced a one-gene FDR-level response, Elfn2 up-regulation, restricted to 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
why_it_matters: This is the only positive downstream Sms signal in the screen and points to a synaptic-adhesion gene rather than to the canonical lysosomal or oxidative programs expected from severe SRS models.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

literature_claim: Severe SMS deficiency can elevate spermidine:spermine ratio and compromise lysosomes, autophagy flux, oxidative balance, and mitochondrial function.

why_it_matters: The absence of a broad secondary stress signature is informative because severe SMS deficiency can damage lysosomes and mitochondria; the P16 sparse neuronal perturbation therefore did not drive cells into the known SRS stress state.

main_caveats: Foxn2 was only sub-threshold at FDR 0.130; protein and metabolite engagement were unmeasured.
summary: 191 MB P MY GABA reduced Sms mRNA but showed no robust downstream transcriptional response.

main_caveats: Neighbor cosines were very small and the Sms signature had only one downstream FDR-level gene.

literature_claim: Snai2/Slug is best established as a regulator of embryonic EMT and stem/progenitor programs rather than a broad postmitotic-neuronal regulator.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation was not assayed, and n_pert was 21-105 per group; the conclusion is a corrected single-nucleus transcriptomic negative in the sampled neuronal nuclei, not whole-organism absence of Snai2 biology.
summary: Snai2-targeted CRISPR was transcriptionally inert across the measured postnatal neuronal surface: 19 measured cell groups, 819 perturbed nuclei in aggregate, and 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 or FDR<0.25.
why_it_matters: This is the central result for Snai2 in this assay. A canonical EMT/stem-cell transcription factor did not trigger a stress, proteostasis, synaptic, or identity rebound in sparsely edited P16-P37/44 NeuN+ neuronal nuclei.

literature_claim: Snail2 can directly repress Cadherin6B during avian neural-crest EMT, and SNAI2 loss in humans affects neural-crest-derived melanocyte development.
main_caveats: The direct Cadherin6B literature is avian embryonic premigratory neural crest; the mouse neuronal assay would detect stable mRNA derepression if the same program were active but intentionally lacks the relevant neural-crest and epithelial lineages.
summary: The expected Slug/Snail2 EMT and neural-crest cadherin program was absent: Cdh1, Cdh6, Ocln, Vim, Fn1, Sox10, Tfap2a, Mitf, Pax3, Krt8, Krt18, and Krt19 all had adjusted P=1.0 in every Snai2-measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: Loss of a repressive EMT factor should derepress adhesion targets in premigratory neural crest, but these genes were either silent or unperturbed here; the screen therefore localizes the Snai2 cadherin/EMT module outside juvenile NeuN+ neurons.

literature_claim: Snail/Slug, ZEB, and Twist families are related core EMT transcription-factor families.

why_it_matters: The null is not simply that all EMT-adjacent transcription factors are invisible to the platform. ZEB paralogs can give neuronal signatures in this exact analysis universe, but those signatures occur in other cell groups and do not converge on Slug/Snai2.

main_caveats: The neighbor ranking used global Wilcoxon-score vectors because Snai2 had no FDR<0.10 genes on which to compute a restricted overlap.
summary: Across the complete model-visible universe, Snai2 had no meaningful whole-signature neighbor: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score correlation was Gabrg2 at r=0.0305 and the strongest negative was Bcl11a at r=-0.0170 over 321,942 matched rows.
why_it_matters: A near-origin signature can acquire formal neighbors by noise. Measuring the formal neighbors showed no Snai2-like downstream module, so no cross-perturbation convergence should be inferred for Slug.

why_it_matters: Snai2 can regulate metabolism through an adult hypothalamic LepRb-neuron epigenetic program, but the P16 acute CRISPR screen shows that basal mixed hypothalamic superclasses do not carry a broad Slug-dependent Lepr mRNA signature.

literature_claim: Single Snca-null mice are viable and show subtle presynaptic dopamine phenotypes, whereas stronger synuclein-family loss or aging exposes broader dysfunction and α-synuclein lowering is therapeutically plausible.
main_caveats: The screen measured RNA, not indels or α-synuclein protein; 215 MB Dopa, a key Parkinson-relevant lineage, was absent for Snca; the P37-44 endpoint cannot test aged synapse maintenance.
summary: Postnatal Snca loss produced a near-pan-neuronal transcriptional buffer: all 21 self-transcript rows trended negative, but 20 of 21 measured cell groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 gene and the whole Snca surface contained only one downstream hit.
why_it_matters: The dominant readout is not failed targeting; it is evidence that a sparse P16 single-gene Snca loss is tolerated at the neuronal nucleus level for 3-4 weeks, consistent with α-synuclein loss producing subtle presynaptic rather than large stress phenotypes in normal juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: Toxic α-synuclein overexpression can block ER-to-Golgi trafficking, and COPG2 encodes a COPI vesicle-coat component involved in Golgi trafficking.

summary: The only robust Snca downstream gene was an isolated decrease of Copg2, the COPI γ2 coatomer subunit, in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
why_it_matters: Copg2 gives the sole molecular foothold for an acute Snca LoF response and touches the secretory trafficking axis linked to α-synuclein toxicity, but its isolation and FDR of 0.0965 make it a hypothesis-generating Pvalb biomarker rather than a COPI pathway call.

literature_claim: α-synuclein is a synuclein-family presynaptic protein that promotes SNARE-complex assembly and shows stronger maintenance phenotypes when all three synucleins are removed.
