summary: Sptb sits in a locally buffered membrane-skeleton neighborhood: the represented αII-spectrin, ankyrin, and adducin perturbations were also null or one-to-two-gene responders in the same cell groups.
why_it_matters: The expected physical relatives were measured rather than assumed; their failure to generate large FDR surfaces argues that this postnatal snRNA screen is insensitive to many single-gene ankyrin/spectrin scaffold lesions as transcriptional perturbations.

main_caveats: The comparison used all Wilcoxon-score coordinates, so a target with no FDR-significant Sptb genes yields rankings among extremely small correlations.
summary: Sptb had no meaningful transcriptomic nearest neighbor; its strongest positive and negative whole-surface correlations were tiny.
why_it_matters: The top neighbor computation did not uncover a hidden disease or stress module: the closest positive score-vector match was Safe_target_30 at r=0.039, while the strongest anticorrelation, Wdr26 at r=-0.029, was a broad responder that simply diverged from Sptb flatness.

literature_claim: U2AF1 is a 3' splice-site recognition factor in the U2AF splicing complex, but no SPTLC2 literature predicts isolated U2af1 induction after Sptlc2 loss.
main_caveats: Each downstream hit is a singleton with FDR between 0.05 and 0.10 in roughly 50 perturbed cells; no multi-gene splicing module was recovered.
summary: Sptlc2 produced exactly two downstream FDR<0.10 hits: U2af1 up in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Creld1 down in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
why_it_matters: The real positive surface is almost minimal and cell-class restricted; neither hit is a recurrent sphingolipid or stress response, so they should be treated as low-confidence markers rather than a pathway.

literature_claim: SPT activity is essential under complete developmental loss, but Sptlc2 heterozygous mice are healthy and SPTLC2 loss-of-function is thought to be haplosufficient relative to dominant SPT overactivity alleles.
main_caveats: Target engagement at DNA was not measured; transcript loss does not quantify biallelic indel frequency.
summary: Pvalb, TH Prkcd Grin2c, and midbrain glutamatergic neurons showed significant Sptlc2 mRNA depletion but no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The most engaged-looking cell groups were the least supportive of an immediate transcriptional stress phenotype, consistent with postmitotic central neurons buffering partial SPTLC2 loss in this time window.

literature_claim: Sptlc2-deficient activated CD8 T cells can develop ER stress and cell death, and the UPR has IRE1, PERK and ATF6 transcriptional outputs that include ATF4, CHOP/DDIT3 and chaperone responses.
main_caveats: The comparator stress induction comes from unrelated target perturbations; the screen lacks lipid measurements and does not assay Xbp1 splicing directly.
summary: The expected ER-stress, ISR, autophagy and sphingolipid-compensation transcript program was absent across every Sptlc2 cell group.
why_it_matters: A lipid enzyme could have signaled its loss through ATF4/DDIT3/HSPA5/HERPUD1/XBP1 or autophagy genes even if the primary lipid defect was invisible to snRNA-seq; the complete absence of these significant calls turns the flat surface into an informative buffered response.

literature_claim: SPTLC2 HSAN1 variants bias substrate use toward alanine/glycine and newer SPTLC2 ALS variants are linked to loss of ORMDL-mediated inhibition rather than simple haploinsufficiency.
main_caveats: The disease-relevant lipid species were not measured, and peripheral sensory and spinal motor neurons were outside the sampled tissue.
summary: Sparse Sptlc2 CRISPR loss-of-function in juvenile central neurons did not phenocopy dominant SPTLC2 neuropathy or ALS mechanisms at the transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: The result supports a variant-class distinction: this assay removes Sptlc2 function, whereas many pathogenic SPTLC2 alleles redirect substrates toward 1-deoxysphingolipids or escape ORMDL feedback to overproduce canonical sphingolipids.

literature_claim: Biochemically close comparators would be SPT complex and downstream de novo sphingolipid enzymes; Asah1 is more distant, belonging to sphingolipid salvage rather than the SPT holoenzyme.
main_caveats: Most same-complex genes were not screened, and the top unbiased correlations were so small that they mainly certify nonconvergence.
summary: Neither unbiased score-neighbor search nor the represented sphingolipid salvage target Asah1 revealed a strong Sptlc2 phenocopy or inverse signature.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation universe converted an apparent flat target into a measurable negative result: Sptlc2 had no coherent transcriptomic neighbor, and pathway-obvious SPT-complex genes were absent as perturbation targets.

literature_claim: Canonical p62 biology would nominate proteostasis and stress pathways, not a three-cell-type, single-gene response surface.
main_caveats: Every downstream call is a single gene; DNA indel formation and p62 protein loss were not measured.
summary: Sqstm1 loss produced a very sparse neuronal transcriptional surface: only 3 of 22 measured cell groups had any downstream FDR<0.10 gene, and each responding group had exactly one such gene.
why_it_matters: In a young, baseline, postmitotic neuronal mosaic perturbation, p62 loss did not behave like a broad proteostasis catastrophe; the interpretable signal is a few cell-type-restricted single-gene responses.

literature_claim: LRFN/SALM proteins, including LRFN5/SALM5, are synaptic adhesion molecules with roles in synapse development and function.
main_caveats: No second Pvalb transcript reached FDR<0.10 after Sqstm1 perturbation, and the same Lrfn5 change recurred with only one other perturbation in this FDR-restricted scan.
summary: Pvalb interneurons were the only forebrain inhibitory class with a robust downstream hit, down-regulating the synaptic adhesion-family transcript Lrfn5.
why_it_matters: The Pvalb hit nominates a synapse-facing rather than canonical autophagy transcript as the most specific forebrain readout of acute Sqstm1 loss, but it remains a one-gene biomarker candidate.

literature_claim: Biallelic SQSTM1 absence has been tied to defective response to mitochondrial depolarization, MICU3 regulates mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake, and SFXN5 is a mitochondrial sideroflexin.
main_caveats: Each cell group contributes one FDR<0.10 mitochondrial gene; no broader mitophagy or oxidative-stress transcript set was induced.
summary: The two non-cortical glutamatergic responses pointed to mitochondrial ion-homeostasis genes: Sfxn5 decreased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Micu3 increased in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This is the only downstream theme that recurred across Sqstm1 responders and is directionally compatible with p62 disease literature that links complete p62 loss to mitochondrial-stress handling, but the measured module is minimal.

literature_claim: p62 and NBR1 connect ubiquitinated cargo and p62 droplets to stress-selective autophagy and Keap1-Nrf2 signaling, whereas autophagy blockade can act through p62 accumulation.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot measure p62 bodies, LC3 lipidation, or autophagic flux directly; it only rejects a robust secondary mRNA program.
summary: Canonical p62-adjacent NRF2/redox, lysosomal-autophagy, proteasome, UPR, and ISR transcripts were absent from the Sqstm1 FDR<0.10 surface.
why_it_matters: Because this assay would have detected a secondary antioxidant or stress transcriptional program, the absence is informative: basal p62 loss left young neurons buffered rather than mounting a detectable Keap1-Nrf2 or unfolded-protein response.

literature_claim: UBA5 activates the UFM1 conjugation cascade and biallelic UBA5 variants can cause early-onset encephalopathy.
main_caveats: This was a restricted comparison over only three Sqstm1 DE features; the Sqstm1-Uba5 whole-surface score correlation was near zero.
summary: Uba5 was the strongest FDR-restricted same-direction neighbor of Sqstm1, sharing Sfxn5 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Micu3 up-regulation in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The recurrence links the sparse Sqstm1 mitochondrial genes to UFM1-pathway perturbation, a proteostasis system with independent neuronal-disease relevance, rather than to the textbook p62 interactors.

literature_claim: p62 acts within selective autophagy and Keap1-Nrf2 signaling, but p62 accumulation downstream of autophagy failure is itself a disease-driving state.
main_caveats: Some core autophagy comparators, especially Atg16l1, had fewer perturbed cells in several groups; Nbr1 itself could not be tested as a target.
summary: Literature-obvious autophagy, NRF2, NF-kB, mTOR, and lysosomal comparators did not phenocopy Sqstm1, and the closest p62-family receptor Nbr1 was not a represented perturbation target.
why_it_matters: The result separates loss of the p62 cargo receptor from global autophagy blockade or NRF2/NF-kB pathway knockout in these postmitotic neurons.

main_caveats: A three-feature target necessarily makes any FDR-overlap neighbor exploratory.
summary: No global positive or inverse signature neighbor was convincing: Esr2, Gprasp2, Adgrg2, and Wdr26 were the top whole-surface score hits but had near-zero correlations and no robust shared Sqstm1 features.
why_it_matters: This rejects the possibility that the Sqstm1 phenotype is simply a weak copy or inverse copy of a broad perturbation already present in the dataset.

literature_claim: SREBP1C preferentially activates fatty-acid and triglyceride synthesis genes, whereas SREBP2 is biased toward cholesterol biosynthesis.
main_caveats: The assay lacks DNA indel sequencing and measures RNA, not SREBP1 cleavage or lipid metabolites.
summary: Srebf1-targeting CRISPR produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic effect in any of the 23 recovered neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: SREBP1 is a transcription factor, so an active basal SREBP1 lipogenic program should have appeared directly in snRNA-seq; the complete absence of Acaca/Fasn/Scd/Elovl6, sterol-gene, Gria2, Nfe2l1, or proteasome responses makes the result a biological basal-state negative rather than a failed self-knockdown call.

literature_claim: SREBP1 and SREBP2 share the SREBP activation architecture but have biased, non-identical outputs and can compensate in some Srebp1-null metabolic tissues.
main_caveats: Srebf2 had no row in 215 MB Dopa and had many groups where only its own transcript reached FDR; the contrast is strongest in the groups with downstream sterol genes.
summary: The direct paralog Srebf2, but not Srebf1, drove a detectable sterol-biosynthetic loss signature in the same neuronal survey.
why_it_matters: The Srebf1 null is not explained by inability of SREBP-family lipid transcripts to be measured: Srebf2 perturbation lowered Insig1, Dhcr24, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Fdft1, Hmgcs1, Sqle, and Ldlr in hypothalamic, thalamic, and midbrain/posterior GABA/glutamate groups in which Srebf1 had zero significant genes.

literature_claim: mTORC1 promotes SREBP-dependent lipid transcription in cultured and hepatic systems, and TSC2 is a negative regulator of mTORC1.
main_caveats: Tsc2 is pleiotropic and produced many non-sterol DE genes; Rptor and Mtor did not reproduce the sterol program in this sparse CRISPR assay.
summary: A Tsc2/Srebf2-opposed sterol module was present, whereas Srebf1 was uncoupled from that neuronal mTORC1-responsive lipid arm.
why_it_matters: Tsc2 loss up-regulated the same sterol genes that Srebf2 loss down-regulated, especially in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, placing the detectable module on a TSC2-to-SREBF2 axis rather than on Srebf1 under basal postmitotic conditions.

009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Similarity was computed on complete Wilcoxon score vectors, so with a flat target the ranking is dominated by residual rank noise rather than significant genes.
summary: Whole-signature neighbors of Srebf1 were themselves near-null, so the closest cosine relationships are not interpretable as a shared pathway.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive and negative neighbors had absolute cosine values below 0.032, and their measured DE surfaces either had no downstream FDR genes or isolated singletons; this rejects Fam149b, Slc32a1, Ep300, Npy1r, Fbxo11, and Vps13b as convergent biology with Srebf1.

literature_claim: Neuronal activity or pathological NMDA receptor activation can regulate nuclear SREBP1, and SREBP1 activation contributes to excitotoxic or ischemic neuronal injury.
main_caveats: The screen did not impose glutamate, ischemia, or seizure-like stimulation and did not measure neuronal survival directly.
summary: The screen does not support a constitutive stress, proteasome, or lipid-toxicity response to Srebf1 loss in juvenile neurons; SREBP1 neurotoxicity is likely activation-context dependent.
why_it_matters: Reports that NMDA receptor stress activates SREBP1 through Insig1 degradation motivate SREBP1-lowering strategies for excitotoxic injury, but the P16-P37 basal CRISPR readout did not induce Insig1, Nfe2l1, proteasome, or sterol-gene changes, so this dataset cannot be read as a stroke-like SREBP1 activation model.

literature_claim: Developing neural cells need endogenous cholesterol synthesis, whereas some adult neurons can survive loss of cell-autonomous cholesterol synthesis by using glial sterols.
main_caveats: The MB Dopa group was not recovered for Srebf2, L5/6 IT is a one-gene edge call, and non-neuronal glia were largely absent from the assay.
summary: Srebf2 loss did not trigger a pan-neuronal lipid response; the FDR<0.10 sterol program was concentrated in hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, and pontine/myelencephalic groups, with only an edge Dhcr24 hit in cortical L5/6 IT neurons.
why_it_matters: SREBP2 is a ubiquitous cholesterol-homeostasis regulator on paper, but this P16-to-P37/44 mosaic neuronal knockout exposed a restricted set of postmitotic neurons that still transcribe an autonomous SREBP2 sterol regulon.

literature_claim: SREBP-2 activates LDL receptor and cholesterol-biosynthesis genes and Srebf2 loss reduces SREBP target expression in hypomorphic mouse tissue.
main_caveats: The assay is nuclear RNA; it did not measure sterol abundance or biosynthetic flux.
summary: The responder genes form a compact SREBP2 cholesterol-biosynthesis module: Dhcr24, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, Hmgcs1, Fdft1, Fdps, Sqle, and Lss were all down-regulated where Srebf2 responded.
why_it_matters: The direction matches direct loss of a transcriptional activator of sterol synthesis rather than an indirect stress signature; 33 of the 34 significant downstream rows were decreases.

literature_claim: INSIG proteins retain SCAP/SREBP in the ER and promote sterol-stimulated HMGCR degradation.
main_caveats: The compensatory interpretation is inferred from Insig1 RNA loss; SCAP trafficking and HMGCR protein turnover were not measured.
summary: Insig1 was the most recurrent Srebf2-dependent gene, falling in six responder groups, while Ldlr fell only in the two strongest MB/P-MY signatures.
why_it_matters: INSIG1 is both an SREBP target and a brake on SCAP/SREBP trafficking and HMGCR stability, so its loss is a built-in partial release of feedback inhibition in cells that have lost SREBP2-driven cholesterol transcription.

literature_claim: Srebf2 deficiency in embryos and liver can affect Srebf1 isoforms and fatty-acid synthesis genes, while SREBP-2 canonical activity is cholesterol-biased.
main_caveats: Absence is defined at FDR<0.10 in snRNA-seq; lowly expressed fatty-acid genes could be missed.
summary: Srebf2 loss in postnatal neurons was sterol-selective rather than broadly lipogenic: Acaca in 155 MB Glut was the only canonical fatty-acid enzyme among the 34 significant downstream rows.
why_it_matters: This separates the juvenile neuronal response from embryo and liver settings where Srebf2 deficiency can secondarily deplete Srebf1 isoforms and fatty-acid synthesis genes.

literature_claim: SREBP2 activates cholesterol biosynthesis genes and the INSIG feedback circuit.
main_caveats: Dhcr24 alone supported the L5/6 IT call, and Insig1 alone supported 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
summary: Dhcr24, Insig1, Cyp51, and Msmo1 were the most recurrent Srebf2-responsive genes and provide a short neuronal engagement panel.
why_it_matters: These genes marked multiple responder classes more reliably than late singletons such as Hmgcr or Lss, so they are better RNA biomarkers for SREBP2 activity in similar neuronal screens.

literature_claim: MARCH6/MARCHF6 controls squalene monooxygenase, HMGCR, and flux through cholesterol synthesis.
main_caveats: Marchf6 matched Srebf2 in 110/151/155 but not in the broadest Srebf2 group, 191 MB P MY GABA.
summary: Marchf6 knockdown, an ER-ubiquitin control point in cholesterol synthesis, was an inverse Srebf2 neighbor and up-regulated 12 of the Srebf2 sterol features at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The opposite Marchf6/Srebf2 RNA signatures connect the neuronal Srebf2 regulon to an ER-associated enzyme-turnover node, but the direction of this transcriptional response is a measured result rather than a simple prediction from MARCH6 biochemistry.

main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to Srebf2 significant sterol features; it identifies convergence but not the upstream mechanism.
summary: The strongest data-driven inverse neighbors were not the canonical SREBP machinery: Mib1 and Dctn1 each up-regulated 32 of the 34 Srebf2 sterol features at FDR<0.10, and Txndc15 was weaker with 5 inverse overlaps.
why_it_matters: This nominates unexpected perturbations that activate the same neuronal cholesterol regulon that Srebf2 is required to maintain, while preserving Txndc15 as subdominant rather than equivalent to Mib1 or Dctn1.

main_caveats: This is a restricted-signature comparison; Phf12 and Uba5 have far broader transcriptional effects than Srebf2.
summary: Among same-direction data-driven neighbors, Phf12 and Uba5 reproducibly lowered the Srebf2 sterol features, whereas Slc7a6os was rejected after FDR-overlap testing.
why_it_matters: The cholesterol module is not unique to Srebf2: unrelated perturbations can make neurons converge onto the same down-regulated sterol state, but logFC-only similarity overcalled Slc7a6os.

literature_claim: SREBP-2 and SREBP-1 are paralogous lipid transcription factors and HMGCR is a major SREBP-regulated enzyme in cholesterol synthesis.
main_caveats: Srebf1 is likely barely active in these neuronal nuclei, and Hmgcr enzymatic loss could be buffered at the protein or lipid level rather than RNA.
summary: The measured obvious relatives did not phenocopy Srebf2: Srebf1 produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in all 23 groups, and Hmgcr produced only two non-sterol hits with no overlap to the Srebf2 signature.
why_it_matters: The Srebf2 neuronal phenotype is not explained by generic SREBP-family knockdown or by perturbing one rate-limiting cholesterol enzyme; it is specifically the transcriptional SREBP2 regulon that is visible here.

literature_claim: SR converts L-serine to the NMDAR coagonist D-serine, and genetic or postsynaptic SR loss is expected to reduce D-serine bioavailability and NMDAR-dependent plasticity.
main_caveats: Sparse CRISPR engagement was not measured by DNA indel sequencing, and D-serine abundance and NMDAR currents were not assayed.
summary: Srr is a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null in this P16-to-P37/44 sparse CRISPR assay: 20 tested cell groups had 0 genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The screen did not uncover a secondary stress, proteostasis, activity, synaptic, redox, autophagy, or compensatory mRNA program after acute neuronal Srr loss. The result is a strong basal-snRNA negative result, not proof that serine racemase biology is absent.

literature_claim: D-serine gates GluN1-containing NMDARs, so GRIN subunits are the immediate receptor-level comparators for Srr.
main_caveats: The receptor-subunit perturbations had their own guide efficiencies and cell counts; Grin2d and Grin3a themselves were weak or flat in this matched surface.
summary: Srr did not phenocopy direct NMDAR-subunit perturbation: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced 144, 31, and 83 FDR<0.10 genes in the same 20 cell groups, whereas Srr produced none and had near-zero score correlations with those targets.
why_it_matters: This separates a diffusible coagonist-supply enzyme from cell-autonomous loss of the receptor core and argues that the Srr null is specific to metabolite/coagonist biology rather than a generic failure to detect NMDAR-pathway perturbations.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on all measured scores, not on Srr FDR genes because there were none.
summary: Whole-surface signature search found no meaningful Srr neighbor: the largest positive Wilcoxon-score correlation was Wdr26 at r=0.0387, and the largest negative was Trpm7 at r=-0.0215.
why_it_matters: The empirical neighborhood places Srr at the noise floor, with safe-target controls among the top ranks and no shared FDR signal, so the null is not hiding a weak version of a known stress or translation module.

literature_claim: SR loss has been tied to developmental synaptogenesis, NMDAR-dependent LTP, GluN2B compensation, BDNF/Akt/mTOR changes, and excitotoxic protection.
main_caveats: The dataset was unstimulated and nucleus-based; phosphorylation, receptor trafficking, D-serine, and synaptic physiology were not measured.
summary: Canonical NMDAR-response and compensation transcripts were absent after Srr perturbation: Arc, Fos, Egr1, Npas4, Bdnf, Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b were never significant in any Srr-tested group.
why_it_matters: Srr disease and neuroprotection phenotypes are likely to be read out first in D-serine abundance, NMDAR currents, LTP, spine biology, or evoked activity rather than in a basal single-nucleus RNA biomarker panel after sparse postnatal LoF.

literature_claim: SSR4/TRAPδ acts at ER entry and N-glycosylation, and PPIB/cyclophilin B is an ER/secretory-pathway foldase.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene passed FDR<0.10, in 47 perturbed nuclei, with no protein or glycosylation readout.
summary: Ssr4 loss produced a single ER-luminal foldase hit, Ppib down in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, without a broader ER-stress or glycosylation transcriptome.
why_it_matters: The only downstream signal lies in the correct organelle class for TRAP biology, but the one-gene and negative direction argue for a narrow local response rather than canonical UPR induction.

literature_claim: SSR4 deficiency is expected to alter TRAP-complex protein abundance and N-glycosylation at the ER.
main_caveats: A lower Ssr4 RNA row does not quantify DNA indels or TRAPδ protein loss.
summary: Three neuronal groups lowered the Ssr4 self-transcript at FDR<0.10 but had no downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result separates visible perturbation of Ssr4 RNA from activation of a secondary transcriptional ER-stress program.

literature_claim: Loss of ER folding/translocation capacity can activate UPR and ERAD genes centered on BiP/HSPA5, and Sec63 acts with BiP at the ER translocon.
main_caveats: The comparison is cross-target rather than same-complex; Ssr1-Ssr3 perturbations were not available.
summary: ER-biogenesis comparators Hspa5 and Sec63 induced detectable ER-stress/ER-translocation programs in matched thalamic or midbrain groups, whereas Ssr4 did not.
why_it_matters: This rejects a generic claim that the Ssr4 null is due to inability of the screen to recover UPR transcripts; ER stress was visible, but for Hspa5/Sec63 rather than Ssr4.

main_caveats: Cosine similarity over near-null z-score surfaces is useful for rejecting strong neighbors, not for resolving weak biology.
summary: Data-driven Ssr4 signature neighbors were negligible across the whole model-visible target universe.
why_it_matters: The top raw neighbors did not share significant genes with Ssr4, preventing a weak one-gene target from being over-labeled as part of an unrelated Smo, Zfp236, Flt3, Zdhhc17, Agtrap, or Dnajc13 module.

literature_claim: Human SSR4 loss of function causes a congenital disorder of glycosylation through TRAP-complex and N-glycosylation defects.
main_caveats: The assay cannot measure glycan occupancy, ER import efficiency, or TRAP protein destabilization directly.
summary: The SSR4-CDG prior does not translate into a broad postmitotic neuronal UPR or N-glycosylation RNA signature after P16 Ssr4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Congenital SSR4 disease can remain compatible with this dataset if the relevant neuronal injury is earlier, protein/glycan-level, or confined to particular high-secretory client loads rather than a pan-neuronal UPR transcriptionopathy.

literature_claim: SSTR5 is a Gi/o-coupled somatostatin receptor, and rodent brain studies report receptor expression in parts of the nervous system, including mouse cortical inhibitory interneurons.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure DNA indels, ligand-evoked second-messenger coupling, electrophysiology, pituitary, pancreas, olfactory bulb, or non-neuronal cells.
summary: Sstr5 loss produced no FDR-supported neuronal transcriptome in any recovered taxonomy group.
why_it_matters: The dominant phenotype is a hard negative across 23 postmitotic NeuN+ neuronal groups, not a hidden cell-type-restricted program: no synaptic, stress, cAMP, proteostasis, or compensatory gene set had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.

literature_claim: Somatostatin receptors signal through Gi/o to inhibit adenylyl cyclase and can couple to calcium, potassium, and CB1-dependent GPCR signaling.
main_caveats: Shared absence is not a phenocopy; most effector perturbations also had sparse on-target information, except Prkaca, and direct Sstr paralogs were absent from the target set.
summary: The Sstr5-null surface did not phenocopy represented Gi/o, cAMP/PKA, calcium, GIRK, or CB1-crosstalk nodes.
why_it_matters: The absence of an Sstr5 transcriptome is supported by matched pathway controls: Sstr1-Sstr4 were not perturbation targets, while Gnao1, Adcy1, Adcy5, Prkaca, Cacna1a, Kcnj6, and Cnr1 were nearly all transcriptionally flat in the same brain-cell taxonomy.

main_caveats: Neighboring used global Wilcoxon z-score correlations; for a target with no FDR genes, tiny nonzero ranks should be interpreted only as a null-distribution check.
summary: Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis placed Sstr5 on the noise floor rather than in a coherent perturbation module.
why_it_matters: The strongest genome-wide correlations were only r=0.040 to r=-0.015 and included safe-target controls; unrelated real responders such as Stxbp1 and Wdr26 had many FDR-supported genes but still did not converge with Sstr5.

literature_claim: SSTR5 knockout changes pancreatic insulin/glucose physiology, and somatostatin receptor ligands are used or studied in pituitary and neuroendocrine tumors.
main_caveats: The dataset has no endocrine tissues and no hormone-secretion readout, so it cannot rank endocrine efficacy or endocrine adverse physiology.
summary: The negative brain result should be read as context displacement of endocrine SSTR5 pharmacology, not as evidence that SSTR5 antagonism or agonism is biologically inert.
why_it_matters: Known SSTR5 phenotypes are strongest in hormone-secreting pituitary and pancreatic settings and often concern secretion rather than steady-state neuronal mRNA, both of which are outside a P16 AAV, NeuN+ brain snRNA-seq screen.

literature_claim: PGGT1B encodes the beta subunit of CAAX protein geranylgeranyltransferase type I; no prior source predicted Pggt1b induction downstream of GM3 synthase loss.
main_caveats: The St3gal5 downstream signature contains only one FDR<0.10 gene, just below q=0.10; no lipid or protein-prenylation measurements were made.
summary: St3gal5 produced a single downstream hit, Pggt1b up in 155 MB Glut, and this was the top Pggt1b induction among all target perturbations measured in that cell group.
why_it_matters: The only FDR-supported responder is preserved as a real but narrow biomarker hypothesis instead of being lost in the otherwise flat surface.

literature_claim: Patient neural-crest models and germline mouse models predict loss of GM3-derived gangliosides, altered receptor/cell-surface state, apoptosis, altered glucose metabolism, and seizure susceptibility after GM3 synthase loss.
main_caveats: The assay cannot see the primary lipid defect, and the perturbation is sparse and postnatal rather than germline.
summary: The St3gal5 surface lacks a canonical GM3-ganglioside, glucose/mitochondrial, immediate-early, UPR/ISR, or apoptosis transcriptional program despite on-target St3gal5 RNA reduction in many groups.
why_it_matters: GM3 synthase loss is expected to cause a biochemical ganglioside lesion, but this screen shows that acute P16 postmitotic neuronal loss does not automatically propagate to a broad nuclear stress or metabolic state.

literature_claim: SPTLC2 initiates sphingolipid biosynthesis upstream of the ceramide-to-LacCer substrate pool used by ST3GAL5, so it is a measurable lipid-pathway comparator but not the same enzymatic step.
main_caveats: Core GM3 paralogs and downstream enzymes were not represented as target perturbations, leaving only upstream or catabolic lipid comparators.
summary: Represented sphingolipid comparators do not phenocopy St3gal5: Sptlc2 responds in 007 and 027 where St3gal5 is flat or weak, and Sptlc2, Asah1, and Psap do not reproduce the 155 MB Glut Pggt1b signal.
why_it_matters: The comparison argues against interpreting Pggt1b as a generic sphingolipid-biosynthesis stress response.

literature_claim: ARX, CDKL5, KCNQ2, CNTNAP2, MECP2, and ST3GAL3-related disorders are clinical differentials for GM3 synthase deficiency because they can share seizures and developmental delay.

main_caveats: The neighbor metric used a restricted 220-feature vector of nominal St3gal5 rows because the actual FDR<0.10 downstream signature had only one gene.

literature_claim: Gabra1 encodes the mouse GABA-A receptor alpha-1 subunit.

why_it_matters: Gabra1 down-regulation is the only point on the 21-group Stag1 surface that survives correction, so any positive Stag1 biology in this screen is thalamic and GABA-A-receptor centered rather than a broad chromatin or stress program.

literature_claim: SA1/STAG1 and SA2/STAG2 are cohesin-ring variants with both specialized and redundant gene-regulatory roles rather than obligate one-to-one substitutes.

summary: The measured cohesin relatives did not phenocopy Stag1: Stag2 opposed the Stag1 Gabra1 effect while Smc1a, Pds5a, Hdac8, and Ctcf were absent or transcriptionally distinct.
why_it_matters: The result argues that a postnatal Stag1 gRNA does not simply report generic cohesin loss in neurons; SA paralog identity and auxiliary cohesin regulators remain separable in this in-vivo neuronal assay.

main_caveats: The FDR-level Stag1 signature has one gene; the full-vector correlation range was compressed and non-anticorrelated, so this is a restricted-signature observation.
summary: Data-driven neighbor analysis collapsed to a one-gene 151 TH Gabra1 axis rather than a multi-gene Stag1 module.
why_it_matters: The strongest same-feature neighbors were functionally diverse perturbations, and the all-feature top neighbor was a flat safe-target profile; thus Gabra1 is best treated as a fragile recurrent thalamic state marker, not as a Stag1-specific cohesin biomarker.

literature_claim: Core RAD21 loss in mouse postmitotic cortical neurons reduces long-loop synaptic, glutamatergic, and late activity-regulated genes.
main_caveats: The literature comparator removes RAD21 or STAG proteins much more completely than this pooled AAV CRISPR mRNA readout demonstrates for Stag1; stimulation-dependent defects could also be missed at baseline.

why_it_matters: The null transcriptome is biologically interpretable: acute postnatal reduction of one SA paralog is far weaker than removing the core cohesin ring during immature cortical-neuron differentiation, so the assay refines the neuronal cohesin prior down to Stag1-specific sufficiency.

literature_claim: STAG2 and other cohesin perturbations can regulate neuronal and oligodendrocyte transcriptional programs, but the published brain models used stronger, earlier, lineage-wide deletions.
main_caveats: AAV CRISPR was sparse and DNA indels were not measured; the Stag2 transcript itself was not significantly depleted in any group, which is expected for this readout and neither proves nor disproves protein loss.
summary: Stag2 produced a single robust response, 55 FDR<0.10 genes, in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and zero FDR<0.10 genes in every other measured Stag2 cell group; 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
why_it_matters: The screen places the postnatal LOF-sensitive neuronal state in a narrow thalamic glutamatergic class rather than across all NeuN+ neurons.

literature_claim: Human STAG2 loss-of-function variants cause neurodevelopmental cohesinopathy, and cohesin depletion in immature postmitotic neurons down-regulates genes related to synaptic transmission, neuronal development, adhesion, connectivity, and signaling.
main_caveats: The DE list is small enough that it is a module, not a genome-wide collapse; chromatin loops were not assayed in these nuclei.
summary: The thalamic Stag2 signature is dominated by down-regulated adhesion, extracellular-matrix, synaptic, and neuronal-signaling genes including Ptprm, Ptprz1, Adamts2, Adamts19, Sema5a, Necab2, Npy1r, Lrrc7, Sez6, Asic2, Begain, and Aplp2.
why_it_matters: The affected gene classes match the neuronal programs that depend on cohesin-mediated long-range chromatin contacts, but here they emerge after P16 Stag2 loss rather than after embryonic Rad21 depletion.

literature_claim: Published neuron cohesin depletion emphasized loss of maturation and synaptic programs.
main_caveats: The up genes are an inferred compensation/remodeling arm; no time course is present to order cause and compensation.
summary: A smaller up-regulated arm, Stmn2, Nipa1, Tspan5, Gabra1, Syt11, Inhbb, Atl1, Tubb4b, Ntm, Adgrl3, Rab6b, and Sav1, accompanies the down-regulated thalamic module.
why_it_matters: The response looks like membrane, neurite, and signaling remodeling layered on a cohesin-sensitive neuronal maintenance program, not simple toxicity.

literature_claim: SMC1A and STAG2 are both cohesin components, and cohesin loss perturbs chromatin-loop-dependent neuronal transcription.
main_caveats: Smc1a had 35 total significant genes versus 55 for Stag2, so convergence is partial.
summary: Smc1a was the strongest positive Stag2 neighbor over the 55-gene thalamic signature, with cosine 0.905 and 14 same-direction shared FDR genes, whereas data-driven negative neighbors had no FDR-supported opposite overlaps.
why_it_matters: A core cohesin subunit independently recovers part of the Stag2 module in the same cell group, supporting an on-cohesin interpretation of the Stag2 signature.

literature_claim: STAG1 and STAG2 have overlapping but distinct cohesin functions, PDS5 proteins regulate cohesin function, and HDAC8 controls the cohesin acetylation cycle.
main_caveats: The assay tested single perturbations in postmitotic neurons; it did not test STAG1 plus STAG2 double loss, PDS5B, or dividing cells.
summary: The literature-obvious relatives Stag1, Pds5a, and Hdac8 did not phenocopy Stag2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Stag1 had only an opposite Gabra1 call, and Pds5a and Hdac8 had no FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The thalamic response distinguishes the STAG2/SMC1A arm from the STAG1 paralog and from several cohesin-cycle regulators in this P16 neuronal assay.

literature_claim: CTCF is a cohesin-associated loop-boundary factor; the Elp1, Brd4, and Ctnnb1 overlaps were data-driven rather than expected same-complex relationships.
main_caveats: The conclusion is based on overlap within the 55 Stag2 genes; each comparator has hundreds of additional DE genes.
summary: Ctcf, Elp1, Brd4, and Ctnnb1 shared the Stag2 thalamic module only as a restricted sub-signature nested inside much larger or broader transcriptional responses.
why_it_matters: The data nominate a thalamic maintenance module that can be reached from cohesin/CTCF and from non-cohesin chromatin or signaling perturbations; it should not be interpreted as STAG2-specific simply because it is strongest in Stag2.

main_caveats: Primary lipid composition, cristae structure, CoQ transport and ferroptosis were not directly assayed; DNA indel burden and STARD7 protein loss were unmeasured.

why_it_matters: The single-gene response nominates a narrow ubiquitin-adaptor/protein-damage marker rather than the broad mitochondrial ISR expected from complete STARD7 loss, but it is a hypothesis rather than a pathway call.

summary: A matched mitochondrial perturbation, Opa1, strongly induced an amino-acid/ISR and mitochondrial transcript program in 191 MB P MY GABA, whereas Stard7 was reduced to Pcmtd1 alone in the same control stratum.
why_it_matters: The absence of Ddit3, Chac1, Herpud1, Shmt2, Mars1 and depressed mt-transcripts after Stard7 is therefore not a generic limitation of single-nucleus Wilcoxon testing in this cell class.

why_it_matters: This turns a genome-wide absence into the central result: in the unchallenged P16-to-P37/P44 NeuN+ brain, STAT1 is not detectably maintaining a basal postmitotic neuronal transcriptional program, even though its canonical IFN outputs are strongly transcriptional in stimulated cells.

Instead, 13 directly measured receptor, IRF, NF-κB, ISGF3, and STAT-paralog comparators produced only five isolated one-gene calls across 290 surfaces and no recurrent IFN module.

why_it_matters: A same-pathway comparison argues that basal postnatal neurons do not translate partial WNK-SPAK/CCC loss into a common snRNA-seq signature; the expected biology remains a phosphorylation and chloride-flux axis.

main_caveats: The comparison used Wilcoxon-score vectors, so it is sensitive to weak nominal ranks; the important result is the tiny absolute correlation, not the identities of the nominal neighbors.
summary: The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no coherent Stk39 neighbor or anti-neighbor; the largest Wilcoxon-score correlations across 355046 matched entries were only +0.032 and -0.027.
why_it_matters: The Stk39 vector is dominated by residual rank noise rather than a latent module shared with another perturbation in the measured universe.

literature_claim: SPAK loss-of-function mice show renal NCC/NKCC2 and vascular NKCC1 phenotypes, and common human STK39 variants have been associated with blood pressure.
main_caveats: Kidney, vascular, and non-neuronal brain cells were not sampled; this is a compartment-refinement rather than a direct test of hypertension biology.
summary: The mouse-neuron Stk39 null does not phenocopy the established renal and vascular SPAK biology that links STK39 to blood pressure.
why_it_matters: It localizes the strong SPAK loss-of-function phenotypes away from this sparse NeuN+ postnatal brain-transcriptome axis and cautions against using a flat neuronal DE surface to argue that the kinase is dispensable in kidney or vascular smooth muscle.

literature_claim: Stmn2 is a neuronal stathmin-family axonal protein whose strong mouse phenotypes are motor/sensory axonal and neuromuscular rather than necessarily acute pan-brain nuclear transcriptomic.
main_caveats: The screen lacks indel and protein measurements; FDR support for the lone downstream hit is at the 10%, not 5%, threshold.
summary: Acute P16 Stmn2 CRISPR loss was almost completely transcriptionally buffered: only one downstream gene, Tuba1a in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, reached FDR<0.10 across 22 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: This establishes that a visible Stmn2 self-transcript reduction can coexist with almost no somatic nuclear DE, so the major biology of Stmn2 loss in this experiment is displaced away from a broad cell-body transcriptional stress response.

literature_claim: Stathmins tune α/β-tubulin heterodimer dynamics and TUBA1A is a major neuronal α-tubulin isotype.
main_caveats: The signature consists of one FDR<0.10 gene; adjacent tubulin, growth-associated, neurofilament, and axon-survival genes were not significant.
summary: The only downstream response was selective Tuba1a down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Tuba1a encodes a neuronal α-tubulin isotype, so this single hit is a narrow microtubule-subunit adjustment, not a full axon-injury, neurofilament, or stress program.

literature_claim: Stmn2 is mechanistically connected to tubulin and microtubule dynamics, so tubulin and microtubule-associated perturbations are obvious comparators.
main_caveats: Several comparator targets had sparse or missing matched groups; comparison is based on gene-level DE, not microtubule polymer measurements.
summary: Stmn2 did not phenocopy direct microtubule-subunit perturbations: Tuba1a loss induced a multi-tubulin replacement program whereas Stmn2 loss only reduced Tuba1a in one group.
why_it_matters: The direct Tuba1a response proves that this snRNA-seq assay can detect tubulin stoichiometry compensation in the same 151 thalamic class and in Pvalb neurons; its absence after Stmn2 argues for pathway-selective buffering rather than a blind readout.

literature_claim: Loss of nuclear TDP-43 causes human STMN2 cryptic splice-polyadenylation, reducing functional stathmin-2, and STMN2 loss contributes to ALS-like motor neuropathy.
main_caveats: The dataset reports gene-level DE by snRNA-seq and cannot detect the human-specific edited cryptic-exon event; Tuba1a co-suppression is only one shared gene.
summary: Tardbp converged with Stmn2 only on 151 Tuba1a suppression and otherwise diverged: Tardbp caused a broad RNA signature without gene-level Stmn2 loss.
why_it_matters: The human TDP-43→STMN2 cryptic-splicing axis cannot be read out as simple mouse Stmn2 mRNA depletion in this pooled gene-level screen; Tardbp has many additional RNA targets and a much broader acute nuclear phenotype.

main_caveats: All correlations were computed over weak, nearly flat Stmn2 DE scores, so failure to find a strong neighbor is more robust than the identity of any rank-ordered neighbor.
summary: The unbiased cross-perturbation nearest neighbors of Stmn2 were essentially uncorrelated and were rejected as biological signature matches.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting random nominal Stmn2 ranks: the best positive neighbor, Cep290, had r=0.031, the best negative neighbor, Klhl7, had r=-0.0166, and the top unbiased neighbors contributed no shared FDR<0.10 Stmn2-responsive program.

literature_claim: Mouse midbrain Stmn2 knockdown can cause dopaminergic neuron degeneration, phosphorylated α-synuclein elevation, and locomotor deficits.
main_caveats: No Stmn2 DE rows exist for this cell group, so this is a coverage finding rather than a measured null.
summary: The Parkinson-relevant 215 MB Dopa class had no Stmn2 rows and therefore the screen did not test the dopaminergic Stmn2 phenotype.
why_it_matters: Stmn2 knockdown has been reported to kill mouse midbrain DA neurons and increase phosphorylated α-synuclein; treating 215 MB Dopa absence as a zero would be a false biological conclusion.

main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured, and flat target mRNA is expected for this CRISPR design; the inference is limited to NeuN-enriched P16-to-P37/44 neuronal nuclei.
summary: Stra6 was transcriptionally flat in every measured NeuN+ neuronal group: 22 of 22 recovered groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the Stra6 self-transcript had FDR=1.0 wherever it was measured.
why_it_matters: This establishes a robust acute postmitotic neuronal null rather than a missed small program; the target-wide best downstream gene still stopped at FDR 0.222.

literature_claim: STRA6 mediates uptake of circulating RBP4-retinol and its loss can impair retinoid signaling at the choroid plexus and in congenital STRA6 malformation syndromes; RA-responsive cells should report altered ligand availability through RAR/RXR-dependent transcriptional targets.
main_caveats: The screen did not sample choroid plexus, vascular endothelium or eye; it tested mosaic neuronal loss rather than systemic or barrier loss.
summary: Loss of Stra6 did not lower a retinoic-acid feedback program in sampled neurons: Rarb/Rarg/Rxra/Rxrb/Rxrg, Cyp26 genes, Dhrs3, Rbp1, Lrat, Rbp4, Ttr, Crabp1/2 and Aldh genes had no FDR<0.10 changes.
why_it_matters: STRA6 disease and mouse phenotypes are retinoid-transport phenotypes, but this result argues that acute cell-autonomous Stra6 disruption in postmitotic NeuN+ neurons is not sufficient to create a detectable RA-starvation transcriptome.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

literature_claim: RAR/RXR heterodimers are the canonical transcriptional receptors for retinoic acid, RARB belongs to the same human retinoid-malformation disease neighborhood as STRA6, and forebrain RAR/RXR signaling can affect adult hippocampal physiology.
main_caveats: Rara was absent from the perturbation target list, RAR/RXR family redundancy was not combinatorially perturbed, and the two receptor hits that did pass FDR were single-gene events.
summary: The measured nuclear retinoid receptors Rarb, Rarg, Rxra, Rxrb and Rxrg did not phenocopy Stra6; cosine similarity to Stra6 was only 0.001-0.021 and each receptor perturbation produced at most one downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: The RA pathway neighbors that were visible in the library also failed to elicit a broad acute neuronal transcriptome, supporting pathway-level buffering or inactivity in the assayed single-gene, postmitotic context.

main_caveats: Because Stra6 itself has no FDR-significant signature, neighbor ranks are dominated by non-significant rank noise and are useful only as a rejection test.
summary: Unbiased score-space comparison did not uncover a hidden Stra6 module: the strongest positive and negative whole-surface neighbors had absolute Wilcoxon-score cosines of only 0.031 or less.
why_it_matters: The null is not only a pathway-specific miss of retinoid genes; across 1,773 targets there was no coherent convergent or anti-correlated transcriptomic program aligned with Stra6.

literature_claim: Germline human STRADA loss and fetal STRADα depletion produce neurodevelopmental epilepsy phenotypes with mTORC1 activation and migration or polarization defects.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured; a single Epn1 DEG is too little to assert a broad Strada program.
summary: Strada loss produced an almost pan-neuronal transcriptional non-response after P16: 21 of 22 measured groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream gene and the 22nd had only Epn1.
why_it_matters: PMSE and embryonic STRADα experiments create a strong prior for LKB1 mislocalization and mTORC1 hyperactivity, but sparse postmitotic Strada loss in juvenile neurons did not acutely re-enter that disease-like program.

literature_claim: EPN1/epsin-1 is annotated as an ENTH-domain endocytic protein involved in clathrin-mediated endocytosis; no established Strada-Epn1 axis was found.
main_caveats: The FDR is 0.056 and no second trafficking gene reached FDR<0.10 under Strada, so this is a single-gene marker candidate.
summary: Epn1 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was the sole FDR<0.10 Strada response.
why_it_matters: Epn1 encodes epsin-1, an endocytic adaptor, so the lone signal suggests a very narrow membrane-trafficking hypothesis rather than an mTOR, ISR, UPR, proteostasis, redox, or synaptic program.

literature_claim: LKB1:STRAD:MO25 acts upstream of AMPK/TSC2 to restrain mTORC1, making a Tsc2-like transcriptional response an expected secondary outcome of an unbuffered Strada loss.
main_caveats: Tsc2 is downstream of many inputs; the contrast rejects a full Tsc2 phenocopy but does not prove that biochemical LKB1 or AMPK activity was unchanged.
summary: Strada did not phenocopy Tsc2 even where a Tsc2 loss response was readily detectable.
why_it_matters: A direct Tsc2 perturbation elicited 636 FDR<0.10 genes in Strada-matched groups, including sterol, lysosomal, PI3K-feedback, stress, and neuronal genes, while the same Tsc2-responsive panel had zero FDR<0.10 entries under Strada.

literature_claim: The inspected targets are pathway neighbors of STRAD/LKB1 signaling through AMPK and mTOR control.
main_caveats: The closest same-complex genes were not represented; isolated single-gene Prkag2 and Mark3 hits are too small for a pathway signature.
summary: Other represented AMPK/mTOR pathway neighbors also failed to converge with Strada.
why_it_matters: Of the core LKB1 complex, Stk11, Stradb, Cab39, and Cab39l were not perturbation targets; among represented neighbors, Mtor, Rptor, Prkaa2, Prkag2, and Mark3 produced zero to six FDR<0.10 genes and no Strada-like 066 Epn1 response.

main_caveats: Correlations of null-like signatures can rank stochastic similarities; Wdr26 had many DE genes but remained only very weakly anticorrelated with Strada.
summary: Whole-transcriptome neighbor search put Strada in a near-null, non-modular signature neighborhood.
why_it_matters: The top positive score-vector correlation was only r=0.0399 and the strongest anticorrelation was only r=-0.0213, so neither standard biological nor data-driven neighbors expose a hidden Strada program.

literature_claim: CHIP is a chaperone-bound substrate E3 whose loss can perturb protein quality control, but STUB1-null iPSC-derived cortical neurons can preserve heat-shock transcription while showing proteomic changes.
main_caveats: DNA indels and CHIP protein were not measured; two groups had near-threshold singletons but no FDR<0.10 downstream gene.
summary: Stub1 loss produced no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups despite a consistent negative Stub1 self-transcript logFC.
why_it_matters: This is a real basal negative result across nearly the whole recovered brain taxonomy, not evidence that Stub1 was unmeasured or that target mRNA had to vanish for indels to matter.

literature_claim: Ubiquitin-proteasome degradation defects can activate the HSF1-controlled heat-shock response, while CHIP links chaperones to UPS substrate triage rather than serving as the proteasome core.
main_caveats: Psmb4/Psmc1 are pathway comparators, not the same molecular complex as CHIP; the contrast is transcriptomic.
summary: Stub1 was uncoupled from core proteasome collapse: Psmb4 and Psmc1 loss caused thousands of DE genes and Psmb4 induced HSF/ISR/autophagy transcripts that Stub1 never induced.
why_it_matters: The absence of Hspa, Dnaj, Atf3/Ddit3, Sqstm1, and proteasome compensation after Stub1 is informative because matched neuronal groups can produce that transcriptional program when the proteasome core is directly perturbed.

literature_claim: CHIP physically and functionally interfaces with Hsp70/Hsp90 chaperones, and HSF1 controls a chaperone-induction program during proteotoxic stress.
main_caveats: Several chaperone targets were not recovered in every cell group; small one-gene DNAJ responses were not interpreted mechanistically.
summary: Hsp70/Hsp90/HSF1/DNAJ comparators were flat or weak and did not converge with Stub1, contrasting with the broad Psmb4/Psmc1 response.
why_it_matters: The matched screen separates two layers of proteostasis: distal chaperone/client regulators are buffered over 3-4 weeks in basal postmitotic neurons, whereas core proteasome subunit loss is not.

literature_claim: CHIP is linked to alpha-synuclein, tau, huntingtin, and polyglutamine protein quality control, and SCAR16 alleles can be functionally different from total CHIP loss.
main_caveats: The screen perturbed loss-of-function alleles of disease genes, not toxic human aggregate expansions or aged Purkinje neurons.
summary: Perturbing aggregate-associated neurodegenerative targets did not recreate a Stub1 program, and Stub1 did not recreate theirs.
why_it_matters: STUB1/CHIP disease biology is better modeled as long-lived protein-client, cerebellar, and allele-specific proteostasis pathology than as a shared acute mRNA endpoint with Snca, Mapt, Htt, or ataxin-family loss in juvenile neurons.

main_caveats: The cosine calculation used full Wilcoxon score vectors dominated by near-null Stub1 entries; the result is strongest as evidence for absence of a robust neighbor.
summary: Unbiased full-transcriptome signature neighbors of Stub1 were near zero in both directions.
why_it_matters: The flat Stub1 surface did not hide a weakly recurring module shared with another target; top data-driven candidates were rejected rather than promoted to biological comparators.

literature_claim: STX16 acts in TGN-retrograde and autophagy-associated SNARE traffic, whereas DDX27 supports nucleolar 47S rRNA processing.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10; a one-gene DDX27 result does not resolve a full ribosome-biogenesis pathway.
summary: Stx16 loss produced a single robust downstream event, Ddx27 down-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, rather than the broad Golgi, autophagy, or stress signature expected from a severe STX16 trafficking defect.
why_it_matters: The screen nominates an exploratory corticofugal nucleolar/ribosome-biogenesis signal while establishing that most of the canonical STX16 program was transcriptionally buffered in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: GARP and STX16-containing SNAREs operate in a common endosome-to-TGN route, and STX16 is coupled to autolysosome biogenesis.
main_caveats: Most exact STX16 co-SNAREs, including Stx6, Vti1a, Vamp4, Vamp7 and Stx17, were not CRISPR targets in the parquet, so the comparison uses represented pathway neighbors.
summary: Measured STX/GARP/retromer/endolysosomal comparators did not phenocopy the Stx16 L5-ET Ddx27 signature; instead Rab7, Cltc, Stxbp1, Vps35 and Vps54 responded in different cell groups where Stx16 was flat.
why_it_matters: This rejects the simplest pathway-member convergence model and shows that the assay can detect trafficking-perturbation transcriptional states, but not after single Stx16 loss under these conditions.

literature_claim: STX16 participates in membrane fusion events whose severe disruption can affect lysosome biogenesis or autophagic flux.
main_caveats: The result excludes a broad mRNA program, not altered vesicle localization, lysosomal pH, or autophagic flux at protein-organelle resolution.
summary: Stx16 perturbation did not induce target-excluding Golgi/SNARE, lysosomal, autophagy, or UPR/ISR transcripts at FDR<0.10 in any recovered cell group.
why_it_matters: The absent secondary program makes the null biologically informative: a nucleus-readable stress or autophagy rebound was not engaged even though such programs would be visible to snRNA-seq if induced strongly.

literature_claim: Familial PHP-Ib STX16-locus deletions disrupt a cis-acting imprinting control element for GNAS exon A/B and cause renal PTH resistance.
main_caveats: The screen measures total gene-level Gnas RNA in neurons, not parent-of-origin GNAS methylation or renal PTH receptor signaling.
summary: Mouse neuronal Stx16 coding perturbation did not reproduce the human STX16-deletion/GNAS-imprinting axis: Gnas was FDR=1.0 in every recovered Stx16 group.
why_it_matters: It argues against reading this coding LoF screen as a model of pseudohypoparathyroidism type Ib, where the pathogenic lesion is a specific cis-regulatory deletion affecting GNAS methylation in an endocrine context.

main_caveats: Cosine similarity was computed on residualized logFC vectors and all top scores were too small to imply functional coupling.
summary: Data-driven whole-surface neighbor search failed to find a meaningful Stx16 convergent or opposing module; the largest residualized cosine magnitudes were near zero.
why_it_matters: The data themselves did not nominate a hidden co-regulated perturbation class, so related-target interpretation should rely on explicit pathway queries rather than on noisy nearest neighbors.

literature_claim: Syntaxin-1 is a plasma-membrane SNARE required for vesicle docking, priming, fusion, and neuronal maintenance; mammals co-express Stx1a and Stx1b, and single Stx1b loss can be partly buffered in central neurons.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation and protein depletion were not measured; snRNA-seq cannot assay quantal release, vesicle docking, or release probability directly.
summary: P16 Stx1b CRISPR produced a pan-measured neuronal transcriptomic null: every recovered cell group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The main measurable result is not a weak named pathway but a broad absence of nuclear reprogramming after sparse postmitotic loss of a presynaptic syntaxin; this constrains STX1B biology in this assay to synaptic physiology, compensation, or unsampled survival phenotypes rather than a cell-autonomous snRNA-seq state change.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Munc18-1/STXBP1 binds syntaxin-1, helps assemble release-competent SNARE complexes, and complete Munc18-1 deletion abolishes neurotransmitter release and causes neuronal degeneration.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic only; Stxbp1 itself had a restricted, not pan-neuronal, response and the shared-direction overlap with Stx1b is zero because Stx1b has no downstream FDR genes.
summary: Stx1b did not phenocopy Stxbp1/Munc18-1, the syntaxin-binding SNARE regulator that generated 140 downstream DE genes in matched groups.
why_it_matters: A physical partner with a much stronger transcriptome response demonstrates that the Stx1b null is not a blanket failure of neurons to respond to every presynaptic perturbation, and it separates the cellular consequence of losing syntaxin-1B from the broader Munc18-1 dependence of vesicle release and neuronal maintenance.

literature_claim: Syntaxin-1 acts with SNARE- and release-cycle proteins including Munc18-1/STXBP1, Munc13s, complexins, synaptobrevin/VAMP proteins, and synaptotagmins to control synaptic vesicle release.
main_caveats: The ranked-neighbor calculation is based on weak Stx1b scores because Stx1b had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes; the correlation result should be read as lack of convergence, not as a positive Coa8 or Fktn relationship.
summary: The ranked Stx1b signature had no meaningful genome-scale or presynaptic-pathway neighbor; the strongest non-safe correlations were only |r|<=0.034 and most SNARE-cycle comparators were transcriptionally null or singleton responders.
why_it_matters: This rejects the idea that Stx1b hides inside a coherent low-amplitude presynaptic-exocytosis transcriptional module; in this dataset, perturbing release machinery is usually read out poorly by steady-state nuclear RNA unless the target has additional roles like Stxbp1.

literature_claim: STX1B variants cause fever-associated and broader epilepsies, and individual pathogenic variants produce distinct loss-of-function, instability, binding, or release-probability phenotypes in neurons.
main_caveats: No patient allele, seizure state, fever challenge, electrophysiology, or protein rescue was assayed.
summary: The absence of an Stx1b nuclear biomarker warns against using this mosaic LoF snRNA-seq readout to rank therapies for variant-specific STX1B epilepsies.
why_it_matters: STX1B alleles can act through protein instability, altered Munc18/Munc13 interactions, or altered fusogenicity; these are biochemical and electrophysiological defects, and the screen neither models missense alleles nor reports vesicle release, so a therapy that rescues STX1B function could look inactive by this endpoint.

literature_claim: STX5 mediates ER-Golgi and intra-Golgi transport, and strong depletion or isoform-specific loss perturbs Golgi organization and glycosylation.
main_caveats: The experiment did not measure DNA indels, STX5A protein, Golgi morphology, trafficking flux or glycosylation.
summary: Stx5a loss produced an almost empty snRNA-seq surface: only two downstream genes reached FDR<0.10 across 21 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Syntaxin-5A is a core ER-Golgi SNARE, so the result is a biological negative for a broad postnatal neuronal stress or trafficking-compensation transcriptome rather than a failed assay; the target transcript itself was expected to be a weak engagement readout under indel-based CRISPR.

literature_claim: SIDT2 localizes to lysosomes and mediates RNautophagy, whereas syntaxin-5 biology centers on ER-Golgi transport.
main_caveats: Both effects are single genes; the cerebellar result uses only 28 perturbed nuclei.
summary: The only FDR-significant Stx5a signals were two isolated cell-group singletons: Sidt2 up in CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic neurons and Copg1 down in cerebellar GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: Sidt2 nominates lysosomal RNA handling and Copg1 directly touches COPI/Golgi retrograde traffic, but each occurs as a one-gene island, so they are biomarkers to follow rather than full programs in this dataset.

literature_claim: STX5 works with ER-Golgi SNAREs and Golgi tethers, while COG and COPI organize retrograde Golgi traffic that interfaces with the same SNARE system.
main_caveats: Only the pathway members represented as perturbation targets could be tested; Bet1, Gosr1, Gosr2, Sec22b and Ykt6 were not target perturbations in this parquet.
summary: Measured Golgi-traffic relatives did not phenocopy Stx5a; COG, COPI, Sar1b, Vcp and Stx16 perturbations were themselves largely flat and never reproduced the two Stx5a singleton genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The dataset directly rejects a simple same-organelle transcriptomic module for the represented ER-Golgi machinery in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Psmc1 and Psmb4 are proteasome components that participate in a transcriptional proteasome-recovery module, and Gfpt1 supplies hexosamine flux for glycosylation rather than serving as an STX5 SNARE partner.
main_caveats: The neighbor metric used subthreshold Stx5a dimensions because Stx5a had only two FDR-significant genes; there was no FDR-significant Sidt2/Copg1 overlap with these neighbors.
summary: A pre-literature restricted-signature search nominated Psmc1, Psmb4 and Gfpt1 as the nearest positive Stx5a neighbors, with Plxnd1, Smo and Ephb2 as the most negative gene-target neighbors.
why_it_matters: The weak Stx5a trends were closer to proteasome and hexosamine-biosynthesis perturbations than to canonical Golgi relatives, suggesting that any residual nuclear response is an indirect proteostasis/glycosylation shadow rather than a clean SNARE-complex signature.

literature_claim: The UPR/ISR and proteasome recovery pathways induce defined mRNA programs after ER or proteasome stress.
main_caveats: Xbp1 splicing, translation attenuation, proteasome activity and autophagic flux were not directly assayed.
summary: Canonical nuclear stress programs expected from severe secretory-pathway failure were not recovered after Stx5a perturbation.
why_it_matters: UPR/ISR, autophagy-lysosome and proteasome bounce-back markers are transcriptional enough for snRNA-seq to see; their absence makes the null informative for surviving P16-perturbed neurons rather than merely a modality miss.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Munc18-1 is an essential, broadly used presynaptic SM protein whose deletion abolishes synaptic vesicle secretion.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq does not measure neurotransmitter release directly, and no DNA indel calls are available.
summary: Stxbp1 drove a restricted postnatal neuronal transcriptional response rather than a universal Munc18-1 loss program: the largest signatures were in L4/5 IT cortical neurons, Pvalb interneurons and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, while many other neuronal classes had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: Munc18-1 is broadly essential for vesicle fusion, so the selective nuclear response identifies where chronic postmitotic release impairment is converted into a cell-autonomous transcriptional state in this assay.

literature_claim: Embryonic Stxbp1 knockout tissue and immature neurons show broad dysregulation of synaptic and developmental profiles.
main_caveats: Data are mRNA from juvenile sparse LoF nuclei, not synaptic physiology or protein abundance.
summary: The dominant cortical IT program was down-regulation of excitatory synaptic and activity-coupled genes, including Nrxn2, Grin2b, Gria3, Homer1 and Dlg4 in L4/5 IT neurons and a smaller Camk2a/Gria3/Cpne6/Plekhg5 module in L2/3 IT neurons.
why_it_matters: The result connects a presynaptic fusion gene to postsynaptic receptor, scaffold and calcium-plasticity transcripts in the same postmitotic neurons, refining Stxbp1 loss from a pure terminal-release defect to a nucleus-detectable synaptic homeostasis state in selected cortical IT cells.

literature_claim: Stxbp1 haploinsufficiency reduces cortical inhibitory neurotransmission through mechanisms involving parvalbumin- and somatostatin-expressing interneurons.
main_caveats: The transcriptomic change does not prove reduced GABA uptake or impaired PV output; SST had only one DE gene in this screen.
summary: Pvalb interneurons engaged an inhibitory-synapse response with strong Slc6a1 down-regulation and additional Erbb4, Neto2, Nxph1, Nalcn and Slc24a2 decreases.
why_it_matters: This is the clearest GABAergic response and aligns the screen with mouse Stxbp1 haploinsufficiency studies in which deficient PV/SST cortical inhibition contributes to hyperexcitability.

literature_claim: MUNC18-1 is selectively required for dense-core vesicle neuropeptide secretion and is not compensated by MUNC18-2 or MUNC18-3 in neurons.
main_caveats: The genes are consistent with secretory compensation but vesicle exocytosis was not measured.
summary: L4/5 IT neurons up-regulated dense-core-vesicle and secretory genes (Nrsn1, Pcsk1n, Scg2, Chgb, Cplx1) together with lipid-feedback genes Insig1 and Dhcr24.
why_it_matters: Munc18-1 is required for neuropeptide dense-core vesicle release as well as synaptic vesicle fusion; the L4/5 up-state suggests the affected cells attempt a secretory/lipid compensation rather than simply losing all synaptic transcripts.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Synaptic function couples exocytosis to endocytic and endosomal sorting pathways, and sorting nexins are trafficking regulators with nervous-system roles.
main_caveats: Several contributing cell groups have only one FDR<0.10 gene, so the cross-cell module is stronger than any isolated one-gene surface.
summary: A membrane-sorting module appeared across the broad L4/5 response and several one-gene effects: Fcho1 and Pacsin1 were down in L4/5 IT neurons, and Ankrd13d, Sort1, Snx1 and Znrf1 were the sole robust hits in ENT/PIR L2/3 IT, L5 ET, SST, and hypothalamic glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: The Stxbp1 surface therefore contains an endocytic/endosomal arm, consistent with vesicle-cycle remodeling, not only receptor or calcium-transcription changes.

literature_claim: Proteasome perturbation affects neuronal synaptic proteostasis and can secondarily alter neuronal stress states.
main_caveats: Based on 18 DE genes; iron and injury state assignments are transcriptomic hypotheses.
summary: Midbrain glutamatergic neurons showed a mixed response with Mt1, Tfrc, Rnft1 and Fos up, but Cntnap1, Clptm1l, Psmc2, Tubb3, Aifm3, Paip2 and Abca2 down.
why_it_matters: This separates the MB response from the cortical receptor/scaffold program and nominates an injury/iron/immediate-early plus membrane-axon state as a secondary consequence of Stxbp1 loss in this cell class.

literature_claim: Some STXBP1 missense variants cause Munc18-1 protein instability or aggregation in addition to simple haploinsufficiency.
main_caveats: Absence of mRNA stress markers does not exclude local protein-quality-control changes at terminals.
summary: Stxbp1 loss did not induce a canonical UPR, heat-shock or proteasome-bounce-back transcriptome in any measured cell group.
why_it_matters: Because a subset of pathogenic STXBP1 missense alleles destabilize or aggregate Munc18-1, an indel LoF signature that lacks Hspa5, Ddit3, Atf4, Xbp1 and coordinated proteasome-gene induction should not be treated as a full phenocopy of misfolded-protein variants.

literature_claim: The ubiquitin-proteasome system regulates synaptic proteostasis; clathrin participates in vesicle membrane recovery and sorting.
main_caveats: The comparison used sparse FDR<0.10 overlaps and the broad Psmb4/Psmc1/Tpr signatures are far larger than the Stxbp1 signature.
summary: The nearest positive Stxbp1 neighbors were not SNARE genes but Psmb4, Tpr, Psmc1 and Cltc; Psmb4 alone shared 74 Stxbp1 significant gene-by-cell features, 67 in the same direction.
why_it_matters: Cross-target convergence embeds the selected Stxbp1 nuclear response in a proteostasis/trafficking stress neighborhood even though Stxbp1 itself did not transcriptionally up-regulate proteasome subunits.

literature_claim: Severe SUCLG1/SCS dysfunction is tied to mtDNA depletion, and diverse mitochondrial insults can induce stress-response transcripts downstream of ATF4/DDIT3 in metabolically susceptible cells.

why_it_matters: The literature maps TANGO2 across several organelle processes, but the perturbation data do not place Tango2 in any of the represented basal neuronal transcriptional modules for those processes.

main_caveats: Cosine similarity was computed from all Wilcoxon scores, not only FDR genes; the finding is quantitative absence of convergence, not a biological relationship to Rel or Crebbp.
summary: Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found only near-zero Tango2 correlations, with Rel as the top positive score-cosine neighbor at 0.028 and Crebbp as the top negative at -0.019.
why_it_matters: The null is not hiding an obvious weak pan-gene module that recurs across other perturbations in the model-visible universe.

literature_claim: Human TDP-43 depletion causes STMN2 and UNC13A cryptic splicing that lowers productive mRNA and protein; TDP-43 cryptic-exon usage is cell-type and species dependent.
main_caveats: The assay would not detect the relevant cryptic junctions, and mouse orthologs need not carry the same intronic cryptic exons as human STMN2 or UNC13A.
summary: Human TDP-43 loss-of-function sentinels did not move in their textbook direction: Unc13a increased at whole-gene level in six mouse groups, whereas Stmn2, Sort1, and Atg4b were not detected as decreased whole-gene transcripts.
why_it_matters: The result warns against reading this mouse juvenile whole-gene assay as a direct STMN2/UNC13A cryptic-splicing reporter; acute Tardbp loss can coexist with Unc13a mRNA compensation instead of the UNC13A depletion expected from human cryptic-exon/NMD biology.

why_it_matters: The strongest Tardbp responses were not pure RNA-processing signatures; they propagated into energy and organelle-maintenance genes implicated in TDP-43-linked stress physiology.

main_caveats: Functional grouping is based on known gene identities, not on an enrichment statistic, and the FDR-positive gene count is very small in 027.

why_it_matters: The strongest molecular neighbors were a proteasome ATPase and spliceosome/co-transcriptional splicing perturbations, not the disease-family comparators one would have chosen from ALS genetics alone; related RBP status therefore does not imply interchangeability in this acute in vivo assay.

literature_claim: TBCD deficiency is severe and developmental, with embryonic knockdown impairing cortical proliferation and radial migration and homozygous mouse knockout causing early embryonic lethality.

literature_claim: Tubulin mRNAs are regulated downstream of microtubule perturbation, and TBCD participates in alpha/beta-tubulin heterodimer production.
main_caveats: The readout is RNA; it does not prove that alpha-tubulin protein or polymerized microtubules increased.

why_it_matters: This is a direct molecular link between a beta-tubulin folding cofactor and alpha-tubulin RNA feedback in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Neuronal maturation and maintenance depend on tightly regulated microtubule networks and tubulin isotypes.
main_caveats: Restricted to one thalamic group; several members of the module are single-gene representatives rather than an enriched large pathway.

main_caveats: The ranking was restricted to the 19 Tbcd FDR<0.10 features and does not imply direct CIC or NMDA-receptor regulation of TBCD.
summary: Cic and Grin1 were the top positive signature neighbors of Tbcd on its 19 significant features, sharing seven and six same-direction thalamic Prkcd hits, respectively.
why_it_matters: The dominant covariance of the Tbcd phenotype is with a thalamic adaptation state rather than with another measured tubulin cofactor.

main_caveats: The comparison is signature-based; Psmb4 and Psmc1 have broad effects outside the Tbcd feature set.

why_it_matters: This contrast separates Tbcd's alpha-tubulin compensation from a generic proteostatic injury response driven by proteasome loss.

literature_claim: TBCD and alpha-tubulins act on the same alpha/beta-tubulin heterodimer economy, and TBCD is regulated through an ARL2-containing complex.
main_caveats: Arl2 itself and the closest cofactor genes were absent from the perturbation universe; Arl2bp is an indirect proxy.

why_it_matters: The result rejects interchangeability of measured alpha-tubulin/paralog and indirect ARL2-axis perturbations with a TBCD cofactor loss in juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: Microtubule perturbations can be discovered transcriptomically through tubulin mRNA responses rather than requiring broad stress-pathway induction.
