summary: Tbcd did not induce a coordinated UPR/ISR, autophagy/lysosome, redox, or proteasome-subunit transcriptional program at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The null stress surface prevents over-reading Tbcd as a broad proteotoxic collapse and focuses the interpretation on tubulin mRNA feedback plus the small 151 TH module.

literature_claim: DNER is a postmitotic neuronal dendritic transmembrane protein that can act as a Notch ligand for glial morphogenesis.
main_caveats: Only one gene crossed FDR<0.10 and the responder had 76 perturbed cells; no protein or Notch-activity readout was measured.
summary: Tbl1x loss produced a single robust downstream event: Dner up-regulation specific to 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Dner encodes a dendrite-localized, Notch-like neuronal ligand, so the one significant transcript points to a cell-cell signaling hypothesis rather than a broad NCoR/Wnt collapse.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: TBL1X/TBL1 and TBL1XR1/TBLR1 are NCoR/SMRT-associated exchange factors used by nuclear receptor and Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: True indel engagement was not measured, and the assay perturbed postmitotic neurons only 3-4 weeks after P16 AAV delivery.
summary: Acute Tbl1x perturbation was globally buffered in juvenile postmitotic neurons.
why_it_matters: A WD40 exchange factor in the NCoR/SMRT-HDAC3 complex could have been expected to alter many nuclear receptor and Wnt transcriptional targets; instead the whole target surface contained 1 FDR<0.10 gene among 355,025 downstream tests.

literature_claim: TBL1X/TBL1 and TBL1XR1/TBLR1 occupy related NCoR/Wnt exchange-factor roles and both have been implicated in Wnt/β-catenin transcription.
main_caveats: Tbl1xr1 itself had only 15 total FDR genes, so the asymmetry is strong for absence of phenocopy but not a complete map of paralog-specific effectors.
summary: Tbl1xr1 did not phenocopy Tbl1x despite being the in-parquet paralog and weak whole-signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The paralog produced a small thalamic/CA response, no MB Glut Dner increase, and only a tiny positive cosine to Tbl1x, so the screen resolves TBL1-family asymmetry rather than interchangeability.

literature_claim: TBL1/TBLR1 recruit β-catenin to Wnt target promoters, while TCF7L2 has postmitotic thalamic identity and excitability functions.
main_caveats: The comparison is genetic and transcriptomic; TBL1X occupancy, β-catenin occupancy, and indel burden were not measured.
summary: Tbl1x is uncoupled from the β-catenin/TCF7L2 thalamic program that is readily detected in this assay.
why_it_matters: Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 perturbations down-regulated overlapping thalamic identity and excitability genes, including Plekhg1, Ramp3, Spock3, Zdhhc22, Lef1, Pcp4, Kcnc2, and Pcsk2, but the same genes were flat after Tbl1x perturbation in matched 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut nuclei.

literature_claim: TBL1X participates in NCoR/SMRT exchange downstream of nuclear receptors, human TBL1X variants cause central hypothyroidism, and the MeCP2 disease axis also uses NCoR/SMRT.
main_caveats: The matched core subunits NCOR1, NCOR2, HDAC3, and GPS2 were not perturbation targets, and pituitary, inner-ear, retinal-pigment, and glial lineages were absent or under-sampled.
summary: Nuclear-receptor and MeCP2/NCoR-related comparators were not Tbl1x-like in the measured neurons.
why_it_matters: Thra and Mecp2 showed small detectable programs in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Tbl1x did not alter the Thra-responsive genes Hr, Adgrb1, or Hcn2; Rarb, Rxra, and Thrb were themselves mostly silent, supporting displacement of TBL1X endocrine and receptor phenotypes outside the sampled neuronal transcriptome.

main_caveats: Cosine was computed on all matched Wilcoxon scores; because Tbl1x has only one FDR gene, restricted-signature comparisons are necessarily single-gene tests.
summary: The data-driven Tbl1x neighborhood does not support a broad convergent module.
why_it_matters: The largest absolute whole-surface cosine was only 0.02368, the strongest positive neighbors did not reproduce Dner, and the strongest negative biological neighbor was only -0.01021; this argues that the Tbl1x call is an isolated MB Glut Dner event rather than a multi-target module.

literature_claim: Previously studied Tbl1xr1 neural phenotypes were prominent in neural progenitors and involved NCOR/MAPK regulation, not a mapped postnatal thalamic neuron program.
main_caveats: Only 15 total downstream FDR<0.10 genes were detected; 151 TH had the largest Tbl1xr1 cell count, and DNA indel engagement was not measured.
summary: Tbl1xr1 loss produced an FDR-defined transcriptional response almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with a single-gene Tet2 response in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut.
why_it_matters: A WD40/NCoR/Wnt coregulator did not behave as a universal neuronal transcriptional dependency after P16; its basal postmitotic requirement was sharply cell-class restricted.

literature_claim: TBL1/TBLR1 support beta-catenin recruitment to Wnt target promoters, whereas VANGL genes are core Wnt/planar-cell-polarity components.
main_caveats: Vangl1 is a single PCP gene; direct beta-catenin occupancy and Wnt ligand state were not measured.
summary: The thalamic signature touched Wnt/PCP through Vangl1 down-regulation, but it did not recover a canonical beta-catenin target program.
why_it_matters: This refines the expectation from TBL1XR1-Wnt literature: postnatal thalamic Tbl1xr1 loss altered a noncanonical/PCP gene while Axin2, Lef1, Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 stayed FDR-flat.

literature_claim: TBL1XR1 participates in regulated nuclear-receptor cofactor exchange, and Tbl1xr1 deficiency in neural progenitors was linked to NCOR/MAPK dysregulation.
main_caveats: The comparison uses the 14-gene FDR signature in one thalamic class and does not prove direct RORA or CIC binding.
summary: Data-driven restricted-signature scoring linked Tbl1xr1 most strongly to Rora and Cic in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The strongest same-direction neighbors were a nuclear receptor and a MAPK-sensitive transcriptional repressor rather than the TBL1 paralog, nominating a nuclear-receptor/MAPK-sensitive thalamic output for follow-up.

literature_claim: TBL1XR1 acts in the NCoR/SMRT-HDAC3 axis rather than the SIN3A scaffold, although both are transcriptional corepressor systems.
main_caveats: Sin3a had a much broader 151 TH signature, so inversion was assessed only on the overlapping Tbl1xr1 genes.
summary: Sin3a perturbation inverted most of the overlapping Tbl1xr1 thalamic genes.
why_it_matters: Loss of a different HDAC-associated corepressor scaffold drove the opposite direction at Prkcg, Rasa4, Ppp2r5d, Vangl1, Kctd16 and Ank3, arguing that the Tbl1xr1 signature is not a generic de-repression response shared by all chromatin corepressors.

literature_claim: TBL1 and TBLR1 can be redundant within NCoR/SMRT complexes but also show target- and context-selective functions.
main_caveats: The screen tested single-gene perturbations; a Tbl1x/Tbl1xr1 double perturbation was not measured.
summary: The closest TBL-family comparator, Tbl1x, was nearly inert and did not phenocopy Tbl1xr1.
why_it_matters: The paralog contrast supports context-specific use of TBL1XR1 versus TBL1X in neurons; Tbl1x single loss was buffered even in the two Tbl1xr1 responder groups.

literature_claim: NEU1 encodes a lysosomal sialidase that removes terminal sialic acids from glycan substrates.
main_caveats: The module contains only two FDR<0.10 genes and no biochemical glycan measurements.
summary: St6galnac6 and Neu1 were both up-regulated in the thalamic Tbl1xr1 response, suggesting a small sialoconjugate/lysosomal glycan remodeling component.
why_it_matters: These up-regulated glycan genes are a secondary program outside canonical NCoR or Wnt readouts and may mark membrane or lysosomal adaptation in the responder thalamic neurons.

main_caveats: n=50 perturbed nuclei and one FDR<0.10 gene; the hit is isolated within the Tbl1xr1 surface.
summary: The entire 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut response was a single up-regulated Tet2 hit.
why_it_matters: Tet2 is a compact hippocampal biomarker candidate for Tbl1xr1 perturbation, but the absence of companion chromatin or DNA-methylation genes makes this an isolated signal rather than a pathway call.

literature_claim: TBL1/TBLR1-dependent cofactor exchange is a nuclear-receptor mechanism that can apply to PPAR-family factors in ligand-regulated settings.
main_caveats: Ligand state was not controlled and PPAR protein activity was not measured.
summary: Ppard induction after Tbl1xr1 loss did not mean that a PPAR perturbation program had been engaged.
why_it_matters: Although PPARD is a nuclear receptor and Tbl1xr1 works with nuclear-receptor coregulators, direct Ppara, Ppard, Pparg, and Ppargc1a perturbations were FDR-flat, so Ppard is better read as a transcript-level component of the Tbl1xr1 TH signature than as its driver.

literature_claim: KCTD16-containing auxiliary subunits interact with GABAB receptors and regulate receptor signaling kinetics.
main_caveats: Functional excitability, calcium signaling, and axon-compartment phenotypes were not measured; this is a transcriptomic hypothesis from a small but FDR-defined module.
summary: The 151 TH response rewired neuronal signaling and scaffold transcripts rather than activating a generic stress or proteostasis program.
why_it_matters: Prkcg and Rasa4 fell while Kctd16, Ank3, Ywhag and Ablim1 rose, pointing to altered calcium/Ras, GABAB-associated and cytoskeletal/scaffold machinery in the one main responder class.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: TBR1 is a postmitotic projection-neuron transcription factor required for early-born cortical glutamatergic differentiation and for cortical, amygdalar, and olfactory wiring.
main_caveats: The screen perturbed postmitotic P16 neurons, not embryonic progenitors; the four responding groups are coarse and do not prove which fine subtype is sensitive.
summary: P16 Tbr1-targeting CRISPR produced a sparse but real response limited to four telencephalic cortical glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: The measured response matches the projection-neuron bias of TBR1 rather than a pan-neuronal stress response: 28 downstream FDR<0.10 calls appeared in L5/6 IT, L4/5 IT, a PIR/ENT/AON IT group, and NP/CT/L6b/OB glutamatergic neurons, while GABAergic, thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, and cerebellar groups were flat.

literature_claim: Embryonic TBR1 work emphasizes Auts2, Grin2b/Reln, Sox5, and laminar fate genes as downstream effectors.
main_caveats: Cpne6 and Gaa are recurrent over only three and two cell groups, respectively; they should be treated as candidate markers, not validated direct TBR1 targets.
summary: Dkk3 down-regulation and Cpne6 up-regulation were the most recurrent markers of the postnatal Tbr1 perturbation state.
why_it_matters: No canonical direct target such as Auts2 or Grin2b reached FDR<0.10; Dkk3 fell in both IT responders, Cpne6 rose in L5/6, L4/5, and NP/CT/L6b, and Gaa rose in L5/6 and NP/CT/L6b, making this small Dkk3/Cpne6/Gaa axis the clearest candidate snRNA biomarker of acute P16 Tbr1 loss.

literature_claim: TBR1 mutants are best known for abnormal axonal projection and layer-6 connectivity, with continuing early-postnatal connectivity phenotypes after layer-6 deletion.
main_caveats: The individual DE genes are not shown here to be direct TBR1 targets; the interpretation is module-level and transcriptomic.
summary: The two IT responses were dominated by membrane, neurite, and axon-growth remodeling rather than cell-death or generic integrated-stress genes.
why_it_matters: Cadm4, Ngef, Arhgef25, Rtn4, Rtn4r, Scube1, Igsf9b, and Sgsm1 moved down whereas Ppfia4 moved up, suggesting a local rebalancing of adhesion, Rho/Ras-family signaling, reticulon/Nogo signaling, and presynaptic scaffold programs after Tbr1-targeting CRISPR in postmitotic cortical IT neurons.

literature_claim: CASK-TBR1 has been reported to activate Grin2b/NMDAR expression and Tbr1 haploinsufficiency affects amygdalar NMDAR activity.
main_caveats: The signature contains few ion genes and lacks electrophysiology; it should be read as a marker of altered channel transcription, not a measured firing phenotype.
summary: Tbr1 perturbation exposed a small ion-handling signature, strongest as Cacna1g up-regulation in NP/CT/L6b neurons and Kcna1/Slc24a2 down-regulation in L5/6 IT neurons.
why_it_matters: The direction is consistent with a compensatory excitability shift rather than the expected direct NMDAR-subunit loss: Grin2b itself was flat in Tbr1 cells, while the calcium channel Cacna1g showed the single strongest NP/CT/L6b signal.

main_caveats: Only two lysosomal genes passed FDR<0.10, so this is a low-confidence secondary program rather than a broad autophagy or UPR call.
summary: A narrow lysosomal catabolic signal accompanied the cortical response.
why_it_matters: Gaa increased in L5/6 IT and NP/CT/L6b while Ctsb decreased in L5/6 IT, indicating that the P16 Tbr1 signature includes a small lysosome-associated homeostatic branch in addition to neurite genes.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Embryonic and neonatal studies predict Auts2, Bcl6, Cdh9, Sox5, Tle4, Wnt7b, Grin2b, Reln, and reciprocal Fezf2/CTIP2 regulation downstream of TBR1.
main_caveats: Absence is transcriptomic and P16-specific; DNA indel status was not measured.
summary: The postnatal sparse Tbr1 response did not recover the canonical embryonic Auts2/Grin2b/Reln/Fezf2/Sox5/Foxp2 laminar-fate program.
why_it_matters: This is the major negative result: in a P16-to-P37/44 assay, Tbr1 targeting changed a small cortical marker set but left the textbook layer-6, layer-5, and ASD-gene targets at FDR 1.0 in the responding groups, showing that this screen queries maintenance or compensation in specified neurons rather than the original embryonic fate switch.

literature_claim: TBR1, SOX5, SATB2, FOXP proteins, Auts2/Reln, and Grin2b are connected by cortical-development or ASD-risk literature.
main_caveats: Most related perturbations were also sparse; lack of overlap is strongest as a matched-screen contrast, not proof that these genes never interact biologically.
summary: Measured TBR1-neighborhood perturbations did not phenocopy Tbr1, and active Grin perturbations diverged by layer and target genes.
why_it_matters: Satb2, Bcl11b, Sox5, Foxp2, Auts2, and Reln had no shared significant gene-group calls with Tbr1; Grin2a/Grin2b produced stronger L2/3-L4/5 signatures but also had zero exact Tbr1 overlap, arguing that Tbr1's acute cortical module is not a generic ASD-TF or NMDAR-loss signature.

main_caveats: A weak Tbr1 signature can make global correlations noisy; the conclusion is absence of a robust neighbor by the tested transcriptomic metric, not absence of all biological neighbors.
summary: The unbiased signature-neighbor search did not identify a robust Tbr1 phenocopy or anti-phenocopy in the model-visible universe.
why_it_matters: The best whole-surface Wilcoxon-score correlations were essentially zero, and the top restricted 28-coordinate neighbors were rejected because their own FDR<0.10 calls did not overlap Tbr1, so the biological interpretation should not lean on a hidden convergent perturbation cluster.

literature_claim: Polr2a encodes the RPB1 subunit of RNA polymerase II; no reviewed Tbx1 literature predicted a CNU-MGE-specific Polr2a response.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10; the affected group contained 67 perturbed nuclei.
summary: Tbx1 produced a single FDR-significant downstream hit, Polr2a down-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: The result prevents the perturbation from being treated as a complete zero, but it confines the positive biology to one basal-transcription gene in one inhibitory cell group.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Tbr1 is a neuron-intrinsic T-box regulator of postmitotic cortical identity, whereas Tbx1-associated cortical phenotypes can be driven non-cell-autonomously from embryonic mesoderm.
main_caveats: Tbr1 and Tbx1 are not paralogs with expected interchangeability; the contrast is family-level and context-level.
summary: Tbr1, but not Tbx1, induced a cortical postmitotic-neuron transcriptional profile under the same assay.
why_it_matters: This rejects a generic explanation that acute P16 CRISPR cannot expose T-box-factor biology in cortical neurons; the absence is specific to Tbx1's context rather than the whole transcription-factor family.

literature_claim: Tbx genes share the T-box DNA-binding family but the reviewed biology assigns different T-box factors to different developmental contexts.
main_caveats: Some paralog perturbations were represented in fewer than 22 matched groups; the result only covers the available postnatal neuronal cell groups.
summary: Most represented Tbx family members were flat or singleton responders and did not phenocopy Tbx1 or Tbr1.
why_it_matters: The assayed T-box genes do not collapse into a shared postnatal neuronal state; family membership alone was a poor predictor of convergence.

literature_claim: Embryonic Tbx1 genetically and transcriptionally couples to FGF signaling, especially Fgf8/Fgf10-associated pharyngeal and anterior-heart-field outputs.
main_caveats: Fgf8 and Fgf10 were not perturbation targets in the parquet; they were only tested as downstream transcripts.
summary: The embryonic Tbx1-FGF/ERK program was absent after P16 neuronal Tbx1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Fgf/ERK genes were present in the DE tables and would have been detected as mRNA changes, so their universal FDR=1.0 argues that the core Tbx1-FGF biology is displaced to embryonic pharyngeal and heart-field contexts.

literature_claim: Genome-wide signature neighbors were nominated de novo rather than from Tbx1 literature.
main_caveats: The full-score cosine includes many null features; the conclusion of nonconvergence is stronger than any ranking among the weak neighbors.
summary: The full Tbx1 DE surface had no robust genome-wide convergence or anti-convergence partner.
why_it_matters: Nearest-neighbor analysis could have revealed a non-obvious compensatory state, but the best cosines were near zero and failed to reproduce the sole Polr2a hit.

literature_claim: Constitutive Tbx1 haploinsufficiency has mouse behavioral consequences in 22q11.2 models, but postnatal brain expression reported by reporter was concentrated in vasculature and 22q11.2 neuropsychiatric disease is multigenic.
main_caveats: The experiment does not test vascular cells, glia, skull, embryonic progenitors, adult behavior, or multigene 22q11.2 hemizygosity.
summary: The 22q11.2 behavioral role of Tbx1 was not reproduced as a broad acute P16 NeuN+ neuronal transcriptome.
why_it_matters: A flat postmitotic neuronal surface narrows likely disease mechanisms toward embryonic, vascular, progenitor, structural, or multigene dosage contexts rather than widespread mature-neuron-autonomous Tbx1 transcription.

literature_claim: Tbx19/Tpit is a highly cell-restricted T-box regulator required for pituitary POMC-expressing corticotroph and melanotroph differentiation, rather than a broad neuronal transcription factor.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured and rare Tbx19-relevant endocrine nuclei would be diluted or absent in the broad NeuN+ brain groups.
summary: Tbx19 CRISPR loss of function produced a pan-assayed neuronal null: all 23 measured brain groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result is not a generic failed-knockdown call; it says that an endocrine POMC-lineage selector is not measurably coupled to juvenile NeuN+ brain transcriptomes in this P16-to-P37/P44 mosaic assay.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Tpit/Tbx19 is restricted to pituitary POMC lineages, whereas Tbr1 regulates regional and laminar identity of postmitotic neocortical neurons.
main_caveats: Tbr1 is a related T-box transcription factor rather than a Tbx19 paralog with expected redundancy; the comparison tests assay visibility and lineage restriction, not biochemical interchangeability.
summary: The flat Tbx19 surface contrasts with the represented brain T-box factor Tbr1, which produced 28 downstream FDR<0.10 genes concentrated in cortical glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: This rejects a trivial explanation that T-box transcription factors or postmitotic transcription-factor perturbations are invisible to the assay; a family member with a cortical postmitotic role was recovered where the pituitary-restricted Tbx19 was not.

main_caveats: Cosines are computed on a null Tbx19 signature; they are useful mainly for rejecting hidden convergence, not for inferring mechanism.
summary: Unbiased whole-surface neighbors did not nominate a Tbx19 module: the strongest positive Wilcoxon-score cosine was Abat at 0.030 and the strongest named-gene negative cosine was Pclo at -0.008.
why_it_matters: The data-driven neighborhood behaves like isotropic noise around zero rather than an unrecognized pathway signature, so Abat, Gria2, Mtnr1b, Pclo and Adra1a were rejected as biological Tbx19 comparators.

literature_claim: Loss of Tpit/Tbx19 in pituitary POMC lineages is expected to reduce Pomc terminal differentiation and derepress alternate pituitary fates.
main_caveats: The absence is interpretable for broad neuronal groups only; the experiment did not perturb Rathke pouch or mature pituitary corticotrophs/melanotrophs.
summary: The expected pituitary POMC and alternate-fate program was absent: Pomc, Pcsk1, Pcsk2, Cpe, Crh, Crhr1, Etv1, Neurod1, Nr5a1, Cga, Lhb and Tshb all had FDR 1.0 in every Tbx19 cell group tested.
why_it_matters: The literature-predicted readout is a directly transcriptional endocrine program and would be visible by snRNA-seq if those pituitary lineages were present; its absence supports lineage displacement rather than a non-transcriptional blind spot.

literature_claim: Tpit belongs to an endocrine pituitary specification network, whereas Tbr1 is a T-box factor with cortical neuronal functions.
main_caveats: Several library comparators had only isolated single-gene FDR hits, so this finding uses absence of coherent recurrence rather than perfect zero across every endocrine-related target.
summary: Canonical pituitary-development comparators were also flat or singleton-only in the neuronal assay, while Tbr1 was the only measured T-box-family comparator with a multi-gene cortical response.
why_it_matters: The comparator panel places the Tbx19 null inside an endocrine-lineage mismatch shared by Prop1, Pou1f1, Lhx3/Lhx4, Hesx1, Otx2 and Pitx factors, rather than inside a missing POMC module that should have emerged in brain neurons.

literature_claim: Tbx2 is a developmental T-box factor whose null and human variant phenotypes are dominated by embryonic organogenesis and craniofacial, skeletal, cardiovascular, endocrine, and immune defects rather than an established pan-neuronal adult maintenance program.
main_caveats: Indel formation was not measured; a flat Tbx2 transcript is expected in this assay and does not by itself prove failed editing.
summary: Tbx2 loss of function produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The screen does not support a broad maintenance role for Tbx2 in P37-P44 NeuN-positive neurons after P16 mosaic CRISPR; the important biology is displaced from this postmitotic neuronal window rather than hiding in a single responsive class.

literature_claim: Embryonic hypothalamic Tbx2 represses Shh downstream of BMP, and cancer-cell TBX2 can repress Cdkn2a/p19ARF and support bypass of senescence.
main_caveats: The expected genes were audited transcript by transcript; this does not exclude transient, rare-cell, or non-neuronal responses outside the broad snRNA groups.
summary: Canonical BMP-Tbx2-Shh/Fgf and Cdkn2a/Cdkn1a senescence readouts were also absent under Tbx2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The null is informative for mature neurons: if Tbx2 were actively repressing the embryonic Shh/Fgf axis or a proliferative senescence module in these cells, snRNA-seq should have captured secondary mRNA changes in Shh, Ptch1/Gli genes, Fgf10, Grem1, Cdkn2a, or Cdkn1a; none passed even targeted FDR inspection.

literature_claim: Tbx2 and Tbx3 can act downstream of BMP signaling and show functional redundancy in embryonic tissues.
main_caveats: Single-gene Perturb-seq cannot test Tbx2/Tbx3 double loss, and some comparator targets were not recovered in every cell group.
summary: The close Tbx2/Tbx3/Tbx4/Tbx5 subfamily and represented BMP/FGF receptor comparators were themselves flat or one-gene responders in the same neuronal DE universe.
why_it_matters: The Tbx2 null is not contradicted by a strong paralog or upstream-receptor phenocopy; the embryonic Tbx2/Tbx3/BMP logic is largely uncoupled from these P16-perturbed neuronal groups.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Tbr1 regulates regional and laminar genes in postmitotic cortical projection neurons.
main_caveats: Tbr1 and Tbx2 belong to different T-box subfamilies, so the result is a context control rather than a paralog test.
summary: Tbr1, another represented T-box transcription factor with postmitotic cortical biology, showed a real cortical glutamatergic response while Tbx2 remained flat in the same broad groups.
why_it_matters: This contrast prevents over-attributing the Tbx2 null to postmitotic timing or to an inability of CRISPR Perturb-seq to detect transcription-factor effects in cortical excitatory neurons after P16 delivery.

literature_claim: No prior was used for this unbiased comparison.
main_caveats: The comparison uses signed Wilcoxon score vectors, not shared FDR genes; because Tbx2 has zero FDR<0.10 genes, every overlap-based high-confidence comparison is empty.
summary: The global Tbx2 signature had no strong positive or negative neighbor; the top correlations were near zero and were carried by flat comparator surfaces.
why_it_matters: The unbiased search did not reveal a hidden Tbx2-like molecular module among 1755 scored targets, so mechanistic interpretation should not be borrowed from the nominal Gpx4, Mycn, Mef2d, Fntb, Nhs, or Sp110 ranks.

literature_claim: Tbx21/T-bet biology is concentrated in lymphoid type-1 programs and, in the mouse brain, olfactory-bulb mitral/tufted projection neurons rather than broad postnatal forebrain and midbrain neurons.
main_caveats: The screen lacks DNA indel measurements and cannot separate absent editing from absent target protein in single cells; however the flat self-transcript is expected for this sparse LoF design and is not by itself evidence of failure.
summary: Tbx21 loss of function produced no robust transcriptional response in any of the 22 measured non-olfactory neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: This converts the dominant zero surface into a biological result: the postnatal, NeuN-enriched, olfactory-bulb-depleted assay did not sample the two lineages in which Tbx21 is expected to be active.

literature_claim: T-bet acts with cytokine/STAT and Runx circuitry to control type-1 lymphoid differentiation and IFN-gamma production.
main_caveats: Ifng and Il12rb2 were not perturbation targets in the parquet, and the assay intentionally undersampled immune cells; the finding is an absence of a neuronal Tbx21/Th1-like program, not a lymphocyte loss-of-function test.
summary: No T-bet type-1 immune module was recovered: expected effector genes such as Ifng, Il12rb2 and Cxcr3 were FDR=1.0 throughout the Tbx21 surface, and represented immune comparators Stat1, Stat4, Runx3 and Rorc were themselves broad nulls in matched neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Tbx21 perturbation in purified neuronal nuclei does not mimic a lymphocyte perturbation or produce an ectopic interferon-gamma axis, so the immune literature should not be projected onto these neuronal nulls.

literature_claim: Tbr1, Tbr2/Eomes and Tbx21 overlap in olfactory-bulb mitral/tufted cells, whereas Tbr1 and Tbr2 also appear in other brain regions.
main_caveats: The comparison uses short Wilcoxon signatures rather than matched OB mitral/tufted neurons, and Eomes/Tbr2 was not available as a perturbation target.
summary: The expected OB T-box relative Tbr1, unlike Tbx21, had 28 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in L5-6 IT, L4-5 IT, L2-3 PIR/AON/ENT, and NP-CT-L6b-OB glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: A same-OB T-box relationship did not translate into postnatal non-OB interchangeability: Tbr1 retains a cortical/deep glutamatergic transcriptomic role that Tbx21 lacks in this tissue scope.

main_caveats: Cosine similarities over all genes are dominated by a flat Tbx21 vector; Arid1a and Glis3 were rejected as robust convergent comparators because their few significant genes did not overlap a Tbx21 FDR signature.
summary: Genome-wide score-neighbor analysis placed Tbx21 next to safe-target and near-null perturbations; the strongest positive cosine was only +0.0406 and the strongest negative was -0.0124.
why_it_matters: The null is not hiding as a weak copy of a stress, proteasome, or immune regulator elsewhere in the screen; it sits in the empirical background-like basin of the perturbation universe.

why_it_matters: This is a broad, FDR-level negative result across glutamatergic and GABAergic forebrain, thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and cerebellar neuronal classes; the few nominal rows are not interpretable as programs.

literature_claim: Loss of TBX22 causes a developmental craniofacial syndrome and Tbx22-null mice show posterior hard-palate osteoblast maturation defects, including reduced Runx2 expression.
main_caveats: The expected palate genes were queried in nuclei from neuronal brain cell groups, not in the affected palate mesenchyme or osteoblast lineage.
summary: The CPX-associated palatal osteogenic program expected from germline Tbx22 loss was absent from the neuronal snRNA-seq response.
why_it_matters: The dataset supports the idea that TBX22 disease biology resides off the sampled neuronal axis: canonical loss causes embryonic palate, tongue, choanal, and osteoblast maturation defects, while P16 neuronal loss did not alter Runx2/Sp7/Alpl/collagen or palatal signaling genes.

literature_claim: Tbx2/Tbx3 have palatal-mesenchyme roles, whereas Tbr1 has a direct cortical projection-neuron identity role.
main_caveats: The Tbr1 response was small and Tbx22 was not recovered in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, the largest Tbr1 responder, so the matched contrast uses the other three Tbr1-responsive groups.
summary: Tbx22 did not converge with represented developmental T-box factors, while the matched neural T-box comparator Tbr1 showed detectable cortical/NP transcriptional effects.
why_it_matters: The contrast rejects a simple T-box-family phenocopy model in this assay: palatal/developmental T-box factors were flat or single-gene responders in neurons, but a neuronally wired T-box factor was measurable, indicating that the screen can recover a T-box transcription-factor effect when the biology is lineage matched.

main_caveats: Cosine neighborhoods of a wholly null target are dominated by weak rank noise; the important result is the near-zero magnitude, not the identities of the named neighbors.
summary: The closest global Tbx22 rank-space neighbors were near zero and were rejected as biological modules.
why_it_matters: Nearest-neighbor analysis over the complete model-visible perturbation universe found no convergent or anti-convergent target capable of explaining the flat Tbx22 surface; Cnnm2 and Prdm16 were themselves null or one-gene signatures, and Wdr26 was a broad responder with negligible negative cosine.

literature_claim: ACBD6 is a lipid acyl-CoA carrier that regulates acyl-CoA transfer reactions; no established source makes Acbd6 a canonical Tbx3 target.
main_caveats: The call is a single gene at FDR=0.077 in only 33 perturbed L5-6 IT nuclei, so it should be treated as a candidate marker, not as a validated Tbx3 lipid program.
summary: Tbx3 produced only one FDR<0.10 downstream call: Acbd6 was reduced in 001 L5-6 IT Glut.
why_it_matters: A developmental transcription factor with strong hypothalamic priors was nearly transcriptionally buffered in this P16-to-P37/44 neuronal assay; the one recovered gene is a lipid acyl-CoA-handling candidate rather than a fate or neuropeptide module.

literature_claim: Tbx3 maintains melanocortin Pomc/Cart and Agrp/Npy identity and hierarchically establishes and maintains KNDy neurons in the hypothalamus.
main_caveats: The screen bins are broad; sparse arcuate or KNDy Tbx3-positive neurons could be diluted below detection, and Kiss1 was not represented among the Tbx3 DE rows.
summary: The expected hypothalamic melanocortin/KNDy neuropeptide program was not recovered after Tbx3 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Loss of Tbx3 in resolved arcuate and KNDy neurons is expected to alter Pomc/Cart, Agrp/Npy, Kiss1/Tac2/Pdyn identity programs, which are transcriptional readouts that snRNA-seq should capture if enough affected neurons were present in a tested bin.

literature_claim: Tbx3 belongs to a developmentally deployed T-box transcription-factor family whose functions are strongly tissue and paralog dependent.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and limited to cell groups recovered for each perturbation; most non-Tbr1 T-box targets were themselves weak in this screen.
summary: Tbx3 did not phenocopy represented T-box relatives; Tbr1, not Tbx3 or Tbx2-subfamily targets, gave the main cortical T-box response.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates T-box DNA-binding-family membership from functional interchangeability in juvenile neurons: the same assay detected a Tbr1 cortical IT/NP program while Tbx3, Tbx2, Tbx4, and Tbx19 were flat or nearly flat.

main_caveats: The ranking was calculated on very weak Tbx3 scores; it is most useful as evidence of isolation, not as a mechanistic neighbor list.
summary: Tbx3 had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor in the global perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The nearest Wilcoxon-score profiles were essentially zero-correlation neighbors and shared no FDR<0.10 Acbd6 response, so the single-gene Tbx3 result should not be promoted to a recurrent cross-perturbation module.

main_caveats: CRISPR indels were not sequenced, and four groups had fewer than 50 perturbed nuclei; a transcriptomic null in neurons is not a test of embryonic mesenchyme.
summary: Tbx4 produced a pan-neuronal transcriptomic zero in this P16-to-P37/P44 mouse-brain CRISPR screen.
why_it_matters: The result argues against an active, cell-autonomous Tbx4-maintained transcriptional program in any of the recovered postmitotic NeuN+ neuronal groups, despite broad coverage of cortical, hippocampal, thalamic, midbrain and cerebellar neurons.

literature_claim: Pathogenic TBX4 dosage is established in lower-limb/pelvic and pulmonary vascular disease and has adult lung-mesenchymal roles.

summary: The neuronal null displaces TBX4 disease biology toward skeletal and pulmonary mesenchymal compartments rather than juvenile brain neurons.
why_it_matters: TBX4 loss-of-function human phenotypes include small patella syndrome and childhood pulmonary arterial hypertension, and TBX4-lineage lung mesenchyme can drive adult fibrosis; this screen did not reveal a direct neuronal transcriptional toxicity axis for Tbx4 loss.

literature_claim: Tbx5 loss in heart decreases cardiac outputs such as ANF/Nppa and Cx40/Gja5, Tbx5 drives Scn5a in the cardiac conduction system, and Tbx4/Tbx5 limb initiation engages Wnt/Fgf signaling.
main_caveats: Absence of these genes from the neuronal responses is expected for the sampled lineage; it should not be read as failure of the published cardiac or limb networks.
summary: Juvenile neuronal Tbx5 perturbation did not recover the canonical Holt-Oram cardiac-output or limb Wnt/Fgf programs.
why_it_matters: Cardiac/forelimb disease biology predicts Nppa, Gja5, Scn5a and Fgf/Wnt-linked outputs after Tbx5 loss; those genes were tested but uniformly FDR=1, and cardiac/FGF comparators were nearly flat and nonconvergent in the same parquet.

literature_claim: Tbx5 is a DNA-binding developmental transcription factor with curated roles in heart and embryonic forelimb morphogenesis.
main_caveats: The P16 mosaic CRISPR assay did not measure DNA indels and several null groups had fewer than 50 perturbed nuclei; a flat self-transcript is expected in this design and does not prove absence of editing.
summary: The postnatal neuronal Tbx5 knockout surface was almost completely buffered at the soma-transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: Across 355046 rows from 21 measured cell groups, Tbx5 produced only one downstream FDR<0.10 event and no FDR-supported ISR, UPR, proteostasis, redox, translation, autophagy or synaptic-collapse program.

literature_claim: Tbx6 is an embryonic T-box transcription factor with restricted primitive-streak, tail-bud and presomitic-mesoderm expression and null phenotypes in somite patterning.
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes crossed FDR<0.10, both at FDR 0.0595; the assay did not measure DNA indels, and the Tbx6 transcript itself did not decrease significantly.
summary: Postnatal Tbx6 loss produced a very small, CTX-CGE GABA-restricted signature: Atosa increased and Dynll2 decreased, both at FDR 0.0595, while the other 21 measured cell groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: A canonical embryonic paraxial-mesoderm transcription factor is not completely featureless in this juvenile brain assay, but its only robust neuronal output is a two-gene interneuron response rather than a mesodermal state change.

literature_claim: In presomitic mesoderm, Tbx6 cooperates with Notch and FGF inputs to activate Mesp2 and participates in Sox2 repression to keep axial cells out of a neural fate.
main_caveats: This is pathway absence in postmitotic neurons only; the experiment was not designed to test embryonic somite formation.
summary: The CTX-CGE GABA signal is uncoupled from the canonical Tbx6-Mesp2/Notch/Sox2 somitogenesis circuit and was not reproduced by measured T-box, Notch, or FGF comparators in the same cell group.
why_it_matters: The assay could query the expected mRNAs, so their absence shows that the neuronal two-gene response is not a replay of the embryonic segmentation-clock program.

literature_claim: No prior literature-defined convergence was needed for the unbiased nearest-neighbor test.
main_caveats: The correlation screen is dominated by a very sparse Tbx6 signature; it is strongest as a rejection of convergence, not as a positive mechanistic link to the near-zero numerical neighbors.
summary: The unbiased nearest-neighbor search yielded only near-zero whole-surface cosines, and Pitx3, Dlx6, Sp7, Ufc1, Uba5 and Cd81 all failed to reproduce the Atosa/Dynll2 pair in CTX-CGE GABA at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The private two-gene CTX-CGE GABA response should be treated as isolated and hypothesis-generating, not as a member of a larger recurrent module recoverable in this screen.

literature_claim: Tcf12 is an E-box bHLH transcription factor expressed during embryonic CNS development and linked to neural precursor expansion and positive regulation of neuronal differentiation.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured and the target transcript itself was flat, as expected for sparse AAV CRISPR; the claim is restricted to detected snRNA changes in surviving NeuN+ nuclei.
summary: Tcf12 loss in the P16-to-P37/44 NeuN+ neuronal assay was a pan-neuronal transcriptional null, not a local effect hidden in one cell group.
why_it_matters: The complete absence of FDR<0.10 downstream genes across 22 measured groups argues that Tcf12 is not an acute maintenance factor for the sampled juvenile postmitotic neuronal transcriptomes, while leaving embryonic and unsampled-lineage roles open.

literature_claim: Tcf12 cooperates with NeuroD1 at E-box-rich cortical migration loci during the progenitor-to-neuron transition and controls embryonic mesodiencephalic dopaminergic specification.
main_caveats: The most direct 215 MB Dopa class lacked Tcf12 rows; absence of the midbrain dopamine program is inferred from other measured neuronal groups.
summary: The embryonic Tcf12-NeuroD1 cortical migration and dopaminergic programs were not reactivated or collapsed after postnatal Tcf12 perturbation.
why_it_matters: snRNA-seq should have detected a secondary transcriptional response if P16 Tcf12 loss destabilized these programs; Wdfy3, Calm1, Kalrn, Angpt2, Nhlh1, Th, Pitx3, Lmx1a, Nr4a2, and Aldh1a1 remained FDR=1.0, separating embryonic chromatin-setting functions from postmitotic maintenance.

literature_claim: TCF3, TCF4, and TCF12 are related class-I E-proteins with overlapping but incomplete redundancy.
main_caveats: Tcf4 itself had only two FDR<0.10 genes, so the contrast is narrow, not a broad Pvalb pathway.
summary: Tcf4, but not its E-protein paralog Tcf12, produced a small Pvalb interneuron signature, demonstrating non-interchangeability of paralogs in this assay.
why_it_matters: Oprd1 and Tmem44 were significantly down-regulated by Tcf4 in Pvalb nuclei yet were completely flat after Tcf12 perturbation, so an E-protein family label alone did not predict the mature interneuron response.

literature_claim: Human TCF12 loss-of-function causes coronal craniosynostosis and Kallmann syndrome, and mouse Tcf12 has embryonic requirements in coronal-suture development.
main_caveats: The screen lacks cranial suture cells and did not recover 215 MB Dopa for Tcf12; GnRH neurons are rare and olfactory bulb was outside the tissue scope.
summary: The neuronal null does not contradict dosage-sensitive craniosynostosis or Kallmann biology; it displaces those TCF12 phenotypes to embryonic suture, GnRH, and olfactory-axis contexts absent from the assay.
why_it_matters: A negative sparse postnatal NeuN+ readout should not de-prioritize TCF12 haploinsufficiency in cranial-suture or GnRH developmental disease, because neither calvarial mesenchyme nor the olfactory/GnRH ontogenetic route was sampled.

literature_claim: No literature claim was used to nominate these pre-literature, data-driven neighbors.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score vectors, not on FDR-thresholded Tcf12 genes because Tcf12 had no such genes.
summary: Data-driven nearest neighbors of the Tcf12 signature were noise-floor rather than mechanistic convergence partners.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive and negative whole-surface correlations were |r|≤0.033 and came from unrelated, mostly flat perturbations, rejecting a hidden Clcn3-, Syncrip-, Nrg3-, or Fntb-like axis for Tcf12.

literature_claim: Mouse Tcf20 loss impairs cortical neurogenesis, and cortical-neuron knockdown alters dendrites, spines, and synaptic genes.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein depletion were not measured; a morphology or circuit phenotype could exist without a surviving-nucleus FDR-level mRNA program.
summary: Acute P16 Tcf20 loss produced no robust cell-autonomous nuclear transcriptome in any of 21 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The result separates the strong TCF20 neurodevelopmental prior from this postmitotic window: the assay did not reproduce embryonic cortical neurogenesis, dendritic-spine, Bdnf, or synaptic mRNA programs after sparse juvenile loss of function.

literature_claim: SPBP/TCF20 can coactivate NRF2-dependent SQSTM1 and LC3B expression after sulforaphane stress in cultured non-neuronal cells.
main_caveats: The prior is stress-induced and HeLa/U2OS-based; the screen did not apply oxidative or electrophilic stress.
summary: The stress-induced NRF2/SQSTM1 branch of SPBP biology was not engaged by Tcf20 loss in baseline neurons.
why_it_matters: If loss of Tcf20 had lowered tonic NRF2-autophagy transcription, Sqstm1, Map1lc3b, Nfe2l2, or a direct Nfe2l2/Sqstm1 comparator signature should have emerged; instead both the Tcf20 readout and direct Nfe2l2/Sqstm1 perturbations were flat or nearly flat in matched groups.

literature_claim: TCF20 and RAI1 are related chromatin proteins; MeCP2 interacts with a TCF20 complex and coregulates neuronal genes with TCF20.
main_caveats: Rai1 and Mecp2 were themselves weak in this acute assay, so the contrast is a statement about this design rather than about protein-complex stoichiometry in development.
summary: The MeCP2-TCF20/RAI1 chromatin axis did not collapse to a single matched signature in the postnatal screen.
why_it_matters: Rai1, the SPBP/TCF20 paralog, was almost as flat as Tcf20; Mecp2 yielded only 33 FDR genes in matched groups; and the Tcf20 vector had near-zero cosines to Rai1 and Mecp2, so this assay did not support simple interchangeability among these physically or evolutionarily related regulators.

main_caveats: The similarity search used all signed Wilcoxon z scores despite Tcf20 having no FDR genes, so it is useful mainly as a safeguard against overinterpreting noise.
summary: Whole-universe Tcf20 signature neighbors were extremely weak and did not define a hidden transcriptomic module.
why_it_matters: The top signed-z cosines were only +0.039 and -0.017; following the nominated neighbors back to their FDR surfaces showed Fbxo11, Ripor2, Zic3, and Gabrb2 were tiny responders and Ranbp2/Dhdds were non-overlapping responders, so nominal Tcf20 ranks should not be read as a real program.

main_caveats: The responding comparators are not TCF20 paralogs; they only establish detectability of some nuclear-regulator responses under the same statistical pipeline.
summary: Other transcriptional or chromatin perturbations generated detectable FDR-level programs where Tcf20 did not.
why_it_matters: Sin3a, Chd8, Tbr1, and Mef2c produced 28 to 3,761 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the Tcf20-matched groups, arguing that the Tcf20 null is not explained by a blanket inability of the platform to detect postnatal transcription-regulator phenotypes.

why_it_matters: Shared E-box binding and embryonic family biology did not translate into a shared P16-to-P44 neuronal snRNA-seq phenotype; even the disease-relevant paralog Tcf4 generated only a two-gene Pvalb response, while Tcf12 was completely flat.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation used signed Wilcoxon scores over matched gene/cell-group rows and should be read as transcriptome-level similarity, not protein-level pathway membership.

why_it_matters: The top positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations were close to zero and included safe-target perturbations, arguing that the absence of FDR hits is not hiding a reproducible low-amplitude Tcf3 state shared with another target.

literature_claim: E2A/Tcf3 can induce early neural-lineage genes and Tcf3/Tcf12 double loss perturbs MGE and oligodendrocyte-lineage developmental programs.
main_caveats: Marker absence in NeuN+ nuclei does not test oligodendrocyte-intrinsic effects, because glia were largely outside the sampled modality.

why_it_matters: The null is program-specific, not just a lack of named ontology enrichment: Sox1/Foxd4/Nodal-related genes, Id1-4, proneural bHLH genes, and OL/MGE markers were all absent at the Tcf3 FDR gate in the measured neurons.

literature_claim: TCF4 is a bHLH transcription factor expressed in postnatal excitatory and inhibitory neurons, and PTHS models nominate cortical/hippocampal excitatory neurons plus PV interneurons as vulnerable populations.
main_caveats: The positive signature contains only two genes and group-level pooling may hide narrower regional effects in the null populations.
summary: Acute postnatal Tcf4 loss produced a responder surface restricted to 052 Pvalb Gaba: 1/23 measured cell groups crossed FDR<0.10, with Oprd1 and Tmem44 both down-regulated.
why_it_matters: Tcf4 is broadly expressed and clinically central, so a near-global null with a small PV-only transcriptomic island argues that the P16 sparse neuronal assay captured a cell-state-specific postmitotic requirement, not the broad embryonic, glial, or circuit phenotypes that dominate Pitt-Hopkins models.

literature_claim: Endogenous delta opioid receptors are functional modulators of mouse hippocampal parvalbumin basket cells.
main_caveats: Tmem44 has no established TCF4/PV mechanism here, Oprd1 regulation is inferred from nuclear RNA rather than receptor protein, and direct TCF4 binding was not measured.
summary: Oprd1 was the strongest biological effector in the Tcf4 PV response, falling by logFC -0.570 at FDR 0.00884 together with Tmem44.
why_it_matters: Oprd1 encodes the delta opioid receptor; its selective loss proposes an opioid/neuromodulatory PV interneuron readout downstream of postnatal Tcf4 rather than a generic reduction of PV identity.

literature_claim: TCF4 acts as a homo- or heterodimeric class-I bHLH E protein, with context-dependent dimer partners, and Tcf3 can partly compensate for Tcf4 in an oligodendrocyte Olig2 system whereas Tcf12 cannot.
main_caveats: Several obvious dimer partners such as Ascl1, Neurog2, Olig2, and Id proteins were not represented as perturbation targets in this parquet.
summary: The represented E-protein paralogs Tcf3 and Tcf12, and the represented class-II bHLH factors Atoh1, Neurod1, and Neurod2, did not phenocopy Tcf4 in Pvalb neurons.
why_it_matters: The Pvalb Oprd1/Tmem44 response is not a generic consequence of perturbing a bHLH gene, sharpening Tcf4 as the active E-protein family member for this postnatal PV readout.

literature_claim: WAC is a neurodevelopmental-disorder gene studied in GABAergic neurons, but the Tcf4-Wac/Psmb4/Cltc convergence is not a canonical TCF4 complex relationship.
main_caveats: Neighbor ranking is restricted to the only two Tcf4 FDR genes and should be read as hypothesis-generating rather than as whole-transcriptome equivalence.
summary: The data-driven positive neighbors of the two-gene Tcf4 PV signature were Psmb4, Wac, Cltc, and Ctcf, whereas the nominal anti-neighbors Arx, Chd2, Kif1b, and Ski did not show FDR-supported opposite regulation of Oprd1/Tmem44.
why_it_matters: Oprd1/Tmem44 behave as a sensitive PV-state module reached from proteasome, WAC, clathrin, and chromatin perturbations more strongly than from textbook TCF4 relatives, but the broad Psmb4/Wac/Cltc inhibitory-synaptic collapse is buffered in Tcf4 cells.

literature_claim: Embryonic cortical, postmitotic-neurite, adult CA1, and prefrontal in utero TCF4 studies nominated Bmp7, Nrxn1, ciliary/membrane genes, and SCN10A/KCNQ1 as TCF4-responsive mechanisms.
main_caveats: The comparison spans bulk/FACS RNA-seq, human or rat systems, and different ages; Scn10a was not even testable in five cell groups because the gene had no row there.
summary: Canonical or proposed TCF4 targets from developmental and excitability literature—Cntnap2, Nrxn1, Bmp7, Rimbp2, Kcnq1, and Scn10a—were absent from the Tcf4 FDR surface.
why_it_matters: Postnatal sparse neuronal Tcf4 loss did not reproduce the embryonic cortical migration, Neurexin/Cntnap2, presynaptic RIMBP2, or SCN10A/KCNQ1 derepression programs, warning against treating those mechanisms as uniformly detectable acute neuronal LoF outputs across juvenile mouse brain cell groups.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Mouse TCF7L2 is maintained strongly in thalamic and selected mesencephalic neurons and functions postnatally as a thalamic terminal selector, whereas its neocortical Wnt role is in embryonic progenitors.
main_caveats: Sparse AAV CRISPR was assayed 3-4 weeks after P16 infection; 009 is a one-gene response and 215 MB Dopa has no Tcf7l2 rows.
summary: Tcf7l2 loss is sharply thalamic-selective in this P16 mosaic neuronal screen: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained 140 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, 009 had only Hp1bp3, 20 measured groups had none, and 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
why_it_matters: The selectivity matches TCF7L2 biology better than a pan-Wnt or pan-neuronal toxicity model and shows that the mostly flat surface is interpretable, not a global failure of CRISPR detection.

literature_claim: Postnatal thalamic Tcf7l2 knockout down-regulates ion-channel, neurotransmitter receptor, G-protein and synaptic-vesicle genes and impairs thalamic firing; Kcnc2, Grin2b, Gabra4 and Cacna1g are among direct or expected TCF7L2-linked terminal genes.
main_caveats: Cacna1g and Slc17a7 trended downward but did not pass FDR<0.10, so the recovered battery is partial.
summary: In 151, the strongest Tcf7l2 program is a mostly down-regulated thalamic terminal excitability and synaptic/neuropeptide battery, including Ramp3, Kcnc2, Pcsk2, Grin2b, Gabbr2, Gabra4, Gabra1, Prkcd, Pcp4 and Cpe.
why_it_matters: These genes are terminal effectors of thalamic firing and synaptic transmission; their recovery shows that postmitotic juvenile perturbation can still erode a TCF7L2-dependent thalamic state.

literature_claim: Embryonic Tcf7l2 loss down-regulates region-specific cell-migration and axon-guidance genes in the thalamo-habenular region and disrupts thalamocortical/thalamo-habenular morphology.
main_caveats: These P16-P37/44 genes are a subset of the embryonic wiring program, and cell morphology or axons were not imaged.
summary: The 151 signature also contains a neuronal projection, adhesion and extracellular-matrix arm: Ntng1, Spon1, Slitrk3, Edil3, Mmp15, Cntn1, Cdh2 and Robo1 are down-regulated.
why_it_matters: Tcf7l2 in embryos organizes thalamo-habenular connectivity; persistence of an adhesion/axon-guidance arm after P16 argues that the postnatal program is not limited to ion channels.

literature_claim: β-catenin is the activating cofactor for TCF/LEF factors and can displace Groucho/TLE repressors; TCF7L2 ChIP in adult thalamus binds synaptic/excitability genes.

why_it_matters: This rejects a simple downstream-transcription-factor chain and places TCF7L2 closest to Ctnnb1 rather than to RORA/PROX1/MEF2 factors in this juvenile cell-autonomous assay.

why_it_matters: The screen distinguishes Tenm3 from targets that trigger stress, proteostasis, synaptic, or identity transcriptional states. Even the two groups with significant Tenm3 self-mRNA decreases remained downstream-null, so modest self-transcript loss does not translate into an acute cell-state program.

literature_claim: Teneurins, latrophilins, and FLRTs form recognition complexes, and Ten3-Lphn2 interactions guide hippocampal target selection.
main_caveats: The comparison is gene-level and transcriptomic; it does not test combinatorial ligand/receptor loss, synaptic morphology, adhesion biochemistry, or teneurin isoform switches.
summary: The measurable Tenm/Lphn axis is null as a single-gene transcriptional module in this dataset: Tenm4 and Adgrl1-Adgrl3, including the Ten3 partner Lphn2/Adgrl2, also had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the 22 Tenm3-matched groups.
why_it_matters: A pathway-level query rejects the possibility that Tenm3 alone was an outlier while paralogous teneurin or latrophilin perturbations produced the expected adhesion-state program. The acute assay also saw only isolated singleton calls among FLRT, LRRTM, neurexin, Dscam, and UNC5 comparators, so this cell-surface synaptic class is generally buffered at the gene-expression layer.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation used all overlapping Wilcoxon-score features; with a zero-FDR target, tiny correlations should be treated as a quality-control statement, not evidence of shared mechanism.

why_it_matters: The top correlations nominated mostly other null targets, not a hidden Tenm3-like module elsewhere in the perturbation universe. This makes subsequent biological interpretation depend on Tenm3 biology and assay displacement rather than on an unrecognized convergent transcriptional program.

literature_claim: Tenm3 loss perturbs developing visual, hippocampal, hypothalamic, and thalamostriatal wiring and biallelic human TENM3 variants cause congenital microphthalmia/coloboma-spectrum disease.

summary: The absent Epha7/Ephb1/Zic2 response reframes Tenm3 biology here as developmental wiring or ocular morphogenesis displaced from a P16 whole-brain neuronal transcriptomic assay, not as a postmitotic stress or identity-collapse program.
why_it_matters: Mouse and human Tenm3 phenotypes involve visual-map formation, hippocampal and thalamostriatal topography, SCN innervation, and congenital eye disease. Those phenotypes predict changes in axon targeting, target-field matching, retinal eye development, or visual guidance genes such as Epha7, Zic2, and Ephb1; none was recovered at FDR<0.10 in the P16 neuronal screen.

literature_claim: CNTROB encodes a centrosomal protein required for centriole duplication and cytokinesis; DCAF15 is a CRL4-DCAF15 substrate receptor that can be co-opted by aryl-sulfonamide molecular glues.
main_caveats: Only two genes pass FDR<0.10, so the pathway assignment is based on the identities of the responders rather than a coordinated gene set.
summary: Tfdp1 produced a narrowly restricted up-response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Cntrob and Dcaf15 were the only two downstream genes reaching FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result converts an otherwise flat DP1 perturbation into a cell-type-selective, two-gene thalamic signature rather than a pan-neuronal E2F response. literature_claim: E2F-DP complexes drive E2F-responsive G1-S transcription in proliferating cells, while postmitotic neuronal E2F1 responses are strongly DNA-damage and context dependent.
main_caveats: The screen is a homeostatic postnatal LoF assay and cannot test Tfdp1 during active progenitor proliferation or after an acute DNA-damage challenge.

why_it_matters: DP1 is expected to control E2F-dependent G1-S transcription in cycling cells; here, the two FDR hits were not Mcm/Pcna/Cdc/Cyclin genes and 21 assayed cell-cycle markers all had FDR=1.0 in the responder. The result argues that P16 loss of Tfdp1 in settled NeuN+ neurons does not reactivate or suppress a coordinated S-phase program.

literature_claim: DP1 and DP2 are the principal DP partners for canonical E2F transcription factors, and DP-family perturbation would be expected to converge if the assayed effect were a shared E2F-DP program.

why_it_matters: DP1 is a core E2F dimerization partner and DP2 is its obvious paralog; direct measurement shows that the small Tfdp1 thalamic response is not a generic consequence of weakening the assayed E2F/DP family members.

summary: Tor1a, Rrm1, and Birc5 were not robustly altered in any Thap1 neuronal cell group.
why_it_matters: The null separates acute postmitotic Thap1 loss from two canonical transcriptional outputs: TOR1A repression in neuroblastoma-like cells and RRM1/E2F cell-cycle regulation in proliferating endothelial cells.

main_caveats: The Prepl perturbation's own 4-feature match was rejected because it was self-transcript reduction; interpretation relies on Camta1 and Ogt as true downstream Prepl comparators.
summary: Prepl is a reusable cross-perturbation effector rather than a Thap1-specific downstream node.
why_it_matters: Camta1 and Ogt down-regulated Prepl in the same cell classes without recapitulating the full Cuedc2/Fam117a arm, warning that Prepl alone is a sensitive biomarker but not a sufficient marker of a complete Thap1-like state.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Ronin/Thap11 is best established as an essential embryonic, ES-cell, and retinal-progenitor transcription factor rather than as a broadly tested postmitotic neuronal regulator.
main_caveats: The screen measures acute sparse LoF in surviving juvenile neurons; it does not quantify DNA indels or THAP11 protein.
summary: Thap11 has an acute postmitotic neuronal transcriptomic role in 22 of 23 recovered classes, but the effect is strongly graded.
why_it_matters: The response is not a failed perturbation masked by the flat Thap11 mRNA row: recurrent genes reappear across many independently sampled classes, while the thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, pineal, and Pvalb GABA groups carry most of the load.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: A genome-scale CRISPR screen identified THAP11, HCFC1, and OGT as transcriptional repressors of PARK2/PARKIN.
main_caveats: PARKIN protein and pUb/mitophagy flux were not measured.
summary: Prkn is a recurrent positive readout of Thap11 loss in mature neurons.
why_it_matters: The 17-class Prkn increase supplies the clearest single-gene confirmation that the known THAP11-PARK2 repression axis operates in postnatal neurons and gives a candidate mRNA biomarker for THAP11 functional inhibition in nuclei where the target transcript itself stays flat.

literature_claim: Ronin/Thap11 activates mitochondrial programs in ES cells and retinal progenitors and THAP11-HCFC1 controls the cobalamin gene MMACHC.
main_caveats: Most measured cell classes showed no FDR<0.10 Mmachc change despite sharing the core signature.
summary: Thap11 loss depresses mitochondrial and cobalamin transcripts in only the strongest neuronal responders.
why_it_matters: The postnatal neuronal phenotype preserves the developmental literature's direction for positive THAP11 control of mitochondrial and MMACHC expression, but it restricts robust MMACHC detection to thalamic, midbrain, and hypothalamic responders rather than all neurons.

literature_claim: THAP11 loss can de-repress PARKIN, a regulator of mitophagy.
main_caveats: Autophagic flux, lysosome function, and mitochondrial turnover are inferred from mRNA and were not directly assayed.
summary: The Parkin rise is embedded in mixed, partly antagonistic autolysosomal and mitochondrial quality-control remodeling.
why_it_matters: Thap11 loss does not simply turn on a complete mitophagy cassette: Prkn, Fyco1, and Htra2 rise, whereas Vps41, Slc38a9, Fundc1, Atg4c, Dnm1l, Tsc2, and Lamtor2 fall, suggesting adaptation around damaged-mitochondria handling and lysosomal nutrient signaling rather than one linear pathway.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: No specific prior Thap11-ciliary neuronal program was identified.
main_caveats: This is a gene-level module; ciliary structure or trafficking was not measured.
summary: A noncanonical centrosome/cilium and endomembrane-trafficking module is the most repeated part of the Thap11 signature.
why_it_matters: Sdccag8, Rabac1, Slc38a7, Acp6, Tcea2, and the reciprocal Cep128/Cep97 changes appear in more classes than MMACHC itself, so the in vivo neuronal output of Thap11 extends beyond the canonical mitochondrial/cobalamin program.

literature_claim: Elongator controls tRNA wobble-uridine modification, and the integrated stress response selectively induces ATF4-associated amino-acid stress genes.
main_caveats: ATF4 protein, eIF2α phosphorylation, and tRNA modification were not measured, so the ISR label is transcriptomic.
summary: Amino-acid and ATF4-like stress transcripts are a thalamic branch, not a pan-neuronal consequence, of Thap11 loss.
why_it_matters: Only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut combined the core mitochondrial/Prkn signature with Asns, Chac1, Slc7a5, Slc7a1, Slc1a4, Mthfd2, and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase induction, explaining why Elp1 and Elp2 converged with Thap11 almost exclusively in that group.

literature_claim: No direct literature claim links Thap11 loss to this postmitotic synaptic mRNA subset.
main_caveats: The finding is mRNA-only and uses selected genes rather than electrophysiology or synapse measurements.
summary: Thap11 perturbation repeatedly downregulates selected mature-neuronal synaptic and excitability genes.
why_it_matters: Cdk5, Napb, Scn2a, Bace1, and Adam22 decreases show that the response reaches neuronal signaling machinery, especially in the broad deep responders, without producing a wholesale neuronal identity loss program.

literature_claim: THAP11 recruits HCF-1 to chromatin, HCFC1 co-occupies THAP11 promoters, and THAP11-HCFC1-OGT converge on repression of PARK2.
main_caveats: Ogt was absent from two Thap11-measured groups and did not phenocopy the 151 thalamic branch.
summary: Ogt is the top measured signature neighbor of Thap11 and shares the recurrent downregulated core in a subset of groups.
why_it_matters: The data-driven top neighbor independently points to the known OGT-HCF1-THAP11 axis and rules against interpreting flat Thap11 self-mRNA as global non-engagement.

literature_claim: THAP proteins share HCF-1-binding logic and HCF-1 interfaces with Sin3 and Set1/Ash2 chromatin complexes.
main_caveats: Hcfc1 and Zfp143 themselves were not represented as perturbation targets, and cross-target comparisons use mRNA signatures rather than protein complexes.
summary: THAP-family and chromatin relatives were not interchangeable with Thap11 in this neuronal assay.
why_it_matters: Thap1, Kmt2a, Crebbp, and Ep300 were weak or oppositely ranked neighbors, and Sin3a was mixed despite many total DEGs; only Setd1a showed a mild positive restricted cosine. The THAP11 effect therefore requires the specific THAP11/OGT limb rather than generic HCF1-associated chromatin perturbation.

literature_claim: ELP1 and ELP2 are Elongator-complex members involved in tRNA modification; proteasome subunits are not established THAP11 partners.
main_caveats: Psmb4/Psmc1 signatures were far broader than Thap11 and had many opposite-direction overlaps; Ranbp2 was explicitly rejected.
summary: Several high-ranked noncanonical neighbors were proteostasis or RNA-translation perturbations, but only Elp1/Elp2 survived as a localized coherent match.
why_it_matters: The top ranks placed Elp1, Psmb4, Elp2, Ranbp2, and Psmc1 near Thap11. Follow-up overlap kept Elp1/Elp2 for the 151 amino-acid branch and Psmb4/Psmc1 as broad, mixed proteasome neighbors, while rejecting Ranbp2 as subthreshold-only.

literature_claim: Thoc1 is essential in early embryos and its requirement can vary strongly across cellular contexts.
main_caveats: The signature is cell-nucleus transcript abundance only; sparse guide counts make one-gene responders difficult to interpret mechanistically.
summary: Acute Thoc1 loss produced a sharply selective neuronal response: 1331 of 1353 FDR-significant downstream rows came from 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: THOC1 is a housekeeping mRNA-export subunit, yet the postmitotic P16 brain assay reveals a cell-state-restricted transcriptional vulnerability rather than a uniform pan-neuronal collapse.

literature_claim: THOC1 is a core THO/TREX subunit coupling RNA polymerase II transcription, mRNA processing, and nuclear export through DDX39B/UAP56 and NXF1-NXT1-associated export machinery.
main_caveats: 10x gene counts cannot directly score nuclear export, RNA localization, R-loop burden, or isoform-level splicing.
summary: The major responders carried a THO/TREX-compatible RNA-biogenesis program, with Sart1, Sf3a3, Dhx38, Exosc10, and Ncbp1 induced while mRNA-export or spliceosome genes including Nxf1, Rnpc3, Snrnp70, Srrm2, and Ddx17 were recurrently repressed.
why_it_matters: The strongest in vivo neuronal signal points back to THOC1's direct domain—mRNP formation, splicing-associated export, and nuclear RNA handling—rather than to an unrelated stress artifact.

literature_claim: THOC1 links elongating RNA polymerase II to RNA-processing factors, and THO also interacts with the Sin3A chromatin complex in R-loop suppression.
main_caveats: The induced chromatin regulators are a transcriptomic correlate; the data do not show chromatin occupancy or histone-state changes.
summary: Thoc1 responders up-regulated many chromatin and transcriptional regulators, including Smarcc2, Gtf2i, Gtf2f1, Med1, Ncor2, Ubtf, Dnmt1, Smarca2, Smarca4, and Kdm6b.
why_it_matters: This preserves the compensatory transcription/chromatin layer of the response, consistent with cells attempting to rebalance transcription-coupled RNA processing rather than simply losing RNA globally.

literature_claim: THO can regulate selected synaptic transcripts and Thoc5 loss affects dopamine-neuron synapse maintenance and survival.
main_caveats: The perturbed Thoc1 target was not recovered in MB Dopa cells, so dopamine-neuron THO vulnerability is not directly tested here.
summary: The broad Thoc1 signatures included neuronal membrane-traffic and cytoskeletal-transport genes: Anxa6, Whamm, Vps35l, Rab11fip4, Ap3d1, Tpcn1, Hook2, Kif1a, Map1b, and Stx1b were recurrently up, while Agrn was recurrently down.
why_it_matters: The response is not limited to nuclear RNA genes; it extends to the trafficking and synaptic-delivery layer that would be needed to buffer altered mRNA export in neurons with long processes.

literature_claim: THOC1 hair-cell deficiency and compromised THOC2/TREX neurodevelopmental models can lead to p53-mediated apoptosis, R-loop accumulation, DNA damage, and cell death.
main_caveats: R-loops and γH2AX are not assayed directly; this is a negative statement about secondary gene-expression programs only.
summary: The Thoc1 neuronal signature lacked the expected overt p53/apoptosis, DNA-damage, UPR, or integrated-stress transcriptional program at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The postnatal neuronal response is therefore better read as RNA-processing and adaptive remodeling, not as the same p53-mediated hair-cell death or embryonic DNA-damage/cell-death phenotype described for stronger THO/TREX disruption.

literature_claim: DDX39B/UAP56 is an accessory TREX factor that engages the THO-containing mRNP export machinery.
main_caveats: Ddx39b itself had few perturbed nuclei in some shared cell groups, so failure to phenocopy outside MB P MY GABA is a moderate-confidence divergence.
summary: Data-driven convergence was strongest with splicing/export/nuclear-pore perturbations, but the exact TREX accessory Ddx39b only gave a small, MB P MY GABA-restricted phenocopy: 21 of 21 shared 191 MB P MY GABA genes matched Thoc1 direction, whereas Ddx39b was flat in 066, 110, 151, and 155.
why_it_matters: The same-complex comparison shows that the Thoc1 signal is not a generic property of every TREX-factor perturbation in every responsive cell group; MB P MY GABA is the clearest shared TREX-sensitive context.

literature_claim: THO/TREX depletion and THO-Sin3A disruption can induce R-loop-associated genome instability.
main_caveats: SETX loss is not molecularly identical to THOC1 loss; R-loop abundance was not directly measured.
summary: Setx, a represented R-loop-resolution target, had zero FDR-significant genes across the whole screen, and Sin3a only partially overlapped Thoc1, arguing against the measured Thoc1 signature being a generic R-loop axis.
why_it_matters: Although THO/TREX can suppress R-loops, the neuronal FDR surface resolves toward splicing/export and chromatin compensation rather than a universal SETX-like R-loop response.

literature_claim: Hr is a thyroid-hormone-regulated brain gene and a corepressor that associates with thyroid hormone receptor and HDACs.
main_caveats: The assay does not distinguish direct TRα binding from short-range secondary effects in this thalamic group.
summary: Acute Thra loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut lowered Hr, the clearest recovered direct thyroid-hormone target, while Thra itself was also FDR-significantly lower in the same nuclei.
why_it_matters: Hr gives an internal positive control for ligand-dependent TRα transcription in one postmitotic glutamatergic thalamic population; the canonical target fires despite the generally modest self-transcript drop expected in this CRISPR design.

literature_claim: Thyroid hormone affects many developing brain processes, including neuronal and glial maturation, migration, synaptogenesis and myelination.
main_caveats: Zfp386 and Rogdi sit just below the q=0.10 cutoff; the conclusion is about this P16-to-P37/44 transcriptional surface, not germline thyroid hormone biology.
summary: The Thra response surface was narrow: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and a borderline one-gene 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut signature had downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: A transcription factor with very broad developmental literature produced only five non-self FDR<0.10 edges in this P16 sparse neuronal LoF assay, arguing for strong stage and cell-state gating of detectable TRα output.

literature_claim: HCN channels shape neuronal excitability and ADGRB1/BAI1 has curated brain-development and seizure-susceptibility annotations.
main_caveats: Only two genes support this module; their coregulation with Hr is transcriptomic and not proof of a direct TRα binding event.
summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Thra loss lowered the neuronal surface/excitability genes Adgrb1 and Hcn2 together with Hr.
why_it_matters: The non-Hr arm links TRα perturbation to thalamic neuronal excitability or synaptic adhesion rather than to a broad stress, proteostasis or UPR program, none of which appeared at FDR<0.10.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation is restricted to five Thra FDR<0.10 non-self edges and should be treated as a restricted-signature comparison.
summary: The noncanonical Thra thalamic edges, not Hr, drove the data-driven neighbor map: Elp1/Bmal1/Rora/Cic converged mainly through Adgrb1 or Hcn2, whereas Zbtb7a/Xrn1/Hnrnpu opposed Adgrb1 and/or Rogdi.
why_it_matters: This separates an Hr-centered thyroid-hormone readout from a broader Adgrb1/Hcn2/Rogdi neuronal-maintenance signature shared with unrelated transcriptional and RNA-homeostasis perturbations.

literature_claim: Thra and Thrb encode thyroid hormone nuclear receptors, and thyroid receptors can regulate transcription from thyroid response elements as RXR heterodimers.
main_caveats: Canonical corepressors Ncor1, Ncor2, Hdac3 and the downstream mediator Hr were not represented as perturbation targets, so the strongest same-complex loss-of-function tests were unavailable.
summary: Represented thyroid-receptor family comparators did not phenocopy Thra: Thrb, Rxra and Rxrg were flat, and Rxrb had only one off-surface singleton outside the Thra responder groups.
why_it_matters: Although TRα acts in the thyroid nuclear-receptor/RXR system, the acute sparse transcriptomic response was TRα-selective rather than a generic consequence of losing any thyroid receptor or RXR partner.

literature_claim: Klf9 and Hr are expected thyroid-hormone target genes, and TRα/thyroid hormone signaling has established roles in GABAergic and cerebellar maturation and in human THRA dominant-negative disease.
main_caveats: The result is a negative transcriptional result in surviving NeuN-positive nuclei; it cannot exclude earlier fate, non-neuronal or circuit-physiology phenotypes.
summary: The assay did not recover the expected broad neurodevelopmental TRα programs: Klf9, Dbp, Nrgn, Aldh1a1, Dio3, Shh, Pvalb and Crip2 never reached FDR<0.10 after Thra perturbation, and all GABAergic and cerebellar bins were downstream-null or weak.
why_it_matters: Resistance-to-thyroid-hormone and hypothyroid phenotypes are interpreted largely through developmental or dominant-negative biology; simple post-P16 neuronal LoF gives a narrow Hr-centered signature, warning against treating adult TRα inhibition as a faithful model of those disease mechanisms.
