009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: TRβ is a chromatin-bound T3-responsive nuclear receptor, but its strongest receptor-beta-specific brain and sensory phenotypes are context restricted rather than expected in every neuron.
main_caveats: No DNA indel assay is available, and the weak self-transcript reduction is expected for this CRISPR design; silence should not be generalized to retina, cochlea, pituitary, or systemic thyroid-hormone physiology.
summary: Sparse postnatal Thrb loss was robustly silent across the sampled neuronal transcriptome: every one of the 21 measured cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and the Thrb mRNA row itself was never significant after correction.
why_it_matters: The primary observation is not a hidden canonical thyroid-hormone program but its absence; it confines cell-autonomous Thrb requirements away from most P16-to-P40 sampled neurons unless the effect needs a different lineage, developmental window, allele class, or receptor combination.

literature_claim: TRα and TRβ use the same T3/RXR/cofactor transcriptional logic, while TRα1 is the TR isoform broadly present in postmitotic and adult neurons.
main_caveats: The Thra comparator response is very small and the strongest single Thra gene, Hr, does not by itself define a full thyroid-hormone program.
summary: The literature-obvious TR network did not converge on Thrb: Thra produced only a five-gene response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, Rxra and Rxrg were fully flat, and Rxrb, Ncoa1, and Ncoa3 each produced only one FDR<0.10 gene with no shared Thrb overlap.
why_it_matters: TRβ ablation in this assay is not an interchangeable proxy for TRα, RXR, or SRC/p160 coactivator perturbation; the small Hr-centered Thra signal in thalamic glutamatergic neurons is the only robust hint that a thyroid-receptor axis was transcriptionally accessible.

main_caveats: The neighbor ranking used all genes, not a Thrb FDR signature; because Thrb had no DE genes, these are diagnostic contrasts rather than mechanistic interactors.
summary: Pre-literature all-gene neighbors confirmed that Thrb sits on a null-like background rather than in a coherent convergent module: its closest positive neighbors Glrb, Bckdhb, Ndufa9, and Ppp2r2b were also completely flat, whereas least-positive comparators such as Psmb4 and Psmc1 produced thousands of DE genes.
why_it_matters: This rejects the apparent all-gene logFC correlation as biological convergence and shows that the same analysis universe can detect large proteasome, transport, or translation perturbation surfaces in sparse cohorts, so Thrb silence is not explained by a universal inability of the screen to call DE.

literature_claim: TRβ is required for HPT-axis feedback, auditory maturation, and M-cone specification, and THRB mutations causing RTHβ usually act as dominant receptor alleles.
main_caveats: The broad hypothalamic and cerebellar groups are not purified TRβ2 feedback neurons, thyrotrophs, cones, or cochlear hair cells; absence of an opsin or cochlear marker signature in forebrain/midbrain/cerebellar nuclei is expected.
summary: The P16 neuronal Thrb CRISPR surface did not recover HPT-axis, retinal-cone, cochlear, or dominant-negative RTHβ programs: Trh, Tshb, Opn1mw, Opn1sw, Tecta, Slc26a5, Hr, and Klf9 all remained at FDR=1 in the Thrb surface.
why_it_matters: Human RTHβ and classic mouse Thrb phenotypes should not be read as predictions for a sparse postmitotic receptor knockout in pooled brain neurons; many disease mechanisms require endocrine feedback, sensory end organs, or mutant receptors that remain on DNA rather than simple Thrb loss.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: TIA1 and its paralog TIAR/TIAL1 bind related RNA motifs and the family can act redundantly in stress-granule and RNA-metabolism pathways.
main_caveats: This assay did not quantify DNA indels, TIA1 protein, stress-granule assembly, or splicing isoforms; each effect group carried a one-gene signature.
summary: Tia1 loss-of-function was transcriptionally buffered in basal juvenile postmitotic neurons: only two downstream FDR hits appeared across 19 recovered cell groups.
why_it_matters: The sparse result is a biological statement about this assay state, not a failed perturbation call: the target transcript itself was weak/flat as expected for CRISPR indels, while the measured downstream surface was almost empty.

literature_claim: DPM1 functions in dolichol-phosphate mannose synthesis for ER glycosylation, whereas ZYG11B is a CUL2 substrate receptor for the Gly/N-degron protein-quality-control pathway; no direct TIA1 link was found for either one.
main_caveats: Each cell class had exactly one FDR<0.10 downstream gene, so these are biomarker hypotheses rather than pathway-level programs.
summary: The two positive Tia1 readouts were single-gene, cell-class-isolated increases of Dpm1 in Pvalb interneurons and Zyg11b in hindbrain GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: Dpm1 nominates ER dolichol-mannose/glycosylation and Zyg11b nominates a CRL2 N-degron quality-control adaptor as possible homeostatic sentinel transcripts, but neither forms a broad TIA1 stress-granule module.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: TIA1 perturbation has been linked to stress-granule assembly, EIF2AK2-mediated stress responses, tau/TDP-43 granule pathology, hippocampal stress-dependent plasticity, immune transcripts, and lipid/membrane transcripts in other systems.
main_caveats: Wilcoxon DE on snRNA-seq cannot detect altered granule assembly, translation, protein aggregation, or alternative isoform ratios directly.
summary: Canonical TIA1 stress-granule, EIF2AK2/ISR-UPR, tau/RBP, and inflammatory sentinel transcripts were measured but absent from the FDR signature.
why_it_matters: The screen would have seen a secondary nuclear RNA stress response if acute Tia1 loss had generated one by 3-4 weeks; instead it uncoupled Tia1 LoF from the programs most expected under arsenite, tauopathy, or immune stress.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: TIA1, TDP-43, ATXN2, MATR3, VCP, FMRP, and hnRNPA2B1 sit in overlapping ALS or RNP-granule/RNA-metabolism disease biology.
main_caveats: The compared perturbations have different recovered cell numbers and target-engagement estimates; TIAL1, G3BP1, G3BP2, and FUS were not available as gene_target perturbations.
summary: Represented ALS/RNA-granule comparators did not phenocopy Tia1: Tardbp and Matr3 were broad responders, Atxn2 and Ddx3x were restricted responders, and Eif2ak4 and Ubp1 were flat without reproducing Dpm1/Zyg11b.
why_it_matters: Shared membership in RNA-binding, stress-granule, or ALS biology was not enough to define a common juvenile-neuron loss-of-function transcriptomic module.

main_caveats: Nearest-neighbor correlations were computed on a near-null Tia1 vector; this is most useful as a rejection of convergence, not as a mechanistic ranking.
summary: A data-driven cross-target search failed to identify a strong Tia1 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Both the residualized whole-transcriptome correlations and the exact two-gene FDR-overlap test indicated that the Tia1 signature was too sparse to form a reusable perturbation module.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Human TIA1 disease mutations promote phase separation and delayed stress-granule disassembly, and mouse tau/TIA1 studies expose chronic stress and neuroinflammatory phenotypes.
main_caveats: The screen covers only 3-4 weeks after sparse coding indels and lacks aged animals, tauopathy, proteomics, granule imaging, and glia-rich readouts.
summary: The P16 mosaic Tia1 LoF surface did not recapitulate ALS/FTD phase-transition or tauopathy expectations, supporting a context- and allele-specific view of TIA1 neurologic risk.
why_it_matters: Disease variants that alter TIA1 low-complexity-domain phase behavior or chronic tau stress should not be assumed to be modeled by sparse postmitotic CRISPR loss of Tia1 in unstressed juvenile neurons.

main_caveats: The assay lacks DNA indel readout and spine, electrophysiology, phosphorylation, and morphology measurements; a flat self-transcript is expected and does not prove failed editing.
summary: Tiam1 was a complete FDR-flat perturbation in the recovered neuronal atlas: all 22 measured Tiam1 cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10, while 215 MB Dopa was not tested.
why_it_matters: This establishes the primary phenotype before applying priors: the screen did not recover a robust nuclear transcriptomic program for postnatal sparse Tiam1 loss in any measured class.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: Tiam1 couples NMDA receptor activity to Rac1-dependent actin remodeling during dendritic arbor and spine development.
main_caveats: The comparison is between receptor-subunit CRISPR and a downstream GEF CRISPR; receptor loss can perturb calcium influx and activity-dependent transcription through Tiam1-independent routes.
summary: Canonical NMDA-receptor/Tiam1 coupling did not translate into a Grin-like transcriptional phenotype: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b produced 238 FDR<0.10 downstream calls in matched cell groups, whereas Tiam1 produced none.
why_it_matters: The same P16-to-P37/P44 snRNA-seq workflow could detect secondary transcriptional consequences of perturbing NMDA receptor subunits, so the Tiam1 null specifically uncouples Tiam1-Rac spine signaling from the nuclear programs elicited by direct NMDAR-subunit loss.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Tiam proteins are Rac GEFs and EphB signaling can recruit Tiam1 to activate Rac1-dependent actin remodeling at developing spines.
main_caveats: Tiam2, the closest paralog, was absent from the perturbation panel, and these null-null comparisons cannot exclude protein-level Rac pathway phenotypes.
summary: The expected Rac/EphB/PAK/WAVE neighborhood was also transcriptionally buffered: Rac1, Cdc42, Pak1-3, Kalrn, Cyfip1, Ephb1/2, Dock3, Limk1, and Tnik generated only four single-gene FDR hits across 251 matched target-cell surfaces and had near-zero correlations to Tiam1.
why_it_matters: Tiam1's null is not an isolated anomaly; in this dataset, multiple actin-cytoskeleton pathway nodes that are expected to act through rapid GTP loading, kinase signaling, and spine actin remodeling lacked a shared nuclear module after sparse juvenile CRISPR loss.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed on weak full-rank Tiam1 scores; they are a rejection analysis, not evidence for those genes being Tiam1 partners.
summary: Pre-literature signature-neighbor analysis found no strong Tiam1 transcriptomic relatives: the top signed-score Pearson correlations were only +0.0346 to Zic1 and -0.0352 to Safe_target_15, and the top neighboring real-gene perturbations were themselves mostly null.
why_it_matters: The unbiased screen-wide search therefore did not nominate an alternative biological module hidden in the Tiam1 ranks; weak positive or negative neighbors should be rejected rather than interpreted as convergent biology.

literature_claim: TIAM1 loss-of-function variants cause a developmental-delay/intellectual-disability/seizure syndrome, Tiam1 and Tiam2 shape hippocampal synapses, and the Rac inhibitor NSC23766 blocks Rac activation by Tiam1/Trio-like GEFs rather than acting as a Tiam1-specific drug.
main_caveats: The dataset contains no behavioral, seizure, electrophysiological, or medicinal-chemistry readout, and 215 MB Dopa was missing for Tiam1.
summary: The absence of a postnatal transcriptional stress signature is not a safety or efficacy green light for Tiam1/Rac inhibition.
why_it_matters: Human TIAM1 loss is neurodevelopmental, mouse Tiam1 loss affects dentate spines and memory, and available Rac inhibitors act at the Rac-GEF interface rather than selectively at Tiam1; this screen only says that sparse juvenile Tiam1 loss did not trigger a broad neuronal nuclear program.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Strong TIMMDC1 loss impairs mitochondrial respiratory complex-I assembly and can cause recessive complex-I deficiency.
main_caveats: Primary complex-I assembly and activity were not assayed, and DNA indels were not measured.
summary: Timmdc1 perturbation produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in every recovered neuronal group.
why_it_matters: A disease-linked complex-I assembly factor was not transcriptionally dominant in juvenile postmitotic neurons after sparse P16 CRISPR, establishing a strong negative snRNA result that must be interpreted separately from protein-level complex-I activity.

direction: ISR absent after Timmdc1, up after Opa1
literature_claim: Mitochondrial dysfunction can induce an ATF4/integrated-stress transcriptional program, and OPA1 loss perturbs inner-membrane cristae and energetics.
main_caveats: Opa1 had higher perturbed-cell counts than Timmdc1 in the responding groups, so it is a qualitative positive comparator rather than a matched-power threshold.
summary: Timmdc1 did not activate the Opa1-like mitochondrial ISR even in cell groups where that program is detectable in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: The absence of Asns/Ddit3/Chac1/Slc7a5/Shmt2 induction argues that Timmdc1 edits did not reach the functional mitochondrial stress threshold, rather than the snRNA readout being blind to such a program.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: TIMMDC1 and NDUFAF family proteins participate in mitochondrial respiratory complex-I biogenesis.
main_caveats: The canonical MCIA genes Acad9, Ecsit, Ndufaf1, and Tmem126b were not represented, and sparse one-gene FDR hits in scattered NDUF targets were not mechanistically interpretable.
summary: Complex-I assembly and NDUF structural perturbations were broadly silent in the Timmdc1-matched neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: The expected complex-I neighborhood did not phenocopy a large stress response: Ndufaf2, Ndufaf4, and Ndufaf5 were all flat, while 22 complex-I targets yielded only 11 DEGs across 308 matched tests. literature_claim: TNFRSF1A/TNFR1 is a death-domain-containing TNF receptor whose ligand-driven complexes can activate NF-kB, JNK/MAPK, apoptosis, or necroptosis.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation and protein loss were not measured; 215 MB Dopa had no Tnfrsf1a rows and cannot be interpreted.
summary: Acute Tnfrsf1a loss of function was a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null: every one of the 22 measured cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This converts the absence of DE from a caveat into a context-specific result: basal juvenile-to-young-adult NeuN+ neurons did not require TNFR1 to maintain a detectable nuclear transcriptome over 3-4 weeks.

literature_claim: Stimulated TNFR1 complexes signal through RIPK1/TRAF/TRADD ubiquitin scaffolds to TAK1-IKK-NF-kB and can induce inflammatory and survival transcripts.
main_caveats: Most proximal TNFR1 adaptors and the Tnf ligand were not represented as perturbation targets; this is a basal neuronal test, not a TNF-addback experiment.
summary: No basal TNF/NF-kB immediate program appeared after Tnfrsf1a perturbation, and measurable intracellular TNFR/NF-kB neighbors were likewise flat.
why_it_matters: The Tnfrsf1a null is not hiding a missed canonical cytokine program: Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Birc2/Birc3, chemokines, Rel-family genes, Jun, and Fos were all FDR=1 after Tnfrsf1a perturbation, while Chuk, Map3k7, Nfkb1, Cyld, and Traf3 perturbations also produced zero robust DE in their measured neuronal groups.

main_caveats: The correlation was computed on all Wilcoxon scores rather than a significant Tnfrsf1a gene set because Tnfrsf1a had no significant genes.
summary: Tnfrsf1a had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor in the complete perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The data-driven nearest neighbors were all essentially zero-correlated and had no shared FDR<0.10 overlap with Tnfrsf1a, so cross-target comparison rejects an unannotated phenocopy module.

why_it_matters: Human TNFRSF1A disease is dominated by autoinflammatory variant biology in immune contexts; the mouse CRISPR result argues against interpreting receptor deletion in postmitotic neurons as sufficient to autonomously induce the inflammatory transcripts associated with pathogenic TNFRSF1A states.

why_it_matters: This converts a flat screen result into a lineage-restricted OX40 statement: in homeostatic postmitotic neurons, acute Tnfrsf4 perturbation does not evoke the T-cell survival, cytokine, stress, or neuronal-remodeling transcriptome expected from an active costimulatory receptor.

literature_claim: OX40, 4-1BB, CD40, BAFF-R, Fas, TNFR, and TRAF/NF-kappaB pathways are prominent TNF-superfamily immune signaling axes, including in CNS autoimmunity when immune or glial compartments are engaged.

summary: Represented TNFR-family and NF-kappaB-neighbor perturbations were also essentially flat in the same neuronal groups: Cd40, Chuk, Map3k7, Nfkb1, Tnfrsf1a, Tnfrsf11a, Tnfrsf9, and Traf3 produced no matched FDR<0.10 genes, while Fas and Tnfrsf13c produced only one to four isolated genes.
why_it_matters: The expected same-family comparators did not reveal a hidden OX40-like neuronal module; they show that the assayed postmitotic neuronal state is broadly refractory to immune TNFRSF/NF-kappaB receptor perturbation rather than being uniquely buffered at Tnfrsf4.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score profiles in the model-visible DE universe; with an all-null Tnfrsf4 vector, the numerical nearest neighbors are best treated as rejection tests rather than biology.
summary: Unbiased cross-target signature search found no meaningful convergence or opposition: the best whole-profile Pearson correlations to Tnfrsf4 were only +0.028 for Ufsp2, +0.027 for Sox11, +0.027 for Erbb3, -0.014 for Eef2, and -0.013 for Arid1b.
why_it_matters: Because even the nearest perturbation neighbors are numerically near zero and often have their own flat or unrelated DE surfaces, Tnfrsf4 should not be assigned to a data-driven neuronal stress or developmental module in this screen.

literature_claim: TNIK has Wnt, JNK, and postsynaptic roles, but those priors do not imply pan-neuronal nuclear RNA changes after sparse postnatal disruption.
main_caveats: The perturbation has no DNA indel validation and no protein or phosphoprotein readout; 215 MB Dopa was not recovered for Tnik.
summary: P16 mosaic Tnik loss produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group.
why_it_matters: The dominant result is a broad absence of nuclear DE, not a hidden weak cell-type effect; proteostasis, ISR/UPR, redox, translation, and synaptic mRNA programs all failed to pass correction because there were no downstream DE genes at all.

literature_claim: TNIK was described as beta-catenin/TCF4-associated and required for optimal TCF/LEF transcription in mouse proliferative intestinal crypts and colorectal cancer cells.
main_caveats: The Wnt comparator response was concentrated in one thalamic group; TCF4 in the Wnt literature denotes TCF7L2, not the separate screen target Tcf4.
summary: Tnik did not phenocopy the CTNNB1-TCF7L2 transcriptional module that is visible in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 perturbations converged on 59 genes in the same thalamic group where Tnik had 179 perturbed nuclei and zero DE genes, so the canonical Wnt transcriptional axis is detectable in this assay but is not TNIK-dependent in this postmitotic context.

main_caveats: The comparison is all-gene and restricted to cell groups shared with Tnik; it deliberately does not infer biology from subthreshold Tnik genes.
summary: The unbiased neighbor search found no meaningful positive or inverse Tnik signature partner.
why_it_matters: The top Wilcoxon-score correlations were only 0.033 to -0.020 and included safe-target controls, rejecting both the apparent positive neighbors and the apparent inverse neighbors as biological convergence.

literature_claim: TNIK inhibitors are pursued to block downstream Wnt signaling in cancer, while TNIK loss in mice and humans perturbs postsynaptic signaling and cognition.
main_caveats: No small-molecule exposure, phosphoproteomics, electrophysiology, dendritic-spine imaging, or behavior was measured in the screen.
summary: The flat snRNA-seq result should not be interpreted as CNS safety for TNIK kinase inhibition.
why_it_matters: TNIK is a druggable Wnt effector, but its neuronal disease biology is concentrated in PSD organization, AMPA/NMDA signaling, kinase activity, and phosphoproteome changes that this nuclear RNA screen did not assay.

literature_claim: Alternative splicing is highly context-dependent because each cell type has a distinct mixture of RNA-binding regulators.
main_caveats: The result is gene-level snRNA-seq; isoform or protein-localization phenotypes could exist in the groups scored null.
summary: Tnpo3 loss produced a sharply uneven total-mRNA response: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA carried most of the 1734 FDR<0.10 downstream gene-cell calls, whereas 11 measured groups had no robust downstream genes.
why_it_matters: A nuclear-import factor for ubiquitous SR splicing proteins was not pan-neuronal in this postnatal mosaic assay; the secondary transcriptional consequence was restricted to a subset of thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, and small cortical/interneuron classes.

literature_claim: TNPO3/Transportin-SR2 is an importin-beta-family nuclear import receptor for phosphorylated RS-domain SR splicing factors, and Prpf6, U2af2, Cdc40, Rnpc3, and Snrnp70 are spliceosome-pathway factors.
main_caveats: The assay measures gene abundance, not SR-protein nuclear localization or splice isoform usage.
summary: The most canonical Tnpo3 module was down-regulation of SR-splicing and RNA-processing transcripts, led by Srrm2, Srsf5, Srsf1, Srsf7, Srsf2, Akap8l, Clk1, and Cstf2.
why_it_matters: TNPO3 imports RS-domain splicing cargoes; loss of Tnpo3 therefore leaves a recurrent total-mRNA footprint on the same RNA-processing system rather than a generic neuronal activation signature.

literature_claim: Nucleoporin TPR is a nuclear-pore-basket component of the TREX-2 mRNA export pathway.
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to Tnpo3 FDR<0.10 gene-cell pairs and does not establish direct physical interaction between Tnpo3 and Tpr.
summary: Tpr, a nuclear-basket mRNA-export perturbation, was the strongest same-direction FDR-overlap neighbor of Tnpo3, sharing 610 same-direction and only 22 opposite-direction significant gene-cell pairs.
why_it_matters: The data-driven neighbor screen links Tnpo3 cargo import with an mRNA-export pore component, extending the response from SR-factor import to a broader nuclear RNA-maturation axis.

literature_claim: Tnpo3 is specialized for RS-domain RNA-processing cargo import rather than classical NLS import or exportin biology.
main_caveats: Tnpo1 and Tnpo2 were not perturbation targets in the parquet, so close transportin paralogs could not be tested.
summary: Spliceosome and RNA-processing perturbations converged with Tnpo3, but broader nuclear-transport perturbations represented in the library did not.
why_it_matters: The matched-parquet comparison rejects a generic karyopherin defect: U2af2, Cdc40, Rnpc3, Snrnp70, and Thoc1 shared 114-313 same-direction calls with Tnpo3, while Kpna3 and Xpo7 shared none and Ranbp2 shared only 27, all in one MB Glut class.

literature_claim: Proteasome impairment can induce a transcriptional recovery or bounce-back response through Nrf1/NFE2L1.
main_caveats: Tnpo3 did not itself induce a full proteasome-subunit bounce-back regulon; the inference comes from cross-perturbation similarity to Psmc1 and Psmb4.
summary: Proteasome-subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 unexpectedly resembled Tnpo3 more than most RNA-processing genes did.
why_it_matters: Psmc1 was the second positive cosine neighbor and Psmb4 had 490 same-direction overlaps, nominating a convergence between splice-factor import failure and proteostasis stress in the same neuronal states.

main_caveats: Col20a1 is not a known Tnpo3 cargo-response gene; high logFC in snRNA-seq should be validated orthogonally before interpreting it as extracellular-matrix remodeling.
summary: Col20a1 was the broadest induced single transcript, significant in eight of ten responding cell groups.
why_it_matters: This recurrent collagen-family mRNA is a compact candidate marker for the Tnpo3-sensitive state, including very small signatures where Col20a1 and Srrm2 were the only robust genes.

literature_claim: Splicing regulators and transcriptional control are coupled and context-dependent.
main_caveats: The DE data identify a transcriptional secondary state but do not specify whether each regulator is a direct splice target.
summary: Broad subcortical responders remodeled transcription and chromatin regulators in both directions: Tcea2 was strongly down, while genes such as Btaf1, Zfp655, Cdk13, Akirin2, and Aff4 were induced.
why_it_matters: The SR-import lesion propagated to the transcriptional apparatus, consistent with a secondary attempt to re-balance RNA production and processing rather than a simple decrease in Tnpo3 mRNA.

literature_claim: Alternative splicing is a major regulator of neuronal excitability, synaptic function, and other mature neuronal properties.
main_caveats: Gene-level down-regulation is secondary and does not measure the splice isoforms of these neuronal transcripts.
summary: The largest 151/155/191 signatures included coordinated loss of neuronal receptor, ion-channel, adhesion, and synaptic transcripts including Grin1, Gria2, Kcnt1, Scn2b, Adam23, Lrrc7, and Syn1.
why_it_matters: Tnpo3 perturbation is not limited to RNA-processing genes; in vulnerable subcortical neurons the secondary state suppresses mature neuronal function genes after only 3-4 postnatal weeks.

main_caveats: Several genes are multifunctional, so this is a transcript set, not a proven organelle phenotype.
summary: A recurrent Rap/Rho, cytoskeletal, ciliary, and trafficking down-branch featured Rap1gap, Arhgef25, Coro6, Ahi1, Ttc4, Ttc8, and Stx16.
why_it_matters: The noncanonical branch connects the RNA-import lesion to cell-shape and intracellular-trafficking regulators, providing genes to monitor outside the core SR-splicing set.

main_caveats: The nuclei were NeuN-enriched and do not show whether induced ligand transcripts result in secreted protein or recruit glia in intact tissue.

why_it_matters: The neuron-enriched assay recovered a cell-intrinsic distress program downstream of RNA-processing imbalance that would have been detectable, but was absent, in the strict null groups.

main_caveats: This branch is small relative to the RNA-processing module and should be treated as a secondary hypothesis.

why_it_matters: Samm50 was the highest-confidence 054 hit and recurred in the broad responders, so the small CNU-MGE response is not isolated noise even though it contains only ten FDR<0.10 genes.

literature_claim: TNPO3 and HNRNPDL are RNA-processing genes mutated in autosomal-dominant limb-girdle muscular dystrophies, while DMD, SGCD, DAG1, and FKTN belong to the broader muscular-dystrophy landscape.

why_it_matters: Dominant TNPO3 myopathy is a muscle disease caused by C-terminal extension variants, so acute postmitotic neuronal loss of Tnpo3 is the wrong allele, lineage, and developmental context for a Dmd/Dag1/Sgcd/Fktn/Hnrnpdl-like program.

main_caveats: Restricted-signature anti-correlation can be driven by low-confidence logFCs; Huwe1 is mixed rather than a reciprocal rescue-like signature.

literature_claim: TNRC6/GW182 scaffolds AGO-miRNA repression, so loss of an active effector can de-repress target mRNAs.

literature_claim: No prior biological claim was used; these were phenotype-first neighbors.

literature_claim: Mammalian TNRC6A, TNRC6B and TNRC6C are miRISC scaffolds and the strongest TNRC6/AGO RNA-seq convergence in cell lines appears after combined paralog impairment.

literature_claim: GW182/TNRC6 recruits CCR4-NOT and can connect miRISC to GIGYF/4EHP-mediated translational repression and to downstream mRNA decay.

literature_claim: Tom40 is the essential beta-barrel pore of the TOM complex through which most nuclear-encoded mitochondrial precursor proteins enter mitochondria.
main_caveats: Indels and TOMM40 protein were not measured, single-nucleus RNA sees only surviving nuclei, and the mean mRNA decrement expected from this platform is small.
summary: Tomm40 loss-of-function produced a pan-neuronal FDR-null surface: 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 23 measured cell groups, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut where the Tomm40 transcript itself fell with logFC -0.923 and FDR 5.46e-07.
why_it_matters: The result argues that survivor nuclei in this acute P16-to-P37/44 CRISPR assay do not mount a steady-state transcriptional response to partial Tomm40 perturbation; it should be read as buffering or survivor selection around an import pore, not as evidence that TOMM40 biology is absent from neurons.

literature_claim: Mitochondrial import impairment is expected to create precursor-overaccumulation stress, cytosolic proteostasis demand, and ATF4-associated mitochondrial stress transcription.
main_caveats: The gene sets were marker-based rather than a formal enrichment test, and some mitochondrial quality-control events, such as PINK1 stabilization, can be predominantly post-translational.
summary: Canonical import-failure transcriptional programs were absent: Tomm40 perturbation produced no FDR<0.10 ISR/ATF, UPRmt-chaperone/protease, proteasome, or TOM-subunit compensation genes.
why_it_matters: A clogged or collapsed TOM pore should overaccumulate mitochondrial precursors and can engage ATF4, chaperone/protease, and ubiquitin-proteasome defenses; the absence of these genes rules out an ongoing import-stress state among recovered Tomm40-edited neuronal nuclei.

literature_claim: OPA1 is a mitochondrial inner-membrane fusion and cristae regulator, so it is a broader mitochondrial-maintenance comparator rather than a TOM-complex member expected to phenocopy Tomm40.
main_caveats: The all-feature signature was dominated by a null target, canonical TOM and TIM import subunits other than Tomm40 were not present as perturbation targets, and Opa1 is a pathway-adjacent, not same-complex, comparator.
summary: Tomm40 had no meaningful whole-surface signature neighbor: the best positive score cosine was only +0.0303 and the strongest non-safe negative was Mecp2 at -0.0142; the broader mitochondrial comparator Opa1 had 241 FDR<0.10 downstream genes where Tomm40 had none.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation structure therefore supports a near-zero Tomm40 signature rather than convergence with a hidden mitochondrial module; Opa1 shows that the same Wilcoxon universe can report a mitochondrial-maintenance perturbation in neuronal nuclei.

literature_claim: Reported TOMM40 poly-T associations involve a noncoding intronic length polymorphism adjacent to APOE, with LOAD associations varying by phenotype, age, and APOE genotype context.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks aged animals, human APOE haplotypes, glia-rich sampling, and explicit TOMM40 regulatory alleles.
summary: The juvenile neuronal coding-loss perturbation did not phenocopy the human TOMM40/APOE regulatory disease axis.
why_it_matters: TOMM40 is genetically discussed in late-onset Alzheimer disease through intronic poly-T haplotypes tied to APOE and to age-dependent phenotypes; a flat acute coding LoF in young mouse NeuN+ nuclei warns against interpreting this screen as evidence for, or against, APOE-linked human TOMM40 alleles.

literature_claim: TPI1 is a homodimeric glycolytic DHAP/G3P isomerase whose deficiency affects red cells and high-energy neural and muscle tissues rather than a single postmitotic thalamic group.
main_caveats: Only two downstream genes passed FDR<0.10 and both were in one group; no DNA indel or enzyme assay is available.
summary: Tpi1 produced a single downstream RNA response in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, where Ogt and Slc25a27 were both down-regulated; all other groups had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: A glycolytic enzyme that should affect ubiquitous cytosolic flux did not make a pan-neuronal transcriptional signature after P16 CRISPR injury. The dataset nominates a narrow thalamic/hypothalamic O-GlcNAc/mitochondrial-coupling axis instead of a broad glycolytic stress program.

literature_claim: GFPT/GFAT controls entry of glycolytic fructose-6-phosphate into de novo hexosamine biosynthesis, and OGT writes O-GlcNAc modifications from the HBP product UDP-GlcNAc.
main_caveats: The convergence is one transcript, Ogt; Gfpt1 and Psmb4 signatures are much larger and therefore not Tpi1 phenocopies.
summary: Ogt was the one Tpi1 downstream gene that converged with other perturbations: Gfpt1 and Psmb4 also down-regulated Ogt in the same 145 MH-LH TH Glut group.
why_it_matters: This turns the Ogt hit from an isolated two-gene observation into a recurrent thalamic/hypothalamic nutrient/proteostasis marker, while also showing that Tpi1 did not recruit the large ISR/UPR program induced by Gfpt1 or the large proteotoxic program induced by Psmb4.

literature_claim: TPI deficiency can elevate DHAP and methylglyoxal and has been linked to oxidative/nitrosative stress; reducing mouse TPI catalytic activity to about 13% alters glycolytic metabolites but is still insufficient to induce disease when protein stability is preserved.
main_caveats: Only selected sentinel genes were tested explicitly in the absence row; metabolite-level DHAP or methylglyoxal changes would be invisible to snRNA-seq.
summary: Tpi1 did not activate the expected glycolytic-compensation, glyoxalase, ISR/UPR, or proteasome-bounce-back transcripts in the effect group or in two high-powered self-depleted groups.
why_it_matters: Severe TPI deficiency would be expected to build DHAP/methylglyoxal and oxidative stress, and the same 145 readout detected Ddit3/Asns/Hspa5/Herpud1/Hyou1 when Gfpt1 was perturbed. Their absence after Tpi1 therefore argues for buffered subthreshold TPI stress rather than an RNA assay unable to see stress.

literature_claim: Tpi1, Hk1, Gpi1, Pfkm, and Eno1 are glycolysis nodes, whereas GFPT1 diverts fructose-6-phosphate into HBP and OGT acts downstream using UDP-GlcNAc to modify proteins.
main_caveats: Only four glycolytic comparators were represented; several lower-glycolysis enzymes and glyoxalase enzymes were not perturbation targets.
summary: The represented glycolytic comparators Hk1, Gpi1, Pfkm, and Eno1 were also mostly transcriptionally flat and did not phenocopy Tpi1 in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, whereas Gfpt1 and Ogt were far broader responders.
why_it_matters: The Tpi1 null surface is not simply because neuronal nuclei cannot respond: the HBP/O-GlcNAc branch and proteasome perturbation can generate hundreds of DE genes with fewer cells, while central glycolytic enzymes form a buffered module in this assay.

literature_claim: TPI deficiency is a recessive multisystem glycolytic disease, but a mouse allele with roughly 13% pan-tissue residual TPI activity developed normally when the TPI dimer was stable.
main_caveats: The screen did not measure protein stability, TPI activity, DHAP, methylglyoxal, or cell loss, so the threshold/stability explanation is inferential.
summary: The sparse P16 neuronal Tpi1 LoF signature is consistent with TPI disease requiring a deeper activity/stability threshold or structurally unstable missense proteins, not uniform mild catalytic reduction alone.
why_it_matters: It warns against reading the neuronal CRISPR null as absence of TPI biology: common patient and mouse disease alleles destabilize dimers or degrade protein in a tissue-skewed way, whereas a sparse indel can simply reduce allele dose without producing a toxic unstable TPI species.

literature_claim: UCP4 is a neuronal inner-mitochondrial uncoupling protein that reduces ROS production and mitochondrial calcium accumulation and can protect neurons during oxidative or mitochondrial stress.
main_caveats: This is a single-gene FDR<0.10 signal, and the screen did not assay mitochondrial membrane potential, ROS, or calcium handling.
summary: Slc25a27/Ucp4 down-regulation is an exploratory mitochondrial-coupling marker of the 145 MH-LH TH Glut Tpi1 response.
why_it_matters: UCP4 can lower neuronal mitochondrial ROS and calcium load; its loss together with Ogt suggests that the only Tpi1 transcriptomic effect may reduce two protective metabolic-stress buffers in this thalamic/hypothalamic group.

main_caveats: Profile correlations are dominated by a very sparse Tpi1 signature and should be interpreted as a rejection of strong convergence, not as precise pathway distances.
summary: Whole-transcriptome Tpi1 signature neighbors were essentially uncorrelated: even the highest absolute Pearson correlations were between -0.016 and 0.031 after self-gene removal.
why_it_matters: The unbiased comparison rejected an unanticipated large shared module; Psmb4 was the only high positive neighbor with a shared significant gene, and that shared gene was just Ogt in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.

literature_claim: Severe thiamine deficiency impairs thiamine-dependent oxidative metabolism and can trigger oxidative stress, ER stress, and autophagy in brain.
main_caveats: The mRNA DE table does not report DNA indels, TPP concentrations, enzymatic flux, or loss of fully edited cells.
summary: Tpk1 loss of function was transcriptomically buffered across every recovered postnatal neuronal group: no group had even one downstream gene at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: TPK1 sits at the entry point to active thiamine diphosphate production, so the assay did test a metabolism gene whose severe deficiency should be capable of producing neuronal stress; the result says that P16 sparse neuronal perturbation did not drive that stress state by P37-44.

literature_claim: TPP produced by TPK1 is a required cofactor for mitochondrial dehydrogenase systems including pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and excludes unrepresented relatives such as Tkt, Slc19a2, Slc19a3, Slc25a19, Pdhb, Bckdha, and Dbt.
summary: Tpk1 did not converge with the measured PDH, OGDH, or BCKDH-axis perturbations, which themselves were almost flat in the Tpk1-matched neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The null is pathway-level rather than an isolated Tpk1 anomaly: weakening enzymes that use thiamine pyrophosphate also failed to produce a broad mitochondrial-stress transcriptome in this acute neuronal assay.

main_caveats: The query used full Wilcoxon-score profiles from a target with no FDR genes, so very small cosines should be interpreted as a rejection set, not mechanistic similarity.
summary: An unbiased all-target signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Tpk1 neighbor; the strongest whole-profile score cosines were only +0.0365 and -0.0197.
why_it_matters: There is no hidden weak module resembling Msi1, Sele, Six3, Dmd, Copg1, or Fbxo11; each candidate was rejected because FDR-level overlap with Tpk1 was zero.

literature_claim: Biallelic TPK1 variants reduce active TPP and cause episodic encephalopathy/Leigh-like syndromes that may respond to thiamine supplementation.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks TPP measurements and does not model febrile illness, chronic germline deficiency, or systemic thiamine transport.
summary: The flat postnatal Tpk1 CRISPR signature is not evidence that neuronal TPK1 suppression is safe or that thiamine rescue is irrelevant.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic TPK1 deficiency is a TPP-lowering Leigh-like disorder in which high-dose thiamine can improve neurologic features; this screen instead delivered mosaic, acute, ungenotyped CRISPR guides to already specified juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: TPM1 and other tropomyosins stabilize and specify actin-filament populations, with TPM1 best known for muscle thin-filament regulation and for cytoskeletal isoforms in non-muscle cells.
main_caveats: The conclusion is transcriptomic; protein depletion, actin-filament architecture, spines, receptor trafficking and electrophysiology were not measured.
summary: Acute postmitotic Tpm1 loss was a near-pan-neuronal transcriptional null: 22 of 23 measured cell groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and the Tpm1 self-transcript was FDR=1.000 in every cell group.
why_it_matters: This sharply limits the interpretation of Tpm1 in this assay to absent broad delayed nuclear RNA remodeling; weak self-transcript reduction is expected for CRISPR indels and is not a failed-KO readout.

main_caveats: Only 21 perturbed dopaminergic nuclei were recovered, the FDR was just below 0.10, and no second FDR-level gene anchors a pathway.
summary: 215 MB Dopa was the only Tpm1 responder, and its response consisted of a single down-regulated gene, Nfxl1.
why_it_matters: The singleton nominates Nfxl1 as a possible dopaminergic marker of Tpm1 perturbation while making clear that the dataset does not support a broader dopaminergic actin or stress program.

literature_claim: Tropomyosin isoforms form distinct actin-filament populations, Tpm4.2 is a major mature postsynaptic tropomyosin, and Tpm3 perturbation can change hippocampal-neuron morphology.
main_caveats: Tpm4 and Tpm2 could not be tested as perturbation targets; convergence was measured at the transcript level, not by actin imaging or neuronal morphology.
summary: The measured actin/tropomyosin comparators did not converge with Tpm1: Tpm3 had no downstream FDR-level genes, Actg1 and Actn4 had near-zero flattened correlations with Tpm1, and Tpm1 did not induce FDR-level Tpm2, Tpm4, Actg1 or Actn4 compensation.
why_it_matters: A lack of paralog and actin-core convergence argues against a hidden generic actin-damage transcriptome and is consistent with isoform- and compartment-specific tropomyosin biology that may be buffered in single-gene snRNA-seq.

main_caveats: Correlation over a nearly null signature is useful for ruling out a strong neighbor but not for inferring anti-correlated biology.
summary: Tpm1 had no meaningful whole-universe signature neighbor: the top positive and negative Wilcoxon-score correlations across other targets were all |r|<=0.026.
why_it_matters: The result rejects the idea that the weak Tpm1 surface is a member of a recurrent Perturb-seq target module; the Dopa Nfxl1 hit is isolated rather than a shared data-driven signature.

literature_claim: Tpm3.1/Tpm3 perturbation alters hippocampal-neuron neurite complexity, growth-cone actin, postsynaptic actin localization, and AIS structure/function.
main_caveats: Tpm3's own transcript was not present in the DE feature universe, and protein-level actin architecture was not assayed.
summary: Tpm3 loss produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq signature in any of the 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: This separates a true absence of nuclear transcriptional response from an untested morphological phenotype: the screen saw no FDR<0.10 stress, synaptic-shutdown, or cytoskeletal gene program after P16 Tpm3 perturbation.

literature_claim: Neurons express compartmentalized tropomyosin isoforms from Tpm1, Tpm3, and Tpm4, with mature postsynapses enriched for Tpm4.2.
main_caveats: Tpm4 was measured only as an endogenous transcript after Tpm3 perturbation; it was not itself a perturbation target in the parquet.
summary: Tpm3 perturbation did not induce Tpm1, Tpm2, or Tpm4 mRNA compensation, and the measurable paralog Tpm1 was also flat in the same cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result rejects a simple nuclear paralog-rebound model for the Tpm3 null; any buffering by other tropomyosins in mature neurons would have to be pre-existing, isoform-local, or post-transcriptional.

main_caveats: Comparator ranks used full Wilcoxon-score vectors; with zero Tpm3 FDR hits, shared-direction overlap is necessarily zero.
summary: The top whole-surface positive and negative signature neighbors of Tpm3 were rejected because all Pearson correlations were near zero.
why_it_matters: A null target can spuriously select nearest neighbors from noise; direct measurement showed that Ndufa10, Tmem63b, Chuk, and Fshr did not expose a hidden gene module shared with Tpm3.

main_caveats: Cell groups are coarse and two taxonomy groups were not recovered for Tpr.
summary: Tpr produced a strongly selective response: 12 of 21 measured groups had FDR<0.10 downstream genes, with 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut accounting for 5371 of 6852 total downstream significant calls.
why_it_matters: The response is not a uniform core-nuclear-pore phenotype; the same sparse P16 CRISPR perturbation generated thousands of genes in some neuronal classes and no robust genes in others.

literature_claim: TPR is a nuclear-basket nucleoporin required for NXF1- and TREX-2-linked mRNA export.
main_caveats: The nuclear RNA assay does not directly measure cytosolic export flux.
summary: Tpr perturbation recurrently altered nuclear transport and NXF1-adjacent export genes, with Ranbp6 and Xpo1 up and Nxf1 down across multiple cell groups.
why_it_matters: This is the most direct recovery of TPR nuclear-basket biology in the neuronal snRNA-seq surface.

literature_claim: TPR and TREX-2 couple nuclear-pore function to NXF1-dependent RNA export and interact with RNA-processing machinery.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot decide whether each down-regulated transcript is a direct export cargo or a secondary transcriptional consequence.
summary: RNA-processing factors were repeatedly down-regulated after Tpr perturbation, including Rnpc3, Srsf5, Srrm2, Ddx17, Cstf2, Pabpn1, and Nxf1.
why_it_matters: The sign-coherent RNA-processing arm argues that the Tpr signature propagates from nuclear export into mRNP maturation and 3-prime-end control rather than changing only transport receptors.

literature_claim: The ubiquitin-proteasome system and UFMylation are proteostasis systems but are not canonical TPR-complex members.
main_caveats: Cross-perturbation similarity is transcriptomic and does not measure protein degradation, UFM1 conjugation, or proteasome activity.
summary: Proteasome and UFMylation perturbations were the top positive cross-target neighbors of Tpr, led by Psmb4, Psmc1, Uba5, and Ufc1.
why_it_matters: This unexpected convergence nominates proteostasis cost as a major downstream state of losing a nuclear-basket export factor in neurons.

literature_claim: Tpr depletion can induce autophagy, and in ependymoma TPR supports an HSF1-MTORC1 state that suppresses autophagy.
main_caveats: Autophagy flux was not measured and many lysosomal markers were not significant.
summary: Tpr-responsive thalamic and midbrain neurons mounted ATF4/ER-stress and ubiquitin-system compensation, while the canonical MTOR-lysosome arm was narrow.
why_it_matters: The stress response explains secondary genes outside the nuclear-pore pathway and refines prior autophagy literature toward an ATF4-biased neuronal response.

literature_claim: TPR loss causes pronounced and unique gene-expression responses downstream of the nuclear basket.
main_caveats: The named transcription factors are markers of the response; their directness downstream of Tpr is unmeasured.
summary: Zinc-finger, Mediator, and chromatin-remodeling genes rose recurrently after Tpr perturbation.
why_it_matters: The chromatin/transcriptional arm broadens the Tpr phenotype beyond export receptors and is consistent with nuclear-basket control of gene expression.

literature_claim: TPR protects proliferating human cells from RNA-mediated replication stress and DNA damage.
main_caveats: Replication-fork stress itself is not present in postmitotic neuronal nuclei; the finding is an RNA/DNA-stress echo.
summary: DNA-repair and genome-maintenance transcripts, including Lig4, Rev1, Smc6, Wapl, Mdm2, and Trp53, were induced in the Tpr response.
why_it_matters: This preserves a genome-stress component of the neuronal signature while separating it from literal S-phase replication stress, which the P16 postmitotic design cannot assay.

literature_claim: Biallelic pathogenic TPR variants cause severe intellectual disability in humans.
main_caveats: The assay models mosaic postnatal loss rather than recessive germline human disease.
summary: Large Tpr signatures included recurrent down-regulation of neuronal effector transcripts such as Agrn, Gria2, Stxbp1, Ptprs, Cyp46a1, Slc22a17, and Unc80.
why_it_matters: The data connect a severe human TPR neurodevelopmental gene to postmitotic neuronal-maintenance mRNAs downstream of nuclear-export stress.

literature_claim: TREX-2/mRNA export and MTOR-autophagy literature nominate Thoc1-like export factors and Mtor as candidate comparators for Tpr.
main_caveats: Nup153, Nup50, GANP, and Nxf1 were not perturbation targets, so the nuclear-basket comparator set was incomplete.
summary: Thoc1 partially phenocopied Tpr, but Ranbp2 and Mtor did not: Ranbp2 shared only 66 FDR-supported Tpr-coordinate genes and Mtor only 3.
why_it_matters: Direct comparator testing rejects two simple stories: Tpr was not reproduced by the assayed nucleoporin relative and its stress output was not reproduced by direct Mtor perturbation.

literature_claim: TPR supports Mad1/Mad2 spindle-assembly-checkpoint robustness in dividing cells.
main_caveats: A postmitotic Perturb-seq assay is not designed to score mitotic checkpoint failure.
summary: The Mad1/Mad2 spindle-checkpoint program expected from TPR in mitotic cells was absent from all postmitotic neuronal Tpr signatures.
why_it_matters: This expected negative prevents misreading the absence of Mad genes as failed perturbation; the relevant mitotic biology lies outside the juvenile neuronal timing of the screen.

literature_claim: Prior work places TRAF3 in TNFR/TLR signaling and in injury-coupled neuronal death, but those effects are generally receptor-, immune-lineage-, or pathology-gated rather than tonic in resting postmitotic neurons.
main_caveats: Trafficked indels were not assayed at DNA level, on-target mRNA shifts are expected to be weak in this platform, and ligand or injury challenges were not applied.
summary: P16 Traf3 CRISPR produced a pan-neuronal FDR null: all 23 measured neuronal groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, and the Traf3 self-transcript was nonsignificant in every group.
why_it_matters: This sharply restricts Traf3 biology in the unchallenged juvenile-to-young-adult NeuN+ brain: it is not a tonic driver of basal neuronal NF-κB, interferon, or stress transcription after cortical and subcortical neurons are specified.

literature_claim: TRAF3 positively links TLR pathways to type-I interferon and, in injured neurons, can lie upstream of TAK1-dependent MAPK/NF-κB apoptotic signaling; loss or degradation of TRAF3 can also release NIK-dependent noncanonical NF-κB signaling.
main_caveats: The gene lists are sentinel transcripts, not a formal enrichment test; lack of a ligand or brain-injury stimulus limits inference about challenged neurons.
summary: No interferon-stimulated, immediate NF-κB/MAPK, oxidative-stress, or apoptosis transcripts were recovered after Traf3 perturbation; the inspected expected genes were present in the DE table but had FDR=1 across all 23 groups.
why_it_matters: TRAF3 can alter exactly these secondary transcriptional programs when TLR3/TNFR/TAK1 pathways are engaged, so their absence argues against readout failure and instead supports a gated pathway that is off in the basal P16-to-P37/44 neuronal assay.

why_it_matters: The null is not hiding inside a broader recurrent perturbation module: the target behaves like a near-zero signature rather than like a member of a coherent brain-cell response cluster.

literature_claim: TRAK1 is a Milton-family mitochondrial motor adaptor whose disruption impairs mitochondrial movement and can cause severe epilepsy or encephalopathy.
main_caveats: DNA indels and TRAK1 protein depletion were not measured; the conclusion is about nuclear RNA rather than mitochondrial localization or motility.
summary: Trak1 loss-of-function was transcriptionally buffered across the juvenile postmitotic neuron panel: only Nop56 in Sst GABA and Synj1 in midbrain glutamatergic neurons reached FDR<0.10, and no ISR, UPR, autophagy, mitophagy, or mitochondrial-transport feedback panel was induced.
why_it_matters: The canonical TRAK1 phenotype is mitochondrial positioning, so this screen shows that the local transport lesion usually does not become a cell-wide nuclear stress program within 3-4 weeks of sparse P16 CRISPR perturbation.

literature_claim: NOP56 is a box C/D snoRNP component involved in ribosome biogenesis.
main_caveats: Single DEG in 57 perturbed nuclei; no second snoRNP or ribosome-biogenesis gene reached FDR<0.10.
summary: Sst GABA was the only forebrain inhibitory class with a robust Trak1 downstream hit, an isolated Nop56 increase.
why_it_matters: Nop56 nominates nucleolar box C/D snoRNP or ribosome-biogenesis tone as the most sensitive nuclear RNA marker in this otherwise flat inhibitory response, but the one-gene signature argues against a broad ribosome-biogenesis program.

literature_claim: SYNJ1 encodes a neuronal phosphoinositide phosphatase with a prominent role in synaptic-vesicle recycling and membrane trafficking.
main_caveats: The response is one gene at FDR 0.0647; Ogt, Opa1, and data-driven neighbors did not reproduce it.
summary: Midbrain glutamatergic neurons showed a single robust Trak1 effect, up-regulation of Synj1.
why_it_matters: SYNJ1 biology links the hit to phosphoinositide-dependent synaptic-vesicle recycling, making it a plausible but isolated readout of membrane/endocytic compensation after mitochondrial-trafficking stress.

literature_claim: Miro/TRAK adaptors link mitochondria to kinesin and dynein motors, and TRAK1/TRAK2 both support transport in young neurons.
main_caveats: The closest paralog and some dynamics genes, including Trak2, Rhot2, Mfn1, Mfn2, and Dnm1l, were not target perturbations in the dataset.
summary: Represented Miro/kinesin arm genes did not phenocopy Trak1: Rhot1, Kif5a, Kif5c, and Klc2 were fully transcriptionally flat, and Klc1 altered only two genes in unrelated classes.
why_it_matters: The result separates the physical mitochondrial motor-adaptor complex from a shared nuclear RNA signature; loss of different parts of the transport apparatus can be locally functional without producing a common snRNA-seq phenotype.

literature_claim: OGT modifies Milton/TRAK to regulate mitochondrial motility, whereas OPA1 controls mitochondrial fusion and cristae quality control.
main_caveats: Ogt is pleiotropic and Opa1 is an inner-membrane GTPase rather than a TRAK-complex member; divergence is informative for detectability, not epistasis.
summary: Ogt and Opa1 produced broad transcriptional responses where Trak1 was nearly flat.
why_it_matters: This rejects a generic claim that the screen cannot detect postnatal mitochondrial or O-GlcNAc biology: nuclear signatures appeared after Ogt or Opa1 perturbation in many of the same neuron classes, but the local TRAK1 transport lesion largely stayed below that nuclear-response threshold.

main_caveats: Signature-neighbor computation used noisy genome-wide Wilcoxon scores from a two-DEG target; it is useful as a rejection of strong convergence, not as a mechanistic ranking.
summary: The unbiased score-neighbor search found no robust Trak1-like global module; the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations were near zero and included safe-target-like null signatures.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-reading the two isolated DEGs as part of a reproducible transcriptome-wide state shared with another perturbation.

literature_claim: JUND is an AP-1-family transcription factor that can regulate oxidative-stress and cell-survival genes.
main_caveats: This is a one-gene signature at FDR=0.0795; Fos, Junb, Egr1/Egr2, UPR, autophagy, and NF-kB markers did not pass FDR.
summary: Trappc10 perturbation produced a single FDR-supported downstream call: Jund was up in 155 MB Glut and no other gene in any measured group reached FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The only nuclear readout of an otherwise buffered TRAPP II perturbation is a low-confidence, possible AP-1/JUND stress-adaptive pulse in midbrain glutamatergic neurons, not a broad trafficking, UPR, autophagy, or immediate-early module.

literature_claim: TRAPPC9 and TRAPPC10 are TRAPP II-specific subunits, and TRAPPC6B preferentially supports TRAPP II such that loss-of-function alleles destabilize TRAPPC9/TRAPPC10 protein and perturb Golgi trafficking.
main_caveats: Shared protein-complex failure was inferred from mRNA signatures only; TRAPP protein abundance, Golgi morphology, and vesicle flux were not measured.
summary: The measured TRAPP relatives do not converge transcriptionally: Trappc6b had a different one-gene response in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, whereas Trappc9 was flat.
why_it_matters: TRAPPC9, TRAPPC10, and TRAPPC6B are physically linked through TRAPP II, so the absence of shared FDR genes shows that partial, mosaic postmitotic neuronal CRISPR does not recreate the stable TRAPP II-loss state seen in patient fibroblasts or germline models.

literature_claim: TRAPP complexes are vesicle-tether/Rab-GEF assemblies linked to secretion and autophagy, and TRAPPC10 knockout cells show impaired membrane trafficking and TRAPPC9 protein loss.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot assay secretory-cargo flux, Golgi morphology, Rab activation, autophagic flux, or TRAPPC9 protein destabilization directly.
summary: Trappc10 perturbation did not activate a coordinated UPR/ISR, autophagy-lysosome, NF-kB, Rab1/Rab11, or TRAPP-subunit transcript program.
why_it_matters: A large secondary nuclear stress program would have been visible if Golgi trafficking failure had propagated to these transcriptional axes; their absence argues that the dominant residual phenotype, if present after P16 neuronal editing, is buffered or subcellular rather than a sustained stress-state conversion.

main_caveats: The neighbor search uses genome-wide Wilcoxon z-scores, so correlations around zero are expected to be dominated by residual noise and cell-group composition.
summary: Trappc10 has no meaningful transcriptomic neighbor in the full perturbation universe; the strongest positive and negative z-score correlations were only r=0.0257 and r=-0.0196.
why_it_matters: This keeps the null-heavy surface from being over-clustered with unrelated perturbations: even the data-driven nearest neighbors explain essentially none of the Trappc10 whole-transcriptome profile.

literature_claim: TRAPPC6B mutations can disrupt ER-to-Golgi/Golgi morphology, and NSDHL is a cholesterol-biosynthesis enzyme that traffics through Golgi to ER membranes and lipid droplets.
main_caveats: Single-gene result at FDR 0.0698; no other tested sterol genes reached FDR<0.10.
summary: The lone robust Trappc6b downstream hit was Nsdhl up-regulation in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
why_it_matters: Nsdhl links the only positive Trappc6b signal to an ER/Golgi-adjacent cholesterol and lipid-droplet enzyme, offering a concrete follow-up marker while making clear that the response is not a broad sterol regulon.

literature_claim: TRAPP dysfunction can perturb ER-to-Golgi trafficking, Golgi morphology, and autophagy-linked membrane traffic.
main_caveats: The test rules out a large steady-state nuclear RNA stress program, not Golgi fragmentation, Rab activity defects, or trafficking kinetics.
summary: Trappc6b perturbation did not trigger a detectable UPR, ISR, lysosomal, or autophagy transcriptional program in any recovered neuronal group.
why_it_matters: Because an ER/Golgi trafficking block could have created a secondary RNA stress state that snRNA-seq would detect, the total absence of these markers argues that surviving postnatal neurons buffered the perturbation rather than mounting a chronic stress transcriptome.

literature_claim: TRAPPC9 and TRAPPC10 are TRAPP II-specific components and TRAPPC6B loss preferentially compromises TRAPP II biology.

why_it_matters: This turns a single-target null into a pathway-level contrast: the TRPA1/TRPV1/TRPM3 sensory module that is linked in peripheral nociception is effectively off-axis in this P16 NeuN+ brain readout.
