literature_claim: Twist2-family proteins regulate Runx2/osteoblast timing, MyoD/MEF2 myogenic transcription, NF-kappaB-dependent cytokine feedback, and Setleis dermal fibroblast programs in mesenchymal or immune lineages.
main_caveats: Absence of these programs in neurons does not falsify their activity in skin, bone, muscle, macrophages, or lymphoid cells.
summary: Canonical Twist2 output genes from dermal fibroblast, osteogenic, and NF-kappaB cytokine biology were completely uncoupled from the postmitotic neuronal Twist2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The expected transcriptional readouts were in the testable gene universe but did not move, arguing that the main Twist2 programs require dermal, mesenchymal, osteogenic, or immune contexts rather than the assayed juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: Twist proteins use E-protein dimer partners and regulate Runx2, MyoD, and MEF2-family differentiation circuits in mesenchymal developmental systems.
main_caveats: Residual correlations are useful only as comparator nominations because Twist2 itself has no FDR-significant genes; Mef2c is an indirect lineage comparator rather than a direct Twist2 partner.
summary: Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor Twist2 literature relatives phenocopied Twist2: residual screen-wide correlations were all tiny, Tcf3/Tcf12/Runx2 were flat, and Mef2c—not Twist2—was the related transcription factor with a clear neuronal response.
why_it_matters: The comparison rejects an artifactual interpretation in which all weak bHLH perturbations collapse into one common signature, and it shows that this assay could detect a transcription-factor perturbation in the same neuronal classes when the TF is active there.

literature_claim: TXNDC15/TMX5 is an ER/Golgi PDI-family protein; SREBP2 controls cholesterol-synthesis/import transcription, but a Txndc15-to-SREBP2 response in juvenile neurons was not established.
main_caveats: The 022 and 191 responses are small; all evidence is mRNA rather than sterol biochemistry or protein stability.
summary: Txndc15 loss up-regulated a compact sterol/SREBP-like program only in 3/22 recovered cell groups, with the main six-gene response in 155 MB Glut and partial echoes in 191 MB P MY GABA and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The biological positive result is a cell-type-restricted ER/sterol transcript program rather than a broad ciliary or UPR signature, and the strong 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut self-depletion with zero downstream genes makes that restriction real rather than a simple engagement artifact.

literature_claim: TXNDC15 loss is expected to impair ciliary transition-zone/Hh biology in ciliated model systems, and ER proteostasis failure can activate ATF6/XBP1/PERK-dependent UPR transcripts.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot score ciliary ultrastructure, Smoothened trafficking, or Xbp1 splicing; it only rejects a robust secondary Hh/UPR abundance program.
summary: Txndc15 perturbation did not recover a canonical ciliary Hedgehog, ciliogenesis, or unfolded-protein-response mRNA program in any recovered cell group.
why_it_matters: TXNDC15 is a ciliary-transition-zone and ER thioredoxin-like protein, so the measured SREBP2/sterol response is pathway-specific rather than an undifferentiated cilia or ER-stress transcriptome.

literature_claim: SREBP2 activates cholesterol synthesis/import genes and March6 loss increases SREBP-regulated cholesterol transcripts.
main_caveats: The Marchf6 convergence is confined to 155 MB Glut in this feature set; no protein degradation or cholesterol flux was measured.
summary: Srebf2 flipped the Txndc15 sterol feature set while Marchf6 converged on the same 155 MB Glut genes; Srebf1 and Hmgcr did not phenocopy.
why_it_matters: Directly measuring related perturbations in the same parquet ties the Txndc15 module to SREBP2-like sterol transcription and an ER MARCHF6-like control point instead of to generic cholesterol-pathway injury.

literature_claim: TXNDC15 and core IFT/Hedgehog genes are linked by primary-cilium control of Smoothened/Gli signaling and congenital ciliopathy biology.
main_caveats: Ciliary comparators could share morphology or trafficking phenotypes that are invisible to nuclear RNA-seq.
summary: Ciliary and Hedgehog pathway targets represented in the screen had 0/9 FDR-level overlaps with the Txndc15 downstream feature set.
why_it_matters: The expected ciliary relatives were testable and failed to explain the observed sterol signature, preventing a default annotation of the Txndc15 response as a generic ciliopathy signature.

main_caveats: The neighbor metric used only the nine Txndc15 downstream feature instances; Pi4kb was a raw-logFC inverse neighbor but was not retained at FDR<0.10.
summary: A restricted data-first search placed Htt, Dctn1, and Mib1 as the strongest positive Txndc15 sterol neighbors and Uba5 and Phf12 as FDR-supported inverse neighbors.
why_it_matters: The sterol cassette recurs across unrelated perturbations in caudal neurons, arguing that it is a reusable homeostatic state rather than a single-gene statistical accident.

literature_claim: U2AF2 encodes a core U2AF spliceosome subunit involved in 3′ splice-site recognition and 3′-end processing.
main_caveats: The readout is total gene abundance rather than isoform usage, so absence of DE does not prove absence of splicing defects.
summary: U2af2 loss-of-function produced a broad whole-gene response mainly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with intermediate Pvalb and hypothalamic responses and many flat cortical/hippocampal groups.
why_it_matters: A core spliceosome factor might have been expected to perturb all neuronal classes, but the gene-level secondary response was anatomically and cell-state restricted in this P16 postmitotic screen.

literature_claim: Splicing factors often sit in autoregulatory and cross-regulatory AS-NMD networks, including conserved SR-factor poison-exon circuits.
main_caveats: snRNA gene counts do not identify the splice isoforms responsible for these abundance changes.
summary: Rsrp1 was the dominant recurrent U2af2 downstream marker, always down when significant; the same signature repeatedly decreased Srrm2, Luc7l2, Srsf5, Tial1, Atp11b, and Wsb1 and increased Map7d1, Nxf1, Xpot, and Cmtr1.
why_it_matters: These genes provide a compact gene-abundance proxy for U2AF2 spliceosome stress in this assay, whereas U2af2 self-mRNA was usually flat.

literature_claim: Impaired proteasome function activates compensatory proteasome recovery and can engage autophagy/aggrephagy programs through NFE2L1-dependent stress signaling.
main_caveats: U2af2 did not induce a clean all-proteasome-subunit NFE2L1 bounce-back; the proteasome link is inferred from cross-perturbation convergence and selected quality-control genes.
summary: Broad U2af2 responders induced ubiquitin/ERAD/chaperone and vacuolar-trafficking genes, including Zfp598, Dnaja2, Dnajb5, Herpud1, Ubr4, Nprl2, Atp6v0b, Atp6v1h, Copb1, Vps35l, and Rab12.
why_it_matters: The signature expands U2af2 biology from splice-site recognition to a secondary proteostasis and membrane-quality-control state likely buffering misprocessed RNA/protein output.

literature_claim: Alternative splicing regulators control neuronal maturation, cortical development, and mature synaptic components.
main_caveats: The measured signal is decreased whole-gene abundance, not direct proof of altered isoforms of these synaptic genes.
summary: The largest U2af2 signatures down-regulated mature neuronal and synaptic effector transcripts, notably Grin1, Gls, Slc17a6, Agrn, Cyp46a1, Vamp1, Stxbp1, Syt2, Kcnc1, and Kcnc2.
why_it_matters: The broad spliceosome-stress state is not limited to RNA-processing genes; it erodes neurotransmission and synaptic-maintenance programs in the same responder neurons.

literature_claim: U2AF2 belongs to spliceosome/3′-splice-site biology; proteasome inhibition is separately known to activate proteostasis recovery programs.
main_caveats: The cross-perturbation metric was computed on U2af2 FDR pairs, so it measures convergence on the U2af2 response rather than all genes in the comparator signatures.
summary: Unbiased signature search placed Psmc1, Psmb4, Prpf6, Cdc40, and Tpr as the top positive U2af2 neighbors.
why_it_matters: The spliceosome neighbors validate the target biology, while the even stronger Psmc1/Psmb4 convergence nominates proteostasis stress as a major secondary response after U2af2 perturbation.

literature_claim: HNRNPC competes directly with U2AF65 at cryptic 3′ splice sites, and UPF3B is a core NMD factor expected to report AS-NMD coupling.
main_caveats: Comparator engagement at indel or protein level is not measured here; no U2af1, Puf60, Sf1, Sf3b1, or Prpf19 comparator was available.
summary: Most matched RNA-processing comparators failed to converge with U2af2: Hnrnpc was slightly anti-correlated, Upf3b and Snrpb were effectively flat, Hnrnpa2b1 and Hnrnph2 had tiny signatures, and Ddx39b overlapped only 14 U2af2 pairs.
why_it_matters: U2af2 does not simply phenocopy perturbation of any RNA-binding, hnRNP, or NMD component at the gene-abundance level; same pathway membership was not sufficient for convergence.

literature_claim: U2AF2 missense variants dysregulate splicing and reduce neuritogenesis, and Drosophila U2af50 knockdown produces developmental MB phenotypes with Rbfox1 among rescue-relevant splicing substrates.
main_caveats: The disease variants are mainly missense or in-frame alleles, whereas this assay is mosaic CRISPR loss-of-function after P16.
summary: P16 U2af2 loss did not reproduce a Rbfox1 total-mRNA response but did depress Nova1, Srrm4, and synaptic-effector transcripts in selected mature neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Human and fly U2AF2 disease models point to early neuritogenesis and splicing-substrate defects; this assay shows which mature neuronal abundance programs remain vulnerable after cell specification.

literature_claim: U2AF2 functions at the protein level in spliceosome assembly and RNA processing.
main_caveats: The actual DNA indel rate and U2AF2 protein abundance were not observed.
summary: Large downstream signatures occurred even though U2af2 self-mRNA was only modestly reduced and often FDR-flat.
why_it_matters: The target transcript should not be used as the sole engagement biomarker in this CRISPR-indel screen; functional lesions can be compatible with preserved or even compensated RNA abundance.

literature_claim: UBA5 is the single E1 of a broadly required UFMylation cascade, and full systemic Uba5 loss is embryonic lethal whereas human hypomorphic UBA5 variants cause early neurologic disease.
main_caveats: The assay measures 3 to 4 week transcriptional consequences of sparse postmitotic editing, not embryonic development or neuronal abundance.
summary: Uba5 perturbation was not pan-neuronal: the high-amplitude response localized to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, with only tiny tails in 066, 054, and 110.
why_it_matters: This converts a canonical housekeeping UFMylation enzyme into a postnatal neuronal vulnerability map: the same P16 mosaic CRISPR perturbation produced thousands of DE genes in selected thalamic/midbrain-linked classes while most cortical, hippocampal, striatal and cerebellar classes were flat.

literature_claim: A genetic UBA5-deficiency model reported widespread mitochondrial abnormalities.
main_caveats: These are nuclear mitochondrial transcripts in snRNA-seq; mitochondrial morphology, respiration and protein UFMylation were not assayed.
summary: Uba5 responders mounted a uniformly upward nuclear-encoded mitochondrial OXPHOS/import program.
why_it_matters: The largest branch of the Uba5 signature is not a simple UFM1-target transcript change; it points to secondary energetic or mitochondrial-proteostasis compensation in the neuron classes that cross the Uba5-loss threshold.

literature_claim: UFMylation supports ER proteostasis and RPL26-dependent ribosome-associated quality control.
main_caveats: The transcriptome shows compensation markers, not autophagic flux or UFM1 conjugate abundance.
summary: Uba5 loss induced an autophagy/ubiquitin-like proteostasis rebound anchored by Sqstm1 and COP9/NEDD8/ubiquitin genes.
why_it_matters: UFMylation is itself a ubiquitin-like ER quality-control cascade, so the recurrent induction of Sqstm1, Ubc, Uba3, Cops genes, Otub1 and Nedd8 is a plausible compensatory attempt to buffer stalled-ribosome and ER proteostasis stress.

literature_claim: UFMylation modifies the ER ribosome QC substrate RPL26/uL24, whereas Elongator controls tRNA wobble-uridine modifications that tune translation elongation.
main_caveats: mRNA increases do not prove increased translation rates; the Elp1 convergence is an indirect comparator, not a same-complex phenocopy.
summary: Translation initiation and elongation RNAs rose alongside the proteostasis response.
why_it_matters: Because UFMylation acts on ER-associated ribosome quality control, induction of Eef and Eif factors suggests a homeostatic protein-synthesis reset rather than a pure reduction in ribosomal output.

literature_claim: TNPO3 imports SR splicing factors, TPR participates in nuclear mRNA export, and Elongator affects translation through tRNA modifications; none is a canonical UFMylation-cascade enzyme.
main_caveats: This is a cross-perturbation transcriptomic relationship; direct RNA export, splicing and tRNA-modification assays were not performed.
summary: SR-splicing and nuclear RNA-processing genes were a recurrent downward arm of the Uba5 signature.
why_it_matters: This nominates RNA maturation and nuclear-cytoplasmic RNA handling as a secondary point of failure after Uba5 loss, a conclusion strengthened by convergence with Tpr and Tnpo3 perturbations rather than by UFMylation literature alone.

literature_claim: MARCH6/MARCHF6 controls degradation of cholesterol-synthesis enzymes including squalene monooxygenase and HMGCR.
main_caveats: The sterol interpretation is transcript-level; sterol metabolites and MARCHF6 substrates were not quantified.
summary: Uba5 down-regulated a sterol/reticulon/v-ATPase lysosomal arm while other stress modules went up.
why_it_matters: The directionally opposed ER module distinguishes the Uba5 state from a generic UPR, in which many ER and lysosome genes would be expected to rise rather than Atp6v0c, Srebf2, Insig1, Hmgcr and Rtn3 falling together.

literature_claim: Human UBA5, UFM1 and UFC1 variants cause severe early neurodevelopmental encephalopathies with seizures and microcephaly.
main_caveats: The assay does not measure firing, synapse number, seizures or morphology.
summary: The broad responders coupled organelle stress to synaptic and neurite transcript remodeling.
why_it_matters: UBA5 disorders manifest as seizures and motor/brain-development phenotypes, and the perturb-seq signature shows how a core ER-ribosome defect can reach neuronal excitability and synaptic-vesicle genes such as Syt11, Sv2a, Grm7, Kcnc2 and Grin2b.

literature_claim: Loss of UFMylation is associated with ER stress and ER-ribosome quality-control defects that can activate UPR pathways.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq does not read PERK, IRE1, ATF6, eIF2alpha phosphorylation or Xbp1 splicing directly; the mismatch is limited to steady-state nuclear target RNAs.
summary: The stress arm was Ddit3/redox-biased and did not recover a full canonical ER-UPR transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: UFMylation literature would predict ER stress after loss of the cascade; this screen did detect a stress program, so the missing Hspa5/Xbp1/Atf3/Dnajb9 induction is informative rather than a readout failure and indicates partial ISR-like remodeling in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: UFC1 acts immediately downstream of UBA5 as the sole UFM1 E2 enzyme, and UFC1 mutations cause a UFMylation brain-development disorder.
main_caveats: Ufc1 was narrower than Uba5, with no robust Ufc1 response in the 145 and 217 Uba5 responder classes.
summary: Ufc1, the sole UFM1 E2, was the strongest same-direction Uba5 neighbor.
why_it_matters: This direct E1-E2 phenocopy confirms that the large thalamic and midbrain Uba5 response is genuinely UFMylation-cascade-like rather than an idiosyncratic Uba5-only stress state.

literature_claim: UFSP2 removes UFM1 from substrates and therefore sits on the opposite, deconjugating side of the UFMylation cycle from UBA5.
main_caveats: Ufsp2 had only 20 total downstream DE genes across the Uba5 responder groups, so this is a restricted-signature result.
summary: Ufsp2 loss did not invert Uba5 loss; the represented UFM1 deconjugase showed only a weak same-direction overlap.
why_it_matters: Opposite signs might be expected for reducing an E1 versus reducing a de-UFMylase, so the measured same-sign 17-gene overlap warns that acute UFSP2 loss is not a simple UFMylation gain-of-function in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: TPR, TNPO3 and ELP1 participate in nuclear RNA export, SR-protein import and tRNA wobble-uridine modification, respectively.
main_caveats: Convergence was computed from DE vectors; it does not prove physical interaction with UBA5.
summary: The strongest data-driven non-UFMylation positive neighbors were Tpr, Tnpo3 and Elp1, linking Uba5 to RNA export/splicing and tRNA-modification stress.
why_it_matters: These neighbors were not chosen from a UFMylation textbook pathway; their measured convergence shows that Uba5 loss lands in a broader RNA/translation proteostasis attractor in the same neuronal classes.

literature_claim: MARCH6/MARCHF6 is an ER E3 ligase regulating cholesterol-synthesis enzyme stability and pathway flux.
main_caveats: The Mib1 and Wac links are data-driven only; Marchf6 provides the sterol-specific literature anchor.
summary: Marchf6 and Mib1 were data-driven negative neighbors because they up-regulated the sterol genes that Uba5 suppressed.
why_it_matters: The inversion triangulates the SREBF2/INSIG1/cholesterol arm as a specific Uba5 output rather than random members of a broad 151/155 signature.

literature_claim: UBE2E2 is an active UBE2E-family ubiquitin/ISG15 E2 that can pair with RING E3 ligases, so an unbuffered single loss could in principle perturb ubiquitin-dependent cell programs.
main_caveats: Functional indels were not measured; several cell groups have fewer than 40 perturbed nuclei; the result is transcriptional rather than ubiquitinomic.
summary: Acute Ube2e2 perturbation was flat across all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups, with 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and a non-significant Ube2e2 self-transcript in every group.
why_it_matters: This is a strong negative transcriptional result in the exact P16-to-P37/44 postmitotic neuronal assay: single Ube2e2 loss did not create a detectable maintenance, proteotoxic-stress, or stress-response state.

literature_claim: UBE2E2 belongs to the ubiquitin-conjugation machinery, but proteasome subunits, ubiquitin-like activation, E3 ligases, and segregases occupy different positions and need not transcriptionally phenocopy a single E2.
main_caveats: The represented comparators are pathway-neighbor rather than same-family UBE2E enzymes; direct Ube2e1 and Ube2e3 perturbations were absent.
summary: Ube2e2 did not phenocopy represented ubiquitin/proteostasis neighbors: Psmb4, Psmc1, Uba5, and Huwe1 were broad responders, but their correlations to Ube2e2 were r=-0.00035 to 0.0179.
why_it_matters: The assay could detect large postmitotic neuronal responses to proteostasis perturbation when present, so the Ube2e2 null is target-selective rather than a general blind spot for ubiquitin-proteasome biology.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Ube2e1, Ube2e2, and Ube2e3 are closely related class-III UBE2E enzymes with overlapping RING E3 partner activity.
main_caveats: Basal paralog protein abundance and enzyme activity were not measured, and Ube2e1/Ube2e3 were not themselves perturbation targets.
summary: Ube2e2 perturbation did not transcriptionally induce the measured UBE2E paralogs Ube2e1 or Ube2e3 in any measured neuronal group.
why_it_matters: The clean null is compatible with UBE2E-family redundancy, but the RNA data rule out a simple paralog-upregulation bounce-back model.

009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Human type-2-diabetes genetics and a mouse β-cell model implicate UBE2E2 up-regulation/overexpression, Nedd4-associated ubiquitin-chain remodeling, and p21 in pancreatic β-cell mass regulation.
main_caveats: The experiment sampled NeuN+ brain nuclei, not pancreas; the perturbation was CRISPR LoF, not β-cell overexpression.
summary: The neuronal Ube2e2 LoF null separates this target's β-cell gain-of-function diabetes axis from a postmitotic neuronal p21/Nedd4, UPR/ISR, heat-shock, or ISG transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic or disease interpretation should not assume that suppressing UBE2E2 in neurons will reproduce the pancreatic β-cell consequences of increased UBE2E2 expression.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on whole Wilcoxon-score vectors; when the index vector is nearly null, tiny correlations can rank highly without biological meaning.
summary: Genome-wide score-vector comparison found no meaningful Ube2e2 signature neighbor: the largest positive Pearson r was 0.026 and the largest negative r was -0.0157.
why_it_matters: The target sits at the origin of the perturbation landscape in this assay; neither data-driven convergence nor anti-convergence nominates a robust pathway outside the flat direct DE surface.

literature_claim: Maternal UBE3A loss is strongly neurodevelopmental, but delayed postnatal loss produces reduced Angelman-like phenotypes relative to congenital loss.
main_caveats: DNA indels and UBE3A protein were not measured; all cell groups were sampled with only 25-84 perturbed nuclei; the result is a negative basal snRNA result rather than a claim that UBE3A protein function is absent.
summary: Ube3a produced a broad weak/null basal snRNA-seq surface: 18 recovered neuronal groups, 713 total perturbed nuclei, measurable Ube3a transcript, but 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every group.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset finding is not a synaptic or proteostasis pathway but the absence of any robust nuclear mRNA program after P16 sparse Ube3a loss-of-function targeting.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: UBE3A regulates Arc protein, AMPA receptor trafficking, dendritic spines, GABAergic seizure circuitry, nuclear functions, and autophagy-associated pathways in chronic models.
main_caveats: The dataset did not quantify Arc or AMPAR protein, surface receptors, dendritic spines, electrophysiology, seizures, or protein autophagy flux.
summary: The established Arc/AMPAR and synaptic substrate axis was absent at FDR<0.10 on the RNA readout: Arc, Gria1, Gria2, Gria3, Dlg4, Cbln1, Gabrb3, Hdac1, and Hdac2 were all FDR 1.0 across Ube3a-measured groups.
why_it_matters: It separates UBE3A's disease-relevant proteolytic, receptor-trafficking, spine, and EEG physiology from an acute cell-autonomous basal mRNA signature.

literature_claim: HERC2 physically binds E6AP/UBE3A and stimulates UBE3A ubiquitin-ligase activity, making HERC2 the biochemical comparator expected to be closest among measured HECT relatives.
main_caveats: The comparison uses downstream snRNA DE only; HERC2 may regulate UBE3A biochemically without producing a shared transcriptional loss-of-function phenotype.
summary: A matched HECT-family comparison showed strong divergence: Huwe1 produced 342 downstream DE genes in Ube3a-matched groups, whereas the UBE3A regulator Herc2 produced only 2 and Hecw2, Hectd4, and Herc1 were flat or nearly flat.
why_it_matters: The observed Ube3a null cannot be generalized to all HECT E3 perturbations; Huwe1 is readily able to generate a neuronal transcriptomic response under the same screen design.

literature_claim: UBE3A, GABRB3, and SNRPN occupy the Angelman/Prader-Willi/Dup15q biological neighborhood, and UBE3A phenotypes intersect with GABAergic and synaptic circuitry.
main_caveats: Disease-locus or circuit relatedness does not require a shared cell-autonomous transcriptomic signature; several comparators had only sparse DE in the matched groups.
summary: Measured Angelman/Dup15q and synaptic disease comparators did not expose a hidden Ube3a-like RNA module: Gabrb3 had 0 matched downstream genes, Snrpn 2, Gria2 1, Fmr1 1, Camk2a 4, Mtor 6, and Mecp2 33, with no shared-direction overlap with Ube3a because Ube3a itself had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes.
why_it_matters: It keeps pathway priors from being mistaken for measured convergence; UBE3A's acute P16 snRNA null stood apart from both 15q-imprinted-locus and synaptic signaling comparators.

main_caveats: Restricted-signature comparison only: the 1800 queried Ube3a features were selected by nominal p value, and none was FDR-significant in the Ube3a perturbation.
summary: The unbiased signature-neighbor analysis failed to identify a robust convergent or anti-convergent module: top positive and negative cosines computed on nominal Ube3a top features were only 0.1168 and -0.0857.
why_it_matters: Because the target has no FDR-level signature, any mechanistic story derived from sub-threshold Ube3a ranks would be dominated by noise; the neighbor search independently supports treating the surface as weak.

literature_claim: UBP1/LBP-1a is a CP2/Grainyhead DNA-binding transcription-factor family member; Ubp1 null biology is strong in early extraembryonic angiogenesis and CP2-family function can be redundant.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein loss were not measured, and this is a 3-4 week mosaic neuronal assay rather than a germline or double-family knockout.
summary: P16 Ubp1 loss-of-function produced no robust downstream transcriptional response in any recovered neuronal group.
why_it_matters: A DNA-binding regulator with severe extraembryonic germline-null biology is effectively buffered at the single-gene, postmitotic-neuron, snRNA-seq level; the result argues against a broad acute neuron-autonomous UBP1 program rather than against guide activity itself.

literature_claim: TFCP2, TFCP2L1, and UBP1 belong to one CP2/Grainyhead subfamily, bind related DNA motifs, dimerize, and can be functionally redundant.
main_caveats: Tfcp2l1, Grhl1, and Grhl3 were absent as perturbation targets; the comparison cannot test double knockouts or the missing family members.
summary: The literature-obvious CP2/Grainyhead comparators Tfcp2 and Grhl2 did not reveal a shared postmitotic-neuronal module with Ubp1.
why_it_matters: The expected related factors were directly queryable: Tfcp2 was completely flat and Grhl2 yielded only one weak Pvalb hit, so the Ubp1 null is part of a measured single-factor CP2-family silence in this neuronal design rather than a missed obvious paralog phenocopy.

main_caveats: Correlations are computed across measured group×gene Wilcoxon-score vectors and intentionally summarize only the model-visible perturbation universe.
summary: An unbiased all-target signature search found no meaningful Ubp1 convergence or anti-convergence.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative neighbors were correlations near zero; Wdr26, the strongest negative neighbor, was a broad responder with zero shared FDR genes because Ubp1 had no downstream FDR genes. Thus no noncanonical data-driven module should be assigned to Ubp1 from this screen.

literature_claim: UBP1-family literature links UBP1 to placental steroidogenic Cyp11A1 regulation and a blood-pressure locus, and links TFCP2-family activity to renal and brain gene-regulatory contexts.
main_caveats: Most expected genes come from peripheral tissues or a TFCP2-family rather than Ubp1-specific brain literature; absence in neurons is therefore a context test, not a failed recovery of a matched positive control.
summary: Known UBP1/TFCP2-family target programs were absent from the postnatal neuronal Ubp1 surface.
why_it_matters: The screen failed to recover steroidogenic/placental, renal/blood-pressure, or TFCP2 brain-adjacent genes such as Cyp11a1, Aqp2, Jag1, Grhl1, Asic2, Gsk3b, and Creb1, consistent with those programs being lineage- or family-context dependent rather than primary outputs of acute Ubp1 loss in NeuN+ neurons.

literature_claim: UBR1 is an N-end-rule E3 ligase whose human deficiency causes Johanson-Blizzard syndrome, and combined Ubr1/Ubr2 loss in mice perturbs embryonic neurogenesis and cardiovascular development.
main_caveats: Only RNA from surviving NeuN+ nuclei was assayed; DNA indels, UBR1 protein, and N-degron substrate abundance were not measured.
summary: Acute Ubr1 loss produced no FDR-level downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 19 neuronal groups in which it was recovered.
why_it_matters: UBR1 is a disease-linked N-degron E3 ligase, but the P16-to-P37/44 mosaic loss-of-function setting did not reveal a broad postmitotic neuronal RNA program; the Johanson-Blizzard and Ubr1/Ubr2 developmental literature should therefore not be read as predicting a large autonomous juvenile-neuron snRNA signature from Ubr1 alone.

literature_claim: UBR1/UBR2-class ligases participate in misfolded-protein and ER-stress quality control, while NFE2L1 drives transcriptional proteasome recovery after proteasome inhibition.
main_caveats: Psmc1 and Psmb4 are core proteasome subunits, not UBR1-family N-recognins; the contrast tests detectability of proteostasis transcription rather than exact pathway epistasis.
summary: Ubr1 was uncoupled from bulk proteasome-stress transcription: canonical ISR/UPR, heat-shock, p62/autophagy and immediate-early markers did not pass FDR, whereas core proteasome perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 produced thousands of DE genes in the same matched cell groups.
why_it_matters: The screen would have detected a large proteotoxic-stress or NFE2L1-like bounce-back state if Ubr1 loss had disabled total proteasome capacity; the observed zero therefore distinguishes substrate-specific N-recognin loss from core 26S proteasome impairment.

literature_claim: Mammals encode several UBR-box N-recognins, and UBR1 and UBR2 have overlapping N-degron recognition with substantially stronger developmental phenotypes when both are removed.
main_caveats: Redundancy is inferred from the literature and the null signature; Ubr2 or double perturbations were not available for direct matched comparison.
summary: The Ubr1 null is consistent with UBR-family buffering, but the directly redundant N-recognins were not perturbation targets in this parquet.
why_it_matters: The most obvious phenocopy test would be Ubr2 or compound Ubr1/Ubr2 loss; because Ubr2, Ubr4, Ubr5, Ubr7 and the upstream Arg/N-degron enzymes Ate1, Ntan1 and Ntaq1 were absent as targets, this screen mainly tests single Ubr1 and cannot exclude combinatorial N-degron dependence.

main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to Wilcoxon-score correlations in a flat Ubr1 signature; it is useful as a negative module call, not as proof of mechanistic relatedness to Gabrb1 or Wdr26.
summary: The data-driven Ubr1 nearest-neighbor search did not nominate a robust biological module: the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations were only +0.038 and -0.033.
why_it_matters: Ubr1 clusters with null-like Safe_target controls and Gabrb1 rather than with an FDR-level responder; the top anti-neighbor Wdr26 is a real responder in several matched groups, but its anticorrelation is too small to define an opposite Ubr1 program.

literature_claim: CTIF directs CBP80/CBP20-dependent pioneer-round translation initiation.
main_caveats: The effect is a single q=0.084 gene; it is not enough to call a broad NMD or translation program.
summary: Uchl1 loss produced a single FDR<0.10 downstream change, Ctif down-regulation, only in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: The only robust responder points to a narrow RNA-surveillance/translation-initiation node rather than a multi-gene ubiquitin, UPR, autophagy, or synaptic program.

literature_claim: UCHL1 loss reduces neuronal monoubiquitin, and proteasome impairment can induce NFE2L1-mediated PSM transcription with linked heat-shock, UPR, and autophagy responses.
main_caveats: The screen measured RNA in neuronal nuclei, not free ubiquitin, ubiquitinated substrates, proteasome activity, or axon-terminal morphology.
summary: Uchl1 did not activate the proteasome-bounce-back, UPR/ISR, or autophagy-lysosome transcriptional programs that are detectable in the same screen after stronger proteostasis lesions.
why_it_matters: UCHL1 stabilizes monoubiquitin in neurons, so severe loss should eventually challenge ubiquitin-dependent proteostasis; the data show that acute postnatal Uchl1 disruption did not cross the transcriptional stress threshold reached by Psmb4 or Hspa5 perturbation.

literature_claim: BAP1 is a large UCH-family deubiquitinase, whereas UCHL1 is a small ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase specialized for small ubiquitin adducts.
main_caveats: Uchl3, Uchl5, and Usp14, the closest UCHL1/proteasomal DUB comparators, were not perturbation targets in the parquet.
summary: Measured deubiquitinase and proteostasis relatives did not phenocopy Uchl1; Bap1 and Usp48 responded in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut while Uchl1 was flat there.
why_it_matters: The result argues that Uchl1 is not producing a generic DUB-loss transcriptome and that UCH-family membership is a poor predictor of postnatal neuronal snRNA output in this assay.

main_caveats: The neighbor search used the top 50 nominally ranked Uchl1 genes per group because the FDR-level Uchl1 signature contains only Ctif; low cosine values should not be overinterpreted mechanistically.
summary: The pre-literature, restricted-signature search found no strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor for Uchl1.
why_it_matters: Uchl1's only FDR<0.10 gene was unique in its matched cell group, and even the top all-target cosine neighbors were weak, so the response is best interpreted as buffered rather than as a member of a larger convergent module.

literature_claim: Human UCHL1 loss and UCHL1 dysregulation are linked to progressive neurodegeneration and Parkinson biology, and full Uchl1 loss in mice produces progressive presynaptic axon-terminal degeneration.
main_caveats: 215 MB Dopa was missing for Uchl1; the screen also excluded spinal cord, peripheral nerves, old ages, and protein aggregate phenotypes.
summary: The acute Uchl1 brain signature did not resemble Snca or Park7 perturbation and did not induce amyloid, tau, synuclein, or synaptic-stress marker transcription in the measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: This separates acute Uchl1 loss in juvenile postmitotic brain nuclei from chronic UCHL1-linked Parkinson, Alzheimer, spinal, and peripheral neurodegeneration, which likely need stronger alleles, longer aging, specific vulnerable neurons, or axon-terminal phenotyping.

literature_claim: Human UFC1 hypomorphic variants impair UFMylation and cause severe early-onset encephalopathy with microcephaly, implying neural vulnerability but not the exact postnatal cell classes affected.
main_caveats: 215 MB Dopa was not recovered; 052 and 066 have only three and two downstream genes.
summary: Ufc1 loss produced a real response in only five of 22 measured neuronal groups, dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The phenotype is not a generic neuronal stress response: the same P16-to-P37/44 perturbation was nearly silent in many cortical, hippocampal, striatal, and cerebellar classes.

literature_claim: UBA5 activates UFM1 and transfers it to the E2 enzyme UFC1 in the UFMylation cascade.
main_caveats: Transcriptome-only comparison; UFM1 conjugation and DNA indels were not assayed.
summary: The same-sign Uba5-Ufc1 overlap ties the Ufc1 signature to UFMylation loss.
why_it_matters: Uba5 was the top unbiased positive neighbor and the only assayed core E1/E2 comparator that robustly recapitulated Ufc1 despite modest Ufc1 mRNA decreases.

literature_claim: UBA5 and UFC1 operate in the same minimal UFM1 conjugation cascade; identical response breadth across neuron types is not established.
main_caveats: Ufc1 in 145 and 217 had especially few perturbed cells.
summary: Uba5 was broader than Ufc1 across midbrain, hypothalamic, and pineal groups.
why_it_matters: Same-cascade perturbations were not interchangeable: Uba5 responses where Ufc1 was flat indicate UFMylation-sensitive groups in which the Ufc1 perturbation stayed below a response threshold.

literature_claim: UFMylation protects ER ribosome quality control and ER homeostasis, so failure of the pathway is expected to communicate with ER-stress signaling.
main_caveats: Atf4 was only nominal in 151 and Hspa5/Xbp1 were not FDR hits.
summary: Ufc1 induced a Ddit3/CHOP-centered stress branch but not a full BiP/Xbp1 ER-UPR.
why_it_matters: The result recovers expected ER-proteostasis distress downstream of UFMylation loss while refining it to a CHOP/translation-stress nuclear signature visible by snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: UFMylation intersects with ER-localized ribosome/protein quality control centered on UFM1 modification of RPL26/uL24.
main_caveats: mRNA compensation was measured, not UFM1 conjugates, proteasome activity, or autophagic flux.
summary: Proteasome, chaperone, and autophagy/lysosome genes rose after Ufc1 loss.
why_it_matters: The Ubc/Pomp/heat-shock/Map1lc3/Sqstm1 program is the clearest secondary compensation to impaired UFMylation-dependent ER protein quality control.

main_caveats: Direct splice-isoform consequences were not assayed.
summary: RNA-processing and splicing transcripts formed a recurring down-regulated arm of the Ufc1 signature.
why_it_matters: Srsf11, Rsrp1, Srsf5, Pnisr, Ddx17, Clk1, and Tcea2 show that the response was not only proteostatic and explain why RNA-processing perturbations were data-driven neighbors.

literature_claim: Biallelic human UFM1/UFC1 mutations impair UFMylation and produce severe early-onset encephalopathy with microcephaly.
main_caveats: The disease is developmental and systemic, whereas this screen is acute and mosaic and did not assay electrophysiology.
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut coupled stress induction to down-regulation of synaptic and excitability genes.
why_it_matters: A developmental-epileptic-encephalopathy gene drove postmitotic suppression of NMDA/AMPA/GABA receptor, vesicle, and ion-channel mRNAs after fate specification.

literature_claim: UFMylation is best characterized as an ER-oriented UFM1 conjugation system with links to proteostasis.
main_caveats: The gene set supports mitochondrial compensation, not a direct mitochondrial UFMylation substrate.
summary: Mitochondrial import, respiratory-chain, and CLPP genes were induced as a secondary Ufc1 branch.
why_it_matters: Tomm, Cox/Nduf, Hspd1, and Clpp genes show that the UFMylation-loss state extended from canonical ER translation biology to mitochondrial quality-control transcripts.

literature_claim: UFM1 is the modifier transferred through UBA5 and UFC1, and UFSP-family proteases process/remove UFM1.
main_caveats: Induced Ufsp2 mRNA does not prove increased de-UFMylase activity.
summary: The strongest Ufc1 responder up-regulated Ufm1 and Ufsp2 transcripts.
why_it_matters: A lesion at the E2 step caused rebound of the modifier and UFM1-specific protease, consistent with pathway-level homeostatic sensing.

main_caveats: snRNA-seq cannot distinguish cell-intrinsic UFMylation stress from altered recent activity state.
summary: Immediate-early and MAPK-feedback genes rose only in the large 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response.
why_it_matters: Egr1, Fos, Junb/Jund, Nr4a genes, Npas4, and Dusp4 add an activity-state or stress-transcription layer to the Ufc1 phenotype.

literature_claim: UFSP2 is the measured UFM1-specific protease comparator; its loss might have been expected to oppose an E2 loss if deconjugation dominated.
main_caveats: Negative-neighbor search was restricted to Ufc1-significant coordinates; Ufsp2 evidence is sparse.
summary: The screen did not contain a robust anti-Ufc1 signature.
why_it_matters: The best opposite-sign neighbors were small and mixed, so the Ufc1 response lacks a clean transcriptomic antagonist interpretable as rescue.

literature_claim: Human UFSP2 and UFMylation genes are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, which motivates neuronal effects but does not specify an acute P16 transcriptional signature.
main_caveats: Only 20 significant gene-by-cell effects were present; engagement was not measured by indel sequencing.
summary: Ufsp2 had a sparse, subcortically restricted response: only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut had downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset result is selectivity and buffering, not a broad failure of UFMylation across the brain.

literature_claim: UBA5 is the UFM1 E1 enzyme, UFC1 is the E2 enzyme, and UFSP2 is a UFM1 deconjugating protease in the same post-translational pathway.
main_caveats: Convergence is calculated from a small Ufsp2 significant signature; Uba5/Ufc1 perturbations have larger n_pert and may have different editing efficiencies.
summary: Uba5 and Ufc1 were the dominant positive signature neighbors of Ufsp2 and recapitulated its 151/155 responder genes in the same direction.
why_it_matters: The data-driven neighbors independently recover the UFMylation cascade, strengthening the interpretation that even the weak Ufsp2 signature is on-pathway.

literature_claim: The UFMylation cascade controls ER-ribosome UFMylation and is linked to ER protein-homeostasis stress programs.
main_caveats: Cross-target breadth could be affected by differences in guide activity and perturbed-cell number.
summary: Ufsp2 converged with but did not phenocopy Uba5/Ufc1: conjugating-enzyme loss induced hundreds to thousands of genes and a stress program whereas Ufsp2 changed only 4 and 16 genes in the matched responders.
why_it_matters: This separates loss of UFM1 conjugation from loss of deUFMylation and shows that UFSP2 is not simply the inverse-rate-limiting version of UBA5 or UFC1 in basal postnatal neurons.

literature_claim: UFMylation is best established at ER-bound ribosomes and ER protein homeostasis rather than as a primary mitochondrial transcription pathway.
main_caveats: Supported by only five FDR<0.10 genes over two cell groups and should be treated as a biomarker hypothesis.
summary: The significant Ufsp2 responder genes included a mitochondrial arm: Pink1 increased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and Cox5a, Ndufa2, Timm8b, and Timm13 increased in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The largest non-canonical clue in the sparse Ufsp2 surface is a possible mitochondrial import/respiratory compensation downstream of a proteostasis perturbation.

literature_claim: The UFMylation literature predicts ER-ribosome and proteostasis effects; neuronal membrane and actin genes are not the canonical first-order readout.
main_caveats: The module is small and functionally heterogeneous.
summary: Ufsp2 responders showed a small neuronal membrane/cytoskeletal module with Tmsb4x and Cfl1 up and Sema6b, C1qtnf4, Atp6v0c, Syt11, and Tspan3 down.
why_it_matters: These genes are practical candidate readouts for the weak deUFMylase response in neurons even though they do not prove a direct UFSP2 substrate relationship.

literature_claim: UFSP2 or UFM1 perturbation can alter UPR signaling in neurons or UFMylated targets in patient fibroblasts, but the UFSP2 p.V115E fibroblasts did not show basal GRP78/spliced-XBP1 activation.
main_caveats: Only transcript levels were assayed; UFMylated protein accumulation was not measured.
summary: Ufsp2 did not induce a canonical UPR/ISR/autophagy transcriptome, even in the two responder classes, despite Uba5 and Ufc1 showing that such genes were detectable in this dataset.
why_it_matters: The negative result prevents over-reading Ufsp2 as a simple ER-stress inducer in basal postnatal neurons and aligns with a model in which deUFMylation defects can remain protein-level unless a stress threshold is crossed.

literature_claim: Germline or embryonic Ulk4 loss perturbs corticogenesis, neural progenitors, neuritogenesis, cell motility, and corpus-callosum formation.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured; 215 MB Dopa was missing for Ulk4; a one-gene response is not evidence that every edited cell lacked protein-level ULK4 activity.
summary: P16 Ulk4 loss produced an almost completely buffered postmitotic neuronal transcriptome: one downstream FDR<0.10 gene in 22 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result refines the strong Ulk4 developmental literature by showing that, once neurons have been specified and sparsely edited in juvenile brain, acute loss does not launch a broad cell-state, stress, autophagy, Hedgehog, or GABAergic-identity program detectable by whole-transcriptome snRNA-seq.

literature_claim: INTS10 is part of the Integrator complex, which regulates small-nuclear-RNA processing and RNA polymerase II pause-release/attenuation.
main_caveats: Supported by one FDR-significant gene in 66 perturbed cells; no broader Integrator program was detected.
summary: Ints10 was the sole Ulk4 downstream hit and was down-regulated only in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: This nominates an Integrator/RNA-processing transcript as a narrow candidate marker of Ulk4 perturbation in central MGE-derived GABAergic neurons, but the absence of other Integrator subunits or RNA-processing genes keeps the claim at single-gene biomarker level.

main_caveats: The data-driven neighbor calculation is restricted to Ulk4's one robust feature; it should be treated as a contrast, not a mechanistic Psmb4-Ulk4 link.
summary: The only data-driven same-feature neighbor of Ulk4 was Psmb4, yet Psmb4 and Psmc1 produced broad proteasome-loss signatures while Ulk4 did not.
why_it_matters: The shared Ints10 decrease is not sufficient to classify Ulk4 as a proteasome-stress perturbation: Psmb4 moved 1142 genes in the same CNU-MGE group and thousands elsewhere, whereas Ulk4 stopped at Ints10.

009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ULK4 can act with STK36 at cilia to promote GLI2 phosphorylation and Hedgehog activation.
main_caveats: Stk36 itself was measured only as a downstream transcript, not as a perturbation target; mature NeuN-positive neurons may have too little active Hh signaling for this cascade to be engaged.
summary: The Stk36/Hedgehog expectation was not recovered: Ulk4 did not move Gli1/Gli2/Ptch/Smo/Stk36 readouts, and Gli1, Gli2, Smo, Ptch1, and Ptch2 perturbations were flat in the Ulk4 responder group.
why_it_matters: Direct ULK4-Hedgehog biology appears displaced to Hh-active ciliated developmental contexts rather than to the mature neuronal nuclear transcriptome assayed here.

literature_claim: Ulk4 mutant mice show fewer Gad67+ cells in amygdala/hippocampus and reduced Pvalb, Sst, Cck, and Npy expression in P12 cortex.
main_caveats: The screen does not estimate cell abundance or long-range circuit assembly, so it cannot test whether Ulk4 affected production or survival of interneurons earlier in life.
summary: Ulk4 did not acutely erase GABAergic transmitter identity: Gad1, Gad2, Slc6a1, Pvalb, Sst, Cck, and Npy were never significant after Ulk4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The GABAergic deficits and anxiety-like behavior of constitutive Ulk4 mutants are therefore more consistent with a developmental abundance/circuit-assembly defect than with a cell-autonomous P16 loss of mature inhibitory-neuron marker transcription.

literature_claim: ULK4 is a pseudokinase in the Unc-51-like kinase family rather than a proven member of the ULK1 autophagy-initiation complex.
main_caveats: Ulk1, Ulk2, and Ulk3 were absent as perturbation targets, so the comparison could only use Rb1cc1 and Becn1.
summary: Autophagy-neighbor perturbations Rb1cc1 and Becn1 did not recapitulate the CNU-MGE Ulk4 signature.
why_it_matters: Although ULK4 belongs to the broader Unc-51-like kinase family, the sparse neuronal data separate the residual Ulk4 signal from canonical ULK1/FIP200/BECN1 autophagy machinery.

literature_claim: Munc13 loss is expected to impair vesicle priming/release, while DPP6 is an auxiliary component of Kv4 A-type K+ channels that regulate dendritic excitability.
main_caveats: This is a one-gene signature at FDR 0.0968; the compensation is inferred from DPP6/Kv4 physiology and was not electrophysiologically tested.
summary: Unc13a perturbation produced a single robust downstream call: Dpp6 was down in 053 Sst Gaba and no other Sst synaptic, Kv4/A-current, immediate-early, or stress marker reached FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Because DPP6 is a Kv4-channel auxiliary protein that promotes A-type K+ current, its selective down-regulation nominates an Sst-specific excitability compensation rather than a broad presynaptic-remodeling transcriptome.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Munc13 and Munc18 cooperate in primed SNARE-complex assembly, and Stxbp1/Munc18-1 is an essential presynaptic disease gene.
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptomic; it does not show that Unc13a and Stxbp1 have different acute electrophysiological effects.
summary: Unc13a did not phenocopy Stxbp1/Munc18-1 despite both proteins acting in synaptic vesicle priming: Stxbp1 produced 140 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 8 of 22 recovered groups, whereas Unc13a produced one downstream gene in 23 groups.
why_it_matters: The broad Stxbp1 response shows that the screen could detect transcriptional consequences of disrupting core presynaptic machinery; the Unc13a null surface is therefore pathway-specific, not a blanket failure of synaptic genes to score.

literature_claim: Munc13 isoforms can substitute for one another at subsets of hippocampal GABAergic and glutamatergic synapses, whereas combined Munc13-1/2 loss abolishes release.
main_caveats: Unc13b and Unc13c had missing cell groups and low perturbed-cell counts in some recovered groups, including 34 cells for the single Unc13b effect.
summary: The neuronal Munc13 paralogs queried in the screen were not interchangeable with Unc13a at the DE level: Unc13b had only one downstream hit in one of 12 recovered groups, and Unc13c had none in 21 groups.
why_it_matters: The expected paralogs were measured directly and rejected as strong transcriptomic phenocopies, which supports a buffered or off-transcriptome interpretation for single Munc13-family perturbations.

literature_claim: CYP46A1 participates in neuronal cholesterol turnover and brevican is a perisynaptic/perineuronal-net extracellular-matrix proteoglycan.

summary: Represented Hedgehog and NF-kB effectors did not reproduce the Usp48 thalamic response, and expected Hh/NF-kB target panels were absent after Usp48 perturbation.
why_it_matters: This rejects the simplest extrapolation from glioblastoma, retinal pigment epithelium, cytokine, and corticotroph literature to P16 postmitotic NeuN+ neurons.

main_caveats: The contrast is signature-neighbor biology rather than a known physical USP48 relationship.

literature_claim: V-ATPase in synaptic vesicles creates the proton gradient used for neurotransmitter loading.

literature_claim: CACNG7/γ-7 is a type-II transmembrane AMPA-receptor regulatory protein that can modulate AMPAR subunit function.

literature_claim: The presynaptic release apparatus contains synaptobrevin/VAMP proteins plus syntaxin-1/SNAP25, Munc13, Munc18-1/STXBP1, synaptotagmins, complexins, and synaptophysin-family vesicle proteins; VAMP2 is the dominant synaptobrevin in many central synapses.

why_it_matters: This separates target engagement at the RNA level from downstream nuclear remodeling: central postmitotic neurons can tolerate a Vamp1 perturbation without changing the expression of the core fusion genes that would be obvious candidates for transcriptional feedback.

why_it_matters: VCP disease is associated with autophagy-lysosome dysfunction, but this perturbation did not show generalized lysosome expansion; it singled out the glucocerebrosidase transcript in a cortical projection-neuron group.

why_it_matters: The data-driven neighbors were ER-proteostasis, UFMylation, and proteasome perturbations rather than arbitrary transcription factors, placing the small Vcp signal within a measured proteostasis network.

literature_claim: p97/VCP, UFMylation enzymes, and proteasome subunits all support protein-quality-control biology.

literature_claim: VCP/p97 is required for ubiquitin-containing autophagosome maturation and IBMPFD mutations impair that function with p62/LC3 accumulation.
