main_caveats: Comparator counts summarize downstream DE size, not direct shared molecular epistasis; Vps13a had no significant genes with which to compute a positive shared-DE overlap.
summary: Endolysosomal and movement-disorder comparators responded where Vps13a stayed flat.
why_it_matters: Rab7, Vps35, Htt, Mtor, Sqstm1, Lamp2, and Atg5 produced FDR-significant downstream genes in the same model-visible universe, including 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, whereas Vps13a produced none; the Vps13a null is therefore not simply a property of all vesicle/autophagy or neurodegeneration-associated perturbations in this assay.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: VPS13A-D are related membrane-contact lipid transporters, VPS13A and VPS13C occupy ER contact sites, and XK is a direct VPS13A partner.
main_caveats: Vps13d and Xk were not represented as targets, and a double-paralog or Vps13a-plus-Xk perturbation was not tested.
summary: The represented VPS13 paralogs did not phenocopy an acute neuronal transcriptome either.
why_it_matters: Vps13b and Vps13c, the two VPS13-family perturbations present alongside Vps13a, also had zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes in matched groups, while the literal VPS13A partner Xk and paralog Vps13d were absent from the parquet; within the represented family, acute single-paralog loss converged on transcriptional silence rather than a shared stress module.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Neighboring was computed from weak score vectors because Vps13a had no FDR-significant genes; the result is mainly a control against over-interpreting nominal rows.
summary: A whole-surface score search did not place Vps13a in a reproducible transcriptional perturbation module.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive and negative Wilcoxon-score neighbors were nearly zero-correlated, and the re-queried top neighbors had no robust overlap with Vps13a; this argues against forcing a Notch, GRID2/AMPA, or other off-target-looking signature onto a perturbation whose own FDR surface is empty.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: VPS13B loss perturbs Golgi integrity, glycosylation, autophagy, neural progenitor proliferation, synapse genes, and early postnatal brain development in Cohen-syndrome models.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured; the assay samples surviving NeuN+ postmitotic nuclei and not progenitors or direct organelle/glycosylation phenotypes.
summary: Vps13b was a strict whole-transcriptome null in all 20 recovered neuronal groups after P16 acute CRISPR perturbation.
why_it_matters: Despite a strong disease prior for VPS13B, the P16-to-P37/P44 NeuN+ snRNA-seq assay found no robust downstream mRNA response, indicating buffering or displacement of the canonical VPS13B phenotypes rather than a cell-type-restricted transcriptional program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: VPS13B-deficient CS neurons were reported to accumulate autophagic vacuoles, increase autophagic flux, dysregulate autophagosome-organization genes, and upregulate ATG4C.
main_caveats: Comparator evidence comes from other perturbation targets rather than Vps13b itself; autophagic flux and organelle morphology were not assayed directly.
summary: The expected autophagy/lysosome mRNA program was absent after Vps13b perturbation, although lysosomal/autophagy perturbations can score in matched cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result separates acute postmitotic Vps13b loss from the autophagy-upregulated state reported in CS iPSC-neuron models and argues against a robust ATG4C/BECN1/SQSTM1/LAMP2-like transcriptional escape in this screen.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: VPS13 proteins are related bridge-like lipid-transfer proteins but occupy distinct organelle contact sites and cause distinct neurological diseases.
main_caveats: Vps13d was not represented as a perturbation target, and flat mRNA phenotypes do not test paralog lipid-transfer activity directly.
summary: The represented VPS13 paralogs Vps13a and Vps13c were also flat and did not form a shared Vps13b-like signature.
why_it_matters: This rejects a simple family-level transcriptomic module for VPS13 perturbations in juvenile postmitotic neurons and is consistent with paralog-specific organelle localizations for VPS13 proteins.

main_caveats: The neighbor scan used all Wilcoxon scores, most of which are nonsignificant for a null target; it is useful only as a negative check for hidden global similarity.
summary: An unbiased whole-surface signature scan found only near-zero positive and negative neighbors for Vps13b.
why_it_matters: The top correlations were so small that they argue against a coherent hidden subthreshold module; the observed Vps13b surface behaves like an FDR-null profile rather than a weak version of a known perturbation state.

literature_claim: RAB6, FAM177A1, and Sec23IP are experimentally supported VPS13B-associated proteins at the Golgi or the ER-exit-site/Golgi interface.
main_caveats: Negative evidence for Cog and AP-family targets is indirect; absence of direct interactors from the perturbation library prevents true same-complex epistasis or phenocopy testing.
summary: Direct Golgi/ERES VPS13B partners were absent as perturbation targets, and represented indirect Golgi/adaptor targets did not converge with Vps13b.
why_it_matters: The screen cannot directly test the most literal Rab6-, FAM177A1-, or Sec23IP-based VPS13B mechanisms; the queryable Cog and AP-family proxies were not informative phenocopies.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: VPS13C loss-of-function is pathogenic in recessive Parkinsonism and can disrupt mitochondrial and lysosomal physiology.
main_caveats: No DNA indel or protein measurement was available; a flat self-transcript in most groups is expected for sparse CRISPR indels and does not prove absent knockout.
summary: Vps13c loss was a pan-null downstream transcriptomic perturbation across all 22 recovered neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: A significant Vps13c self-transcript decrease in 155 MB Glut still produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes, arguing that this P16-to-P37/44 basal nuclear-RNA assay did not convert partial Vps13c loss into a stable transcriptional state.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: VPS13C loss has been linked to lysosomal lipid defects, PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy, mtDNA-dependent cGAS/STING signaling, and acute lysosomal repair in cellular models.
main_caveats: Marker absence only tests stable nuclear RNA; lipid composition, organelle morphology, and acute lysosome-damage repair were not assayed.
summary: Vps13c did not induce a durable lysosome, autophagy, mitophagy, UPR/ISR, or IFN-STING RNA program in any measured group.
why_it_matters: The markers most directly suggested by VPS13C biology were systematically absent at FDR<0.10, so the null is not hiding an obvious secondary stress program in the snRNA readout.

literature_claim: VPS13C sits on the late endosome/lysosome axis and VPS35 is an endosomal retromer Parkinson gene, so endolysosomal perturbations were the expected neighbors to test.
main_caveats: Rab10 and Lrrk2, the closest phospho-Rab10 partners from dopaminergic-neuron literature, were not represented as targets in this parquet.
summary: Rab7, Vps35, and Vps54 elicited endomembrane transcriptional responses where Vps13c stayed flat.
why_it_matters: The matched-screen contrast rejects a generic explanation that this dataset cannot detect lysosomal trafficking perturbations in postnatal neurons; Vps13c is specifically buffered or off-axis relative to Rab7 and Vps35/Vps54 hits.

literature_claim: Human VPS13 paralogs are bridge-like lipid-transfer proteins with disease links but distinct organelle/contact-site localizations.
main_caveats: Vps13d was not represented as a perturbation target, and Vps13a/Vps13b lacked rows in a few Vps13c-matched groups.
summary: Vps13a and Vps13b did not phenocopy Vps13c or produce their own FDR<0.10 neuronal signatures.
why_it_matters: The expected paralog comparison shows a family-level absence of basal postnatal neuronal RNA responses for the VPS13 lipid-transfer targets represented here rather than a Vps13c-specific hidden module.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation is necessarily restricted to the basal Wilcoxon logFC profiles in this parquet.
summary: The data-driven whole-transcriptome neighbor search found no meaningful Vps13c signature module.
why_it_matters: After removing the screen-wide gene-by-cell-type mean, Vps13c's best positive and negative neighbors had correlations near zero; follow-up should therefore focus on Vps13c mechanism rather than a strong transcriptomic co-module nominated by this screen.

literature_claim: Vps35 loss can disrupt neuronal endosomal cargo trafficking, neurite maturation, lysosomal function, and survival in embryonic or neonatal pyramidal neurons.
main_caveats: The CNU-MGE GABA response is only a single FDR<0.10 downstream gene; the dopaminergic group was not recovered for Vps35.
summary: Vps35 loss produced a sharply restricted transcriptional response: 30 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and one Serac1 hit in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, with no downstream FDR<0.10 genes in the other 20 measured groups.
why_it_matters: The result argues that acute postmitotic retromer disruption is not a pan-neuronal transcriptional stressor in this assay; the interpretable biology is concentrated in one thalamic glutamatergic subclass plus an isolated GABAergic lipid-remodeling signal.

literature_claim: VPS35/retromer has been reported to regulate excitatory neurotransmitter receptor trafficking to synapses.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq measures altered mRNA abundance, not receptor surface trafficking or electrophysiology.
summary: The 151 TH Vps35 program hit receptor, excitability, calcium, and synaptic-neurite genes rather than a bulk lysosomal response.
why_it_matters: Genes such as Atp2a2, Grin2b, Rims3, Plekhg1, L1cam, Kcnc2, Lrrc7, Cttnbp2, Sez6l2, and Septin7 make the robust Vps35 signature look like selective membrane/synaptic remodeling, whereas core autophagy and lysosomal transcripts remained below the FDR gate.

literature_claim: SERAC1 is a phospholipid-remodeling gene linked to mitochondrial function and intracellular cholesterol trafficking.
main_caveats: Single-gene signature in 53 perturbed cells; no other mitochondrial or lysosomal gene passed FDR<0.10 in this group.
summary: Serac1 up-regulation was the only Vps35-dependent transcript in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: SERAC1 connects the isolated GABAergic response to phospholipid, mitochondrial, and cholesterol handling; as a one-gene FDR 0.063 signal it is best treated as a cell-type-specific candidate marker of endomembrane lipid compensation, not as proof of a complete mitochondrial program.

literature_claim: Rab7 cooperates with Rab5 to recruit the VPS26/VPS29/VPS35 retromer subcomplex to endosomes.
main_caveats: The genome-wide Vps35-Rab7 correlation was small because the Vps35 DE surface is sparse; the conclusion relies on the FDR-supported overlap in 151 rather than on a large global correlation.
summary: Rab7, the top whole-surface positive neighbor, partially reproduced the 151 TH Vps35 signature while adding a large adaptive lysosome/proteasome program that Vps35 lacked.
why_it_matters: The overlap ties the Vps35 thalamic genes to late-endosomal trafficking, but the extra Rab7 induction of Lamp2, Sqstm1, Ctsd, Map1lc3b, vacuolar-ATPase, and proteasome transcripts shows that this assay would have detected a generalized endolysosomal stress response had Vps35 produced one.

literature_claim: VPS35L is the VPS35-like subunit of Retriever, a retromer-related but independent recycling complex, and the PD-linked VPS35-D620N mutation perturbs WASH/FAM21 association.
main_caveats: Vps26a, Vps26b, Vps26c, and Vps29 were not perturbation targets, and Vps35l/Washc4 self-transcript depletion was weak in these two groups.
summary: Vps35l/Retriever and Washc4 did not phenocopy Vps35 in the Vps35 responder groups.
why_it_matters: Although Retriever is a retromer-related VPS35L complex and WASH interfaces with both Retriever/CCC and VPS35, the measured Vps35l and Washc4 perturbations produced zero robust same-direction hits across the 31 Vps35 downstream features, arguing that the 151 TH program is a canonical-retromer-branch response rather than a generic WASH-associated recycling response.

literature_claim: Vps35/retromer has been linked to APP/BACE1/Sort1 trafficking, lysosomal-autophagy defects, mitochondrial quality control, late-onset VPS35-related Parkinson disease, and VPS35-D620N-driven LRRK2-Rab signaling.
main_caveats: The assay does not measure APP or BACE1 protein localization, Rab phosphorylation, mitochondrial morphology, or aged dopaminergic survival; the MB Dopa group was missing for Vps35.
summary: The acute Vps35 loss signature did not recover the expected APP/BACE1/Sort1, autophagy-lysosome, mitochondrial MUL1/Mfn2, or LRRK2-Rab10 transcriptional programs.
why_it_matters: APP, Bace1, Sort1, Atg9a, Ctsd, Sqstm1, Mfn2, Mul1, Lrrk2, and Rab10 were flat in the Vps35 responder groups, and App, Sorl1, Snca, Park7, Atp13a2, Dnajc13, and Synj1 knockouts failed to phenocopy the Vps35 31-gene signature; this separates a P16-P44 Vps35 LoF transcriptional phenotype from chronic AD/PD cargo and D620N disease mechanisms.

main_caveats: The Vps35-Camta1 genome-wide score correlation was only -0.0165; this is a restricted-signature hypothesis, not evidence that CAMTA1 is a retromer regulator.
summary: Camta1 was the weak whole-surface negative neighbor and significantly opposed a subset of Vps35-up genes in 151 TH.
why_it_matters: Camta1 down-regulated Coro6, Vwa5b2, Hapln4, Kifc2, and Dgkz where Vps35 up-regulated them, preserving a data-nominated anti-signature that is invisible from retromer priors.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: VPS35L is a Retriever subunit required for retromer-independent surface-cargo recycling, and strong VPS35L loss can impair LRP1/LDLR surface abundance and autophagic function.
main_caveats: The experiment measured nuclear RNA, not surface cargo proteins, autophagic flux, or DNA indels; the conclusion is restricted to assayed P16 postmitotic neurons.
summary: Acute Vps35l perturbation produced no FDR<0.10 downstream transcriptional program in any of the 22 measured neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Retriever loss is expected to perturb endosomal cargo recycling and, in strong cell models, autophagy; the mouse-brain result therefore refines the biology to say that P16 sparse loss in postmitotic neurons does not elicit a cell-autonomous snRNA stress, lysosomal, cholesterol, or cargo-mRNA response over 3-4 weeks.

literature_claim: Retriever is structurally related to retromer and coupled to CCC/WASH within Commander, but is biochemically distinct from the VPS35 retromer complex.
main_caveats: Rab7 is an upstream broad endolysosomal GTPase rather than a Commander subunit; Washc4 had only 25-76 perturbed cells per measured group.
summary: The Vps35l null did not collapse all endosomal trafficking biology: Rab7 and, more weakly, Vps35 produced FDR-level responses in the same thalamic group where Vps35l had 205 cells and zero downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This directly rejects a purely low-power or pathway-undetectability explanation for Vps35l in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; connected endolysosomal perturbations can write detectable lysosomal, cholesterol, and neuronal RNAs, whereas Retriever/Commander loss through Vps35l did not.

main_caveats: The neighbor statistic used only subthreshold Vps35l Wilcoxon features, because no FDR-level Vps35l genes were available for a robust overlap test.
summary: A model-wide signature-neighbor search found no meaningful Vps35l convergence or opposition: the best cosine was only 0.092 and the strongest anticorrelation was -0.047.
why_it_matters: Because the nearest positive and negative neighbors were computed before using pathway priors and were still near zero, the Vps35l surface is better interpreted as a true absence of detectable RNA response than as a small branch of a known transcriptional module.

literature_claim: Human VPS41/HOPS disease has movement-disorder and cerebellar involvement, whereas this acute screen perturbed postmitotic neurons only after P16.
main_caveats: The responder signatures contain one FDR gene per group, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 22 perturbed nuclei.
summary: Vps41 produced a sparse, caudally biased transcriptional response: exactly one FDR<0.10 downstream gene in each of 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 217 P MY Pineal Glut and 308 CB GABA, a weak sub-threshold trace in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in the other measured cortical, forebrain, thalamic, hypothalamic and interneuron groups.
why_it_matters: The positive biology is not a pan-neuronal HOPS-failure program after P16 editing; the few cells that cross a transcriptional threshold are caudal/glutamatergic, GABAergic or cerebellar neuronal groups, consonant with but much narrower than the cerebellar and movement-disorder vulnerability reported for chronic VPS41/HOPS disease.

direction: Mcoln1 and Dpp7 up after Vps41 and Rab7 perturbation
literature_claim: Mammalian VPS41 is required for late endosome-lysosome fusion, HOPS is linked to RAB7, MCOLN1 couples lysosomes to TFEB signalling, and DPP7 is a proline-cleaving peptidase.
main_caveats: Only two Vps41 downstream genes support the lysosomal branch; the Rab7 perturbation was much broader than Vps41.
summary: The canonical part of the Vps41 response was a weak lysosomal compensation module: Mcoln1 was induced in 155 MB Glut and Dpp7 in 191 MB P MY GABA, and Rab7 perturbation independently induced the same two genes in the same cell groups.
why_it_matters: VPS41 is a HOPS late-fusion subunit and RAB7 is the HOPS-recruiting late-endosomal GTPase; same-direction Mcoln1 and Dpp7 convergence argues that the two lysosomal hits are on-pathway biology rather than isolated false discoveries.

main_caveats: Single FDR gene in only 22 Vps41-perturbed nuclei; nearby sterol genes were nominal but not FDR significant and are intentionally not used to call a pathway.
summary: 217 P MY Pineal Glut responded to Vps41 with an isolated, very large Idh1 induction rather than a corrected lysosomal-gene set.
why_it_matters: A soluble NADPH/redox gene can be the most sensitive transcript in this low-count caudal class, cautioning that Vps41 stress can appear outside textbook lysosomal markers in single-nucleus data.

literature_claim: TIMM17-family proteins function in TIM23-dependent import of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial presequence proteins.
main_caveats: Single FDR gene at FDR 0.0668; no orthogonal mitochondrial measurements were made.
summary: 308 CB GABA carried an isolated up-regulation of Timm17a, a mitochondrial inner-membrane import component, with no accompanying lysosomal FDR genes.
why_it_matters: This marks a possible mitochondrial-import branch of Vps41 stress in cerebellar GABA neurons, distinct from the Mcoln1/Dpp7 lysosomal branch.

direction: Rab7 partial convergence; other comparators rejected or divergent
literature_claim: HOPS/VPS41 is mechanistically adjacent to Rab GTPase and dynein-dynactin endolysosomal transport, but not identical to upstream autophagy initiation or retromer/GARP/EARP complexes.
main_caveats: The rank correlations were numerically small, and no same-complex HOPS subunit other than Vps41 was represented in the parquet.
summary: Cross-perturbation structure was Rab7-centered but shallow: Rab7 was the top positive score neighbor and the only comparator sharing Vps41 FDR genes, whereas Dctn1 was a broader sterol-biogenesis neighbor and Vps35, Vps53/Vps54, Vps13-family, Atg5, Becn1, Ctsb, Lamp2 and Tmem106b did not phenocopy Vps41.
why_it_matters: The measurable relatives separate HOPS/Rab7 late fusion from retromer/GARP/EARP trafficking, autophagy initiation and single lysosomal-enzyme loss; Vps41 is not just a generic lysosomal perturbation signature in this screen.

literature_claim: Strong VPS41 depletion or disease variants delay autophagic/endocytic cargo delivery and constitutively activate the TFEB/TFE3 lysosome-autophagy axis.
main_caveats: The screen measured nuclear RNA only 3-4 weeks after mosaic LoF and did not assay cargo flux, LC3-II, SQSTM1 protein, TFEB localization or DNA indels.
summary: The expected TFEB/TFE3-autophagy transcriptional expansion after VPS41 inhibition was largely absent: Vps41 yielded only four FDR genes total and only two lysosomal/autophagy hits, Mcoln1 and Dpp7, across 22 measured groups.
why_it_matters: VPS41 disease variants can drive constitutive TFEB/TFE3-linked lysosomal biogenesis, so its absence here means acute P16 sparse neuronal editing does not recapitulate the chronic VPS41 patient-cell program and that a broad CLEAR signature is not a useful universal biomarker for Vps41-edited nuclei in this assay.

literature_claim: VPS53 is a core subunit shared by GARP and EARP; severe mutations in GARP/EARP subunits cause vesicle-sorting defects and neurodevelopmental disease.
main_caveats: True editing was not measured by DNA indel sequencing; weak Vps53 own-transcript effects are expected in this platform and do not rule out functional knockout.
summary: Vps53 produced only three FDR<0.10 downstream calls across 21 measured neuronal groups, all up-regulated and confined to 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: A shared GARP/EARP trafficking subunit did not generate a broad postmitotic neuronal transcriptome after P16 sparse CRISPR; most of its acute biology was buffered or displaced outside this nuclear RNA readout.

literature_claim: DDIT3/CHOP is a stress-induced transcription factor activated in ER stress and other damaging states.
main_caveats: Only two genes reached FDR<0.10; Rhoq is not specific to GARP/EARP biology, and Ddit3 by itself does not define a complete UPR.
summary: The strongest Vps53 responder was 191 MB P MY GABA, where Rhoq and Ddit3 were the only corrected downstream genes.
why_it_matters: Coupling of a Rho-family transcript with Ddit3/CHOP nominates a narrow posterior or midbrain GABA stress state rather than a whole-brain GARP/EARP failure signature.

literature_claim: FARP1 is a RhoGEF that can promote dendritic growth in neurons.
main_caveats: Single-gene signature; no other synaptic, dendritic, or stress genes were significant in this group.
summary: Vps53 up-regulated only Farp1 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The isolated cortical signal points toward a possible RhoGEF/dendritic-morphology compensation while preserving that the evidence is one FDR-significant transcript, not a broader cortical program.

literature_claim: VPS53 and VPS54 are both subunits of the GARP tethering complex, and Vps54 hypomorphism destabilizes GARP in wobbler mice.
main_caveats: VPS53 is also an EARP subunit whereas VPS54 is GARP-specific; CRISPR engagement strength could differ across targets.
summary: Vps54, the represented same-GARP-complex partner, had a 45-gene response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Vps53 was weak in that thalamic group and Vps54 did not share Vps53's 005 or 191 responder genes.
why_it_matters: The result rejects a simple same-complex transcriptomic phenocopy and suggests that acute P16 Vps53 loss is not equivalent to Vps54 loss in the sampled neurons.

literature_claim: DDIT3/CHOP is part of stress programs downstream of damaging conditions including ER stress.
main_caveats: Atp2a2 and Psmc1 benchmark stress induced by different primary lesions; their signatures demonstrate detectability, not mechanistic identity.
summary: Vps53 did not activate a full UPR/ISR module, despite one Ddit3 hit in 191 MB P MY GABA and clear detectability of Ddit3/Chac1/Xbp1/Herpud1/Hspa5/Asns after Atp2a2 perturbation in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: The absence of a broad ER or lysosomal stress transcriptome is informative: Vps53 did not drive the kind of secondary nuclear stress response that the assay can detect for other perturbations.

literature_claim: GARP, STX16, TBC1D23, COG, retromer, and HOPS-related proteins all participate in Golgi or endosomal membrane traffic.
main_caveats: Several comparators were weak or single-gene responders; absence of transcriptomic overlap does not exclude shared biochemical cargo-sorting defects.
summary: Other represented Golgi, endosome-to-TGN, and endolysosomal perturbations, including Tbc1d23, Stx16, Cog4, Cog5, Vps35, Vps35l, and Vps41, failed to converge on Vps53's Farp1/Rhoq/Ddit3 responder genes.
why_it_matters: The corrected Vps53 surface is not a generic TGN/endosomal tether signature; it is narrower than nearby vesicle-trafficking perturbations and cannot be explained by any measured trafficking comparator.

literature_claim: Vps54 loss in mice is better known for wobbler motor-neuron degeneration, male-germline defects, and early embryonic lethality than for isolated thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c responses.
main_caveats: The 151 class is a broad snRNA-seq group; 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut were not tested for Vps54.
summary: Acute Vps54 loss produced one FDR-scale neuronal response, confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with 45 downstream genes while 20 other measured cell groups had none.
why_it_matters: A GARP/wobbler gene can be transcriptionally visible in a thalamic glutamatergic class, but the response is far from pan-neuronal despite ubiquitous vesicle-trafficking biology.

literature_claim: The primary GARP lesion is impaired endosome-to-TGN trafficking and M6PR/lysosomal enzyme sorting; chronic Vps54 mutation causes motor-neuron survival phenotypes.
main_caveats: Gene assignment to synaptic, secretory, and axonal programs is transcript-based; no vesicle trafficking, morphology, or protein-localization assay was measured in the same nuclei.
summary: The 151 Vps54 program is biased toward loss of mature neuronal signaling, peptide processing, and axon/neurite transcripts rather than induction of a canonical lysosomal rescue program.
why_it_matters: This places the acute survivor-cell readout downstream of GARP at synaptic and structural maintenance, providing a transcriptional correlate of neuronal dysfunction without directly recapitulating the protein-sorting lesion.

literature_claim: Egr1 is an immediate-early transcription factor tied to neuronal activity, stress, and plasticity responses.
main_caveats: Jun and Egr1 have many upstream regulators; this pair is a marker hypothesis, not a resolved AP-1 mechanism.
summary: Vps54 splits the 151 immediate-early axis: Egr1 is the strongest decreased gene whereas Jun is one of only eight up-regulated FDR genes.
why_it_matters: The Egr1-down/Jun-up pair is a compact candidate marker for the acute Vps54-responsive state and argues against a simple global increase or decrease in activity-regulated transcription.

literature_claim: GARP/Vps54 deficiency misroutes M6PR-dependent lysosomal cargo and perturbs sphingolipid homeostasis, while Rab7 perturbation tests an endolysosomal stress state in the same cell class.
main_caveats: The screen measures mRNA only; lipid accumulation and lysosomal enzyme missorting could occur below a transcriptional threshold.
summary: Vps54 did not activate the UPR/ISR, proteasome, lysosomal hydrolase, or sphingolipid transcripts that a severe GARP trafficking collapse would be expected to secondarily expose to snRNA-seq.
why_it_matters: The absent stress modules make the positive 151 signature biologically specific rather than a generic endolysosomal damage program.

literature_claim: Rab7 controls late-endosomal/lysosomal traffic and Grin1 encodes the NMDAR1 ion-channel subunit; neither belongs to the GARP complex.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed only over the 45 Vps54 FDR genes; several high-cosine neighbors, including Atp6ap2 and Vps53, had no FDR-scale overlap on those genes.
summary: The top data-driven positive neighbors of the Vps54 151 signature were Grin1, Pitpna, Atp6ap2, Vps53, and Rab7 by 45-gene cosine; Rab7, Grin1, Psmb4, Prpf6, and U2af2 shared many same-direction FDR genes on that restricted signature.
why_it_matters: The Vps54 module is reproducible against unrelated perturbations and is not explained by GARP membership alone.

literature_claim: Rab7 is a late-endosomal/lysosomal Rab GTPase, whereas GARP is a TGN tether for retrograde cargo; both impinge on endolysosomal homeostasis but at different compartments.
main_caveats: Only Rab7 is a direct endolysosomal comparator in this screen; the overlap need not mean physical Rab7-GARP coupling in 151 neurons.
summary: Rab7 most strongly shares the Vps54 151 down-shifted neuronal tail but extends to lysosomal, sterol, autophagy, PERK, and apoptosis genes that are absent after Vps54 perturbation.
why_it_matters: This separates an endosomal late-stress program that the assay can detect from the much narrower Vps54 state, making the Vps54 nulls for Lamp/Cts/Sptlc transcripts informative rather than a readout failure.

literature_claim: VPS53 is a core subunit shared by GARP and EARP, and human VPS53 variants cause progressive cerebello-cerebral atrophy.
main_caveats: Vps53 DNA editing and protein loss were not measured; the contrast is a transcriptomic non-phenocopy under this delivered gRNA context.
summary: The represented GARP/EARP subunit Vps53 continuously shadows the Vps54 45-gene vector but does not reach an FDR-scale Vps54 phenocopy.
why_it_matters: Same-complex membership is insufficient to predict acute neuronal Perturb-seq output: Vps53 ranked fourth by restricted cosine, yet had 0 FDR<0.10 genes in 151 and only 3 across all matched groups.

literature_claim: Retromer, GARP, and TGN SNAREs cooperate in retrograde delivery of endosomal cargo to the TGN.
main_caveats: Stx16 and Stx5a were nearly flat in this screen, so the negative comparison is most decisive for Vps35.
summary: Retromer/TGN-SNARE pathway neighbors Vps35, Stx16, and Stx5a failed to converge with Vps54 in the 151 signature even though Vps35 was itself active there.
why_it_matters: The Vps54 151 response is not a generic consequence of disrupting every retrograde cargo route to the TGN.

literature_claim: GARP mutations perturb sphingolipid homeostasis and inhibition of sphingolipid synthesis improves wobbler mouse outcomes.
main_caveats: The comparison is mRNA-based; sphingolipid intermediates were not measured, and CRISPR Sptlc2 loss is not identical to pharmacologic myriocin exposure.
summary: The Vps54 151 transcriptome neither nominated sphingolipid-enzyme genes nor showed an opposite FDR-scale relationship to Sptlc2, Asah1, or Cert1 perturbations.
why_it_matters: Myriocin-class sphingolipid suppression is protective in wobbler mice, but this acute brain-neuron signature would not by itself recover that therapeutic direction.

literature_claim: Zc3h13 encodes an m6A writer-complex factor and Atp1b2/AMOG encodes the Na,K-ATPase beta2 adhesion/pump subunit, but neither is an established Vsx1 target.
main_caveats: Only two genes pass FDR<0.10 and the Vsx1 self-transcript is not depleted; DNA indel engagement is not measured.
summary: Vsx1 produced a tiny but FDR-controlled response restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA: Zc3h13 and Atp1b2 were both up-regulated, and no other measured cell group had a downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: The result localizes all robust postnatal brain transcriptomic activity of Vsx1 to one hypothalamic/cerebral-nuclei GABA group and reduces the screen phenotype to two candidate validation genes rather than a canonical retinal or spinal program.

main_caveats: The metric is necessarily a two-feature sparse comparison because Vsx1 has only two FDR-controlled downstream genes.
summary: The data-driven Vsx1 neighbors in 066 were single-anchor contrasts: Zbtb7a alone converged through Atp1b2 up-regulation, whereas Ogt, Hnrnpu, and Psmb4 opposed Vsx1 through Atp1b2 or Zc3h13 down-regulation embedded in broader signatures.
why_it_matters: Because the neighbor search was run before using retinal priors, it shows that the measurable Vsx1 state is not dominated by the textbook Vsx1/Vsx2 axis and that each of the two Vsx1 genes can be decoupled by other perturbations in the same cell group.

literature_claim: Vsx1 and Chx10/Vsx2 are the mouse paired-like CVC paralogs and participate with V2 and retinal transcription-factor networks during development.
main_caveats: Some relevant retinal and V2 factors, including Irx5, Prdm8, Bhlhe22, Bhlhe23, Ascl1, and Foxn4, were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Vsx2 and other represented retinal/V2 transcription-factor relatives did not phenocopy the 066 Vsx1 signature; Vsx2 had 0 FDR genes in 066 and only one FDR gene across its whole 22-group surface.
why_it_matters: The expected paralog and developmental-neighbor tests convert a negative comparison into a result: the postnatal CNU-HYa HY signal is not a generic paired-like CVC, retinal, or V2-interneuron transcription-factor state.

literature_claim: Germline Vsx1 loss affects retinal cone-bipolar terminal differentiation and embryonic spinal V2 precursor identity programs.
main_caveats: The assay would detect transcript changes in these genes if present in sampled nuclei, but it contains neither retina nor spinal cord and excludes hindbrain.
summary: The canonical Vsx1 loss programs were absent: retinal genes including Rcvrn, Neto1, Cabp5, Tacr3, Prkca, Grm6, Trpm1, and Vsx2 and embryonic V2 markers including Prox1, Insm1, Pax6, Lhx3, Lhx4, and Gata3 had 0 FDR<0.10 responses.
why_it_matters: This supports a tissue- and timing-limited interpretation of the null surface rather than a failed Perturb-seq readout: the programs known to sit downstream of Vsx1 live in retina or embryonic spinal/hindbrain lineages that this P16 brain screen did not sample at the decisive window.

comparators: all other Il34-measured targets in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
literature_claim: IL-34 is a neuronally produced CSF1R ligand that supports microglial development and postnatal cortical microglial maturation.
main_caveats: Only Il34 crossed FDR<0.10, at q=0.0648 in 86 perturbed nuclei; microglia were not profiled, so the predicted receiver-cell consequence is unmeasured.
summary: Vsx2 perturbation induced a singleton Il34 response in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
why_it_matters: Il34 encodes a neuronal CSF1R ligand for microglia; its induction nominates a non-cell-autonomous neuron-to-microglia axis even though the NeuN-enriched assay did not sample the recipient microglia.

literature_claim: Vsx2 has strong developmental functions in retina and embryonic V2a lineages, not a known pan-neuronal maintenance role across mature forebrain, thalamic, midbrain, or cerebellar neurons.
main_caveats: Cell classes were coarse and DNA indels were not measured; absence of a target-mRNA drop is an engagement caveat, not a failed-KO call.
summary: The Vsx2 perturbation was a near-null, cell-restricted singleton: 1 downstream gene in 1 of 22 measured cell groups, 21 null groups, and 215 MB Dopa missing.
why_it_matters: The result localizes the measurable P16 young-brain transcriptomic response to one deep glutamatergic class rather than a broad visual-system homeobox program.

literature_claim: Vsx1 is the mouse paired-like CVC paralog of Vsx2, and Rax/Six3/Pax6/Otx2/Crx/Lhx3 sit in the retinal or V2a developmental networks in which Vsx2 acts.
main_caveats: The tested tissue is far from the retina and spinal embryonic lineages in which these transcription factors normally cooperate; most comparator signatures were also singleton or null.
summary: Retinal/V2a transcription-factor relatives failed to phenocopy Vsx2 in the same measured brain groups.
why_it_matters: The contrast rejects the idea that the Il34 singleton is a generic consequence of perturbing paired-like or eye-field homeodomain genes in this assay.

literature_claim: No biological literature claim was needed; these were data-nominated nearest neighbors.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed over a mostly null Vsx2 vector, so it is most useful as evidence for non-convergence.
summary: Unbiased signature search found no meaningful Vsx2 neighbor: the top positive and negative real-gene correlations were only +0.0335 for Ndufb7 and -0.0186 for Npy5r.
why_it_matters: Because the strongest genome-wide neighbors are effectively orthogonal, the single Il34 hit should be treated as a focused observation rather than as part of a conserved multi-gene perturbation module.

literature_claim: Retinal Vsx2 loss reduces progenitor expansion and bipolar genesis and can change photoreceptor/RPE fate programs.
main_caveats: This is not evidence against the retinal mechanism itself; the screen sampled postmitotic brain neurons, not optic cup or retina.
summary: The canonical retina program expected from Vsx2/Chx10 loss was absent from the measured brain-neuron surface.
why_it_matters: Vsx2 loss in retina affects retinal progenitor expansion, bipolar genesis, and photoreceptor/RPE fate balance, but none of the assayed retinal progenitor, bipolar, photoreceptor, or RPE marker genes moved at FDR<0.10 here.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: WAC loss of function causes a neurodevelopmental syndrome, and WAC has been studied in GABAergic MGE-derived neurons.
main_caveats: The 16 positive groups include several one- to ten-gene signatures; 215 MB Dopa was missing for Wac and cannot be scored.
summary: Wac loss was transcriptionally active in 16 of 22 measured neuronal groups but was strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba rather than in all Wac-expressing neurons.
why_it_matters: A WAC chromatin/autophagy adaptor could have looked pan-neuronal; instead the post-P16 mosaic knockout exposed a state-restricted response and warns against averaging the disease gene across the whole brain.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: WAC links RNF20/RNF40 to active transcription and human WAC haploinsufficiency produces cognitive and behavioral neurodevelopmental phenotypes.
main_caveats: Most genes are markers of neuronal state or synaptic function, not proven direct H2Bub targets in these nuclei.
summary: The dominant Wac downstream direction was repression of neuronal and synaptic marker transcripts, recurring as Lgi3, Septin5, Ache, C1qtnf4, Eno2, Syp, and related receptor or transporter genes across cortical, thalamic, midbrain, GABAergic, and cerebellar responders.
why_it_matters: The result turns an adaptor/chromatin disease gene into a concrete postmitotic neuronal phenotype: acute Wac loss tends to dampen selected mature-neuron programs instead of simply shutting down global transcription.

literature_claim: Embryonic MGE-derived GABAergic neurons have been used as a disease-relevant experimental context for WAC structure-function studies.
main_caveats: The broad Pvalb taxonomy pools subtypes; the data are snRNA end points and do not measure interneuron firing.
summary: Pvalb interneurons carried a coherent inhibitory/fast-spiking marker decrease after Wac loss, including Pvalb, Kcnab3, Gabrg2, Gabra1, Grin2d, and Syp down-regulation.
why_it_matters: The Pvalb result explains why the GABAergic arm of the Wac surface is not all-or-none: 052 Pvalb Gaba was a 143-gene responder whereas 053 Sst Gaba had no FDR<0.10 genes.

literature_claim: WAC is a nuclear adaptor for transcription-coupled H2B monoubiquitination by RNF20/RNF40 and UBE2A/B.
main_caveats: The compensatory label is inferential; H2Bub, RNF20/RNF40 occupancy, and RNA isoform changes were not directly assayed.
summary: Large Wac responders induced RNA-processing, transcription, chromatin, and ubiquitin-conjugation factors, including Adarb1, Luc7l2, Msi2, Rbm4, Ube2b, Clk1, Srsf9, Wdr33, Cpsf6, Atrx, and Kmt2a.
why_it_matters: The upward arm of the signature is consistent with a nuclear compensation program: Wac perturbation does not merely lower neuronal transcripts; it also increases machinery that could adjust RNA maturation and chromatin state.

literature_claim: PSMC1 and PSMB4 are proteasome components, whereas SIN3A scaffolds histone-deacetylase corepressor complexes rather than belonging to the RNF20/RNF40/WAC H2Bub complex.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed on transcriptomic signatures, so it does not prove that WAC directly regulates proteasome assembly or SIN3A complexes.
summary: The unbiased Wac signature neighbors were proteasome-subunit perturbations Psmc1 and Psmb4 and the chromatin corepressor Sin3a; they reproduced hundreds of Wac significant gene-by-cell features, mainly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This non-obvious convergence places the Wac state on a proteostasis/chromatin-response axis that was not nominated by the RNF20/RNF40 textbook complex alone.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: WAC/Wacky supports energy-mediated mTORC1 activation and starvation-induced autophagy through TTT-Pontin/Reptin and GM130/GABARAP mechanisms.
main_caveats: The assay reads steady-state nuclear RNA, not LC3 lipidation, mTOR phosphorylation, or autophagic flux; a flux change without a secondary RNA program would be missed.
summary: The expected mTORC1/autophagy arm of WAC biology was not recovered: core Map1lc3, Gabarap, Sqstm1, Ulk, Atg5/Becn1, Mtor, and Rptor transcripts were non-significant after Wac perturbation, and Mtor, Rptor, Atg5, and Becn1 perturbations were not Wac-like.
why_it_matters: The negative result separates Wac neuronal transcriptional remodeling from starvation-autophagy phenotypes described in dividing cells and flies; the present postmitotic nuclei would have detected a secondary autophagy-associated transcriptome, and it was absent.

main_caveats: This is a signature-level contrast, not a mechanistic epistasis experiment.
summary: Zbtb7a and Uba5 were the top signed negative Wac neighbors, reversing many of the 151 TH Wac features such as Eno2, Ache, Vgf, Clk1, and Msi2.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that broad transcriptional or ubiquitin-system stress is not sufficient to generate the Wac program; related-looking perturbations can move the same neuronal state genes in the opposite direction.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Pathogenic WASHC4 variants destabilize WASH and cause intellectual-disability and endo-lysosomal disease phenotypes.
main_caveats: DNA indels and WASHC4 protein were not measured; four taxonomy groups were missing rather than null.
summary: Washc4 CRISPR produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq response in any of the 19 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result sharply defines the measured phenotype: acute postmitotic Washc4 perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across every tested group rather than selective for one cortical, inhibitory, thalamic, midbrain, or cerebellar class.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Severe chronic SWIP/WASHC4 dysfunction alters WASH-endosomal, lysosomal, ER-chaperone, and postsynaptic protein modules.
main_caveats: The Washc4 test is mRNA-only and acute; the comparator UPR signal was concentrated in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic groups.
summary: Expected WASH/Commander/Retromer, ER-stress, lysosomal-enzyme, and synaptic-module transcripts were not recovered after Washc4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The severe WASHC4 literature predicts protein-complex destabilization with endo-lysosomal and ER-proteostasis consequences; their absence at RNA FDR in 551 tested gene-by-cell entries indicates that the acute P16 CRISPR condition did not reach the secondary transcriptional state, even though UPR mRNAs were detectable in the same dataset after Sec63 perturbation.

literature_claim: WASH, Retromer, Retriever, and CCC/Commander complexes cooperate in endosomal cargo sorting and recycling.
main_caveats: Other core WASH subunits were not perturbation targets, and the Vps35 response is modest and mostly restricted to one cell group.
summary: Retromer Vps35, but not WASH-pathway Washc4 or Retriever Vps35l, produced a small thalamus-biased transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: Endosomal recycling membership did not imply phenocopy: a pathway neighbor generated 30 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and one in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, whereas Washc4 had no shared FDR genes because it had no FDR genes at all.

main_caveats: Correlation was computed over all overlapping Wilcoxon-score entries; a target with no significant genes has a noise-dominated profile.
summary: Washc4 had no meaningful data-driven positive or negative signature neighbors in the full perturbation universe.
why_it_matters: The nearest-neighbor search did not reveal a hidden convergent module that could rescue mechanistic interpretation from subthreshold Washc4 genes; the largest absolute real-target correlation was only 0.0263.

literature_claim: WDFY3/Alfy is CNS-enriched and acts as a selective-autophagy scaffold, but that literature does not specify a broad acute P16 neuronal RNA response.
main_caveats: The screen measures nuclear RNA 3-4 weeks after P16 mosaic CRISPR; DNA indels and protein depletion are not directly measured.
summary: Wdfy3 loss produced a sharply restricted postnatal neuronal response: 32 FDR<0.10 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and only Stmn4 in 155 MB Glut, with the other 20 measured groups lacking robust downstream hits.
why_it_matters: The screen does not support a pan-neuronal acute Wdfy3 stress program; it localizes detectable LoF consequences to two glutamatergic subcortical classes despite Wdfy3 being present in each measured DE table.

literature_claim: Mouse Wdfy3 literature implicates Alfy in CNS axon guidance, mitochondrial transport/axon-guidance proteomes, and cortical projection-neuron morphology.
main_caveats: The thalamic signature is only 32 genes, so the module is compact and cannot establish the primary molecular substrate of Wdfy3.
summary: The main 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut program was a neuronal AP-1 / synaptic-vesicle / membrane downshift rather than a canonical autophagy transcriptome: Jun, Jund, Scg2, Chgb, Syt1, Syt11, Gpm6a, Tspan7, Kcnc2, and Kctd16 were all lower.
why_it_matters: These genes nominate a postmitotic neuronal-state effect that intersects WDFY3 connectivity biology but is mechanistically narrower than aggregate clearance.

main_caveats: Recurrence is across only two cell groups, and only one gene was significant in 155 MB Glut.
summary: Stmn4 was the only Wdfy3 downstream gene recurrent across both detected responder groups, down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Stmn4 provides the cleanest RNA marker for the sparse Wdfy3 neuronal response and ties the small MB Glut signal to the larger thalamic program rather than to an unrelated single-gene outlier.

literature_claim: ALFY/WDFY3 links p62/LC3/ATG5 aggregate clearance to allele-specific DVL3-Wnt brain-size regulation and modifies mutant huntingtin pathology.
main_caveats: Absence is transcriptomic; defective autophagic flux or cargo accumulation could be post-transcriptional unless it secondarily activated RNA stress/autophagy genes.
summary: Wdfy3 did not elicit the expected aggrephagy, mitophagy, lysosomal, or DVL3-Wnt transcriptional rebound, and targeted perturbations of Atg5, Atg16l1, Becn1, Map1lc3a, Rb1cc1, Sqstm1, Htt, Vcp, Ctnnb1, and Lrp6 failed to phenocopy the Wdfy3 151/155 signature.
why_it_matters: Because core autophagy and Wnt perturbations were directly represented and in some cases responded elsewhere, their non-overlap argues that postmitotic Wdfy3 is not behaving as a simple core-macroautophagy or beta-catenin/Wnt perturbation in this juvenile snRNA readout.

literature_claim: Alfy loss disrupts neuronal wiring and is enriched in membrane fractions, but Dctn1 was not a literature-predicted Wdfy3 phenolog.
main_caveats: The initial #1 positive cosine neighbor, Zdhhc17, lacked FDR-level shared genes and was rejected; Dctn1 convergence is partial and does not include Dctn1 sterol-program genes in Wdfy3.
summary: Dctn1 was the strongest FDR-supported positive neighbor of Wdfy3, matching 13 Wdfy3 features in the same direction across the thalamic and MB Glut responders, while adding a broad sterol/lipid response absent from Wdfy3.
why_it_matters: The data-driven neighbor links the Wdfy3 module to dynein/dynactin-type transport biology without collapsing the two genes into one phenotype: Dctn1 is broader and dominated by cholesterol genes, whereas Wdfy3 is restricted.

main_caveats: The top raw negative neighbor, Scn1b, had only one FDR-level opposing overlap and was rejected as a robust anti-phenocopy; Grin1 is data-driven but not a known Wdfy3 pathway member.
summary: Grin1 opposed rather than copied Wdfy3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with 13 FDR<0.10 Wdfy3 features changing in the opposite direction under NMDAR loss.
why_it_matters: The Wdfy3 thalamic state is not a generic consequence of weakening excitatory receptor signaling; several genes reduced by Wdfy3, including Jun, Stmn4, Gpm6a, Kctd16, Scg2, Syt11, and Tspan7, rose after Grin1 perturbation.

literature_claim: Human WDR26 haploinsufficiency produces a broad neurodevelopmental syndrome with intellectual disability, seizures, hypotonia, and abnormal gait, but prior clinical data did not define the vulnerable postnatal neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The screen does not test embryonic development or behavior, and the cell groups are broad neuronal aggregates.
summary: Basal P16 Wdr26 loss generated a sharply non-cortical response: 7 of 21 measured cell groups had FDR<0.10 downstream genes, dominated by 308 CB GABA, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, while 14 measured telencephalic/cortical groups had none.
why_it_matters: The response is a cell-state maintenance phenotype in selected postmitotic neurons, not a universal consequence of WDR26 loss across all neurons that expressed a measured Wdr26 transcript.

literature_claim: WDR26 depletion can alter chromatin accessibility and gene-expression profiles in mammalian cells.
main_caveats: The dataset measures RNA abundance rather than splice isoforms or chromatin accessibility.
summary: A recurrent RNA-processing and nuclear-transport module is the most penetrant Wdr26 downstream signature: Srrm2 fell in every responder and Hnrnpu, Kpna1, Luc7l2, Ccnl2, Ddx24, Son, and Arglu1 were repeatedly lower.
why_it_matters: The shared down-regulation of splicing and nuclear RNA-handling genes provides a common molecular readout tying the small hypothalamic/thalamic signatures to the much broader midbrain, pontomedullary, and cerebellar states.

literature_claim: WDR26 is a CTLH E3-ligase subunit and disease mutations can impair CTLH assembly or WDR26-dependent substrate recruitment.
main_caveats: The convergence is downstream and does not identify WDR26-CTLH protein substrates in neurons; Psmc1/Psmb4 signatures were much larger and were not concordant in 308 CB GABA.
summary: Wdr26 converged with proteasome-subunit perturbations in diencephalic and midbrain responders: Psmc1 and Psmb4 were the top two same-direction FDR-overlap neighbors, especially in 066, 155, and 191.
why_it_matters: This links Wdr26 loss to a downstream ubiquitin/proteasome-state response even though the target is a CTLH substrate adaptor rather than a core proteasome subunit.

literature_claim: WDR26 loss of function is linked to a human syndrome including intellectual disability, seizures, and abnormal gait.
main_caveats: mRNA shifts are indirect; the experiment did not record neuronal firing, synaptic physiology, or behavior.
summary: Wdr26 loss reconfigured synaptic and ion-channel transcripts, from recurrent Kcna2, Scn1b, Atp1a3, Atp1b1, and Grin2b decreases to a broad cerebellar shift involving Cacna1g, Cacna1a, Grik1, Grid2, Grm7, Kcnt1, Grin2d, and Gria4.
why_it_matters: A postmitotic perturbation was sufficient to move excitability genes that plausibly sit closer to seizure and motor phenotypes than the canonical Axin/MAPK readouts.

literature_claim: WDR26 had been reported to protect H2O2-challenged neural cells and to promote hypoxia-induced Parkin mitophagy in cardiomyocytes.
main_caveats: No ROS, mitochondrial potential, or mitophagy flux was measured, so the measured genes are a transcriptomic proxy.
summary: A mitochondrial and amino-acid-metabolic arm was reduced after Wdr26 perturbation, with Nat8l down in four responders and Cyc1, Slc25a3, Samm50, Atp5d, Ndufb5, and Gls lower within the thalamic, midbrain, and pontomedullary signatures.
why_it_matters: The result moves WDR26 stress biology into postnatal neurons and nominates mitochondrial/metabolic fragility as a companion to the synaptic state.

main_caveats: Col11a2 and Bcan are interpreted as snRNA state markers from NeuN-enriched nuclei; protein deposition was not assayed.
summary: Col11a2 was one of the largest induced transcripts in Wdr26 responders, recurring in 110, 155, 191, and 308, accompanied by Ptprz1 induction and mixed Bcan and collagen-family changes.
why_it_matters: The ECM/adhesion-like arm is a strong marker of the Wdr26 perturbed state and could help stratify Wdr26-responsive neurons from flat cell types.

literature_claim: mTORC1 inhibition can regulate UCK2 turnover through the CTLH-WDR26 E3 ligase.
main_caveats: This is a signature-level relationship; Uck2 protein turnover and mTORC1 activity were not measured.
summary: Tsc2 was the top positive signed-score neighbor of Wdr26 and shared 133 same-direction versus 9 opposite robust Wdr26-signature features, with a purely same-direction 55-gene overlap in 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: The Tsc2 comparison nominates an mTOR-proximal state as a non-obvious Wdr26 neighbor and connects the neuronal Wdr26 signature to CTLH-WDR26 regulation by the mTORC1 axis.

literature_claim: WDR26 has been reported to suppress MAPK, to bind Axin1 in canonical Wnt signaling, and to scaffold Gβγ/PLCβ2 signaling in leukocytes.
main_caveats: Some pathway-responsive genes were detected; the conclusion is that these were not the dominant or cross-perturbation-matched state.
summary: Canonical Wnt, MAPK/AP-1, and Gβγ/PI3K/Rac expectations were weakly and sparsely recovered: Axin2 was induced in 155 and 191 and Jun/Mapk genes appeared in 191 or 308, but represented pathway-node perturbations did not phenocopy Wdr26.
why_it_matters: The postnatal neuronal phenotype is not reducible to the classical Axin/MAPK or leukocyte Gβγ scaffolding models; it is dominated instead by proteostasis, RNA-processing, synaptic, metabolic, and trafficking modules.

main_caveats: The mechanistic source of the opposition was not resolved, and the Dnajb4 score-only anti-neighbor was rejected because it had no robust overlap.
summary: Ranbp2 was a cerebellar anti-neighbor: in 308 CB GABA it overlapped 153 Wdr26 significant genes and flipped the sign of 152 of them.
why_it_matters: A large Wdr26 cerebellar signature is therefore signed and specific, not merely a generic response to any perturbation that yields many DE genes in cerebellar GABA neurons.

literature_claim: WDR26 can scaffold Gβγ signaling and has been linked to Rac-dependent migratory signaling in non-neuronal systems.
main_caveats: Rac1 itself did not phenocopy Wdr26 in this dataset, so the cytoskeletal program should not be reduced to a single Gβγ/Rac pathway.
summary: Wdr26 loss coupled its RNA/synaptic response to cytoskeletal and vesicle-trafficking remodeling, with recurrent Dync1h1, Actr1b, Hook2, Hap1, Pak3, Septin3, Stmn3/Stmn4, and cerebellar Kalrn/Arhgap26/Srgap2 changes.
why_it_matters: The data nominate axonal transport, small-GTPase, and vesicle modules as part of the neuronal Wdr26 state alongside ubiquitin biology.

literature_claim: Human WDR37 missense variants and Drosophila wdr37 loss produce neurodevelopmental, seizure-like, and motor phenotypes, but those organismal phenotypes do not specify a resting postnatal neuronal transcriptome.
main_caveats: No DNA indel, protein, morphology, survival, or evoked physiology readout was collected; 215 MB Dopa was not recovered.
summary: Wdr37 loss was a pan-neuronal transcriptomic null, with 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in all 22 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The null covers cortical, hippocampal, striatal, hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain/pons-medulla, pineal, and cerebellar neuronal groups rather than one underpowered slice; the flat Wdr37 transcript is expected for pooled CRISPR indels and is not used as a failure call.

literature_claim: Wdr37 p.Ser129Phe zebrafish embryos up-regulate cholesterol-biosynthesis pathways, and Pacs1-Wdr37 disruption in lymphocytes alters ER Ca2+ handling with ER and oxidative stress.
main_caveats: Marker-gene testing is not a formal gene-set enrichment test, and the literature signals came from embryos or lymphocytes rather than resting juvenile neurons.
summary: The embryonic zebrafish cholesterol signal and the lymphocyte ER/oxidative-stress readout of Pacs1-Wdr37 disruption were absent after P16 Wdr37 CRISPR in neurons.
why_it_matters: This argues against an unobserved but transcriptionally obvious stress bounce-back: if Wdr37-deficient juvenile neurons had mounted a cholesterol, ISR/UPR, oxidative, or autophagy response, the assayed marker transcripts should have generated corrected DE.

literature_claim: WDR37 homodimerizes and binds PACS1/PACS2, and clinical reports have framed WDR37, PACS1, and PACS2 as a related disease axis.
main_caveats: Pacs1 was not measured in 217 P MY Pineal Glut and all cross-target comparisons are transcriptomic rather than ER-calcium measurements.
summary: The WDR37-PACS1-PACS2 physical axis was jointly buffered in the acute neuronal CRISPR surface: Pacs2 was fully null and Pacs1 had only a single FDR<0.10 call.
why_it_matters: The strongest known WDR37 interactors do not reveal a hidden PACS-axis transcriptome in the same postmitotic neuronal assay, supporting contextual buffering of the ER-calcium/sorting axis rather than a Wdr37-only anomaly.

literature_claim: WDR proteins form a broad scaffold family; WDR37 disease has CHARGE-like developmental features, but WD-repeat membership alone does not imply functional interchangeability.
main_caveats: Wdr26 is not a Wdr37 paralog and the Wdr26 program was concentrated in subcortical and cerebellar groups.
summary: The Wdr37 null was not a WD-repeat-family readout floor: Wdr26, another WD-repeat neurodevelopmental target, produced 3,128 corrected DEGs in matched groups where Wdr37 had none.
why_it_matters: This contrast rejects a simple explanation that WD40 scaffolds or weak self-transcript measurements are generically invisible to the screen; the null is specific to Wdr37/PACS/CHD7-like biology in this context.

009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Cosines were computed on Wilcoxon score vectors over rows shared with Wdr37; missing cell groups and flat signatures make the exact neighbor ordering unstable.
summary: Whole-transcriptome signature-neighbor analysis found no coherent Wdr37 module: the strongest positive and negative score-vector cosines were only 0.035 and -0.029.
why_it_matters: The data-driven step did not nominate a hidden pathway neighbor; most apparent Wdr37 neighbors were themselves null or nearly null, and even the top strong responder, Wdr26, had negligible directional similarity.

literature_claim: WDR48/UAF1 is a cofactor for USP1, USP12, and USP46, and full UAF1 loss has strong phenotypes in proliferating and embryonic contexts.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured; the assay tests basal postmitotic nuclear RNA after mosaic AAV-CRISPR rather than protein ubiquitination or embryonic proliferation.
summary: Acute P16 Wdr48 perturbation produced no adjusted downstream transcriptomic response in any of 19 recovered neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The result establishes that postmitotic juvenile neurons tolerate Wdr48 indel perturbation without a detectable basal snRNA-seq stress, DNA-damage, or synaptic transcriptional program.

literature_claim: Loss of UAF1/WDR48 disrupts USP1-mediated FANCD2 and PCNA deubiquitination and homologous recombination in cycling cells and mouse embryos.
main_caveats: Absence of a transcriptomic damage program does not exclude FANCD2 or PCNA ubiquitination changes in unsampled proliferating lineages.
summary: The USP1-UAF1 Fanconi/homologous-recombination branch did not appear as Fanconi, p53, or DNA-damage DE, and represented repair comparators Atr and Ddb2 were also null.

summary: The two Xrn1 signatures were nearly direction-balanced, not globally up-regulated: 151 had 15 up and 14 down genes, and 155 had 11 up and 10 down genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: A simple loss of a 5′→3′ exonuclease could have been expected to accumulate many direct mRNA substrates; the observed balanced nucleus-visible signature supports steady-state buffering and secondary remodeling.

literature_claim: Xrn1/XRN1 can act as a post-transcriptional negative regulator of autophagy, with Xrn1 loss increasing ATG transcripts or autophagy in yeast and mammalian cells.
main_caveats: The gene set is small and infers endolysosomal state from RNA, not lysosome pH or autophagic flux.
summary: Xrn1 responders down-regulated lysosomal, V-ATPase, and ER-lumen genes, including Psap, Ap3m1, Atp6v0c, Hyou1, Hsp90b1, Atp6v0e2, Atp6v0a1, Cyp46a1, and Tmem59l.
why_it_matters: The strongest shared secondary biology was an endomembrane and acidification-associated decrease, despite external literature predicting autophagy derepression after XRN1 loss in yeast and mammalian cell models.

main_caveats: The interpretation groups annotated neuronal genes but does not include electrophysiology or synapse morphology.
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut uniquely up-regulated an adhesion/synaptic/cAMP block containing Adgrb1, Rap1gap2, Ppp1r9b, Rims2, Adcy1, Agap3, Shank1, Nt5c2, Nsmf, and Hrh3.
why_it_matters: This separates the 151 response from a generic RNA-decay stress response and nominates synaptic signaling genes as local biomarkers of the Xrn1 state in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.

main_caveats: The module is inferred from a limited FDR gene set and does not measure chromatin modifications.
summary: 155 MB Glut up-regulated RNA and chromatin regulators including Pnrc1, Dhx9, Dnmt3a, Brd2, Pura, Chd2, Myt1l, Apc2, and Maged1.
why_it_matters: The 155 signature looks like transcriptional/RNA-regulatory compensation layered on endolysosomal down-regulation, reinforcing that the snRNA signature is a remodelled steady-state output rather than a direct XRN1 substrate list.

main_caveats: The neighbor metric was restricted to significant Xrn1 features and does not prove direct physical interaction.
summary: Tpr, Cdc40, U2af2, and Thoc1 were the robust positive cross-perturbation neighbors of Xrn1 across the 50 significant Xrn1 group-gene features.
why_it_matters: This empirical convergence places Xrn1 with a nuclear RNA-processing and RNA-export/splicing neighborhood in this screen instead of with the expected cytoplasmic miRNA or decapping relatives.

literature_claim: Rab7 regulates transport to late endosomes and lysosomes, making its opposite signature a functionally interpretable endolysosomal contrast after Rab7 was nominated by the dataset.
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptomic and does not by itself order Xrn1 and Rab7 in one pathway.
summary: Rab7 and Elp1 opposed rather than copied the Xrn1 signature, with zero same-direction shared FDR genes and 10 or 9 opposing Xrn1 group-gene calls, respectively.
why_it_matters: The Rab7 contrast is especially informative because Xrn1 down-regulated several lysosomal/V-ATPase genes while a late-endosomal Rab7 perturbation moved many of the same genes in the opposite direction.

literature_claim: AGO-TNRC6, CCR4-NOT, and NMD pathways feed into cytoplasmic mRNA decay processes in which XRN1 can degrade downstream RNA fragments.
main_caveats: Direct decapping factors, Xrn2, and several core NMD factors were not represented as perturbation targets.
summary: Measured miRNA, CCR4-NOT, and NMD perturbations did not phenocopy Xrn1: Dicer1, Ago2, Tnrc6a, Tnrc6b, Cnot1, and Upf3b were flat or weak and shared at most one Xrn1 FDR gene.
why_it_matters: XRN1 participates downstream of miRNA/TNRC6 deadenylation and NMD, so this direct rejection shows that the postnatal neuronal Xrn1 state is not a generic consequence of weakening these upstream mRNA-silencing branches.

literature_claim: Strong XRN1 loss can derepress autophagy or cause PKR-dependent stress in yeast, mammalian cells, and interferon-activated cancer cells.
main_caveats: The screen lacked infection, exogenous interferon, non-neuronal immune cells, and flux measurements.
summary: Xrn1 did not induce a canonical ISR, IFN, or autophagy-transcription program in its two responder groups.
why_it_matters: This passes the readout gate for a real negative: if the cytoplasmic decay lesion had escalated to a cell-stress transcriptional state, nuclear snRNA-seq should have captured genes such as Atf4, Ddit3, Asns, Chac1, Hspa5, Lamp2, Sqstm1, Atg5, Atg7, or Becn1, but they were not FDR-significant.

literature_claim: XRN1 is being characterized as a cancer dependency whose complete loss can activate dsRNA-sensing or PKR stress in sensitive cancer contexts.
main_caveats: This is a sparse CRISPR neuronal screen without a small-molecule inhibitor or interferon stimulation, so it is a risk hypothesis rather than a toxicity result.
summary: The neuronal Xrn1 signature did not reproduce the interferon/PKR pharmacodynamic direction being explored for XRN1 cancer targeting and instead exposed a narrow neuronal endolysosomal/synaptic footprint.
why_it_matters: Any XRN1 inhibitor program should not assume the same dsRNA-sensing output in postmitotic neurons; neuronal liability may require RNA-decay, synaptic, and lysosomal assays rather than only IFN biomarkers.

literature_claim: XYLT1 initiates proteoglycan GAG chains, and GAG-bearing proteoglycans can affect neural migration, axon guidance, synaptogenesis and perineuronal-net plasticity.
main_caveats: The screen measured nuclear RNA in sparse postmitotic NeuN+ cells, not GAG length, sulfation, proteoglycan secretion, perineuronal nets, morphology or electrophysiology.
summary: Xylt1 loss produced a pan-neuronal null nuclear transcriptome rather than a stress, proteostasis, or synaptic transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: This is the primary result: in 23 assayed neuronal groups after P16 sparse CRISPR, every group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, so the assay did not reveal a cell-autonomous P37-P44 nuclear response to perturbing the GAG-chain initiating enzyme.

literature_claim: XylT1/XylT2 initiate the CS/DS/HS/heparin tetrasaccharide linker, B3GAT3 completes that linker, and EXT1/EXT2 polymerize heparan sulfate.
main_caveats: Many upstream linker genes and Xylt2 were not perturbed; B3gat3 and Ext2 effects were very small and should not be mechanistically interpreted gene by gene.
summary: Represented GAG-pathway perturbations did not form a shared Xylt1-like module.
why_it_matters: B3gat3, Ext1 and Ext2 are the pathway-near comparators available in the parquet. Ext1 was fully flat, B3gat3 and Ext2 had only singleton/small responses in cell groups where Xylt1 was flat, and correlations with the Xylt1 signature were near zero; the expected shared proteoglycan-biosynthesis pathway therefore does not collapse to a common acute neuronal DEG signature here.

main_caveats: Similarity was computed on Wilcoxon-score vectors dominated by null genes, so it is a diagnostic for absence of convergence rather than a mechanistic association.
summary: The unbiased signature-neighbor search placed Xylt1 near the origin of the perturbation space.
why_it_matters: The top positive whole-universe neighbor was only r=0.0324 and the strongest named-gene anti-neighbor was only r=-0.0196; after measuring both, Msx2 was nearly null and Ranbp2 had strong cell-type-specific responses that were absent from Xylt1. The nominal Xylt1 ranks therefore should not be read as a hidden coherent module.

literature_claim: XYLT1-associated Baratela-Scott/Desbuquois-spectrum disease and Xylt1 animal phenotypes are developmental and ECM centered, especially in cartilage, while GAGs also influence neural wiring and synaptic plasticity.
main_caveats: The null snRNA surface cannot exclude earlier neuronal wiring defects, astrocyte- or microglia-dependent ECM effects, or extracellular glycan changes without a secondary nuclear response.
summary: The XYLT1 disease axis is displaced away from acute postmitotic neuronal gene regulation.
why_it_matters: Human XYLT1 deficiency causes a developmental skeletal/neurodevelopmental syndrome and mouse/zebrafish work points to cartilage ECM and GAG-chain structure. The screen shows no P16-to-P44 neuronal nuclear correlate across cortex, hippocampus, striatum, hypothalamus, thalamus, midbrain, dopaminergic and cerebellar classes, suggesting that disease-relevant assays should prioritize developmental, ECM/glycomic and non-neuronal contexts over acute mature-neuron DEG biomarkers.

literature_claim: YEATS2 is an ATAC-complex H3K27ac reader whose depletion in NSCLC reduces promoter H3K9ac and ribosomal protein gene expression.
main_caveats: DNA indels, YEATS2 protein, H3K27ac, and H3K9ac were not assayed; most groups contained only 20-80 perturbed nuclei.
summary: Yeats2 is transcriptome-flat across the juvenile postmitotic neuronal surface: no measured cell group had a downstream FDR<0.10 gene, despite direct measurement of the Yeats2 transcript in every recovered group.
why_it_matters: A chromatin-reader perturbation that is essential for ribosomal and growth programs in NSCLC does not automatically create a broad acute snRNA-seq signature in already specified mouse neurons; the negative surface is therefore a biological refinement, not an assay failure.

literature_claim: ATAC is a defined multi-subunit acetyltransferase complex and YEATS2 is one of four human YEATS-domain chromatin readers.
main_caveats: True same-complex and same-domain comparators were unavailable; Ep300, Crebbp, and Atxn7 are indirect neighbors, not YEATS2 paralogs.
summary: The direct ATAC/YEATS comparator layer was mostly not present in the perturbation panel, and the represented H3-acetylation neighbors did not phenocopy Yeats2.
why_it_matters: The ATAC model predicts that YEATS2 should act with ZZZ3, KAT2A/GCN5, CCDC101/SGF29, and other ATAC subunits, but none of those subunits or the MLLT1/MLLT3/YEATS4 paralogs were perturbation targets; among indirect chromatin relatives, Crebbp had a 16-gene thalamic response whereas Ep300 and Atxn7 were flat.

main_caveats: Because Yeats2 itself had no FDR<0.10 genes, this is a whole-surface signed-score comparison rather than shared-DEG overlap among Yeats2 responders.
summary: The model-visible universe found no meaningful signed transcriptomic neighbor for Yeats2.
why_it_matters: The largest positive and negative correlations of Yeats2 signed Wilcoxon scores were near zero; even B9d1, the strongest non-safe positive neighbor with a real response, produced its 25-gene signal in cerebellar GABA where Yeats2 had no downstream genes.

literature_claim: FAME4 is caused by an intronic repeat expansion in YEATS2, and FAME repeat expansions occur in several unrelated host genes.
main_caveats: The screen models CRISPR LoF, not the toxic expanded-repeat allele; 215 MB Dopa was absent for Yeats2.
summary: Loss-of-function signatures across represented FAME repeat-locus host genes do not converge on a Yeats2-like neuronal state.
why_it_matters: Samd12 and Rapgef2 were completely flat, Stard7 and Tnrc6a had only one or two downstream genes, and Marchf6 instead induced a strong sterol-gene program; this agrees better with FAME as an intronic repeat disorder that can arise in unrelated host genes than with a shared host-gene LoF transcriptomic mechanism.

main_caveats: Three of the four responder cell groups had only one or two downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
summary: Ylpm1 produced a small, cell-restricted gene-abundance response, with 20 downstream FDR<0.10 hits across only 4 of 20 measured groups and 16 of those hits in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a ubiquitous transcriptional consequence of acute Ylpm1 loss in postmitotic neurons and focuses interpretation on a narrow midbrain-glutamatergic response.

literature_claim: YLPM1/ZAP3 is a nuclear PP1/RNA-binding-complex protein and nuclear speckles concentrate pre-mRNA splicing and processing factors.
main_caveats: Gene-level snRNA-seq cannot show that SRSF protein abundance, speckle composition, or alternative splicing changed.
summary: In 155 MB Glut, Ylpm1 loss lowered the SR splicing-factor transcripts Srsf6 and Srsf5 and raised Atxn2l.
why_it_matters: This is the only coherent RNA-processing signal in the Ylpm1 surface and is consistent with adaptation to a nuclear RNP perturbation rather than a global loss of splicing factors.

main_caveats: The genes are scattered E3 or ubiquitin-pathway components, not a measured proteasome-core induction.
summary: Responder cells showed a small ubiquitin-ligase arm: Shprh, Dcaf11, and Ube2o were up in 155 MB Glut, and Fbxl17 was up in 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
why_it_matters: The measured response is not solely an RNA-processing signature; it also nominates protein-turnover or E3-ligase remodeling as an acute adaptation to Ylpm1 loss.

main_caveats: No direct YLPM1-to-Inha mechanism is established here; 191 MB P MY GABA had only one downstream hit.
summary: Inha was down in both 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, making it the only recurrent downstream Ylpm1 FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: Recurrence across two independently tested responder groups makes Inha a compact candidate marker of the Ylpm1 state in midbrain / pons-medulla neuronal classes.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Zap3 regulates mTert and proliferation in embryonic stem cells, and YLPM1 loss promotes GIST proliferation, OXPHOS, and cell-cycle gene sets.
main_caveats: The screen was not designed to measure telomerase enzymatic activity or telomere length; the negative is for gene-level RNA abundance.
summary: The postnatal neuronal Ylpm1 perturbation did not induce the Tert, shelterin, or cell-cycle program expected from proliferative YLPM1 models.
why_it_matters: This uncouples the mouse in vivo postmitotic transcriptomic phenotype from the embryonic stem-cell telomerase phenotype and the GIST proliferation phenotype.

main_caveats: The Tpr and Setd1a calls use only the 20 Ylpm1 FDR<0.10 coordinates; full-profile Wilcoxon-score correlations were close to zero.
summary: The strongest data-derived Ylpm1 relationships were non-obvious: full-profile neighbors were very weak, whereas a restricted FDR-coordinate comparison selected Tpr as the top convergent perturbation and Setd1a as the top anti-neighbor.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation layer prevents over-assigning Ylpm1 to its textbook PP1 complex and identifies a narrow Tpr-like 155 MB Glut signature that would not be nominated from the canonical literature alone.

literature_claim: YLPM1/ZAP3 biochemically belongs to a nuclear PP1/RNA-binding complex, while SON is a nuclear-speckle scaffold whose loss should be more structural.
main_caveats: The direct ZAP3 partners KHDRBS1, ILF2, ILF3, NCOA5, RBMX, and PPP1CA were not present as perturbation targets, so the direct complex itself could not be phenotypically ordered.
summary: Canonical RNA-processing target perturbations were far broader than Ylpm1 and only partly overlapped its significant genes; Son did not phenocopy Ylpm1 in the matched groups.
why_it_matters: Ylpm1 behaves as a selective, buffered branch of nuclear RNP biology rather than as a core nuclear-speckle scaffold gene.

literature_claim: Perturbing nuclear RNP or speckle factors can be expected to produce secondary RNA-processing stress or compensation if the factor is limiting.
main_caveats: DNA indels and protein depletion were not measured, so the finding is buffering of the assayed RNA phenotype rather than proof of complete protein loss.
summary: Ylpm1 was significantly down at the transcript level in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but produced 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: These groups are internally controlled examples showing that a measurable Ylpm1 RNA decrease can be transcriptionally buffered in vivo.

literature_claim: Constitutive nervous-system YME1L loss in mice produces cell-type-restricted retinal and spinal phenotypes and does not cause broad brain atrophy or neuroinflammation, even though it changes mitochondrial substrate proteins.
main_caveats: The screen measures nuclear RNA in surviving NeuN-enriched brain nuclei only; DNA indels, YME1L protein, OPA1 isoforms, mitochondrial morphology, and axonal transport were not assayed.
summary: Yme1l1 loss did not create a robust cell-autonomous nuclear RNA signature in any recovered postmitotic brain neuron group.
why_it_matters: This is the central result for the perturbation: across recovered brain neurons the P16-to-P37/P44 mosaic CRISPR assay supports a pan-null FDR surface rather than a hidden cortical, GABAergic, thalamic, midbrain, or cerebellar responder.

literature_claim: YME1L normally processes OPA1 and YME1L loss alters OMA1-dependent OPA1 processing and mitochondrial shape in cells and nervous tissue.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic; post-translational OPA1 isoform changes after Yme1l1 editing could have occurred without creating an RNA signature.
summary: The YME1L-to-OPA1 biochemical edge was not transcriptionally transmitted: Opa1 was a robust comparator responder in matched cells, but Yme1l1 had zero shared FDR genes.
why_it_matters: Direct Opa1 perturbation proved that the assay can report a mitochondrial inner-membrane stress state, while upstream Yme1l1 perturbation did not phenocopy it; YME1L biology is therefore buffered or displaced rather than simply unreadable by the platform.

literature_claim: Mitochondrial defects can activate an ATF4/DDIT3 integrated-stress transcriptional program, but the path to ISR depends on the mitochondrial lesion and cellular metabolic state.
main_caveats: Absence is called only at the 3-4 week endpoint; transient ISR immediately after editing would not be captured.
summary: Yme1l1 did not induce the Opa1-like ATF4/ISR amino-acid program that the same screen detected through Asns, Ddit3, Chac1, Slc7a5, Cars, Mars1 and one-carbon genes after Opa1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: This gates the null away from a generic snRNA readout failure: a secondary mitochondrial ISR was measurable in matched neuronal groups, but Yme1l1 sat below that transcriptional threshold.

why_it_matters: The maximum whole-surface Wilcoxon-score correlation to any other target was only 0.0259, so the few nominal Yme1l1 ranks do not form a reproducible biological module that can be rescued by comparator analysis.
