literature_claim: Constitutional YWHAE/Ywhae loss is linked to abnormal brain development and 14-3-3 epsilon has established roles in neuronal migration and morphogenesis.
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic null only; indel burdens, 14-3-3 epsilon protein, phosphorylation, neuronal morphology, and cell abundance were not measured.
summary: Acute P16 Ywhae perturbation produced a pan-measured downstream transcriptomic null: no cell group had any non-Ywhae gene below FDR 0.10.
why_it_matters: The result refines a gene with strong developmental genetics by showing that sparse juvenile loss of one 14-3-3 epsilon allele product does not automatically create a nuclear-RNA stress, synaptic, or migration-remnant signature in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Mammalian 14-3-3 proteins are structurally related homo/heterodimeric scaffolds; epsilon, zeta, and gamma have brain-development roles, while isoforms can be both redundant and target-specific.
main_caveats: Only Ywhag and Ywhaz, not every 14-3-3 paralog, were represented as targets; DNA editing and 14-3-3 protein stoichiometry were not measured.
summary: The measured 14-3-3 paralogs Ywhag and Ywhaz also lacked a broad single-isoform downstream program, rather than converging with Ywhae on a shared neuronal RNA module.
why_it_matters: Ywhag showed stronger recurrent self-transcript depletion than Ywhae but still only one downstream FDR gene, so the family comparison argues for postmitotic 14-3-3 isoform buffering rather than a Ywhae-specific technical failure.

main_caveats: The assay tested mRNA abundance, not NDEL1 or DCX phosphorylation/stability, Rho-GTPase activity, F-actin, or neurite morphology.

literature_claim: No literature comparator was prespecified for this unbiased screen-wide search.
main_caveats: Cosine was computed over Wilcoxon score vectors; it is useful for rejecting large shared modules here but should not be interpreted as a phenotypic distance for non-transcriptional effects.
summary: A data-driven whole-universe neighbor search did not reveal a hidden Ywhae-like module: the strongest non-safe positive cosines were only +0.031 and +0.030 and the strongest non-safe anticorrelations were about -0.016.
why_it_matters: Cross-perturbation signal is therefore too small to nominate Timp3, Trappc9, Wdr26, or Tpr as mechanistic Ywhae partners in this assay; the null is global rather than being a missed named pathway.

literature_claim: 14-3-3 proteins participate in many phosphorylation-dependent signaling complexes and RAF-family links have been described at family level.

why_it_matters: The 14-3-3 scaffold surface in juvenile neurons is not equivalent to acute loss of a RAF kinase target, reinforcing that the Ywhae null should not be expanded into a generic MAPK claim.

why_it_matters: This preserves the only FDR<0.10 responder as a selective VGF/neurosecretory hypothesis instead of over-interpreting the rest of the flat surface.

literature_claim: 14-3-3ζ binds cytoskeletal and synaptic components in mouse hippocampus, while Pfn2 controls synaptic actin polymerization and vesicle exocytosis in mouse brain.
main_caveats: Single downstream gene at FDR 0.0598 from 34 perturbed nuclei; Pfn2 is an indirect actin/synaptic readout, not a proven direct YWHAZ client.

why_it_matters: The only FDR<0.10 event maps to a neuron-enriched actin regulator, fitting the literature that 14-3-3ζ mainly interfaces with cytoskeletal and synaptic protein machinery rather than launching a broad RNA stress state in postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: Mammalian 14-3-3 isoforms can heterodimerize and share survival-signaling clients such as BAD and FOXO-class proteins, but single isoform losses can also be compensated by the remaining isoforms.
main_caveats: Only Ywhae and Ywhag, not every 14-3-3 paralog, were targeted in this screen; the comparison is transcriptomic and not proteomic.
summary: The assayed 14-3-3 paralogs did not phenocopy each other after P16 CRISPR: Ywhaz, Ywhag, and Ywhae were all nearly flat, and their lone hits were in different cortical IT groups.
why_it_matters: Shared 14-3-3 clients do not translate into an interchangeable acute postnatal transcriptome; the family behaves as a buffered, isoform-specific phosphoscaffold system in this assay.

literature_claim: 14-3-3 proteins regulate RAF, AKT-FOXO, BAD, apoptosis, autophagy, and trafficking through phosphorylation-dependent binding events.
main_caveats: Absence is limited to mRNA secondaries over 3-4 weeks in surviving NeuN+ nuclei; phosphorylation, BAD/FOXO localization, and synaptic physiology were not assayed.
summary: Ywhaz did not induce the canonical apoptosis, FOXO/IEG, UPR/ISR, or autophagy/lysosome programs that might have been expected from a 14-3-3ζ signaling LoF.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates Ywhaz from phospho-signaling pathways that can produce transcriptional secondaries: Tsc2 loss strongly induced mTOR-lysosomal, metabolic, immediate-early, and apoptosis-related genes in the same analysis universe, whereas Ywhaz did not.

literature_claim: No a priori literature comparator was used for this screen-wide nearest-neighbor result.
main_caveats: The correlation is attenuated because the Ywhaz signature itself contains only one FDR<0.10 downstream gene.
summary: No data-driven non-safe perturbation converged strongly with Ywhaz across the whole measured signature.
why_it_matters: The Pfn2 hit is not embedded in a broad recurrent CRISPR state or a common transcriptomic module; the closest positive and negative neighbors had absolute feature-z-scored correlations of only about 0.02 and failed to copy Pfn2 in the responding group.

literature_claim: YY1 has strong developmental and glial functions in cortex, mid-hindbrain neuroepithelium, and oligodendrocyte progenitors.
main_caveats: The assay perturbed P16 NeuN+ postmitotic neurons, so it cannot rank embryonic progenitors or glia.
summary: Yy1 loss produced a posteriorly enriched neuronal transcriptome rather than a pan-neuronal response.
why_it_matters: The largest effects were in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, which together carried 83% of all significant Yy1 rows, whereas several cortical, hippocampal and inhibitory classes were flat or nearly flat.

literature_claim: YY1 can activate and repress transcription through promoter and enhancer binding.
main_caveats: The assay does not distinguish direct YY1 targets from secondary components of the recurrent response.
summary: A compact, recurrent YY1 core crossed many otherwise small responders.
why_it_matters: Wsb1 repression and the reciprocal up-regulation of Leng8, Drosha and Rnpc3 appeared across cortical, Pvalb, midbrain/thalamic and cerebellar groups, separating a shared YY1 axis from group-specific posterior modules.

literature_claim: YY1 DNA binding can help recruit Polycomb proteins through YAF2 and other cofactors.
main_caveats: Pcgf2 and Ring1 were measured as downstream transcripts, not perturbed comparators in this screen.
summary: Yy1 perturbation rewired Polycomb/chromatin transcripts with Pcgf2 down and Ring1 up instead of a uniform PRC shutdown.
why_it_matters: YY1 is biochemically connected to Polycomb recruitment, yet this postmitotic neuronal response changed PRC1-related genes in opposite directions, suggesting homeostatic balancing of chromatin regulators after Yy1 loss.

main_caveats: Functional consequences for miRNA processing or splicing were not measured.
summary: YY1 loss repeatedly affected RNA-processing genes.
why_it_matters: Drosha and Rnpc3 were recurrently induced while Tial1 and several splicing-associated factors were reduced, showing that the broad posterior response is not limited to chromatin genes.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The inference is transcriptomic; lysosomal and trafficking flux were not assayed.
summary: Posterior YY1 responders contained a vesicle and endolysosomal-trafficking arm.
why_it_matters: The coordinated Lman2l, Exoc4, Vps35l and Fig4 decreases with Bicd2, Stx16 and Lamtor4 increases point to organelle-trafficking adaptation after loss of a nuclear regulator.

literature_claim: Heterozygous YY1 disruption causes the neurodevelopmental Gabriele-de Vries syndrome.
main_caveats: The screen measured acute mouse neuronal nuclei, not human heterozygous development or physiology.
summary: Several broad responders down-regulated excitability and synaptic genes.
why_it_matters: GRIN, GRIK, GABA-receptor, neurexin, calcium-channel and acetylcholinesterase transcript losses provide a postmitotic neuronal route by which YY1 haploinsufficiency could impair circuit function, distinct from the better established progenitor-survival phenotype.

literature_claim: During embryonic cortical development, Yy1 maintains progenitor biosynthetic programs including metabolism and protein translation.
main_caveats: Ribosomal transcripts can be sparse in snRNA-seq, but the broad posterior signatures were large enough to detect many other nuclear-encoded metabolic genes.
summary: The postnatal Yy1 metabolic response did not recapitulate the embryonic ribosome/biosynthetic collapse.
why_it_matters: Embryonic cortical Yy1 loss is expected to impair protein synthesis and metabolism; here mitochondrial and metabolic transcripts changed in both directions and no cytosolic or mitochondrial ribosomal protein genes crossed FDR<0.10, localizing that canonical biosynthetic requirement to a different developmental window.

literature_claim: Stronger YY1 loss can impair homologous recombination and, in embryonic mid-hindbrain neuroepithelium, provoke cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis.
main_caveats: The measured cell-cycle/DNA-repair genes are surrogate transcripts; DNA damage, indels and apoptosis were not assayed.
summary: Postmitotic Yy1 loss induced a small chromosomal/DNA-repair-like signal without a p53-Cdkn1a arrest signature.
why_it_matters: This separates the Yy1-INO80 genome-stability literature from the apoptotic neuroepithelial knockout phenotype: the P16 neuronal perturbation exposed Hjurp/Rad51c/Smc2/Cdc7 changes but not a robust Cdkn1a, Bax, Bbc3 or Pmaip1 response.

literature_claim: YY1 disease biology is rooted in transcriptional and chromatin dysregulation, but YY2 and Polycomb core factors were not represented as perturbation targets in the parquet.
main_caveats: The convergence is a sparse FDR-overlap metric dominated by posterior responsive groups.
summary: Data-driven signature search placed Yy1 closest to BRD4/CHD8/PHF12/WAC/ADNP-class chromatin perturbations, not to a measured YY1 paralog or PRC core member.
why_it_matters: The strongest high-purity overlaps were with Brd4, Chd8, Phf12, Wac, Adnp and Arid1a, suggesting that the acute Yy1 neuronal state shares a disease-chromatin module with several unrelated chromatin regulators.

main_caveats: Psmb4 and Psmc1 had very broad signatures, so overlap counts are inflated by signature size and are less specific than the Brd4/Chd8 overlaps.
summary: Proteasome-subunit perturbations were the top broad, non-textbook positive sparse neighbors of Yy1.
why_it_matters: Psmb4 and Psmc1 shared hundreds of significant Yy1 features, but only about two thirds were same-direction, so the relationship is best read as convergence onto a broad secondary stress/proteostasis surface rather than a clean YY1 phenocopy.

literature_claim: YY1 belongs to a broad chromatin/transcriptional regulatory space, not a single linear pathway.
main_caveats: Divergence is computed from shared significant cell-gene features and does not prove direct regulatory antagonism.
summary: SETD1A, ZBTB7A, THOC1 and SIN3A diverged from Yy1 despite hitting the same posterior groups.
why_it_matters: The negative sparse neighbors shared many Yy1 features but usually in the opposite direction, proving that large thalamic/midbrain DE alone does not guarantee convergence and sharpening Yy1's direction within the chromatin/RNA-regulator landscape.

literature_claim: YY1 is an enhancer-looping and chromatin regulator, making CTCF and chromatin co-regulators plausible comparators a priori.
main_caveats: Absence of convergence can reflect weak engagement for some comparators; it is not a statement about their embryonic loss-of-function phenotypes.
summary: ASH1L, EP300, KMT2A, CREBBP and CTCF did not phenocopy Yy1 in the same assay universe.
why_it_matters: This rejects the trivial model that any chromatin or 3D-genome perturbation gives the Yy1 posterior signature; some plausible literature comparators were flat or weakly overlapping when measured with the same controls and cell taxonomy.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

literature_claim: ZBTB10/RINZF encodes a nuclear C2H2/BTB-domain transcriptional regulator, a class often used for DNA binding and transcriptional repression.
main_caveats: No DNA indel calls or protein measurements are available; the conclusion is limited to basal snRNA-seq 3-4 weeks after sparse P16 AAV-PHP.eB CRISPR perturbation.
summary: Zbtb10 CRISPR loss produced no robust downstream transcriptome in any recovered postmitotic neuronal class.
why_it_matters: A BTB-ZF transcriptional regulator can be measurably present yet transcriptionally dispensable in the juvenile-to-young-adult neuronal states tested; the absence is broad enough to be interpreted as a context-specific negative result rather than a single underpowered cell-type failure.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: RINZF/ZBTB10 can interfere with Sp1 activation at the gastrin CACC element, and ZBTB10 overexpression in MDA-MB-231 cells decreases Sp1, Sp3, Sp4, VEGF, VEGFR1, and survivin.
main_caveats: Loss-of-function in neurons is the reciprocal perturbation of overexpression or miR-27a inhibition in proliferating cancer cells; protein-level Sp activity was not measured.
summary: The cancer-derived ZBTB10/RINZF-Sp angiogenic/survival circuit was not derepressed in postnatal neurons.
why_it_matters: If the breast-cancer and gastrin-promoter circuit were operating in these neurons, loss of a ZBTB10 Sp repressor should have moved Sp1, Sp3, Sp4 or Sp-dependent survival/angiogenic targets; those RNAs were detected by the assay but none had FDR<0.10 in any measured group.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

literature_claim: ZBTB proteins share BTB and C2H2-zinc-finger architecture but have diverse dimerization choices and target repertoires.
main_caveats: Zbtb11, Zfp131, Zbtb4 and Bcl6 were not represented as perturbation targets, so the family comparison is restricted to the ZBTB genes present in the parquet.
summary: The ZBTB-family comparison separates Zbtb10 from the broad Zbtb7a neuronal program and from smaller Zbtb18/Zbtb38 effects.
why_it_matters: Family membership did not predict a shared postmitotic-neuron signature: Zbtb7a produced 2639 matched FDR<0.10 DE calls and Zbtb18/Zbtb38 produced sparse Pxdn/Msra/Rcn2 responses, whereas Zbtb10, Zbtb16, Zbtb20, and Zbtb21 were flat over matched groups.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Cosine similarity was calculated over Wilcoxon-score vectors; because Zbtb10 has no robust DE genes, the ranking is useful mainly as a guard against missed convergence, not for mechanistic naming.
summary: An unbiased score-vector search found no meaningful phenocopy or anti-phenocopy for Zbtb10.
why_it_matters: The flatness is not hiding a coherent sub-FDR module shared with another perturbation: the strongest non-safe positive and negative neighbors had absolute cosine similarity no larger than 0.034, and their own FDR<0.10 surfaces were flat or nearly flat.

literature_claim: Zbtb16/PLZF is a DNA-binding transcriptional regulator with strong neural phenotypes when removed from embryonic progenitor contexts.
main_caveats: DNA indels and PLZF protein depletion were not measured; no Zbtb16 rows were recovered in 215 MB Dopa; sparse PVH/ARC or non-neuronal effects could be diluted or absent from the assayed nuclei.
summary: Acute P16 Zbtb16 loss produced a genome-wide transcriptional zero across the recovered neuronal brain surface.
why_it_matters: Zbtb16 encodes a nuclear DNA-binding transcriptional regulator, so a flat 22-cell-group snRNA-seq surface is a biologically meaningful postmitotic buffering result rather than a target-gene-expression QC failure.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: PLZF acts in embryonic forebrain, spinal-cord, and hindbrain progenitors to tune proneural, FGFR3/STAT3, Fgf, and deep-layer cortical programs; germline Zbtb16 deletion reduces Tbr1-positive layer-6 neurons.
main_caveats: The assay perturbed after corticogenesis in broad cell groups; absence of a postmitotic maintenance signature does not test embryonic progenitor abundance or earlier fate specification.
summary: The embryonic deep-layer-corticogenesis and FGF-neural-progenitor program is not reactivated by Zbtb16 CRISPR in juvenile postmitotic forebrain neurons.
why_it_matters: The result separates a known germline cortical-size and layer-6 liability from an acute requirement for Zbtb16 to maintain P16-P44 projection-neuron transcriptional identity.

literature_claim: Adult Zbtb16 is induced by cold, fasting, and glucoprivation in PVH and ARC through glucocorticoid signaling, and local knockdown alters cold thermogenesis, glycemic control, and food intake.
main_caveats: The pertinent PVH and ARC populations are sparse within coarse taxonomy groups, and the screen did not impose cold, fasting, glucoprivation, or glucocorticoid challenge.
summary: The adult PVH/ARC energy-deficit axis was not captured as a basal Zbtb16 transcriptional response in the hypothalamus-containing groups.
why_it_matters: Zbtb16 can be a glucocorticoid- and energy-deficit-responsive hypothalamic regulator, but the screen shows that removing it in unstimulated juvenile NeuN-positive cells is not sufficient to trigger a detectable PVH/ARC secondary program.

literature_claim: PLZF can repress transcription by recruiting SMRT, Sin3A, HDAC, and N-CoR corepressor complexes through its BTB/POZ architecture.
main_caveats: The parquet includes Sin3a, Hdac5, and Hdac8 but not every canonical PLZF-associated HDAC or nuclear receptor corepressor, so the contrast localizes absence to the measured chromatin comparators.
summary: PLZF-linked Sin3/HDAC repression is not rate-limited by Zbtb16 in these postmitotic neurons.
why_it_matters: Direct PLZF biochemistry would make Sin3A/HDAC biology an obvious place to look; the measured Sin3a surface was broad whereas Zbtb16 was completely flat, arguing that any Sin3A-dependent neuronal transcription is driven by other DNA-binding factors in this assay.

literature_claim: ZBTB16/PLZF belongs to the BTB/POZ zinc-finger transcription-factor family, whose members share repressor-domain architecture but have context-specific DNA binding and cofactors.
main_caveats: Zbtb7a and Sin3a are broad positive controls for perturbability, not mechanistic phenocopies of Zbtb16; Zbtb21 was represented in only 21 of the 22 matched groups.
summary: BTB-ZF factors are not interchangeable in the neuronal screen: Zbtb7a was a broad responder, Zbtb18/Zbtb38 were weakly focal, and Zbtb16/Zbtb20/Zbtb10/Zbtb21 were flat.
why_it_matters: The family-level contrast rules out the idea that a shared BTB-ZF domain architecture is enough to predict a CRISPR snRNA-seq phenotype in juvenile neurons.

literature_claim: No literature prior was used to nominate these neighbors; they came from a full cross-perturbation score-correlation scan.
main_caveats: Correlations involving a zero-gene Zbtb16 surface quantify residual rank noise rather than mechanistic convergence.
summary: The unbiased signature-neighbor search found no coherent positive or negative Zbtb16 module.
why_it_matters: The strongest Wilcoxon-score correlations to every other target were close to zero and the named neighbors themselves had no multi-gene signatures, anchoring the interpretation of Zbtb16 as a null target rather than as a member of an unexpected hidden module.

literature_claim: PXDN/peroxidasin catalyzes collagen IV crosslinking in basement membranes, but it is not a canonical Zbtb18 embryonic-neurogenesis effector.
main_caveats: Pxdn alone is a marker, not a full ECM module; snRNA-seq does not measure collagen IV crosslinks or peroxidasin activity.
summary: Zbtb18 loss induced a recurrent Pxdn-positive extracellular-matrix marker in only four of 22 measured cell groups.
why_it_matters: Pxdn is the only gene that recurred across Zbtb18 responders, shifting the postnatal readout away from the expected cortical fate genes toward a sparse basement-membrane/peroxidase-associated marker.

literature_claim: Pxdn, Clstn2, Man2a2, and Endou have annotated ECM, synaptic-adhesion, glycan-processing, and RNA-endoribonuclease functions, respectively, but no prior source links this exact four-gene cassette to Zbtb18 in thalamic neurons.
main_caveats: The program is only four genes; Endou is biologically isolated from the other three and should be treated as a marker until functionally tested.
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut responder added Endou, Clstn2, and Man2a2 to the shared Pxdn response.
why_it_matters: This quartet nominates 151 as the clearest postnatal Zbtb18-sensitive state and suggests a small secretory/RNA-processing, synaptic-adhesion, and N-glycan remodeling response rather than a restart of a broad proneurogenic program.

literature_claim: Embryonic RP58/Zbtb18 represses Ngn2/Neurog2, NeuroD1, Rnd2, Id2 and additional non-neuronal programs during cortical differentiation and migration.
main_caveats: The experiment does not sequence DNA indels, so it cannot distinguish complete LoF survivors from weakly edited nuclei; however the absence spans measured expected genes, not just Zbtb18 self-expression.
summary: Postnatal Zbtb18 loss did not derepress the expected Pax6/Neurog2/Neurod1/Rnd2/Id cortical-neurogenesis program.
why_it_matters: The negative result is mechanistically informative: the P16 mosaic assay perturbs neurons after the embryonic RP58 rheostat that regulates proneurogenic genes and migration effectors has largely executed.

literature_claim: Zbtb18 is a BTB/POZ zinc-finger transcription factor, making other ZBTB targets obvious same-family comparators, but the literature does not predict this thalamic Zbtb7a-Zbtb18 convergence.
main_caveats: The overlap is restricted to three thalamic genes and Zbtb7a itself has a much broader DE surface than Zbtb18.
summary: Zbtb7a, not the textbook Zbtb16/Zbtb20 family comparators, was the top same-direction Zbtb18 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The measurable ZBTB-family comparison argues against simple family interchangeability: Zbtb7a was a broad responder that partially converged on the 151 Pxdn/Clstn2/Man2a2 branch, whereas Zbtb16 and Zbtb20 were flat in all matched groups.

literature_claim: No Zbtb18-specific literature was found that predicts Rora, Ctnnb1, or Ehmt1 to control this exact four-gene thalamic signature.
main_caveats: The ranking is based on only seven Zbtb18 significant gene-by-cell features; Rora Endou was FDR=0.0625 and therefore a weak but signed member of the two-gene opposite overlap.
summary: Rora and Ctnnb1 opposed separable branches of the 151 Zbtb18 signature, while Ehmt1 shared only Endou up-regulation.
why_it_matters: The strongest negative neighbors were not cortical Zbtb18-network factors; they route through the same thalamic marker genes in the opposite direction, making the 151 state a compact convergence/divergence node for otherwise unrelated perturbations.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Tbr1 is part of the embryonic corticothalamic/subcerebral layer-identity network with Fezf2.
main_caveats: Only counts, not the full Tbr1 program, were compared; the finding separates assay detectability from Zbtb18 timing but does not define the Tbr1 mechanism.
summary: Tbr1 stayed transcriptionally active in several postnatal cortical groups where Zbtb18 was flat.
why_it_matters: This rules out a blanket explanation that all cortical developmental transcription factors are invisible in the assay: Tbr1 produced 28 FDR<0.10 genes across matched groups, including L5-6 IT and NP-CT-L6b-OB groups in which Zbtb18 produced none.

literature_claim: Pathogenic human ZBTB18 variants are associated with intellectual disability and frequent brain-structure abnormalities, and experimental work places Zbtb18 in embryonic transcription-factor circuits.
main_caveats: AAV CRISPR LoF is not a heterozygous germline patient allele and cannot test dominant missense gain-of-binding or altered-specificity mechanisms.
summary: Juvenile mosaic Zbtb18 LoF produced a sparse marker response rather than a transcriptomic model of ZBTB18-related malformation disease.
why_it_matters: Human ZBTB18 disease is dominated by neurodevelopmental structural and cognitive phenotypes; this dataset suggests that the adult-like neuronal consequences of acute P16 LoF are residual and cell-type-selective, so the disease mechanism should remain anchored to embryonic fate specification and migration unless an allele is known to act postmitotically.

literature_claim: Most Zbtb20 brain roles described in mouse are embryonic hippocampal or cortical specification and gliogenesis programs rather than pan-neuronal maintenance programs at P37-P44.
main_caveats: The assay does not measure DNA indels or electrophysiology; the flat self-transcript is expected for this CRISPR platform and does not prove lack of functional cutting.
summary: Sparse P16 Zbtb20 loss was transcriptionally buffered across every neuronal cell group recovered for this target: 22 measured groups and 371,796 downstream Wilcoxon tests produced zero genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The result is a real negative surface, not just a weak signal in one class; it says that Zbtb20 does not acutely re-open its large developmental fate programs in juvenile-to-young-adult neurons under this mosaic CRISPR design.

literature_claim: Embryonic Zbtb20 directly represses isocortical projection-neuron transcription factors during CA1 fate acquisition and collaborates with Sox9/NFIA during astrocytogenesis.
main_caveats: The grouped hippocampal cluster is not purified CA1, and Fezf2 and Tle4 were measured only as transcripts, not as perturbation targets.
summary: The expected Zbtb20 CA1/isocortical repression module was absent: Cux1, Cux2, Fezf2, Foxp2, Mef2c, Rorb, Satb2, Sox5, Tbr1, Tle4 and Zfpm2, together with CA1 or gliogenic markers, had 0 of 396 Zbtb20 tests at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Zbtb20 can bind and repress these projection-neuron determinants during CA1 development, so their failure to de-repress after a P16 perturbation localizes that regulatory circuit to the developmental specification window rather than to stable juvenile neuronal identity maintenance detectable by snRNA-seq.

main_caveats: A cosine comparison cannot exclude a CA1-subcluster effect that was diluted below the cell-group DE surface.
summary: Unbiased signature search found no meaningful Zbtb20 neighbor: after group-by-gene standardization across the full parquet, the top cosine similarities were Snta1 0.018, Scamp5 0.016 and Gucy2e 0.016, and the most negative was Gabra3 -0.017.
why_it_matters: The nominal Zbtb20 ranks do not hide a coherent low-amplitude module that recurs under other perturbations; the screen-wide comparison collapses the putative Zbtb20 signature to noise-scale correlations.

literature_claim: Zbtb20 is part of a BTB-ZF transcription-factor family and its embryonic program intersects multiple projection-neuron and astrocyte fate factors.
main_caveats: Zbtb7a is a family comparator, not a one-to-one Zbtb20 paralog; overlap is assessed only by FDR DE at the coarse cell-group level.
summary: The screen could detect related transcription-factor perturbations in the same matched cell groups, but they did not converge with Zbtb20: Zbtb7a produced 2,639 FDR<0.10 genes and Mef2c, Prox1 and Tbr1 produced 109, 64 and 28 respectively across the 22 Zbtb20-matched groups, whereas Zbtb20 produced zero.
why_it_matters: This rejects the technical explanation that all BTB-zinc-finger or cortical fate-factor perturbations were generically silent; the flat surface is specific to postmitotic Zbtb20 loss rather than to the target class as a whole.

literature_claim: Primrose syndrome arises from heterozygous pathogenic ZBTB20 variants, and Primrose-associated missense variants in the DNA-binding domain have been interpreted as dominant negative rather than simple nulls.
main_caveats: The screen is not an allele-resolved disease model and does not assay cortical progenitors or astrocytes.
summary: The null surface is consistent with Primrose-syndrome biology being poorly modeled by simple postnatal neuronal LoF: the disease is linked to heterozygous ZBTB20 variants, many described as dominant-negative missense alleles, while the assay introduces sparse CRISPR LoF after neuronal specification.
why_it_matters: A therapeutic or disease-model screen that wants ZBTB20 biology should perturb embryonic cortical/hippocampal or astroglial contexts, or introduce the human allelic mechanism, rather than expect a strong P37-P44 neuronal transcriptomic signature from P16 LoF.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Developmental and Down-syndrome studies predict that changing ZBTB21 can affect neural patterning or CRE-dependent synaptic gene expression.
main_caveats: DNA editing and protein depletion were not measured; the assay perturbed normal postmitotic neurons rather than embryos or trisomic neurons.
summary: Zbtb21 loss produced no robust downstream snRNA-seq signature in any of the 21 measured neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: The main phenotype is a real absence of a basal postnatal transcriptional response, not a hidden signal in one cortical or inhibitory subclass: every tested group had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite 1,257 total Zbtb21-perturbed nuclei across groups.

literature_claim: ZBTB21 antagonizes CREB/CBP-p300-dependent CRE transcription and can cooperate with cohesin- or ZBTB-associated chromatin regulation.
main_caveats: The most direct ZBTB partners, Zbtb14/Zfp161 and Zbtb7b, were not represented as perturbation targets; overlap is assessed at the snRNA DE level, not by chromatin occupancy.
summary: CREB/CBP and cohesin/ZBTB comparators were not globally inert, so the Zbtb21 zero is pathway-selective rather than a universal failure of these cell groups to respond to transcriptional or chromatin regulators.
why_it_matters: In matched groups, Creb1, Crebbp, Smc1a, Stag2, and Zbtb7a each produced FDR<0.10 genes where Zbtb21 did not, including the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class. Thus Zbtb21 loss does not recapitulate the broader CREB/coactivator, cohesin, or ZBTB-family perturbation surfaces measured in the same analysis universe.

main_caveats: Because Zbtb21 itself has no FDR<0.10 genes, this conclusion is about the weakness of whole-vector neighbor statistics, not evidence that Klhl20 or Fbxo11 are mechanistic relatives.
summary: A prior-free full-universe neighbor search found no convincing positive or negative Zbtb21 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top score-correlation neighbors were Klhl20 in the same direction and Fbxo11 in the opposite direction, but the absolute correlations were tiny and those targets had only two and one FDR<0.10 genes, respectively; Zbtb21 therefore did not nominate a robust hidden convergent module.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: ZBTB38/CIBZ is a methyl-CpG-associated zinc-finger/BTB transcription factor whose loss perturbs proliferation, replication, and early embryonic Nanog/Sox2 programs in proliferative contexts.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not assayed, and a protein-truncating indel can leave Zbtb38 mRNA unchanged; the robust downstream surface is nevertheless genuinely sparse.
summary: P16 CRISPR loss of Zbtb38 produced a sparse postmitotic neuronal transcriptome: only 3 downstream FDR<0.10 genes distributed across 2 of 22 measured cell groups, with every self-transcript test at FDR=1.0.
why_it_matters: Zbtb38 is an essential methyl-CpG-linked developmental regulator in other systems, so the near-flat juvenile neuronal DE surface is itself a stage-refining result rather than a failed knockdown call.

literature_claim: USP9X-stabilized ZBTB38 limits ROS toxicity, and MSRA repairs methionine-sulfoxide oxidative protein damage.
main_caveats: The program is only two genes; Abhd12b function is predicted and the screen did not directly measure ROS, oxidized proteins, or lipids.
summary: The clearest responder was a small 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut up-signature containing Msra and Abhd12b.
why_it_matters: Msra up-regulation gives a cell-restricted hint that loss of the ZBTB38 methyl-reader can be met by oxidative-protein repair in thalamic glutamatergic neurons, concordant with prior evidence that the USP9X/ZBTB38 axis buffers reactive oxygen species.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: ERC-55/reticulocalbin is an endoplasmic-reticulum EF-hand calcium-binding protein.
main_caveats: This is a singleton FDR gene; canonical UPR/ISR genes were not part of the FDR<0.10 Zbtb38 response.
summary: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut showed an isolated Rcn2 up-regulation.
why_it_matters: Rcn2 encodes an ER-lumen EF-hand calcium-binding reticulocalbin, making this a narrow ER/calcium-handling marker candidate rather than evidence for a full unfolded-protein response.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: The conclusion is restricted to the Wilcoxon-score cosine and FDR-overlap metrics over this parquet.
summary: Whole-surface score neighbors were essentially at the noise floor and did not share any responder genes in the two Zbtb38 effect groups.
why_it_matters: The best data-nominated positive neighbors, Kcnab2 and Ndufb9, and the best negative neighbors, Prr12 and Hbs1l, are not interpretable as a convergent or anti-convergent Zbtb38 module.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: ZBTB38 belongs to the zinc-finger/BTB class of transcriptional regulators, motivating but not guaranteeing family-level phenocopy tests.
main_caveats: The closest methyl-CpG ZBTB paralogs Zbtb4 and Zbtb33/Kaiso were not target perturbations in the parquet.
summary: Represented BTB-ZF family perturbations did not phenocopy Zbtb38; Zbtb7a was a broad neuronal responder yet had a whole-surface cosine of -0.0004 with Zbtb38 and no shared Rcn2/Msra/Abhd12b FDR genes.
why_it_matters: The sparse Zbtb38 response is not a generic zinc-finger/BTB perturbation state, and broad family responders can be orthogonal to Zbtb38 even in the matched thalamic group.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: CIBZ/Zbtb38 can recruit CtBP and, in embryonic stem or epiblast contexts, supports G1/S progression and Nanog/Sox2 expression.
main_caveats: RBBP6, MCM10, USP9X, ZBTB4, and ZBTB33 were not represented as perturbation targets, so their convergence could only be assessed through downstream genes and represented indirect relatives.
summary: The expected methyl-CpG/CtBP and embryonic Sox2/Nanog axes were uncoupled from the observed P16 neuronal Zbtb38 signature.
why_it_matters: Ctbp1 and Sox2 perturbations were directly testable and had small TH responses, and Mecp2 responded in TH, but none converged on the three Zbtb38 genes; canonical targets including Nanog, Sox2, Mcm10, Xiap, Cdkn1a, Cdkn1c, Il1r2, Myog, T, and Mesp1 also stayed non-significant after Zbtb38 perturbation.

literature_claim: ZBTB7A/LRF is a BTB/POZ zinc-finger transcription factor with highly context-dependent transcriptional outputs across developmental, blood, lymphoid, metabolic, and chromatin programs.
main_caveats: The self-transcript was not FDR-significantly depleted in any group, so DNA-level indel formation is inferred only indirectly; small signatures in hippocampal, Sst, CTX-CGE, Dopa, and cerebellar groups should not be over-interpreted gene by gene.
summary: Zbtb7a loss was a broad but graded postmitotic neuronal perturbation: 22 of 23 measured groups had at least one downstream FDR<0.10 gene, whereas 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA was the only FDR-level nonresponder.
why_it_matters: A transcription factor famous for blood, lymphoid, and tumor contexts still produced an acute cell-autonomous neuronal RNA state after P16 delivery; the biology is therefore not limited to embryonic fate specification or non-neuronal lineages.

literature_claim: ZBTB7A can repress glycolytic genes including PFKP and GLUT3/SLC2A3 in cancer cells, and ZBTB7A loss can alter glycolytic versus oxidative metabolism.
main_caveats: Only a small subset of glycolytic genes reached FDR<0.10, and neuronal snRNA-seq cannot directly measure glycolytic flux.
summary: The cancer-cell glycolysis target axis was recovered only partially: Pfkp and Slc2a3 were de-repressed in the strongest thalamic/Pvalb responders, with Eno2 recurrently up, but the full HK2/PKM-like Warburg cassette was not a pan-neuronal output.
why_it_matters: This separates a conserved direction of ZBTB7A transcriptional repression from the proliferative metabolic state in which it was discovered.

main_caveats: Gene functions are inferred from marker membership; the assay did not measure lysosomal proteolysis, GPCR trafficking, or organelle morphology directly.
summary: Zbtb7a loss rewired endomembrane and lysosome-related transcripts, with Rab34/Cd63/Gaa/Ctsl/Gprasp1/2 recurrently up and Stx16/Ppip5k1/Gpr108/Tspan17/Tmem106c/P2rx4 recurrently down.
why_it_matters: The dominant RNA response is not a single canonical ZBTB7A effector but a membrane-trafficking compensation that plausibly changes receptor and lysosomal handling in mature neurons.

literature_claim: Heterozygous ZBTB7A variants cause a human neurodevelopmental syndrome with intellectual disability and macrocephaly.
main_caveats: RNA shifts are not electrophysiology; several genes move in opposite synaptic directions, so the result supports synaptic remodeling rather than a simple gain or loss of synapses.
summary: A synaptic and excitability layer accompanied the trafficking response: Cacng7, Syn1, Atp8a2, Dnm1, and Kcnab/Kcn channel genes fell in high responders, while Akap5, Nlgn2, Stx1a, and Ptprn rose in selected classes.
why_it_matters: Human ZBTB7A variants are syndromic and developmental, but the screen shows that acute loss in already postmitotic mouse neurons can still perturb transcripts for synaptic vesicles, AMPA-receptor auxiliary subunits, ion channels, and postsynaptic anchoring.

main_caveats: The evidence is transcriptomic and concentrated in a subset of classes; peptide processing or secretion was not assayed.
summary: High Zbtb7a responders acquired a neurosecretory/peptidergic component, led by Vgf, Pnoc, Ptprn, and Stx1a in thalamic, Pvalb, MGE, CTX-CGE, and midbrain groups.
why_it_matters: This program is cell-type-restricted and secondary to the recurrent Gpc1/Pnma3/Pnck core, showing that the same Zbtb7a knockout couples to different effector genes in different neuronal lineages.

literature_claim: UBA5 and UFC1 are consecutive enzymes in the UFM1 conjugation cascade, a pathway tied to ER proteostasis and UBA5-associated developmental encephalopathy.
main_caveats: The UFMylation link is co-signature evidence; Zbtb7a is not known to encode a UFMylation component, and classic UPR markers were limited rather than globally induced.
summary: The nearest FDR-backed positive signatures were not ZBTB7A paralogs but UFMylation/proteostasis perturbations: Uba5 and Ufc1, with Tpr as another broad positive neighbor, shared hundreds of Zbtb7a-directional genes.
why_it_matters: This cross-perturbation result nominates proteostasis and RNA/endomembrane stress as the dataset-nearest biology for neuronal Zbtb7a loss, independent of the erythroid and glycolysis literature priors.

literature_claim: In erythroid cells, LRF/ZBTB7A and BCL11A independently repress fetal globin, and LRF acts through a NuRD repressor mechanism.
main_caveats: The screen targeted only Chd4, Gatad2b, and Mbd2 among many possible NuRD subunits; a weak Chd4 match in one thalamic group could reflect shared chromatin remodeling rather than the globin-silencing complex itself.
summary: Canonical fetal-globin partners did not phenocopy Zbtb7a in neurons: Chd4 weakly overlapped in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Bcl11a, Bcl11b, Mbd2, and Gatad2b were essentially flat.
why_it_matters: The directly measured negative relatives prevent over-assigning the adult neuronal signature to the LRF/BCL11A/NuRD architecture defined in erythroid globin silencing.

literature_claim: ZBTB7A has been linked to ARF/p53 regulation, cancer-cell survival and apoptosis, HSP90/KLHL20-dependent protein stability, and metabolic regulation in proliferative systems.
main_caveats: A single p53-associated gene, Ccng1, was induced in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, so complete p53 inactivity cannot be inferred biochemically.
summary: The postnatal neuronal response was uncoupled from the classic ARF/p53/MYC and HSP90-KLHL20 circuitry: Trp53, Cdkn2a, Myc, Hsp90ab1, Klhl20, Pparg, and Ppargc1a perturbations were flat or near-flat and did not reconstruct the Zbtb7a surface.
why_it_matters: Zbtb7a LoF in juvenile neurons is not simply a p53-on or tumor-metabolism state, even though those axes dominate many proliferative-cell studies.

main_caveats: The negative-neighbor analysis is restricted to Zbtb7a significant genes and should be read as a signature contrast, not as direct biochemical antagonism.
summary: The top negative neighbors Chd8 and Yy1 inverted parts of the Zbtb7a signature, most visibly for Usp11, Wsb1, Rsrp1, and Ache, arguing that Zbtb7a is not a generic chromatin-factor loss-of-function response.
why_it_matters: Opposite signatures among transcriptional regulators are as informative as convergence: they show that the recurrent Gpc1/Usp11/Stx16 program is directional and target-specific within the same screen.

literature_claim: Human, fly and mouse studies identify ZC3H14/dNab2 as a conserved neuronal RNA-binding protein required for brain function.
main_caveats: The DE readout is gene-level nuclear RNA 3-4 weeks after a mosaic P16 perturbation, so it does not assay poly(A)-tail length or synaptic protein abundance directly.
summary: Zc3h14 loss produced a narrow, postmitotic steady-state RNA response in only five of 21 measured neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: This refines a broadly expressed intellectual-disability RNA-binding protein into a much more cell-state-restricted snRNA-seq phenotype at P37-44: most groups had no FDR<0.10 downstream gene, while 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut carried the multi-gene core of the response.

literature_claim: ZC3H14 controls poly(A)-tail length, interacts with THO/TREX, and can act antagonistically to PABPN1/PAXT in nuclear RNA surveillance.
main_caveats: The strongest claim is the direction of Pabpn1/Cstf2 transcript feedback; the dataset does not measure PABPN1 protein, RNA export, tail length or lncRNA surveillance.
summary: The two strongest responder glutamatergic groups changed RNA-maturation genes in the direction of a compact nuclear poly(A)/3′-processing feedback.
why_it_matters: Pabpn1 repression in both multi-gene responders and Cstf2 repression in 155 MB Glut place another nuclear poly(A)-binding factor and the cleavage-stimulation machinery downstream of Zc3h14 rather than recovering the broad target-mRNA losses expected from complete disruption of RNA surveillance.

literature_claim: No prior ZC3H14-Zcchc18 relationship was identified.
main_caveats: Zcchc18 is a marker, not a proven effector, in this dataset.
summary: Zcchc18 was the recurrent positive marker of the Zc3h14 response.
why_it_matters: Among only 14 FDR<0.10 target-derived gene×cell hits, Zcchc18 was induced in all three midbrain/thalamic effect groups, making it the cleanest measured candidate marker of postnatal Zc3h14 perturbation.

literature_claim: V-ATPase subunits acidify intracellular organelles and TRAPP complexes mediate vesicular trafficking, including trafficking steps linked to autophagy.
main_caveats: Only two trafficking-associated genes were significant, both in one cell class.
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response included a small endomembrane acidification/trafficking branch.
why_it_matters: Atp6v0b and Trappc14 up-regulation links the strongest Zc3h14 responder to V-ATPase/TRAPP vesicle biology, but direct V-ATPase or TRAPP subunit perturbations did not reproduce this module, arguing that the branch is secondary compensation rather than a generic organelle-acidification loss phenotype.

literature_claim: Mouse Zc3h14 loss alters expression of synaptic proteins, and Agrin has reported roles in CNS synaptic development, plasticity and signaling.
main_caveats: The dataset measures Agrn mRNA only; no Agrin protein, extracellular matrix or synapse morphology was assayed.
summary: Zc3h14 decreased Agrn in midbrain glutamatergic neurons but did not reproduce a canonical Agrn-Lrp4-MuSK pathway signature.
why_it_matters: The Agrn hit connects the perturbation to a synaptic extracellular-matrix organizer in a cell group with robust RNA-processing changes, extending prior synaptic-protein work beyond Dlg4/Mapt clients; flat Lrp4 and Musk perturbations argue that Agrn loss is a Zc3h14-linked downstream marker, not wholesale phenocopy of Agrn receptor signaling.

literature_claim: INHA encodes the inhibin alpha subunit, part of the activin/inhibin branch of the TGF-β superfamily.
main_caveats: This is a one-gene branch with no measured downstream activin/inhibin pathway response.
summary: Inha induction nominates a single-cell-state neuroendocrine/TGF-β-family output of Zc3h14 loss in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Inha was the second strongest midbrain-glutamatergic hit, separating the 155 MB Glut response from the 151 thalamic RNA-processing module and suggesting that Zc3h14 loss can couple RNA-processing perturbation to secreted-ligand state changes.

literature_claim: No direct Wdr26-Zc3h14 relationship was identified before the dataset comparison.
main_caveats: Neighbor ranking used the 14 Zc3h14 FDR features; Wdr26 has a much broader signature than Zc3h14, so the convergence is module-level, not a full phenocopy.
summary: Wdr26, not a canonical ZC3H14 partner, was the top positive data-driven neighbor and shared the midbrain Zcchc18/Pabpn1/Cstf2 module.
why_it_matters: The strongest cross-perturbation convergence came from an unbiased whole-universe search rather than from the THO/TREX or Fragile-X priors, pointing to a broader neuronal RNA-processing state that can be reached by unrelated perturbations.

literature_claim: ZC3H14 physically interacts with THO/TREX factors and loss of either ZC3H14 or THOC1/THOC5 extends bulk poly(A) tails in neuronal cells.
main_caveats: Only Thoc1 and Ddx39b were target perturbations in the parquet; Thoc5 and Alyref were not target perturbations.
summary: Zc3h14 did not phenocopy the measurable THO/TREX and cleavage-polyadenylation comparators.
why_it_matters: Although ZC3H14 physically interacts with THO components and was expected to share RNA-processing consequences, Thoc1 was broad but directionally different, Ddx39b responded only in one matched group without exact overlap, and Cstf2 itself was transcriptionally silent as a perturbation; the P16 snRNA phenotype therefore isolates a Zc3h14-specific feedback rather than a generic THO/TREX failure state.

literature_claim: Drosophila dNab2 interacts genetically and biochemically with the Fragile-X ortholog and with Ataxin-2 to regulate neuronal mRNAs and morphology.
main_caveats: The prior network is strongest in Drosophila; Fmr1 had a modest positive restricted cosine but no exact FDR-level overlap.
summary: Fragile-X/Ataxin-2 relatives measured in the screen were largely flat where Zc3h14 responded.
why_it_matters: The lack of Fmr1 or Atxn2 phenocopy keeps the Drosophila dNab2-Fmr1-Atx2 genetic network from being over-projected onto acute mouse P16 loss; the Zc3h14 snRNA signature is not a generic neuronal RBP-loss state.

literature_claim: No ZC3H14-FLRT3 relationship was identified.
main_caveats: The rejection applies to robust FDR-level transcriptomic convergence, not to non-transcriptional FLRT3 biology.
summary: The apparent top negative neighbor, Flrt3, was rejected after full-surface follow-up.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting a 14-feature anticorrelation: Flrt3 was the lowest cosine neighbor but had only a single weak FDR hit in the matched groups and no significant overlap with Zc3h14.

literature_claim: ZDHHC17 is a neuronal palmitoyltransferase with synaptic and cytoskeletal substrates or interactors, including SNAP25, PSD95, GAD65, HTT, CLIP3, and MAP6.
main_caveats: Only one downstream gene reached FDR<0.10, and Tubb3 is interpreted as a transcriptional sentinel rather than a proven direct palmitoylation substrate.
summary: Zdhhc17 induced a single robust downstream hit, Tubb3 down, only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The perturbation is not globally silent: it exposes one thalamic glutamatergic state that couples Zdhhc17 loss to a nuclear tubulin transcript, while the rest of the atlas is buffered.

literature_claim: ZDHHC17 acts mainly through palmitoylation of existing proteins, and partial HIP14 expression can rescue most Hip14-null phenotypes in vivo.
main_caveats: The actual DNA-editing rate and ZDHHC17 protein depletion are unmeasured.
summary: 155 MB Glut showed significant Zdhhc17 self-transcript reduction without any downstream FDR<0.10 gene.
why_it_matters: The midbrain result separates target mRNA reduction from a propagated transcriptional phenotype, making the weak result biologically informative rather than a simple low-cell-count failure.

literature_claim: HIP14/ZDHHC17 regulates palmitoylation-dependent trafficking and clustering of neuronal substrates including SNAP25, PSD95/DLG4, GAD65, synaptotagmin I, HTT, CSP, CLIP3, and MAP6.
main_caveats: Absence of substrate mRNA DE does not test substrate palmitoylation or synaptic localization directly.
summary: Canonical HIP14 substrate and synaptic receptor mRNAs were absent from the Zdhhc17 FDR<0.10 surface.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues that acute Zdhhc17 loss is not read out by transcription of its substrates; detecting the canonical mechanism would require palmitoyl-proteomics, localization, synaptic-vesicle, or electrophysiology assays.

literature_claim: HIP14 palmitoylates huntingtin and Hip14-null mouse phenotypes overlap Huntington-disease-like striatal pathology.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and sparse; it does not assay HTT palmitoylation or mutant-HTT gain of function.
summary: Acute Htt and Zdhhc17 perturbations diverged: Htt produced sterol/lipid genes whereas Zdhhc17 produced Tubb3 only.
why_it_matters: The result refines the Huntington link by showing that HIP14-ZDHHC17 loss is not equivalent to Htt lowering on the juvenile neuronal transcriptomic axis.

literature_claim: PSD95/DLG4 is a HIP14 substrate, and ZDHHC17 loss produces synaptic functional deficits in mouse models.
main_caveats: NMDAR genes are pathway-neighbor comparators rather than direct ZDHHC17 substrates.
summary: Dlg4/Psd95 was downstream-flat like Zdhhc17, whereas NMDAR-subunit perturbations generated measurable RNA responses.
why_it_matters: Same synaptic neighborhood did not imply a shared DE surface: scaffold/palmitoylation defects remained buffered, while receptor-subunit loss fed back to the nucleus.

literature_claim: No prior comparator was used; this was a whole-parquet Wilcoxon-score nearest-neighbor search.
main_caveats: Cosine values are tiny because the Zdhhc17 downstream signature is almost null; the neighbor ranking is useful as a negative benchmark, not as a mechanistic module.
summary: The data-driven neighbor search found only near-zero positive neighbors and a broad Uba5 negative neighbor.
why_it_matters: Zdhhc17 lacks a robust recurring co-perturbation module in this atlas, and the Uba5 contrast shows that broad secondary transcription was detectable in the exact thalamic and midbrain classes where Zdhhc17 was nearly flat.

literature_claim: Mouse-brain Zeb1 LoF work emphasized embryonic cortical neural progenitors, division orientation, germinal-zone exit and migration.
main_caveats: 145 and 217 are one-gene signatures; 217 is based on only 30 perturbed nuclei.
summary: Zeb1 loss was almost silent in most postmitotic brain neurons but reproducibly activated a small thalamic/midbrain-enriched module.
why_it_matters: The positive biology is concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with one-gene recurrences in 145, 191 and 217 rather than in embryonic-neocortex-like populations.

literature_claim: ZEB-family repressors recruit CtBP; ZEB1 represses epithelial polarity genes including PATJ; AP1M2, PATJ, F11R and STXBP2 are linked to polarized sorting, tight junctions or trafficking.
main_caveats: Only Patj among the classic PATJ/CRB3/HUGL2 set was FDR-significant; several observed genes are module members rather than proven direct ZEB1 targets.
summary: The main Zeb1 transcriptomic output is de-repression of an epithelial junction, polarity and vesicle-trafficking cassette.
why_it_matters: All FDR-supported hits were up, matching loss of a transcriptional repressor and nominating Patj, Ap1m2, F11r, and Stxbp2 rather than generic neuronal identity genes.

literature_claim: ZEB proteins recruit CtBP co-repressors, and CTBP2 cooperates with ZEB1 during neocortical development.
main_caveats: Ctbp2 was not a perturbation target; Ctbp1 reproduced the 145/151 core but not the full 155/191/217 Zeb1 surface.
summary: Ctbp1 perturbation partially phenocopied the Zeb1 module in the same thalamic groups.
why_it_matters: A directly measured co-repressor perturbation recovered Stxbp2, F11r, Ap1m2, St3gal4, Hook2 and Usp43 in the same direction, making the ZEB/CtBP axis the strongest mechanistic comparator in the screen.

literature_claim: ZEB1 and ZEB2 are related E-box repressors linked to EMT/TGF-beta signaling, and Zeb2 has documented embryonic neuronal roles including midbrain dopaminergic development.
main_caveats: Some comparator perturbations had fewer recovered cell groups than Zeb1, and Ctbp2 itself was not assayed.
summary: The expected paralog and upstream EMT/TGF-beta pathway neighbors did not phenocopy Zeb1.
why_it_matters: Zeb2, TGF-beta receptor, SMAD, Snai2, Twist2 and E-protein perturbations were directly queried and failed to recover the Stxbp2-Ap1m2-F11r-Patj module.

literature_claim: Embryonic and adult progenitor studies connect ZEB1 to neurogenic self-renewal, neuronal differentiation, migration and PARD6B/Neurod1 regulation; epithelial studies identify CRB3, HUGL2 and PATJ as ZEB1-repressed polarity genes.
main_caveats: A promoter-bound direct target in embryonic progenitors need not remain detectably regulated in mature neurons.
summary: Postnatal Zeb1 loss did not induce the canonical embryonic neural-progenitor or full epithelial MET target set.
why_it_matters: Pard6-family, Pard3, Chl1, Limk2, Neurod1 and Etv5 were flat across all 23 groups, and Cdh1/Crb3/Llgl2/Ocln were flat even in responders; the screen therefore recovered a narrow PATJ/F11R/AP1M2 branch.

main_caveats: The neighbor scan used the model-visible Wilcoxon surface, not independent protein or chromatin phenotypes.
summary: Whole-transcriptome global signature neighbors were numerically weak and were not accepted as biological phenocopies.
why_it_matters: The top non-safe global neighbors had absolute Wilcoxon-score correlations of only 0.027 or less and no exact FDR overlap with Zeb1, whereas Ctbp1 emerged only in the robust-module overlap scan.

main_caveats: Absence of secondary stress transcription does not exclude subtle electrophysiological or synaptic phenotypes.
summary: Zeb1 did not look like a generic neuronal stress, proteasome-bounce-back or synaptic-downregulation perturbation.
why_it_matters: All Zeb1 FDR hits were up and sparse, whereas Psmc1 and Psmb4 caused thousands of DE genes with synaptic/ion-channel losses and stress or ubiquitin markers.

literature_claim: Zeb2 has strong embryonic roles in forebrain pyramidal neurons and MGE-derived interneurons.
main_caveats: L2/3 and CTX-CGE signatures are only one to two genes and near the FDR cutoff; DNA editing was not measured.
summary: Zeb2 responded in only four of 22 measured neuronal groups, with 11 of the 15 total FDR<0.10 downstream entries concentrated in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
why_it_matters: The response surface argues against a pan-neuronal juvenile requirement and nominates Pvalb GABA neurons as the main postmitotic residual target class.

direction: Rasd2/Plcl1/Patj up; Dlx6/Dcx/Zfp536 down; embryonic guidance genes absent
literature_claim: Embryonic Zeb2 is required downstream of Dlx1/2 for cortical interneuron migration and MGE fate, while Dlx5/6 are important for Pvalb interneuron development.
main_caveats: Only 11 genes passed FDR<0.10 in Pvalb; the Rasd2 interpretation is marker-based and not proof of a full striatal fate conversion.
summary: P16 Zeb2 loss in Pvalb neurons induced a mixed terminal-state signature rather than the embryonic Nkx2-1/Unc5b guidance program.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive signal keeps interneuron biology in view for Mowat-Wilson disease but shifts the assayed phenotype from embryonic migration/fate choice to a small maintenance-age Pvalb state change.

direction: junction/polarity genes up after loss of ZEB-family repression
literature_claim: ZEB2 is usually a transcriptional repressor and can recruit NuRD and CtBP co-repressors through defined protein domains.
main_caveats: Patj itself is not established here as a direct Zeb2 target, and Cdh1/Cldn4 were absent.
summary: Patj was the only recurrent Zeb2-induced gene, rising in both L4/5 IT and Pvalb neurons and aligning with a ZEB-family polarity/junction module seen for Zeb1 and Ctbp1 in other groups.
why_it_matters: A single polarity scaffold may be a sensitive neuronal readout of a transcriptional-repression axis that, in non-neuronal EMT systems, includes junctional genes, while showing that the full epithelial program is mostly inaccessible in NeuN+ nuclei.

direction: Otof and Slf2 up; Phyhip down
main_caveats: FDR values were 0.055-0.071 and no pathway-level second hit corroborated these genes.
summary: The non-Pvalb responder groups contained only marker-sized signatures: Otof up and Phyhip down in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Slf2 up in 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
why_it_matters: These FDR<0.10 observations should be preserved as real cell-restricted signals, but their one- or two-gene scope indicates that Zeb2 loss was strongly buffered in those postmitotic neurons.

literature_claim: ZEB2 is a SMAD-binding ZEB transcription factor that can recruit CtBP and NuRD, and Dlx genes are upstream or neighboring regulators of interneuron programs.
main_caveats: The comparison uses transcriptomic convergence only; several pathway genes had few perturbed cells in 007 or 046.
summary: Canonical ZEB/SMAD/NuRD relatives did not phenocopy the acute Zeb2 signature in matched responder groups.
why_it_matters: Direct perturbation comparison rejects the simplest model that juvenile Zeb2 loss is equivalent to lowering Zeb1, a BMP/TGFβ receptor-SMAD arm, CtBP, or NuRD activity.

main_caveats: Full-vector correlations are useful for rejection here because the largest absolute r was only 0.056; the small Zeb2 signature limits positive overlap statistics.
summary: The unbiased nearest-neighbor search found only near-zero full-surface correlations, and broad Eef2/Psmb4/Zbtb7a perturbations overlapped the Zeb2 hits only sparsely.
why_it_matters: The Zeb2 DE surface is idiosyncratic rather than a generic stress, translation, or proteasome response, despite the fact that such broad signatures are detectable in the same universe.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Embryonic and lineage-specific Zeb2 models deregulate Sfrp1/Wnt, Ntf3/Fgf9 feedback, Unc5/Netrin guidance, Ninein-dependent axon growth, and BMP/SMAD-responsive programs.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq would miss purely morphological axon defects, but it should have detected secondary transcriptional induction of the queried target genes if present.
summary: Expected Wnt/Sfrp1, Ntf3/Fgf9, Ninein, netrin-guidance, BMP/SMAD, and EMT genes were not recovered after postnatal Zeb2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Absence of these programs is informative: many canonical Zeb2 phenotypes require embryonic progenitors, early postmitotic projection growth, or non-neuronal contexts that the P16 NeuN+ assay did not sample.

literature_claim: Zeb2 down-regulation can permit BMP-SMAD-dependent midbrain dopaminergic axon growth and striatal innervation in developmental models.
main_caveats: The warning is based on missing dopaminergic recovery plus Pvalb off-axis activity, not on a direct measurement of edited midbrain dopamine neurons.
summary: Zeb2 was not tested in 215 MB Dopa, the group closest to the published dopaminergic axon-growth model, while Pvalb neurons were the strongest measured responders.
why_it_matters: The result warns against extrapolating this mostly flat juvenile dataset to dopaminergic ZEB2-lowering strategies or to all neuronal classes.

literature_claim: Published ZFAT functional studies emphasize embryonic blood islands, T cells, adipocytes, and centromeres rather than thalamic or midbrain glutamatergic neurons.
main_caveats: Each responding cell group had only one downstream FDR<0.10 gene; the Zfat transcript itself was up-regulated, and DNA indels were not measured.
summary: Zfat produced a two-gene downstream surface restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with Setd1a up in 151 and D6Wsu163e down in 155.
why_it_matters: The main biological output of postnatal neuronal Zfat loss was not a canonical hematopoietic, immune-survival, stress, or synaptic program but a very narrow glutamatergic response.

literature_claim: SETD1A is a histone H3K4 methylation regulator implicated in neuronal development and neuropsychiatric disease.
main_caveats: The Zfat-Setd1a link is not established in prior literature, and the shared 155 MB Glut readout is one gene, D6Wsu163e.
summary: The only robust thalamic Zfat downstream gene was the H3K4 methyltransferase Setd1a, and Setd1a perturbation itself strongly affected the same thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: A single-gene Zfat response still points to a chromatin-regulatory neighborhood that is active and detectable in these neuronal bins; this helps separate a buffered Zfat response from a globally insensitive DE assay.

literature_claim: ZFAT can recruit KAT2B and BRD4 at centromeres to control centromeric ncRNA, while SETD1A is a distinct transcriptional chromatin regulator.
main_caveats: BRD4 convergence was judged only from gene-level snRNA; centromeric satellite RNAs were not measured.
summary: Brd4 and Setd1a perturbations generated broad signatures in the same responder bins in which Zfat generated only one gene per group.
why_it_matters: The contrast rejects a simple model in which loss of Zfat phenocopies the KAT2B-H4K8ac-BRD4 centromeric axis or a generic chromatin-regulator knockout on gene-level neuronal mRNA.

literature_claim: Zfat-ZsGreen reporter mice showed signal in CA1 pyramidal cells and cerebellar Purkinje cells, suggesting possible nervous-system functions.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq groups are broad and 10x snRNA may dilute a subset-specific CA1 or Purkinje response.
summary: CA1/DG and cerebellar GABA bins were null despite published Zfat reporter signal in CA1 pyramidal and Purkinje cells.
why_it_matters: The result refines reporter expression into an acute loss-of-function statement: expression in a neuronal subtype did not guarantee a detectable P16-to-P37/44 cell-body mRNA requirement.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Zfat directly regulates Tal1, Lmo2, and Gata1 in embryonic blood islands and supports FoxO1/Akt/autophagy-dependent survival in T cells and adipocyte maintenance in adipocytes.
main_caveats: The queried effector perturbations test pathway behavior in neurons, not the original yolk-sac, T-cell, or adipocyte contexts.
summary: The Tal1/Lmo2/Gata1 blood-island program and the FoxO1/Akt/Brpf1 immune-survival program were not recovered after neuronal Zfat perturbation.
why_it_matters: This separates Zfat's established lineage functions from the juvenile postmitotic neuronal setting and explains why absent canonical genes are biologically expected rather than a technical failure.

main_caveats: Neighbor ranking used all matched Wilcoxon-score rows and can be dominated by weak distributed noise when the seed perturbation has only two FDR-significant downstream genes.
summary: The top genome-wide Zfat signature neighbors had absolute cosine below 0.026 and did not reproduce the two Zfat downstream genes in matched responder groups.
why_it_matters: The negative neighbor test prevents over-interpreting near-zero all-transcriptome ranks as a real module and shows that Zfat did not join a robust convergence class in this dataset.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Nt5c3 is a cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase; ZFHX2 pain work suggested possible olfactory involvement, but did not nominate an Nt5c3 regulon.
main_caveats: Singleton result at FDR 0.089 from 78 perturbed nuclei; not enough genes to define a pathway.
summary: Zfhx2 produced a single weak downstream hit, Nt5c3 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
why_it_matters: This is the entire FDR<0.10 Zfhx2 response and therefore marks a narrow piriform/anterior-olfactory/entorhinal effect rather than a broad ZFHX2 transcription-factor regulon.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ZFHX2 p.R1913K/p.R1907K and Zfhx2-null models alter pain behavior and DRG expression of pain/neuropeptide genes including Gal, Sst, Gfra3, and Ptgir.
main_caveats: DRG and peripheral sensory neurons were not sampled, so the result is a central-brain uncoupling, not a test of nociceptors.
summary: The central Zfhx2 perturbation did not recover the DRG pain/neuropeptide genes Gal, Sst, Gfra3, and Ptgir, and represented pain comparators Gal, Ntrk1, Trpa1, and Trpv1 did not phenocopy it.
why_it_matters: It localizes the established analgesia biology away from the sampled postnatal central-neuron bins and prevents interpreting the screen-wide central null as a refutation of DRG ZFHX2 function.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Neighbor ranks are based on transcriptome-wide score correlations; they are useful here mainly as negative controls because Zfhx2 itself has only one FDR<0.10 gene.
summary: A model-wide Wilcoxon-score neighbor search found only near-zero Zfhx2 correlations, and the top apparent neighbor Hspa5 did not share the 009 Nt5c3 response.
why_it_matters: It keeps the data-driven comparison from turning a nearly null signature into a spurious convergence claim.

summary: Represented cohesin/CTCF comparators were not Zfp609 phenocopies: Smc1a and Stag2, two proteins recovered in Zfp609 pull-downs, produced convergent DE in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Zfp609 had zero significant genes there.
why_it_matters: The dataset can register transcriptional responses to chromosome-organization factors in the same postnatal assay, but Zfp609 itself is uncoupled from those responses; this matches the prior that the Zfp609/Nipbl embryonic promoter-enhancer program is largely cohesin-independent.

literature_claim: Zfp612 encodes a KRAB/C2H2 zinc-finger protein, a class of locus-specific repressors whose effects are shaped by DNA binding and local chromatin rather than by the pan-genomic action expected for a core silencing cofactor.
main_caveats: snRNA-seq measured host genes but not indels or repeat-derived transcripts; two responding groups have only one or two significant genes.
summary: Zfp612 loss produced a host-gene response in only 2 of 23 measured neuronal groups: two genes in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and one gene in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The dominant phenotype is not a pan-neuronal KRAB repressor collapse; it is an extremely sparse, cell-class-restricted response that remains visible despite a flat self-transcript.

literature_claim: KRAB-ZFP loss should derepress direct targets; independently, NOTUM enzymatically removes Wnt palmitoleate and suppresses Wnt signaling.
main_caveats: Notum is a single transcript; the dataset does not show direct ZFP612 binding at Notum or coordinated induction of other Wnt-regulatory genes.
summary: Notum is the strongest Zfp612-responsive transcript: it increased about two-fold in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and no other gene in that cell group reached FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Notum is a secreted Wnt-deacylating antagonist, so its selective induction nominates a Wnt-inhibitory marker of Zfp612 loss in a thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic context without implying a broad Wnt pathway signature.

literature_claim: NrCAM supports neuronal adhesion, axon growth/guidance and synapse formation, while the direct effect of KRAB-ZFP loss is expected to be transcriptional derepression.
main_caveats: Single-gene pathway call; the sign implies an indirect or compensatory link rather than a proven bound target.
summary: Nrcam was the only down-regulated FDR<0.10 transcript after Zfp612 perturbation and the only adhesion/axon-guidance gene in the corrected signature.
why_it_matters: A decrease in an L1-family neuronal adhesion molecule is directionally hard to explain as simple release of KRAB repression, pointing to an indirect circuit-maturation or adhesion adjustment in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.

literature_claim: Neuronal IMPACT antagonizes GCN2/eIF2α signaling and promotes neurite outgrowth.
main_caveats: Impact is a singleton FDR signal; it should be treated as a buffering hypothesis, not a measured phospho-eIF2α response.
summary: Impact was selectively up-regulated with Nrcam down in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, without a canonical ER/ISR stress cassette.
why_it_matters: Because IMPACT opposes the GCN2/eIF2α stress kinase in neurons, its isolated increase is most consistent with a small translational-stress buffering axis rather than a full unfolded-protein or amino-acid-starvation response.

literature_claim: KRAB-ZFP/KAP1 systems can silence broad retroelement-linked chromatin domains, and human ZNF23 gain-of-function in dividing cancer cells engages cell-cycle/apoptosis biology.
main_caveats: Repeat RNAs were not quantified; absence is therefore for host-gene secondary programs, not for every possible repeat-derived transcript.
summary: The two real Zfp612 response groups did not show the canonical programs that would make the nulls a readout failure: broad KRAB/KAP1 target derepression, host innate immunity, cell-cycle entry, or a multi-gene ER/ISR signature.
why_it_matters: The assay can recover a stress cassette in matched groups under Gfpt1 perturbation, so the absence of Ddit3/Asns/Hspa5/Herpud1-type induction in Zfp612 cells is informative; the corrected Zfp612 phenotype is Notum, Nrcam, and Impact only.

literature_claim: KRAB-ZFPs can recruit KAP1-associated SETDB1 and NuRD/CHD4 silencing machinery.
main_caveats: Trim28/KAP1 itself was not a represented perturbation; Zkscan and Zscan targets are broad family controls, not close Zfp612 paralogs.
summary: Zfp612 did not phenocopy represented KRAB-associated chromatin effectors or broad zinc-finger comparators.
why_it_matters: Setdb1 and Chd4 had many corrected genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but failed to share Notum, Impact, or Nrcam, while Gatad2b, Zkscan1, Zkscan16, and Zscan26 were also essentially orthogonal. The Zfp612 program is therefore not a generic SETDB1/NuRD/KRAB-family response.

main_caveats: Score-cosine neighbors were computed over Wilcoxon scores; this is a transcriptome-level comparison and can miss convergence at unmeasured repeats or proteins.
summary: Unbiased whole-surface signature search also classified Zfp612 as almost neighborless: the largest non-self Wilcoxon-score cosine was 0.0345 and a safe-target signature was the nominal nearest neighbor.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation background argues that the three-gene Zfp612 outcome is a buffered or context-idiosyncratic perturbation, not the edge of a larger recurrent module shared with other strong perturbations.

why_it_matters: Ehmt1 and Setdb1 produced real downstream genes despite similarly weak own-transcript changes, so H3K9-linked chromatin perturbations were not globally invisible to the assay; Zfp644 was specifically dispensable for the acute mature-neuron transcriptome under this design.

why_it_matters: The main result is not a hidden small pathway but broad postnatal transcriptional buffering: acute, sparse Zfp804a coding loss after neuronal specification does not launch a cell-autonomous nuclear RNA program in the assayed NeuN+ populations.

main_caveats: The neighbor calculation used all matched Wilcoxon scores because Zfp804a had no FDR<0.10 gene set; it is a negative diagnostic, not a mechanistic module.
summary: The pre-literature score-profile neighbor search nominated no credible convergent module for Zfp804a.
why_it_matters: The top positive and negative perturbation neighbors were essentially uncorrelated, and most had zero or only one to three robust DE genes, so cross-target analysis rejects these as biological phenocopies rather than forcing a pathway label onto a flat signature.

why_it_matters: Human rs1344706 effects are fetal-splice/expression effects, whereas this assay perturbed the coding gene in already specified juvenile mouse neurons; the all-null surface therefore maps the disease-relevant displacement toward fetal isoform regulation and early circuitry rather than an acute maintenance transcriptome.

why_it_matters: LDHB sits at the lactate-pyruvate redox node, so the one positive signature nominates a narrow metabolic state rather than the broad chromatin or stress response expected from a global KRAB/SETDB1 disruption.

main_caveats: The neighborhood was computed from Wilcoxon-score vectors; because Zfp846 is almost flat, tiny correlations are expected to be unstable.

why_it_matters: The top full-transcriptome cosine neighbors were near zero and failed to share the only Zfp846 FDR gene, so cross-perturbation analysis rejects an apparent module instead of overinterpreting rank-noise around a one-gene response.

why_it_matters: SETDB1, a core enzyme recruited by KRAB-ZFP systems, generated 45 FDR<0.10 annotated-gene changes across the same 22 groups, including a 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Tasor/Atf7ip/protocadherin response, whereas Zfp846 was flat in those groups and did not share the 217 P MY Pineal Glut Ldhb effect.
